text: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists on Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Psychiatric Safety and Antidepressant Potential.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, but concerns about their mental health effects have been raised
title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists on Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Psychiatric Safety and Antidepressant Potential.

text: . Early safety reports linked them to suicidal thoughts and worsening depression; however, evidence remained mixed and unclear. A systematic search was conducted across three databases for studies published between 2021 and May 2026. Out of 617 records identified, 11 studies were finally included after quality checks using appropriate appraisal tools based on study design
title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists on Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Psychiatric Safety and Antidepressant Potential.

text: . This review was not prospectively registered. Data from over 4.9 million patients across eleven primary studies showed that GLP-1RAs did not increase psychiatric risk overall. Ten out of eleven primary studies confirmed either safety or protective psychiatric effects
title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists on Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Psychiatric Safety and Antidepressant Potential.

text: . Increased psychiatric risk was seen in one obesity-specific study; this may partly reflect surveillance or detection bias, though this was not directly tested. Only one of the 11 included studies directly measured mood using validated questionnaires and found that semaglutide was associated with lower (better) depression and anxiety scores
title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists on Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Psychiatric Safety and Antidepressant Potential.

text: . GLP-1 receptor agonists appear to maintain a safe neuropsychiatric profile, with an emerging signal that mood may benefit, currently limited to a single scale-based study among those formally included; most existing evidence remains diagnostic-code-based rather than scale-based. For T2DM patients with stable mood disorders, there is no justification for withholding these medications
title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists on Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Psychiatric Safety and Antidepressant Potential.

text: . For weight management, clinicians may consider baseline mental health screening before starting treatment. Future research must use validated continuous mood rating tools rather than administrative diagnostic codes to properly measure psychological benefits.
title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists on Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Psychiatric Safety and Antidepressant Potential.

text: Suprabasal Blistering as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Bullous Pemphigoid: Histopathologic-Immunofluorescence Discordance Complicated by Sepsis.. Bullous pemphigoid is the most common autoimmune subepidermal blistering disease, typically diagnosed through a combination of clinical features, histopathology, and direct immunofluorescence (DIF)
title: Suprabasal Blistering as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Bullous Pemphigoid: Histopathologic-Immunofluorescence Discordance Complicated by Sepsis.

text: . However, histopathological findings can be misleading when re-epithelialization shifts the blister plane from subepidermal to suprabasal, mimicking pemphigus vulgaris
title: Suprabasal Blistering as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Bullous Pemphigoid: Histopathologic-Immunofluorescence Discordance Complicated by Sepsis.

text: . We present the case of a 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus, diabetic neuropathy, and a sacral pressure ulcer admitted with a three-week history of generalized tense bullae in a symmetric distribution across the trunk and extremities, with subsequent oral mucosal involvement. The disease was classified as severe bullous pemphigoid
title: Suprabasal Blistering as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Bullous Pemphigoid: Histopathologic-Immunofluorescence Discordance Complicated by Sepsis.

text: . Skin biopsy revealed a suprabasal blister with eosinophilic infiltrate, a pattern classically associated with pemphigus vulgaris; however, DIF demonstrated linear immunoglobulin G and complement C3c deposition at the dermoepidermal junction, confirming bullous pemphigoid and categorically ruling out pemphigus
title: Suprabasal Blistering as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Bullous Pemphigoid: Histopathologic-Immunofluorescence Discordance Complicated by Sepsis.

text: . Initial treatment with systemic corticosteroids and immunosuppressants was complicated by septic shock secondary to a catheter-related bloodstream infection, hospital-acquired pneumonia, and urinary tract infection, requiring vasopressor support, adjustment of the immunosuppressive regimen, and antimicrobial escalation
title: Suprabasal Blistering as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Bullous Pemphigoid: Histopathologic-Immunofluorescence Discordance Complicated by Sepsis.

text: . The patient also developed progressive multifactorial anemia, sepsis-associated coagulopathy, and upper gastrointestinal bleeding
title: Suprabasal Blistering as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Bullous Pemphigoid: Histopathologic-Immunofluorescence Discordance Complicated by Sepsis.

text: . Following multidisciplinary management, she achieved near-complete resolution of skin lesions and clinical recovery, and was discharged with plans for rituximab as definitive steroid-sparing therapy.  This case highlights two critical lessons: first, a suprabasal blister on histopathology does not exclude bullous pemphigoid, as re-epithelialization can alter the apparent cleavage plane, making
title: Suprabasal Blistering as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Bullous Pemphigoid: Histopathologic-Immunofluorescence Discordance Complicated by Sepsis.

text: can alter the apparent cleavage plane, making DIF indispensable for an accurate diagnosis; second, severe bullous pemphigoid requiring intensive immunosuppression carries a substantial risk of sequential nosocomial infections warranting close microbiological surveillance, early source control, and timely modulation of immunosuppressive regimens.
title: Suprabasal Blistering as a Diagnostic Pitfall in Bullous Pemphigoid: Histopathologic-Immunofluorescence Discordance Complicated by Sepsis.

text: Strengthening gestational diabetes mellitus prevention, diagnosis, and care in Africa: evidence and policy priorities from a systematic review, meta-analysis, and bibliometric analysis.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is an increasing public health challenge in Africa, contributing substantially to maternal and neonatal morbidity
title: Strengthening gestational diabetes mellitus prevention, diagnosis, and care in Africa: evidence and policy priorities from a systematic review, meta-analysis, and bibliometric analysis.

text: . Evidence from our systematic review, meta-analysis, and bibliometric analysis shows that inconsistent screening practices, reliance on selective rather than universal testing, and limited health system capacity contribute to underdiagnosis and poor pregnancy outcomes
title: Strengthening gestational diabetes mellitus prevention, diagnosis, and care in Africa: evidence and policy priorities from a systematic review, meta-analysis, and bibliometric analysis.

text: . GDM is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal complications and increases the long-term risk of type-2 diabetes for mothers and offspring. Our bibliometric findings reveal uneven research capacity, limited regional collaboration, and evidence gaps across Africa
title: Strengthening gestational diabetes mellitus prevention, diagnosis, and care in Africa: evidence and policy priorities from a systematic review, meta-analysis, and bibliometric analysis.

text: . We propose five policy priorities: standardising GDM screening, strengthening prevention, expanding access to diagnostics and treatment, improving workforce capacity and follow-up, and increasing investment in African-led research to improve maternal health and reduce the intergenerational burden of diabetes.
title: Strengthening gestational diabetes mellitus prevention, diagnosis, and care in Africa: evidence and policy priorities from a systematic review, meta-analysis, and bibliometric analysis.

text: Comorbid Cardiovascular-Liver Disease Disparities: Current Understanding and Future Directions.. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent chronic liver disease and a multisystem cardiometabolic disorder. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in this population
title: Comorbid Cardiovascular-Liver Disease Disparities: Current Understanding and Future Directions.

text: . This review examines disparities in the recognition and management of coexisting cardiovascular and metabolic liver disease. Shared metabolic and inflammatory pathways link liver disease with obesity, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and CVD
title: Comorbid Cardiovascular-Liver Disease Disparities: Current Understanding and Future Directions.

text: . Differences in measured disease prevalence across racial and ethnic groups must be interpreted separately from genetic susceptibility and in the context of structural inequities, diagnostic practices, and access to care. Socioeconomic disadvantage and sex- and gender-related barriers may further affect diagnosis and treatment
title: Comorbid Cardiovascular-Liver Disease Disparities: Current Understanding and Future Directions.

text: . Resmetirom and semaglutide have expanded treatment options for selected adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), but unequal access to fibrosis assessment, insurance coverage, and longitudinal care may limit their benefits
title: Comorbid Cardiovascular-Liver Disease Disparities: Current Understanding and Future Directions.

text: . An equity-centered cardio-hepatology framework should integrate early risk identification, stepwise noninvasive fibrosis assessment, individualized cardiovascular prevention, and access to indicated liver-directed therapies. Treatment and quality measures should reflect clinical eligibility rather than medication use alone
title: Comorbid Cardiovascular-Liver Disease Disparities: Current Understanding and Future Directions.

text: . Inclusive research and coordinated long-term care are needed to evaluate whether these strategies narrow disparities.
title: Comorbid Cardiovascular-Liver Disease Disparities: Current Understanding and Future Directions.

text: The causal relationship between diabetes mellitus and hashimoto thyroiditis: A two-sample mendelian randomization analysis.
title: The causal relationship between diabetes mellitus and hashimoto thyroiditis: A two-sample mendelian randomization analysis.

text: . This study aims to investigate the genetic correlation and potential causal relationship between diabetes mellitus (DM) and Hashimoto thyroiditis (HT), and to assess the effects of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) on HT risk, with the goal of informing thyroid-function monitoring in patients with DM and improving HT management
title: The causal relationship between diabetes mellitus and hashimoto thyroiditis: A two-sample mendelian randomization analysis.

text: . We used linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) to estimate the genetic correlation between DM and HT. We then performed two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR) using data from genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to evaluate potential causal effects of DM subtypes on HT
title: The causal relationship between diabetes mellitus and hashimoto thyroiditis: A two-sample mendelian randomization analysis.

text: . We selected single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) as instrumental variables (IVs) and applied the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method along with complementary sensitivity analyses to estimate causal effects. We assessed heterogeneity using Cochran's Q test and identified outlier SNPs with MR-PRESSO (Mendelian Randomization Pleiotropy RESidual Sum and Outlier)
title: The causal relationship between diabetes mellitus and hashimoto thyroiditis: A two-sample mendelian randomization analysis.

text: . We used the MR-Egger intercept to test for directional pleiotropy. Finally, we performed a leave-one-out analysis to evaluate whether any single SNP unduly influenced the MR estimates. LDSC showed a significant negative genetic correlation between DM and HT (rG = -0.3285, SE = 0.062, P = 1.20 × 10-7), with evidence of nonzero SNP heritability (h2P < .005)
title: The causal relationship between diabetes mellitus and hashimoto thyroiditis: A two-sample mendelian randomization analysis.

text: . In two-sample MR analyses of DM overall, the IVW estimate suggested increased HT risk in UK Biobank (OR = 7.26, 95% CI = 1.95-27.11, P < .05) and was directionally consistent in FinnGen (OR = 1.08, 95% CI = 1.02-1.14, P < .05)
title: The causal relationship between diabetes mellitus and hashimoto thyroiditis: A two-sample mendelian randomization analysis.

text: . Subtype-specific MR analyses supported a causal effect of T2DM on HT (OR = 1.10, 95% CI = 1.05-1.16, P < .05), whereas there was no evidence for a causal effect of T1DM (OR = 1.04, 95% CI = 0.97-1.12, P > .05). We provide genetic support for a causal relationship between T2DM liability and higher HT risk, with no evidence of a direct causal effect for T1DM
title: The causal relationship between diabetes mellitus and hashimoto thyroiditis: A two-sample mendelian randomization analysis.

text: . These findings motivate periodic thyroid-function assessment and integrated endocrine-metabolic care in T2DM, and warrant multi-ancestry and mechanistic studies to refine risk prediction and identify actionable biology.
title: The causal relationship between diabetes mellitus and hashimoto thyroiditis: A two-sample mendelian randomization analysis.

text: Efficacy and mechanistic insights of dapagliflozin in hypertension management.. Hypertension remains one of the leading modifiable risk factors for cardiovascular disease and premature mortality worldwide. Blood pressure (BP) management is particularly challenging in patients with coexisting type 2 diabetes (T2D), chronic kidney disease (CKD), or heart failure (HF)
title: Efficacy and mechanistic insights of dapagliflozin in hypertension management.
journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)

text: . Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have become an integral component of contemporary cardiorenal therapy and have consistently demonstrated additional BP-lowering effects across diverse clinical settings
title: Efficacy and mechanistic insights of dapagliflozin in hypertension management.
journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)

text: . This narrative review synthesizes the current clinical evidence regarding the antihypertensive effects of dapagliflozin and summarizes the biological mechanisms that may contribute to these effects, including osmotic diuresis and natriuresis, weight reduction, modulation of the sympathetic nervous system, enhanced uric acid excretion, and attenuation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and
title: Efficacy and mechanistic insights of dapagliflozin in hypertension management.
journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)

text: of oxidative stress, inflammation, and vascular dysfunction
title: Efficacy and mechanistic insights of dapagliflozin in hypertension management.
journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)

text: . Across clinical studies, reductions in systolic BP (SBP) generally exceed those in diastolic BP (DBP), although the physiological basis underlying this differential response remains incompletely understood. Dapagliflozin has demonstrated good tolerability and antihypertensive effects in clinical applications, its long-term use may be limited by the risk of genital infections
title: Efficacy and mechanistic insights of dapagliflozin in hypertension management.
journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)

text: . Collectively, the available evidence supports dapagliflozin as a cardiorenal therapeutic agent that may provide additional BP-lowering benefits in patients with hypertension and concomitant T2D, CKD, or HF, rather than as a substitute for conventional antihypertensive therapy. Future hypertension-focused clinical studies are warranted to further define its role in hypertension management
title: Efficacy and mechanistic insights of dapagliflozin in hypertension management.
journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)

text: . Global hypertension crisis: affects over a billion adults, major risk for heart disease and premature death.Dapagliflozin benefits: additional blood pressure benefits complement its cardiorenal protection.Dapagliflozin risks: potential for genital infections, but offers a new hypertension treatment option.
title: Efficacy and mechanistic insights of dapagliflozin in hypertension management.
journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)

text: Resistant Hypertension: State of the Art Review.
title: Resistant Hypertension: State of the Art Review.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

text: . Resistant hypertension, defined as blood pressure above target despite treatment with at least three antihypertensive agents (including a diuretic) or controlled blood pressure requiring four or more medications, affects over 140 million individuals globally and confers increased risks of heart failure, stroke, and chronic kidney disease progression
title: Resistant Hypertension: State of the Art Review.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

text: . A considerable proportion of cases represent apparent resistant hypertension, in which pseudo-resistance due to inaccurate blood pressure measurement, medication nonadherence, or white-coat effect has not yet been excluded
title: Resistant Hypertension: State of the Art Review.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

text: . Ambulatory and home blood pressure monitoring are therefore central to confirming true resistance and identifying high-risk phenotypes, including nocturnal hypertension and abnormal dipping patterns. Excluding pseudo-resistance and secondary causes remains essential before escalating therapy
title: Resistant Hypertension: State of the Art Review.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

text: . Resistant hypertension commonly coexists with obesity, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease (CKD), and is driven by overlapping mechanisms of aldosterone excess, sodium and water retention, and sympathetic activation
title: Resistant Hypertension: State of the Art Review.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

text: . Guideline-directed treatment centers on optimization of lifestyle measures and triple therapy with renin-angiotensin system blockade, a calcium channel blocker, and a thiazide-like diuretic, followed by a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist as preferred fourth-line agent
title: Resistant Hypertension: State of the Art Review.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

text: . In patients with CKD, careful assessment of volume status, diuretic selection, kidney function, and hyperkalemia risk is particularly important. Recent therapeutic advances have expanded options for patients who remain uncontrolled. Newly FDA-approved agents aprocitentan and baxdrostat provide additional pharmacologic options for patients inadequately controlled on existing therapy
title: Resistant Hypertension: State of the Art Review.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

text: . Renal denervation offers a separate device-based approach for selected patients, while investigational RNA-based and other neuromodulatory therapies may further broaden future treatment options
title: Resistant Hypertension: State of the Art Review.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

text: . Future management is likely to move toward more precise, phenotype-guided treatment integrating ambulatory blood pressure patterns, renin-aldosterone biology, volume status, kidney function, and cardiometabolic comorbidities. Improved diagnostic precision and mechanism-based treatment strategies may reduce persistent treatment gaps and improve long-term cardiovascular and kidney outcomes.
title: Resistant Hypertension: State of the Art Review.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

text: Associations between Inflammatory Markers, Micronutrients, and Disease Severity in COVID-19 Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.. The management of treatment strategies in COVID-19 is critical, especially in patients with type 2 diabetes
title: Associations between Inflammatory Markers, Micronutrients, and Disease Severity in COVID-19 Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
journal: Iranian journal of allergy, asthma, and immunology

text: . Non-enzymatic glycation of transmembrane protease serine 2 and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 during COVID-19 in patients with diabetes may exacerbate immune dysregulation and inflammation
title: Associations between Inflammatory Markers, Micronutrients, and Disease Severity in COVID-19 Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
journal: Iranian journal of allergy, asthma, and immunology

text: . Elevated inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1, IL-2, IL-6, IL-7, and IL-10, tumor necrosis factor-α, interferon-γ, granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 have been observed in COVID-19 patients
title: Associations between Inflammatory Markers, Micronutrients, and Disease Severity in COVID-19 Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
journal: Iranian journal of allergy, asthma, and immunology

text: . This review aims to assess the relationship between inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein, and micronutrients (vitamins D and C, zinc, and copper) with the severity of COVID-19 infection in patients with type 2 diabetes. A narrative review was conducted through a comprehensive literature search of English-language articles published between 2000 and 2025
title: Associations between Inflammatory Markers, Micronutrients, and Disease Severity in COVID-19 Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
journal: Iranian journal of allergy, asthma, and immunology

text: . The databases searched included PubMed, Scopus, the ISI Web of Science, Cochrane, and Embase. Search terms included COVID-19, infections, type 2 diabetes mellitus, interleukins, and micronutrients. English-language scientific articles, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses were included, while studies lacking sufficient information, letters, comments, and editorials were excluded
title: Associations between Inflammatory Markers, Micronutrients, and Disease Severity in COVID-19 Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
journal: Iranian journal of allergy, asthma, and immunology

text: . Evidence suggests that immune-boosting components such as proteins, vitamins, and minerals can enhance immunity to infections. Vitamins D and C, zinc, and copper play supportive roles in immune function, potentially modulating the inflammatory response in COVID-19 patients with type 2 diabetes. High levels of inflammatory cytokines correlate with increased disease severity in this population
title: Associations between Inflammatory Markers, Micronutrients, and Disease Severity in COVID-19 Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
journal: Iranian journal of allergy, asthma, and immunology

text: . Understanding the interplay between inflammatory markers and micronutrients may guide improved therapeutic strategies for managing COVID-19 in diabetic patients. Further research is warranted to clarify these relationships and optimize clinical outcomes.
title: Associations between Inflammatory Markers, Micronutrients, and Disease Severity in COVID-19 Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
journal: Iranian journal of allergy, asthma, and immunology

text: Predictors of treatment response to semaglutide for weight management.. The emergence of weekly, injectable glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists has revolutionized the obesity management landscape
title: Predictors of treatment response to semaglutide for weight management.

text: . Numerous studies have shown high efficacy as well as great variability in weight loss, highlighting the need for this mini review, summarizing current evidence about predictors of semaglutide-related weight loss. The first well-known determinant of semaglutide-induced weight loss is the presence of type 2 DM which is associated with significantly lower body weight reduction
title: Predictors of treatment response to semaglutide for weight management.

text: . The second predictor is sex, with females exhibiting a greater weight loss than males by a mean 6%. In addition, higher maintenance dose of 7.2 mg is superior to standard 2.4 mg dose in weight reduction by a mean 3%
title: Predictors of treatment response to semaglutide for weight management.

text: . There is no clear association of age and baseline body mass index with the magnitude of semaglutide-driven weight loss, except for the possibility of adolescence enhancing and overweight reducing this treatment effect
title: Predictors of treatment response to semaglutide for weight management.

text: . The potential impact of genetic polymorphisms of individual treatment response to semaglutide remains incompletely understood, limited so far to a modest effect of specific variants in GLP1 receptor gene. Another potential predictor of response could be obesity phenotype, with preliminary data supporting greater effectiveness of semaglutide in individuals with ''hungry gut'' phenotype
title: Predictors of treatment response to semaglutide for weight management.

text: . Type of lifestyle modification does not seem to have a significant effect on the variability of semaglutide-driven weight loss. Further studies are needed to expand knowledge about predictors of response to semaglutide, paving the way for validated predictive models in order to guide clinical decision-making and provision of personalized obesity care.
title: Predictors of treatment response to semaglutide for weight management.

text: Case Report: A novel 1, 171 bp GCK promoter/exon 1 deletion in a Chinese pedigree: correcting a misdiagnosis of MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant.
title: Case Report: A novel 1, 171 bp GCK promoter/exon 1 deletion in a Chinese pedigree: correcting a misdiagnosis of MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant.

text: . Maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) comprises a heterogeneous group of autosomal dominant monogenic diabetes disorders; accurate molecular diagnosis is essential, as different subtypes require fundamentally distinct management strategies
title: Case Report: A novel 1, 171 bp GCK promoter/exon 1 deletion in a Chinese pedigree: correcting a misdiagnosis of MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant.

text: . In a Chinese pedigree initially misdiagnosed as MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant, we aimed to identify the true genetic etiology through comprehensive genetic analysis (including copy number variation [CNV] detection) and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), and to illustrate the clinical consequences of rigorous variant interpretation
title: Case Report: A novel 1, 171 bp GCK promoter/exon 1 deletion in a Chinese pedigree: correcting a misdiagnosis of MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant.

text: . Detailed clinical evaluation, whole-exome sequencing (WES), whole-genome sequencing (WGS), multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA), segregation analysis, and CGM monitoring were performed across three generations of the pedigree
title: Case Report: A novel 1, 171 bp GCK promoter/exon 1 deletion in a Chinese pedigree: correcting a misdiagnosis of MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant.

text: . We identified a 1, 171 bp GCK deletion (chr7:44, 228, 224-44, 229, 394 [GRCh37], encompassing the β-cell promoter, exon 1, and part of intron 1) that co-segregated with diabetes across three generations. This deletion removes the β-cell promoter while leaving the hepatic promoter intact, predicting selective loss of the pancreatic glucokinase isoform
title: Case Report: A novel 1, 171 bp GCK promoter/exon 1 deletion in a Chinese pedigree: correcting a misdiagnosis of MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant.

text: . The deletion was classified as pathogenic under ACMG/AMP criteria using the ClinGen Monogenic Diabetes Expert Panel specifications. Segregation analysis revealed that an INS variant (NM_000207.3:c.4G>A, p.Ala2Thr; rs535989053) did not co-segregate with diabetes: it was inherited from the euglycaemic maternal grandfather (fasting glucose 5.0 mmol/L, HbA1c 5.2%) and was absent in the proband
title: Case Report: A novel 1, 171 bp GCK promoter/exon 1 deletion in a Chinese pedigree: correcting a misdiagnosis of MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant.

text: . Under ACMG/AMP criteria, the INS variant meets criteria for a benign allele (BS1, BP2). The proband (isolated MODY2) exhibited a characteristic "plateau-like" stable mild hyperglycemia (coefficient of variation [CV] 14.35%). The elder brother, who carries both variants, showed a similar stable pattern (CV 13.41%)
title: Case Report: A novel 1, 171 bp GCK promoter/exon 1 deletion in a Chinese pedigree: correcting a misdiagnosis of MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant.

text: . The mother, who also carries both variants, had been treated with insulin for ten years under the erroneous MODY10 diagnosis; upon discontinuation of insulin, her glycemic control remained stable, with CGM metrics comparable to those of her children. This case underscores the critical importance of CNV analysis and segregation studies in monogenic diabetes diagnostics
title: Case Report: A novel 1, 171 bp GCK promoter/exon 1 deletion in a Chinese pedigree: correcting a misdiagnosis of MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant.

text: . The identification of a large GCK deletion corrected the initial misdiagnosis of MODY10-based on an incidental INS variant-and enabled appropriate genetic counseling and discontinuation of unnecessary insulin therapy. CGM emerges as a valuable ancillary tool for distinguishing MODY2 from MODY10 and for reassuring patients that pharmacological treatment is not required.
title: Case Report: A novel 1, 171 bp GCK promoter/exon 1 deletion in a Chinese pedigree: correcting a misdiagnosis of MODY10 based on an incidental INS variant.

text: Rapid Succession of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteremia and Candidemia in a Patient with Refractory Pemphigus Vulgaris: A Lethal Therapeutic Challenge.. Immunosuppressed patients with extensive skin barrier disruption face extraordinary risks for polymicrobial infections
title: Rapid Succession of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteremia and Candidemia in a Patient with Refractory Pemphigus Vulgaris: A Lethal Therapeutic Challenge.

text: . The rapid, sequential emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteremia and candidemia in such hosts constitutes a particularly lethal complication with limited therapeutic options. We report a 74-year-old woman with refractory pemphigus vulgaris (PV), type 2 diabetes mellitus, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease who developed a cascade of MDR infections over a 14-day hospitalization
title: Rapid Succession of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteremia and Candidemia in a Patient with Refractory Pemphigus Vulgaris: A Lethal Therapeutic Challenge.

text: . Following initial methicillin-resistant  This case starkly illustrates the catastrophic potential of rapid, sequential MDR infections in profoundly immunocompromised hosts with skin barrier defects
title: Rapid Succession of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteremia and Candidemia in a Patient with Refractory Pemphigus Vulgaris: A Lethal Therapeutic Challenge.

text: . It underscores the critical importance of early microbiological surveillance, the clinical urgency of dynamic antimicrobial stewardship, and the imperative for multidisciplinary management to navigate the irreconcilable conflict between necessary immunosuppression and life-threatening infection.
title: Rapid Succession of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteremia and Candidemia in a Patient with Refractory Pemphigus Vulgaris: A Lethal Therapeutic Challenge.

text: Describing pharmacists' perspectives on current practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use in people with diabetes.. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends prescribing glucagon for people with diabetes (PWD) using insulin or at high risk of hypoglycemia; however, prescribing rates remain low
title: Describing pharmacists' perspectives on current practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use in people with diabetes.
journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

text: . Few studies have examined practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use from pharmacists' perspectives. This study aimed to describe pharmacists' perspectives on current practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use in PWD
title: Describing pharmacists' perspectives on current practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use in people with diabetes.
journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

text: . A voluntary, electronic survey questionnaire was distributed to 1,624 members of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy Ambulatory Care and Endocrine and Metabolism Practice and Research Networks. Categorical, Likert, and open-ended questions were used to evaluate practice scope, patient population, and knowledge and perceptions related to glucagon use
title: Describing pharmacists' perspectives on current practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use in people with diabetes.
journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

text: . Statistical analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics and the Stats iQ function within the Qualtrics® platform. Of the 186 respondents included, most pharmacists practiced in urban areas (58.2%) and primary care (83.1%), with a mean of 10.6 years of experience managing PWD
title: Describing pharmacists' perspectives on current practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use in people with diabetes.
journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

text: . Respondents estimated that 23.5% of their patients with diabetes have an active glucagon prescription, and 42.1% fill their prescription
title: Describing pharmacists' perspectives on current practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use in people with diabetes.
journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

text: . In hypothetical patients, respondents were most likely to recommend or prescribe glucagon for PWD with a history of hypoglycemia requiring medical attention (95.7%), recurrent hypoglycemia (89.6%), or using intensive insulin regimens, including continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (82.3-93.9%)
title: Describing pharmacists' perspectives on current practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use in people with diabetes.
journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

text: . Respondents were less likely to do so for people with type 2 diabetes using basal insulin only (38.4%) or secretagogues (17.1%), or PWD with a history of an isolated hypoglycemic event (17.7%). The most frequently identified barriers to outpatient glucagon use were cost (75.5%), patient health literacy regarding when to use glucagon (71.7%), and insurance coverage (68.2%)
title: Describing pharmacists' perspectives on current practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use in people with diabetes.
journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

text: . Current practices among pharmacists engaged in outpatient diabetes management may not fully align with recommendations for glucagon use, highlighting opportunities for pharmacists to support strategies that optimize appropriate glucagon prescribing for high-risk patients.
title: Describing pharmacists' perspectives on current practices and barriers to outpatient glucagon use in people with diabetes.

text: Diabetes and the role of primary care: a global perspective.. The global prevalence of diabetes is rising rapidly, with the steepest increases and greatest unmet need occurring in low-income and middle-income countries
title: Diabetes and the role of primary care: a global perspective.

text: . Despite strong evidence that early detection and continuous management reduce morbidity and mortality, many health systems face persistent gaps in diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of people with diabetes. Primary care is the most accessible platform for screening and care coordination, and is central to addressing these challenges
title: Diabetes and the role of primary care: a global perspective.

text: . Primary care-led models, including nurse-led and pharmacist-led interventions, integrated multidisciplinary teams, and digitally enabled care pathways, have shown improvements in glycaemic control, cardiometabolic outcomes, and health-care use in people with type 2 diabetes across primary care and community settings
title: Diabetes and the role of primary care: a global perspective.

text: . Global initiatives, such as the WHO Global Diabetes Compact and UN non-communicable disease targets, emphasise strengthening primary care to deliver equitable, cost-effective diabetes care at scale
title: Diabetes and the role of primary care: a global perspective.

text: . Future priorities include workforce development, addressing health inequalities, scalable implementation strategies, and robust evaluation of long-term outcomes to enable person-centred type 2 diabetes care across diverse health-system contexts.
title: Diabetes and the role of primary care: a global perspective.

text: Efficacy of the digital therapeutic glucura combined with CGM in the treatment of type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled trial over 6 months.. title: Efficacy of the digital therapeutic glucura combined with CGM in the treatment of type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled trial over 6 months.

text: Survodutide Once Weekly in Adults with Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes.. For persons living with both type 2 diabetes and obesity, weight management may be the most effective therapy for type 2 diabetes. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have potent weight-reducing effects, and other mechanisms may confer additional benefits
title: Survodutide Once Weekly in Adults with Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

text: . Survodutide is an investigational glucagon receptor-GLP-1 receptor dual agonist with potential weight-reducing and metabolic benefits
title: Survodutide Once Weekly in Adults with Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

text: . In this multinational, double-blind, phase 3 trial involving adults with type 2 diabetes and a body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of 27 or more, we randomly assigned participants in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous survodutide (3.6 mg or 6.0 mg) or placebo
title: Survodutide Once Weekly in Adults with Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

text: . The two primary end points were the percent change in body weight and a reduction in body weight of at least 5% from baseline to week 76. Among 752 participants (250 in the 3.6-mg survodutide group, 251 in the 6.0-mg survodutide group, and 251 in the placebo group), the mean age at baseline was 55.7 years, and the mean BMI was 36.5; 49.3% were men
title: Survodutide Once Weekly in Adults with Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

text: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.
title: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.

text: . Lifestyle modification is increasingly recognized as a critical component in the management of chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly among elderly individuals with type 2 diabetes, a population at high risk of disease progression and comorbidities
title: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.

text: . While pharmacological treatment remains central, growing evidence highlights the role of dietary patterns and physical activity in potentially influencing renal and metabolic outcomes. However, the extent and consistency of these effects remain unclear, particularly in older diabetic populations
title: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.

text: . This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence from both intervention and observational studies examining dietary patterns, dietary interventions, physical activity, and related lifestyle exposures associated with renal and metabolic outcomes in older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease
title: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.

text: . A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. A total of 31 eligible studies were included in the final analysis
title: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.

text: . Healthier dietary patterns-particularly Mediterranean, plant-based, low-sodium, and moderated protein approaches-were generally associated with favorable renal and metabolic outcomes, although the certainty of evidence varied across themes
title: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.

text: . Sodium restriction reduced blood pressure and albuminuria, while moderated protein intake was associated with favorable renal outcomes when nutritional status was carefully monitored. Physical activity interventions improved glycemic control, blood pressure, and functional capacity, with possible indirect benefits for renal function
title: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.

text: . Evidence regarding antioxidant supplementation and very low-carbohydrate diets remains limited and inconclusive. Dietary patterns and physical activity are associated with renal and metabolic outcomes among elderly individuals with type 2 diabetes
title: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.

text: . These findings suggest that nutrition-focused lifestyle interventions may be considered supportive components of routine care, although stronger evidence is required. However, further large-scale, high-quality, and long-term studies are needed to establish definitive recommendations and develop tailored intervention strategies for this high-risk population
title: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.

text: . https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251087535, identifier PROSPERO (CRD420251087535).
title: Dietary patterns and physical activity in relation to renal and metabolic outcomes among older adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.

text: Streamlining intrapartum glycemic control: Subcutaneous insulin for intrapartum diabetes management.. Optimal strategies for intrapartum glycemic control among patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remain uncertain
title: Streamlining intrapartum glycemic control: Subcutaneous insulin for intrapartum diabetes management.

text: . In 2024, our labor and delivery unit implemented a subcutaneous (SC) insulin protocol to replace routine intravenous (IV) insulin initiation when glucose exceeded a treatment threshold. title: Streamlining intrapartum glycemic control: Subcutaneous insulin for intrapartum diabetes management.

text: . We conducted a retrospective cohort quality improvement study of patients with GDM or T2DM who delivered at ≥36 weeks between March 2021 and December 2025. July 2024, when the protocol was introduced, was excluded as a washout period. The intervention included both a shift to SC insulin-first management and standardization of intrapartum glycemic treatment to a target of ≤ 120 mg/dL
title: Streamlining intrapartum glycemic control: Subcutaneous insulin for intrapartum diabetes management.

text: . The primary outcome was a composite of neonatal hypoglycemia or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission for hypoglycemia within 24 h of life. Secondary outcomes included IV insulin duration and RN satisfaction. Outcomes were compared before and after implementation
title: Streamlining intrapartum glycemic control: Subcutaneous insulin for intrapartum diabetes management.

title: Streamlining intrapartum glycemic control: Subcutaneous insulin for intrapartum diabetes management.

title: Streamlining intrapartum glycemic control: Subcutaneous insulin for intrapartum diabetes management.

text: Pharmacological treatment strategies to prevent heart failure across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic spectrum: an EJHF Expert Consensus Statement.. Heart failure (HF) remains a major cause of morbidity, mortality, and increased healthcare costs worldwide, and is recognized as the result of progressive cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome
title: Pharmacological treatment strategies to prevent heart failure across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic spectrum: an EJHF Expert Consensus Statement.

text: . Obesity, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease frequently coexist and interact through shared pathophysiological mechanisms that promote HF onset, especially with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
title: Pharmacological treatment strategies to prevent heart failure across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic spectrum: an EJHF Expert Consensus Statement.

text: . This European Journal of Heart Failure (EJHF) Expert Consensus Statement synthesizes contemporary evidence supporting pharmacological strategies to prevent HF across the CKM spectrum
title: Pharmacological treatment strategies to prevent heart failure across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic spectrum: an EJHF Expert Consensus Statement.

text: . Foundational therapies, including renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and incretin-based agents, demonstrate complementary benefits in reducing HF events, cardiovascular death, and chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression in high-risk populations
title: Pharmacological treatment strategies to prevent heart failure across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic spectrum: an EJHF Expert Consensus Statement.

text: . Early, parallel initiation of these therapies may modify disease trajectory and attenuate progression from at-risk and pre-HF stages to overt clinical HF. This document further emphasizes the need for an up-front, accelerated implementation strategy supported by structured monitoring, multidisciplinary CKM care pathways, and proactive management of laboratory abnormalities
title: Pharmacological treatment strategies to prevent heart failure across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic spectrum: an EJHF Expert Consensus Statement.

text: . Overcoming barriers such as clinical inertia, safety misperceptions, polypharmacy, cost constraints, and inequities in access is essential to translate evidence into population-level impact. Harmonization of prevention frameworks across cardiology, nephrology, endocrinology, and primary care societies is urgently required
title: Pharmacological treatment strategies to prevent heart failure across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic spectrum: an EJHF Expert Consensus Statement.

text: . Integrated, cross-disciplinary implementation of evidence-based CKM management offers a realistic opportunity to reduce incident HF and mitigate its growing global burden.
title: Pharmacological treatment strategies to prevent heart failure across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic spectrum: an EJHF Expert Consensus Statement.

text: Evaluation of cancer frequency and characteristics in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in primary health care: a descriptive cross-sectional study.
title: Evaluation of cancer frequency and characteristics in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in primary health care: a descriptive cross-sectional study.

text: . This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, types, and duration of diagnosed cancers among adult type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients in a primary care setting in Türkiye and to examine associated clinical and demographic factors according to T2DM duration. T2DM is a growing global health concern linked to increased risks of various cancers
title: Evaluation of cancer frequency and characteristics in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in primary health care: a descriptive cross-sectional study.

text: . Epidemiological data suggest a complex relationship involving shared risk factors and pathophysiological mechanisms such as hyperinsulinemia, inflammation, and obesity. This descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted at an education-family health centre (EFHC), analysing medical records and patient interviews
title: Evaluation of cancer frequency and characteristics in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in primary health care: a descriptive cross-sectional study.

text: . The sample included 442 patients with T2DM registered at Marmara University Tuzla EFHC, of whom 152 had a diagnosed cancer. Data collected encompassed cancer prevalence, types, sociodemographic characteristics, clinical features (including body mass index, T2DM duration, comorbidities), and cancer duration. The prevalence of cancer among T2DM patients was 34.4%
title: Evaluation of cancer frequency and characteristics in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in primary health care: a descriptive cross-sectional study.

text: . The most common cancers were prostate in men and breast in women. No significant correlation was observed between T2DM duration and cancer duration; however, breast cancer was less frequent among women with longer T2DM duration compared to their cancer duration. A high rate of obesity and comorbidities was noted in the cohort
title: Evaluation of cancer frequency and characteristics in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in primary health care: a descriptive cross-sectional study.

text: . Cancer prevalence among Turkish T2DM patients in primary care is notably high, highlighting the importance of integrated screening and risk factor management. These findings underscore the need for targeted preventive strategies and personalized patient care to reduce cancer-related morbidity and mortality in diabetic populations.
title: Evaluation of cancer frequency and characteristics in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in primary health care: a descriptive cross-sectional study.

text: Global Landscape and Thematic Evolution of Selective GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and GLP-1-Based Multi-Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Bibliometric Analysis.. To characterize the global development, collaboration structure, publication landscape, citation influence and thematic evolution of research on selective GLP-1 receptor agonists and GLP-1-based multi-receptor agonists in T2DM
title: Global Landscape and Thematic Evolution of Selective GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and GLP-1-Based Multi-Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Bibliometric Analysis.

text: . A bibliometric analysis was conducted on 3736 original articles published between 2004 and 2025 and retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Publication trends, research contributions, collaboration networks, citation impact and thematic evolution were evaluated using complementary bibliometric indicators and network analysis. Annual publication output increased substantially
title: Global Landscape and Thematic Evolution of Selective GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and GLP-1-Based Multi-Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Bibliometric Analysis.

text: . Selective-only studies remained the cumulative core of the evidence base, while mixed/comparative and multi-receptor-only studies expanded rapidly in recent years. The United States led in research output and international connectivity, and Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly were the most prominent institutional contributors based on author affiliation analysis
title: Global Landscape and Thematic Evolution of Selective GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and GLP-1-Based Multi-Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Bibliometric Analysis.

text: . Diabetes, Obesity and Metabolism was the leading source journal. Research output was highly concentrated across countries but more widely distributed across institutions and authors. Thematic emphasis shifted from incretin biology and glycemic efficacy toward cardiovascular and kidney outcomes, obesity, integrated treatment strategies and real-world evidence
title: Global Landscape and Thematic Evolution of Selective GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and GLP-1-Based Multi-Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Bibliometric Analysis.

text: . Major trials, particularly LEADER and REWIND, and ADA/EASD consensus statements exerted strong citation influence. Sensitivity analysis supported the overall robustness of the principal findings. Research on GLP-1-based agonists in T2DM has expanded rapidly and shifted toward an integrated cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework
title: Global Landscape and Thematic Evolution of Selective GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and GLP-1-Based Multi-Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Bibliometric Analysis.

text: . Studies of selective GLP-1RAs remain central to the literature, while studies of newer GLP-1-based multi-receptor agonists are contributing to its diversification. Evidence remains comparatively less developed for longer-term outcomes of emerging agents, treatment sustainability in routine care, patient experience and diverse populations and settings.
title: Global Landscape and Thematic Evolution of Selective GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and GLP-1-Based Multi-Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Bibliometric Analysis.

text: Effects of a Low-Carbohydrate Diet Combined With Exercise on HbA1c in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Bayesian Multilevel Network and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.. The relative benefits of carbohydrate-restricted diets (CRDs) combined with exercise in adults with type 2 diabetes remain uncertain
title: Effects of a Low-Carbohydrate Diet Combined With Exercise on HbA1c in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Bayesian Multilevel Network and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.

text: . We compared regimens and explored incremental benefits, dose-response associations and potential effect modifiers. Four databases were searched from inception to 31 August 2026 for English-language randomized controlled trials (RCTs). A Bayesian multilevel model synthesized arm-level changes in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) across eligible post-baseline assessments
title: Effects of a Low-Carbohydrate Diet Combined With Exercise on HbA1c in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Bayesian Multilevel Network and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.

text: . An auxiliary frequentist network meta-analysis evaluated network structure and inconsistency; Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) assessed 20 prespecified comparisons. Dose-response and moderator analyses were exploratory. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane tool for randomized trials. Twenty-four RCTs involving 2038 participants were included
title: Effects of a Low-Carbohydrate Diet Combined With Exercise on HbA1c in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Bayesian Multilevel Network and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.

text: . Compared with pooled active/passive controls, aerobic training plus a moderately low-carbohydrate diet was associated with lower HbA1c (posterior median mean difference, -0.53 percentage points; 95% credible interval, -0.76 to -0.28). Estimates for other combined regimens were less precise
title: Effects of a Low-Carbohydrate Diet Combined With Exercise on HbA1c in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Bayesian Multilevel Network and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.

text: . The auxiliary network had two disconnected components, and confidence was very low for all 20 assessed comparisons. Under the specified priors, the Bayes factor favoured the model without treatment-specific effects (BF10 = 0.034)
title: Effects of a Low-Carbohydrate Diet Combined With Exercise on HbA1c in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Bayesian Multilevel Network and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.

text: . Higher prescribed exercise doses were associated with larger reductions versus pooled controls, but an incremental benefit over exercise or CRD alone was not established. Matched carbohydrate-dose contrasts were imprecise. Limitations of the arm-level model, sparse evidence and very low confidence in the assessed auxiliary-network comparisons leave comparative benefits uncertain
title: Effects of a Low-Carbohydrate Diet Combined With Exercise on HbA1c in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Bayesian Multilevel Network and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.

text: . The findings do not establish a preferred regimen, an incremental benefit over either component alone, or a specific dietary or exercise prescription.
title: Effects of a Low-Carbohydrate Diet Combined With Exercise on HbA1c in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Bayesian Multilevel Network and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.

text: Cost-Effectiveness of Sotagliflozin in Heart Failure Patients with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fractions - Results from SOLOIST-WHF.
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Sotagliflozin in Heart Failure Patients with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fractions - Results from SOLOIST-WHF.

text: . In the SOLOIST-WHF trial (Effect of Sotagliflozin on Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Post Worsening Heart Failure) evaluating patients with type 2 diabetes and recent worsening heart failure, initiation of sotagliflozin before or soon after hospital discharge reduced cardiovascular and heart failure-related clinical events, including hospitalizations and urgent visits
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Sotagliflozin in Heart Failure Patients with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fractions - Results from SOLOIST-WHF.

text: . We assessed the long-term cost-effectiveness of sotagliflozin in the overall trial population and according to ejection fraction subtype, including heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF ≥50%) and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF <50%)
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Sotagliflozin in Heart Failure Patients with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fractions - Results from SOLOIST-WHF.

text: . A patient-level Markov microsimulation model incorporating treatment effects observed in SOLOIST-WHF, national cost estimates, and externally derived health-state utility values was used to project lifetime clinical and economic outcomes from a healthcare payer perspective. Net monthly treatment costs for sotagliflozin were estimated at $434
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Sotagliflozin in Heart Failure Patients with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fractions - Results from SOLOIST-WHF.

text: . Lifetime projections included healthcare expenditures, cardiovascular and heart failure events, survival, and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) comparing sotagliflozin with placebo among patients eligible for SOLOIST-WHF. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were expressed as cost per QALY gained, and uncertainty was evaluated through sensitivity analyses
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Sotagliflozin in Heart Failure Patients with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fractions - Results from SOLOIST-WHF.

text: . Across the lifetime horizon, sotagliflozin increased quality-adjusted survival by 0.39 QALYs (4.43 vs. 4.04) and life expectancy by 0.64 life-years (7.12 vs. 6.48) compared with placebo, with an incremental cost of $29,449 (95% uncertainty interval [UI]: $26,610-$32,528), corresponding to an ICER of $75,510 per QALY gained (UI: $55,640-$98,300)
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Sotagliflozin in Heart Failure Patients with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fractions - Results from SOLOIST-WHF.

text: . Among patients with HFpEF, treatment produced gains of 0.43 QALYs (4.53 vs. 4.10) and 0.68 life-years (7.14 vs. 6.46) at an incremental cost of $30,587 (UI: $28,459-$35,826), yielding an ICER of $71,135 per QALY (UI: $61,482-$87,652). In patients with HFrEF, sotagliflozin increased outcomes by 0.37 QALYs (4.33 vs. 3.96) and 0.63 life-years (7.09 vs
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Sotagliflozin in Heart Failure Patients with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fractions - Results from SOLOIST-WHF.

text: . 3.96) and 0.63 life-years (7.09 vs. 6.46) with incremental costs of $32,425 (UI: $31,011-$38,127), resulting in an ICER of $87,635 per QALY (UI: $74,751-$112,287). Improvements in QALYs were primarily driven by reductions in cardiovascular events, and results were most sensitive to medication cost and readmission rates
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Sotagliflozin in Heart Failure Patients with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fractions - Results from SOLOIST-WHF.

text: . At an estimated monthly price of $434, sotagliflozin represents a clinically beneficial and economically favorable treatment for patients with diabetes and recent worsening heart failure across ejection fraction groups, with slightly greater cost-effectiveness observed among patients with HFpEF than HFrEF (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03521934).
title: Cost-Effectiveness of Sotagliflozin in Heart Failure Patients with Preserved and Reduced Ejection Fractions - Results from SOLOIST-WHF.

text: Bridging the gap in early cardio-renal risk prevention in type 2 diabetes: evidence, guidelines, and real-world insights from the PRECARE NO LiMITS initiative.. Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is associated with a substantial burden of cardiovascular and renal complications
title: Bridging the gap in early cardio-renal risk prevention in type 2 diabetes: evidence, guidelines, and real-world insights from the PRECARE NO LiMITS initiative.

text: . Although current evidence supports early implementation of organ-protective strategies, therapeutic inertia and uncertainty regarding guideline implementation may delay treatment intensification
title: Bridging the gap in early cardio-renal risk prevention in type 2 diabetes: evidence, guidelines, and real-world insights from the PRECARE NO LiMITS initiative.

text: . The goal of this review is to discuss the rationale for early cardiorenal protection in T2D and to explore real-world perspectives on the use of SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists through insights from the PRECARE NO LiMITS initiative
title: Bridging the gap in early cardio-renal risk prevention in type 2 diabetes: evidence, guidelines, and real-world insights from the PRECARE NO LiMITS initiative.

text: . This narrative review integrates current evidence with exploratory findings from the PRECARE NO LiMITS project, a multicentre educational initiative involving diabetologists from ten diabetes centres in Lombardy, Italy. The initiative included two descriptive clinician survey rounds, conducted at baseline (T0) and after six months (T1), together with moderated expert discussions
title: Bridging the gap in early cardio-renal risk prevention in type 2 diabetes: evidence, guidelines, and real-world insights from the PRECARE NO LiMITS initiative.

text: . At T1, a higher proportion of respondents reported considering SGLT2 inhibitor initiation in a greater proportion of patients with early cardiorenal risk markers, including albuminuria and mildly reduced eGFR, even in the absence of established cardiovascular or renal disease
title: Bridging the gap in early cardio-renal risk prevention in type 2 diabetes: evidence, guidelines, and real-world insights from the PRECARE NO LiMITS initiative.

text: . Survey responses also suggested greater consideration of risk-based treatment strategies extending beyond glycaemic control alone. Persistent perceived barriers included reliance on HbA1c as a primary driver of treatment intensification, uncertainty regarding the timing and implementation of organ-protective therapies, and concerns related to treatment complexity and access
title: Bridging the gap in early cardio-renal risk prevention in type 2 diabetes: evidence, guidelines, and real-world insights from the PRECARE NO LiMITS initiative.

text: . Given the descriptive nature of the survey, differences between T0 and T1 should be interpreted as exploratory
title: Bridging the gap in early cardio-renal risk prevention in type 2 diabetes: evidence, guidelines, and real-world insights from the PRECARE NO LiMITS initiative.

text: . Overall, these exploratory observations, considered alongside current evidence and guideline recommendations, highlight the potential value of a proactive approach to T2D management focused on early identification of cardiorenal risk and appropriate consideration of organ-protective therapies
title: Bridging the gap in early cardio-renal risk prevention in type 2 diabetes: evidence, guidelines, and real-world insights from the PRECARE NO LiMITS initiative.

title: Determinants of quality of life among older adults with recurrent diabetic foot ulcers.

text: . Older adults (≥60 years) had significantly lower physical functioning and general health scores (p < 0.05). title: Determinants of quality of life among older adults with recurrent diabetic foot ulcers.

text: . Physical HRQoL is poorer among older adults with recurrent DFUs, primarily mediated by psychosocial distress. There is a relationship between depression, distress, and poor quality of life
title: Determinants of quality of life among older adults with recurrent diabetic foot ulcers.

text: . Moreover, depression and distress independently predicted lower physical QoL, and better self-care is a predictor of QoL. Integrated management addressing psychological well-being and self-care behaviours may enhance the overall patient outcomes.

title: Bridging the evidence-to-practice gap in cardiometabolic prevention: from episodic care to lifelong, system-wide responsibility.

title: Bridging the evidence-to-practice gap in cardiometabolic prevention: from episodic care to lifelong, system-wide responsibility.

text: Penile Prosthesis Implantation in a Patient With Post-polio Residual Paralysis and Pelvic Deformity: A Case Report.. Penile prosthesis implantation is the gold-standard treatment for men with erectile dysfunction refractory to conservative therapies
title: Penile Prosthesis Implantation in a Patient With Post-polio Residual Paralysis and Pelvic Deformity: A Case Report.

text: . Surgical implantation may become technically challenging in patients with significant musculoskeletal deformities because altered pelvic anatomy can affect patient positioning and corporal access
title: Penile Prosthesis Implantation in a Patient With Post-polio Residual Paralysis and Pelvic Deformity: A Case Report.

text: . We report the case of a 50-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus and post-polio residual paralysis associated with fixed pelvic deformity who presented with severe erectile dysfunction refractory to phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors, low-intensity extracorporeal shockwave therapy, and intracavernosal injections
title: Penile Prosthesis Implantation in a Patient With Post-polio Residual Paralysis and Pelvic Deformity: A Case Report.

text: . A Shah malleable penile prosthesis was successfully implanted through a penoscrotal approach despite difficulties related to pelvic tilt and altered corporal orientation. title: Penile Prosthesis Implantation in a Patient With Post-polio Residual Paralysis and Pelvic Deformity: A Case Report.

text: Etiologies, Clinical Profiles, and Treatment Outcomes in Thai Children and Adolescents With Youth-Onset Diabetes.. Youth-onset diabetes is a chronic condition requiring lifelong management, and achieving optimal glycemic control remains challenging. title: Etiologies, Clinical Profiles, and Treatment Outcomes in Thai Children and Adolescents With Youth-Onset Diabetes.
journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society

text: . We further examined clinical characteristics, therapeutic outcomes, and factors associated with glycemic control in type 1 diabetes (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). We conducted a prospective cross-sectional Pediatric Diabetes Registry Project in 2 phases: initial (March 2016-August 2018) and follow-up (March 2019-March 2020). Individuals diagnosed before age 18 years were recruited
title: Etiologies, Clinical Profiles, and Treatment Outcomes in Thai Children and Adolescents With Youth-Onset Diabetes.
journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society

text: . Data on clinical profile, glycemic control, treatment, and complications were collected. Three hundred participants were recruited at baseline. The majority (77%, n = 231) had T1D, and 15.3% (n = 46) had T2D. The mean HbA1c in T1D was 8.96% ± 1.98%, with 22.5% achieving good glycemic control
title: Etiologies, Clinical Profiles, and Treatment Outcomes in Thai Children and Adolescents With Youth-Onset Diabetes.

text: . Multivariate analysis revealed that older age (OR 1.16, 95% CI 1.01-1.32, p = 0.031) and self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) ≥ 4 times/day (OR 4.85, 95% CI 1.85-12.71, p = 0.001) were positively associated with good control.
