text: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.. Dietary guidelines shape food policy, education, and food systems worldwide
title: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.

text: . Recent controversies in dietary guideline development, together with rising burdens of diet-related chronic disease and increasing environmental pressures, highlight the need for globally relevant dietary guidance aligned with both human and planetary health. We developed an evidence-informed International Food Guide Pyramid emphasizing optimal carbohydrate-containing staple foods
title: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.

text: . The International Carbohydrate Quality Consortium (ICQC) developed the proposed framework using a four-step evidence-review process involving comparison of major national and regional dietary guideline systems, integration of evidence syntheses and selected primary studies, and expert consensus
title: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.

text: . Quantitative intake ranges from the EAT-Lancet Commission reference diet informed the relative visual proportions of food groups, while the guiding principles were derived from convergence across dietary guideline systems and complementary evidence syntheses
title: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.

text: . The resulting pyramid depicts a plant-forward omnivorous dietary pattern supported by epidemiological and clinical evidence indicating benefits for cardiometabolic health and chronic disease prevention. Vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and legumes constitute foundational components of the pyramid
title: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.

text: . Nuts, seeds, and unsaturated plant oils are emphasized as primary fat sources, while foods high in saturated fat are generally limited. Animal-source foods are included in modest amounts, with plant protein sources emphasized, poultry and fish preferred over red meat, and dairy incorporated in modest amounts, consistent with dietary patterns associated with lower environmental impacts
title: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.

text: . Carbohydrate quality is emphasized through prioritization of whole-grain foods alongside traditional low-glycemic index grain staples, favoring carbohydrate sources rich in dietary fiber, intact plant cells, and micronutrients while limiting sugars consumed in low-nutrient forms, particularly sugar-sweetened beverages
title: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.

text: . The framework also accommodates vegan and other primarily plant-based dietary patterns. This evidence-informed International Food Guide Pyramid integrates quantitative modeling and qualitative evidence synthesis to provide a coherent, flexible, and globally adaptable dietary framework aligned with both human and planetary health
title: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.

text: . STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: This work presents an evidence-informed International Food Guide Pyramid developed through a structured synthesis of major national and regional dietary guideline systems, quantitative modeling from the EAT-Lancet Commission, and complementary evidence syntheses
title: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.

text: . By translating areas of convergence across these independent evidence-based sources into a practical visual framework, it provides a globally adaptable approach to dietary guidance that explicitly incorporates carbohydrate quality and both human and planetary health.
title: Toward International Dietary Guidance: A Food Guide Pyramid for Human and Planetary Health.

text: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery as a Therapeutic Option for MASLD: Outcome, Mechanism, and Long-Term Implications.. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease and a major hepatic manifestation of metabolic syndrome. It is closely linked to obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus
title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery as a Therapeutic Option for MASLD: Outcome, Mechanism, and Long-Term Implications.

text: . While many patients display a steatotic liver, some progress to steatohepatitis, fibrosis, and cirrhosis, increasing the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Current management targets metabolic risk factors. Metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) has therefore emerged as both an obesity treatment and a therapeutic option for MASLD
title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery as a Therapeutic Option for MASLD: Outcome, Mechanism, and Long-Term Implications.

text: . This narrative review summarizes evidence on clinical outcomes, efficacy, and mechanisms. Histology-based studies show MASLD resolution and relevant fibrosis regression after MBS, with durable benefits. Comparative studies indicate superiority over lifestyle intervention and conservative treatment, while direct comparisons with modern drugs (e.g. GLP-1 agonists) remain limited
title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery as a Therapeutic Option for MASLD: Outcome, Mechanism, and Long-Term Implications.

text: . GLP-1 agonists) remain limited. Mechanistic studies suggest that MASLD remission by MBS is driven through a combination of sustained weight loss and surgery-specific effects on hepatic lipid metabolism, mitochondrial function, glucose metabolism, incretin and bile acid signalling, adipose tissue biology, and the gut-liver axis
title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery as a Therapeutic Option for MASLD: Outcome, Mechanism, and Long-Term Implications.

text: . Emerging evidence suggests fewer liver-related events and lower HCC incidence, with potential benefits in selected high-risk patients. In conclusion, MBS is not merely a weight loss intervention, but a disease-modifying, multi-system metabolic therapy with direct hepatic effects
title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery as a Therapeutic Option for MASLD: Outcome, Mechanism, and Long-Term Implications.

text: . Die metabolische Dysfunktion-assoziierte steatotische Lebererkrankung (MASLD) ist die häufigste chronische Lebererkrankung und eine hepatische Manifestation des metabolischen Syndroms
title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery as a Therapeutic Option for MASLD: Outcome, Mechanism, and Long-Term Implications.

text: . Sie ist eng mit der Adipositas und dem Typ-2-Diabetes mellitus verknüpft.Während viele Betroffene im Stadium der Steatose verbleiben, kann die Erkrankung zur Steatohepatitis, Fibrose und Zirrhose voranschreiten und das Risiko für ein hepatozelluläres Karzinom erhöhen. Aktuelle Therapiekonzepte zielen vor allem auf die Behandlung metabolischer Risikofaktoren ab
title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery as a Therapeutic Option for MASLD: Outcome, Mechanism, and Long-Term Implications.

text: . Die metabolische und bariatrische Chirurgie (MBS) hat sich daher als effektive Therapie der Adipositas und relevante Behandlungsoption bei MASLD etabliert. Diese narrative Übersichtsarbeit fasst die Evidenz zur klinischen Wirksamkeit und biologischen Grundlage der MBS bei MASLD zusammen. Histologie-basierte Studien zeigen eine MASLD-Remission und relevante Fibroseregression nach MBS
title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery as a Therapeutic Option for MASLD: Outcome, Mechanism, and Long-Term Implications.

text: . Vergleichende Studien belegen eine Überlegenheit gegenüber Lebensstilinterventionen und konservativer Therapie, während direkte Vergleiche mit modernen Medikamenten (z.B. GLP-1-Agonisten) begrenzt sind. Mechanistisch beruht die Remission auf Gewichtsverlust sowie vielfältigen metabolischen Effekten nach MBS
title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery as a Therapeutic Option for MASLD: Outcome, Mechanism, and Long-Term Implications.

text: . Neue Erkenntnisse deuten zudem auf weniger Leberkomplikationen und eine geringere HCC-Inzidenz nach MBS hin. Zusammenfassend ist die MBS eine effektive, krankheitsmodifizierende, multisystemische Therapie der MASLD.

text: MASLD: Established Knowledge and Emerging Directions - Guideline Updates.. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has become a major global health challenge, largely driven by the increasing prevalence of obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus
title: MASLD: Established Knowledge and Emerging Directions - Guideline Updates.

text: . The disease spectrum ranges from isolated steatosis to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with progressive fibrosis
title: MASLD: Established Knowledge and Emerging Directions - Guideline Updates.

text: . Advanced fibrosis substantially increases the risk of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and cardiovascular complications, thereby contributing significantly to morbidity and mortality.Although lifestyle modification remains the cornerstone of therapy, pharmacological treatment is gaining importance in patients with progressive disease or high-risk profiles
title: MASLD: Established Knowledge and Emerging Directions - Guideline Updates.

text: . Advances in the understanding of MASLD pathophysiology have enabled the development of targeted therapies addressing hepatic lipid accumulation, insulin resistance, inflammation, and fibrogenesis
title: MASLD: Established Knowledge and Emerging Directions - Guideline Updates.

text: . Promising clinical data have been reported for resmetirom, semaglutide, tirzepatide, survodutide, lanifibranor, and fibroblast growth factor-21 analogues including efruxifermin, pegozafermin, and efimosfermin.This review summarises current and emerging diagnostic and therapeutic strategies and provides practical guidance for clinical management
title: MASLD: Established Knowledge and Emerging Directions - Guideline Updates.

text: Beyond insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) normalization: portal insulin and hepatic growth hormone (GH) sensitivity across metabolic disease.. Clinical management of growth hormone (GH) deficiency, acromegaly, and diabetes mellitus is dominated by single-analyte targets: serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) in the GH disorders and glycated hemoglobin in diabetes
title: Beyond insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) normalization: portal insulin and hepatic growth hormone (GH) sensitivity across metabolic disease.

text: . This reductive framework obscures a central regulatory fact: GH does not autonomously dictate hepatic IGF-1 output. Whether GH is translated into IGF-1 by the hepatocyte is gated by the concentration of insulin reaching the liver through the portal vein
title: Beyond insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) normalization: portal insulin and hepatic growth hormone (GH) sensitivity across metabolic disease.

text: . We propose liver sensitivity to GH (LSG), operationally defined as portal-insulin-determined hepatic GH receptor (GHR) availability, as a unifying variable that places type 1 and type 2 diabetes, obesity, liver failure, and acromegaly on a single continuum rather than treating them as separate phenomena
title: Beyond insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) normalization: portal insulin and hepatic growth hormone (GH) sensitivity across metabolic disease.

text: . We develop the molecular basis of insulin-dependent GHR regulation, distinguish the divergent roles of portal versus systemic insulin, and argue that this distinction explains why subcutaneous insulin therapy in type 1 diabetes corrects glycemia while leaving the hepatic GH-resistant state intact
title: Beyond insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) normalization: portal insulin and hepatic growth hormone (GH) sensitivity across metabolic disease.

text: . We then re-examine the weight-gain liability of insulinotropic antidiabetic agents, the discordant GH/IGF-1 signatures produced by GLP-1 receptor agonists, the prognostic and potentially therapeutic role of IGF-1 in cirrhosis, and the metabolic limitations of current acromegaly treatment targets when viewed through the LSG framework
title: Beyond insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) normalization: portal insulin and hepatic growth hormone (GH) sensitivity across metabolic disease.

text: . The aim is to give the treating physician a mechanistic, rather than purely biochemical, account of how metabolism behaves in these states.
title: Beyond insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) normalization: portal insulin and hepatic growth hormone (GH) sensitivity across metabolic disease.

text: Exploring the impact of adult obesity in Spain: Insights from a systematic literature review.. Spain ranks among the European countries with the highest obesity prevalence, yet the evidence on the full spectrum of its impact has not been systematically consolidated

text: . This was a systematic literature review (SLR) conducted to evaluate the epidemiological, clinical, humanistic, and economic impact of obesity in Spain. title: Exploring the impact of adult obesity in Spain: Insights from a systematic literature review.

title: Exploring the impact of adult obesity in Spain: Insights from a systematic literature review.

title: Exploring the impact of adult obesity in Spain: Insights from a systematic literature review.

text: Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Blood Pressure Management: A Systematic Review of Clinical Effects, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Barriers.. Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) have been proposed as mediators of the relationship between the intestinal microbiome and blood pressure (BP), but their therapeutic relevance in humans remains uncertain
title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Blood Pressure Management: A Systematic Review of Clinical Effects, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Barriers.

text: . This systematic review evaluated the effects of direct SCFA administration and interventions modifying endogenous fecal or circulating SCFAs on BP in adults. MEDLINE via PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 1, 2022, through May 31, 2026
title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Blood Pressure Management: A Systematic Review of Clinical Effects, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Barriers.

text: . The review was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement, with study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment performed independently by two reviewers. Six randomized controlled trials were included and synthesized narratively because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity
title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Blood Pressure Management: A Systematic Review of Clinical Effects, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Barriers.

text: . Three trials evaluated direct butyrate administration, while three assessed exercise, plant-derived, dietary, prebiotic, or physical therapy interventions that modified endogenous SCFAs. Direct administration produced inconsistent effects
title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Blood Pressure Management: A Systematic Review of Clinical Effects, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Barriers.

text: . Conventional oral butyrate increased daytime systolic and diastolic BP relative to placebo in adults with hypertension, whereas acute colon-targeted delivery reduced daytime systolic BP relative to a lower concentration in a small crossover trial. A further oral trial in type 2 diabetes mellitus reported within-group BP reductions without a demonstrated between-group effect
title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Blood Pressure Management: A Systematic Review of Clinical Effects, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Barriers.

text: . Indirect interventions generally increased plasma or fecal SCFAs alongside improvements in selected BP outcomes, but their multicomponent effects and the absence of formal mediation analyses precluded attributing these responses specifically to SCFAs
title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Blood Pressure Management: A Systematic Review of Clinical Effects, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Barriers.

text: . Fecal and circulating measurements also showed different relationships with BP, indicating that these compartments are not biologically interchangeable. One study was judged at low risk of bias, two had some concerns, and three were at high risk. Current evidence does not demonstrate a uniform antihypertensive effect of increasing SCFA availability or a reproducible dose-response relationship
title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Blood Pressure Management: A Systematic Review of Clinical Effects, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Barriers.

text: . Future trials should compare oral and colon-targeted formulations, measure fecal and circulating SCFAs concurrently, use 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring as the primary outcome, and evaluate whether treatment responses vary by exposure and cardiometabolic phenotype.
title: Short-Chain Fatty Acids in Blood Pressure Management: A Systematic Review of Clinical Effects, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Barriers.

text: Distinct metabolomic signatures of SGLT2 inhibitor vs. sulfonylurea in a paired human liver biopsy study.. This study aimed to elucidate how sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and sulfonylureas differentially modulate hepatic metabolism in persons with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D)
title: Distinct metabolomic signatures of SGLT2 inhibitor vs. sulfonylurea in a paired human liver biopsy study.

text: . In this 48-week randomized, open-label, parallel-group trial, Japanese participants with type 2 diabetes and biopsy-confirmed MASLD received either tofogliflozin or glimepiride. Paired liver biopsy samples and serum were collected at baseline and after 48 weeks
title: Distinct metabolomic signatures of SGLT2 inhibitor vs. sulfonylurea in a paired human liver biopsy study.

text: . We performed a post hoc metabolomic analysis to assess hepatic and systemic metabolic shifts and their correlations with histological and clinical parameters. Tofogliflozin treatment significantly increased hepatic glucose 1-phosphate and acetyl-CoA levels, reflecting a metabolic shift toward ketogenesis and gluconeogenesis

title: Risk of diabetic ketoacidosis with sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors in type 2 diabetes: A nationwide cohort study.

title: Risk of diabetic ketoacidosis with sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors in type 2 diabetes: A nationwide cohort study.

text: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.. To assess differential changes in prescribing uptake of dapagliflozin and empagliflozin relative to canagliflozin in England following the July 2023 expansion of heart failure guideline recommendations
title: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.

text: . Controlled interrupted time series (ITS) analysis using segmented regression with Newey-West SEs and month fixed effects to account for seasonality. National monthly primary care prescribing data in England (January 2019-December 2025). Aggregate prescribing data were analysed at the drug level. Primary outcome: monthly utilisation measured in defined daily doses (DDDs)
title: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.

text: . monthly prescription items, market share of total SGLT2 inhibitor DDDs and net ingredient cost (NIC). Overall utilisation increased for all three monotherapy SGLT2 inhibitors, but prescribing trajectories diverged markedly following the intervention. Dapagliflozin's market share rose from 33.2% to 55.9%, while empagliflozin declined to 41.0% and canagliflozin to 3.1%
title: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.

text: . The controlled ITS model showed no immediate step change at July 2023. However, dapagliflozin demonstrated a significant differential postintervention slope increase relative to canagliflozin (β=0.042, 95% CI 0.035 to 0.049; p<0.001), corresponding to an additional 4.3% monthly growth. Empagliflozin showed a smaller but significant relative increase (β=0.015, 95% CI 0.008 to 0.022; p<0.001)
title: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.

text: . Counterfactual analysis estimated 68.4 million excess dapagliflozin DDDs and 21.2 million excess empagliflozin DDDs over the postintervention period. Results were consistent across prespecified breakpoint and formulation sensitivity analyses; however, an exploratory NIC-adjusted analysis attenuated the dapagliflozin differential slope by 33%, indicating sensitivity to concurrent price changes
title: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.

text: . SGLT2 inhibitor uptake in English primary care has been highly heterogeneous. The marked acceleration in dapagliflozin prescribing from July 2023, against stable background trends for canagliflozin, is temporally consistent with expanded heart failure guideline recommendations. However, several important limitations preclude definitive causal attribution
title: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.

text: . First, because this study analysed aggregate prescribing data without patient-level indications, we cannot directly attribute observed changes to heart failure rather than to diabetes, chronic kidney disease or other factors
title: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.

text: . Second, the substantial concurrent reduction in dapagliflozin's NIC (from £1.38 to £0.35 per DDD) represents a competing explanation; exploratory adjustment for NIC attenuated the dapagliflozin estimate by approximately one-third, though this magnitude cannot be interpreted as a causal attribution because NIC may be endogenous
title: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.

text: . The observation that empagliflozin, which experienced a more modest price change, showed a smaller differential effect is hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation with methods that can separate guideline from price effects. Third, the ecological design inherently limits causal inference
title: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.

text: . These findings highlight that class-wide guideline updates do not translate into uniform prescribing and underscore the importance of monitoring drug-specific adoption patterns while considering the complex interplay of clinical, economic and policy factors.
title: Differential uptake of SGLT2 inhibitors in England following heart failure guideline expansion: a controlled interrupted time series analysis.

text: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.. title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: . China has the world's largest population with these conditions, but has scarce prospective, community-based data to estimate the true burden of chronic liver disease. title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: . The CHESS-LiverHealth project was an investigator-initiated, prospective, community-based cohort study conducted at 18 sites corresponding to county-level units in 13 provincial-level administrative regions in China. Community-dwelling adults aged 18 years or older were enrolled and underwent vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE)
title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: . We report cross-sectional baseline data from this study. The primary outcome was the prevalence of liver fibrosis, as estimated by a liver stiffness measurement (LSM) of 8 kPa or more
title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: . Secondary outcomes included the prevalence of liver fibrosis at higher LSM thresholds (≥10 kPa and ≥12 kPa), steatotic liver disease (controlled attenuation parameter ≥248 dB/m) and its severity categories, and steatotic liver disease subtypes-metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD), and alcohol-associated liver
title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: disease (MetALD), and alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD)-together with factors associated with these outcomes
title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: . Between Sept 23, 2024, and Jan 23, 2026, 38 859 individuals entered the recruitment pathways, of whom 29 023 were enrolled. title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: . These individuals had a median age of 51·0 years (IQR 38·0-60·0); 11 548 (44·9%) were male and 14 188 (55·1%) were female. The prevalence of LSM of 8 kPa or more was 4·4% (95% CI 4·2-4·7; n=1136), LSM 10 kPa or more was 1·6% (1·5-1·8; n=421), and LSM 12 kPa or more was 0·8% (0·7-0·9; n=205)
title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: . Steatotic liver disease was present in 43·7% (43·1-44·3; n=11 242) of participants, with MASLD in 39·5% (38·9-40·1; n=10 162), MetALD in 2·0% (1·8-2·2; n=516), and ALD in 1·6% (1·5-1·8; n=411) of participants. The highest prevalences of LSM of 8 kPa or more were observed in individuals with obesity (10·7% [9·8-11·6]; n=487 of 4560) and type 2 diabetes (10·7% [9·7-11·8]; n=365 of 3400)
title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: . In multivariable analyses, male sex, older age, heavy alcohol consumption, an Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test score of 16 or more, overweight or obesity, central obesity, prediabetes or type 2 diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, and an increasing number of cardiometabolic risk factors were independently associated with both LSM of 8 kPa or more and steatotic liver disease
title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: . Chronic viral hepatitis was also independently associated with LSM of 8 kPa or more. Liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease are prevalent in community-dwelling Chinese adults, driven by metabolic factors and alcohol consumption. These findings identify chronic liver disease as a major public health challenge in China
title: Prevalence of liver fibrosis and steatotic liver disease in community-dwelling adults in China (the CHESS-LiverHealth project): cross-sectional baseline data from a prospective cohort study.

text: . Community-based, non-invasive screening integrated with metabolic and alcohol risk assessment might offer a crucial opportunity for early detection and targeted interventions to curb the progression to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. text: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.. Prediabetes affects nearly one in three U.S. adults-often progressing to type 2 diabetes within 10 years
title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: . Although prediabetes is increasingly identified in primary care and prevention strategies exist, uptake remains low, particularly in urban safety-net settings. This translational gap reflects the complexity of prevention, which is preference- and context-sensitive
title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: . Mobile health could bridge this gap and improve engagement, but effective design requires understanding patient needs, barriers, and care context. Guided by the Obesity-Related Behavioral Intervention Trials (ORBIT) model, this formative study identified perspectives on prediabetes and diabetes prevention and translated them into components of a patient-facing digital intervention
title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: . Semi-structured qualitative interviews were conducted among 24 adult primary care patients with documented prediabetes in an urban safety-net health system. title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: . Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using rapid qualitative analysis
title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: . Participants (mean age 58.8 years; 83% women; 46% African American/Black; 46% Hispanic/Latino) described six interrelated themes: understanding the diagnosis; making informed treatment decisions; integrating lifestyle change into daily life; finding motivation; staying on track with behavior change; and navigating prevention within health and financial constraints
title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: . Themes revealed gaps in risk understanding, counseling, and action planning and were mapped to preliminary app features. title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: . Nearly 98 million US adults have prediabetes and, without action, many will develop type 2 diabetes within 10 years. For most people, primary care is where prediabetes is first identified and where prevention efforts could have the greatest impact
title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: . Yet despite growing recognition of prediabetes, many patients leave these visits without the support, guidance, or tools needed to take meaningful action. title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: . These gaps are especially pronounced in safety-net health systems serving low-income communities already facing significant social and financial barriers to health. title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: . Findings inspired the design of a mobile health tool to complement primary care by helping patients understand their options and take sustained action toward diabetes prevention.
title: Applying the ORBIT model to design a patient-facing mHealth app for diabetes prevention in urban primary care: translating patient perspectives into app design.

text: Stakeholder Perspectives on the Integration of AI in Diabetes Care: Systematic Review of Qualitative Studies.. AI is increasingly being integrated into diabetes care, with growing evidence supporting its potential to improve clinical decision-making, risk prediction, and self-management
title: Stakeholder Perspectives on the Integration of AI in Diabetes Care: Systematic Review of Qualitative Studies.

text: . However, the lived experiences, expectations, and concerns of those involved in its implementation have not been adequately synthesized. This study aims to synthesize qualitative evidence on the perspectives of patients, caregivers, health care professionals (HCPs), and other stakeholders regarding the integration of AI in diabetes management
title: Stakeholder Perspectives on the Integration of AI in Diabetes Care: Systematic Review of Qualitative Studies.

text: . We searched MEDLINE via PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, CINAHL, and PsycINFO from inception to February 17, 2026
title: Stakeholder Perspectives on the Integration of AI in Diabetes Care: Systematic Review of Qualitative Studies.

text: . Eligible studies examined the perspectives of adult patients, caregivers, health care professionals, or administrators on AI-enabled tools for diabetes management, self-management, clinical decision support, or the prevention of complications, and used qualitative methods or reported a separately analyzable qualitative component
title: Stakeholder Perspectives on the Integration of AI in Diabetes Care: Systematic Review of Qualitative Studies.

text: . Tools required an identifiable data-driven function for prediction, classification, recommendation, personalization, or decision support. title: Stakeholder Perspectives on the Integration of AI in Diabetes Care: Systematic Review of Qualitative Studies.

title: Stakeholder Perspectives on the Integration of AI in Diabetes Care: Systematic Review of Qualitative Studies.

title: Stakeholder Perspectives on the Integration of AI in Diabetes Care: Systematic Review of Qualitative Studies.

title: Stakeholder Perspectives on the Integration of AI in Diabetes Care: Systematic Review of Qualitative Studies.

text: Potential Diagnostic and Therapeutic Role of Amino Acids in Diabetic Kidney Disease: An Updated Review.. Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease. Amino acids play a crucial role in both the diagnosis and treatment of DKD
title: Potential Diagnostic and Therapeutic Role of Amino Acids in Diabetic Kidney Disease: An Updated Review.

text: . This review examines the mechanism by which amino acids exert their biological effects and their relevance to the diagnosis and management of DKD. A literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science
title: Potential Diagnostic and Therapeutic Role of Amino Acids in Diabetic Kidney Disease: An Updated Review.

text: . Search terms included "DKD", "Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM)", "Blood Pressure (B.P)", "Proteinuria", "microalbuminuria", "Inflammatory cytokines", "homocysteine", "nephrotoxicity", and "amino acids" used to identify relevant studies
title: Potential Diagnostic and Therapeutic Role of Amino Acids in Diabetic Kidney Disease: An Updated Review.

text: . Several studies demonstrated that amino acid supplementation attenuates serum transforming growth factor-β (TGF- β) levels and the urinary albumin- to-creatinine ratio, and improves metabolic parameters in patients with T2DM. Improvements in kidney function and B.P were also observed, suggesting that amino acid supplementation may prevent the progression of microalbuminuria
title: Potential Diagnostic and Therapeutic Role of Amino Acids in Diabetic Kidney Disease: An Updated Review.

text: . Patients with DKD exhibit altered levels of inflammatory cytokines and homocysteine. In some studies, combination therapy was more effective in reducing nephrotoxicity. Metabolomics profiling of urinary and serum metabolic pathways has emerged as a promising approach for identifying potential diagnostic biomarkers in patients with DKD
title: Potential Diagnostic and Therapeutic Role of Amino Acids in Diabetic Kidney Disease: An Updated Review.

text: . Candidate biomarkers include tryptophan, threonine, citrulline, methionine and homovanillic acid sulphate. Abnormal amino acid metabolism in DKD is associated with oxidative stress, inflammatory and immune dysregulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, iron death and dysregulated autophagy. Drugs that interrupt the renin-angiotensin- aldosterone system can help control these changes
title: Potential Diagnostic and Therapeutic Role of Amino Acids in Diabetic Kidney Disease: An Updated Review.

text: . Abnormal amino acid metabolism in DKD is closely linked to oxidative stress, inflammatory responses and immune responses, as well as mitochondrial dysfunction, iron death and impaired autophagy. Altered amino acid profiles in DKD may serve as early diagnostic markers
title: Potential Diagnostic and Therapeutic Role of Amino Acids in Diabetic Kidney Disease: An Updated Review.

text: . Metabolomic approaches enable detection of changes in non-essential amino acids and early kidney damage before the onset of proteinuria, reflecting changes in the local renal microenvironment that precede clinically detectable proteinuria.
title: Potential Diagnostic and Therapeutic Role of Amino Acids in Diabetic Kidney Disease: An Updated Review.

text: "An illustrative socio-biological cascade of the concentric model for health-bound networks: social determinants, social support and biological responses".. Health has been associated with social support. Supported patients with complex health issues have a better chance of living healthier, longer lives and enjoying a better quality of life
title: "An illustrative socio-biological cascade of the concentric model for health-bound networks: social determinants, social support and biological responses".

text: . Research indicates that physical, mental, and emotional health are connected to both biological and social determinants. This paper proposes a conceptual, society-to-biology model, the Concentric Model for Health-Bound Networks, that explores the complexity of social support and integrates the foundational principles of systems biology and systems thinking
title: "An illustrative socio-biological cascade of the concentric model for health-bound networks: social determinants, social support and biological responses".

text: . This transdisciplinary model conceptualizes the sources of support for patients requiring care as dynamic, concentric social networks. The model is informed by current understanding of the interdependence between disease and social support
title: "An illustrative socio-biological cascade of the concentric model for health-bound networks: social determinants, social support and biological responses".

text: . The Concentric Model for Health-Bound Networks attempts to clarify the configuration of care-intensive social support by maintaining and transforming diverse, overlapping webs of support that change dynamically
title: "An illustrative socio-biological cascade of the concentric model for health-bound networks: social determinants, social support and biological responses".

text: . Drawing upon network science and systems thinking, this model examines how these approaches apply to the capacity of social support to improve health outcomes and inform clinical practice. While the Concentric Model for Health-Bound Networks is untested, complex, care-intensive social support requires dynamic models that adapt to complexity
title: "An illustrative socio-biological cascade of the concentric model for health-bound networks: social determinants, social support and biological responses".

text: . Via a transdisciplinary socio-biological approach called the Socio-Biological Cascade, feedback may co-occur across the Social Determinants of Health, social support, and biological processes
title: "An illustrative socio-biological cascade of the concentric model for health-bound networks: social determinants, social support and biological responses".

text: . Type 2 diabetes management, with its overlap of complex biological processes and individualized health-related requirements, serves as a theoretical example of how social support informs the Socio-Biological Cascade and its possible implications for health
title: "An illustrative socio-biological cascade of the concentric model for health-bound networks: social determinants, social support and biological responses".

text: . Changes in the composition, quality, change over time, and structural integrity of health-bound support networks may mediate or modify relationships between social determinants of health and biological stress, inflammatory, and metabolic responses, thereby affecting chronic disease outcomes
title: "An illustrative socio-biological cascade of the concentric model for health-bound networks: social determinants, social support and biological responses".

text: . It is hypothesized that the dynamics of patient-centered social support, informed by the Social Determinants of Health and applying the Socio-Biological Cascade and Concentric Model for Health-Bound Networks, can elucidate complex health outcomes.
title: "An illustrative socio-biological cascade of the concentric model for health-bound networks: social determinants, social support and biological responses".

text: Implementing 1:1 Lifestyle Medicine Coaching Visits for Management of Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: Cone Health Reidsville Endocrinology.. Lifestyle medicine (LM) provides a high-value framework for treating and potentially reversing chronic diseases, such as type 2 diabetes (T2D), obesity, cardiovascular diseases, and some cancers
title: Implementing 1:1 Lifestyle Medicine Coaching Visits for Management of Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: Cone Health Reidsville Endocrinology.

text: . Yet, the field of LM is still growing, and few examples exist of how to successfully implement LM into clinical care. This paper describes the implementation of 1:1 lifestyle medicine (LM) coaching visits for 45 patients with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes (T2D), (mean HbA1c 10.5%) and on multiple diabetes medications, at Cone Health's Reidsville Endocrinology practice in North Carolina, USA
title: Implementing 1:1 Lifestyle Medicine Coaching Visits for Management of Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: Cone Health Reidsville Endocrinology.

text: . In brief, during routine endocrinology visits, the lead physician of the LM program at Cone Health, who is trained in LM, identified patients with uncontrolled T2D where scheduling allowed him to fit in some additional time for coaching. Forty-five interested patients selected over a period of several weeks from Spring of 2022 to Fall of 2022 made the first cohort
title: Implementing 1:1 Lifestyle Medicine Coaching Visits for Management of Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: Cone Health Reidsville Endocrinology.

text: . During a typical LM encounter, immediately after addressing their referral concerns with a routine endocrinology consult, verbally consenting patients were personally invited to learn more about LM. They were provided with a packet of materials focused predominately on prescribing nutrition and exercise as treatment for chronic disease
title: Implementing 1:1 Lifestyle Medicine Coaching Visits for Management of Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: Cone Health Reidsville Endocrinology.

text: . The physician spent an additional 10-15 minutes with each verbally consenting patient to go through selected materials in the packet, focusing largely on nutrition and physical activity, and successfully billed for the additional time. The patients were encouraged to take the packet home for further learning and return to their next routine visits with questions and to engage in further coaching
title: Implementing 1:1 Lifestyle Medicine Coaching Visits for Management of Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: Cone Health Reidsville Endocrinology.

text: . Following this brief but intensely focused coaching session which was done in addition to the routine endocrinology visit, lifestyle medicine coaching was able to be incorporated into subsequent, routine endocrinology visits in many of the initially identified patients. The majority of these patients also accepted a referral to a dietitian in the same practice
title: Implementing 1:1 Lifestyle Medicine Coaching Visits for Management of Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: Cone Health Reidsville Endocrinology.

text: . This experience highlights a model for potentially integrating LM coaching into routine practice and, consistent with previous research, highlights the importance of a site champion for successful LM implementation. Future research is needed to formally assess the success of coaching visits, particularly in terms of assessing health outcomes in patients who engaged in the 1:1 coaching.
title: Implementing 1:1 Lifestyle Medicine Coaching Visits for Management of Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: Cone Health Reidsville Endocrinology.

text: A Novel Approach to Managing "Double Diabetes" in a Pediatric Patient on Insulin Pump Therapy: An Off-Label Use of a Fixed-Ratio Insulin Degludec/Liraglutide Combination.. title: A Novel Approach to Managing "Double Diabetes" in a Pediatric Patient on Insulin Pump Therapy: An Off-Label Use of a Fixed-Ratio Insulin Degludec/Liraglutide Combination.

title: A Novel Approach to Managing "Double Diabetes" in a Pediatric Patient on Insulin Pump Therapy: An Off-Label Use of a Fixed-Ratio Insulin Degludec/Liraglutide Combination.

text: . We present the case of an 11-year-old girl with antibody-positive T1D on an insulin pump who developed significant features of DD, including obesity, acanthosis nigricans, and escalating insulin requirements that exceeded her pump reservoir capacity

text: . Over an eight-month follow-up period, the patient demonstrated modest weight loss (-2.2 kg) and a reduction in BMI z-score, with a marked improvement in glycemic control. text: Orforglipron: An Oral GLP-1 Receptor Agonist for Obesity Treatment.. To describe the properties of a newly approved oral glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist for the treatment of obesity. title: Orforglipron: An Oral GLP-1 Receptor Agonist for Obesity Treatment.

text: Perioperative management of SGLT2 inhibitors: balancing euglycaemic ketoacidosis risk and cardiorenal benefits.. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are established therapies for type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, creating a perioperative need to balance prevention of euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis (euDKA) against cardiorenal protection
title: Perioperative management of SGLT2 inhibitors: balancing euglycaemic ketoacidosis risk and cardiorenal benefits.

text: . Fasting, surgical stress, infection, reduced carbohydrate intake, insulin dose reduction, and hypovolaemia can amplify glycosuria and ketogenesis and precipitate euDKA. Most guidelines recommend withholding SGLT2 inhibitors for 3-4 days before elective surgery, although recommendations vary by agent, procedure, fasting duration, diabetes status, and monitoring capacity
title: Perioperative management of SGLT2 inhibitors: balancing euglycaemic ketoacidosis risk and cardiorenal benefits.

text: . Emerging evidence indicates competing perioperative risks and benefits. Inadequate withholding and emergency surgery are associated with high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and ketoacidosis, whereas observational studies associate preoperative use with lower risks of acute kidney injury and short-term mortality
title: Perioperative management of SGLT2 inhibitors: balancing euglycaemic ketoacidosis risk and cardiorenal benefits.

text: . Heart failure withdrawal studies further suggest that cardiovascular and volume-regulatory benefits may diminish rapidly after interruption. These findings challenge uniform withholding but do not support routine perioperative continuation
title: Perioperative management of SGLT2 inhibitors: balancing euglycaemic ketoacidosis risk and cardiorenal benefits.

text: . Management should be stratified by treatment indication, glycated haemoglobin, insulin dependence, hepatic and kidney function, infection and volume status, surgical urgency and invasiveness, expected fasting duration, and access to ketone and acid-base monitoring
title: Perioperative management of SGLT2 inhibitors: balancing euglycaemic ketoacidosis risk and cardiorenal benefits.

text: . Patients at high metabolic risk generally require an adequate preoperative withholding interval and intensified monitoring, whereas low-risk patients treated primarily for heart failure or chronic kidney disease require individualised multidisciplinary assessment
title: Perioperative management of SGLT2 inhibitors: balancing euglycaemic ketoacidosis risk and cardiorenal benefits.

text: . Future studies should define indication- and risk-based withholding and restart strategies and jointly evaluate euDKA, acute kidney injury, worsening heart failure, myocardial injury, mortality, and postoperative recovery.
title: Perioperative management of SGLT2 inhibitors: balancing euglycaemic ketoacidosis risk and cardiorenal benefits.

title: The clinical relevance of obesity and glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies for chronic weight management in patients treated by obstetrician-gynecologists and gynecologists: A non-systematic narrative review.

title: The clinical relevance of obesity and glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies for chronic weight management in patients treated by obstetrician-gynecologists and gynecologists: A non-systematic narrative review.

text: Pharmacological intersections between type 2 diabetes and cancer: Metabolic crosstalk, antidiabetic therapies and clinical implications.. title: Pharmacological intersections between type 2 diabetes and cancer: Metabolic crosstalk, antidiabetic therapies and clinical implications.

title: Indices of obesity, malnutrition and inflammation are strong predictors of mortality in adults with type 2 diabetes: the FIELD study.

title: Indices of obesity, malnutrition and inflammation are strong predictors of mortality in adults with type 2 diabetes: the FIELD study.
