text: Type 5 diabetes mellitus: revisiting malnutrition-related diabetes.. A distinct form of diabetes occurring in lean, young individuals with a history of undernutrition was first described in the 1950s asa paradoxical combination of severe hyperglycemia, low body weight, and the absence of ketosis
title: Type 5 diabetes mellitus: revisiting malnutrition-related diabetes.

text: . Historically termed malnutrition-relateddiabetes mellitus (MRDM), it was recognized as a separate entity by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1985 but was removedfrom formal classification in 1999 due to insufficient mechanistic evidence
title: Type 5 diabetes mellitus: revisiting malnutrition-related diabetes.

text: . Over the following two decades, research in low- and middle-income countries revealed unique metabolic traits of malnutrition-associateddiabetes, distinguishing it from type 1 and type 2 diabetes
title: Type 5 diabetes mellitus: revisiting malnutrition-related diabetes.

text: . In 2025, the International Diabetes Federation (IDF) formally endorsed recognitionof type 5 diabetes mellitus (T5DM), which is estimated to affect approximately 20-25 million people worldwide and predominantlyaffects young individuals with low body mass index living in low- and middle-income countries
title: Type 5 diabetes mellitus: revisiting malnutrition-related diabetes.

text: . T5DM is characterized by impaired insulin secretion, preserved insulin sensitivity, resistance to ketosis despite severe hyperglycemia, and absence of autoimmune markers. Early-life undernutrition is increasingly recognized as a factor disrupting pancreatic organogenesisand β-cell development, resulting in persistent structural deficits and limited functional β-cell reserve in adulthood
title: Type 5 diabetes mellitus: revisiting malnutrition-related diabetes.

text: . Effective management necessitates an integrated nutritional and pharmacological approach. Incorrectly classifying the condition as type 1diabetes may lead to unnecessary lifelong intensive insulin therapy, while misclassification as type 2 diabetes may lead to an inappropriatefocus on insulin resistance-targeted therapies
title: Type 5 diabetes mellitus: revisiting malnutrition-related diabetes.

text: . Although T5DM is most commonly reported in low- and middle-income countries, awareness is essential in high-income settings, particularly among migrant populations from regions affected by chronic undernutrition. Further research is needed to develop standardized diagnostic criteria, improve prevention strategies, and establish evidence-based treatment guidelines.
title: Type 5 diabetes mellitus: revisiting malnutrition-related diabetes.

text: Association Between Type of Antidiabetic Treatment and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.. Maintaining adequate glycemic control remains a major challenge in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
title: Association Between Type of Antidiabetic Treatment and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Patients requiring insulin therapy often have longer disease duration and more advanced metabolic deterioration, which may influence the relationship between type of antidiabetic treatment and glycemic control. This study aimed to evaluate the association between type of antidiabetic treatment and glycemic control in patients with T2DM
title: Association Between Type of Antidiabetic Treatment and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed a clinical database of 995 patients with T2DM treated at a specialized metabolic and cardiovascular center in southern Tamaulipas, Mexico. Patients were classified into two treatment groups: oral antidiabetic therapy and combined insulin plus oral antidiabetic therapy. Glycemic control was defined as glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) ≤7%
title: Association Between Type of Antidiabetic Treatment and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Descriptive analyses were performed, and continuous and categorical variables were compared using Student's t-test and chi-squared test, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the independent association between type of antidiabetic treatment and glycemic control, adjusting for age, sex, diabetes duration, and body mass index (BMI)
title: Association Between Type of Antidiabetic Treatment and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . A total of 995 patients were included: 780 (78.4%) received oral antidiabetic therapy, and 215 (21.6%) received combined insulin plus oral antidiabetic therapy. Overall, 192 patients (19.3%) achieved glycemic control, while 803 (80.7%) remained uncontrolled
title: Association Between Type of Antidiabetic Treatment and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Glycemic control was achieved in 172 patients (22.1%) in the oral antidiabetic therapy group and 20 patients (9.3%) in the combined insulin plus oral antidiabetic therapy group. Type of antidiabetic treatment was significantly associated with glycemic control (χ²=17.59; p<0.001)
title: Association Between Type of Antidiabetic Treatment and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . In the adjusted logistic regression model, oral antidiabetic therapy was independently associated with higher odds of achieving glycemic control compared with combined insulin plus oral antidiabetic therapy (OR=2.35; 95% CI: 1.41-3.93; p=0.001). Longer diabetes duration was negatively associated with glycemic control, whereas BMI was not independently associated
title: Association Between Type of Antidiabetic Treatment and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Type of antidiabetic treatment was significantly associated with glycemic control in patients with T2DM. However, the lower probability of glycemic control among patients receiving combined insulin plus oral antidiabetic therapy likely reflects longer disease duration and greater disease severity rather than reduced treatment effectiveness
title: Association Between Type of Antidiabetic Treatment and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . These findings highlight the importance of early optimization of diabetes management before progression to advanced disease requiring insulin therapy.
title: Association Between Type of Antidiabetic Treatment and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.

text: Variation in Treatment Patterns of Type 2 Diabetes in Older Patients.. To estimate the proportion of older patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and HbA1c above or below goal at provider level and explore factors associated with patients being above or below goal
title: Variation in Treatment Patterns of Type 2 Diabetes in Older Patients.

text: . We used 2023 Cleveland Clinic electronic health records, including patients ≥ 65 years old with T2D, ≥ 1 diabetes medication and ≥ 1 HbA1c measurement. Patients were assigned to their listed primary care provider or the one they saw most frequently and stratified into good, intermediate, or poor health
title: Variation in Treatment Patterns of Type 2 Diabetes in Older Patients.

text: . Outcomes were patients being above, at, and below goal, defined as HbA1c greater than, 0%-1.5% lower than, and ≥ 1.5% lower than goal, respectively. HbA1c goals were < 7.5% for patients with good, < 8% intermediate and < 9% poor health. We included 406 providers and 15 865 patients
title: Variation in Treatment Patterns of Type 2 Diabetes in Older Patients.

text: . We included 406 providers and 15 865 patients. Across providers, 52.1% (range: 10%-87.9%) of patients were below goal (13.4% in those with good, 42.0% intermediate, 76.0% poor health); 11.3% (range: 0.0%-36.4%) were above goal (25.1% in those with good, 13.7% intermediate, 6.7% poor health). There was significant variation across providers (p < 0.001)
title: Variation in Treatment Patterns of Type 2 Diabetes in Older Patients.

text: . In a multivariable model, having endocrinology providers (vs. internal medicine) decreased the adjusted relative risk ratio (aRRR) of being below goal (aRRR = 0.69; 95% CI: 0.57-0.82) and increased the probability of being above goal (aRRR = 1.65; 95% CI: 1.33-2.05)
title: Variation in Treatment Patterns of Type 2 Diabetes in Older Patients.

text: . Substantial provider-level variation suggests that individualised glycemic management for older adults remains difficult to operationalise in routine care. Clinical decision support tools that automate assessment of health status and recommend glycemic goals may help clinicians better align glycemic management with patient needs.
title: Variation in Treatment Patterns of Type 2 Diabetes in Older Patients.

text: Responders Vs. Non-Responders or How to Predict the Response to GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist Therapy.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists have transformed the pharmacological management of type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity, yet substantial interindividual variability in treatment response remains a defining clinical challenge
title: Responders Vs. Non-Responders or How to Predict the Response to GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist Therapy.

text: . Narrative review. PubMed was searched to 25 May 2026 (English language, human studies, 2005-2026) for biological, genetic, metabolic, hormonal, behavioural and psychosocial predictors of differential response
title: Responders Vs. Non-Responders or How to Predict the Response to GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist Therapy.

text: . Evidence is organised across three clinically distinct contexts: glycaemic control in T2D; weight loss in people with overweight or obesity without T2D; and dual metabolic benefit in those with both conditions
title: Responders Vs. Non-Responders or How to Predict the Response to GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist Therapy.

text: . Response heterogeneity is most pronounced in obesity without diabetes, where non-response-commonly defined as less than 5% total body weight loss-affects approximately 10% of participants in controlled trials, with real-world cohorts suggesting a higher frequency in routine practice; glycaemic non-response in T2D is less common but clinically significant
title: Responders Vs. Non-Responders or How to Predict the Response to GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist Therapy.

text: . Across all three contexts, early on-treatment response is the most readily actionable predictor currently available
title: Responders Vs. Non-Responders or How to Predict the Response to GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist Therapy.

text: . A recent large genome-wide association study reported associations between variation in the GLP1R drug-target gene and both weight-loss efficacy and gastrointestinal tolerability, and between agent-specific GIPR variants and nausea and vomiting with tirzepatide; these self-reported, single-cohort and as-yet unreplicated findings remain hypothesis-generating rather than a basis for
title: Responders Vs. Non-Responders or How to Predict the Response to GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist Therapy.

text: hypothesis-generating rather than a basis for individual-level genotyping
title: Responders Vs. Non-Responders or How to Predict the Response to GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist Therapy.

text: . Metabolic, microbiome and neuroendocrine predictors are at a comparably preliminary stage. No single baseline characteristic reliably predicts response. Structured assessment of early on-treatment response is currently the most defensible basis for individualising therapy; genetic, metabolic and microbiome markers require prospective replication before clinical application.
title: Responders Vs. Non-Responders or How to Predict the Response to GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist Therapy.

journal: Australian health review : a publication of the Australian Hospital Association

title: Divergent complication patterns of type 2 diabetes in African individuals who are lean versus overweight or obese: a multi-cohort analysis.

text: Severe Uncontrolled Pancreatogenic Diabetes in a Patient With Prior Alcoholic Pancreatitis and Partial Pancreatectomy.. Pancreatogenic diabetes mellitus (type 3c diabetes mellitus, T3cDM) is an underrecognized form of secondary diabetes resulting from pancreatic exocrine disease, including chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic resection
title: Severe Uncontrolled Pancreatogenic Diabetes in a Patient With Prior Alcoholic Pancreatitis and Partial Pancreatectomy.

text: . It is frequently misclassified as type 2 diabetes mellitus, leading to delayed diagnosis and suboptimal management. We present a case of a 57-year-old female with a history of chronic alcoholic pancreatitis status post partial pancreatectomy who presented with severe uncontrolled hyperglycemia and medication nonadherence
title: Severe Uncontrolled Pancreatogenic Diabetes in a Patient With Prior Alcoholic Pancreatitis and Partial Pancreatectomy.

text: . Laboratory evaluation revealed a serum glucose of 668 mg/dL, hemoglobin A1c of 19%, and a low C-peptide level with normal insulin levels while receiving exogenous insulin, consistent with impaired endogenous insulin secretion and pancreatogenic diabetes
title: Severe Uncontrolled Pancreatogenic Diabetes in a Patient With Prior Alcoholic Pancreatitis and Partial Pancreatectomy.

text: . Despite repeated counseling and multiple attempts to optimize insulin therapy, the patient persistently refused insulin administration, resulting in refractory hyperglycemia throughout hospitalization
title: Severe Uncontrolled Pancreatogenic Diabetes in a Patient With Prior Alcoholic Pancreatitis and Partial Pancreatectomy.

text: . This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of distinguishing pancreatogenic diabetes from type 2 diabetes mellitus in patients with underlying pancreatic disease and emphasizes the importance of recognizing characteristic clinical features, including prior pancreatic injury and reduced endogenous insulin production
title: Severe Uncontrolled Pancreatogenic Diabetes in a Patient With Prior Alcoholic Pancreatitis and Partial Pancreatectomy.

text: . Early identification of T3cDM is essential because its pathophysiology and management differ substantially from type 2 diabetes mellitus and often require early insulin-based therapy to improve glycemic control and reduce long-term metabolic complications.
title: Severe Uncontrolled Pancreatogenic Diabetes in a Patient With Prior Alcoholic Pancreatitis and Partial Pancreatectomy.

text: BMI trajectories and their relation to medication, comorbidities, and healthcare service use among people with type 2 diabetes mellitus.. To identify BMI trajectories after type 2 diabetes (T2D) diagnosis and examine associations with laboratory measures, medication use, comorbidities, and healthcare utilization
title: BMI trajectories and their relation to medication, comorbidities, and healthcare service use among people with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

text: . We analyzed BMI trajectories in 3,539 adults with T2D in North Karelia (2011-2014) and followed until 2024. BMI trajectory classes were estimated using growth mixture modeling. Regression models were used to assess differences in measurement activity, treatment intensity and diabetes medication use between the classes
title: BMI trajectories and their relation to medication, comorbidities, and healthcare service use among people with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

text: . Three BMI trajectories were identified: stable (77.7 %), increasing (14.6 %), and decreasing (7.7 %). HbA1c and LDL cholesterol measurement activity was lowest in the decreasing class. Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 agonists varied over time, peaking in the decreasing class in 2015 and in the increasing class in 2024
title: BMI trajectories and their relation to medication, comorbidities, and healthcare service use among people with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

text: . Comorbidities increased in all classes but differed in pattern: the increasing class accumulated more chronic kidney and urinary tract diseases, obesity related diagnoses, sleep disorders, and chronic lower respiratory diseases, whereas the decreasing class had higher prevalence of dementia and cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases. Healthcare utilization was highest in the decreasing class
title: BMI trajectories and their relation to medication, comorbidities, and healthcare service use among people with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

text: . These findings reveal considerable heterogeneity in long-term outcomes among people with T2D and highlight the need for continuous monitoring and targeted support to maintain metabolic control and manage comorbidity burden.
title: BMI trajectories and their relation to medication, comorbidities, and healthcare service use among people with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

title: Quantum machine learning in diabetes and metabolism: Applications and translational challenges.

title: Quantum machine learning in diabetes and metabolism: Applications and translational challenges.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine

text: . Hardware limitations associated with noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices, data encoding, and privacy considerations emerged as key barriers to clinical translation. title: Quantum machine learning in diabetes and metabolism: Applications and translational challenges.

text: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of quinazoline-carbazole derivatives as dual TXNIP/DYRK1A inhibitors for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.. text: . The quinazoline scaffold constitutes the core pharmacophore of TXNIP inhibitors. Harmine, a prototypical DYRK1A inhibitor bearing a β-carboline scaffold, has demonstrated robust β-cell proliferative activity. Carbazole serves as a structurally simplified bioisostere of β-carboline
title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of quinazoline-carbazole derivatives as dual TXNIP/DYRK1A inhibitors for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

title: Intramedullary Nailing of Femoral Shaft Fractures: Implications of Interlocking Screw Breakage.

text: . Our study examined patients with femoral shaft fractures treated with IMN who developed interlocking screw breakage to evaluate outcomes and complications. Methods The retrospective cohort study included 551 patients with femoral shaft fractures (AO Foundation (AO)/Orthopaedic Trauma Association (OTA) 32A/B/C) treated with IMN at a level one trauma center
title: Intramedullary Nailing of Femoral Shaft Fractures: Implications of Interlocking Screw Breakage.

text: . Inclusion criteria were acute fractures treated definitively with IMN and a minimum one-year follow-up. Patient demographics, fracture characteristics (including OTA classification), and radiographic union at one year were recorded. Radiographs were reviewed preoperatively, postoperatively, and at clinical follow-up visits
title: Intramedullary Nailing of Femoral Shaft Fractures: Implications of Interlocking Screw Breakage.

text: . Results Interlocking screw failure occurred in 31 patients (5.6%), of whom 24 had complete one-year follow-up. A total of 185 patients were included in the final analysis (24 with and 161 without screw breakage). There were no significant differences in age (48.5 vs 46.0 years,
title: Intramedullary Nailing of Femoral Shaft Fractures: Implications of Interlocking Screw Breakage.

text: Association Between Estimated Glucose Disposal Rate and Chronic Kidney Disease in Elderly Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study in Zhejiang, China.. To examine the association between estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) and study-defined chronic kidney disease (CKD) among elderly patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in Zhejiang Province, China
title: Association Between Estimated Glucose Disposal Rate and Chronic Kidney Disease in Elderly Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study in Zhejiang, China.

text: . This cross-sectional study included 713 elderly T2DM patients (≥60 years) from Zhejiang Province, conducted between March and November 2018 as part of the China National Diabetic Chronic Complications Study. Study-defined CKD was operationally defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m Among 713 participants, 245 (34.36%) met the study-defined CKD criteria
title: Association Between Estimated Glucose Disposal Rate and Chronic Kidney Disease in Elderly Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study in Zhejiang, China.

text: . Each 1-unit increase in eGDR was associated with lower odds of study-defined CKD after multivariable adjustment (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.70-0.86; p < 0.001). Compared with the lowest eGDR tertile, the adjusted ORs (95% CIs) were 0.51 (0.35-0.76) for the middle tertile and 0.31 (0.20-0.48) for the highest tertile (both p < 0.001)
title: Association Between Estimated Glucose Disposal Rate and Chronic Kidney Disease in Elderly Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study in Zhejiang, China.

text: . RCS analysis demonstrated an approximately linear inverse association between eGDR and study-defined CKD (p for nonlinearity > 0.05). eGDR was inversely associated with UACR (ρ = -0.277, p < 0.001) whereas the association between eGDR and eGFR was not statistically significant. The discriminative ability of eGDR for study-defined CKD was modest (AUC = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.61-0.70)
title: Association Between Estimated Glucose Disposal Rate and Chronic Kidney Disease in Elderly Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study in Zhejiang, China.

text: . The direction of the association was generally consistent across subgroups, with no significant interactions. Lower eGDR was associated with a higher prevalence of study-defined CKD in elderly patients with T2DM, with an approximately linear cross-sectional association
title: Association Between Estimated Glucose Disposal Rate and Chronic Kidney Disease in Elderly Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study in Zhejiang, China.

text: . Prospective studies are needed to establish temporality and assess whether eGDR adds information beyond established CKD assessment.
title: Association Between Estimated Glucose Disposal Rate and Chronic Kidney Disease in Elderly Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study in Zhejiang, China.

text: Prevalence, risk factors and adverse health outcomes of osteosarcopenia in middle-aged and older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus-a scoping review.. Osteoporosis and sarcopenia are increasingly recognised as important complications of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D). As both conditions share common pathophysiological mechanisms, they can coexist in the same individual
title: Prevalence, risk factors and adverse health outcomes of osteosarcopenia in middle-aged and older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus-a scoping review.
journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA

text: . The coexistence of osteoporosis and sarcopenia, known as osteosarcopenia (OS), is an emerging geriatric syndrome. Compared with its individual components, OS has received much less attention. The overall objective of this scoping review was to summarise the existing literature on the prevalence, risk factors, biomarkers, and adverse health outcomes associated with OS in adults with T2D aged ≥ 40
title: Prevalence, risk factors and adverse health outcomes of osteosarcopenia in middle-aged and older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus-a scoping review.
journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA

text: . A search was conducted in eight online databases (Ovid MEDLINE®, Embase (Ovid), PubMed, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus and PsycINFO) and grey literature sources for relevant articles published in English up to 31 July 2024. A total of ten articles reporting findings from nine distinct studies (7 cross-sectional, 2 case-control) were included
title: Prevalence, risk factors and adverse health outcomes of osteosarcopenia in middle-aged and older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus-a scoping review.
journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA

text: . Despite significant heterogeneity in its definition, OS was shown to be prevalent in T2D. The risk of OS was increased in individuals with T2D who had poor β-cell function, low body mass index, and smaller waist circumference. Insulin resistance, duration of T2D, glycaemic control, and metformin, sulfonylurea and insulin use were not shown to be significant risk factors
title: Prevalence, risk factors and adverse health outcomes of osteosarcopenia in middle-aged and older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus-a scoping review.
journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA

text: . Osteocalcin was a potentially useful biomarker of OS in T2D, and OS may be associated with falls and leg fractures in T2D. In conclusion, this scoping review revealed a paucity of information about OS in T2D. Longitudinal studies with comprehensive phenotyping are required to address the many knowledge gaps.
title: Prevalence, risk factors and adverse health outcomes of osteosarcopenia in middle-aged and older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus-a scoping review.
journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA

text: Superimposed entrapment neuropathy in diabetes: Evidence review and algorithm for referral decisions.. Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is common, disabling, and associated with substantial risk of foot ulceration and lower extremity complications
title: Superimposed entrapment neuropathy in diabetes: Evidence review and algorithm for referral decisions.

text: . A subset of patients develops superimposed peripheral nerve entrapment, which can exacerbate pain, impair protective sensation, and contribute to microcirculatory dysfunction. Although surgical decompression has been studied for more than three decades, awareness of entrapment features remains low in primary care, and guidance on patient selection is limited
title: Superimposed entrapment neuropathy in diabetes: Evidence review and algorithm for referral decisions.

text: . This review summarizes current evidence on the clinical identification of focal nerve compression in patients with DPN and evaluates outcomes of decompression in appropriately selected patients
title: Superimposed entrapment neuropathy in diabetes: Evidence review and algorithm for referral decisions.

text: . Across randomized controlled trials and observational studies, decompression is associated with reductions in neuropathic pain, improvements in selected sensory measures, and lower recurrence of neuropathic foot ulcers in patients who exhibit clinical features of entrapment
title: Superimposed entrapment neuropathy in diabetes: Evidence review and algorithm for referral decisions.

text: . Based on this evidence, we propose a structured clinical algorithm to support primary care clinicians in identifying potential candidates for surgical evaluation. The algorithm emphasizes confirmation of DPN, screening for characteristic entrapment findings, assessment of prognostic indicators, optimization of conservative care, and appropriate referral
title: Superimposed entrapment neuropathy in diabetes: Evidence review and algorithm for referral decisions.

text: . This approach aims to improve recognition of superimposed compression neuropathy and to provide practical guidance for evaluation and referral within primary care settings.
title: Superimposed entrapment neuropathy in diabetes: Evidence review and algorithm for referral decisions.

text: Adult vaccination coverage and missed preventive care opportunities among Filipino adults with diabetes: A cross-sectional study.. Adults with diabetes mellitus are at increased risk of vaccine-preventable infections and complications
title: Adult vaccination coverage and missed preventive care opportunities among Filipino adults with diabetes: A cross-sectional study.

text: . Despite recommendations for adult immunization, uptake remains suboptimal in many low- and middle-income countries, including the Philippines, where data remain limited
title: Adult vaccination coverage and missed preventive care opportunities among Filipino adults with diabetes: A cross-sectional study.

text: . This cross-sectional study assessed adult immunization coverage and associated clinical and sociodemographic factors among Filipino adults with diabetes recruited from inpatient, outpatient, and community outreach settings at a tertiary hospital
title: Adult vaccination coverage and missed preventive care opportunities among Filipino adults with diabetes: A cross-sectional study.

text: . Uptake of influenza, pneumococcal, herpes zoster, hepatitis B, tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis (Td/Tdap), and COVID-19 vaccines was evaluated using prespecified operational definitions. Crude associations and parsimonious multivariable logistic regression models were examined; COVID-19 vaccination was not modeled because only six participants were unvaccinated
title: Adult vaccination coverage and missed preventive care opportunities among Filipino adults with diabetes: A cross-sectional study.

text: . Among 284 participants (mean age 61.5 ± 12.7 y, 55.6% females), uptake was 44.4% for influenza, 49.6% for pneumococcal, 18.1% for herpes zoster, 15.5% for hepatitis B, 23.2% for Td/Tdap, and 97.9% for the primary COVID-19 series. Males had lower adjusted odds of influenza and pneumococcal vaccination, while increasing age was associated with pneumococcal uptake
title: Adult vaccination coverage and missed preventive care opportunities among Filipino adults with diabetes: A cross-sectional study.

text: . Middle and high household income and diabetes duration of 5-10 y were associated with influenza vaccination. Among adults aged ≥50 y, male sex and high income were associated with herpes zoster vaccination. High income was also associated with hepatitis B and Td/Tdap uptake
title: Adult vaccination coverage and missed preventive care opportunities among Filipino adults with diabetes: A cross-sectional study.

text: . Provider recommendation was associated with all outcomes, while lack of provider recommendation, failure to prioritize vaccination, and financial constraints were common reasons for non-vaccination. Uptake was uneven and low for most recommended adult vaccines. Integrating vaccine assessment and counseling into diabetes care while addressing financial and access barriers may improve uptake.
title: Adult vaccination coverage and missed preventive care opportunities among Filipino adults with diabetes: A cross-sectional study.

text: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.. The risk of diabetic microvascular complications is well established among smokers with type 2 diabetes. However, whether and to what extent this excess risk declines according to smoking cessation duration remains unclear
title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.

text: . To investigate the association between smoking cessation duration and the risk of incident diabetic microvascular complications in patients with diabetes
title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.

text: . This nationwide, population-based cohort study included participants first diagnosed with type 2 diabetes in Korea between 2003 and 2013 and whose smoking status was assessed at least 4 times across repeated health checkups, with a final checkup during 2009 to 2013. Data were analyzed from November 10, 2025, to April 16, 2026. Smoking status and cessation duration
title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.

text: . Smoking status and cessation duration. Quitters were defined as participants who reported current smoking at their initial health checkup and reported smoking cessation at all subsequent checkups without relapse. Continuous smokers were defined as participants who consistently reported current smoking at every health checkup
title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.

text: . Among quitters, smoking cessation duration was categorized as less than 2, 2 to 3, 4 to 5, 6 to 7, and 8 or more years. Outcomes of interest were incident diabetic microvascular complications, including diabetic nephropathy, retinopathy, and neuropathy, identified using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) diagnostic codes
title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.

text: . Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate unadjusted and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95% CIs. A total of 209 698 adults (mean [SD] age, 57.2 [10.3] years; 127 823 [61.0%] female) were included in the analyses
title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.

text: . Compared with continuous smokers, cessation for 8 or more years was associated with a lower risk of all microvascular complications (aHR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.70-0.95), diabetic nephropathy (aHR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.64-0.94), diabetic retinopathy (aHR, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.36-0.97), and diabetic neuropathy (aHR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.66-0.98)
title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.

text: . Smoking cessation for 6 to 7 years was associated with lower risk of diabetic neuropathy (aHR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.64-0.89). In subgroup analyses by sex, these associations were significant only among male participants (eg, all microvascular complications: aHR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.70-0.95)
title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.

text: . In this retrospective cohort study of patients with diabetes, smoking cessation for 8 or more years was associated with a lower risk of all diabetic microvascular complications, diabetic nephropathy, retinopathy, and neuropathy compared with continuous smoking
title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.

text: . These associations were observed mainly among male participants, underscoring the potential importance of sustained long-term smoking cessation for microvascular risk reduction.
title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Diabetic Microvascular Complications.

text: Diabetic Neuropathies.. This article provides an update on the biological mechanisms and risk factors for the varied manifestations of diabetes-associated nerve injury, and reviews current diagnostic and treatment approaches. Diabetic peripheral neuropathy was recently identified as one of the top five leading global neurologic causes of disease burden
title: Diabetic Neuropathies.

text: . Multiple metabolic derangements beyond hyperglycemia, such as the metabolic syndrome, drive diabetic peripheral neuropathy pathogenesis. Social determinants of health are also increasingly seen as important contributors
title: Diabetic Neuropathies.

text: . The biological effects of diabetes are detrimental to both peripheral nerve axons and Schwann cells, and disruptions to the intricate Schwann cell-axon relationship in the diabetic environment are becoming better understood. With improved technology and larger data sets, genetic and epigenetic contributors to diabetic peripheral neuropathy and neuropathic pain are also emerging
title: Diabetic Neuropathies.

text: . Diabetes-associated nerve injury is highly prevalent and results in a marked reduction in quality of life and increased mortality. Despite this disease burden, screening for its many manifestations remains insufficient. Disease-modifying treatments are also limited, necessitating the early implementation of preventative measures
title: Diabetic Neuropathies.

text: . To reduce nerve injury burden in people with diabetes, clinicians must work in multidisciplinary teams and tailor treatments to the patient's symptoms and risk factors.
title: Diabetic Neuropathies.

text: The silent risk: cardiometabolic burden and etiology of young stroke in a South Asian migrant cohort, United Arab Emirates.. Young-adult stroke in the Arabian Gulf remains poorly characterized, despite a resident population dominated by South Asian labor migrants in whom cardiometabolic disease is often under-diagnosed
title: The silent risk: cardiometabolic burden and etiology of young stroke in a South Asian migrant cohort, United Arab Emirates.

text: . We therefore aimed to characterize the etiology and vascular risk-factor burden of young stroke in a single-center United Arab Emirates cohort, testing whether the recorded risk profile reflects true prevalence or diagnostic gaps
title: The silent risk: cardiometabolic burden and etiology of young stroke in a South Asian migrant cohort, United Arab Emirates.

text: . In this retrospective cohort study, we reviewed all patients aged 18-49 years with radiologically confirmed stroke admitted to a secondary-care hospital in Ras Al Khaimah between January 2020 and March 2026, applying adjudicated subtype classification, and used a pre-specified multivariable model to identify factors associated with ischemic presentation
title: The silent risk: cardiometabolic burden and etiology of young stroke in a South Asian migrant cohort, United Arab Emirates.

text: . Of 421 patients screened, 314 met criteria (mean age 41.0 years; 81.2% male; 65.6% South Asian)
title: The silent risk: cardiometabolic burden and etiology of young stroke in a South Asian migrant cohort, United Arab Emirates.

text: . Objectively measured risk far exceeded documented history: only 49.0% had recorded hypertension, yet 74.5% had elevated admission blood pressure; dyslipidemia was documented in 15.9%, yet an abnormal lipid profile was found in 73.9% of those tested; and 29% of all diabetes was first diagnosed at the stroke admission
title: The silent risk: cardiometabolic burden and etiology of young stroke in a South Asian migrant cohort, United Arab Emirates.

text: . Small-vessel occlusion was the leading determined ischemic subtype, and diabetes was the only factor independently associated with ischemic stroke (adjusted OR 2.34, 95% CI 1.35-4.07)
title: The silent risk: cardiometabolic burden and etiology of young stroke in a South Asian migrant cohort, United Arab Emirates.

text: . South Asian patients differed chiefly by sex and ischemic predominance rather than independent metabolic excess, indicating that ethnicity defined the exposed population while diabetes and hypertension were the operative mechanisms
title: The silent risk: cardiometabolic burden and etiology of young stroke in a South Asian migrant cohort, United Arab Emirates.

text: . We conclude that, in this workforce, the low recorded prevalence of vascular risk reflects widespread under-diagnosis, not low true prevalence-stroke was frequently the first presentation of unmanaged cardiometabolic disease, identifying accessible primary care and workplace screening as concrete prevention priorities.
title: The silent risk: cardiometabolic burden and etiology of young stroke in a South Asian migrant cohort, United Arab Emirates.

text: Foot self-care knowledge and behaviors among adults with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional survey in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.. Diabetic foot complications are a major cause of morbidity, disability, and amputation worldwide, yet many complications are preventable through effective self-care
title: Foot self-care knowledge and behaviors among adults with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional survey in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.

text: . Limited evidence is available on foot self-care knowledge and behaviours among adults with diabetes in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates. This study aimed to assess foot self-care knowledge and behaviours and identify factors associated with these outcomes among adults with diabetes mellitus in Ras Al Khaimah
title: Foot self-care knowledge and behaviors among adults with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional survey in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.

text: . A cross-sectional study was conducted among 384 adults with diabetes attending selected primary healthcare centres and the Diabetes Centre at Ibrahim Bin Obaidullah Hospital in Ras Al Khaimah. Participants were selected using convenience sampling
title: Foot self-care knowledge and behaviors among adults with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional survey in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.

text: . Data were collected using a structured validated questionnaire comprising an eight-item knowledge scale and the 29-item Nottingham Assessment of Functional Foot Care. Data were analysed using SPSS version 22. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses. Most participants had poor foot-care knowledge (77.3%)
title: Foot self-care knowledge and behaviors among adults with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional survey in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.

text: . Regarding foot self-care behaviours, 69.3% reported moderate behaviour, 26.0% poor behaviour, and 4.7% good behaviour. Knowledge category was significantly associated with foot self-care behaviour category (χ² = 9.784, p = 0.008; Cramer's V = 0.160)
title: Foot self-care knowledge and behaviors among adults with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional survey in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.

text: . In multivariable logistic regression, females had lower odds of good knowledge than males (AOR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.23-0.90, p = 0.023), and participants with type 2 diabetes had lower odds of good knowledge than those with type 1 diabetes (AOR = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.21-0.87, p = 0.020)
title: Foot self-care knowledge and behaviors among adults with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional survey in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.

text: . In multivariable linear regression, female gender (B = 3.80, 95% CI: 1.99-5.61, p < 0.001), family history of diabetes (B = 1.89, 95% CI: 0.30-3.48, p = 0.020), and knowledge category (B = 1.83, 95% CI: 0.07-3.60, p = 0.041) were positively associated with foot self-care behaviour scores, while educational status (B = -1.57, 95% CI: -2.64 to -0.51, p = 0.004) and history of foot ulcer (B =
title: Foot self-care knowledge and behaviors among adults with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional survey in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.

text: -0.51, p = 0.004) and history of foot ulcer (B = -5.60, 95% CI: -7.81 to -3.38, p < 0.001) were negatively associated
title: Foot self-care knowledge and behaviors among adults with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional survey in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.

text: . Gaps were identified in foot-care knowledge and self-care behaviours among participants. Factors associated with knowledge and foot self-care behaviours should be considered when developing targeted foot-care education and support for adults with diabetes in primary and secondary healthcare settings.
title: Foot self-care knowledge and behaviors among adults with diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional survey in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates.

title: GABA ameliorates diabetic kidney disease-induced podocyte injury via JAML-FPR2 axis-mediated suppression of macrophage infiltration.

text: . In streptozotocin (STZ)-induced DKD mice, GABA administration significantly improved renal function by reducing serum creatinine, urea nitrogen, 24-hour urine protein, attenuated glomerular hypertrophy/mesangial expansion, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine production (TNF-α, IL-1β, iNOS) in renal tissue and serum. GABA inhibited glomerular macrophage infiltration (CD68
title: GABA ameliorates diabetic kidney disease-induced podocyte injury via JAML-FPR2 axis-mediated suppression of macrophage infiltration.

text: From risk classification to clinical action: a prespecified paired pilot benchmark of public large language model interfaces for diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.. Large language models (LLMs) may assist in the prevention of diabetes-related foot ulcers; however, their performance in classification may not translate effectively to context-dependent decisions
title: From risk classification to clinical action: a prespecified paired pilot benchmark of public large language model interfaces for diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.

text: . This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy, clinical actionability, reproducibility, and safety of five public LLM web interfaces in the context of the International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot (IWGDF) 2023 risk stratification and preventive management
title: From risk classification to clinical action: a prespecified paired pilot benchmark of public large language model interfaces for diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.

text: . A prespecified, paired, blinded, noninterventional pilot benchmark was conducted using 20 translated, de-identified, curated cases structured in a fixed clinical sequence and evenly distributed across the four IWGDF risk categories. These input conditions represent an idealized, best-case benchmark rather than routine clinical documentation
title: From risk classification to clinical action: a prespecified paired pilot benchmark of public large language model interfaces for diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.

text: . Each interface assessed all cases under standardized no-search conditions. The primary outcome was exact agreement with a frozen multidisciplinary consensus risk category. Additional outcomes included screening frequency, need for referral, specialty and urgency of referrals, completeness, interreviewer reliability, repeated-generation stability, and safety
title: From risk classification to clinical action: a prespecified paired pilot benchmark of public large language model interfaces for diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.

text: . Each interface classified 20/20 cases in concordance with the frozen IWGDF reference (100%; Wilson 95% CI 83.9%-100.0%). The 16.1-percentage-point interval below the observed ceiling indicates limited precision and remains compatible with clinically meaningful error in new cases
title: From risk classification to clinical action: a prespecified paired pilot benchmark of public large language model interfaces for diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.

text: . Of 100 primary outputs, agreement was observed in 89/100 (89.0%) for referral need, 68/75 (90.7%) for referral specialty, and 92/100 (92.0%) for urgency. Median information-item and mandatory-measure coverage was 100.0% for both measures; however, completeness scoring had limited inter-reviewer reliability and should be interpreted cautiously
title: From risk classification to clinical action: a prespecified paired pilot benchmark of public large language model interfaces for diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.

text: . In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating four-case repeated-generation substudy, all-three-generation consensus concordance was observed in 16/20 interface-case combinations for referral need, 14/15 eligible combinations for specialty, and 19/20 combinations for urgency. These descriptive counts are not estimates of failure probability or tail behavior
title: From risk classification to clinical action: a prespecified paired pilot benchmark of public large language model interfaces for diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.

text: . Under the prespecified curated no-search benchmark conditions, no major safety errors were observed among 140 outputs; this absence of observed events does not establish safety in routine clinical use. Performance was highest for structured guideline mapping, though reliability diminished in referral and individualized management across repeated generations
title: From risk classification to clinical action: a prespecified paired pilot benchmark of public large language model interfaces for diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.

text: . These findings highlight the necessity for auditable, clinician-supervised decision support instead of autonomous deployment.
title: From risk classification to clinical action: a prespecified paired pilot benchmark of public large language model interfaces for diabetes-related foot ulcer prevention.

text: Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes using genomics and proteomics: the HUNT Study (ProtRS for T2D).. Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a multifactorial metabolic disorder with an increasing global prevalence and significant health burdens. Early identification of individuals at high risk is crucial for timely intervention and prevention of T2D and complications
title: Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes using genomics and proteomics: the HUNT Study (ProtRS for T2D).
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

text: . This study aims to investigate the association between the blood plasma proteome and T2D, identify protein biomarkers associated with incident T2D, and explore the underlying biological pathways involved in the disease development in the Trøndelag Health Study (HUNT). The HUNT Study is a population-based cohort with four waves of enrolment beginning in 1984
title: Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes using genomics and proteomics: the HUNT Study (ProtRS for T2D).
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

text: . Samples from HUNT3 were analysed with SomaScan including 3,221 using SomaScanv4.0 (HUNT-Soma5k, ∼5,000 proteins) and 2,181 on SomaScanv4.1 (HUNT-Soma7k, ∼7,000 proteins)
title: Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes using genomics and proteomics: the HUNT Study (ProtRS for T2D).
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

text: . We performed logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) to generate the protein risk scores, and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) to identify potential biological pathways for incident T2D. We identified 313 (308 proteins) and 142 (128 proteins) aptamers that are significantly associated with incident T2D, in HUNT-Soma5k and HUNT-Soma7k, respectively
title: Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes using genomics and proteomics: the HUNT Study (ProtRS for T2D).
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

text: . In HUNT-Soma5k, MXRA8 has strongest association with decreased risk and PLXB2 has strongest association with increased risk; while IGFBP2 has strongest association with decreased risk and INHBC has strongest association with increased risk for incident T2D in HUNT-Soma7k. The most significant pathway from GO Biological Process is organic acid metabolic process in both datasets
title: Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes using genomics and proteomics: the HUNT Study (ProtRS for T2D).
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

text: . The associated proteins and biological pathways identified represent insights into the underlying molecular mechanism of T2D and may serve as potential biomarkers for risk prediction and prevention for T2D. Type 2 diabetes (T2D) leads to substantial morbidity, including cardiovascular, renal, and neurological complications
title: Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes using genomics and proteomics: the HUNT Study (ProtRS for T2D).
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

text: . Identifying individuals at elevated risk before clinical onset is essential, as early intervention can prevent progression from pre-diabetes and support timely lifestyle modification. In this study, we evaluated circulating proteins as predictors of future T2D using high-throughput, targeted proteomics
title: Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes using genomics and proteomics: the HUNT Study (ProtRS for T2D).
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

text: . We identified hundreds of proteins associated with incident T2D, including 10 proteins not previously reported in other cohorts. These findings may enhance early risk prediction and inform more personalized prevention strategies.
title: Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes using genomics and proteomics: the HUNT Study (ProtRS for T2D).
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

text: Plasma Proteomic Signatures for Early Risk Stratification Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Stages 0-2.. Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stages 0-2 represent a potentially modifiable period before overt cardiovascular complications, yet molecular markers that identify individuals at higher downstream risk remain insufficiently defined
title: Plasma Proteomic Signatures for Early Risk Stratification Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Stages 0-2.

text: . We investigated whether plasma proteomic signatures could characterize early CKM-related molecular risk and improve prediction of incident cardiovascular, kidney and mortality outcomes. We analysed 43 709 UK Biobank participants with CKM stages 0-2 and measurements of 2920 plasma proteins
title: Plasma Proteomic Signatures for Early Risk Stratification Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Stages 0-2.

text: . Multivariable Cox models evaluated protein associations with 11 incident outcomes after excluding participants with the corresponding condition at baseline
title: Plasma Proteomic Signatures for Early Risk Stratification Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Stages 0-2.

text: . We further assessed modelled prediagnostic protein patterns, stage-related proteomic patterns across baseline CKM stage groups, and the incremental value of outcome-specific and recurrent protein panels beyond clinical models using Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT)-aligned covariates
title: Plasma Proteomic Signatures for Early Risk Stratification Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Stages 0-2.

text: . A total of 157 proteins showed directionally concordant associations across all 11 outcomes, including 155 positive and 2 inverse associations. Population-level models across time-to-outcome intervals identified differences in GDF15, TNFRSF10B, WFDC2 and NT-proBNP between incident cases and matched reference participants
title: Plasma Proteomic Signatures for Early Risk Stratification Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Stages 0-2.

text: . Eleven of the 155 proteins with positive associations across all 11 outcomes were consistently elevated across baseline CKM stage groups 0-2. title: Plasma Proteomic Signatures for Early Risk Stratification Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Stages 0-2.

title: Plasma Proteomic Signatures for Early Risk Stratification Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Stages 0-2.

Augmented reality-assisted Tai Chi for adults with diabetes-associated cognitive impairment: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.. Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (DACI) undermines diabetes self-management and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality
title: Augmented reality-assisted Tai Chi for adults with diabetes-associated cognitive impairment: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.

text: . Although mind-body exercise may improve cognition, its benefits are often limited by the lack of timely, precise, individualised instruction and feedback in adults with cognitive impairment. Augmented reality (AR) systems can deliver performance-adaptive, visually anchored cues and auditory prompts in real-world settings, but their cognitive and metabolic benefits in DACI remain unknown
title: Augmented reality-assisted Tai Chi for adults with diabetes-associated cognitive impairment: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.

text: . This trial will compare AR-assisted Tai Chi (iTaiChi), instructor-led Tai Chi (TaiChi) and standard care in adults with DACI and explore underlying metabolic and neurobiological mechanisms
title: Augmented reality-assisted Tai Chi for adults with diabetes-associated cognitive impairment: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.

text: . In this randomised controlled trial, 246 community-dwelling adults aged 45-75 years with DACI will be enrolled and randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio to a TaiChi group, an iTaiChi group or a standard care group. All participants will receive standard care
title: Augmented reality-assisted Tai Chi for adults with diabetes-associated cognitive impairment: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.

text: . All participants will receive standard care. In addition, participants assigned to the two exercise groups will undertake a standardised Yang-style 24-form Tai Chi programme three times weekly for 12 weeks. The primary outcome is the change in Montreal Cognitive Assessment Score. Secondary outcomes include physical health related parameters and brain health related parameters
title: Augmented reality-assisted Tai Chi for adults with diabetes-associated cognitive impairment: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.

text: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.. Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of vision loss among working-age adults worldwide
title: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . AI-assisted automated image reading has effectively alleviated the human resource challenges in large-scale remote screenings, yet there is limited analysis on the impact of complex ocular factors on the diagnostic efficacy of AI
title: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . This study aimed to systematically analyze the impact of multiple ocular factors on the diagnostic efficacy of the EVisionAI system in detecting DR and vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy (VTDR) during large-scale screening of residents with diabetes in resource-limited regions
title: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . This cross-sectional study used a multistage stratified random sampling method to screen residents with type 2 diabetes at primary health centers in resource-limited regions
title: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Data collection involved structured questionnaires (for basic and disease information), hemoglobin A Between October 21 and November 12, 2024, 1847 participants with type 2 diabetes (aged 32-91 years) were enrolled, of whom 1748 (94.6%) completed the screening process and 3392 eyes were eligible for DR analysis
title: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Participants had a mean age of 67.17 (SD 8.52) years and mean diabetes duration of 9.13 (SD 6.97) years, with 19.2% (335/1748) having DR and 7.4% (129/1748) having VTDR
title: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Although EVisionAI's diagnostic efficacy was comparable to that of ophthalmologists (sensitivity: 90.61%, 95% CI 87.89%-92.79%; specificity: 98.99%, 95% CI 98.52%-99.31%), some ocular factors-including pupil size, refractive media opacity, and tessellated fundus (TF)-significantly impaired its efficiency
title: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Severe refractive media opacity and TF reduced its sensitivity to 80.95% and 82.86%, respectively, and these factors interfered more with early-stage DR detection than VTDR (97.45% detected), particularly in eyes with severe TF changes (sensitivity decreased to 60.71%). Most notably, severe vitreous degeneration-induced opacity almost invariably led to VTDR misdiagnosis
title: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Additionally, pupil dilation improved the sensitivity of EVisionAI for diagnosing DR (excluding early-stage DR) but had minimal impact on specificity. EVisionAI achieved high diagnostic accuracy for large-scale DR screening in resource-limited regions, yet its performance for early-stage disease was diminished by severe ocular factors
title: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Optimizing for these factors is therefore essential to maximize its clinical utility in primary care settings with limited specialist access.
title: Ocular Factors Affecting AI Diagnosis in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening for Resource-Limited Regions: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: Clinical Burden of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Jordanian Patients with Diabetes: A 11-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.. Peripheral neuropathy is among the complications associated with diabetes and is often accompanied by numbness, which can cause tissue damage and lead to the formation of diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs)
title: Clinical Burden of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Jordanian Patients with Diabetes: A 11-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . This research aimed to investigate the prevalence and clinical outcomes of DFU among diabetic patients in Jordan. A retrospective longitudinal cohort study was conducted between January 2013 and December 2023. All patients with DFU attending the University of Jordan Hospital and above 18 years of age were retrospectively followed up for at least one year
title: Clinical Burden of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Jordanian Patients with Diabetes: A 11-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . Mortality rates were considered as secondary outcomes. A total of 3131 DFU patients were identified, with 1648 inpatients and 1483 outpatients. Overall, the cumulative percentage of the prevalence of DFU during the 11 years was 6.57%
title: Clinical Burden of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Jordanian Patients with Diabetes: A 11-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . DFUs were found to have increased the length of stay in hospitals (mean = 9.46 days), a high number of complicated cases of ulcers with infections: Inpatient (37.2%), outpatient (25.3%); and significant amputations: minor amputations (20.4%), major amputations (12.4%). The prevalence of infected ulcers among DFU patients was 12.2%
title: Clinical Burden of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Jordanian Patients with Diabetes: A 11-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . The mean survival time was 70.4 days (±3.3), with a 95% confidence interval of 64.0 to 76.9 days. The number of conditions, including gangrene, myocardial infarction, kidney disease, retinopathy, and neuropathy, were marginally linked to increased mortality risks
title: Clinical Burden of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Jordanian Patients with Diabetes: A 11-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . Despite the progress that has been achieved in the management and treatment of diabetes, the frequent hospitalizations, infections, and limb amputations that occur as a result of DFUs underscore the importance of effective management and prevention of the disease.
title: Clinical Burden of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Jordanian Patients with Diabetes: A 11-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: Improving Pediatric Glycemic Control with Smart Insulin Pens: The Current Trends and Future Prospects.. Pediatric diabetes management remains challenging, as many young patients struggle to hit glycemic targets due to developmental factors and treatment burdens
title: Improving Pediatric Glycemic Control with Smart Insulin Pens: The Current Trends and Future Prospects.

text: . Smart insulin pens are a game-changing "connected MDI" alternative, with "pump-like" features such as bolus calculators and automated Insulin-on-Board tracking for non-pump users. This review explores the clinical effectiveness, economic impact, and prospects of SIPs in pediatrics, including patient and caregiver insights and long-term effects on glycemic control
title: Improving Pediatric Glycemic Control with Smart Insulin Pens: The Current Trends and Future Prospects.

text: . Caregivers and patients agree SIPs are accessible and easy to use due to user-friendly interfaces, data-driven approaches, and remote monitoring. Evidence shows SIPs improve safety and adherence, with a 31.4% reduction in daily hypoglycemia, a 24.4% decrease in nocturnal hypoglycemia, and a drop in Time Below Range Level 2 from 2.82% to 2.18%
title: Improving Pediatric Glycemic Control with Smart Insulin Pens: The Current Trends and Future Prospects.

text: . By tracking insulin-on-board, SIPs prevent insulin stacking and enable safe correction doses; users correcting within three hours of a previous dose spend more time in range without increased hypoglycemia. SIPs also cut missed boluses by up to 43% in youth. Economically, SIPs save about SEK 124,270 per patient by delaying complications
title: Improving Pediatric Glycemic Control with Smart Insulin Pens: The Current Trends and Future Prospects.

text: . However, adoption remains limited due to socioeconomic barriers, with 82% of clinics citing insurance issues and lower use among Medicaid beneficiaries. Barriers include the learning curve and device costs, which can be addressed through subsidies and training programs. Future AI developments, like hypoglycemia prediction, promise to further personalize pediatric care
title: Improving Pediatric Glycemic Control with Smart Insulin Pens: The Current Trends and Future Prospects.

text: . Overall, SIPs benefit pediatric diabetes management, but more research, including clinical trials, is needed to confirm optimal outcomes.
title: Improving Pediatric Glycemic Control with Smart Insulin Pens: The Current Trends and Future Prospects.

text: Artificial intelligence driven prognostic models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review.. Diabetic retinopathy remains a leading cause of preventable blindness among individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus and is driven by the increasing global burden of diabetes
title: Artificial intelligence driven prognostic models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review.

text: . Early identification of individuals at high risk is essential for timely intervention. In recent years, artificial intelligence, including machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising approach for prognostic modelling. However, evidence on artificial intelligence-driven models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk remains fragmented
title: Artificial intelligence driven prognostic models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review.

text: . This systematic review aims to synthesise current evidence on artificial intelligence-driven prognostic models for predicting the risk of diabetic retinopathy among individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus, focusing on model characteristics, predictor variables, performance, and validation strategies
title: Artificial intelligence driven prognostic models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review.

text: . A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect was performed for studies published between January 2016 and December 2025. Eligible studies included those applying artificial intelligence-based models for diabetic retinopathy risk prediction in adult populations with type 2 diabetes mellitus and reporting model performance metrics
title: Artificial intelligence driven prognostic models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review.

text: . Data were extracted and synthesised narratively, and methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. A total of 1040 records were identified, with eight studies included after screening. A wide range of artificial intelligence algorithms was applied, with ensemble models such as extreme gradient boosting and random forest demonstrating superior performance
title: Artificial intelligence driven prognostic models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review.

text: . Key predictors consistently included glycated haemoglobin levels, duration of diabetes, blood pressure, lipid profile, and renal function markers, alongside emerging metabolomic biomarkers. Model performance ranged from moderate to excellent, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values between 0.68 and 0.97
title: Artificial intelligence driven prognostic models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review.

text: . Most studies employed internal validation techniques such as cross-validation or training and testing data splits, while external validation was largely absent. Overall methodological quality was high, although variability in study design, predictor selection, and reporting was observed
title: Artificial intelligence driven prognostic models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review.

text: . Artificial intelligence-driven prognostic models show substantial potential in predicting diabetic retinopathy risk among individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus, particularly through the integration of clinical and highdimensional data
title: Artificial intelligence driven prognostic models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review.

text: . Despite promising predictive performance, limitations in external validation, heterogeneity, and reporting of clinical utility hinder translation into practice. Future research should prioritise external validation, standardised reporting frameworks, and clinically interpretable models to enhance applicability in real-world healthcare settings.
title: Artificial intelligence driven prognostic models for predicting diabetic retinopathy risk in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review.

text: Assessment of Glycemic Control Among Prospective Hajj Pilgrims With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Tangerang City, Indonesia.. Diabetes Mellitus Type 2 (T2DM) is a significant health concern for Hajj pilgrims, with glycaemic control crucial for their well-being during the pilgrimage

More than 50% of Hajj pilgrims with T2DM had comorbid conditions such as hypertension, cardiomegaly, and hyperlipidaemia

journal: Journal of the ASEAN Federation of Endocrine Societies

text: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are widely used in tumor therapy, and the immune-related adverse events (irAEs) they induce can involve multiple organs
title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.

text: . As an organ with both endocrine and exocrine functions, pancreatic involvement may manifest as acute pancreatitis, new-onset diabetes mellitus, or even a combination of both. Among these, ICI-induced acute pancreatitis concurrent with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus (FT1DM) is extremely rare but highly critical and easily missed in clinical practice
title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.

text: . A 59-year-old male patient with squamous cell carcinoma of the left base of the tongue received toripalimab combined with chemotherapy. On day 7 after treatment, he presented with nausea, vomiting, and altered mental status
title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.

text: . Emergency examination revealed hyperglycemia (17.4 mmol/L), severe diabetic ketoacidosis (blood ketones 9.52 mmol/L, pH 7.28), and significantly elevated serum amylase (370 U/L). Abdominal CT showed swelling of the body and tail of the pancreas with surrounding exudation, consistent with acute pancreatitis
title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.

text: . His glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) was normal (5.4%), pancreatic autoantibodies were negative, and islet function was completely lost. He was diagnosed with toripalimab-associated acute pancreatitis (Grade 3) concurrent with FT1DM. ICIs were permanently discontinued immediately
title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.

text: . ICIs were permanently discontinued immediately. The patient was treated with fasting, fluid replacement, somatostatin to inhibit pancreatic enzyme secretion, and intensive insulin pump therapy for glycemic control. Glucocorticoids were not administered
title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.

text: . Glucocorticoids were not administered. After 11 days of comprehensive treatment, his symptoms resolved, and he was discharged upon normalization of pancreatic enzymes and blood glucose levels. PD-1 inhibitors can simultaneously impair both the endocrine and exocrine functions of the pancreas, leading to the coexistence of acute pancreatitis and FT1DM
title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.

text: . Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion for this dual injury. For patients receiving ICI therapy, emergency evaluation of pancreatic function is warranted once gastrointestinal symptoms or unexplained hyperglycemia/ketosis occur. Early drug withdrawal and individualized management centered on supportive care can effectively prevent life-threatening complications
title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.

text: . Notably, this case represents the first report of such dual pancreatic injury in a patient with locally advanced tongue base squamous cell carcinoma receiving first-cycle toripalimab combined with paclitaxel plus cisplatin chemoimmunotherapy, with distinct atypical clinical manifestations and a faster steroid-free recovery trajectory compared with the single previously published
title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.

text: compared with the single previously published toripalimab-associated case.
title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pancreatitis with fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report.

text: Identification of risk factors for type 2 diabetes across age-based proxies of early and late postmenopausal stages in prediabetic women.. Prediabetes is increasingly prevalent, and women transitioning through menopause may face a particularly elevated risk of progressing to type 2 diabetes (T2DM)
title: Identification of risk factors for type 2 diabetes across age-based proxies of early and late postmenopausal stages in prediabetic women.

text: . Estrogen deficiency promotes adiposity, insulin resistance, and inflammation, potentially amplifying the metabolic burden of aging. However, the determinants of T2DM in these women remain insufficiently characterized. This retrospective study included 229 prediabetic women evaluated at a tertiary-care hospital and followed for up to 5.5 years
title: Identification of risk factors for type 2 diabetes across age-based proxies of early and late postmenopausal stages in prediabetic women.

text: . Prediabetes was defined according to ADA criteria and women were classified as premenopausal (< 51 years), early postmenopausal (51-60 years), or late postmenopausal (> 60 years). Clinical and biochemical variables were analyzed for hazard ratios (HR) of T2DM using Cox regression, and Kaplan-Meier curves. During follow-up, 18% of premenopausal and 35% of postmenopausal women developed T2DM
title: Identification of risk factors for type 2 diabetes across age-based proxies of early and late postmenopausal stages in prediabetic women.

text: . Higher BMI predicted T2DM in both groups. In postmenopausal women, IGT (HR: 2.59), hypertension (HR: 3.91), lower HDL-C (HR: 0.96), lower vitamin D (HR: 0.93), and reduced eGFR (HR: 0.97) were independently associated with T2DM. Stratification revealed that early post-menopause carried the highest incidence of T2DM
title: Identification of risk factors for type 2 diabetes across age-based proxies of early and late postmenopausal stages in prediabetic women.

text: . In early post-menopause, higher BMI and uric acid, and lower vitamin D were independent predictors, whereas in late post-menopause, hypertension and reduced eGFR were the strongest determinants. Risk Factors associated with progression to T2DM in prediabetic women appear to differ across age-defined menopausal stages
title: Identification of risk factors for type 2 diabetes across age-based proxies of early and late postmenopausal stages in prediabetic women.

text: . Excess adiposity remains a key factor, whereas early post-menopause is characterized by additional associations with hyperuricemia and vitamin D deficiency. In late post-menopause, hypertension and declining renal function appear to be more prominent. These findings support stage-specific risk assessment and tailored preventive strategies in prediabetic women.
title: Identification of risk factors for type 2 diabetes across age-based proxies of early and late postmenopausal stages in prediabetic women.

text: Risk Factor Analysis of Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Diabetic Kidney Disease and Hypertension: A Retrospective Study.. journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)

text: . Although traditional risk factors such as dyslipidemia, smoking, and decreased renal function have been shown to be associated with increased cardiovascular events, evidence for the higher-risk subgroup of "DKD with hypertension" remains relatively limited
title: Risk Factor Analysis of Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Diabetic Kidney Disease and Hypertension: A Retrospective Study.
journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)

text: .
