text: A dual-modal optical probe for photoacoustic and urine detection of NE activity in atherosclerosis and diabetic complications.. Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease of the arterial wall, and neutrophil elastase (NE) has emerged as a key mediator of plaque inflammation and destabilization
title: A dual-modal optical probe for photoacoustic and urine detection of NE activity in atherosclerosis and diabetic complications.

text: . In this study, an NE-activatable hemicyanine-based optical probe (NP) was designed and synthesized. Upon specific cleavage by NE, significant activation of absorption, fluorescence, and photoacoustic signals was achieved. In vitro experiments confirmed excellent NE responsiveness, high selectivity, and favorable stability
title: A dual-modal optical probe for photoacoustic and urine detection of NE activity in atherosclerosis and diabetic complications.

text: . In vivo studies demonstrated dual hepatic and renal metabolic pathways with good biosafety. The application potential of NP was investigated in three mouse models: healthy controls, atherosclerotic (AS) mice fed a high-fat diet, and AS mice with concurrent diabetes (AS+DM) induced by low-dose streptozotocin
title: A dual-modal optical probe for photoacoustic and urine detection of NE activity in atherosclerosis and diabetic complications.

text: . Using photoacoustic imaging, NP sensitively detected increased NE activity within aortic plaques and renal tissues, with the AS+DM group exhibiting the highest signal enhancement. Urine fluorescence analysis further validated the non-invasive diagnostic potential. Collectively, NP represents a promising optical tool for the assessment of plaque inflammation and atherosclerotic disease burden.
title: A dual-modal optical probe for photoacoustic and urine detection of NE activity in atherosclerosis and diabetic complications.

text: Adolescent Obesity: A Stepwise Clinical Approach.. Adolescent obesity is one of the most pressing pediatric public health challenges of this generation, with a near tripling of prevalence over three decades. Most adolescents with obesity have an exogenous cause, but a small proportion harbor pathological causes that warrant timely recognition
title: Adolescent Obesity: A Stepwise Clinical Approach.

text: . The Indian context is distinctive as complications develop at lower BMI thresholds, low birth weight and a family history of type 2 diabetes are key predictors of metabolic risk, and metabolically healthy obesity is observed in around 40% of obese children
title: Adolescent Obesity: A Stepwise Clinical Approach.

text: . Stepwise evaluation distinguishing exogenous from pathological causes, followed by screening for metabolic and mechanical complications, provides cost-effective assessment. Management combines structured lifestyle change with judicious pharmacotherapy and bariatric surgery in carefully selected adolescents
title: Adolescent Obesity: A Stepwise Clinical Approach.

text: . Prevention strategies anchored in early-life nutrition, physical activity, sleep, and screen-time regulation remain the cornerstone of long-term control.
title: Adolescent Obesity: A Stepwise Clinical Approach.

text: A comparative evaluation of generative AI chatbots for patient-oriented advice on painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy: safety, accuracy, guideline concordance, actionability, and readability.
title: A comparative evaluation of generative AI chatbots for patient-oriented advice on painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy: safety, accuracy, guideline concordance, actionability, and readability.

text: . Patients with painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (PDPN) increasingly use generative artificial intelligence chatbots for information on symptoms, treatment, foot care, and when to seek professional help. Their usefulness depends on safety, accuracy, guideline concordance, actionability, and readability
title: A comparative evaluation of generative AI chatbots for patient-oriented advice on painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy: safety, accuracy, guideline concordance, actionability, and readability.

text: . To compare five publicly accessible generative AI chatbots in answering standardized patient-oriented questions about PDPN. Methods: Sixty standardized English-language questions covering eight clinical domains were submitted once to ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek, and Doubao in separate single-turn conversations, yielding 300 responses
title: A comparative evaluation of generative AI chatbots for patient-oriented advice on painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy: safety, accuracy, guideline concordance, actionability, and readability.

text: . Five reviewers independently assessed safety, accuracy, guideline concordance, and actionability using predefined criteria. Guideline concordance was scored against six mapped elements per question and converted to a percentage. Actionability was assessed using seven binary criteria with prespecified question-level applicability. Readability was evaluated using six established indices
title: A comparative evaluation of generative AI chatbots for patient-oriented advice on painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy: safety, accuracy, guideline concordance, actionability, and readability.

text: . Paired comparisons used Cochran's Q test for safety and Friedman tests for non-binary outcomes, followed by multiplicity-adjusted pairwise analyses. All 300 responses were analyzed. Inter-rater agreement was high for safety (Fleiss'  The five chatbots showed distinct performance patterns across content quality and readability
title: A comparative evaluation of generative AI chatbots for patient-oriented advice on painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy: safety, accuracy, guideline concordance, actionability, and readability.

text: . Although no overall safety difference was detected, every system generated at least one response with a plausible pathway to inappropriate self-management, delayed assessment, medication or product misuse, or preventable injury. Chatbots may support general patient education, but medication decisions, foot-risk assessment, and urgent-care triage require professional verification.
title: A comparative evaluation of generative AI chatbots for patient-oriented advice on painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy: safety, accuracy, guideline concordance, actionability, and readability.

text: Herpes Zoster in Aging Patients: Risk Factors and Prevention Strategies.. Herpes zoster (HZ), also known as shingles, is caused by varicella-zoster virus reactivation and can lead to long-term complications such as postherpetic neuralgia (PHN). Risk of HZ and related complications increases with age, presence of chronic conditions, and immunosuppression
title: Herpes Zoster in Aging Patients: Risk Factors and Prevention Strategies.

text: . The United States (US) has an increasingly aging and multimorbid population; therefore, knowledge of risk factors and prevention opportunities for HZ are of critical importance to inform broad efforts to prevent this disease. To consolidate information on risk factors for adults aged ≥50 years and opportunities to address gaps in HZ prevention, a narrative review was conducted
title: Herpes Zoster in Aging Patients: Risk Factors and Prevention Strategies.

text: . In addition to well-known risk factors for HZ, such as immunocompromising conditions and immunosuppressive treatments, this review highlights risk factors less recognized in the existing literature
title: Herpes Zoster in Aging Patients: Risk Factors and Prevention Strategies.

text: . These risk factors (which include certain cardiovascular and chronic respiratory conditions, as well as diabetes, chronic kidney disease, end-stage kidney disease [ESKD], and multimorbidity) are pertinent to comprehensive preventive care
title: Herpes Zoster in Aging Patients: Risk Factors and Prevention Strategies.

text: . Several studies identified increased risks of adverse HZ outcomes, including PHN and functional decline during and following HZ episodes, in adults aged ≥50 years, with risk usually exacerbated by underlying medical conditions
title: Herpes Zoster in Aging Patients: Risk Factors and Prevention Strategies.

text: . Observational studies have shown that patients with HZ were at increased risk for certain acute cardiovascular disease events (e.g, major adverse cardiovascular events and post-herpetic cerebrovascular accidents), especially in the weeks and months following HZ
title: Herpes Zoster in Aging Patients: Risk Factors and Prevention Strategies.

text: . For US adults aged ≥50 years and immunocompromised adults aged ≥19 years, the recombinant zoster vaccine is recommended for the prevention of HZ by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. However, gaps in prevention remain
title: Herpes Zoster in Aging Patients: Risk Factors and Prevention Strategies.

text: . However, gaps in prevention remain. Opportunities exist to improve HZ prevention in adults aged ≥50 years, particularly among those with comorbidities, by expanding medical societies' dissemination tactics for vaccination guidelines and recommendations, and empowering specialists to both incorporate risk assessment into routine care and encourage vaccination guideline adherence.
title: Herpes Zoster in Aging Patients: Risk Factors and Prevention Strategies.

text: Perioperative cognitive dysfunction in bladder cancer patients, causal factors, and possible interventions.. Bladder cancer (BC) primarily necessitates surgical and oncological interventions; however, patients frequently encounter a substantial burden of perioperative neurocognitive disorders, which compromise clinical outcomes and treatment compliance
title: Perioperative cognitive dysfunction in bladder cancer patients, causal factors, and possible interventions.

text: . While individual risks are recognized, a comprehensive synthesis identifying the overlapping clinical determinants and promoters of this decline remains essential. This review aims to elucidate the specific mechanisms underlying perioperative cognitive impairment in surgical BC patients and highlight targeted preventive strategies
title: Perioperative cognitive dysfunction in bladder cancer patients, causal factors, and possible interventions.

text: . Evidence demonstrates that perioperative cognitive decline in this population is highly multifactorial. Key demographic and clinical predictors include advanced age and clinical frailty, which are compounded by chronic cerebral small vessel disease secondary to long-term tobacco smoking, hypertension, and metabolic diseases
title: Perioperative cognitive dysfunction in bladder cancer patients, causal factors, and possible interventions.

text: . Furthermore, surgical and procedural risks, such as frequent instrumentation and catheterization, are associated with bleeding and a higher incidence of recurrent urinary tract infections, which induce systemic inflammation and may precipitate acute disorientation or delirium
title: Perioperative cognitive dysfunction in bladder cancer patients, causal factors, and possible interventions.

text: . Anesthesia-related factors, including preoperative benzodiazepine use, intraoperative hypotension, prolonged anesthesia duration, and the omission of neuromuscular blockade reversal agents, significantly exacerbate post-surgical cognitive vulnerability. All these factors, with systemic inflammation, may cause cerebral hypoperfusion that precipitates delirium
title: Perioperative cognitive dysfunction in bladder cancer patients, causal factors, and possible interventions.

text: . Metabolic comorbidities, particularly diabetes mellitus, synergistically exacerbate infection risks, while psychological distress (severe anxiety and depression) and neurotoxic chemotherapy protocols serve as vital indicators of post-surgical cognitive vulnerability. Cognitive function heavily dictates urological care trajectories
title: Perioperative cognitive dysfunction in bladder cancer patients, causal factors, and possible interventions.

text: . Incorporating routine, structured preoperative cognitive and frailty screenings is imperative to risk-stratify patients, implement tailored pre-habilitation, and optimize both cognitive and oncological outcomes.
title: Perioperative cognitive dysfunction in bladder cancer patients, causal factors, and possible interventions.

text: Moisturizer formulations for diabetic foot xerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.. Foot xerosis in people with diabetes increases the risk of skin fissuring, ulceration and complications like amputation, sepsis and death. Preventive skin care is therefore important, yet evidence-based guidance on the most effective formulations remains limited
title: Moisturizer formulations for diabetic foot xerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
journal: Frontiers in clinical diabetes and healthcare

text: . This systematic review aimed to identify effective ingredients and formulations to treat diabetic foot xerosis. A literature search was conducted in Medline, Cinahl, Embase, CENTRAL and Scopus. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving adults with diabetes and foot xerosis (without ulcers) that compared topical formulations were eligible
title: Moisturizer formulations for diabetic foot xerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
journal: Frontiers in clinical diabetes and healthcare

text: . Reviewers screened studies, extracted data, assessed risk of bias and certainty of evidence in accordance with Cochrane Intervention Review standards. Outcomes included xerosis severity, skin hydration, skin barrier integrity and adverse events. Meta-analyses of RCTs were conducted. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024579919). Eleven articles reporting twelve RCTs were included
title: Moisturizer formulations for diabetic foot xerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
journal: Frontiers in clinical diabetes and healthcare

text: . Functional creams (i.e., base formulations with added ingredients, most commonly humectants, intended to enhance their effect) significantly reduced xerosis severity compared with standard base formulations after both two weeks (standardized mean difference [SMD] -0.58, 95% CI -1.05 to -0.11) and four weeks (SMD -0.30, 95% CI -0.46 to -0.14). text: Surgical repair of femoral artery access complications: a comparison of hemorrhagic and occlusive injuries.. To evaluate outcomes following surgical repair of common femoral artery (CFA) access complications and compare hemorrhagic and occlusive injuries
title: Surgical repair of femoral artery access complications: a comparison of hemorrhagic and occlusive injuries.

title: Surgical repair of femoral artery access complications: a comparison of hemorrhagic and occlusive injuries.

Among 172 patients undergoing surgical CFA repair, 100 (58.1%) had hemorrhagic and 72 (41.9%) occlusive injuries
title: Surgical repair of femoral artery access complications: a comparison of hemorrhagic and occlusive injuries.

text: . Among 149 patients with available follow-up, 42.3% developed a groin wound complication and 28.2% developed a CDC-defined infection. Infection rates were significantly higher following hemorrhagic compared with occlusive injury (34.9% vs 19.7%; P = .040)
title: Surgical repair of femoral artery access complications: a comparison of hemorrhagic and occlusive injuries.

text: . title: Surgical repair of femoral artery access complications: a comparison of hemorrhagic and occlusive injuries.

text: . In multivariable analysis, hemorrhagic injury and BMI ≥30 were independently associated with 90-day SSI of the groin. Surgical repair of CFA access complications is associated with substantial postoperative morbidity, particularly wound infection
title: Surgical repair of femoral artery access complications: a comparison of hemorrhagic and occlusive injuries.

text: . Hemorrhagic injuries represent a high-risk subgroup and should be considered distinct from occlusive injuries, warranting tailored treatment and preventive strategies.

text: Nutritional Deficiencies, Complications, and Nutrition Therapy/Counseling in Pediatric Patients Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used to treat childhood obesity, prediabetes, and type 2 diabetes. We examined nutritional deficiency incidence and nutrition therapy/counseling (NT/C) utilization among pediatric GLP-1RA users
title: Nutritional Deficiencies, Complications, and Nutrition Therapy/Counseling in Pediatric Patients Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . We analyzed Inovalon administrative claims data from 2017 to 2022 covering over 100 million patients to identify 2,031 GLP-1RA users aged 10-17 years who met continuous enrollment criteria and had no prior diagnosis of nutritional deficiency
title: Nutritional Deficiencies, Complications, and Nutrition Therapy/Counseling in Pediatric Patients Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . Nutritional deficiencies were identified using the International Classification of Diseases, 10th edition codes for up to 1 year following GLP-1RA initiation. NT/C visits, time to first NT/C visit, and differences in nutritional deficiency diagnoses by NT/C consultation were assessed. Results are reported as proportions and means, with group comparisons using chi-square tests
title: Nutritional Deficiencies, Complications, and Nutrition Therapy/Counseling in Pediatric Patients Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . The mean age was 15 (±1.8) years, 61.5% were female, and 62.6% had obesity. Liraglutide (78.6%), dulaglutide (10.4%), and semaglutide (9.1%) were the most prescribed GLP-1RA drugs
title: Nutritional Deficiencies, Complications, and Nutrition Therapy/Counseling in Pediatric Patients Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . Within 1 year, 16.88% of patients were diagnosed with at least one nutritional deficiency or deficiency-related complication, most frequently vitamin D deficiency (12.4%), followed by nutritional anemia (1.55%), and iron-deficiency anemia (1.44%). Only 23.3% had NT/C visit within 180 days (mean time to first visit: 149 days)
title: Nutritional Deficiencies, Complications, and Nutrition Therapy/Counseling in Pediatric Patients Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . Patients with NT/C consultations had higher rates of nutritional deficiencies and deficiency-related complications than those without (23.2% vs. 14.8%,  Nutritional deficiencies are a meaningful and under-recognized risk among pediatric patients receiving GLP-1RA therapy. Current care patterns suggest missed opportunities for proactive and preventative nutrition support
title: Nutritional Deficiencies, Complications, and Nutrition Therapy/Counseling in Pediatric Patients Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . Integration of NT/C care into pediatric GLP-1RA treatment may support healthy growth and long-term outcomes.
title: Nutritional Deficiencies, Complications, and Nutrition Therapy/Counseling in Pediatric Patients Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: Redefining weight management after liver transplantation with glucagon-like peptide one and gastric inhibitory polypeptide receptor agonists.. Obesity is a challenging complication that many liver transplant recipients face
title: Redefining weight management after liver transplantation with glucagon-like peptide one and gastric inhibitory polypeptide receptor agonists.

text: . Liver transplantation is the sole life-saving procedure in many end-stage liver diseases, but the underlying pathology, in addition to some immunosuppressive regimens, may worsen the metabolic status of many patients
title: Redefining weight management after liver transplantation with glucagon-like peptide one and gastric inhibitory polypeptide receptor agonists.

text: . A comprehensive management plan to prevent further metabolic complications, like metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, chronic renal dysfunction, and diabetes, is essential to obtain a favourable prognosis and a better quality of life
title: Redefining weight management after liver transplantation with glucagon-like peptide one and gastric inhibitory polypeptide receptor agonists.

text: . glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and GLP-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonists have been approved for long-term weight management by the United States Food and Drug Administration and other regulatory authorities. While this pharmacotherapeutic intervention revolutionised obesity management, it comes with many limitations
title: Redefining weight management after liver transplantation with glucagon-like peptide one and gastric inhibitory polypeptide receptor agonists.

text: . Their long-term safety profile, optimal dosing, duration of treatment and outcomes are still insufficiently studied, specifically in the transplant recipient population
title: Redefining weight management after liver transplantation with glucagon-like peptide one and gastric inhibitory polypeptide receptor agonists.

text: . This review aims to explore the pathophysiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, and burden of metabolic complications in liver transplant recipients and to review available data on the potential use of GLP-1 and GLP-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonists in mitigating these complications among this vulnerable population.
title: Redefining weight management after liver transplantation with glucagon-like peptide one and gastric inhibitory polypeptide receptor agonists.

text: Impact of Clinical Factors on Bone Microarchitecture in Patients with Turner Syndrome.. Patients affected by Turner syndrome (TS) suffer from bone fragility and a high risk of fractures. The health of bone microarchitecture has proven to be a very important element in reducing the risk of fractures
title: Impact of Clinical Factors on Bone Microarchitecture in Patients with Turner Syndrome.
journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets

text: . The present study aimed to describe bone characteristics of patients with TS and highlight clinical factors that can influence bone microarchitecture, evaluated by the trabecular bone score (TBS). This single-centre retrospective study included 41 patients with TS who attended the Endocrinology Day Hospital of the CTO Hospital of Rome between 2016 and 2024
title: Impact of Clinical Factors on Bone Microarchitecture in Patients with Turner Syndrome.
journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets

text: . Anthropometric, clinical, and densitometric data were collected and analysed using unadjusted univariate models, age- and body mass index-adjusted models, and multivariate analysis to investigate their effects on TBS. There was a positive association between TBS and duration of estrogen replacement therapy (ERT)
title: Impact of Clinical Factors on Bone Microarchitecture in Patients with Turner Syndrome.
journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets

text: . Patients who were constantly treated with ERT showed higher bone mineral density (BMD) at the lumbar spine and femoral neck (p=0.026 and p=0.040, respectively) and TBS (p=0.031). The presence of metabolic diseases appeared to have a negative influence on TBS (p=0.034)
title: Impact of Clinical Factors on Bone Microarchitecture in Patients with Turner Syndrome.
journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets

text: . Regular ERT and longer treatment duration appear to be the most important factors to significantly improve BMD and TBS levels in patients with TS. On the contrary, diagnosis of metabolic diseases significantly affect bone microarchitecture
title: Impact of Clinical Factors on Bone Microarchitecture in Patients with Turner Syndrome.
journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets

text: . Healthcare providers should pay particular attention to timely ERT and the prevention of metabolic complications, since these are the main factors that appear to improve bone architecture in this specific population.
title: Impact of Clinical Factors on Bone Microarchitecture in Patients with Turner Syndrome.
journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets

text: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Sarcopenia in Patients With Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.. To systematically evaluate the prevalence and influencing factors of diabetic foot sarcopenia
title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Sarcopenia in Patients With Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
journal: Journal of foot and ankle research

text: . We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, SinoMed, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP databases from inception until June 10, 2025, for studies reporting the prevalence and/or influencing factors of sarcopenia in patients with diabetic foot. All meta-analyses were performed using R software (version 4.4.2)
title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Sarcopenia in Patients With Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
journal: Journal of foot and ankle research

text: . A total of 1164 patients with diabetic foot ulcers were included in 7 studies. Meta-analysis showed that the prevalence of diabetic foot sarcopenia was 31% (95% CI: 0.22-0.41). Pooling of data from two studies indicated a significant association between longer diabetes duration and sarcopenia (OR = 3.33, 95% CI: 1.61-6.87, and p < 0.01)
title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Sarcopenia in Patients With Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
journal: Journal of foot and ankle research

text: . The evidence for other factors was insufficient for meta-analysis. This review confirms a high prevalence of sarcopenia in patients with diabetic foot. Although an association with longer diabetes duration was observed, this is based on limited studies and requires further validation
title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Sarcopenia in Patients With Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
journal: Journal of foot and ankle research

text: . These findings advocate for the consideration of early sarcopenia screening and preventive strategies within comprehensive diabetic foot care, potentially mitigating muscle loss and improving long-term outcomes.
title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Sarcopenia in Patients With Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
journal: Journal of foot and ankle research

text: Effect of synbiotic supplementation and psychobiotic diet on prenatal and postnatal depression and anxiety in women with gestational diabetes: a three-arm randomised controlled trial protocol.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is one of the most prevalent metabolic disorders during pregnancy and may lead to various short-term and long-term complications for both the mother and the fetus
title: Effect of synbiotic supplementation and psychobiotic diet on prenatal and postnatal depression and anxiety in women with gestational diabetes: a three-arm randomised controlled trial protocol.

text: . It is also associated with psychological disorders, such as anxiety and depression, the prevalence of which is reported to be two to four times higher than that among healthy pregnant women. Psychobiotics may improve cognitive and emotional function through modulation of the gut-brain axis
title: Effect of synbiotic supplementation and psychobiotic diet on prenatal and postnatal depression and anxiety in women with gestational diabetes: a three-arm randomised controlled trial protocol.

text: . Therefore, this study was designed to evaluate the prophylactic effects of synbiotic supplementation and a psychobiotic diet during pregnancy in women with GDM who do not have clinically significant depressive symptoms or psychiatric disorders at baseline
title: Effect of synbiotic supplementation and psychobiotic diet on prenatal and postnatal depression and anxiety in women with gestational diabetes: a three-arm randomised controlled trial protocol.

text: . The primary outcomes are antenatal depression and pregnancy-related anxiety at 38 weeks of gestation; secondary outcomes include postpartum depression and anxiety at 4-6 weeks after birth, maternal metabolic indices at 38 weeks of gestation and selected maternal and neonatal outcomes assessed immediately after birth. This is a randomised, controlled, three-arm parallel trial
title: Effect of synbiotic supplementation and psychobiotic diet on prenatal and postnatal depression and anxiety in women with gestational diabetes: a three-arm randomised controlled trial protocol.

text: . A total of 102 pregnant women diagnosed with GDM between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation will be randomly assigned (1:1:1) to one of three groups: a synbiotic capsule (Group 1), a psychobiotic diet (Group 2) and a placebo capsule (control group). Allocation will be performed using block randomisation, stratified by parity
title: Effect of synbiotic supplementation and psychobiotic diet on prenatal and postnatal depression and anxiety in women with gestational diabetes: a three-arm randomised controlled trial protocol.

text: . Regardless of group assignment, all participants will receive a standardised healthy diet education session in accordance with the Iranian Ministry of Health protocols. The intervention will be administered from the time of GDM diagnosis (28 weeks of gestation) until 4 weeks postpartum
title: Effect of synbiotic supplementation and psychobiotic diet on prenatal and postnatal depression and anxiety in women with gestational diabetes: a three-arm randomised controlled trial protocol.

text: . Outcomes will be assessed through maternal and neonatal medical records, laboratory analyses, the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, Revised Pregnancy-Related Anxiety Questionnaire, Postpartum Specific Anxiety Scale-Research Short Form and a 3 day dietary food record. Data analysis will be performed according to the modified intention-to-treat approach
title: Effect of synbiotic supplementation and psychobiotic diet on prenatal and postnatal depression and anxiety in women with gestational diabetes: a three-arm randomised controlled trial protocol.

text: . Additionally, a per-protocol analysis will be conducted for participants with an adherence rate of ≥90%. The study protocol has been approved by the Ethics Committee of Tabriz University of Medical Sciences (IR.TBZMED.RCE.1404.565). Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed journals and presentations at relevant scientific conferences. IRCT20220926056046N7.
title: Effect of synbiotic supplementation and psychobiotic diet on prenatal and postnatal depression and anxiety in women with gestational diabetes: a three-arm randomised controlled trial protocol.

text: Association of hyperglycaemia during pregnancy with future risk of type 2 diabetes among women: a nested case-control study using a US health administrative database.. To quantify the risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) among women based on the number of abnormal values on 100-gram oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT)
title: Association of hyperglycaemia during pregnancy with future risk of type 2 diabetes among women: a nested case-control study using a US health administrative database.

text: . A 1:5 matched case-control study nested to a cohort of pregnant women was conducted. Conditional logistic regression was employed to estimate the independent association between glucose levels and future risk of T2DM. This study used a large multicentre electronic health records (EHRs) database-Cerner Real-World Data (CRWD) between 2000 and 2016, covering approximately 21.6% of US inpatient EHRs
title: Association of hyperglycaemia during pregnancy with future risk of type 2 diabetes among women: a nested case-control study using a US health administrative database.

text: . We identified a cohort of 130 172 pregnant women registered in the CRWD between 2000 and 2016 and were followed up until the end of 2016. A nested case-control study was conducted within this cohort, comprising 1 390 cases and 6 950 matched controls
title: Association of hyperglycaemia during pregnancy with future risk of type 2 diabetes among women: a nested case-control study using a US health administrative database.

text: . Adjusted Odds Ratios for the risk of T2DM among women with one abnormal value and at least two abnormal values on OGTT diagnosed by the National Diabetes Data Group criteria, as compared with those women with normal OGTT values, were 5.69 (95% CI 4.34 to 7.47) and 13.20 (95% CI 10.52 to 16.57), respectively
title: Association of hyperglycaemia during pregnancy with future risk of type 2 diabetes among women: a nested case-control study using a US health administrative database.

text: . Women with one abnormal value on the 100-gram OGTT had a significantly higher risk of developing T2DM compared with women with normal glucose value.
title: Association of hyperglycaemia during pregnancy with future risk of type 2 diabetes among women: a nested case-control study using a US health administrative database.

text: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.. Despite advances in cardiovascular prevention, patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remain at increased risk of developing subclinical myocardial dysfunction before overt cardiovascular disease becomes clinically apparent
title: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.

text: . Whether anatomically defined non-obstructive coronary atherosclerosis is associated with impaired myocardial work before obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) develops remains unknown
title: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.

text: . This study investigated the association between coronary atherosclerotic burden on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and myocardial work in patients with T2DM and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)
title: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.

text: . In this retrospective cross-sectional study, consecutive T2DM patients who underwent both CCTA and transthoracic echocardiography a median of 41 days apart (interquartile range 31-57) were categorized by Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS 2.0) categories 0-2. Global work efficiency (GWE) was the predefined primary outcome
title: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.

text: . Associations with myocardial work were evaluated using Jonckheere-Terpstra trend analyses and multivariable linear regression, with CAD-RADS modelled both as an ordinal term and categorically, and with adjustment extended beyond the original covariate set to include body mass index, diabetes duration, smoking, heart rate and estimated glomerular filtration rate
title: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.

text: . Secondary outcomes were corrected for multiplicity using the Holm procedure. Among 114 patients (CAD-RADS 0, n = 21; CAD-RADS 1, n = 46; CAD-RADS 2, n = 47), GWE declined progressively across increasing CAD-RADS categories (98.0 ± 0.4%, 96.2 ± 1.1% and 93.0 ± 3.5%), while global wasted work increased (37 [interquartile range 32-44], 67 [61-77] and 98 [90-103] mmHg%; both p for trend <0.001)
title: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.

text: . Global longitudinal strain (GLS) did not differ significantly (-20.1 ± 2.1%, -19.7 ± 1.9% and -19.3 ± 3.1%; p for trend = 0.239), and left ventricular ejection fraction remained normal in every category although a modest downward trend was present (p for trend = 0.011)
title: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.

text: . Each one-category increase in CAD-RADS was independently associated with a 2.69 percentage-point lower GWE (95% CI -3.36 to -2.03) and a 30.6 mmHg% higher global wasted work (95% CI 28.0 to 33.3; both p < 0.001), with consistent findings for the Agatston score
title: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.

text: . In patients with T2DM and preserved LVEF, non-obstructive coronary atherosclerosis was independently associated with impaired myocardial mechanical efficiency, whereas global longitudinal strain did not differ significantly across categories
title: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.

text: . Because the design was cross-sectional, these findings describe an association and cannot establish causality or temporal sequence; prospective studies are required to determine whether myocardial work adds incremental prognostic value.
title: Association Between Non-Obstructive Coronary Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Work in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Coronary CT Angiography Study.

text: Impact of Semaglutide, Liraglutide and Tirzepatide on Cardiometabolic Outcomes: A Comparative Narrative Review.. Cardiometabolic disorders such as type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), obesity and cardiovascular disease (CVD) remain major global health challenges
title: Impact of Semaglutide, Liraglutide and Tirzepatide on Cardiometabolic Outcomes: A Comparative Narrative Review.

text: . Incretin-based therapies, including the GLP-1 receptor agonists semaglutide and liraglutide, and the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide, are increasingly used to address hyperglycaemia and obesity, and have been evaluated for both cardiometabolic risk markers and selected cardiovascular and renal outcomes
title: Impact of Semaglutide, Liraglutide and Tirzepatide on Cardiometabolic Outcomes: A Comparative Narrative Review.

text: . This review summarizes and contrasts the pharmacology of semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide, distinguishing between surrogate cardiometabolic risk markers (e.g., glycaemic control, body weight and lipid parameters) and confirmed clinical outcomes, including major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and renal endpoints
title: Impact of Semaglutide, Liraglutide and Tirzepatide on Cardiometabolic Outcomes: A Comparative Narrative Review.

text: . Recent data were synthesized from pivotal randomized clinical trial programs, SUSTAIN and PIONEER (semaglutide), LEADER (liraglutide) and SURPASS and SURMOUNT (tirzepatide), as well as meta-analyses, post hoc analyses and observational studies addressing mechanistic and long-term cardiometabolic outcomes
title: Impact of Semaglutide, Liraglutide and Tirzepatide on Cardiometabolic Outcomes: A Comparative Narrative Review.

text: . All three agents improved HbA1c, weight and cardiometabolic outcomes, with tirzepatide generally showing greater reductions across clinical trials. Semaglutide and liraglutide consistently improved BMI, lipid profile and cardiovascular risk, while tirzepatide shows promise pending CVOT data
title: Impact of Semaglutide, Liraglutide and Tirzepatide on Cardiometabolic Outcomes: A Comparative Narrative Review.

text: . Renal outcomes were favourable across the class, though results varied by baseline characteristics and trial design. Semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide are key therapies for type 2 diabetes and cardiometabolic disease. Tirzepatide's dual activity may enhance metabolic and lipid outcomes, while semaglutide and liraglutide have strong evidence for cardiovascular and renal safety
title: Impact of Semaglutide, Liraglutide and Tirzepatide on Cardiometabolic Outcomes: A Comparative Narrative Review.

text: . However, comparisons are based on indirect evidence and should be interpreted cautiously.
title: Impact of Semaglutide, Liraglutide and Tirzepatide on Cardiometabolic Outcomes: A Comparative Narrative Review.

text: Lactation as a targeted intervention for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy: understanding the cardioprotective relationship.. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy portend future cardiovascular risk and warrant implementation of evidence-based, preventive strategies. Lactation is an underrecognized, time-sensitive health behavior that improves cardiovascular outcomes across the life course
title: Lactation as a targeted intervention for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy: understanding the cardioprotective relationship.

text: . This narrative review covers the relationships between maternal cardiovascular disease and lactation, including recent epidemiologic, translational, and clinical literature
title: Lactation as a targeted intervention for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy: understanding the cardioprotective relationship.

text: . We reviewed published studies linking breastfeeding, lactation and cardiometabolic risk factors (including hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes), and cardiovascular disease, presenting evidence from large cohort studies and randomized trials
title: Lactation as a targeted intervention for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy: understanding the cardioprotective relationship.

text: . We also review mechanistic pathways, including endocrine regulation, metabolic adaptations, and anti-inflammatory effects mediated by key lactation-related hormones. The literature search was conducted in April and May of 2026 using PubMed and Open Evidence searches
title: Lactation as a targeted intervention for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy: understanding the cardioprotective relationship.

text: . Breastfeeding is an important health-related behavior with meaningful cardioprotective benefits, especially for mothers facing elevated cardiovascular risk after a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy
title: Lactation as a targeted intervention for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy: understanding the cardioprotective relationship.

text: . Evidence-based, multidisciplinary care for patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, should include prompt lactation support, guideline‑concordant maternity care, and early postpartum interventions designed to improve maternal health across the life course
title: Lactation as a targeted intervention for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy: understanding the cardioprotective relationship.

text: . Recognizing lactation as a component of preventive cardiology offers an important opportunity to reduce the long-term burden of hypertension and cardiovascular disease among women.
title: Lactation as a targeted intervention for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy: understanding the cardioprotective relationship.

text: Harnessing Nature's Arsenal: The multitarget anticancer and antidiabetic networks of saponins.. Saponins from medicinal plants are structurally diverse, naturally occurring amphiphilic glycoside molecules with broad biological activities. They are primarily classified into triterpenoid and steroidal types based on their aglycone scaffolds
title: Harnessing Nature's Arsenal: The multitarget anticancer and antidiabetic networks of saponins.

text: . This review systematically examines their multi-pathway, multi-target regulatory networks. It highlights their roles in both antitumor and antidiabetic interventions, as well as the miRNA-mediated epigenetic crosstalk between cancer and diabetes
title: Harnessing Nature's Arsenal: The multitarget anticancer and antidiabetic networks of saponins.

text: . Saponins combat cancer by inducing multiple programmed cell death modalities, causing cell cycle arrest, inhibiting metastasis and angiogenesis, disrupting metabolic reprogramming, and overcoming drug resistance. Their antidiabetic effects involve improving insulin resistance, inhibiting gluconeogenesis, protecting pancreatic β-cells, and preventing and treating diabetic complications
title: Harnessing Nature's Arsenal: The multitarget anticancer and antidiabetic networks of saponins.

text: . In reviewed studies, individual saponins link to multiple anticancer phenotypes and improved certain antidiabetic endpoints. Yet evidence is mostly compound/model-specific, so shared pathway and miRNA convergence across studies is seen as an indirect link or hypothesis
title: Harnessing Nature's Arsenal: The multitarget anticancer and antidiabetic networks of saponins.

text: . To address poor solubility and bioavailability, lipid-based nanoparticles are proposed as a delivery platform for improved stability and targeted application in both cancer and diabetes. This review integrates current knowledge to advance mechanistic understanding and promote saponins as multi-targeted therapeutics for cancer and diabetes.
title: Harnessing Nature's Arsenal: The multitarget anticancer and antidiabetic networks of saponins.

text: Optimizing cardiac surgery outcomes in morbid obesity: Surgical, anesthetic, perfusion, and critical care considerations, a narrative review.. The global prevalence of morbid obesity is increasing, presenting challenges in cardiac surgery
title: Optimizing cardiac surgery outcomes in morbid obesity: Surgical, anesthetic, perfusion, and critical care considerations, a narrative review.

text: . Morbid obesity (body mass index ≥40 kg/m This narrative review identified relevant literature through targeted searches of PubMed and Google Scholar, supplemented by screening the reference lists of key articles
title: Optimizing cardiac surgery outcomes in morbid obesity: Surgical, anesthetic, perfusion, and critical care considerations, a narrative review.

text: . Search terms included combinations of "cardiac surgery," "morbid obesity," "obesity," "cardiopulmonary bypass," "anesthesia," "perfusion," "postoperative complications," and "critical care." Studies were mapped to perioperative domains, including anesthesia and respiratory management, surgical and wound-related considerations, perfusion and cardiopulmonary bypass strategy, intensive care unit
title: Optimizing cardiac surgery outcomes in morbid obesity: Surgical, anesthetic, perfusion, and critical care considerations, a narrative review.

text: bypass strategy, intensive care unit (ICU) outcomes, renal complications, atrial fibrillation, bleeding, thromboembolism, and mortality
title: Optimizing cardiac surgery outcomes in morbid obesity: Surgical, anesthetic, perfusion, and critical care considerations, a narrative review.

text: . The evidence base was predominantly observational and review-based, with limited randomized evidence. Obesity poses multifactorial challenges in cardiovascular surgery by altering cardiac morphology, hemodynamics, and perioperative outcomes
title: Optimizing cardiac surgery outcomes in morbid obesity: Surgical, anesthetic, perfusion, and critical care considerations, a narrative review.

text: . Associated comorbidities such as diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, and pulmonary hypertension increase operative risk and complicate anesthetic and perfusion management. Obese patients demonstrate altered pharmacokinetics, reduced pulmonary compliance, and heightened inflammation, requiring individualized strategies
title: Optimizing cardiac surgery outcomes in morbid obesity: Surgical, anesthetic, perfusion, and critical care considerations, a narrative review.

text: . Available evidence suggests that lean body mass-informed perfusion, selected off-pump CABG, and early extubation may reduce complications, although high-quality randomized evidence remains limited. Cardiac surgery in morbidly obese patients requires a coordinated, physiology-driven perioperative strategy to address obesity-specific anatomical and functional challenges
title: Optimizing cardiac surgery outcomes in morbid obesity: Surgical, anesthetic, perfusion, and critical care considerations, a narrative review.

text: . Tailored anesthetic, perfusion, and surgical approaches, supported by close multidisciplinary collaboration, are central to optimizing outcomes. Further research is needed to refine perioperative protocols, improve risk stratification beyond BMI, and clarify long-term cardiovascular outcomes following surgery in this population.
title: Optimizing cardiac surgery outcomes in morbid obesity: Surgical, anesthetic, perfusion, and critical care considerations, a narrative review.

text: Inulin- and Butyrate-Mediated HIF-1α Butyrylation Prevent Diabetic Ferroptosis and Cardiomyopathy by Maintaining Iron Homeostasis.. title: Inulin- and Butyrate-Mediated HIF-1α Butyrylation Prevent Diabetic Ferroptosis and Cardiomyopathy by Maintaining Iron Homeostasis.

text: . We sought to identify the role of hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) in regulating myocardial iron homeostasis and ferroptosis in DCM, as well as evaluate the preventive effects of inulin on ferroptosis-induced DCM and elucidate its mechanism
title: Inulin- and Butyrate-Mediated HIF-1α Butyrylation Prevent Diabetic Ferroptosis and Cardiomyopathy by Maintaining Iron Homeostasis.

title: Inulin- and Butyrate-Mediated HIF-1α Butyrylation Prevent Diabetic Ferroptosis and Cardiomyopathy by Maintaining Iron Homeostasis.

text: . Targeting the HIF-1α-FTH/FTMT axis via inulin, butyrate, or alternative approaches may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for alleviating DCM and other diabetes complications.

title: Sick Day Medication Guidance for Adults with Chronic Kidney Disease in Outpatient Settings.

text: Hormonal metabolic burden in diabetic retinopathy: the diabetic retina as an endocrine-responsive target organ.. Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is usually interpreted as a complication of chronic hyperglycemia and vascular injury. title: Hormonal metabolic burden in diabetic retinopathy: the diabetic retina as an endocrine-responsive target organ.

title: Hormonal metabolic burden in diabetic retinopathy: the diabetic retina as an endocrine-responsive target organ.

title: Hormonal metabolic burden in diabetic retinopathy: the diabetic retina as an endocrine-responsive target organ.

text: Eriocitrin Attenuates Diabetic Cardiomyopathy by Regulating Copper Homeostasis and Cuproptosis-Associated Pathways via SIRT7/YAP/ATP7A Signalling.. Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major complication of diabetes mellitus, with limited therapeutic strategies available
title: Eriocitrin Attenuates Diabetic Cardiomyopathy by Regulating Copper Homeostasis and Cuproptosis-Associated Pathways via SIRT7/YAP/ATP7A Signalling.

text: . Cuproptosis, a novel form of copper-dependent cell death, has been implicated in cardiac dysfunction but remains unexplored in DCM. Here, we investigated the effects of Eriocitrin, a natural flavonoid, on DCM and examined the potential involvement of copper homeostasis, cuproptosis-associated molecular alterations and SIRT7/YAP/ATP7A signalling
title: Eriocitrin Attenuates Diabetic Cardiomyopathy by Regulating Copper Homeostasis and Cuproptosis-Associated Pathways via SIRT7/YAP/ATP7A Signalling.

text: . Using high-fat diet and streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, along with high-glucose-treated cardiomyocytes, we demonstrated that Eriocitrin improved cardiac function, attenuated myocardial remodelling and corrected glucose and lipid metabolism
title: Eriocitrin Attenuates Diabetic Cardiomyopathy by Regulating Copper Homeostasis and Cuproptosis-Associated Pathways via SIRT7/YAP/ATP7A Signalling.

text: . Mechanistically, Eriocitrin improved myocardial copper homeostasis by enhancing ATP7A and ATP7B expression and reducing copper accumulation and cuproptosis-associated molecular alterations. Loss of SIRT7 impaired these effects, suggesting that SIRT7-associated YAP/ATP7A signalling contributes to Eriocitrin-mediated cardioprotection
title: Eriocitrin Attenuates Diabetic Cardiomyopathy by Regulating Copper Homeostasis and Cuproptosis-Associated Pathways via SIRT7/YAP/ATP7A Signalling.

text: . The therapeutic efficacy of Eriocitrin showed similar protective trends to tetrathiomolybdate, a copper chelator. These findings suggest that Eriocitrin alleviates experimental DCM in association with improved myocardial copper homeostasis and attenuation of cuproptosis-associated molecular alterations, with SIRT7-associated YAP/ATP7A signalling potentially contributing to these effects
title: Eriocitrin Attenuates Diabetic Cardiomyopathy by Regulating Copper Homeostasis and Cuproptosis-Associated Pathways via SIRT7/YAP/ATP7A Signalling.

text: . Diabetic heart disease is a serious complication of diabetes with limited specific treatments. This study suggests that Eriocitrin, a natural compound found in citrus fruits, may protect the diabetic heart partly by improving copper regulation in cardiac cells. These effects were associated with changes in SIRT7/YAP/ATP7A signalling and proteins linked to copper‐dependent cellular injury
title: Eriocitrin Attenuates Diabetic Cardiomyopathy by Regulating Copper Homeostasis and Cuproptosis-Associated Pathways via SIRT7/YAP/ATP7A Signalling.

text: . Further studies are needed to determine the precise mechanism and therapeutic potential of Eriocitrin in diabetic heart disease.
title: Eriocitrin Attenuates Diabetic Cardiomyopathy by Regulating Copper Homeostasis and Cuproptosis-Associated Pathways via SIRT7/YAP/ATP7A Signalling.

text: Fucoxanthin Ameliorates Diabetic Kidney Disease via Modulating the Gut Microbiota and Tryptophan-Kynurenine Metabolic Pathway.. This study employs a multiomics approach to investigate the protective effects of fucoxanthin (Fu) and explore its potential association with metabolic and signaling pathways in diabetic mice induced by a high-fat diet combined with streptozotocin (STZ) administration
title: Fucoxanthin Ameliorates Diabetic Kidney Disease via Modulating the Gut Microbiota and Tryptophan-Kynurenine Metabolic Pathway.

text: . Diabetic model mice were randomly divided into normal control (NC), diabetic model, low-dose Fu (50 mg/kg/day), and high-dose Fu (100 mg/kg/day) groups
title: Fucoxanthin Ameliorates Diabetic Kidney Disease via Modulating the Gut Microbiota and Tryptophan-Kynurenine Metabolic Pathway.

text: . After 6 weeks of intervention, Fu treatment was associated with dose-dependent improvements in glucose and lipid metabolism, reduced oxidative stress, decreased expression of inflammatory cytokines (tumor necrosis factor-α [TNF-α], interleukin-6 [IL-6], and IL-1β) and renal fibrosis markers (TGF-β1, α-SMA, and Col1a1), along with notable attenuation of renal pathological damage
title: Fucoxanthin Ameliorates Diabetic Kidney Disease via Modulating the Gut Microbiota and Tryptophan-Kynurenine Metabolic Pathway.

text: . Exploratory analyses indicated that these phenotypic improvements were accompanied by reduced renal IDO1 expression, favorable shifts in tryptophan (Trp) metabolism, and upregulated AhR/CYP1A1 signaling. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed that Fu treatment was associated with a restoration of diabetes-altered gut microbiota β-diversity
title: Fucoxanthin Ameliorates Diabetic Kidney Disease via Modulating the Gut Microbiota and Tryptophan-Kynurenine Metabolic Pathway.

text: . Serum metabolomics identified that Fu administration correlated with alterations in multiple metabolites (including 5'-S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine, LPC 16:0, and bile acids), which are linked to key pathways such as Trp metabolism and bile acid biosynthesis. Network pharmacology predictions further suggested potential multitarget interactions of Fu with the PI3K-Akt and AGE-RAGE signaling pathways
title: Fucoxanthin Ameliorates Diabetic Kidney Disease via Modulating the Gut Microbiota and Tryptophan-Kynurenine Metabolic Pathway.

text: . Collectively, these findings indicate that Fu exerts potential renoprotective effects in diabetic mice, which are accompanied by a normalization of Trp-AhR pathway-related metabolism and concurrent attenuation of inflammatory, oxidative, and fibrotic responses
title: Fucoxanthin Ameliorates Diabetic Kidney Disease via Modulating the Gut Microbiota and Tryptophan-Kynurenine Metabolic Pathway.

text: . While causal functional links remain to be fully elucidated, these observations provide a preliminary basis for further mechanistic investigation and support the potential of Fu as a dietary supplement or adjunctive strategy for diabetic kidney disease (DKD).
title: Fucoxanthin Ameliorates Diabetic Kidney Disease via Modulating the Gut Microbiota and Tryptophan-Kynurenine Metabolic Pathway.

GPx4 interaction with ubiquitin ligase TRIM46 and with mitochondrial membrane transporters was analyzed by immunofluorescence and by co-IP
title: Regulation of Glutathione Peroxidase 4 in Diabetic Retinopathy.

title: Regulation of Glutathione Peroxidase 4 in Diabetic Retinopathy.

text: Assessment of the Association of Periodontitis and Diabetes Mellitus with Alzheimer's Disease in a Mouse Model.. The purpose of the present study was to investigate how periodontitis and diabetes mellitus (DM) are associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD) through microRNA (miRNA) using AD model mice. The experimental period was 8 weeks
title: Assessment of the Association of Periodontitis and Diabetes Mellitus with Alzheimer's Disease in a Mouse Model.

text: . The experimental period was 8 weeks. Twenty-four male knock-in mice (B6-AppNL-G-F/NL-G-F/J) were divided into four groups: control group fed a normal diet (C), DM group fed a high-fat/sucrose diet (DM), periodontitis (P) group, and DM + periodontitis (DM+P) group. Memory performance was compared using the Y-maze test
title: Assessment of the Association of Periodontitis and Diabetes Mellitus with Alzheimer's Disease in a Mouse Model.

text: . Next-generation sequencing was performed on brain samples, and fold changes in miRNA expression were calculated by comparing the DM+P and C groups. Integrated miRNA-mRNA analysis identified putative miRNA-targeted mRNAs, and protein expression of the top candidate gene was assessed. Memory function in the DM+P group was significantly lower than in the C group
title: Assessment of the Association of Periodontitis and Diabetes Mellitus with Alzheimer's Disease in a Mouse Model.

text: . Among the seven mRNAs identified by the integrated analysis, Neurod1 showed the greatest decrease in expression, and it was predicted to be regulated by miR-693-3p. Neurod1 protein expression in the hippocampus was significantly lower in the DM+P group than the C group
title: Assessment of the Association of Periodontitis and Diabetes Mellitus with Alzheimer's Disease in a Mouse Model.

text: . Our results suggest that the combined exposure to periodontitis and DM was associated with AD-like pathological changes and identified the miR-693-3p/Neurod1 pair as a candidate regulatory axis.
title: Assessment of the Association of Periodontitis and Diabetes Mellitus with Alzheimer's Disease in a Mouse Model.

text: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.. Postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a clinically important complication after surgery for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage
title: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Reported DVT incidence and associated risk factors vary across studies because of differences in patient characteristics, surgical procedures, assessment windows, and screening strategies
title: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . This meta-analysis aimed to synthesize the currently available observational evidence on the incidence and risk factors of lower-extremity DVT after surgery for spontaneous or hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage. This Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses -compliant review was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews
title: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang, Chinese Biomedical Literature, and China Science and Technology Journal were searched from inception to April 24, 2026. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Pooled incidence estimates were calculated using a random-effects model
title: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for clinically comparable risk factors using fixed-effect or random-effects models according to between-study heterogeneity. Subgroup analysis, leave-one-out sensitivity analysis, funnel-plot assessment, and exploratory Egger regression were performed where appropriate
title: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Fifteen observational studies involving 3378 patients were included, all of which were conducted in China. Fourteen studies comprising 3280 patients and 683 DVT events contributed to the incidence analysis. The pooled incidence of postoperative lower-extremity DVT was 23% (95% CI: 18%-28%; I2 = 91.96%), and leave-one-out sensitivity analysis showed estimates ranging from 21% to 24%
title: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Factors associated with higher odds of DVT included older age (OR = 2.45, 95% CI: 1.76-3.39), elevated D-dimer level (OR = 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01-1.05), higher Caprini score (OR = 2.39, 95% CI: 1.55-3.67), hypertension (OR = 3.69, 95% CI: 2.31-5.88), diabetes mellitus (OR = 2.58, 95% CI: 1.52-4.38), prolonged bedridden duration (OR = 4.30, 95% CI: 2.91-6.37), postoperative lower-limb motor
title: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: CI: 2.91-6.37), postoperative lower-limb motor dysfunction (OR = 3.59, 95% CI: 1.16-11.13), and venous catheterization (OR = 2.57, 95% CI: 1.98-3.33)
title: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Available Chinese observational evidence suggests that postoperative lower-extremity DVT is frequently reported after surgery for spontaneous or hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage. Its occurrence is associated with impaired mobility, coagulation activation, vascular-metabolic comorbidity, and perioperative invasive exposure
title: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Given the observational evidence base, geographical concentration, and substantial heterogeneity, prospective multicenter studies with standardized screening protocols are needed to confirm these findings and optimize postoperative DVT prevention strategies.
title: Incidence and risk factors for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in postoperative patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: Impact of renal iron overload on sickle cell nephropathy in a humanized mouse model.. Increased morbidity and mortality are associated with iron overload in sickle cell disease (SCD). Renal iron accumulation, a direct consequence of intravascular hemolysis, occurs in both patients and murine model of SCD, and correlates with albuminuria, an early marker of kidney injury
title: Impact of renal iron overload on sickle cell nephropathy in a humanized mouse model.
journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology

text: . We aimed to investigate the role of kidney-specific iron accumulation and underlying mechanisms contributing to iron overload-mediated SCD nephropathy in humanized sickle cell disease (HbSS) mice. In addition, as sex differences in renal phenotype exist, we examined sex disparities in iron-associated toxicity in murine SCD
title: Impact of renal iron overload on sickle cell nephropathy in a humanized mouse model.
journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology

text: . Iron chelation significantly reduced renal iron accumulation and subsequently prevented a decline in kidney function and disease progression only in male HbSS mice. Examining the mechanisms of kidney injury, secondary to renal iron accumulation, revealed the presence of oxidative stress and concurrent absence of ferroptosis in HbSS mice
title: Impact of renal iron overload on sickle cell nephropathy in a humanized mouse model.
journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology

text: . In addition, the proximal tubule from HbSS male mice had reduced basal mitochondrial respiration compared with HbSS female mice. Iron chelation had no effect on any of the tested injury-mediated pathways but did reduce proinflammatory signature in the kidneys of HbSS mice
title: Impact of renal iron overload on sickle cell nephropathy in a humanized mouse model.
journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology

text: . These results demonstrate that iron chelation exerts nephroprotective effects in male HbSS mice, whereas enhanced mitochondrial quality in HbSS female may account, at least in part, for potential sex differences in SCD nephropathy.
title: Impact of renal iron overload on sickle cell nephropathy in a humanized mouse model.
journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology

text: Awareness of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Makkah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a chronic liver condition characterized by excessive fat accumulation in hepatocytes, affecting individuals globally
title: Awareness of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Makkah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . With a prevalence of 32% among adults, NAFLD is linked to obesity, metabolic disorders, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), yet awareness remains disproportionately low, reaching as low as 4.4% in some developed countries like the US, despite its high prevalence. In Saudi Arabia, specifically the Makkah region, data regarding public awareness are scarce
title: Awareness of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Makkah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . This study aims to bridge this gap by assessing NAFLD awareness and its predictors among Makkah residents. A cross-sectional study was conducted using an electronic questionnaire (Google Forms) distributed through social media platforms, with 716 participants (aged ≥18 years) included, who are adult residents of Makkah, Saudi Arabia
title: Awareness of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Makkah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . The questionnaire gathered demographic information and assessed NAFLD knowledge. The survey instrument was self-constructed; while formal psychometric validation was not conducted, content validity was ensured through review by academic faculty experts. Data were analyzed using RStudio (version 4.3.1). Descriptive statistics, Pearson's chi-square, and Fisher's exact tests were utilized
title: Awareness of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Makkah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify significant predictors of awareness, with results reported as odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Of the 716 participants, 80% were female, and 54.1% were aged 18-25 years. Only 30.3% were aware of NAFLD, primarily through the Internet (59.9%). Awareness of symptoms was critically low (17.9%)
title: Awareness of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Makkah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Awareness of symptoms was critically low (17.9%). Significant predictors included higher education (p = 0.010) and older age (p = 0.038). Notably, participants with a family history of NAFLD were 32.7 times more likely to be aware of the condition (OR = 32.7, p < 0.001). The study reveals significant gaps in NAFLD awareness and knowledge among Makkah residents
title: Awareness of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Makkah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Given that the internet is the leading source of information, we recommend launching interactive social media campaigns led by trusted healthcare professionals to provide simplified, evidence-based content. In addition, increasing local research and conducting awareness days in public places are essential steps
title: Awareness of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Makkah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . These practical actions will bridge the knowledge gap, support early detection, and help prevent serious liver complications.
title: Awareness of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease in Makkah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: [Expert consensus on initial combination lipid-lowering therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension (2026)].. The prevalence of hypertension in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus is as high as 60% to 76%, and the coexistence of these two conditions further increases the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)
title: [Expert consensus on initial combination lipid-lowering therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension (2026)].

text: . Lipid management is a critical component in the prevention and management of ASCVD. Recent studies have shown that initiating combination lipid-lowering therapy, compared with statin monotherapy, leads to a more rapid and significant reduction in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and significantly lowers the risk of cardiovascular events
title: [Expert consensus on initial combination lipid-lowering therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension (2026)].

text: . To further clarify the initial combination lipid-lowering strategy for patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, experts in cardiology and endocrinology collaborated to develop this consensus
title: [Expert consensus on initial combination lipid-lowering therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension (2026)].

text: . The consensus emphasizes that, on the basis of lifestyle interventions, active initiation of combination therapy with statins and cholesterol absorption inhibitors, supplemented with proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitors when necessary, should be implemented to reduce LDL-C to target levels as early as possible
title: [Expert consensus on initial combination lipid-lowering therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension (2026)].

text: . For patients with hypertriglyceridemia, the addition of icosapent ethyl or fibrates is recommended to further reduce residual cardiovascular risk or the risk of pancreatitis
title: [Expert consensus on initial combination lipid-lowering therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension (2026)].

text: . 2型糖尿病合并高血压发生率高达60%~76%，两者共病使动脉粥样硬化性心血管疾病（ASCVD）风险进一步升高。血脂管理是防治ASCVD的关键环节。近年的研究结果显示，起始联合降脂治疗较他汀类药物单药治疗可更快速、显著地降低低密度脂蛋白胆固醇（LDL-C）水平，并显著降低心血管事件发生风险。为进一步明确2型糖尿病合并高血压患者的起始联合降脂策略，心血管病学与内分泌学专家协作制订本共识。本共识强调在健康生活方式干预的基础上，积极起始联合他汀类药物与胆固醇吸收抑制剂治疗，必要时联合前蛋白转化酶枯草溶菌素转化酶9抑制剂，尽早将LDL-C降低至目标值；对伴高甘油三酯血症患者，推荐联合二十碳五烯酸乙酯或贝特类药物，进一步降低心血管残余风险或胰腺炎风险。.

text: Melatonin and Artificial Light: Effects on Maternal and Fetal Health During Pregnancy.. The placenta produces melatonin during pregnancy, a hormone essential for circadian regulation and maternal-fetal metabolic, hormonal, and immunological modulation. Throughout pregnancy, melatonin production increases progressively, being synthesized by both the pineal gland and the placenta
title: Melatonin and Artificial Light: Effects on Maternal and Fetal Health During Pregnancy.

text: . Since exposure to artificial light at night (ALAN) reduces pineal melatonin secretion, it is hypothesized that light pollution may negatively impact women's health, maternal health, and fetal development due to the inhibition of both pineal and placental synthesis. This study aimed to analyze the role of melatonin during pregnancy and the effects of exposure to ALAN on maternal-fetal health
title: Melatonin and Artificial Light: Effects on Maternal and Fetal Health During Pregnancy.

text: . The following search terms (" Exposure to ALAN reduces melatonin production and is associated with adverse maternal-fetal outcomes, including reduced fertility, sleep disturbances, preterm birth, metabolic alterations, gestational diabetes, hypothyroidism, altered gut microbiota, mood symptoms, excessive gestational weight gain, fetal growth changes, and congenital heart defects
title: Melatonin and Artificial Light: Effects on Maternal and Fetal Health During Pregnancy.

text: . Animal studies demonstrate causal effects of melatonin disruption, including impaired offspring development, inflammation, altered metabolic and hormonal rhythms, and pregnancy complications, whereas melatonin supplementation shows protective effects. These findings highlight the maternal circadian-melatonin axis as a potential target for preventive strategies
title: Melatonin and Artificial Light: Effects on Maternal and Fetal Health During Pregnancy.

text: . Although evidence is insufficient to recommend melatonin supplementation, antenatal counseling may include circadian hygiene measures, such as reducing evening light and screen exposure, maintaining regular sleep schedules, and optimizing nighttime darkness
title: Melatonin and Artificial Light: Effects on Maternal and Fetal Health During Pregnancy.

text: . Light-based interventions, including biodynamic lighting and blue-light-blocking glasses, remain promising but require further clinical validation. It is concluded that melatonin plays a central role in regulating pregnancy and that exposure to ALAN poses a risk to maternal-fetal health
title: Melatonin and Artificial Light: Effects on Maternal and Fetal Health During Pregnancy.

text: . Mitigation strategies, such as lighting that mimics natural light, the use of blue light-blocking glasses, and the combination of light and sleep, may represent relevant preventive measures for maternal-fetal health.
title: Melatonin and Artificial Light: Effects on Maternal and Fetal Health During Pregnancy.

text: Bone microarchitecture and microfractures in disorganized bone in a young female with pycnodysostosis and atypical femur fractures: A case for novel fracture prediction technology using ALIGNOGRAM. title: Bone microarchitecture and microfractures in disorganized bone in a young female with pycnodysostosis and atypical femur fractures: A case for novel fracture prediction technology using ALIGNOGRAM

text: . The inability to resorb bone leads to sclerosis, with increased bone mineral density (BMD) but paradoxically increased bone fragility. We report a case of a young female with PYCD with multiple fragility fractures including bilateral atypical femur fractures (AFF)
title: Bone microarchitecture and microfractures in disorganized bone in a young female with pycnodysostosis and atypical femur fractures: A case for novel fracture prediction technology using ALIGNOGRAM

text: . Areal and volumetric bone density were supranormal, measured by dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and high-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography (HR-pQCT), respectively. However, bone disorganization was prominent, observed on visual assessment of HR-pQCT images, with microfractures and sclerotic intramedullary lesions. ALIGNOGRAM
