text: Association Between Periodontal Health and Perioperative Glycemic Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Dental Procedures Under General Anesthesia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.. Introduction Periodontitis and diabetes are closely related, but the influence of periodontal disease severity on perioperative glycemic outcomes during dental procedures under general anesthesia remains unclear
title: Association Between Periodontal Health and Perioperative Glycemic Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Dental Procedures Under General Anesthesia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . This study evaluated the association between periodontal disease severity and perioperative glycemic outcomes in diabetic patients. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 72 patients with diabetes who underwent elective dental procedures under general anesthesia between January 2015 and December 2018
title: Association Between Periodontal Health and Perioperative Glycemic Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Dental Procedures Under General Anesthesia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . The patients were categorized into mild periodontitis (n = 43) and severe periodontitis (n = 29) groups. Demographic, diabetic, periodontal, anesthetic, and perioperative data were retrieved from the electronic medical records. Periodontal parameters included plaque index, bleeding on probing, probing pocket depth, clinical attachment loss, and the number of remaining teeth
title: Association Between Periodontal Health and Perioperative Glycemic Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Dental Procedures Under General Anesthesia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . Perioperative glycemic outcomes were assessed using preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative blood glucose levels; glycemic variability; and the incidence of hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia. Postoperative complications were also assessed. Statistical analysis was then performed
title: Association Between Periodontal Health and Perioperative Glycemic Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Dental Procedures Under General Anesthesia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . Statistical analysis was then performed. Results Patients with severe periodontitis had significantly higher glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels than those with mild disease (8.9 ± 1.3% vs. 7.6 ± 1.2%; p < 0.001). Mean preoperative (185.6 ± 42.4 vs. 142.3 ± 38.1 mg/dL), intraoperative (210.8 ± 48.2 vs. 155.4 ± 41.5 mg/dL), postoperative (225.1 ± 52.3 vs
title: Association Between Periodontal Health and Perioperative Glycemic Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Dental Procedures Under General Anesthesia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . 161.2 ± 45.8 mg/dL), and mean perioperative blood glucose levels (207.2 ± 43.5 vs. 153.0 ± 38.2 mg/dL) were significantly higher in patients with severe periodontitis (all p < 0.001). Glycemic variability was also significantly greater (41.3 ± 14.2 vs. 28.5 ± 10.1; p < 0.001)
title: Association Between Periodontal Health and Perioperative Glycemic Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Dental Procedures Under General Anesthesia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . 28.5 ± 10.1; p < 0.001). Perioperative hyperglycemia was observed in 22 (75.9%) patients with severe periodontitis compared with 12 (27.9%) patients with mild periodontitis (p < 0.001)
title: Association Between Periodontal Health and Perioperative Glycemic Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Dental Procedures Under General Anesthesia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . Surgical site infection occurred in 9 (31.0%) and 3 (7.0%) patients (p = 0.014), delayed wound healing in 11 (37.9%) and 4 (9.3%) patients (p = 0.006), and hospital stay exceeding 24 hours in 15 (51.7%) and 8 (18.6%) patients (p = 0.004), respectively. title: Association Between Periodontal Health and Perioperative Glycemic Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Dental Procedures Under General Anesthesia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

Conclusion Severe periodontitis was associated with poorer perioperative glycemic control, greater glycemic variability, and more frequent postoperative complications in diabetic patients undergoing dental procedures under general anesthesia. title: Association Between Periodontal Health and Perioperative Glycemic Outcomes in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Dental Procedures Under General Anesthesia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . Prospective studies are needed to determine whether periodontal management can improve perioperative outcomes.

text: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.. Gestational diabetes (GDM) is frequently associated with adverse neonatal outcomes, but the underlying mechanisms linking maternal hyperglycemia to fetal harm are not fully understood
title: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Oxidative stress has been suggested as a key pathway; however, studies simultaneously evaluating multiple oxidative and antioxidant biomarkers in umbilical cord blood are limited
title: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . This study aimed to investigate the impact of GDM on the fetus by comprehensively evaluating oxidative stress and antioxidant defense mechanisms in umbilical cord blood and to examine their potential associations with neonatal clinical outcomes
title: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Umbilical cord blood samples were analyzed for malondialdehyde (MDA), membrane attack complex (MAC), total antioxidant status (TAS), total oxidant status (TOS), oxidative stress index (OSI), ischemia-related modified albumin (IMA), 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG), advanced glycation end products (AGEs), reduced glutathione (GSH), and glutathione peroxidase (GPx)
title: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Neonatal clinical outcomes were recorded and compared between pregnancies with and without GDM. After correction for multiple biomarker comparisons, MAC, 8-OHdG, and TOS differed significantly between the GDM and non-GDM groups. MAC and 8-OHdG levels were higher in the GDM group, whereas TOS was lower
title: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . OSI was higher in the Mann-Whitney analysis but did not remain significant after BH-FDR correction. Exploratory multivariate analyses supported a group-level difference in the combined oxidative-stress biomarker profile, as confirmed by MANOVA and permutation testing
title: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . The Spearman heatmap showed that maternal HbA1c was most prominently associated with OSI and also correlated positively with 8-OHdG and GSH. Although neonatal complications were more frequent in the GDM group, oxidative-stress markers were not consistently associated with specific neonatal complications
title: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . These findings suggest that GDM is associated with a selective fetal redox-related biomarker pattern rather than a uniform global increase in oxidative stress
title: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . The combined biomarker profile and HbA1c-related heatmap correlations indicate that long-term maternal glycemic exposure may influence fetal oxidant-antioxidant balance and oxidative DNA-damage signals, while antioxidant-related responses may remain partially preserved
title: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . The comprehensive evaluation of multiple oxidative and antioxidant biomarkers, particularly the inclusion of rarely studied AGEs and IMA, provides a broader perspective on fetal exposure to GDM and its pathophysiological mechanisms.
title: Association between umbilical cord oxidative stress and early neonatal outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden characterized by progressive loss of renal function and high cardiovascular morbidity and mortality
title: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, initially developed as glucose-lowering agents, have demonstrated pleiotropic metabolic and cardiorenal benefits. However, previous evidence syntheses have not fully clarified the magnitude of metabolic, hemodynamic, renal surrogate, and safety effects specifically in patients with diabetic CKD
title: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was conducted up to December 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with diabetic CKD were included
title: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Outcomes were prespecified and grouped as primary renal surrogate marker outcomes (eGFR and UACR), secondary metabolic and hemodynamic outcomes (glycated hemoglobin, body weight, and blood pressure indicators), and safety outcomes (urinary tract infection and volume depletion-related adverse events). Meta-analyses were performed using RevMan 5.3 and R version 4.4.2 software
title: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . A total of 17 randomized controlled trials involving 29,192 participants were included. For secondary metabolic and hemodynamic outcomes, SGLT2 inhibitors significantly reduced glycated hemoglobin levels (MD = -0.40%, 95% CI: -0.44 to -0.36), body weight (MD = -1.36 kg, 95% CI: -1.55 to -1.18), and systolic blood pressure (MD = -2.98 mm Hg, 95% CI: -3.44 to -2.52)
title: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . For primary renal surrogate marker outcomes, no statistically significant differences were observed in eGFR (MD = 0.25 mL/min/1.73 m2, 95% CI: -0.08 to 0.57) or UACR (MD = -31.55 mg/g, 95% CI: -137.21 to 74.12)
title: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Regarding safety outcomes, SGLT2 inhibitors did not significantly increase the risk of urinary tract infections (RR = 1.20, 95% CI: 0.94 to 1.54) but were associated with a significantly higher risk of volume depletion-related adverse events (RR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.16-1.59)
title: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . In patients with diabetic CKD, SGLT2 inhibitors significantly improve glycemic control, reduce body weight, and lower systolic blood pressure, while showing neutral short- to medium-term effects on eGFR and albuminuria. These neutral surrogate-marker findings should be interpreted alongside large outcome trials showing long-term cardiorenal protection
title: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Although SGLT2 inhibitors increase the risk of volume depletion-related adverse events, their overall safety profile remains acceptable with appropriate clinical monitoring.
title: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Metformin in Elderly Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Muscle Strength, Muscle Mass, and Physical Function: Positive or Negative Correlation?

title: Prevalence of Chronic Complications After Inaugural Admission in Intensive Care Unit for Type 1 Diabetes in the SFDT1 Cohort: The INAUGURAL Study.

text: . We assessed the association between inaugural intensive care unit (ICU) admission and long-term diabetes-related outcomes in adults. This cross-sectional analysis used data from the Société Francophone du Diabète-Cohorte Diabète de Type 1 (SFDT1) cohort
title: Prevalence of Chronic Complications After Inaugural Admission in Intensive Care Unit for Type 1 Diabetes in the SFDT1 Cohort: The INAUGURAL Study.

title: Prevalence of Chronic Complications After Inaugural Admission in Intensive Care Unit for Type 1 Diabetes in the SFDT1 Cohort: The INAUGURAL Study.

text: . Among 3548 adults with type 1 diabetes (median duration 20 years [IQR 10-30]), 377 (10.6%) reported inaugural ICU admission. Retinopathy was more prevalent in the ICU group (36.6 vs. 31.4%; p < 0.05), including proliferative forms (11.1 vs. 7.7%; p < 0.05). These differences remained significant after adjustment (p < 0.05)
title: Prevalence of Chronic Complications After Inaugural Admission in Intensive Care Unit for Type 1 Diabetes in the SFDT1 Cohort: The INAUGURAL Study.

text: Hand and shoulder diagnoses are associated with substantial bodily pain compared to vascular complications and long-term glycaemic control in people with long-term type 1 diabetes.. text: Development and Pilot Clinical Evaluation of DiaBuddy, a Point-of-Care Decision Support Tool for Children and Adolescents with Insulin-Treated Diabetes.
title: Development and Pilot Clinical Evaluation of DiaBuddy, a Point-of-Care Decision Support Tool for Children and Adolescents with Insulin-Treated Diabetes.

text: . Background - Optimal management of insulin-treated pediatric and adolescent diabetes, particularly type 1 diabetes (T1D), requires precise insulin dosing and sick-day decision-making; deficiencies in either predispose to hypoglycemia, suboptimal glycaemic control, and diabetic ketoacidosis
title: Development and Pilot Clinical Evaluation of DiaBuddy, a Point-of-Care Decision Support Tool for Children and Adolescents with Insulin-Treated Diabetes.

text: . We developed DiaBuddy™, a guideline-aligned mobile decision support tool, and evaluated its accuracy versus expert guidance and clinical changes observed during pilot evaluation in children and adolescents with insulin-treated diabetes
title: Development and Pilot Clinical Evaluation of DiaBuddy, a Point-of-Care Decision Support Tool for Children and Adolescents with Insulin-Treated Diabetes.

text: . Methods - The preclinical validation compared DiaBuddy and family recommendations (N = 37) for 20 insulin-dosing and 20 sick-day vignettes against a pediatric endocrinologist gold standard. The prospective single-arm pilot study explored changes over 12 weeks in 20 children and adolescents with insulin-treated diabetes
title: Development and Pilot Clinical Evaluation of DiaBuddy, a Point-of-Care Decision Support Tool for Children and Adolescents with Insulin-Treated Diabetes.

text: . HbA1c was the primary clinical outcome; CGM-derived metrics, PedsQL quality-of-life scores, application use, and satisfaction were exploratory secondary outcomes
title: Development and Pilot Clinical Evaluation of DiaBuddy, a Point-of-Care Decision Support Tool for Children and Adolescents with Insulin-Treated Diabetes.

text: . Results - In the preclinical study, DiaBuddy showed lower absolute relative deviation for basal (5.0 ± 6.7% vs 24.2 ± 25.9%), bolus (6.9 ± 10.9% vs 45.3 ± 48.8%), and combined doses (6.3 ± 9.3% vs 39.0 ± 37.8%; all P < 0.001) than families
title: Development and Pilot Clinical Evaluation of DiaBuddy, a Point-of-Care Decision Support Tool for Children and Adolescents with Insulin-Treated Diabetes.

text: . DiaBuddy™ achieved ≥90% accuracy across all sick-day domains versus 27-70% for families; and provided a guideline-concordant response in 94.5% of instances in which family responses were erroneous, including all instances involving an incorrect family hospitalisation decision
title: Development and Pilot Clinical Evaluation of DiaBuddy, a Point-of-Care Decision Support Tool for Children and Adolescents with Insulin-Treated Diabetes.

text: . In the clinical study, HbA1c declined from 9.18 ± 1.99% to 8.48 ± 1.44% (p = 0.049) and the PedsQL score increased from 76.5 ± 8.6 to 89.1 ± 7.1 (+12.6 points, P < 0.001) with no change in CGM metrics. Application satisfaction was high (mean score 44.1 ± 4.1 out of 50) with most wishing to continue using it. Conclusions - DiaBuddy delivered guideline-aligned guidance in vignette testing
title: Development and Pilot Clinical Evaluation of DiaBuddy, a Point-of-Care Decision Support Tool for Children and Adolescents with Insulin-Treated Diabetes.

text: . In this single-centre, uncontrolled pilot, observed changes in HbA1c and PedsQL are hypothesis-generating and require evaluation in an adequately powered multicentre randomised controlled trial.
title: Development and Pilot Clinical Evaluation of DiaBuddy, a Point-of-Care Decision Support Tool for Children and Adolescents with Insulin-Treated Diabetes.

text: Glycaemic trends, trajectories and control during TB treatment and its association with TB treatment outcome among patients with TB-diabetes multimorbidity.. title: Glycaemic trends, trajectories and control during TB treatment and its association with TB treatment outcome among patients with TB-diabetes multimorbidity.

text: . Analytical cross-sectional study was conducted, involving secondary analysis of an implementation study conducted at 13 Tuberculosis clinics in KPK and Punjab from June 2022 to June 2025. title: Glycaemic trends, trajectories and control during TB treatment and its association with TB treatment outcome among patients with TB-diabetes multimorbidity.

text: . Glycaemic trends, trajectories, and control status were reviewed, TB treatment outcomes were assessed at six months and associations were assessed using complete case and imputed datasets. Among 251 participants, the mean age was 52.0±12.7 years and 60.6% (152/251) were males. Overall, 74.5% (187/251) achieved successful while 64 (25.5%) experienced unsuccessful TB treatment outcomes
title: Glycaemic trends, trajectories and control during TB treatment and its association with TB treatment outcome among patients with TB-diabetes multimorbidity.

title: Glycaemic trends, trajectories and control during TB treatment and its association with TB treatment outcome among patients with TB-diabetes multimorbidity.

Binary logistic regression showed higher odds of experiencing unsuccessful outcome as compared to successful outcome due to uncontrolled RBG (OR=6.9; 95%CI: 1.8-27.7) and HbA1c (OR=9.0; 95%CI: 2.3-36.0). title: Glycaemic trends, trajectories and control during TB treatment and its association with TB treatment outcome among patients with TB-diabetes multimorbidity.

text: . A propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study was performed using the TriNetX multi-institutional database. Adults aged 18-90 years who underwent primary TKA with documented HbA1c greater than 8% 3m -1y preoperatively, who were able to decrease it to under 7.5% <3m preoperatively
title: Postoperative Glycemic Deterioration and Outcomes After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Does It Matter?

text: . HbA1c values obtained 1-2 years postoperatively were used to define cohorts: cohort 1 (HbA1c <7.5%) and cohort 2 (HbA1c ≥8.0%). Outcomes included early medical complications (30- and 90-day) and arthroplasty-specific complications within five years, including periprosthetic joint infection, revision surgery, mechanical loosening, and periprosthetic fracture
title: Postoperative Glycemic Deterioration and Outcomes After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Does It Matter?

text: . After matching a total of 3,200 patients met the inclusion criteria, with 1,600 patients in each cohort after matching. There were no significant differences in 30- or 90-day medical complications between groups. At five years, rates of periprosthetic joint infection, revision surgery, mechanical loosening, and periprosthetic fracture were also similar
title: Postoperative Glycemic Deterioration and Outcomes After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Does It Matter?

text: . Elevated postoperative HbA1c at 1-2 years following TKA was not independently associated with increased risk of complications or implant failure when perioperative glycemic control was optimized. These findings suggest that once early healing occurs under adequate glycemic conditions, later deterioration in glycemic control may have a limited impact on arthroplasty outcomes.

text: Central Auditory Pathway Dysfunction in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Narrative Review of Auditory Brainstem Response Alterations.. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is increasingly recognized as a disorder affecting both the peripheral and central nervous systems
title: Central Auditory Pathway Dysfunction in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Narrative Review of Auditory Brainstem Response Alterations.

text: . Although diabetic neuropathy has traditionally been associated with peripheral nerve damage, accumulating evidence suggests that central auditory pathways are also vulnerable to chronic hyperglycaemia
title: Central Auditory Pathway Dysfunction in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Narrative Review of Auditory Brainstem Response Alterations.

text: . This narrative review synthesizes current evidence regarding auditory brainstem response (ABR) abnormalities in adults with T2DM, with emphasis on their pathophysiological basis, characteristic electrophysiological alterations, clinical associations, and potential diagnostic significance
title: Central Auditory Pathway Dysfunction in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Narrative Review of Auditory Brainstem Response Alterations.

text: . A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar identified 10 observational studies published between 2000 and 2024 that evaluated ABR parameters in adults with T2DM
title: Central Auditory Pathway Dysfunction in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Narrative Review of Auditory Brainstem Response Alterations.

text: . Across the included studies, the most consistent findings were prolonged wave III and wave V absolute latencies together with extended interpeak intervals (I-III, III-V, and I-V), while wave I latency remained normal in most patients, indicating predominant central auditory pathway dysfunction
title: Central Auditory Pathway Dysfunction in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Narrative Review of Auditory Brainstem Response Alterations.

text: . A smaller proportion of studies demonstrated additional peripheral auditory nerve involvement, suggesting mixed neuropathic changes. Higher glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) levels and longer duration of diabetes were generally associated with greater ABR abnormalities, supporting the role of cumulative metabolic injury in central neural conduction delay
title: Central Auditory Pathway Dysfunction in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Narrative Review of Auditory Brainstem Response Alterations.

text: . Despite methodological heterogeneity and predominantly cross-sectional study designs, the evidence consistently indicates that the auditory brainstem is an early target of diabetes-related neural injury. ABR represents a non-invasive and reproducible tool with potential utility for detecting subclinical central diabetic neuropathy before overt auditory impairment becomes clinically evident
title: Central Auditory Pathway Dysfunction in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Narrative Review of Auditory Brainstem Response Alterations.

text: . Further multicentre longitudinal studies using standardized ABR protocols are required to validate its diagnostic and prognostic value in routine clinical practice.
title: Central Auditory Pathway Dysfunction in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Narrative Review of Auditory Brainstem Response Alterations.

text: Assessment of monotherapy and combination therapy with canagliflozin, metformin, and fenugreek seed extract in experimental diabetic osteopathy.. Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycaemia and is associated with multiple systemic complications
title: Assessment of monotherapy and combination therapy with canagliflozin, metformin, and fenugreek seed extract in experimental diabetic osteopathy.

text: . Chronic hyperglycaemia and related metabolic disturbances can impair bone remodelling and compromise bone quality and microarchitecture, increasing skeletal vulnerability. The effects of different antidiabetic treatment combinations on diabetes-associated skeletal alterations remain insufficiently characterized
title: Assessment of monotherapy and combination therapy with canagliflozin, metformin, and fenugreek seed extract in experimental diabetic osteopathy.

text: . We investigated the effects of canagliflozin alone and in combination with metformin and fenugreek seed extract on glycaemic control and skeletal alterations in a high-fat diet (HFD)-streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic rat model
title: Assessment of monotherapy and combination therapy with canagliflozin, metformin, and fenugreek seed extract in experimental diabetic osteopathy.

text: . Diabetes was induced in female Wistar rats using a HFD followed by STZ (35 mg/kg, intraperitoneally), and animals were treated orally for 12 weeks with canagliflozin (10 or 20 mg/kg), fenugreek seed extract (400 mg/kg), canagliflozin (10 mg/kg) plus metformin (200 mg/kg), or canagliflozin (10 mg/kg) plus metformin (200 mg/kg) and fenugreek seed extract (400 mg/kg)
title: Assessment of monotherapy and combination therapy with canagliflozin, metformin, and fenugreek seed extract in experimental diabetic osteopathy.

text: . At the end of the treatment period, glycaemic and skeletal parameters were assessed, including serum insulin, HbA1c, serum TRAP activity, urinary calcium excretion, femoral trabecular microarchitecture and histological changes
title: Assessment of monotherapy and combination therapy with canagliflozin, metformin, and fenugreek seed extract in experimental diabetic osteopathy.

text: . Diabetic rats exhibited marked hyperglycaemia and deterioration of femoral trabecular microarchitecture, with reductions in bone volume fraction, trabecular thickness, trabecular number and connectivity density (Conn. D) and increases in trabecular separation and structural model index (SMI)
title: Assessment of monotherapy and combination therapy with canagliflozin, metformin, and fenugreek seed extract in experimental diabetic osteopathy.

text: . Treatment with canagliflozin, fenugreek seed extract and combination regimens attenuated these diabetes-associated alterations. At week 12, the canagliflozin-metformin-fenugreek combination reduced fasting blood glucose by approximately 57.8% and HbA1c by approximately 47.4% compared with diabetic controls and was associated with improved trabecular microarchitectural parameters
title: Assessment of monotherapy and combination therapy with canagliflozin, metformin, and fenugreek seed extract in experimental diabetic osteopathy.

text: . Serum TRAP activity and urinary calcium excretion were also reduced by approximately 26.1% and 31.4%, respectively. Histological findings were consistent with the micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) observations
title: Assessment of monotherapy and combination therapy with canagliflozin, metformin, and fenugreek seed extract in experimental diabetic osteopathy.

text: . Overall, canagliflozin-based combination treatments were associated with improved metabolic control and attenuation of femoral trabecular deterioration in this experimental model, supporting further investigation of their skeletal effects and underlying mechanisms.
title: Assessment of monotherapy and combination therapy with canagliflozin, metformin, and fenugreek seed extract in experimental diabetic osteopathy.

text: Acquired generalized lipodystrophy complicated by fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report with review of literature and immunological insights.. Acquired generalized lipodystrophy (AGL) is a rare disorder characterized by progressive loss of subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue and severe metabolic disturbances, including diabetes mellitus (DM)
title: Acquired generalized lipodystrophy complicated by fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report with review of literature and immunological insights.

text: . Although AGL is typically associated with type 2 DM, clinical experience with patients affected by both AGL and Fulminant type 1 DM (FT1DM) remains limited. We report a case of a 50-year-old man with long-standing (4-year) FT1DM who developed AGL, with histopathological and immunological evaluation and long-term follow-up after metreleptin therapy
title: Acquired generalized lipodystrophy complicated by fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report with review of literature and immunological insights.

text: . The patient presented with rapid deterioration of glycemic control and extreme insulin resistance, requiring a marked increase in insulin dose. Imaging studies revealed generalized loss of subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue, and skin biopsy demonstrated marked adipose tissue atrophy with infiltration of CD3
title: Acquired generalized lipodystrophy complicated by fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report with review of literature and immunological insights.

text: Dose-response and time-course effects of ecnoglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy.. Ecnoglutide, a novel long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, is considered a promising therapeutic option for the treatment of diabetes
title: Dose-response and time-course effects of ecnoglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy.

text: . This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ecnoglutide in adults with type 2 diabetes and to further investigate its dose-time relationship. This study followed the PRISMA guidelines and systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library, with the search updated through February 2026
title: Dose-response and time-course effects of ecnoglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy.

text: . Randomized controlled trials comparing ecnoglutide with placebo or the active control, dulaglutide, were included. The primary outcome was the change in HbA1c (%). Secondary outcomes included FPG, PPG, 7-point SMBG, body weight, adverse events, and serious adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB-2 tool
title: Dose-response and time-course effects of ecnoglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy.

text: . Meta-analyses employed a random-effects model, and mean differences and risk ratios were calculated with 95% confidence intervals. Three randomized controlled trials involving 977 participants were included
title: Dose-response and time-course effects of ecnoglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy.

text: . Compared with placebo, ecnoglutide significantly reduced HbA1c (MD = -1.40, 95% CI -1.65, -1.14, p < 0.00001), FPG (MD = -1.98, 95% CI -2.34, -1.63, p < 0.00001), PPG (MD = -4.88, 95% CI -6.32, -3.44, p < 0.00001), and body weight (MD = -2.16, 95% CI -2.62, -1.71, p < 0.00001)
title: Dose-response and time-course effects of ecnoglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy.

text: . Additionally, compared with the placebo group, the incidence of adverse events was higher in the ecnoglutide group (OR = 2.03, 95% CI 1.24-3.32, p = 0.005), while there was no significant difference in the incidence of serious adverse events
title: Dose-response and time-course effects of ecnoglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy.

text: . Dose-response analysis showed that ecnoglutide exhibited a clear dose-dependent relationship for HbA1c, FPG, and body weight at doses ranging from 0.4 to 1.2 mg, while PPG was less affected by dose. Time-response analysis indicated that the hypoglycemic efficacy of ecnoglutide peaked around week 35 and subsequently plateaued, whereas body weight exhibited a sustained linear downward trend
title: Dose-response and time-course effects of ecnoglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy.

text: . Ecnoglutide significantly improved glycemic control and reduced body weight, although it was associated with a higher incidence of adverse events without increasing serious adverse events. Despite these promising findings, the evidence remains limited and requires confirmation in larger, multicenter randomized controlled trials
title: Dose-response and time-course effects of ecnoglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy.

text: . https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261327235, identifier CRD420261327235.
title: Dose-response and time-course effects of ecnoglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy.

text: The effectiveness of self-care interventions in working-age adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. The prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is rapidly increasing among working-age adults. This group faces unique challenges in sustaining effective self-care due to social and occupational demands
title: The effectiveness of self-care interventions in working-age adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of self-care interventions on glycemic control and self-care behaviors among working-age adults with T2DM. We searched nine databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CBM, CNKI, CQVIP, and Wan Fang) to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from January 2020 to April 2025
title: The effectiveness of self-care interventions in working-age adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Eligible studies included 18-60-year-old adults with T2DM receiving self-care interventions. Review Manager 5.4 was employed to calculate pooled mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB2 tool. Forty-seven RCTs with 6,464 participants met the inclusion criteria
title: The effectiveness of self-care interventions in working-age adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Compared to controls, self-care interventions significantly reduced HbA1c (MD -0.26, 95% CI -0.43 to -0.09), total cholesterol (MD -0.15, 95% CI -0.28 to -0.02), body mass index (MD -0.52, 95% CI -1.01 to -0.03), and increased high-density lipoproteins levels (MD 0.19, 95% CI 0.06 to 0.33)
title: The effectiveness of self-care interventions in working-age adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Improvements were also observed in self-care behaviors (SMD 0.74, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.86) and self-efficacy (SMD 1.14, 95% CI 0.51 to 1.76). No significant effects were found for fasting blood glucose or 2-hour plasma glucose. Substantial heterogeneity existed across studies
title: The effectiveness of self-care interventions in working-age adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Substantial heterogeneity existed across studies. Self-care interventions improved glycemic control and related outcomes in working-age adults with T2DM, although high heterogeneity and variable study quality limited interpretation and generalizability
title: The effectiveness of self-care interventions in working-age adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Future trials should adopt standardized reporting systems for interventions, robust design, and longer follow-up to better inform clinical practice and public health policy. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251037017, identifier CRD420251037017.
title: The effectiveness of self-care interventions in working-age adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: COVID-19 and subsequent risk of coded diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.. Evidence remains limited regarding whether coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is associated with the subsequent risk of EHR-recorded diabetic retinopathy (DR) during available follow-up in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
title: COVID-19 and subsequent risk of coded diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.

text: . We evaluated the risk of EHR-recorded DR and clinically relevant DR subtypes after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection during follow-up within a maximum 5-year analytic window. This retrospective multicenter cohort study used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network
title: COVID-19 and subsequent risk of coded diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.

text: . Adults with T2DM were classified into COVID-19 and control groups between January 1, 2020, and June 30, 2022. A 6-month landmark design was applied to reduce early outcome misclassification. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 773,768 patients were included in each group. The primary outcome was electronic health record (EHR)-recorded incident DR
title: COVID-19 and subsequent risk of coded diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.

text: . Secondary outcomes included EHR-recorded DR subtypes (non-proliferative DR, proliferative DR, and diabetic macular edema) and glycemic events, including hyperglycemia (glucose ≥180 mg/dL), poor glycemic control (HbA1c ≥9%), and hypoglycemia (glucose <70 mg/dL). Secondary and supportive analyses were exploratory and were not adjusted for multiplicity
title: COVID-19 and subsequent risk of coded diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.

text: . Median follow-up was 1,487 days in the COVID-19 group and 1,634 days in controls. EHR-recorded incident DR occurred more frequently in the COVID-19 group than in the control group (2.17% vs. 1.64%; absolute risk difference, 0.53 percentage points; hazard ratio [HR], 1.51; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.48-1.55; p<0.001)
title: COVID-19 and subsequent risk of coded diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.

text: . COVID-19 was also associated with higher risks of non-proliferative DR (HR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.49-1.58), proliferative DR (HR, 1.67; 95% CI, 1.57-1.78), and diabetic macular edema (HR, 1.75; 95% CI, 1.67-1.83). In addition, COVID-19 was associated with increased risks of glycemic events
title: COVID-19 and subsequent risk of coded diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.

text: . The associations remained consistent across sensitivity analyses, including survivor-only, healthcare-visit-restricted, eye-care-visit-restricted, 1-year landmark, and 2-year landmark models. Exploratory severe-COVID analysis showed a similar direction of association
title: COVID-19 and subsequent risk of coded diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.

text: . Among adults with T2DM, COVID-19 was associated with an increased risk of EHR-recorded incident DR, including coded vision-threatening subtypes (proliferative DR and diabetic macular edema), during follow-up
title: COVID-19 and subsequent risk of coded diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.

text: . These findings suggest a possible association between COVID-19 and subsequent EHR-recorded DR during available follow-up, although residual confounding and differential ophthalmic surveillance cannot be excluded.
title: COVID-19 and subsequent risk of coded diabetic retinopathy in patients with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter propensity score-matched cohort study.

text: Serum FAM19A5 in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and its association with metabolic and inflammatory parameters: A case-control study.
title: Serum FAM19A5 in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and its association with metabolic and inflammatory parameters: A case-control study.

text: . We aimed to investigate serum levels of FAM19A5, a novel adipokine implicated in inflammation and metabolic regulation, and to examine its association with key metabolic and inflammatory markers in individuals newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
title: Serum FAM19A5 in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and its association with metabolic and inflammatory parameters: A case-control study.

text: . This case-control study included 54 patients with newly diagnosed T2DM and 54 age- and sex-matched normoglycemic controls aged 35 to 65 years. Continuous variables were summarized according to their distributions and compared using the independent-samples t test or Mann-Whitney U test, as appropriate
title: Serum FAM19A5 in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and its association with metabolic and inflammatory parameters: A case-control study.

text: . Spearman rank correlation was used to examine associations in the pooled sample, with false discovery rate correction for multiple testing. Subgroup analyses were conducted by metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, and body mass index (BMI) category
title: Serum FAM19A5 in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and its association with metabolic and inflammatory parameters: A case-control study.

text: . The incremental value of FAM19A5 beyond conventional markers was explored using multivariable logistic regression and DeLong comparisons of the areas under the curve (AUCs). Serum FAM19A5 was lower in the T2DM group than in controls (376.1 [312.1-577.6] vs 554.5 [365.6-1524.2] ng/L; P < .001)
title: Serum FAM19A5 in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and its association with metabolic and inflammatory parameters: A case-control study.

text: . In the pooled sample, FAM19A5 was inversely correlated with fasting glucose (ρ = -0.266, P = .005), 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test (ρ = -0.308, P = .001), and HbA1c (ρ = -0.212, P = .028), but not with BMI, waist circumference, lipid parameters, homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), or high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP)
title: Serum FAM19A5 in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and its association with metabolic and inflammatory parameters: A case-control study.

text: . After false discovery rate correction, the associations with fasting and 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test remained significant. Within the T2DM group, FAM19A5 was lower in patients with metabolic syndrome (P = .004), insulin resistance (HOMA-IR > 2.71; P = .023), or BMI ≥25 kg/m² (P = .021). FAM19A5 alone showed poor discrimination for T2DM (AUC: 0.684; sensitivity: 66.7%; specificity: 53.7%)
title: Serum FAM19A5 in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and its association with metabolic and inflammatory parameters: A case-control study.

text: . Adding FAM19A5 to a model containing BMI, HOMA-IR, and hs-CRP improved model fit (likelihood-ratio χ² = 13.1, P < .001) but not discrimination (AUC: 0.920 vs 0.943; DeLong P = .154). Serum FAM19A5 levels were lower in newly diagnosed T2DM and remained independently associated with diabetes status after adjustment for BMI, HOMA-IR, and hs-CRP
title: Serum FAM19A5 in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and its association with metabolic and inflammatory parameters: A case-control study.

text: . Correlations with glycemic measures were weak, and FAM19A5 alone had poor discriminatory performance. These findings support further investigation of FAM19A5 as a molecule of potential mechanistic interest, but not as a clinically useful diagnostic biomarker. Larger longitudinal studies are needed.
title: Serum FAM19A5 in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and its association with metabolic and inflammatory parameters: A case-control study.

text: Feasibility of Multi-Wavelength LED Irradiation on the Skull and Preliminary Glycemic Outcomes in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes: A Prospective Pilot Study.. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by impaired glucose homeostasis, insulin resistance, and progressive β-cell dysfunction
title: Feasibility of Multi-Wavelength LED Irradiation on the Skull and Preliminary Glycemic Outcomes in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes: A Prospective Pilot Study.

text: . Increasing evidence suggests that glucose homeostasis is regulated not only by peripheral metabolic organs but also by central nervous system and autonomic pathways. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has been reported to modulate mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, vascular responses, and neural activity; however, its potential influence on glycemic outcomes remains largely unexplored
title: Feasibility of Multi-Wavelength LED Irradiation on the Skull and Preliminary Glycemic Outcomes in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes: A Prospective Pilot Study.

text: . This prospective pilot study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of applying multi-wavelength LED irradiation to a predefined cranial region and to explore preliminary glycemic outcomes in individuals with T2DM. Seven participants with physician-diagnosed T2DM receiving stable antidiabetic medication regimens were enrolled
title: Feasibility of Multi-Wavelength LED Irradiation on the Skull and Preliminary Glycemic Outcomes in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes: A Prospective Pilot Study.

text: . Multi-wavelength LED irradiation (660, 850, and 940 nm) was applied bilaterally to the predefined S3 region of the skull
title: Feasibility of Multi-Wavelength LED Irradiation on the Skull and Preliminary Glycemic Outcomes in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes: A Prospective Pilot Study.

text: . Irradiation parameters included an irradiance of 5 mW/cm Following the four-week intervention, fasting blood glucose and mean blood glucose were significantly reduced ( Multi-wavelength LED irradiation applied to the predefined S3 region of the skull was feasible, safe, and well tolerated in individuals with T2DM
title: Feasibility of Multi-Wavelength LED Irradiation on the Skull and Preliminary Glycemic Outcomes in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes: A Prospective Pilot Study.

text: . The observed preliminary glycemic outcomes support the feasibility of further investigation in larger randomized controlled trials. However, because of the small sample size, absence of a control group, and exploratory study design, the present findings should be interpreted cautiously and should not be considered evidence of clinical efficacy or causal effects.
title: Feasibility of Multi-Wavelength LED Irradiation on the Skull and Preliminary Glycemic Outcomes in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes: A Prospective Pilot Study.

text: Comparative Evaluation of Traditional and Emerging Glycemic Biomarkers in Diabetes.. Diabetes mellitus is a worldwide metabolic disorder that can be debilitating to many if uncontrolled. Biomarkers, such as hemoglobin A1C and glycated albumin, are central to the effort to control diabetes
title: Comparative Evaluation of Traditional and Emerging Glycemic Biomarkers in Diabetes.

text: . These each have their own advantages and disadvantages, and there is much ongoing research into development of improved biomarkers and biomarker measurement methods. Continuous glucose monitoring is also widely used to closely monitor diabetes in patients today. Increasingly, however, there has been research focusing on the use of biomarkers in alternative mediums, such as tear fluid or saliva
title: Comparative Evaluation of Traditional and Emerging Glycemic Biomarkers in Diabetes.

text: . This review efficiently summarizes the current biomarkers used clinically today, their advantages and disadvantages, and the biomarkers on the horizon that could advance how diabetes is treated in the future.
title: Comparative Evaluation of Traditional and Emerging Glycemic Biomarkers in Diabetes.

text: Mobile Health Interventions to Support Self-Management in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes.. Youth with type 1 diabetes face demanding daily self-management requirements. Mobile health interventions are a promising approach for supporting diabetes self-management both within clinical care and in everyday contexts
title: Mobile Health Interventions to Support Self-Management in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes.

text: . This review synthesizes recent evidence published between 2018 and 2024 on mobile health interventions designed to support self-management in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes. Forty-four studies met inclusion criteria. Most were early-phase evaluations emphasizing feasibility, usability, and engagement
title: Mobile Health Interventions to Support Self-Management in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes.

text: . Across modalities, mHealth interventions were most successful at lowering hemoglobin A1c when they provided real-time, actionable support during insulin dosing or carbohydrate estimation. Engagement trajectory emerged as an important determinant of clinical benefit, suggesting that initial usability alone are insufficient to produce meaningful clinical impact
title: Mobile Health Interventions to Support Self-Management in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes.

text: . Mobile health interventions for youth with type 1 diabetes are feasible, acceptable, and effective for improving self-management processes and psychosocial outcomes. Glycemic improvements occur selectively when interventions provide point-of-need decision support and when engagement is sustained
title: Mobile Health Interventions to Support Self-Management in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes.

text: . Future research should prioritize mechanisms of action, strategies to support long-term engagement, and rigorous effectiveness-implementation trials to support scalable clinical impact.
title: Mobile Health Interventions to Support Self-Management in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes.

text: Plasma Homocysteine as a Biomarker for Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study From Western Algeria.. Background Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of premature morbidity and mortality among individuals living with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM)
title: Plasma Homocysteine as a Biomarker for Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study From Western Algeria.

text: . Although overt cardiovascular events are uncommon during childhood, endothelial dysfunction and subclinical atherosclerosis develop early, making timely cardiovascular risk assessment essential. Plasma homocysteine has emerged as a potential biomarker of vascular injury; however, its clinical value in pediatric T1DM remains controversial, and evidence from African populations is scarce
title: Plasma Homocysteine as a Biomarker for Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study From Western Algeria.

text: . This study aimed to evaluate plasma homocysteine concentrations in children and adolescents with T1DM and to investigate their relationship with cardiovascular risk profiles and diabetes-related complications. Methods A cross-sectional observational study was conducted at the Department of Pediatrics B, in the university hospital center of Oran, Algeria
title: Plasma Homocysteine as a Biomarker for Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study From Western Algeria.

text: . A total of 50 children and adolescents aged 5-19 years with confirmed T1DM were included. Demographic, anthropometric, clinical, and laboratory data were retrospectively collected from medical records. Plasma total homocysteine (tHcy) concentrations, glycemic control, lipid profile, diabetes duration, insulin therapy, nephropathy, and cardiovascular risk factors were analyzed
title: Plasma Homocysteine as a Biomarker for Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study From Western Algeria.

text: . Hyperhomocysteinemia prevalence was determined, and its association with cardiovascular risk stratification was assessed using descriptive and inferential statistical analyses. Results The study included 27 male (54%) and 23 female patients (46%), and hyperhomocysteinemia was identified in 17 of 50 participants (34%)
title: Plasma Homocysteine as a Biomarker for Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study From Western Algeria.

text: . Plasma tHcy concentrations were significantly higher in participants with HbA1c >7.5% than in those with HbA1c ≤7.5% (18.9 ± 5.8 vs. 11.8 ± 3.9 μmol/L; Student's t-test, t = 4.44, p < 0.001)
title: Plasma Homocysteine as a Biomarker for Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study From Western Algeria.

text: . text: Diabetic Myonecrosis: An Under-Recognised Complication of Poorly Controlled Diabetes with a High Morbidity- A Clinico-Radiological Study.. Diabetic myonecrosis is an uncommon and under-recognised complication of diabetes mellitus. title: Diabetic Myonecrosis: An Under-Recognised Complication of Poorly Controlled Diabetes with a High Morbidity- A Clinico-Radiological Study.
journal: Indian journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . This retrospective study included 30 patients diagnosed with diabetic myonecrosis between 2002 and 2024. Diagnosis - based on clinical suspicion, supported by characteristic ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging. Demographic data, diabetes characteristics, biochemical parameters, imaging features, management approaches, recurrence, and mortality were analysed
title: Diabetic Myonecrosis: An Under-Recognised Complication of Poorly Controlled Diabetes with a High Morbidity- A Clinico-Radiological Study.
journal: Indian journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . The mean age was 49.1 ± 11.7 years, with a mean diabetes duration of 12.6 ± 6.9 years and poor glycaemic control (HbA1c 8.83 ± 1.88%). Acute limb pain and swelling were the most common presentations (93.3%), predominantly involving the thigh and calf muscles
title: Diabetic Myonecrosis: An Under-Recognised Complication of Poorly Controlled Diabetes with a High Morbidity- A Clinico-Radiological Study.
journal: Indian journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . MRI revealed characteristic muscle oedema and infarction, frequently extending beyond the quadriceps to involve hamstrings, adductors, and posterior compartments. journal: Indian journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . Diabetic myonecrosis should be considered in patients with diabetes who present with acute localised muscle pain; the presence of advanced CKD, significant proteinuria, or hypoalbuminemia identifies those at increased risk of adverse outcomes. MRI is the diagnostic modality of choice

text: Prevalence and Microbial Association of Onychomycosis in Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Observational Study..  Onychomycosis is a common fungal nail infection among individuals with diabetes mellitus and may contribute to diabetic foot complications by altering the local microbial environment and increasing the risk of secondary bacterial infection
title: Prevalence and Microbial Association of Onychomycosis in Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Observational Study.

text: . This study aimed to determine the prevalence of onychomycosis and evaluate its association with clinical and microbiological characteristics among patients with diabetic foot ulcers.  This retrospective observational study included 226 adult patients with diabetic foot ulcers treated at a tertiary referral center in South Kerala, India
title: Prevalence and Microbial Association of Onychomycosis in Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Observational Study.

text: . Clinical records were reviewed to obtain demographic, clinical, and microbiological data. Onychomycosis was diagnosed based on compatible clinical findings with microbiological confirmation using potassium hydroxide microscopy and/or fungal culture. Categorical variables were summarized using frequencies and percentages
title: Prevalence and Microbial Association of Onychomycosis in Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Observational Study.

text: . Univariate binary logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with onychomycosis.  Of the 226 patients included in the study, 85 (37.6%) had confirmed onychomycosis. Among patients with onychomycosis, 35 (41.2%) were aged 61-70 years, 54 (63.5%) were male, and 60 (70.6%) had diabetes duration >10 years
title: Prevalence and Microbial Association of Onychomycosis in Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Observational Study.

text: . Poor glycemic control (HbA1c >9%) was observed in 43 (50.6%) patients, while peripheral neuropathy was present in 73 (85.9%). Polymicrobial ulcer cultures were identified in 44 (51.8%) patients with onychomycosis. Gram-negative bacilli were isolated in 49 (57.6%) patients,   More than one-third of patients with diabetic foot ulcers had concomitant onychomycosis
title: Prevalence and Microbial Association of Onychomycosis in Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Observational Study.

text: . Longer duration of diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, polymicrobial infection, Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation, and osteomyelitis were significantly associated with onychomycosis. Routine nail examination and timely identification of fungal nail infection may complement comprehensive diabetic foot assessment and help identify patients at increased risk of complicated foot infections.
title: Prevalence and Microbial Association of Onychomycosis in Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Observational Study.

text: Off-label Use of the Tandem t: slim X2™ with Control IQ® in Pregnancy: Insights from Five Case Studies.. Hybrid closed-loop systems (HCLS), such as the Tandem t: slim X2™, are widely used in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and have well-established benefits in glycemic control. However, evidence supporting their use during pregnancy and the peripartum period remains limited
title: Off-label Use of the Tandem t: slim X2™ with Control IQ® in Pregnancy: Insights from Five Case Studies.

text: . We conducted a descriptive observational case series from August 2024 to February 2026 of five pregnant women with T1DM using the Tandem t: slim X2™ with Control- IQ® off-label during pregnancy, labor, and the early postpartum period
title: Off-label Use of the Tandem t: slim X2™ with Control IQ® in Pregnancy: Insights from Five Case Studies.

text: . Glycemic control improved during pregnancy, with mean TIRp increasing from 50.9±17.9% before HCLS initiation to 61.0±14.4% in the third trimester, alongside a reduction in HbA1c from 7.2±1.0% to 6.0±0.5%. Preeclampsia occurred in three of the five cases
title: Off-label Use of the Tandem t: slim X2™ with Control IQ® in Pregnancy: Insights from Five Case Studies.

text: . Preeclampsia occurred in three of the five cases. In Cases 1 to 4, HCLS remained in automated mode during labor and delivery, with Sleep Activity activated for 33%-40% of the time and latethird- trimester settings maintained. Case 5 suspended HCLS before labor and restarted two days postpartum
title: Off-label Use of the Tandem t: slim X2™ with Control IQ® in Pregnancy: Insights from Five Case Studies.

text: . Mean pregnancy-specific time in range (TIRp) during labor and delivery was 64.3±10.7%, with minimal hypoglycemia (1.5±2.6%). Early postpartum period (days 1-3) mean TIR was 80.8±14.6%, and time below range (TBR) was 2.3±1.1%. Neonatal hypoglycemias were reported in three of the five cases
title: Off-label Use of the Tandem t: slim X2™ with Control IQ® in Pregnancy: Insights from Five Case Studies.

text: . This case series suggests that Tandem t: slim X2™ Control-IQ® is safe and may improve glycemic control during pregnancy and the peripartum period. Further studies comparing this approach with standard care are needed to comprehensively evaluate its effects on glycemic control and maternal and neonatal outcomes.
title: Off-label Use of the Tandem t: slim X2™ with Control IQ® in Pregnancy: Insights from Five Case Studies.

text: Effect of Self-Acupressure on Neuropathic Pain and HbA1c in Type 2 Diabetes.. This study aimed to determine the effect of self-administered acupressure on peripheral neuropathic pain and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels in patients with type 2 diabetes. This study was designed as a parallel-group randomized controlled trial with intervention (n = 30) and control (n = 30) groups
title: Effect of Self-Acupressure on Neuropathic Pain and HbA1c in Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses

text: . Participants in the intervention group performed self-administered acupressure on designated points three times per week for a duration of 3 months. No intervention was applied to the control group. In both groups, HbA1c levels and neuropathic pain levels (Douleur Neuropathique 4 [DN4]) were assessed at the beginning of the data collection process and after 3 months
title: Effect of Self-Acupressure on Neuropathic Pain and HbA1c in Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses

text: . Sample size calculation was based on an assumed effect size of Cohen's d = 0.50; statistical significance was set at p < .05, and the main outcomes were reported with 95% confidence intervals
title: Effect of Self-Acupressure on Neuropathic Pain and HbA1c in Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses

text: . Following the intervention, the total DN4 score for neuropathic pain in the intervention group showed a statistically significant decrease compared to the control group (7.07 ± 1.46 → 3.73 ± 1.39) (p < .001). Similarly, postintervention HbA1c levels in the intervention group were significantly lower than those in the control group (8.60 ± 1.62 → 7.41 ± 1.21) (p < .001)

journal: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses

text: . Self-administered acupressure may be effective in lowering HbA1c and neuropathic pain levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes. title: Effect of Self-Acupressure on Neuropathic Pain and HbA1c in Type 2 Diabetes.

text: Rapid Deterioration of Glycaemic Control Revealing Interval Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer Despite a Recent Normal CT Scan.. New-onset diabetes in the elderly or acute deterioration of glycaemic control in already known diabetics is sometimes linked with suspicion of pancreatic malignancy
title: Rapid Deterioration of Glycaemic Control Revealing Interval Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer Despite a Recent Normal CT Scan.

text: . We report the case of an 81-year-old woman with long-standing, type 2 diabetes, well-controlled on gliclazide, who developed worsening glycaemic control over four months. A contrast-enhanced CT scan performed for an unrelated indication four months earlier was reported as normal
title: Rapid Deterioration of Glycaemic Control Revealing Interval Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer Despite a Recent Normal CT Scan.

text: . She presented with symptomatic hyperglycaemia with acutely deranged capillary blood sugar levels and a markedly elevated glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c), without evidence of infection or other precipitating factors
title: Rapid Deterioration of Glycaemic Control Revealing Interval Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer Despite a Recent Normal CT Scan.

text: . Repeat imaging demonstrated a necrotic pancreatic mass with metastatic disease and concurrent saddle pulmonary embolism. This case demonstrates that pancreatic malignancy may become apparent despite previously normal imaging and illustrates the diagnostic challenge when longstanding diabetes suddenly deteriorates.
title: Rapid Deterioration of Glycaemic Control Revealing Interval Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer Despite a Recent Normal CT Scan.

text: Identification of differentially expressed plasma small extracellular vesicles miRNAs as biomarkers for type 2 diabetes.. The prevalence of Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) has increased over the years. text: . This study aimed to identify sets of dysregulated miRNAs in plasma small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) as biomarkers for T2D diagnosis. This study was part of the Rice Intervention for Chronic Health (RICH) trial. Plasma sEVs were isolated from T2D and control subjects and characterized. The sEVs-miRNAs expressions were compared using next generation sequencing and validated using digital PCR
title: Identification of differentially expressed plasma small extracellular vesicles miRNAs as biomarkers for type 2 diabetes.

text: . Bioinformatic analyses were performed to study the roles of dysregulated miRNAs. Plasma proteins were profiled to study the systemically dysregulated T2D pathways. The levels of miR-142-3p and miR-454-3p were increased in plasma sEVs of T2D subjects. Among a subgroup of T2D subjects in whom glycemic control improved (n = 13), these two upregulated miRNAs also decreased
title: Identification of differentially expressed plasma small extracellular vesicles miRNAs as biomarkers for type 2 diabetes.

This study provided preliminary evidence of sEVs-miRNAs in future clinical use for T2D management.

text: Glycemic control predicts the Brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels in diabetic neuropathy patients with a diabetic duration of at least 5 years: A cross-sectional study.. Diabetic neuropathy is one of the complications of diabetes that occurs due to poor glycemic control
title: Glycemic control predicts the Brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels in diabetic neuropathy patients with a diabetic duration of at least 5 years: A cross-sectional study.

text: . Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) levels can increase when patients are first diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus and can change in response to glycemic control conditions throughout the course of the disease. However, the correlation between glycemic control and BDNF remains unclear
title: Glycemic control predicts the Brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels in diabetic neuropathy patients with a diabetic duration of at least 5 years: A cross-sectional study.

text: . The objective of this study was to investigate whether glycemic control can predict the BDNF levels in patients with diabetic neuropathy, based on diabetic duration. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 8 patients with diabetic neuropathy who were treated at a clinic in Central Java
title: Glycemic control predicts the Brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels in diabetic neuropathy patients with a diabetic duration of at least 5 years: A cross-sectional study.

text: . We use glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels as a parameter of glycemic control, which were measured according to the National Glycohemoglobin Standardization Program. BDNF serum levels were evaluated using the Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) method in the laboratory. Analysis was performed using ANCOVA tests
title: Glycemic control predicts the Brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels in diabetic neuropathy patients with a diabetic duration of at least 5 years: A cross-sectional study.

text: . Analysis was performed using ANCOVA tests. Together, HbA1c levels, diabetic duration, and interactions between diabetic duration and HbA1c explained 9.9% of variability in BDNF levels (p=0.046). However, HbA1c levels explained 8.1% of the variability in BDNF levels (p = 0.011), with only minor contributions from diabetic duration and interaction them
title: Glycemic control predicts the Brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels in diabetic neuropathy patients with a diabetic duration of at least 5 years: A cross-sectional study.

text: . The HbA1c levels significantly explained the variability in BDNF levels in patients with diabetic neuropathy regardless of diabetic duration.
title: Glycemic control predicts the Brain-derived neurotrophic factor levels in diabetic neuropathy patients with a diabetic duration of at least 5 years: A cross-sectional study.

text: Efficacy of Automated Insulin Delivery Systems in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.. Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems couple continuous glucose monitoring with an algorithm that modulates subcutaneous insulin in real time
title: Efficacy of Automated Insulin Delivery Systems in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.

text: . The efficacy of these systems in children and adolescents-whose management is complicated by variable insulin requirements, unpredictable food intake, and caregiver dependence-warrants dedicated synthesis
title: Efficacy of Automated Insulin Delivery Systems in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.

text: . We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov to June 30, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing AID with non-automated insulin therapy in participants aged 18 years or younger with type 1 diabetes
title: Efficacy of Automated Insulin Delivery Systems in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.

text: . The protocol specified that, if more than 10 eligible trials were identified, inclusion would be restricted to reports published on or after January 1, 2020; this criterion was subsequently applied. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis
title: Efficacy of Automated Insulin Delivery Systems in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.

text: . Ten trials involving 888 children and adolescents aged 1-18 years met the inclusion criteria. Where time in range was the primary endpoint, AID conferred between-group increases of 8.7 to 12.4 percentage points, equivalent to roughly two to three additional hours in target range daily, with the largest effect observed in children aged 2 to under 6 years
title: Efficacy of Automated Insulin Delivery Systems in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.

text: . Where HbA1c was the primary endpoint, reductions of 0.32% to 0.5% favored AID, with the greatest absolute benefit among participants furthest from target.
