text: Community Care Consultations for Veterans with Diabetic Foot Ulcers.. To quantify community care consultations for patients with newly diagnosed diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs), identify associated patient- and facility-level characteristics, and measure time to specialty care within and outside the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). A retrospective cohort study
title: Community Care Consultations for Veterans with Diabetic Foot Ulcers.
journal: The American journal of managed care

text: . A retrospective cohort study. This study included patients 65 years and older with newly diagnosed DFUs who received specialty care between 2019 and 2023. Data were sourced from the VHA Corporate Data Warehouse and linked Medicare data
title: Community Care Consultations for Veterans with Diabetic Foot Ulcers.
journal: The American journal of managed care

text: . Community care consultation was defined as receiving specialized consultations (ie, podiatry, vascular surgery, infectious disease, endocrinology) at a community health care system within 1 year of DFU diagnosis
title: Community Care Consultations for Veterans with Diabetic Foot Ulcers.
journal: The American journal of managed care

text: . Patient demographics, comorbidities, and facility characteristics were analyzed with multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models to assess factors associated with community care consultation while controlling for facility-level clustering. A total of 60,121 patients with a new diagnosis of DFU were included. Of these, 29.2% had a community care consultation
title: Community Care Consultations for Veterans with Diabetic Foot Ulcers.
journal: The American journal of managed care

text: . Those receiving community care were more often older, White, living in a rural area, and cared for in lower-complexity facilities. Patients were more frequently referred to community care for vascular surgery, infectious disease, and endocrinology consultations than for podiatry
title: Community Care Consultations for Veterans with Diabetic Foot Ulcers.
journal: The American journal of managed care

text: . For all specialties, the time to a new consultation was longer for community care than for a consultation within the VHA. Community care consultations for patients with DFUs in the VHA system were substantial but varied significantly across facilities. Rural and lower-complexity facilities relied more on community care, particularly for vascular surgery, infectious disease, and endocrinology
title: Community Care Consultations for Veterans with Diabetic Foot Ulcers.
journal: The American journal of managed care

text: . Future research should explore the impact of community care on DFU outcomes and strategies to enhance multidisciplinary care coordination.
title: Community Care Consultations for Veterans with Diabetic Foot Ulcers.
journal: The American journal of managed care

text: Targeting neurovascular dysfunction in diabetic neuropathic pain: a review of mechanism-based pharmacotherapy beyond gabapentinoids.. Diabetic neuropathic pain (DNP) is a condition that affects about 20-30% of people with diabetes, significantly reducing health-related quality of life and having a significant economic impact on healthcare economics
title: Targeting neurovascular dysfunction in diabetic neuropathic pain: a review of mechanism-based pharmacotherapy beyond gabapentinoids.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

text: . Although conventional "gold standard" treatments such as gabapentinoids, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), and tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) are widely used in the clinic, a substantial number of patients have poor results with these medications in terms of the quality of their analgesia or their systemic side effects
title: Targeting neurovascular dysfunction in diabetic neuropathic pain: a review of mechanism-based pharmacotherapy beyond gabapentinoids.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

text: . In order to overcome these drawbacks, this review examines the status of the current pharmacotherapy and evaluates the new classes of drugs in late-stage clinical development
title: Targeting neurovascular dysfunction in diabetic neuropathic pain: a review of mechanism-based pharmacotherapy beyond gabapentinoids.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

text: . A thorough search of PubMed, Google Scholar, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov (2015-2025) of randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses reveals a clear ceiling effect for the traditional gabapentinoids in terms of therapeutic benefit
title: Targeting neurovascular dysfunction in diabetic neuropathic pain: a review of mechanism-based pharmacotherapy beyond gabapentinoids.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

text: . On the other hand, new mechanistically targeted therapies like selective Nav1.7 sodium channel blockers, alternative voltage-gated calcium channel ligands, and angiotensin II AT2 receptor antagonists show therapeutic potential and achieve marked improvement in pain scores while maintaining improved safety profiles
title: Targeting neurovascular dysfunction in diabetic neuropathic pain: a review of mechanism-based pharmacotherapy beyond gabapentinoids.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

text: . Moreover, new lines of therapy are emerging with the incorporation of advanced non-systemic and integrative treatments such as the development of nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems, phytoconstituents with therapeutic properties, structured physical exercise and advanced neuromodulation therapies, which are aimed at reducing the effect of neuroinflammation and microvascular damage
title: Targeting neurovascular dysfunction in diabetic neuropathic pain: a review of mechanism-based pharmacotherapy beyond gabapentinoids.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

text: . Finally, modern management of DNP is shifting to a mechanism-based approach. A change from a generic, empirical drug prescription to a more precise, individual-based approach to drug prescription (phenotypic pain profile) has great potential to improve therapeutic outcomes, especially for refractory diabetic neuropathy.
title: Targeting neurovascular dysfunction in diabetic neuropathic pain: a review of mechanism-based pharmacotherapy beyond gabapentinoids.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

text: Endocrinologists' Perspectives on Early Screening for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Phenomenological Study in Four Chinese Based Hospitals.
title: Endocrinologists' Perspectives on Early Screening for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Phenomenological Study in Four Chinese Based Hospitals.
journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy

text: . This study aims to explore endocrinologists' awareness and current practices regarding early screening for diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN), and to further analyze their experiences, barriers, and potential optimization strategies in implementing DPN screening within clinical practice. Methods: A qualitative study based on Husserl's phenomenological framework was conducted
title: Endocrinologists' Perspectives on Early Screening for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Phenomenological Study in Four Chinese Based Hospitals.
journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy

text: . Twelve endocrinologists (3 male, 9 female; age range 29-47 years; clinical experience 3-23 years) from four tertiary hospitals in China were recruited via purposive sampling. Semi-structured in-depth interviews were used
title: Endocrinologists' Perspectives on Early Screening for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Phenomenological Study in Four Chinese Based Hospitals.
journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy

text: . Semi-structured in-depth interviews were used. This phenomenological approach was chosen to explore the lived experiences and subjective perceptions of physicians regarding DPN screening, as quantitative methods cannot capture such contextual richness. Data were analyzed using NVivo 20.0 with Colaizzi's seven-step method
title: Endocrinologists' Perspectives on Early Screening for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Phenomenological Study in Four Chinese Based Hospitals.
journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy

text: . Five major themes and 11 sub-themes were identified: The most predominant finding was that, despite endocrinologists' recognition of the necessity and urgency of early DPN screening, its implementation is critically limited by three interrelated barriers: insufficient physician training and heavy workloads, limitations of screening tools (eg subjectivity of physical exams and high cost of
title: Endocrinologists' Perspectives on Early Screening for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Phenomenological Study in Four Chinese Based Hospitals.
journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy

text: subjectivity of physical exams and high cost of electromyography), and poor patient compliance due to lack of awareness and financial constraints.Other themes included current screening practices and optimization strategies
title: Endocrinologists' Perspectives on Early Screening for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Phenomenological Study in Four Chinese Based Hospitals.
journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy

text: . This study indicates that despite the critical role of early DPN screening in diabetes management, its implementation remains constrained by limited healthcare resources, limitations of screening tools, and patient-related barriers, such as awareness and affordability
title: Endocrinologists' Perspectives on Early Screening for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Phenomenological Study in Four Chinese Based Hospitals.
journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy

text: . Therefore, it is recommended to enhance physician training, standardize screening protocols, and improve patient adherence through policy support and health education to promote the widespread adoption of DPN screening.
title: Endocrinologists' Perspectives on Early Screening for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Phenomenological Study in Four Chinese Based Hospitals.
journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy

text: 'Development and evaluation of naringin-loaded phytosomes for the management of diabetic neuropathy: in vitro and in vivo studies'.. Diabetic neuropathy (DN), a common complication of type 2 diabetes, is associated with oxidative stress, inflammation, and persistent hyperglycemia. Naringin, a flavonoid with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, is limited by poor bioavailability
title: 'Development and evaluation of naringin-loaded phytosomes for the management of diabetic neuropathy: in vitro and in vivo studies'.

text: . This study aimed to develop and optimize a naringin-loaded phytosomal formulation to enhance bioavailability and evaluate its efficacy in DN. Naringin-loaded phytosomes were prepared and optimized using a Box-Behnken design to achieve high entrapment efficiency, favorable particle size, polydispersity index (PDI), and zeta potential
title: 'Development and evaluation of naringin-loaded phytosomes for the management of diabetic neuropathy: in vitro and in vivo studies'.

text: . In silico docking assessed binding with PPAR-γ, α-glycosidase, AMPK, NF-κB, and Nrf2. Ex vivo intestinal permeability studies evaluated absorption. In vivo efficacy was tested in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats by assessing pain thresholds, biochemical parameters, antioxidant enzyme activities, TNF-α levels, and gastric emptying time
title: 'Development and evaluation of naringin-loaded phytosomes for the management of diabetic neuropathy: in vitro and in vivo studies'.

text: . The optimized formulation showed 93% entrapment efficiency, desirable particle size, low PDI, stable zeta potential, and enhanced permeability. Docking confirmed strong binding to molecular targets regulating glucose metabolism and oxidative stress
title: 'Development and evaluation of naringin-loaded phytosomes for the management of diabetic neuropathy: in vitro and in vivo studies'.

text: . In vivo, naringin phytosomes significantly improved pain thresholds, reduced glucose and lipid levels, increased antioxidant enzyme activities, decreased TNF-α, and improved delayed gastric emptying compared to plain naringin. Phytosomal delivery markedly enhanced naringin's bioavailability and therapeutic potential in DN, likely due to improved uptake and multi-targeted action
title: 'Development and evaluation of naringin-loaded phytosomes for the management of diabetic neuropathy: in vitro and in vivo studies'.

text: . These findings support naringin phytosomes as a promising candidate for DN management, meriting further clinical evaluation.
title: 'Development and evaluation of naringin-loaded phytosomes for the management of diabetic neuropathy: in vitro and in vivo studies'.

text: Macrovascular burden profiles in diabetes-related foot ulceration: a latent class analysis of a regional Australian cohort.. To identify patterns of co-occurring macrovascular complications among people with diabetes-related foot ulceration (DFU) using latent class analysis (LCA) and describe characteristics associated with identified profiles
title: Macrovascular burden profiles in diabetes-related foot ulceration: a latent class analysis of a regional Australian cohort.

text: . Single-centre retrospective clinical audit with secondary observational analysis of routinely collected data. Townsville University Hospital, North Queensland, Australia. 381 adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes and at least one documented DFU managed between 2015 and 2020. LCA of ischaemic heart disease, stroke, peripheral vascular disease and heart failure
title: Macrovascular burden profiles in diabetes-related foot ulceration: a latent class analysis of a regional Australian cohort.

text: . Model selection considered information criteria, class size, classification certainty, stability and clinical interpretability. Secondary analyses compared demographic and clinical characteristics between classes. Mortality was examined descriptively because follow-up duration was inconsistently available
title: Macrovascular burden profiles in diabetes-related foot ulceration: a latent class analysis of a regional Australian cohort.

text: . A two-class model had the lowest Akaike information criterion (1464.6), Bayesian information criterion (BIC) (1500.1) and sample-size-adjusted BIC (1471.5), identifying a higher-burden profile (94/381, 24.7%) and lower-burden profile (287/381, 75.3%)
title: Macrovascular burden profiles in diabetes-related foot ulceration: a latent class analysis of a regional Australian cohort.

text: . Conditional probabilities in higher-burden versus lower-burden profiles were 80.7% vs 20.9% for ischaemic heart disease, 29.6% vs 5.1% for stroke, 63.1% vs 25.8% for peripheral vascular disease and 37.5% vs 5.6% for heart failure
title: Macrovascular burden profiles in diabetes-related foot ulceration: a latent class analysis of a regional Australian cohort.

text: . Compared with the lower-burden profile, the higher-burden profile had older age (68.83 vs 63.89 years; p=0.001), lower Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) (51.24 vs 65.77 mL/min/1.73 m²; p<0.001), higher creatinine (156.69 vs 120.39 µmol/L; p=0.013), and more hypertension (93.6% vs 78.0%; p=0.002), dyslipidaemia (87.2% vs 70.3%; p=0.002) and chronic kidney disease (54.3% vs 24.4%;
title: Macrovascular burden profiles in diabetes-related foot ulceration: a latent class analysis of a regional Australian cohort.

text: and chronic kidney disease (54.3% vs 24.4%; p<0.001)
title: Macrovascular burden profiles in diabetes-related foot ulceration: a latent class analysis of a regional Australian cohort.

text: . Smoking status differed overall (p=0.017), with current smoking more common in the higher-burden profile (38.0% vs 24.3%). Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) did not differ (8.30% vs 8.46%; p=0.628). Recorded mortality was higher in the higher-burden profile (29/78, 37.2% vs 28/269, 10.4%; p<0.001)
title: Macrovascular burden profiles in diabetes-related foot ulceration: a latent class analysis of a regional Australian cohort.

text: . Among people with DFU, LCA identified higher-macrovascular-burden and lower-macrovascular-burden profiles that largely reflected cumulative macrovascular disease rather than distinct biological phenotypes. These exploratory findings require replication in contemporary multicentre cohorts.
title: Macrovascular burden profiles in diabetes-related foot ulceration: a latent class analysis of a regional Australian cohort.

text: Associations of Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health score with prevalent microvascular complications stratified by sex and menopausal status in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.
title: Associations of Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health score with prevalent microvascular complications stratified by sex and menopausal status in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.

text: . To assess the association between Life's Essential 8 (LE8) cardiovascular health score and prevalent microvascular complications in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and to explore whether this association differed by sex and menopausal status. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 4527 adults with T2DM in the Metabolic Management Center (MMC) registry
title: Associations of Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health score with prevalent microvascular complications stratified by sex and menopausal status in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.

text: . LE8 scores were calculated based on the American Heart Association framework and categorized into low, moderate and high tiers using the 25th and 75th percentiles as cut-offs. Prevalent composite microvascular complications were defined as diabetic kidney disease, diabetic retinopathy and/or diabetic peripheral neuropathy
title: Associations of Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health score with prevalent microvascular complications stratified by sex and menopausal status in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.

text: . Multivariable logistic regression estimated prevalence ORs and 95% CIs for the associations of LE8 scores with prevalent microvascular complications. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses and interaction testing by sex and menopausal status were also conducted. Participants included 2894 men (63.9%), 557 premenopausal women (12.3%) and 1076 postmenopausal women (23.8%)
title: Associations of Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health score with prevalent microvascular complications stratified by sex and menopausal status in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.

text: . Higher LE8 scores were associated with lower prevalence odds of microvascular complications. Compared with the low LE8 group, the adjusted prevalence OR for the high LE8 group was 0.43 (95% CI 0.36 to 0.52). The inverse association differed by sex and menopausal status (p for interaction=0.027) and appeared strongest in premenopausal women (high LE8 OR: 0.17, 95% CI 0.09 to 0.33)
title: Associations of Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health score with prevalent microvascular complications stratified by sex and menopausal status in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.

text: . The RCS curves showed broadly similar inverse associations across groups. Higher LE8 scores are inversely associated with prevalent microvascular complications in Chinese adults with T2DM. The inverse association appeared strongest in premenopausal women. These findings suggest that sex and menopausal status should be considered when interpreting the observed association.
title: Associations of Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health score with prevalent microvascular complications stratified by sex and menopausal status in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.

text: Association of Chronic Vascular Complications of Diabetes With Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy: The Silesia Diabetes-Heart Project.. Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (CAN) is a serious but frequently underdiagnosed complication of diabetes mellitus (DM)
title: Association of Chronic Vascular Complications of Diabetes With Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy: The Silesia Diabetes-Heart Project.

text: . Increasing evidence suggests that CAN may coexist with other diabetes-related complications implicating the need for comprehensive screening and holistic risk assessment in people with DM. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between selected microvascular and macrovascular complications of DM with CAN
title: Association of Chronic Vascular Complications of Diabetes With Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy: The Silesia Diabetes-Heart Project.

text: . This single-center observational study included 728 adults with DM (median age 56 (IQR 42, 67) years, 53% female) participating in the Silesia Diabetes-Heart Project. Clinical data, biochemical parameters, and the presence of diabetic vascular complications, namely diabetic retinopathy (DR), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) were collected
title: Association of Chronic Vascular Complications of Diabetes With Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy: The Silesia Diabetes-Heart Project.

text: . CAN was assessed using cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests (CARTs) in accordance with the Toronto Consensus criteria. Participants were classified as having no CAN, early CAN, or definite CAN. Associations between diabetic vascular complications and CAN were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression models. CAN was present in 48.2% of participants (early CAN 32.4%, definite CAN 15.8%)
title: Association of Chronic Vascular Complications of Diabetes With Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy: The Silesia Diabetes-Heart Project.

text: . Increasing CAN severity was associated with older age, longer DM duration, higher HbA CAN is common in individuals with DM and is associated with microvascular complications, particularly DR, with a more modest association for CKD
title: Association of Chronic Vascular Complications of Diabetes With Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy: The Silesia Diabetes-Heart Project.

text: . These findings support the concept that CAN reflects systemic vascular injury in DM and highlight the importance of routine autonomic assessment especially in people with DR and CKD to identify those at increased risk of CAN.
title: Association of Chronic Vascular Complications of Diabetes With Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy: The Silesia Diabetes-Heart Project.

text: GLP-1 receptor agonists and ocular safety- Pharmacokinetic insights into ischemic optic neuropathy and diabetic retinopathy risk: A review.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have transformed the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity, but their expanding use has raised concerns about ocular safety
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and ocular safety- Pharmacokinetic insights into ischemic optic neuropathy and diabetic retinopathy risk: A review.

text: . This narrative review aimed to evaluate associations between individual GLP-1 RAs and the risk of developing non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) or diabetic retinopathy (DR), with particular emphasis on whether pharmacokinetic exposure and formulation explain within-class heterogeneity
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and ocular safety- Pharmacokinetic insights into ischemic optic neuropathy and diabetic retinopathy risk: A review.

text: . PubMed was searched through June 2026, without a lower date limit, for human clinical trials, observational studies, and meta-analyses reporting quantitative ocular outcomes; reference lists, regulatory prescribing information, and pharmacokinetic data were also reviewed. Reported hazard ratios ranged from 1.29 to 7.64 for NAION and from 0.42 to 1.76 for DR
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and ocular safety- Pharmacokinetic insights into ischemic optic neuropathy and diabetic retinopathy risk: A review.

text: . The most consistent NAION signal involved high-exposure subcutaneous semaglutide, whereas findings for oral semaglutide, liraglutide, dulaglutide, exenatide, and tirzepatide were absent, inconsistent, or weaker
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and ocular safety- Pharmacokinetic insights into ischemic optic neuropathy and diabetic retinopathy risk: A review.

text: . DR worsening was likewise most evident with high-bioavailability subcutaneous semaglutide, but appeared more closely related to rapid, large reductions in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), particularly reductions of at least 2%, than to a class-specific retinal effect
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and ocular safety- Pharmacokinetic insights into ischemic optic neuropathy and diabetic retinopathy risk: A review.

text: . Observational exposure patterns supported a preliminary, hypothesis-generating NAION threshold at a steady-state concentration (Css) of approximately 30-55 nmol/L
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and ocular safety- Pharmacokinetic insights into ischemic optic neuropathy and diabetic retinopathy risk: A review.

text: . Semaglutide 7.2 mg, with an estimated Css of approximately 230 nmol/L, and highly bioavailable oral orforglipron warrant formulation-specific postmarketing ocular surveillance, although direct evidence of NAION risk remains unavailable. Current evidence does not support class-wide prescribing restrictions
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and ocular safety- Pharmacokinetic insights into ischemic optic neuropathy and diabetic retinopathy risk: A review.

text: . An individualized approach considering patient-specific ocular risk, agent, formulation, and dose is more appropriate, while prospective studies with standardized ophthalmic endpoints are needed to establish causality and validate pharmacokinetic and pharmacogenomic risk parameters.
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and ocular safety- Pharmacokinetic insights into ischemic optic neuropathy and diabetic retinopathy risk: A review.

text: Managing Complex Wounds After Treatment Failure: Patterns Identified in an Advanced Wound Healing Center.. Chronic wounds remain a significant clinical challenge despite advances in dressings, biologics, and adjunctive therapies
title: Managing Complex Wounds After Treatment Failure: Patterns Identified in an Advanced Wound Healing Center.

text: . Patients referred to advanced wound centers following unsuccessful treatment often demonstrate recurring and potentially correctable factors that contribute to delayed healing
title: Managing Complex Wounds After Treatment Failure: Patterns Identified in an Advanced Wound Healing Center.

text: . Drawing upon observations from a quaternary referral wound center, this article focuses on recurring and potentially correctable factors encountered during evaluation of wounds that have failed to progress despite prior care. Although these patterns are neither novel nor unexpected, they continue to recur despite well-established wound care principles and treatment guidelines
title: Managing Complex Wounds After Treatment Failure: Patterns Identified in an Advanced Wound Healing Center.

text: . This article highlights common pitfalls identified in patients referred for advanced wound care evaluation
title: Managing Complex Wounds After Treatment Failure: Patterns Identified in an Advanced Wound Healing Center.

text: . Commonly encountered issues include inadequate implementation of compression therapy and lower extremity elevation, ineffective offloading in diabetic foot ulcers, limited attention to patient adherence and behavioral factors, and incomplete evaluation of underlying contributors to wound chronicity
title: Managing Complex Wounds After Treatment Failure: Patterns Identified in an Advanced Wound Healing Center.

text: . Additional patterns include continued use of outdated or nonevidence-based topical agents, misapplication of debridement principles (particularly removal of stable eschar), and incomplete evaluation of underlying pathophysiology such as vascular insufficiency
title: Managing Complex Wounds After Treatment Failure: Patterns Identified in an Advanced Wound Healing Center.

text: . Patients are frequently referred after undergoing advanced interventions, including hyperbaric oxygen therapy and grafting procedures, before optimization of fundamental wound care principles
title: Managing Complex Wounds After Treatment Failure: Patterns Identified in an Advanced Wound Healing Center.

text: . In these settings, suboptimal patient selection and sequencing of therapy, particularly in the presence of uncontrolled edema or inadequate offloading, may contribute to prolonged treatment without clinical benefit. These observations highlight recurring gaps between recommended care and real-world execution
title: Managing Complex Wounds After Treatment Failure: Patterns Identified in an Advanced Wound Healing Center.

text: . Recognition of these recurring pitfalls may improve wound healing outcomes, promote more effective use of advanced therapies, and reduce the need for escalation of care.
title: Managing Complex Wounds After Treatment Failure: Patterns Identified in an Advanced Wound Healing Center.

text: A multimodal manual therapy, exercise, and psychological intervention for painful diabetic neuropathy: the NeuOst feasibility randomised controlled trial.. People with painful diabetic neuropathy lack effective and tolerable treatments. Physical and psychological interventions may help but require further study and combination to maximise effects
title: A multimodal manual therapy, exercise, and psychological intervention for painful diabetic neuropathy: the NeuOst feasibility randomised controlled trial.

text: . This single-site, 3-arm, parallel, randomised feasibility trial tested whether a multimodal intervention combining manual therapy, exercise, and psychologically informed conversations ("NeuOst") was feasible, and a full-scale trial possible
title: A multimodal manual therapy, exercise, and psychological intervention for painful diabetic neuropathy: the NeuOst feasibility randomised controlled trial.

text: . Adults with painful diabetic neuropathy were randomised 1:1:1 to either (1) 5 individual sessions of NeuOst, (2) 5 sessions of a high-similarity control intervention with the same osteopaths, or (3) usual care
title: A multimodal manual therapy, exercise, and psychological intervention for painful diabetic neuropathy: the NeuOst feasibility randomised controlled trial.

text: . Allocation was computer-generated, and blinding was intended for assessors, research and administrative staff, and participants receiving NeuOst or the high-similarity control intervention. Feasibility and acceptability were assessed using predefined criteria. Exploratory clinical outcomes included pain, disability, and quality of life, collected up to 16 weeks post-randomisation
title: A multimodal manual therapy, exercise, and psychological intervention for painful diabetic neuropathy: the NeuOst feasibility randomised controlled trial.

text: . Thirty-six participants were randomised; targets were met for eligibility (64%), consent (88%), retention (89%), blinding, fidelity, data completeness, and acceptability. Mean NeuOst session attendance was 82%, and satisfaction was high (mean 4.8/5). No serious adverse reactions occurred. Minor adverse responses were reported by 25% of NeuOst and 42% of control intervention participants
title: A multimodal manual therapy, exercise, and psychological intervention for painful diabetic neuropathy: the NeuOst feasibility randomised controlled trial.

text: . Recruitment rates indicated that modified procedures would be needed for a larger trial. Clinical outcomes were uncertain compared with control and promising compared with usual care. The NeuOst intervention was safe, acceptable, and feasible. The trial design proved largely workable, with areas for refinement identified. Findings support progression to an effectiveness trial.
title: A multimodal manual therapy, exercise, and psychological intervention for painful diabetic neuropathy: the NeuOst feasibility randomised controlled trial.

text: Single-cell RNA sequencing in diabetic foot ulcers: pathogenesis, biomarkers, and translational potential.. Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU), a common diabetic complication driven by impaired angiogenesis, neuropathy and metabolic disorders, has complex pathogenesis and poses great challenges to clinical management
title: Single-cell RNA sequencing in diabetic foot ulcers: pathogenesis, biomarkers, and translational potential.
journal: Frontiers in clinical diabetes and healthcare

text: . Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), an emerging transcriptomic technique, allows disease profiling at single-cell resolution. This review summarizes recent advances in scRNA-seq-based DFU research, revealing that JMJD3-mediated macrophage polarization failure and dysregulated IGF-1-SP1-CD248 pathway hinder wound repair, with
title: Single-cell RNA sequencing in diabetic foot ulcers: pathogenesis, biomarkers, and translational potential.
journal: Frontiers in clinical diabetes and healthcare

text: Moxibustion combinations for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a network meta-analysis of 40 randomised trials.. Moxibustion, an external treatment used in traditional Chinese medicine, is increasingly applied to diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN). We compared the effectiveness of the principal moxibustion-containing treatment combinations for this condition
title: Moxibustion combinations for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a network meta-analysis of 40 randomised trials.

text: . We searched for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) available by 14 April 2026. Sources were PubMed, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Medical Database and VIP Database
title: Moxibustion combinations for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a network meta-analysis of 40 randomised trials.

text: . The resulting network meta-analysis (NMA) covered moxibustion (MOXI) and combinations with acupuncture therapy (ACU), massage therapy (MT), internal herbal medicine (IHM), external herbal medicine (EHM) or conventional treatment (CT)
title: Moxibustion combinations for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a network meta-analysis of 40 randomised trials.

text: . Outcomes included common peroneal and median motor nerve conduction velocity (MNCV), sensory nerve conduction velocity (SNCV), Toronto Clinical Scoring System (TCSS) score and markedly effective rate. Random-effects models in Stata MP 17.0 generated mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs)
title: Moxibustion combinations for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a network meta-analysis of 40 randomised trials.

text: . Evidence certainty was graded with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Forty studies involving 3,718 participants were included. Moderate-certainty evidence favoured MOXI+EHM over CT for common peroneal MNCV (MD = 6.14 m/s, 95% CI 3.82 to 8.46). Evidence also favoured MOXI+EHM for median MNCV (MD = 6.35 m/s, 95% CI 2.35 to 10.36)
title: Moxibustion combinations for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a network meta-analysis of 40 randomised trials.

text: . The corresponding estimate for common peroneal SNCV was MD = 8.44 m/s (95% CI 4.80 to 12.08). For median SNCV, MOXI+ACU outperformed CT (MD = 6.61 m/s, 95% CI 1.29 to 11.92). MOXI+EHM showed a similar effect (MD = 4.32 m/s, 95% CI 1.01 to 7.63). Certainty for this outcome ranged from moderate to very low
title: Moxibustion combinations for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a network meta-analysis of 40 randomised trials.

text: . Moderate-certainty evidence also showed that MOXI+EHM reduced TCSS scores (MD=-2.55 points, 95% CI -3.81 to -1.30). MOXI+EHM (RR = 1.74, 95% CI 1.27 to 2.40) and MOXI+ACU (RR = 1.59, 95% CI 1.05 to 2.41) increased the markedly effective rate versus CT
title: Moxibustion combinations for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a network meta-analysis of 40 randomised trials.

text: . Moderate-certainty evidence suggests that MOXI+EHM may improve nerve conduction, clinical symptoms and signs, and the markedly effective rate in patients with DPN. Moxibustion-based combination therapy may therefore offer a useful adjunct to conservative DPN management, although the findings require confirmation in rigorous trials
title: Moxibustion combinations for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a network meta-analysis of 40 randomised trials.

text: Pharmacological modulation of peripheral nerve excitability-a novel way to investigate sodium channel subtypes in humans.. Despite considerable progress in pain management, recommended systemic pharmacotherapy often comes with a high risk of serious side effects adversely affecting quality of life
title: Pharmacological modulation of peripheral nerve excitability-a novel way to investigate sodium channel subtypes in humans.

text: . Hence, topical routes of drug administration are currently gaining popularity in painful conditions such as diabetic peripheral neuropathy. Voltage-gated sodium channels (Nav) are expressed in peripheral nerves and are crucial for development and maintenance of neuropathic pain
title: Pharmacological modulation of peripheral nerve excitability-a novel way to investigate sodium channel subtypes in humans.

text: . Subtypes Nav1.7, 1.8, and 1.9 are highly expressed in nociceptors and are therefore interesting targets for topical pharmacotherapeutics. The aim of this study was to assess pharmacologically modulated excitability of peripheral sensory nerves using the human experimental perception threshold tracking technique, an indirect method for measuring the excitability of peripheral nerves
title: Pharmacological modulation of peripheral nerve excitability-a novel way to investigate sodium channel subtypes in humans.

text: . This randomized, placebo-controlled, and double-blinded study included 20 healthy participants. A novel electrical stimulation protocol-the Sodium channel Excitability Nociceptor Testing protocol-was used to identify alterations in Nav1.7, 1.8, and 1.9 after applying 3 (5% lidocaine, 10% phenytoin, and 2% mepyramine) topical pharmacological drugs
title: Pharmacological modulation of peripheral nerve excitability-a novel way to investigate sodium channel subtypes in humans.

text: . There was a significant difference in the relative increase in the perception threshold after drug application between drugs (P < 0.01) and between drugs and placebo (P < 0.01), except for phenytoin (P = 0.22). The computational model suggests that lidocaine and mepyramine caused different alterations of the Nav1.7, 1.8, and 1.9 currents
title: Pharmacological modulation of peripheral nerve excitability-a novel way to investigate sodium channel subtypes in humans.

text: . The Sodium channel Excitability Nociceptor Testing protocol can be used to investigate differential pharmacological alterations of specific Nav subtypes. This may lead to better insight of neurophysiological mechanisms of sensory afferents, forming the basis for targeted drug development, leading the way to stratified treatment regimens of peripheral pain.
title: Pharmacological modulation of peripheral nerve excitability-a novel way to investigate sodium channel subtypes in humans.

text: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.. Thyroid eye disease (TED) is a complex autoimmune disorder and the most common extrathyroidal manifestation of Graves' disease, characterized by orbital inflammation, tissue remodelling, and varying degrees of functional and cosmetic impairment
title: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.

text: . Although often mild, moderate-to-severe and sight-threatening forms can significantly compromise vision and quality of life. Advances in the understanding of TED pathophysiology - particularly the roles of orbital fibroblasts, thyrotropin receptor and insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor signalling- have transformed its diagnostic and therapeutic landscape
title: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.

text: . This manuscript provides a comprehensive and updated overview of epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation and management of TED. Current treatment strategies emphasize early risk-factor modification, restoration of euthyroidism, and a multidisciplinary approach tailored to disease activity and severity
title: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.

text: . Intravenous glucocorticoids remain the cornerstone of therapy for active moderate-to-severe disease, whereas adjunctive immunosuppressive agents and orbital radiotherapy are used in selected cases
title: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.

text: . The advent of targeted biologic therapies, particularly teprotumumab, as well as rituximab and tocilizumab, has significantly expanded therapeutic options and enabled a more personalized, phenotype-driven approach. Surgical rehabilitation continues to play a pivotal role in the inactive phase
title: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.

text: . Emerging therapies targeting novel molecular pathways hold promise for further improving patient outcomes. Despite these advances, challenges related to accessibility, cost, long-term safety and optimal patient selection persist. Ongoing research and international collaboration are expected to refine management strategies and enhance the quality of life of patients with TED
title: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.

text: . Thyroid eye disease (TED) is an autoimmune condition where the body’s immune system mistakenly attacks the muscles, fat and tissues surrounding the eyes. Driven by autoantibodies that target shared receptors (such as TSHR and IGF1R) in both the thyroid and orbit, activated connective tissue cells (fibroblasts) cause tissue swelling, fat expansion and scarring behind the eye
title: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.

text: . While TED can affect anyone, it is most common in women and individuals of African American or white descent
title: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.

text: . Typical symptoms include: Redness, swelling and severe eyelid retraction (pulled-back eyelids).Eye bulging (proptosis) and double vision (diplopia).Dry eye issues, ocular discomfort and corneal breakdown.In severe cases, compressed vision nerves (dysthyroid optic neuropathy, or DON), which threatens eyesight
title: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.

text: . TED usually develops within 18 months of a hyperthyroidism diagnosis (most commonly linked to Graves’ disease). It typically follows a two-phase pattern according to the classic Rundle model: an active inflammatory phase lasting 6–24 months, followed by an inactive, chronic phase marked by tissue scarring and fibrosis
title: How to manage thyroid eye disease: recent advances - a narrative review.

text: Targeting Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis, and NRF2 Signaling with Dietary Polyphenols in Diabetic Microvascular Complications: An Integrative Review.. Diabetic retinopathy, diabetic kidney disease, and diabetic peripheral neuropathy remain major causes of visual loss, kidney failure, pain, disability, and reduced quality of life despite improvements in glycemic and cardiovascular risk management
title: Targeting Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis, and NRF2 Signaling with Dietary Polyphenols in Diabetic Microvascular Complications: An Integrative Review.

text: . Oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, iron dyshomeostasis, lipid peroxidation, and sterile inflammation are shared features of these complications and converge on regulated cell-death programs
title: Targeting Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis, and NRF2 Signaling with Dietary Polyphenols in Diabetic Microvascular Complications: An Integrative Review.

text: . Ferroptosis is driven by iron-dependent phospholipid peroxidation when glutathione peroxidase 4 and complementary antioxidant systems are insufficient, whereas pyroptosis is an inflammatory lytic process executed by gasdermins after activation of inflammasome-associated or other inflammatory caspases
title: Targeting Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis, and NRF2 Signaling with Dietary Polyphenols in Diabetic Microvascular Complications: An Integrative Review.

text: . Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) connects these pathways by regulating glutathione synthesis, lipid peroxide detoxification, iron handling, mitochondrial homeostasis, and redox-sensitive inflammatory signaling
title: Targeting Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis, and NRF2 Signaling with Dietary Polyphenols in Diabetic Microvascular Complications: An Integrative Review.

text: . Dietary polyphenols may influence this network through electrophilic or kinase-dependent NRF2 activation, preservation of the SLC7A11-glutathione-GPX4 axis, modulation of iron and lipid metabolism, and inhibition of NF-kappaB, TXNIP, NLRP3, caspase-1, and gasdermin signaling
title: Targeting Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis, and NRF2 Signaling with Dietary Polyphenols in Diabetic Microvascular Complications: An Integrative Review.

text: . This integrative review critically examines mechanistic, preclinical, and human evidence for these effects in the diabetic retina, kidney, and peripheral nerve. The strongest direct preclinical evidence currently concerns corilagin, resveratrol, isoquercetin, quercetin, epigallocatechin gallate, punicalagin, and selected anthocyanin-rich or phenolic extracts
title: Targeting Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis, and NRF2 Signaling with Dietary Polyphenols in Diabetic Microvascular Complications: An Integrative Review.

text: . Human studies suggest possible benefits for albuminuria, retinal edema, endothelial function, and neuropathic outcomes, but they rarely measure ferroptosis- or pyroptosis-specific biomarkers and their results are heterogeneous
title: Targeting Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis, and NRF2 Signaling with Dietary Polyphenols in Diabetic Microvascular Complications: An Integrative Review.

text: . The proposed ferroptosis-pyroptosis-NRF2 network should therefore be viewed as a biologically plausible integrative framework rather than a clinically validated linear pathway. Future trials require chemically characterized interventions, exposure biomarkers, tissue-relevant pharmacokinetics, prespecified regulated-cell-death panels, and clinically meaningful microvascular endpoints.
title: Targeting Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis, and NRF2 Signaling with Dietary Polyphenols in Diabetic Microvascular Complications: An Integrative Review.

text: Nanosilver Dressings and 12-Week Healing in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Propensity Score-Matched Study.. Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are associated with prolonged morbidity and limb-related complications
title: Nanosilver Dressings and 12-Week Healing in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Propensity Score-Matched Study.

text: . This single-center retrospective cohort study compared nanosilver and alginate primary dressing strategies in patients managed within a multidisciplinary diabetic-foot program between January 2020 and December 2023
title: Nanosilver Dressings and 12-Week Healing in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Propensity Score-Matched Study.

text: . Among 393 screened patients, 361 formed the unmatched cohort, including 121 treated with nanosilver and 240 with alginate dressings; 1:1 propensity-score matching generated 115 matched pairs. The single primary endpoint was complete wound healing at week 12
title: Nanosilver Dressings and 12-Week Healing in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Propensity Score-Matched Study.

text: . Healing occurred in 87 of 115 patients (75.7%) receiving nanosilver and 65 of 115 (56.5%) receiving alginate dressings (matched OR, 2.47; 95% CI, 1.32-4.84; P = 0.003; matched RR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.11-1.62)
title: Nanosilver Dressings and 12-Week Healing in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Propensity Score-Matched Study.

text: . At least 50% wound-area reduction at week 4 occurred in 82.6% versus 67.0% (matched OR, 2.80; 95% CI, 1.32-6.46; Holm-adjusted P = 0.015), and median time to complete healing was 45 versus 58 days (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.22-2.05; Holm-adjusted P < 0.004). The primary association remained similar in the extended measured-confounding sensitivity analysis (adjusted OR, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.17-4.56)
title: Nanosilver Dressings and 12-Week Healing in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Propensity Score-Matched Study.

text: . Other clinical and safety outcomes were exploratory. Nanosilver dressing use was associated with greater 12-week complete healing and shorter time to closure in this matched tertiary-care cohort; prospective multicenter validation is required.
title: Nanosilver Dressings and 12-Week Healing in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Retrospective Propensity Score-Matched Study.

text: Indirect traumatic optic neuropathy in a high-risk diabetic adolescent: A rare clinical presentation.. Indirect traumatic optic neuropathy (ITON) is a rare but severe complication of craniofacial trauma. Its management remains controversial, ranging from high-dose corticosteroids and surgical decompression to observation. Comorbidities may significantly impact therapeutic decision-making
title: Indirect traumatic optic neuropathy in a high-risk diabetic adolescent: A rare clinical presentation.

text: . We report the case of a 16-year-old male patient with poorly controlled type 1 diabetes (HbA1c = 11%) who sustained a road traffic accident with craniofacial trauma. On day 3, he developed acute visual loss in his right eye. Imaging revealed a right zygomatic tripod fractures without ocular involvement and optic nerve elongation on Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), consistent with ITON
title: Indirect traumatic optic neuropathy in a high-risk diabetic adolescent: A rare clinical presentation.

text: . This case highlights a dramatic therapeutic dilemma: attempting to preserve vision at the cost of significant systemic risks. The rarity of ITON in young patients and the absence of specific guidelines for diabetic patients, make decision-making particularly challenging. Multidisciplinary discussion; Ophthalmology, maxillofacial surgery, endocrinology, intensive care was crucial
title: Indirect traumatic optic neuropathy in a high-risk diabetic adolescent: A rare clinical presentation.

text: . The management of ITON in patients with uncontrolled diabetes raises critical therapeutic, prognostic, and ethical issues. This case emphasizes the need to tailor treatment strategies and carefully weigh comorbidities in the risk-benefit balance.
title: Indirect traumatic optic neuropathy in a high-risk diabetic adolescent: A rare clinical presentation.

The proportion of patients achieving ≥50% pain relief remained at 65.6% in US cohort versus 66.7% in FL cohort at 4 weeks post-treatment, and 63.3% in US cohort versus 64.0% in FL cohort at 12 weeks post-treatment, with no significant inter-cohort differences at all follow-up time points. text: Clinical applications of invasive spinal cord stimulation in neurological disorders: a narrative review.. Invasive spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is used in selected patients with refractory chronic neuropathic pain and has also been explored in spinal cord injury, disorders of consciousness, and Parkinson's disease. However, the strength of evidence differs substantially across indications
title: Clinical applications of invasive spinal cord stimulation in neurological disorders: a narrative review.

text: . This review summarizes the current clinical applications of invasive SCS and distinguishes relatively established pain indications from emerging neurological applications. We conducted a structured search of PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, Wanfang, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure
title: Clinical applications of invasive spinal cord stimulation in neurological disorders: a narrative review.

text: . The search was supplemented by reference tracking for landmark studies and a targeted update of relevant publications from 2024 to 2026. Randomized evidence is concentrated in chronic pain populations
title: Clinical applications of invasive spinal cord stimulation in neurological disorders: a narrative review.

text: . Conventional SCS has shown benefit in selected patients with failed back surgery syndrome, while 10-kHz SCS produced greater pain reduction than conventional low-frequency stimulation in patients with chronic back and leg pain. Burst stimulation was noninferior to tonic stimulation in the SUNBURST trial and was preferred by most participants
title: Clinical applications of invasive spinal cord stimulation in neurological disorders: a narrative review.

text: . Randomized evidence also supports 10-kHz SCS in refractory painful diabetic neuropathy. Evidence for complex regional pain syndrome suggests short- to intermediate-term pain relief, although long-term benefit remains uncertain
title: Clinical applications of invasive spinal cord stimulation in neurological disorders: a narrative review.

text: . By contrast, applications in diabetic foot complications, spinal cord injury, and disorders of consciousness are supported mainly by small, heterogeneous, or uncontrolled studies. Recent blinded trials have not demonstrated a clear benefit of SCS for Parkinsonian gait impairment. The clinical evidence supporting invasive SCS varies considerably across neurological indications
title: Clinical applications of invasive spinal cord stimulation in neurological disorders: a narrative review.

text: . Its role is comparatively well supported in selected chronic neuropathic pain populations, particularly chronic back and leg pain after spinal surgery and painful diabetic neuropathy
title: Clinical applications of invasive spinal cord stimulation in neurological disorders: a narrative review.

text: . Evidence for non-pain neurological disorders remains limited, and these applications should remain investigational until further controlled studies clarify patient selection, stimulation parameters, durability of response, and safety.
title: Clinical applications of invasive spinal cord stimulation in neurological disorders: a narrative review.

text: Evaluating Improvement in Pain and Sensory Function When Using High-Frequency (10-kHz) Spinal Cord Stimulation in Individuals With Painful Diabetic Neuropathy: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (PDN-Sensory).
title: Evaluating Improvement in Pain and Sensory Function When Using High-Frequency (10-kHz) Spinal Cord Stimulation in Individuals With Painful Diabetic Neuropathy: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (PDN-Sensory).

text: . The PDN-Sensory randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluated the effects of high-frequency 10-kHz spinal cord stimulation (10-kHz SCS) on pain and sensory function in individuals with painful diabetic neuropathy (PDN). Participants were randomized 1:1 to conventional medical management (CMM) alone or 10-kHz SCS plus CMM
title: Evaluating Improvement in Pain and Sensory Function When Using High-Frequency (10-kHz) Spinal Cord Stimulation in Individuals With Painful Diabetic Neuropathy: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (PDN-Sensory).

text: . The primary and key secondary end points were the proportions of participants with pain response (≥50% lower limb pain relief) and sensory improvement (≥3-point reduction in modified Toronto Clinical Neuropathy Score [mTCNS]). Hierarchical secondary outcomes included intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD), sleep, and health and neuropathy-related quality of life (QoL)
title: Evaluating Improvement in Pain and Sensory Function When Using High-Frequency (10-kHz) Spinal Cord Stimulation in Individuals With Painful Diabetic Neuropathy: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (PDN-Sensory).

text: . IENFD and mTCNS assessments were allocation blinded. A total of 91 participants were randomly assigned to CMM alone (n = 50) or 10-kHz SCS plus CMM (n = 41). In a modified intention-to-treat worst-case analysis, 27 of 34 participants in the 10-kHz SCS group who underwent a temporary trial achieved the primary outcome, versus 2 of 50 CMM-alone participants (P < 0.001)
title: Evaluating Improvement in Pain and Sensory Function When Using High-Frequency (10-kHz) Spinal Cord Stimulation in Individuals With Painful Diabetic Neuropathy: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (PDN-Sensory).

text: . Among those with 6-month data, mTCNS sensory improvement was observed in 16 of 29 (55.2%) 10-kHz SCS participants versus 12 of 48 (25.0%) CMM-alone participants (P = 0.01). The mean change in lower-calf IENFD was 0.58 fibers/mm with 10-kHz SCS versus -0.07 with CMM alone (P = 0.03). Eight of 10 hierarchical secondary end points were met (including sleep and QoL)
title: Evaluating Improvement in Pain and Sensory Function When Using High-Frequency (10-kHz) Spinal Cord Stimulation in Individuals With Painful Diabetic Neuropathy: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (PDN-Sensory).

text: . The PDN-Sensory RCT replicated previous pain-reduction findings and showed prespecified, objective improvements in sensory function and IENFD. These 6-month findings support clinically meaningful benefit and are consistent with a potential disease-modifying effect that requires longer-term confirmation.
title: Evaluating Improvement in Pain and Sensory Function When Using High-Frequency (10-kHz) Spinal Cord Stimulation in Individuals With Painful Diabetic Neuropathy: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (PDN-Sensory).

text: Changing Patterns of Specialty Care for Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Rural and Urban Veterans Following the VA MISSION Act.. The Veterans Affairs (VA) Maintaining Internal Systems and Strengthening Integrated Outside Networks (MISSION) Act expanded eligibility for community-based care particularly for Veterans facing geographic or capacity-related barriers
title: Changing Patterns of Specialty Care for Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Rural and Urban Veterans Following the VA MISSION Act.

text: . Patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) require timely specialty management and are vulnerable to fragmented care, yet little is known about how the MISSION Act reshaped patterns of DFU-related specialty care within and outside the VA. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of Veterans aged 65 or older with a new DFU diagnosis in VA between 2016 and 2022
title: Changing Patterns of Specialty Care for Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Rural and Urban Veterans Following the VA MISSION Act.

text: . We identified DFU-related specialty encounters (podiatry, vascular surgery, infectious diseases and endocrinology) and categorised community encounters as VA-paid or Medicare-paid. We assessed annual trends in community specialty care and changes in the proportion and payer type of care before and after the MISSION Act
title: Changing Patterns of Specialty Care for Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Rural and Urban Veterans Following the VA MISSION Act.

text: . Among 76 398 patients, VA-paid community specialty care increased substantially following the MISSION Act, with larger relative growth among rural Veterans (rural: +119%; urban: +96%). In contrast, Medicare-paid DFU specialty care declined during the same period (rural: -12%; urban: -13%)
title: Changing Patterns of Specialty Care for Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Rural and Urban Veterans Following the VA MISSION Act.

text: . Following the MISSION Act, reliance on VA-paid community specialty care increased markedly for Veterans with DFU, particularly in rural areas, while reliance on Medicare-paid care decreased.
title: Changing Patterns of Specialty Care for Diabetic Foot Ulcers Among Rural and Urban Veterans Following the VA MISSION Act.

text: Uncommon indications in chronic pain for intrathecal drug delivery systems: a narrative review of the literature.. Intrathecal drug delivery systems (IDDS) have been used successfully for a number of refractory chronic pain conditions. The most common pain indications for the use of IDDS include cancer-related pain and postlaminectomy syndrome
title: Uncommon indications in chronic pain for intrathecal drug delivery systems: a narrative review of the literature.

text: . IDDS can also be used to treat a variety of other less common refractory pain conditions, including central neuropathic pain, peripheral neuropathic pain and craniofacial pain
title: Uncommon indications in chronic pain for intrathecal drug delivery systems: a narrative review of the literature.

text: . The aim of this article was to review the existing literature on the efficacy and clinical utility of IDDS for the management of uncommon pain indications, including spinal cord injury-related pain, transverse myelitis, diabetic painful neuropathy, postherpetic neuralgia and craniofacial pain to inform clinicians on the state of the current evidence of IDDS use in these challenging pain
title: Uncommon indications in chronic pain for intrathecal drug delivery systems: a narrative review of the literature.

text: evidence of IDDS use in these challenging pain conditions
title: Uncommon indications in chronic pain for intrathecal drug delivery systems: a narrative review of the literature.

text: . PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL and Cochrane databases were searched with keywords. Additionally, reference lists of retrieved articles and relevant reviews were manually screened to identify additional publications. Articles were screened for relevance using Covidence by three reviewers. Eligible studies included the use of IDDS for refractory uncommon pain conditions
title: Uncommon indications in chronic pain for intrathecal drug delivery systems: a narrative review of the literature.

text: . Exclusion criteria included non-English studies, animal studies, studies that focused on non-pain indications and abstracts without accompanied full text
title: Uncommon indications in chronic pain for intrathecal drug delivery systems: a narrative review of the literature.

text: . Given heterogeneity and largely descriptive data, findings were analyzed narratively by descriptive categories.The use of IDDS for refractory pain in patients with select pain conditions is supported primarily by observational studies and small clinical trials
title: Uncommon indications in chronic pain for intrathecal drug delivery systems: a narrative review of the literature.

text: . Current evidence suggests that the IDDS may provide meaningful analgesia in carefully selected patients with central and peripheral pain, and facial neuropathic pain; however, the magnitude of pain relief and durability of response is variable. These findings are likely reflective of the limited evidence as a result of selective utilization of this therapy in clinical practice
title: Uncommon indications in chronic pain for intrathecal drug delivery systems: a narrative review of the literature.

text: . Based on limited evidence, IDDS may provide meaningful clinical benefit in patients with refractory uncommon pain syndromes. Future research can help to define the use of IDDS in this challenging patient population.
title: Uncommon indications in chronic pain for intrathecal drug delivery systems: a narrative review of the literature.

text: Pain alleviation in diabetic neuropathy using hybrid closed loop insulin pumps (PAINLESS) - A randomised crossover trial protocol.. Painful diabetic neuropathy (PDN) is a common complication of diabetes that leads to significant co-morbidity. Emerging evidence suggests glycaemic variability may be linked to fluctuations in pain intensity
title: Pain alleviation in diabetic neuropathy using hybrid closed loop insulin pumps (PAINLESS) - A randomised crossover trial protocol.

text: . Hybrid closed loop (HCL) systems reduce glycaemic variability, raising the possibility that they may modify pain intensity. This study aims to evaluate the effects of HCL use on pain intensity in people with PDN. PAINLESS is a two-centre, randomised cross-over study, recruiting 49 adults with type 1 diabetes and PDN
title: Pain alleviation in diabetic neuropathy using hybrid closed loop insulin pumps (PAINLESS) - A randomised crossover trial protocol.

text: . Each participant will complete two 12-week intervention periods in a randomised sequence (1:1): one with standard care including continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) and one with HCL using the Tandem t:slim X2 insulin pump with Control-IQ technology
title: Pain alleviation in diabetic neuropathy using hybrid closed loop insulin pumps (PAINLESS) - A randomised crossover trial protocol.

text: . The primary outcome is the change in 7-day average 24-hour pain intensity [rated on a numerical scale from 0-10 (NRS)] from baseline to the end of each 12-week intervention period as measured by daily pain diaries
title: Pain alleviation in diabetic neuropathy using hybrid closed loop insulin pumps (PAINLESS) - A randomised crossover trial protocol.

text: . Secondary outcomes include measures of pain trajectory/durability [responder rates (30% and 50% pain reduction in 7-day NRS), and the AUC for daily NRS scores], functional and quality of life outcomes [Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), and Short Form of the Brief Pain Inventory (BPI-MSF)], mood [Beck Depression Inventory (BDI)], health status [EQ-5D-5L], and global improvement [participant and
title: Pain alleviation in diabetic neuropathy using hybrid closed loop insulin pumps (PAINLESS) - A randomised crossover trial protocol.

text: Clinical utility and medical necessity of high-purity type I collagen in hard-to-heal wound management: a review of evidence.. Hard-to-heal wounds remain a major healthcare challenge due to persistent inflammation, extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation, impaired angiogenesis and failure to progress through normal healing pathways
title: Clinical utility and medical necessity of high-purity type I collagen in hard-to-heal wound management: a review of evidence.

text: . Standard wound care alone often fails to achieve timely wound closure, necessitating biologically active therapies that restore the wound microenvironment
title: Clinical utility and medical necessity of high-purity type I collagen in hard-to-heal wound management: a review of evidence.

text: . High-purity type I collagen (HPTC) (Helicoll, EnColl Corp, Fremont, CA, US) is a uncrosslinked skin substitute designed to function as a biologically active ECM scaffold that supports tissue regeneration rather than serving solely as a passive wound covering. A comprehensive literature review was conducted of the clinical, mechanistic, technical and economic evidence supporting HPTC
title: Clinical utility and medical necessity of high-purity type I collagen in hard-to-heal wound management: a review of evidence.

text: . The evidence base included six randomised controlled trials (RCTs), pooled analyses, comparative studies, observational investigations and health-economic evaluations spanning diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs), venous leg ulcers (VLUs), pressure ulcers (PUs), burns, donor sites, surgical wounds and complex wounds
title: Clinical utility and medical necessity of high-purity type I collagen in hard-to-heal wound management: a review of evidence.

text: . Across hard-to-heal wound studies, HPTC consistently demonstrated improved healing outcomes compared with active comparators and standard therapies. DFU studies demonstrated complete closure rates up to 83.3% compared with approximately 51.7% in comparator groups, with ≥50% wound reduction observed in 85-88% of patients at 4 weeks
title: Clinical utility and medical necessity of high-purity type I collagen in hard-to-heal wound management: a review of evidence.

text: . VLU studies demonstrated closure rates approaching 70% compared with 43.3% for comparators, while PU studies demonstrated closure rates of approximately 75%. Mechanistically, preserved native collagen structure enabled physiological cell adhesion, growth factor binding, protease modulation, angiogenesis, fibroblast recruitment and ECM restoration
title: Clinical utility and medical necessity of high-purity type I collagen in hard-to-heal wound management: a review of evidence.

text: . No significant safety concerns or serious adverse events attributable to HPTC were reported. Economic analyses further demonstrated favourable cost-effectiveness, reduced application frequency and lower overall treatment costs relative to competing advanced wound therapies. HPTC is supported by multiple clinical studies that demonstrate efficacy across multiple hard-to-heal and acute wound types
title: Clinical utility and medical necessity of high-purity type I collagen in hard-to-heal wound management: a review of evidence.

text: . Preservation of native collagen architecture, absence of chemical crosslinking, physiologically relevant scaffold structure and favourable safety and economic profiles collectively support its role as an evidencebased advanced wound therapy. Evidence supports HPTC's clinical utility and integration into routine wound care practice for management of complex wounds
title: Clinical utility and medical necessity of high-purity type I collagen in hard-to-heal wound management: a review of evidence.

text: . These findings validate HPTC's medical necessity and economic value, underscoring its status as an advanced wound therapy with emerging supportive evidence rather than an experimental or investigational intervention. Funding for the preparation of this manuscript was provided by Encoll Corp (Fremont, CA, US), manufacturer of HPTC
title: Clinical utility and medical necessity of high-purity type I collagen in hard-to-heal wound management: a review of evidence.

text: . The author reports receiving support related to development of this review. The sponsor reviewed the manuscript for scientific accuracy but did not control the final interpretation or conclusions.
