text: Plasma-activated water as a wound rinse solution in patients with diabetes-related foot ulcers in two Australian hospitals: study protocol for a phase I double-blinded, randomised controlled trial.
title: Plasma-activated water as a wound rinse solution in patients with diabetes-related foot ulcers in two Australian hospitals: study protocol for a phase I double-blinded, randomised controlled trial.

text: . Patients living with diabetes-related foot ulcers (DFU) often have non-healing wounds that, despite ongoing clinical management and wound debridement as standard of care, can proceed to infection and lower limb amputation. Additionally, treatment guidelines do not recommend most topical antibiotics or antiseptic treatments, limiting complements to surgical wound debridement
title: Plasma-activated water as a wound rinse solution in patients with diabetes-related foot ulcers in two Australian hospitals: study protocol for a phase I double-blinded, randomised controlled trial.

text: . We present a protocol for a phase I randomised controlled trial testing the safety and efficacy of plasma-activated water as an antiseptic for preventing infection and promoting ulcer healing. This protocol describes a single-centre, two-armed (1:1 allocation), double-blinded, randomised controlled trial of plasma-activated water (PAW) for the treatment of non-healing DFU
title: Plasma-activated water as a wound rinse solution in patients with diabetes-related foot ulcers in two Australian hospitals: study protocol for a phase I double-blinded, randomised controlled trial.

text: . 20 participants will be randomised to the control (standard care with 10-minute treatment with saline-soaked gauze twice weekly for 6 weeks) or intervention group (same but with 10-minute treatment with PAW-soaked gauze instead)
title: Plasma-activated water as a wound rinse solution in patients with diabetes-related foot ulcers in two Australian hospitals: study protocol for a phase I double-blinded, randomised controlled trial.

text: . Primary outcome is the safety and tolerability of PAW in treating non-healing wounds, while secondary outcome is the effect on promoting wound healing and antimicrobial activity. The Central Adelaide Local Health Network Human Research Ethics Committee (2025/HRE00207) has approved the study. Results will be presented at international conferences and published in a peer-reviewed clinical journal
title: Plasma-activated water as a wound rinse solution in patients with diabetes-related foot ulcers in two Australian hospitals: study protocol for a phase I double-blinded, randomised controlled trial.

text: . This trial was registered in the Australia New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (registration number ACTRN12625000902493) on 20 August 2025.
title: Plasma-activated water as a wound rinse solution in patients with diabetes-related foot ulcers in two Australian hospitals: study protocol for a phase I double-blinded, randomised controlled trial.

text: Application of Smart Hydrogels in Diabetic Wound Management: Microenvironment-Responsive Strategies and Clinical Translation Challenges.. Diabetic wounds (DWs), characterized by pathological features of healing stagnation and limited regeneration, pose significant clinical challenges in chronic wound management and contribute to substantial consumption of healthcare resources
title: Application of Smart Hydrogels in Diabetic Wound Management: Microenvironment-Responsive Strategies and Clinical Translation Challenges.

text: . Although current clinical interventions heavily rely on debridement, offloading, and traditional wound dressings, their therapeutic efficacy often falls short of expectations due to limitations in providing only a physical barrier function
title: Application of Smart Hydrogels in Diabetic Wound Management: Microenvironment-Responsive Strategies and Clinical Translation Challenges.

text: . Furthermore, the pathogenesis of DWs involves a complex interplay of multiple pathological factors, including peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, and foot infections, which further complicates wound management
title: Application of Smart Hydrogels in Diabetic Wound Management: Microenvironment-Responsive Strategies and Clinical Translation Challenges.

text: . In recent years, hydrogels have demonstrated significant potential in the biomedical field of DW management due to their biological versatility, tunable physicochemical properties, and excellent hydrophilicity
title: Application of Smart Hydrogels in Diabetic Wound Management: Microenvironment-Responsive Strategies and Clinical Translation Challenges.

text: . By loading specific therapeutic agents, hydrogels can achieve on-demand drug release tailored to the unique physiological microenvironment of DWs and optimize the microenvironment across different stages of wound healing
title: Application of Smart Hydrogels in Diabetic Wound Management: Microenvironment-Responsive Strategies and Clinical Translation Challenges.

text: . This study systematically evaluates smart hydrogel-based integrated diagnosis and therapy strategies by analyzing pathological characteristics and clinical limitations of DWs (particularly diabetic foot ulcers), aiming to provide references for developing clinically translatable dressing systems and establish theoretical frameworks with practical guidelines for next-generation intelligent
title: Application of Smart Hydrogels in Diabetic Wound Management: Microenvironment-Responsive Strategies and Clinical Translation Challenges.

text: guidelines for next-generation intelligent dressings incorporating AI-driven data and clinical stability.
title: Application of Smart Hydrogels in Diabetic Wound Management: Microenvironment-Responsive Strategies and Clinical Translation Challenges.

text: Peripheral nerve biopsy in pure neural leprosy: a 26-year experience in Brazil.. Brazil ranks second globally in leprosy burden, with approximately 25 000 cases reported in 2022
title: Peripheral nerve biopsy in pure neural leprosy: a 26-year experience in Brazil.

text: . This study aimed to analyse the 26-year experience (1997-2023) in nerve biopsies at a specialized leprosy outpatient clinic, focusing on their usefulness in diagnosing peripheral neuropathy in patients with clinical and neurophysiological features suggestive of leprosy but lacking dermatological lesions
title: Peripheral nerve biopsy in pure neural leprosy: a 26-year experience in Brazil.

text: . Tissue samples were preserved in glutaraldehyde, buffered formalin and liquid nitrogen, with histopathological analysis using various staining techniques and molecular testing on frozen material. In 819 cases, 529 were diagnosed with leprosy (64.6% overall leprosy diagnosis rate), and 207 pure neural leprosy cases were confirmed
title: Peripheral nerve biopsy in pure neural leprosy: a 26-year experience in Brazil.

text: . Other conditions identified included vasculitis, diabetic neuropathy and amyloidosis, while 16.5% of cases yielded inconclusive results. The predominant clinical symptoms included sensory disorders (85.7%), localized paraesthesia (70.3%) and muscle weakness (59.4%), with multiple mononeuropathies frequently observed on electroneuromyography
title: Peripheral nerve biopsy in pure neural leprosy: a 26-year experience in Brazil.

text: . The most biopsied nerves were the ulnar cutaneous branch (50.6%), sural (37.2%) and superficial peroneal (6.8%). Nerve biopsy proved valuable for confirming leprosy and distinguishing differential diagnoses in complex cases, particularly when clinical findings alone were insufficient
title: Peripheral nerve biopsy in pure neural leprosy: a 26-year experience in Brazil.

text: . Integrating clinical-pathological correlation optimized diagnostic accuracy, underscoring the importance of this tool in managing suspected neural leprosy and guiding treatment in challenging cases.
title: Peripheral nerve biopsy in pure neural leprosy: a 26-year experience in Brazil.

text: Shoulder Injuries Secondary to Proning: Sequelae of Long COVID Syndrome: A Case Report.. Prolonged proning is widely used in the management of severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), most notably during the COVID-19 pandemic. Although brachial plexus injuries are recognized complications, structural shoulder injuries remain rarely reported
title: Shoulder Injuries Secondary to Proning: Sequelae of Long COVID Syndrome: A Case Report.

text: . We report a case of a patient who developed a glenoid fracture and persistent shoulder dysfunction following prolonged proning for COVID-19-related ARDS. Clinical assessment, radiological findings, and management strategies are detailed
title: Shoulder Injuries Secondary to Proning: Sequelae of Long COVID Syndrome: A Case Report.

text: . This case highlights unique mechanical and physiological risk factors for structural shoulder injury during proning, including obesity, diabetic neuropathy, prolonged intensive care unit stay, and positioningrelated stress. Structural glenohumeral injuries should be considered in patients presenting persistent shoulder dysfunction after prolonged proning
title: Shoulder Injuries Secondary to Proning: Sequelae of Long COVID Syndrome: A Case Report.

text: . Awareness and preventive positioning strategies are essential.
title: Shoulder Injuries Secondary to Proning: Sequelae of Long COVID Syndrome: A Case Report.

text: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.. Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are serious complications of diabetes, and consist of chronic wound healing, chronic biofilm infection, impaired angiogenesis, oxidized stress, and persistent inflammation
title: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.

text: . Standard treatments such as systemic antibiotics and growth factors have been found to be ineffective due to poor tissue penetration, degradation and antimicrobial resistance. The aim of this review is to critically analyze advanced strategies for combination therapy using antibiotics, growth factors and/or nanocarriers in order to better manage DFU
title: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.

text: . Literature was searched in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar databases from January 2010 to March 2026 using keywords related to DFUs, antibiotics, growth factors, nanocarriers, biofilms, and wound healing. Combination nanotherapeutic systems exhibited potential to improve local drug delivery, disrupt biofilms, promote angiogenesis and support tissue regeneration
title: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.

text: . Stimuli-responsive and sequential-release platforms could enhance therapeutic precision by synchronizing antimicrobial and regenerative functions. Controlled release and modulation of the wound microenvironment are also enhanced by engineering scaffolds and multifunctional biomaterials
title: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.

text: . Yet the hurdles of biosafety, oxidative cytotoxicity, manufacturing scale-up, regulatory approval, and extended clinical duration remain significant obstacles to translation. Advanced multifunctional nanotherapeutics represent promising emerging strategies for precision-based DFU treatment and may improve infection control, tissue regeneration, and clinical healing outcomes
title: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.

text: . DFUs are serious sores that may occur in people who have diabetes that can be hard to heal. The wounds may get infected, heal slowly and sometimes result in amputation. The use of traditional antibiotics and wound dressings can be ineffective due to inadequate delivery of drugs to the wound, or the ability of bacteria to form protective biofilms that prevent antibiotic effectiveness
title: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.

text: . New technologies for drug delivery have emerged in recent years that could enhance diabetic wound healing. Scientists are working on a new form of drug delivery that involves tiny, micro-carriers that carry antibiotics, growth factors and other therapeutic agents directly to the wound
title: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.

text: . Such systems can aid regulate infection, cut back swelling, encourage new blood vessels to form, and assist tissues to heal. In this review, the modern combination therapies which simultaneously solve multiple problems associated with DFUs are discussed, which include the use of antibiotics, growth factors and nanocarriers
title: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.

text: . It also features the latest technologies like smart drug delivery systems, hydrogels, nanofibers, and engineered scaffolds which can help to deliver medicines in a controlled manner. These methods have yielded positive results in lab and preclinical studies but have yet to be tested clinically for long-term safety and efficacy
title: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.

text: . In conclusion, the future of diabetic foot ulcer treatment with advanced nanotechnology-based therapies holds promise for more effective and personalized treatment options.
title: Combination therapy strategies for diabetic foot ulcers: synthesizing antibiotics, growth factors, and nanocarriers in modern wound management.

text: Molecular mechanisms of autophagy disorder in diabetic neuropathy: Focusing on signaling pathways and regulation of lipid metabolism.. Diabetic neuropathy, a prevalent and debilitating complication of diabetes mellitus, is characterized by progressive neuronal dysfunction
title: Molecular mechanisms of autophagy disorder in diabetic neuropathy: Focusing on signaling pathways and regulation of lipid metabolism.

text: . This study investigates the role of autophagy dysregulation in the pathogenesis of diabetic neuropathy and explores potential therapeutic interventions. Using a combination of in vitro and in vivo models, we demonstrate that chronic hyperglycemia leads to impaired autophagic flux in neurons, evidenced by decreased LC3I/II ratio and increased p62 accumulation
title: Molecular mechanisms of autophagy disorder in diabetic neuropathy: Focusing on signaling pathways and regulation of lipid metabolism.

text: . This autophagy dysfunction is associated with alterations in key signaling pathways, including mTOR activation and AMPK inhibition. Transcriptomic analysis reveals dysregulation of autophagy-related transcription factors, notably TFEB, FOXO3, and NRF2
title: Molecular mechanisms of autophagy disorder in diabetic neuropathy: Focusing on signaling pathways and regulation of lipid metabolism.

text: . We identify a novel bidirectional relationship between autophagy impairment and lipid metabolism dysregulation, suggesting a potential vicious cycle contributing to neuronal dysfunction
title: Molecular mechanisms of autophagy disorder in diabetic neuropathy: Focusing on signaling pathways and regulation of lipid metabolism.

text: . These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying diabetic neuropathy and highlight promising avenues for therapeutic intervention, potentially leading to improved management strategies for this challenging complication.
title: Molecular mechanisms of autophagy disorder in diabetic neuropathy: Focusing on signaling pathways and regulation of lipid metabolism.

text: Assessment of Diabetes Risk in Patients With Hepatitis B: A Machine Learning Approach Integrating 11 Inflammatory and Immune Indicators.. Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with an increased risk of diabetes; however, early detection of diabetes remains challenging due to silent progression in early stages
title: Assessment of Diabetes Risk in Patients With Hepatitis B: A Machine Learning Approach Integrating 11 Inflammatory and Immune Indicators.

text: . Given that 30%-50% of diabetic patients develop severe complications such as cardiovascular disease, renal failure, and neuropathy, timely risk assessment is critical for prevention. We developed a machine learning model using data from 14,287 HBV-positive adults across eight NHANES cycles (2003-2018) to identify diabetes
title: Assessment of Diabetes Risk in Patients With Hepatitis B: A Machine Learning Approach Integrating 11 Inflammatory and Immune Indicators.

text: . Eleven inflammation-immune composite indicators were integrated with demographic and biochemical parameters. Following LASSO variable selection and a 7:3 train-test split, seven algorithms were compared. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the ROC curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA)
title: Assessment of Diabetes Risk in Patients With Hepatitis B: A Machine Learning Approach Integrating 11 Inflammatory and Immune Indicators.

text: . The Artificial Neural Network (ANN) emerged as the optimal model for diabetes risk assessment. It achieved an AUC of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.80-0.85) and an accuracy of 82% (95% CI: 0.79-0.85). SHAP analysis identified age and UHR as the most influential predictors, while HRR showed significant protective effects
title: Assessment of Diabetes Risk in Patients With Hepatitis B: A Machine Learning Approach Integrating 11 Inflammatory and Immune Indicators.

text: . This study presents a robust, interpretable model for diabetes risk assessment in HBV patients that integrates novel inflammation-immune composite indicators. These findings highlight the model's utility as a potential clinical tool for screening individuals with undiagnosed diabetes.
title: Assessment of Diabetes Risk in Patients With Hepatitis B: A Machine Learning Approach Integrating 11 Inflammatory and Immune Indicators.

title: The relationship between digital health literacy, self-efficacy, and self-management behaviors in patients with diabetes-related foot disease: a cross-sectional study.

title: The relationship between digital health literacy, self-efficacy, and self-management behaviors in patients with diabetes-related foot disease: a cross-sectional study.

title: The relationship between digital health literacy, self-efficacy, and self-management behaviors in patients with diabetes-related foot disease: a cross-sectional study.

title: The relationship between digital health literacy, self-efficacy, and self-management behaviors in patients with diabetes-related foot disease: a cross-sectional study.

text: Efficacy and Safety of Ion Channel Modulators in Painful Diabetic Neuropathy.. To systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of ion channel modulators for the treatment of painful diabetic neuropathy (PDN). We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in PDN patients treated with ion channel modulators
title: Efficacy and Safety of Ion Channel Modulators in Painful Diabetic Neuropathy.

text: . The primary outcome was the pain score. Secondary outcomes included the visual analog scale (VAS) score, 30% and 50% pain reduction, patient global impression of change (PGIC), sleep interference score, adverse events, and treatment discontinuation. Independent authors extracted the data and assessed the quality
title: Efficacy and Safety of Ion Channel Modulators in Painful Diabetic Neuropathy.

text: . Heterogeneity among studies was quantified using the I  A total of 36 RCTs comprising 6611 participants with PDN were included in the analyses, of which 21 were evaluated with calcium channel blockers, 12 with sodium channel blockers, 2 with TRPA1 antagonists, and 1 with P2X3 antagonists
title: Efficacy and Safety of Ion Channel Modulators in Painful Diabetic Neuropathy.

text: . Compared with placebo, ion channel modulators, particularly calcium channel blockers (mirogabalin, pregabalin, gabapentin, crisugabalin) and sodium channel antagonists (oxcarbazepine, lacosamide, lamotrigine, sodium valproate), can significantly reduce pain, VAS, and sleep interference scores, improve PGIC, and increase the proportion of patients achieving 30% and 50% pain reduction
title: Efficacy and Safety of Ion Channel Modulators in Painful Diabetic Neuropathy.

text: . The therapeutic effects of the TRPA1 antagonists and P2X3 antagonists did not differ significantly from those of the control. title: Efficacy and Safety of Ion Channel Modulators in Painful Diabetic Neuropathy.

text: . Ion channel modulators, especially calcium channel blockers and sodium channel antagonists, have favourable safety profiles and beneficial effects on reducing pain and improving the quality of life of patients with PDN.
title: Efficacy and Safety of Ion Channel Modulators in Painful Diabetic Neuropathy.

text: Integrative neuromodulation in diabetic foot infections: electroacupuncture-driven macrophage reprogramming and synergy with antimicrobial biomaterials.. Diabetic foot infections (DFIs) are characterized by persistent bacterial biofilms and impaired host immune defenses
title: Integrative neuromodulation in diabetic foot infections: electroacupuncture-driven macrophage reprogramming and synergy with antimicrobial biomaterials.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

text: . Within the diabetic microenvironment, peripheral neuropathy disrupts neuro-immune feedback loops, contributing to the arrest of resident macrophages in a pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype. This phenotypic arrest impairs efferocytosis and sustains chronic inflammation, which conventional antimicrobial therapies frequently fail to resolve
title: Integrative neuromodulation in diabetic foot infections: electroacupuncture-driven macrophage reprogramming and synergy with antimicrobial biomaterials.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

text: . Electroacupuncture (EA) serves as a neuromodulatory intervention capable of reversing this immune dysfunction. By stimulating specific somato-autonomic reflexes-including the vagal-adrenal and sympathoadrenal axes-EA activates the systemic cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway (CAP)
title: Integrative neuromodulation in diabetic foot infections: electroacupuncture-driven macrophage reprogramming and synergy with antimicrobial biomaterials.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

text: . The subsequent release of neurotransmitters, acting on receptors such as the α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7nAChR) on macrophages, inhibits pro-inflammatory cascades and promotes polarization toward the pro-repair M2 phenotype
title: Integrative neuromodulation in diabetic foot infections: electroacupuncture-driven macrophage reprogramming and synergy with antimicrobial biomaterials.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

text: . Concurrently, EA-induced localized neuropeptide release and vasodilation mitigate the ischemic microenvironment, providing metabolic support for sustained pathogen clearance
title: Integrative neuromodulation in diabetic foot infections: electroacupuncture-driven macrophage reprogramming and synergy with antimicrobial biomaterials.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

text: . Furthermore, this review proposes a translational "Vanguard and Commander" approach, integrating the localized biofilm-disrupting properties of advanced antimicrobial biomaterials (the "vanguard") with the sustained immune reprogramming mediated by EA (the "commander")
title: Integrative neuromodulation in diabetic foot infections: electroacupuncture-driven macrophage reprogramming and synergy with antimicrobial biomaterials.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

text: . This integration links material science with bioelectronic neuromodulation to coordinate the tissue repair process spatiotemporally. Ultimately, this combined approach provides an opioid-sparing, integrative therapeutic strategy for the management of refractory diabetic wound infections.
title: Integrative neuromodulation in diabetic foot infections: electroacupuncture-driven macrophage reprogramming and synergy with antimicrobial biomaterials.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Predicting the Path to Attrition: Multidomain Risk Assessment in Diabetic Foot Ulcer Offloading Randomized Controlled Trials.

text: Effect of motivational behavioral change-integrated rehabilitation nursing on recovery and prognosis in patients with hypertension and diabetic foot ulcers.. title: Effect of motivational behavioral change-integrated rehabilitation nursing on recovery and prognosis in patients with hypertension and diabetic foot ulcers.

title: Effect of motivational behavioral change-integrated rehabilitation nursing on recovery and prognosis in patients with hypertension and diabetic foot ulcers.
