text: Construction and Validation of a Long-Term Visual Prognosis Prediction Model for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Vitrectomy Based on Machine Learning.. This study aims to develop a machine-learning-based risk prediction model for a long-term visual prognosis in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) following pars plana vitrectomy (PPV)
title: Construction and Validation of a Long-Term Visual Prognosis Prediction Model for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Vitrectomy Based on Machine Learning.

text: . We analysed 609 PDR patients (609 eyes) who underwent PPV at Shanxi Eye Hospital from January 1, 2022, to January 1, 2025. The dataset was randomly split into training and validation sets at an 8:2 ratio. Candidate risk factors were identified using LASSO regression, followed by multivariate logistic regression to determine independent predictors
title: Construction and Validation of a Long-Term Visual Prognosis Prediction Model for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Vitrectomy Based on Machine Learning.

text: . Machine learning algorithms were then trained to construct the prediction model, with performance evaluated by AUC-ROC, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Calibration was assessed via calibration curves, and clinical utility by decision curve analysis (DCA)
title: Construction and Validation of a Long-Term Visual Prognosis Prediction Model for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Vitrectomy Based on Machine Learning.

text: . LASSO regression and multivariate logistic regression indicated that several factors influenced postoperative long-term visual prognosis
title: Construction and Validation of a Long-Term Visual Prognosis Prediction Model for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Vitrectomy Based on Machine Learning.

text: . These included Renal Insufficiency (OR = 6.932, 95% CI: 3.394-14.158), Preoperative iris neovascularization (OR = 7.674, 95% CI: 3.699-15.920), Silicone oil tamponade (OR = 2.799, 95% CI: 1.641-4.707), Indirect bilirubin (IBIL) (OR = 0.902, 95% CI: 0.829-0.981) (p < 0.05). LightGBM was found to be the best for predicting postoperative long-term visual prognosis risk in PDR patients
title: Construction and Validation of a Long-Term Visual Prognosis Prediction Model for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Vitrectomy Based on Machine Learning.

text: . The LightGBM model demonstrated good calibration in both training and validation sets. DCA of the validation set showed clinical net benefit at low-to-moderate risk thresholds, outperforming both 'treat-all' and 'treat-none' strategies
title: Construction and Validation of a Long-Term Visual Prognosis Prediction Model for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Vitrectomy Based on Machine Learning.

text: . In conclusion, this study developed a machine learning-based prognostic model for long-term visual prognosis in PDR patients after PPV, visualized as a proof-of-concept web calculator to assist clinical staff in early risk identification and support personalised treatment planning, pending external validation and prospective evaluation.
title: Construction and Validation of a Long-Term Visual Prognosis Prediction Model for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Vitrectomy Based on Machine Learning.

text: Interrelationship between Serum FGF21, GDF15, and Microalbuminuria as Predictive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.. Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable visual loss in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), yet current screening largely detects disease after microvascular damage has occurred
title: Interrelationship between Serum FGF21, GDF15, and Microalbuminuria as Predictive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

text: . This review synthesizes emerging evidence that three measurable biomarkers - fibroblast growth factor-21 (FGF21), growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF15), and microalbuminuria -capture complementary dimensions of early DR pathobiology
title: Interrelationship between Serum FGF21, GDF15, and Microalbuminuria as Predictive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

text: . FGF21 reflects hepatometabolic stress and adaptive signaling via the β-Klotho-FGFR1 axis; GDF15 mirrors mitochondrial/integratedstress-response activation with systemic effects through the glial cell-derived neurotrophic factor family receptor-α-like (GFRAL) REarranged during Transfection (RET); and microalbuminuria indicates systemic endothelial dysfunction and increased microvascular
title: Interrelationship between Serum FGF21, GDF15, and Microalbuminuria as Predictive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

text: dysfunction and increased microvascular permeability
title: Interrelationship between Serum FGF21, GDF15, and Microalbuminuria as Predictive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

text: . We narratively integrate cross-sectional, cohort, and meta-analytic studies in human T2DM populations (excluding type 1 diabetes and animal experiments) and map these signals onto a unified metabolic-renal-retinal framework
title: Interrelationship between Serum FGF21, GDF15, and Microalbuminuria as Predictive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

text: . Across studies, higher circulating FGF21 and GDF15 associate with DR presence and severity, while microalbuminuria correlates with DR grade and predicts progression independent of glycemic control
title: Interrelationship between Serum FGF21, GDF15, and Microalbuminuria as Predictive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

text: . We propose a tri-biomarker model in which chronic lipotoxicity and oxidative stress elevate FGF21/GDF15, drive endothelial injury detectable as microalbuminuria, and together forecast early retinal microangiopathy
title: Interrelationship between Serum FGF21, GDF15, and Microalbuminuria as Predictive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

text: . Translational implications include risk stratification before funduscopic changes, therapy monitoring for metabolic/mitochondrial targets, and development of multimarker algorithms alongside OCTA imaging
title: Interrelationship between Serum FGF21, GDF15, and Microalbuminuria as Predictive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

text: . To our knowledge, this is the first review to integrate FGF21, GDF15, and microalbuminuria as a coherent predictive axis for early DR in T2DM, highlighting priorities for longitudinal validation and population-specific cut-offs.
title: Interrelationship between Serum FGF21, GDF15, and Microalbuminuria as Predictive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

text: Microvascular Diseases of the Eye: Retinal Vasculature as a Cardiometabolic Biomarker.. Microvascular disease of the eye encompasses both structural and functional changes to the retinal vessels
title: Microvascular Diseases of the Eye: Retinal Vasculature as a Cardiometabolic Biomarker.

text: . Cardiometabolic disorders, such as hypertension and diabetes, are associated with early, measurable abnormalities in the retinal microvascular network that often emerge before cardiovascular disease becomes detectable. These features can be directly, noninvasively assessed with a multitude of evolving imaging techniques
title: Microvascular Diseases of the Eye: Retinal Vasculature as a Cardiometabolic Biomarker.

text: . Furthermore, these vascular changes can be used to predict future cardiac events, making them promising biomarkers for systemic disease. Early detection is essential, as retinal microvascular pathology not only reflects systemic health but, in certain conditions, can be detrimental to vision
title: Microvascular Diseases of the Eye: Retinal Vasculature as a Cardiometabolic Biomarker.

text: . Therefore, clinical evaluation requires a combination of ocular-specific strategies and a focus on underlying metabolic risk factors. As screening techniques advance, integrating assessment of the ocular microcirculation into broader cardiovascular care may become increasingly valuable.
title: Microvascular Diseases of the Eye: Retinal Vasculature as a Cardiometabolic Biomarker.

text: Association between cataract surgery and diabetic retinopathy incidence and progression: an 11-year population-based retrospective cohort study.. To evaluate the association between cataract surgery and the incidence and progression of diabetic retinopathy (DR) in a population-based cohort of patients with diabetes. A nationwide population-based retrospective cohort study
title: Association between cataract surgery and diabetic retinopathy incidence and progression: an 11-year population-based retrospective cohort study.

text: . A nationwide administrative claims database in Taiwan covering more than 99% of the population, with longitudinal follow-up from 2010 to 2021. Adult patients (≥20 years) with diabetes mellitus and cataract were identified. Patients with prior cataract surgery before the first recorded cataract diagnosis were excluded
title: Association between cataract surgery and diabetic retinopathy incidence and progression: an 11-year population-based retrospective cohort study.

text: . A total of 15 360 patients who underwent first-time cataract surgery and 15 846 patients without surgery were included. After two-stage matching (1:2 age-matching and sex-matching followed by 1:1 propensity score matching), 7837 matched pairs were analysed. Not applicable. The primary outcomes were (1) incident DR and (2) DR progression within 6 months and 1 year after the index date
title: Association between cataract surgery and diabetic retinopathy incidence and progression: an 11-year population-based retrospective cohort study.

text: . Incident DR was defined as new-onset non-proliferative DR (NPDR) or proliferative DR (PDR). DR progression was defined as transition from no DR to NPDR/PDR or from NPDR to PDR. Outcomes were identified using diagnostic codes recorded at least twice in outpatient visits or once during hospitalisation
title: Association between cataract surgery and diabetic retinopathy incidence and progression: an 11-year population-based retrospective cohort study.

text: . Cataract surgery was associated with higher risks of both incident DR and DR progression within 1 year. In the 1:2 matched cohort, the adjusted ORs were 3.40 (95% CI 2.65 to 4.36) for incident DR and 3.11 (95% CI 2.47 to 3.92) for DR progression. Similar findings were observed in the 1:1 propensity score-matched analysis
title: Association between cataract surgery and diabetic retinopathy incidence and progression: an 11-year population-based retrospective cohort study.

text: . Absolute event rates at 1 year showed DR progression in approximately 3.1% of patients undergoing surgery compared with 1% in the non-surgical group. Increased risk was also associated with more intensive antidiabetic treatment. Cataract surgery in patients with diabetes was associated with an increased risk of incident DR and disease progression, particularly within the first postoperative year
title: Association between cataract surgery and diabetic retinopathy incidence and progression: an 11-year population-based retrospective cohort study.

text: . These findings support the consideration of cataract surgery as a clinically relevant risk window for enhanced retinal monitoring. Incorporating surgical history into DR risk stratification and screening strategies may improve early detection and inform postoperative care pathways.
title: Association between cataract surgery and diabetic retinopathy incidence and progression: an 11-year population-based retrospective cohort study.

text: An explainable deep learning approach for automated detection and grading of diabetic retinopathy from fundus images.. Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable blindness, and it is important to accurately detect it as early as possible, as well as to measure the severity to provide early clinical indicators
title: An explainable deep learning approach for automated detection and grading of diabetic retinopathy from fundus images.

text: . Fundus image assessment in the manual mode is subjective and labor-intensive, and is hard to scale, which has encouraged automated approaches. Current deep learning methods are usually based on either convolutional neural networks (CNNs) or transformer-based ones, focusing on local lesion features or global retina context separately
title: An explainable deep learning approach for automated detection and grading of diabetic retinopathy from fundus images.

text: . In addition, relational dependencies among lesions that are clinically significant in the case of severity development are under-modeled. This paper introduces a relational, hybrid deep learning model that integrates convolutional, transformer-based, and graph attention models to classify binary and multiclass DR
title: An explainable deep learning approach for automated detection and grading of diabetic retinopathy from fundus images.

text: . A ResNet-Graph Attention Network (ResNet-GAT) is introduced to explicitly model spatial relational dependencies among regional feature descriptors and iscompared with independent stand-alone ResNet-50 and Swin Transformer models. Also, a hybrid ResNet-Swin Transformer model combines fine-grained lesion representations and hierarchical global context
title: An explainable deep learning approach for automated detection and grading of diabetic retinopathy from fundus images.

text: . Experiments with the APTOS 2019 data show that the hybrid model has an accuracy of 98.09% with a Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) of 0.9618 when used to classify binary, and 94.89% with a QWK of 0.9726 when used to classify five classes of severity. Robustness is proven by cross-dataset inference on IDRiD
title: An explainable deep learning approach for automated detection and grading of diabetic retinopathy from fundus images.

text: . The interpretability analysis performed through Grad-CAM shows that the predictions are made based on clinically significant areas, such as microaneurysms, hemorrhages, and exudates. It is demonstrated that performance and interpretability are enhanced by a combination of local, global, and relational representations in automated screening of DR.
title: An explainable deep learning approach for automated detection and grading of diabetic retinopathy from fundus images.

text: Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cell Dysfunction and Suprachiasmatic Nucleus-Mediated Circadian Disruption in Humans: A Systematic Review.. Circadian entraining input to the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) is primarily from intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs)
title: Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cell Dysfunction and Suprachiasmatic Nucleus-Mediated Circadian Disruption in Humans: A Systematic Review.

text: . While several retinal and optic nerve diseases are associated with ipRGC dysfunction, the role of ipRGC dysfunction in the context of SCN-mediated circadian disruption remains incompletely understood. We performed a systematic review of human studies examining relationships between ipRGC dysfunction and circadian effects. Databases were searched from inception until Apr 2026
title: Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cell Dysfunction and Suprachiasmatic Nucleus-Mediated Circadian Disruption in Humans: A Systematic Review.

text: . Studies were independently assessed for risk of bias, screened, and data extracted by two reviewers. Due to high methodological variability, results were summarised qualitatively. GRADE was used to assess the certainty of evidence. 3632 records were identified, of which 10 studies were included, 8 focused on ipRGC functional measures, and 2 on ipRGC structural measures
title: Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cell Dysfunction and Suprachiasmatic Nucleus-Mediated Circadian Disruption in Humans: A Systematic Review.

text: . Across the 8 functional-measures studies, ipRGC dysfunction and impairment in one or more SCN-mediated circadian outcomes were consistently observed, and this association was independently corroborated in 6 of the 8 studies
title: Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cell Dysfunction and Suprachiasmatic Nucleus-Mediated Circadian Disruption in Humans: A Systematic Review.

text: . Advanced glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy showed the greatest evidence of circadian disruption, including decreased melatonin excretion, delayed or altered dim-light melatonin onset, and failure to suppress melatonin with light exposure. Both ipRGC function and circadian regulation were preserved in mitochondrial optic neuropathies
title: Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cell Dysfunction and Suprachiasmatic Nucleus-Mediated Circadian Disruption in Humans: A Systematic Review.

text: . Two additional studies showed strong links between post-illumination pupil response (PIPR) and melatonin-related circadian measures. In two post-mortem ipRGC structural measure studies, ipRGC density was reduced by 76.9% in severe diabetic retinopathy compared with controls, and age-related ipRGC dendritic atrophy was observed
title: Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cell Dysfunction and Suprachiasmatic Nucleus-Mediated Circadian Disruption in Humans: A Systematic Review.

text: . Evidence in humans suggests a directionally consistent but very low-certainty relationship between SCN circadian disruption and ipRGC dysfunction, but the pattern and severity of disruption differ across disease states. PIPR has the potential to serve as a non-invasive marker of circadian disruption
title: Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cell Dysfunction and Suprachiasmatic Nucleus-Mediated Circadian Disruption in Humans: A Systematic Review.

text: . The overall certainty of evidence is still very low, however, and requires larger, long-term studies with standardized circadian phenotyping.
title: Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cell Dysfunction and Suprachiasmatic Nucleus-Mediated Circadian Disruption in Humans: A Systematic Review.

text: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.. Diabetic retinopathy is the leading cause of blindness in US adults. Fewer than half of patients with diabetes in rural areas complete the recommended screening that could prevent blindness
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . Store-and-forward teleophthalmology and mobile pop-up eye clinics have each been shown to improve screening access, but studies examining the implementation of both modalities within the same rural primary care system are lacking
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . This study aimed to identify multilevel facilitators and barriers to implementing teleophthalmology and pop-up eye clinics for diabetic eye care in 2 rural primary care clinics in upstate New York
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . We conducted a mixed methods implementation study with prospective semistructured interviews and retrospective, descriptive electronic health record data at 2 university-affiliated primary care clinics classified as "isolated rural," guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR)
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . Electronic health record data from 885 adults with diabetes were used to characterize patient demographics and eye care use. Patients were categorized into 3 groups: eye exam with an eye doctor (n=586), on-site primary care-based eye exam (n=91; teleophthalmology n=39 and pop-up clinic n=52), or no recent eye exam (n=208)
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . Semistructured interviews were conducted with 20 patients (n=5 per subgroup) and 14 staff members (primary care clinicians, optometrists, and administrative personnel), purposively sampled to capture diverse perspectives across eye care pathways and roles. Interviews were coded using CFIR domains and analyzed thematically until no new themes emerged
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . Patients in the on-site primary care eye exam group were the most socially disadvantaged, with the lowest proportions reporting no transportation needs (42/91, 46.2%), no housing instability (28/91, 30.8%), and no food insecurity (36/91, 39.6%). Over 18 months, 58.4% (52/89) of scheduled pop-up clinic appointments were completed, and 92.3% (36/39) of teleophthalmology images were gradable
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . Pop-up clinics detected higher rates of diabetic retinopathy (11/52, 21.2% vs 3/39, 7.7%), cataract (29/52, 55.8% vs 3/39, 7.7%), and reduced visual acuity (23/52, 44.2% vs 11/39, 28.2%) than teleophthalmology. Qualitative analysis revealed that patients viewed both modalities as a convenient "one-stop shop" and valued trust in primary care staff
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . Staff identified complementary barriers: training and workflow complexity for teleophthalmology, and underutilization and scheduling challenges for pop-up clinics
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . Implementation champions across roles proposed an integrated workflow in which same-day teleophthalmology becomes a default component of annual diabetes visits, with targeted referral to pop-up clinics for patients with abnormal findings
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . Primary care-based eye programs in rural settings preferentially reached socially vulnerable patients with diabetes and detected substantial unmet eye pathology. However, operating teleophthalmology and pop-up clinics as separate programs led to inefficiencies in both programs
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: . A stakeholder-driven integrated model embedding teleophthalmology into routine diabetes care, with targeted pop-up clinic referrals, may improve the reach, efficiency, and sustainability of diabetic eye screening in rural populations.
title: Implementing Diabetic Eye Care in Rural Primary Care Through Teleophthalmology and Pop-Up Clinics: Mixed Methods Study.

text: Enhancing early diabetic retinopathy detection: a fine-tuned NASNet framework with robust validation and external generalization.. Early detection of diabetic retinopathy (DR) is critical for preventing irreversible vision loss among patients with diabetes mellitus
title: Enhancing early diabetic retinopathy detection: a fine-tuned NASNet framework with robust validation and external generalization.

text: . Automated screening systems based on deep learning have demonstrated substantial promise in improving diagnostic efficiency and scalability. This study proposes a robust multiclass DR classification framework using a fine-tuned NASNetLarge architecture applied to retinal fundus images
title: Enhancing early diabetic retinopathy detection: a fine-tuned NASNet framework with robust validation and external generalization.

text: . The model leverages transfer learning from ImageNet and incorporates a structured fine-tuning protocol to adapt high-level features to DR-specific patterns. Experiments were conducted on the publicly available APTOS 2019 Blindness Detection dataset, comprising five DR severity classes
title: Enhancing early diabetic retinopathy detection: a fine-tuned NASNet framework with robust validation and external generalization.

text: . The model was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (AUC) metrics. To ensure robustness, experiments were repeated across five independent runs and reported as mean ± standard deviation. External validation was performed using the EyePACS dataset to assess generalisability
title: Enhancing early diabetic retinopathy detection: a fine-tuned NASNet framework with robust validation and external generalization.

text: . The fine-tuned NASNet model achieved 97.52% ± 0.42 accuracy with strong per-class AUC values (≥ 0.98). External validation yielded 93.42% accuracy and an AUC value of 0.941, confirming generalization capability. Comparative analysis against EfficientNet-B4, DenseNet121, and Vision Transformer (ViT-B16) demonstrated superior performance under identical conditions
title: Enhancing early diabetic retinopathy detection: a fine-tuned NASNet framework with robust validation and external generalization.

text: . The proposed framework shows strong potential as an automated DR screening tool for early-stage detection and large-scale population screening.
title: Enhancing early diabetic retinopathy detection: a fine-tuned NASNet framework with robust validation and external generalization.

text: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition in Diabetic Macular Oedema: Emerging Evidence for Stage-Dependent Systemic-Retinal Responsiveness.. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors exert systemic cardiometabolic, renal and vascular effects that may influence retinal health, yet whether their effects on diabetic macular oedema (DMO) are stage-dependent remains unclear
title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition in Diabetic Macular Oedema: Emerging Evidence for Stage-Dependent Systemic-Retinal Responsiveness.

text: . We synthesized real-world, interventional and mechanistic evidence on responsiveness across disease stages and retinal phenotypes. In this scoping review (PRISMA-ScR; prospectively registered, UMIN000061304), we searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO-ICTRP and Google Scholar for studies published from January 2014 to April 2026
title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition in Diabetic Macular Oedema: Emerging Evidence for Stage-Dependent Systemic-Retinal Responsiveness.

text: . Two reviewers independently screened and charted records. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis, so a qualitative meta-summary with exploratory E-value analyses was performed. Forty studies were included
title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition in Diabetic Macular Oedema: Emerging Evidence for Stage-Dependent Systemic-Retinal Responsiveness.

text: . Forty studies were included. Large administrative databases consistently associated SGLT2 inhibitor use with a 16%-35% lower DMO incidence (hazard ratio 0.65-0.84) and hazard ratios of 0.53-0.94 for diabetic retinopathy progression
title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition in Diabetic Macular Oedema: Emerging Evidence for Stage-Dependent Systemic-Retinal Responsiveness.

text: . In established DMO, observational studies reported hazard ratios of 0.39-0.81 for anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) injections, corticosteroid therapy and repeat vitrectomy, with the first-vitrectomy estimate non-significant, and attenuation in severe non-proliferative or proliferative retinopathy
title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition in Diabetic Macular Oedema: Emerging Evidence for Stage-Dependent Systemic-Retinal Responsiveness.

text: . The only randomized trial (COMET) did not meet its primary endpoint; its fellow-eye and phenotype-specific subgroup analyses were exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Proposed mechanisms include suppression of microglial activation, oxidative stress and angiopoietin-2/VEGF signalling, although translational evidence remains preclinical
title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition in Diabetic Macular Oedema: Emerging Evidence for Stage-Dependent Systemic-Retinal Responsiveness.

text: . This predominantly observational evidence suggests that SGLT2 inhibitors may be associated with slower DMO disease kinetics across retinopathy stages, with reduced treatment burden most evident before severe retinopathy. Systemic SGLT2 inhibition may complement, rather than replace, anti-VEGF therapy, which remains the cornerstone of DMO management
title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition in Diabetic Macular Oedema: Emerging Evidence for Stage-Dependent Systemic-Retinal Responsiveness.

text: . These findings support prospective stage- and phenotype-stratified investigation.
title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition in Diabetic Macular Oedema: Emerging Evidence for Stage-Dependent Systemic-Retinal Responsiveness.

text: Exploring the Relationship Between Health Biomarkers and Performance on a Novel Color Perimetry Device in Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes.. Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) is a leading cause of vision loss. Functional measurements (color vision and contrast sensitivity) are sensitive to early changes in eyes even before retinopathy is present
title: Exploring the Relationship Between Health Biomarkers and Performance on a Novel Color Perimetry Device in Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes.

text: . This study evaluates a novel color perimetry device as an indicator of diabetic eye disease. 40 subjects (age-matched) were divided into 3 groups by HbA1c or previous diagnosis (control ≤5.6%, prediabetes 5.7-6.4%, diabetes ≥6.5%). Additional health metrics gathered included: BMI, body fat %, total cholesterol, HDL/LDL levels, blood glucose, and blood pressure
title: Exploring the Relationship Between Health Biomarkers and Performance on a Novel Color Perimetry Device in Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes.

text: . Novel color perimetry which measures chromatic thresholds at 4 locations 3 degrees from the fovea for 5 colors (achromatic, red, green, blue, and yellow) was completed. Mars contrast and L'Anthony D15 color testing were also completed. Lens photos excluded those with cataracts
title: Exploring the Relationship Between Health Biomarkers and Performance on a Novel Color Perimetry Device in Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes.

text: . Lens photos excluded those with cataracts. There were differences between the groups for HbA1c (p<0.001), BMI (p=0.046), body fat % (p=0.020), and color perimetry for the yellow condition only (p=0.013). The achromatic condition was highly associated with Mars contrast sensitivity (p<0.001)
title: Exploring the Relationship Between Health Biomarkers and Performance on a Novel Color Perimetry Device in Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes.

text: . HbA1c was associated with both parvocellular (average of red and green) (p=0.014) and koniocellular (average of blue and yellow) color perimetry performance (p=0.022). HbA1c is associated with color perimetry across both retinal pathways. The yellow condition in particular holds promise as a biomarker for presence of functional changes in diabetes prior to the onset of retinopathy
title: Exploring the Relationship Between Health Biomarkers and Performance on a Novel Color Perimetry Device in Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes.

text: . Other health metrics did not influence chromatic thresholds. More research needs to be done to evaluate color perimetry in these patient groups to understand these relationships.
title: Exploring the Relationship Between Health Biomarkers and Performance on a Novel Color Perimetry Device in Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes.

text: Longitudinal Insights from Ultrawide Field Imaging Referrals in Diabetic Patients: A Three-Year Analysis at a Tertiary Center.
title: Longitudinal Insights from Ultrawide Field Imaging Referrals in Diabetic Patients: A Three-Year Analysis at a Tertiary Center.

text: . To characterize diabetic retinopathy (DR) severity and predominantly peripheral lesion (PPL) status among patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) imaged using ultrawide-field (UWF) photography at a tertiary center in Egypt following introduction of the first national UWF camera and certified reading center. This prospective, cross-sectional study included all patients imaged from Feb2022 to Jan2025
title: Longitudinal Insights from Ultrawide Field Imaging Referrals in Diabetic Patients: A Three-Year Analysis at a Tertiary Center.

text: . UWF images were graded using the ETDRS severity scale, and PPLs were evaluated on non-steered color images. Demographic and clinical variables, including DM duration, treatment, HbA1c, age, and age of onset, were collected. Temporal trends in DR severity, PPL prevalence, and patient characteristics were assessed using linear regression and generalized estimating equation models
title: Longitudinal Insights from Ultrawide Field Imaging Referrals in Diabetic Patients: A Three-Year Analysis at a Tertiary Center.

text: . A total of 61,095 eyes from 26,170 patients were imaged; 47.5% had DM. Among 29,828 diabetic eyes, 34.9% had no DR; 17.2%, 10.8%, and 6.5% had mild, moderate, and severe NPDR; and 25.0% had PDR
title: Longitudinal Insights from Ultrawide Field Imaging Referrals in Diabetic Patients: A Three-Year Analysis at a Tertiary Center.

text: . The proportion of eyes with no DR increased significantly over time, while moderate NPDR and PDR declined (all  Implementation of UWF imaging and certified grading was followed by a shift toward imaging patients with earlier DR and reduced fluorescein angiography use. UWF deployment may facilitate earlier DR detection and triage in resource-limited settings.

text: Glaucoma spectrum findings among the Yanomami Indigenous people of the Brazilian Amazon.. This study provides the first systematic characterisation of IOP, optic disc C/D ratio, and fundoscopic findings in the Yanomami, one of the largest and most geographically isolated Indigenous peoples of the Amazon, and identifies findings suggestive of glaucoma
title: Glaucoma spectrum findings among the Yanomami Indigenous people of the Brazilian Amazon.

text: . Cross-sectional observational study conducted June-August 2024 at the Yanomami Indigenous Health House (CASAI-Y), Boa Vista, Brazil. One hundred fifty-eight self-identified Yanomami individuals aged  ≥ 5 years were examined. Non-contact tonometry (Huvitz HNT-7000), portable non-mydriatic fundus photography (Eyer), portable slit-lamp biomicroscopy, and direct ophthalmoscopy were performed
title: Glaucoma spectrum findings among the Yanomami Indigenous people of the Brazilian Amazon.

text: . C/D ratio was graded by fundus photographic review. Associations were assessed by OR with 95% CI, Student t test, one-way ANOVA, Fisher exact test, and Spearman and Pearson correlation. P values were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure
title: Glaucoma spectrum findings among the Yanomami Indigenous people of the Brazilian Amazon.

text: . Among 151 participants with assessable IOP (secondary glaucoma case excluded from descriptive analysis), mean IOP was 13.64 mmHg (SD 1.59) OD and 13.93 mmHg (SD 1.75) OS; ocular hypertension was identified in 1 participant (0.66%). Mean C/D ratio was 0.261 (SD 0.129) OD and 0.267 (SD 0.138) OS among 148 participants; 3 (2.03%) had C/D  > 0.5 in at least one eye
title: Glaucoma spectrum findings among the Yanomami Indigenous people of the Brazilian Amazon.

text: . No significant IOP-C/D correlation was found (Spearman rₛ = 0.105, P = .210 OD; rₛ = 0.058, P = .496 OS). Secondary angle-closure glaucoma was confirmed in one participant (IOP 35/55 mmHg, 360° synechiae, no light perception). Two further participants had findings suggestive of primary glaucoma
title: Glaucoma spectrum findings among the Yanomami Indigenous people of the Brazilian Amazon.

text: . Ocular trauma was associated with retinal cicatricial lesions (OR 13.41; 95% CI 2.55-70.35; P = .008; P adj = .036) and, without retaining significance after adjustment for multiple comparisons, with fundoscopic abnormality (OR 7.98; 95% CI 1.26-50.55; P = .04; P adj = .10); both estimates rest on 7 trauma-exposed participants. No diabetic retinopathy was identified
title: Glaucoma spectrum findings among the Yanomami Indigenous people of the Brazilian Amazon.

text: . No diabetic retinopathy was identified. This study provides the first quantitative ophthalmic baseline for the Yanomami regarding IOP, optic disc morphology, and fundoscopic findings. Primary open-angle glaucoma does not appear to constitute a relevant burden. Secondary glaucoma from complicated cataract is the most preventable severe presentation. Angle-closure glaucoma remains uncharacterised
title: Glaucoma spectrum findings among the Yanomami Indigenous people of the Brazilian Amazon.

text: . Angle-closure glaucoma remains uncharacterised. Cataract surgical access, camerular angle screening, and glaucoma investigation are unmet priorities in this population.
title: Glaucoma spectrum findings among the Yanomami Indigenous people of the Brazilian Amazon.

text: Development of a patient journey map for diabetic retinopathy: exploring evidence from qualitative research.. The World Health Organization has emphasized people-centered health, shifting focus from disease to patient needs
title: Development of a patient journey map for diabetic retinopathy: exploring evidence from qualitative research.

text: . Patient Journey Mapping has emerged as a valuable methodological approach to support healthcare and nursing management by visualizing patient experiences and identifying service improvement opportunities. Despite extensive clinical research on diabetic retinopathy (DR), the phases and dimensions of its healthcare management process remain poorly understood
title: Development of a patient journey map for diabetic retinopathy: exploring evidence from qualitative research.

text: . This study aimed to: (a) synthesize existing qualitative evidence on the experiences, emotions, and healthcare needs of persons with DR across screening, perioperative, and extended treatment stages; (b) conduct semi-structured interviews to contextualize and enrich the synthesized evidence; and (c) develop an integrated Patient Journey Map to inform tailored healthcare interventions
title: Development of a patient journey map for diabetic retinopathy: exploring evidence from qualitative research.

text: . This study employed a two-phase qualitative evidence mapping and interview design. Phase 1 comprised a narrative literature review with systematic search to map existing qualitative evidence, with data analyzed using thematic synthesis. Phase 2 involved semi-structured interviews with 13 persons with DR at a Chinese university hospital, with data analyzed using qualitative content analysis
title: Development of a patient journey map for diabetic retinopathy: exploring evidence from qualitative research.

text: . Literature and interview findings were integrated through triangulation to construct a comprehensive Patient Journey Map. Quality was assessed using CASP and GRADE-CERQual; reporting followed ENTREQ guidelines. Twenty-five studies were included, describing patient experiences across screening, perioperative, and post-acute care phases, forming a preliminary framework
title: Development of a patient journey map for diabetic retinopathy: exploring evidence from qualitative research.

text: . Interviews with 13 persons with DR enriched these findings and established a complete journey trajectory. The proposed Patient Journey Map visually illustrates patient experiences and behaviors across the care continuum. This evidence provides a theoretical foundation for developing tailored diabetes care recommendations based on individual needs
title: Development of a patient journey map for diabetic retinopathy: exploring evidence from qualitative research.

text: . Patient Journey Mapping contributes to improving healthcare management processes and supports healthcare managers in optimizing service delivery. Not applicable.
title: Development of a patient journey map for diabetic retinopathy: exploring evidence from qualitative research.

text: Smartphone-based fundus imaging in global eye care: Closing the gap.. Smartphone-based fundus imaging (SBFI) is an emerging approach with potential relevance for global ophthalmic care, including in low- and middle-income countries and other resource-constrained settings
title: Smartphone-based fundus imaging in global eye care: Closing the gap.
journal: Progress in retinal and eye research

text: . This scoping review, based on a structured literature search, synthesizes current SBFI technology, clinical and teaching applications, implementation challenges and future directions
title: Smartphone-based fundus imaging in global eye care: Closing the gap.
journal: Progress in retinal and eye research

text: . Analysing 30 hardware solutions (based on three principal technical designs) and 274 scientific publications and other relevant sources, we found that some SBFI devices can provide fields of view and image quality sufficient to support screening or triage for referable diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma-related optic nerve head changes, and selected retinopathy of prematurity applications
title: Smartphone-based fundus imaging in global eye care: Closing the gap.
journal: Progress in retinal and eye research

text: . Reported sensitivity, specificity and gradability varied by disease, device, protocol, operator, and reference standard; no universal performance threshold could be inferred. After brief training, allied healthcare workers can acquire useable images in selected settings, suggesting that SBFI may support task-shifted screening and referral pathways
title: Smartphone-based fundus imaging in global eye care: Closing the gap.
journal: Progress in retinal and eye research

text: . Artificial intelligence may further support scalability by assisting image-quality and protocol compliance assessment, frame selection, montage generation and disease classification. However, costs, maintenance requirements, data governance and domain shift remain important implementation considerations
title: Smartphone-based fundus imaging in global eye care: Closing the gap.
journal: Progress in retinal and eye research

text: . Key challenges include variable image quality and fields of view, heterogeneous reporting, smartphone compatibility, regulatory compliance, photobiological safety verification, data security, and patient privacy. We therefore suggest minimum reporting standards to increase comparability across studies
title: Smartphone-based fundus imaging in global eye care: Closing the gap.
journal: Progress in retinal and eye research

text: . Large-scale implementation and cost-effectiveness studies are needed to determine whether improved access to ophthalmic imaging can translate into sustainable and equitable eye-care services.

text: Treatment of foveal-involving tractional retinal detachments from proliferative diabetic retinopathy with intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy.. title: Treatment of foveal-involving tractional retinal detachments from proliferative diabetic retinopathy with intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy.

Outcome measures included visual acuity, foveal reattachment, need for vitrectomy, number of intravitreal injections, and average interval between injections. 12 eyes of 10 patients were included. 75% of eyes (n = 9) had foveal reattachment with anti-VEGF therapy alone
title: Treatment of foveal-involving tractional retinal detachments from proliferative diabetic retinopathy with intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy.

text: . The average time from TRD diagnosis to foveal reattachment was 15 months. title: Treatment of foveal-involving tractional retinal detachments from proliferative diabetic retinopathy with intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy.

text: . At a last follow-up (mean 27.8 months), mean logMAR VA was to 1.36 (20/453) among all patients and 1.01 (20/204) among patients who had foveal reattachment. In this cohort of eyes treated with intravitreal anti-VEGF for fovea-off TRD from PDR retinopathy, we observed visual and anatomic stability, and, in some cases, improvement.

text: Association between arterial stiffness and choroidal vascular in type 2 diabetes: more pronounced in individuals aged 30 to 50 years.. title: Association between arterial stiffness and choroidal vascular in type 2 diabetes: more pronounced in individuals aged 30 to 50 years.

text: . This study includes 177 eyes from 95 patients with T2D underwent clinical assessment and wide-field OCTA imaging (24 × 20 mm, TowardPi BMizar)
title: Association between arterial stiffness and choroidal vascular in type 2 diabetes: more pronounced in individuals aged 30 to 50 years.

title: Association between arterial stiffness and choroidal vascular in type 2 diabetes: more pronounced in individuals aged 30 to 50 years.

text: Diabetic Retinopathy: From Molecular Mechanisms to Modern Therapy.. Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains one of the leading causes of vision loss. Its development is driven by complex interconnected pathophysiological mechanisms triggered by chronic hyperglycemia
title: Diabetic Retinopathy: From Molecular Mechanisms to Modern Therapy.

text: . Traditional diagnostic approaches, which rely on detecting visible microangiopathies, often identify the disease only after significant and progressive retinal damage had already occurred. Consequently, current therapeutic strategies are largely focused on managing advanced, proliferative stages of DR
title: Diabetic Retinopathy: From Molecular Mechanisms to Modern Therapy.

text: . A major direction in modern ophthalmology is the shift toward identifying and intervening at stages that precede clinical DR manifestations
title: Diabetic Retinopathy: From Molecular Mechanisms to Modern Therapy.

text: . This review presents current data on the pathogenesis and molecular mechanisms of DR, discusses associated biochemical alterations revealed through multi-omics approaches, and examines methods for preclinical diagnostics, innovative therapeutic strategies, and novel targets for early pathogenetic intervention
title: Diabetic Retinopathy: From Molecular Mechanisms to Modern Therapy.

text: . Overall, the evidence suggests that that effective treatment options for DR might include multi-target therapeutic approaches extending beyond the blockade of angiogenesis and aimed at addressing metabolic, inflammatory, and oxidative disorders causing neurodegeneration and vascular dysfunction.
title: Diabetic Retinopathy: From Molecular Mechanisms to Modern Therapy.

text: Biomaterials in Retinal Surgery: Engineering the Future.. To review current and emerging biomaterials in retinal surgery-vitreous tamponade agents, retinal prostheses, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) transplant scaffolds, intraocular drug delivery platforms, and gene therapy vectors-with emphasis on the authors' oxime-crosslinked hyaluronic acid vitreous substitute. Narrative expert review
title: Biomaterials in Retinal Surgery: Engineering the Future.

text: . Narrative expert review. Systematic review methodology was not used; no protocol registration, prespecified eligibility criteria, dual independent screening, or PRISMA flow diagram was undertaken. Published preclinical animal studies, Phase I to III clinical trials, US Food and Drug Administration approvals, and real-world evidence on biomaterials in posterior segment surgery
title: Biomaterials in Retinal Surgery: Engineering the Future.

text: . No individual patient data were accessed. A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, supplemented by Google Scholar, was performed from January 2018 to March 2026 across 5 domains: vitreous tamponade agents; retinal prostheses; scaffold-based RPE transplantation; nanoparticle and sustained-release drug delivery; and gene therapy vectors
title: Biomaterials in Retinal Surgery: Engineering the Future.

title: Biomaterials in Retinal Surgery: Engineering the Future.

title: Biomaterials in Retinal Surgery: Engineering the Future.

text: Association between SGLT-2 inhibitor use and retinal microvascular parameters in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus: A cross-sectional study.. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) are widely used in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) and may have neuroprotective and microvascular benefits
title: Association between SGLT-2 inhibitor use and retinal microvascular parameters in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus: A cross-sectional study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and its complications

text: . This study investigated SGLT-2i therapy effects on retinal microvasculature using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) in T2DM patients. This cross-sectional study included 100 T2DM patients (46 receiving SGLT-2i, 54 non-users). Patients underwent comprehensive evaluation, including OCTA
title: Association between SGLT-2 inhibitor use and retinal microvascular parameters in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus: A cross-sectional study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and its complications

text: . Central macular thickness (CMT), superficial capillary vascular density (SCVD), deep capillary vascular density (DCVD), and radial peripapillary capillary (RPC) density were measured. BMI and HbA1c were recorded. The SGLT-2i group had significantly higher weight and BMI (p < 0.01). Visual acuity and CMT did not differ between groups
title: Association between SGLT-2 inhibitor use and retinal microvascular parameters in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus: A cross-sectional study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and its complications

text: . However, non-users exhibited significantly higher DCVD in the whole retina, parafovea, and perifovea, and higher SCVD in the perifovea (p < 0.05). RPC densities in the inferior nasal and superior temporal regions were significantly higher in non-users (p < 0.05). SGLT-2i users showed lower retinal vessel densities compared to non-users
title: Association between SGLT-2 inhibitor use and retinal microvascular parameters in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus: A cross-sectional study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and its complications

text: . Due to the cross-sectional design, causality cannot be established; these results do not prove SGLT-2i adversely affects retinal microvasculature. Rather, these are hypothesis-generating observations. Prospective longitudinal studies are needed to clarify whether these findings reflect actual treatment effects or underlying patient characteristics.
title: Association between SGLT-2 inhibitor use and retinal microvascular parameters in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus: A cross-sectional study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and its complications

text: Glycosylation-Associated Macrophage Signatures Define a Diagnostic Model for Diabetic Retinopathy via Single-Cell Analysis.. Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of vision loss, with macrophages and glycosylation dysregulation implicated in DR pathogenesis. However, the potential as diagnostic biomarkers has been rarely investigated
title: Glycosylation-Associated Macrophage Signatures Define a Diagnostic Model for Diabetic Retinopathy via Single-Cell Analysis.

text: . We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets to profile DR cell landscapes. The immune cell heterogeneity was dissected, and glycosylation-related transcriptional programs were delineated in DR. Machine learning-based diagnostic modeling was also conducted to identify macrophage differentiation-related glycosylation genes (MDRGGs)
title: Glycosylation-Associated Macrophage Signatures Define a Diagnostic Model for Diabetic Retinopathy via Single-Cell Analysis.

text: . Macrophages exhibited elevated abundance in proliferative DR and showed intense interactions with other monocytes. Endothelial cells were subdivided into four subtypes, with Endo_KCNQ3 representing a dominant proliferative and highly glycosylated phenotype. Monocytes were clustered into three subtypes; Mono_RGS1 emerged as a transitional phenotype in the monocyte-to-macrophage trajectory
title: Glycosylation-Associated Macrophage Signatures Define a Diagnostic Model for Diabetic Retinopathy via Single-Cell Analysis.

text: . Macro_MIR181A1HG was identified as a proliferative and glycosylation-active macrophage subset. A total of 100 MDRGGs were identified. Among them, seven hub genes (AKAP13, SRGAP2, AFF1, ARHGAP24, RNF149, PTK2B, ATP1B3) were incorporated into a diagnostic model
title: Glycosylation-Associated Macrophage Signatures Define a Diagnostic Model for Diabetic Retinopathy via Single-Cell Analysis.

text: . The model achieved high predictive accuracy in both training and external validation cohorts (AUC > 0.85) and was further validated via nomogram and decision curve analyses. Glycosylation is closely associated with macrophage heterogeneity in DR. A seven-gene MDRGG-based diagnostic model demonstrated robust diagnostic performance in DR.
title: Glycosylation-Associated Macrophage Signatures Define a Diagnostic Model for Diabetic Retinopathy via Single-Cell Analysis.

text: Association of GLP1-Receptor Agonists With Diabetic Retinopathy.. Secondary outcomes included vision impairment or blindness and occurrence of retinopathy procedures. PS-matched overall cohort included 98 082 pairs of GLP1-RA or DPP4i users. GLP1-RA users had higher risk of NVTDR (11.05% vs
title: Association of GLP1-Receptor Agonists With Diabetic Retinopathy.

text: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.. Traditional systems of ocular disease diagnosis and many deep learning-based systems are limited in their practice to analyzing fundus images from a single eye, often using raw, unprocessed data
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: . This fails to include the critical correlation between bilateral eyes, has several issues such as low image contrast, noise, and class imbalance, and generally concentrates on the detection of no more than a single disease
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: . In order to bridge the gap, Enhanced Diabetic Retinopathy Detection through Multimodal Integration of Fundus Imaging Features and Clinical Demographic Information utilizing Verifiable Convolutional Neural Network (DD-FIF-CDI-VCNN) is proposed
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: . In the initial phase, the fundus images of the eyes along with their corresponding demographic information are sourced from the Ocular Disease Recognition, which acts as the main feed for the proposed framework
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: . During the pre-processing stage, it uses Robust Consensus Tobit Kalman Filtering (RCTKF) to resize the fundus images, normalizes the pixel intensities, and reduces noise in the process of quality improvement for subsequent feature extraction
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: . The pre-processed fundus images are provided to the ResNet-fused External Attention Network (ResfEANet) based feature extraction that extracts rich visual and texture features from the retinal images. In parallel to this, the demographic attributes are fed to a feature extraction module using TabNet which converts the structured affected person facts into a meaningful function vector
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: . This aims at making sure that relevant patient-specific styles are encoded and prepared for integration with visual functions. Then, the visible and texture capabilities extracted from the fundus photos are combined with the demographic attributes the usage of Hierarchical Multi-Scale Feature Fusion (HMSFF)
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: . This creates a complete representation that leverages both imaging and structured affected person statistics. This blended feature set is the input to the categorization model for correct diabetic retinopathy detection
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: . Next, this fused characteristic vector, combining the features extracted from the fundus images with their corresponding demographic attributes, is passed to a Verifiable Convolutional Neural Network (VCNN)-based classifier model
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: . This comprehensive multi-modal representation ensues, rendering the VCNN model capable of accurate detection of diabetic retinopathy classifying normal and diabetes, thereby enhancing predictability and robustness compared with the unimodal approach. The VCNN parameters are fine-tuned by the Warthog Optimization Algorithm (WOA) to ensure improved convergence and better detection performance
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: . The proposed DD-FIF-CDI-VCNN method is analyzed under performance metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-Score, Area under Curve (AUC) and Error rate when compared with existing models.
title: Enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection via multimodal fusion of fundus imaging features and clinical demographic information using verifiable convolutional neural network.

text: Evaluation of spatial distribution of initial marking strategy among inexperienced graders in diabetic retinopathy: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis.. Manual diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading may prefer certain regions and underestimate others. It is unclear if inexperienced graders' initial marking strategy reflects a specialist's marking pattern
title: Evaluation of spatial distribution of initial marking strategy among inexperienced graders in diabetic retinopathy: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis.

text: . By the virtual ocular learning platform (VIOLA), we evaluated if initial DR-lesion markings among inexperienced graders spatially corresponded to a specialist-based lesion map. title: Evaluation of spatial distribution of initial marking strategy among inexperienced graders in diabetic retinopathy: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis.

text: . We divided images into quadrants and counted the initial three markings per lesion type, per image, per grader. A retinal specialist served reference for annotation of all DR-lesions. The primary outcome was difference in spatial distribution of DR-markings across quadrants relative to the reference, further characterised with spatial metrics. p-Value < 0.05 indicated statistical significance
title: Evaluation of spatial distribution of initial marking strategy among inexperienced graders in diabetic retinopathy: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis.

text: . Across 24 images, 97 graders marked 16 925 DR-lesions: 1633 microaneurysms (MA), 3228 haemorrhages, 1549 hard exudates (HE), 3081 cotton wool spots (CWS), 3844 intraretinal microvascular abnormalities (IRMA), 1832 new vessels (NV) and 1758 panretinal photocoagulation scars (PRP)
title: Evaluation of spatial distribution of initial marking strategy among inexperienced graders in diabetic retinopathy: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis.

text: . A difference was observed across all lesion types (χ Most lesion types demonstrated high sensitivity, but low PPV, indicating a liberal marking approach. Distribution of initial markings from inexperienced graders spatially misaligns with a specialist-derived lesion map across all lesion types
title: Evaluation of spatial distribution of initial marking strategy among inexperienced graders in diabetic retinopathy: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis.

text: . As the ICDR-scale depends on identifying the most severe lesion type, systematically inconsistent search strategies may pose a risk for overlooking important lesions under time constraints. The results support the promotion of attention guiding during DR-training.

text: REFA-DINO: A Relative-Efficient Fusion Attention Framework for Binary and Multiclass Diabetic Retinopathy Classification.. Diabetic retinopathy (DR) has become a major cause of preventable blindness, and its early detection is crucial for maintaining vision in diabetic patients
title: REFA-DINO: A Relative-Efficient Fusion Attention Framework for Binary and Multiclass Diabetic Retinopathy Classification.

text: . Existing computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems still face challenges in detecting early-stage lesions, integrating local and global features, and maintaining consistent performance in binary and multiclass settings
title: REFA-DINO: A Relative-Efficient Fusion Attention Framework for Binary and Multiclass Diabetic Retinopathy Classification.

text: . To address these limitations, this study proposes a relative-efficient fusion attention framework (REFA-DINO) that integrates a convolutional local-feature learning module with a transformer-based global contextual method. The architecture employs a relative-efficient fusion adapter (REFA) block comprising two branches, EfficientNet and attention-enhanced patch embedding
title: REFA-DINO: A Relative-Efficient Fusion Attention Framework for Binary and Multiclass Diabetic Retinopathy Classification.

text: . EfficientNet extracts lesion-sensitive retinal features, and an attention-enhanced patch-embedding module is used to generate token representations. An adaptive relative position-aware cross-attention mechanism is introduced to enable effective interaction among heterogeneous features, which are further processed through the DINO-based transformer module
title: REFA-DINO: A Relative-Efficient Fusion Attention Framework for Binary and Multiclass Diabetic Retinopathy Classification.

text: . The extracted global representations are passed to the linear classification head for DR classification. REFA-DINO is evaluated on two diverse and large-scale fundus imaging datasets, EyePACS and APTOS, for binary and multiclass classification
title: REFA-DINO: A Relative-Efficient Fusion Attention Framework for Binary and Multiclass Diabetic Retinopathy Classification.

text: . The proposed framework achieved accuracies of 98.60% and 93.77% for binary classification and 85.52% and 87.51% for multiclass classification on the APTOS and EyePACS datasets, respectively. A comparative analysis against state-of-the-art methods, cross-corpora evaluation, and an ablation study are also conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed REFA-DINO
title: REFA-DINO: A Relative-Efficient Fusion Attention Framework for Binary and Multiclass Diabetic Retinopathy Classification.

text: . Compared with state-of-the-art methods, the REFA-DINO framework enhances binary classification on both the EyePACS and APTOS datasets, with significant improvements over the strongest baselines. The proposed approach attains up to 6.19% and 9.39% improvement in the binary and multiclass classification accuracy on EyePACS
title: REFA-DINO: A Relative-Efficient Fusion Attention Framework for Binary and Multiclass Diabetic Retinopathy Classification.

text: . Likewise, it achieves an improvement of 2.64% on the binary classification score on APTOS with competitive multiclass classification performance. Experimental findings highlight the robustness and generalizability of the REFA-DINO framework in classifying DR.
title: REFA-DINO: A Relative-Efficient Fusion Attention Framework for Binary and Multiclass Diabetic Retinopathy Classification.

text: Diagnostic Role of Multimodal Imaging in Optic Disc Diseases.. The aim of this narrative review was to provide a disease-oriented diagnostic framework for selecting and integrating multimodal imaging techniques according to the suspected optic disc disorder. A non-systematic PubMed search was performed to identify relevant literature on optic disc diseases and related imaging appearances
title: Diagnostic Role of Multimodal Imaging in Optic Disc Diseases.

text: . Searches included a combination of terms related to disease features and imaging modalities. The recent introduction of non-invasive imaging devices, such as optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography (OCTA), has allowed a remarkable step forward in the knowledge of the optic disc
title: Diagnostic Role of Multimodal Imaging in Optic Disc Diseases.

text: . OCT has revolutionized the diagnosis and monitoring of glaucomatous eyes, providing useful quantitative biomarkers. Fundus examination and color fundus photography are the first step for evaluation of optic disc edema, which requires further exams, including fundus autofluorescence, to exclude the presence of optic disc drusen, ocular ultrasound and in certain cases, fluorescein angiography
title: Diagnostic Role of Multimodal Imaging in Optic Disc Diseases.

text: . Although still limited, OCTA could give a support in the evaluation of vascular diseases that involve the optic disc, such as anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, retinal vein occlusion and proliferative diabetic retinopathy
title: Diagnostic Role of Multimodal Imaging in Optic Disc Diseases.

text: Research Progress of Diabetes-related Glaucoma: Mechanisms, Impacts and Management Strategies.. Diabetes mellitus (DM), a highly prevalent metabolic disorder, is increasingly recognised for its significant association with glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible vision loss
title: Research Progress of Diabetes-related Glaucoma: Mechanisms, Impacts and Management Strategies.
journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)

text: . This review systematically synthesises recent advances in understanding DM-related glaucoma, focusing on its epidemiological links, core pathophysiological mechanisms and contemporary management strategies
title: Research Progress of Diabetes-related Glaucoma: Mechanisms, Impacts and Management Strategies.
journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)

text: . The review elaborates on the dual-pathway model of glaucoma pathogenesis in diabetics, encompassing the aqueous humour dynamics pathway leading to neovascular glaucoma and the intraocular pressure -independent neurodegenerative pathway causing direct retinal ganglion cell injury
title: Research Progress of Diabetes-related Glaucoma: Mechanisms, Impacts and Management Strategies.
journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)

text: . These pathways are driven by chronic hyperglycaemia, microvascular dysfunction, oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. The presence and severity of diabetic retinopathy, particularly proliferative diabetic retinopathy, markedly heighten the risk. The potential neuroprotective roles of anti-diabetic agents like metformin and GLP-1 receptor agonists beyond glycemic control are discussed
title: Research Progress of Diabetes-related Glaucoma: Mechanisms, Impacts and Management Strategies.
journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)

title: Research Progress of Diabetes-related Glaucoma: Mechanisms, Impacts and Management Strategies.
journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)

text: . Finally, the need for individualised, multidisciplinary management to preserve vision is emphasised, and future research directions, including mechanistic studies and precision medicine approaches are outlined.

text: A decade of artificial intelligence research in ophthalmology: Global trends and transferable insights for medical AI.
title: A decade of artificial intelligence research in ophthalmology: Global trends and transferable insights for medical AI.

text: . To characterize global trends in ophthalmic AI research from 2015-2025 and drive transferable insights into the broader evolution of AI in medicine, we conducted a systematic bibliometric analysis of original AI articles in ophthalmology indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and Pubmed from 2015 to 2025
title: A decade of artificial intelligence research in ophthalmology: Global trends and transferable insights for medical AI.

text: . Publications were screened and categorized using an LLM-assisted pipeline with predefined labels, and agreement between LLM-assisted classifications and human grading was evaluated. We analyzed temporal trends and emergence patterns across study design, model architecture, disease focus, and data modalities
title: A decade of artificial intelligence research in ophthalmology: Global trends and transferable insights for medical AI.

text: . Among 12,911 included articles, annual publications increased at a compound annual growth rate of 39.7%, from 108 in 2015-3061 in 2025. Four key shifts were identified. Study design: Development studies (88.3%) dominated through the period, whereas evaluation studies (7.4%) began to emerge in 2019
title: A decade of artificial intelligence research in ophthalmology: Global trends and transferable insights for medical AI.

text: . Model architecture: Classical deep learning (71.8%) became the most prevailing approach from 2017, while foundation model studies (0.6%) increased sharply in 2024-2025
title: A decade of artificial intelligence research in ophthalmology: Global trends and transferable insights for medical AI.

text: . Disease focus: Diabetic retinopathy (32.9%), glaucoma (17.5%), and age-related macular degeneration (12.6%) remained the leading disease areas, while corneal diseases (7.0%), cataract (4.3%) and myopia (3.4%) emerged after 2019-2020 and grew rapidly
title: A decade of artificial intelligence research in ophthalmology: Global trends and transferable insights for medical AI.

text: . Data modalities: Among image-based modalities (84.1%), color fundus photography and retinal optical coherence tomography remained dominant but plateaued after 2019, whereas text-based modalities (5.5%) continued to rise after 2022
title: A decade of artificial intelligence research in ophthalmology: Global trends and transferable insights for medical AI.

text: . Over the past decade, ophthalmic AI research expanded rapidly and evolved from narrow image-based deep learning toward broader work spanning evaluation studies, foundation models, multimodal data integration, and a wider spectrum of eye diseases. These trajectories may extend beyond ophthalmology, offering broader insights into how medical AI matures toward clinical evaluation and translation.
title: A decade of artificial intelligence research in ophthalmology: Global trends and transferable insights for medical AI.

title: FLNA promotes the progression of diabetic retinopathy by increasing M1 macrophages.

title: FLNA promotes the progression of diabetic retinopathy by increasing M1 macrophages.

Quantitative PCR (q-PCR) measured mRNA levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and Western blotting assessed protein levels of FLNA, AMPK, and phosphorylated-AMPK (p-AMPK). Key findings revealed  Our study identifies FLNA as a key regulator in DR progression, primarily by enhancing M1 macrophage-mediated inflammation and AMPK phosphorylation
title: FLNA promotes the progression of diabetic retinopathy by increasing M1 macrophages.
