text: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes and Safety Profiles of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.. Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
title: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes and Safety Profiles of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

text: . Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have been assessed in several large cardiovascular outcome trials (CVOTs); however, the individual agents differ in molecular structure, pharmacology, and the populations studied, and their reported effects range from neutral to clearly beneficial
title: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes and Safety Profiles of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

text: . This review compares the cardiovascular efficacy and safety of GLP-1 RAs across all eligible randomized, placebo-controlled CVOTs in T2DM and quantitatively pools the primary outcome
title: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes and Safety Profiles of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

text: . Following the PRISMA 2020 statement, ClinicalTrials.gov, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to 15 December 2025 for randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled CVOTs comparing a GLP-1 RA with placebo in adults with T2DM and reporting adjudicated major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) as a primary or co-primary endpoint
title: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes and Safety Profiles of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

text: . The protocol was not prospectively registered. Two reviewers independently performed screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment (Cochrane RoB 2), and certainty of evidence was rated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE)
title: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes and Safety Profiles of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

text: . Findings were synthesized narratively and, for the primary MACE outcome, pooled using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model on the log-hazard-ratio scale, with heterogeneity quantified by I² and Cochran's Q, leave-one-out sensitivity analysis, and small-study assessment by funnel plot and Egger's test. Nine trials enrolling 69,730 participants met the eligibility criteria
title: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes and Safety Profiles of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

title: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes and Safety Profiles of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

text: . The composite benefit was driven by reductions in myocardial infarction and stroke, with a neutral effect on hospitalization for heart failure. title: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes and Safety Profiles of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

text: . Between-agent and between-trial heterogeneity preclude a definitive ranking of individual agents.

text: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively assess the diagnostic accuracy of fundus image-based deep learning models in the grading of diabetic retinopathy. title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: for severe NPDR (stage 3), and 78.82% (95% CI: 71.76%-85.13%) for PDR (stage 4)

title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . DL exhibits high sensitivity and substantial potential for DR grading, particularly in screening for no DR and vision-threatening DR. title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Mapping diabetic eye exam non-adherence across urban-rural communities: A GIS-based regional analysis of socioeconomic disadvantage in the Rochester, NY Metropolitan Statistical Area.

title: Mapping diabetic eye exam non-adherence across urban-rural communities: A GIS-based regional analysis of socioeconomic disadvantage in the Rochester, NY Metropolitan Statistical Area.

text: Content-based retrieval of fundus images and diabetic retinopathy detection using variants of local texture features.. Content-based retinal image analysis plays a crucial role in the early diagnosis of ocular diseases
title: Content-based retrieval of fundus images and diabetic retinopathy detection using variants of local texture features.

text: . In this study, we proposed a novel approach for efficient content-based retinal image retrieval and Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) detection using variants of local texture features derived from Local Binary Pattern (LBP), Local Ternary Pattern (LTP), and Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM)
title: Content-based retrieval of fundus images and diabetic retinopathy detection using variants of local texture features.

title: Content-based retrieval of fundus images and diabetic retinopathy detection using variants of local texture features.

text: . Subsequently, we trained machine learning models, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree, and Random Forest, on the extracted features to effectively retrieve retinal images and detect DR. title: Content-based retrieval of fundus images and diabetic retinopathy detection using variants of local texture features.

text: . A key innovation of this study lies in the fusion of multiple texture-based features, creating a comprehensive representation that integrates high-level semantic information with fine-grained local patterns. title: Content-based retrieval of fundus images and diabetic retinopathy detection using variants of local texture features.

text: . Further, a metaheuristic approach for feature selection and optimization is employed, comparing Differential Evolution, Genetic Algorithm, and Particle Swarm Optimization to identify the most effective features for retrieval. Differential Evolution achieved the highest precision of 90.67 % for retrieving the top 10 relevant images
title: Content-based retrieval of fundus images and diabetic retinopathy detection using variants of local texture features.

text: . The proposed hybrid approach demonstrates the effectiveness of integrating classical image analysis methods with machine learning for DR detection and content-based image retrieval. text: Duration-dependent decoupling of the macular neurovascular unit in type 2 diabetes without retinopathy: A topographic analysis using ultra-widefield OCT angiography.
title: Duration-dependent decoupling of the macular neurovascular unit in type 2 diabetes without retinopathy: A topographic analysis using ultra-widefield OCT angiography.

text: . To characterize duration-dependent topographic macular neurovascular unit (NVU) alterations in type 2 diabetes (T2DM) without diabetic retinopathy (DR) using 26×21 mm ultra-widefield swept-source OCT angiography (UWF-SS-OCTA) and evaluate its diagnostic utility for long-duration eyes

title: Duration-dependent decoupling of the macular neurovascular unit in type 2 diabetes without retinopathy: A topographic analysis using ultra-widefield OCT angiography.

text: . Ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thickness was derived from the 26 × 21 mm OCTA scan. ANCOVA adjusted for age, sex, BMI, hypertension, IOP with false discovery rate correction, multivariable regression, and ROC/decision curve analyses were used
title: Duration-dependent decoupling of the macular neurovascular unit in type 2 diabetes without retinopathy: A topographic analysis using ultra-widefield OCT angiography.

text: . Longer duration was associated with progressive GCIPL thinning and deep-predominant DVD reduction across nearly all macular zones (q < 0.05); the DVD deficit was most pronounced in the outer ring. SVD showed nasal-temporal asymmetry; selective nasal inner loss in ≥10-year group. GCIPL-DVD coupling, present in controls, attenuated in ≥10-year group, indicating NVU decoupling
title: Duration-dependent decoupling of the macular neurovascular unit in type 2 diabetes without retinopathy: A topographic analysis using ultra-widefield OCT angiography.

text: . Duration independently predicted GCIPL (β=-0.32) and DVD-M 12-21 (β=-0.23) after adjustment (P < 0.01). title: Duration-dependent decoupling of the macular neurovascular unit in type 2 diabetes without retinopathy: A topographic analysis using ultra-widefield OCT angiography.

text: . Preclinical NVU decoupling, which is predominant in the deep capillary plexus and nasally asymmetric, already occurs in T2DM without fundoscopic DR and progresses with disease duration. Deep-layer UWF-SS-OCTA metrics may strengthen risk stratification before clinical retinopathy.
title: Duration-dependent decoupling of the macular neurovascular unit in type 2 diabetes without retinopathy: A topographic analysis using ultra-widefield OCT angiography.

text: Reaching the unreached: Task-shifting diabetic retinopathy screening in urban slums of low- and middle-income countries.. title: Reaching the unreached: Task-shifting diabetic retinopathy screening in urban slums of low- and middle-income countries.

text: . These communities often remain outside the reach of conventional health systems due to systemic neglect, migratory lifestyles, and fragile infrastructure. title: Reaching the unreached: Task-shifting diabetic retinopathy screening in urban slums of low- and middle-income countries.

text: . This review synthesizes global evidence on community and allied health worker (CAHW)-led DR screening initiatives in urban slum contexts, drawing from 22 studies conducted across Asia, Africa, Latin America, and Oceania. In addition, field experience from a DR screening program in Dharavi, Mumbai, one of Asia's largest informal settlements, is included to illustrate operational realities
title: Reaching the unreached: Task-shifting diabetic retinopathy screening in urban slums of low- and middle-income countries.

text: . Findings highlight the transformative potential of task-shifting DR screening responsibilities to CAHWs, many of whom are recruited from the communities they serve. title: Reaching the unreached: Task-shifting diabetic retinopathy screening in urban slums of low- and middle-income countries.

text: . With structured training and supervision, CAHWs were found capable of taking on responsibilities conventionally reserved for ophthalmic professionals. title: Reaching the unreached: Task-shifting diabetic retinopathy screening in urban slums of low- and middle-income countries.

text: . Despite clear benefits, challenges persist. Programs often lack standardized competency frameworks, adequate incentives, digital tools, and integrated referral systems. Addressing these gaps is essential for sustaining impact.
title: Reaching the unreached: Task-shifting diabetic retinopathy screening in urban slums of low- and middle-income countries.

text: A Roadmap for National Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in Croatia: Integrating European Evidence, Telemedicine, and AI.. Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable blindness among working-age adults

text: Active Learning Under Expert-Budget Constraints: A Human-in-the-Loop Pipeline for Diabetic Retinopathy Lesion Detection.. title: Active Learning Under Expert-Budget Constraints: A Human-in-the-Loop Pipeline for Diabetic Retinopathy Lesion Detection.

text: . Across three independent random seeds, random sampling dominates at cold start (mean mAP@50 0.14→0.25 over R0-R1), whereas Hybrid-Diversity converges to the highest mAP@50, Precision, and Recall by R7 (431 images; mAP@50 0.40, Precision 0.55, Recall 0.41), with MC Dropout close behind; by R8, the labeled pool is exhausted and all strategies converge to the same final model
title: Active Learning Under Expert-Budget Constraints: A Human-in-the-Loop Pipeline for Diabetic Retinopathy Lesion Detection.

text: . A clinician crossover analysis of 36 paired clinical images, controlling for per-clinician speed bias and per-image difficulty bias, shows no statistically significant difference in overall per-image labeling time between AI-assisted and manual annotation (p=0.52), but a statistically significant increase in confirmed lesion detections under AI assistance (p=0.0058), driven predominantly
title: Active Learning Under Expert-Budget Constraints: A Human-in-the-Loop Pipeline for Diabetic Retinopathy Lesion Detection.

text: AI assistance (p=0.0058), driven predominantly (84-100% of the net increase) by microaneurysms, the lesion type most prone to being missed unaided
title: Active Learning Under Expert-Budget Constraints: A Human-in-the-Loop Pipeline for Diabetic Retinopathy Lesion Detection.

text: . The results indicate that, under expert-budget constraints, AL strategy choice should be staged: random sampling for cold start, uncertainty-and-diversity sampling once the model has matured, and that AI assistance trades a modest, lesion-burden-dependent time cost for a measurable gain in the sensitivity of microaneurysm detection.
title: Active Learning Under Expert-Budget Constraints: A Human-in-the-Loop Pipeline for Diabetic Retinopathy Lesion Detection.

text: Artificial intelligence for early detection of diabetic retinopathy: A vision transformer-based approach.. Early identification of diabetic retinopathy (DR), which is a primary cause of vision impairment globally, is a crucial phasis for effective intervention and treatment
title: Artificial intelligence for early detection of diabetic retinopathy: A vision transformer-based approach.

text: . Traditional screening workflows rely on manual diagnosis by ophthalmologists, which remains the gold standard but can be time-consuming and subject to variability due to human factors. To support and enhance the screening process, artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools have shown promise in automating DR detection, particularly with recent advances in deep learning
title: Artificial intelligence for early detection of diabetic retinopathy: A vision transformer-based approach.

text: . However, medical images with long-range dependencies and spatial linkages can be challenging for CNN-based algorithms to handle. This paper proposes a Vision Transformer (ViT)-based model, specifically using a Compact Convolutional Transformer (CCT), for early automated detection of DR
title: Artificial intelligence for early detection of diabetic retinopathy: A vision transformer-based approach.

text: . The model uses self-attention techniques to improve feature extraction and classification performance; combining three main stages: the CCT tokenizer, transformer encoder, and sequence pooling. The proposed approach was trained on public datasets (EyePACS and APTOS 2019) and evaluated against state-of-the-art deep learning architectures
title: Artificial intelligence for early detection of diabetic retinopathy: A vision transformer-based approach.

text: . Our experimental findings demonstrate that ViT performs among the best in the current state of the art with an overall accuracy of 97% and F1-scores above 0.95 across all DR severity levels. Our system is primarily designed for the pre-screening stage of diabetic retinopathy workflows, enabling rapid and reliable identification of potential DR cases for further clinical evaluation
title: Artificial intelligence for early detection of diabetic retinopathy: A vision transformer-based approach.

text: . These results highlight the potential of transformer-based designs in medical picture analysis, as well as the implications for telemedicine and e-health solutions in real-time, especially in cases of low-resource settings.
title: Artificial intelligence for early detection of diabetic retinopathy: A vision transformer-based approach.

text: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN PREDIAGNOSTIC MACULAR THICKNESS WITH RISK OF AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION.. To determine whether specific prediagnostic macular thickness are associated with an increased risk of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). A total of 40,078 UK Biobank participants without baseline AMD who underwent optical coherence tomography imaging were included
title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN PREDIAGNOSTIC MACULAR THICKNESS WITH RISK OF AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION.

text: . Macular thickness measurements were obtained through optical coherence tomography across nine subfields of the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study. Latent Profile Analysis was used to classify distinct prediagnostic macular thickness profiles, while cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios between the identified profiles
title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN PREDIAGNOSTIC MACULAR THICKNESS WITH RISK OF AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION.

text: . Two distinct prediagnostic macular thickness profiles were identified. Compared with Profile 1 (n = 31,942), Profile 2 (n = 8,136) was characterized by thinner inner and outer superior subfields, alongside thicker central and other outer subfields
title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN PREDIAGNOSTIC MACULAR THICKNESS WITH RISK OF AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION.

text: . Profile 2 was associated with significantly increased AMD risk compared with Profile 1 (hazard ratio, 1.59; 95% confidence interval, 1.32-1.90; P < 0.001). After adjustment for all covariates, the observed association persisted (hazard ratio, 1.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-1.67; P < 0.001). Distinct prediagnostic macular thickness patterns are associated with elevated AMD risk
title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN PREDIAGNOSTIC MACULAR THICKNESS WITH RISK OF AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION.

text: . These findings provide novel insights into potential early macular structural changes before AMD diagnosis, and may serve as novel biomarkers for early identification of AMD.
title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN PREDIAGNOSTIC MACULAR THICKNESS WITH RISK OF AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION.

text: An integrated deep learning and Bayesian computational method-based quantification of angiogenesis in the chick embryo model.. Angiogenesis is the process of the formation of new blood vessels from existing vessels, and it sits directly at the intersection of normal physiology and multiple diseases
title: An integrated deep learning and Bayesian computational method-based quantification of angiogenesis in the chick embryo model.
journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

text: . Normal physiological activities like embryonic development and tissue homoeostasis require precise regulation. Diseased conditions occur when angiogenesis is dysregulated, which drives tumour growth when excessive or leads to diabetic retinopathy-like conditions when insufficient
title: An integrated deep learning and Bayesian computational method-based quantification of angiogenesis in the chick embryo model.
journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

text: . Researchers are working on therapeutic interventions, and mechanistic studies have made reliable angiogenesis screening essential. Cell-based assays suffer from limited direct physiological relevance, and animal-based models are complex but expensive and raise ethical questions
title: An integrated deep learning and Bayesian computational method-based quantification of angiogenesis in the chick embryo model.
journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

text: . In this work, we have developed an integrated deep-learning method for the quantitative estimation of angiogenesis from chick embryo-based experimental data. The chick embryo-based yolk sac membrane model (YSM) provides a complex environment for animal models without the cost of other studies. The model developed here offers a direct optical window providing detailed time-based information
title: An integrated deep learning and Bayesian computational method-based quantification of angiogenesis in the chick embryo model.
journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

text: . The lack of available image analysis tools capable of handling these specific optical characteristics has hindered this assay for a long time. Subsequently, we have designed a pipeline for angiogenesis image analysis tailored to the YSM assay
title: An integrated deep learning and Bayesian computational method-based quantification of angiogenesis in the chick embryo model.
journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

text: . Here, we have integrated standard image processing (channel separation and CLAHE enhancement) with deep learning and a Bayesian hierarchical Gompertz Gaussian process model for probabilistic vessel length forecasting. This is validated pharmacologically against the VEGF, anti-VEGF antibody, and hydrocortisone treatment groups
title: An integrated deep learning and Bayesian computational method-based quantification of angiogenesis in the chick embryo model.
journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

text: . Analysis tools tailored for this assay have not been well reported as the YSM assay has a low signal-to-background ratio (red vessels against a yellow background), which has challenged experienced researchers.
title: An integrated deep learning and Bayesian computational method-based quantification of angiogenesis in the chick embryo model.
journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

text: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Treatment Capacity in Student-Run Free Clinics: A National Assessment.. To characterize ophthalmic resources and evaluate diabetic retinopathy screening, treatment, and referral practices among student-run free clinics in the United States that provide ophthalmology services
title: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Treatment Capacity in Student-Run Free Clinics: A National Assessment.

text: . A cross-sectional survey was distributed to 54 student-run free clinics identified through a national network. The 17-item survey assessed clinic demographics, funding sources, ophthalmic equipment availability, diabetic retinopathy screening and treatment practices, referral pathways, perceived barriers, and resource needs. Of the 54 clinics contacted, 21 (39%) responded, representing 13 states
title: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Treatment Capacity in Student-Run Free Clinics: A National Assessment.

text: . All clinics reported caring for patients with diabetic retinopathy (100%), glaucoma (81%), and cataracts (76%). Primary funding sources included grants (38%) and alternative funding mechanisms (29%)
title: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Treatment Capacity in Student-Run Free Clinics: A National Assessment.

text: . Commonly available equipment included slit lamps (67%) and indirect ophthalmoscopes (52%), while advanced imaging modalities such as optical coherence tomography were available in only 14% of clinics. Diabetic retinopathy screening was performed in 95% of clinics, primarily via dilated retinal examination (55%)
title: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Treatment Capacity in Student-Run Free Clinics: A National Assessment.

text: . Only 14% of clinics (3/21) reported access to diabetic retinopathy treatment via external referral pathways, and none provided treatment on site. Key barriers to comprehensive care included insufficient funding, lack of diagnostic equipment, and limited availability of trained clinical personnel
title: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Treatment Capacity in Student-Run Free Clinics: A National Assessment.

text: . Student-run free clinics commonly provide diabetic retinopathy screening but lack the capacity to deliver definitive treatment, relying primarily on external referral pathways. Strengthening academic partnerships and expanding treatment access may improve equitable, vision-preserving care for underserved populations.
title: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Treatment Capacity in Student-Run Free Clinics: A National Assessment.

text: Diabetic Retinopathy in Primary Healthcare in a Brazilian Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Teleophthalmology.. Diabetic retinopathy is a complication of diabetes and the leading cause of irreversible blindness in people of working age
title: Diabetic Retinopathy in Primary Healthcare in a Brazilian Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Teleophthalmology.

text: . This study aims to estimate the prevalence of diabetic retinopathy among individuals taking insulin who attend the primary healthcare in the municipality of Jardinópolis, state of São Paulo, Brazil
title: Diabetic Retinopathy in Primary Healthcare in a Brazilian Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Teleophthalmology.

text: . This is a cross-sectional study with a sample of 152 participants, in which data collection occurred in March 2023 by means of interviews, laboratory exams and fundoscopy with a portable retinal camera mounted onto a device attached to a smartphone
title: Diabetic Retinopathy in Primary Healthcare in a Brazilian Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Teleophthalmology.

text: . The captured images were automatically analysed by means of deep learning algorithms for grading retinal alterations, as well as diabetic retinopathy. The prevalence of diabetic retinopathy was estimated to be 28.3% (95% CI 21.1-35.4), with most of the cases corresponding to mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (65.1%)
title: Diabetic Retinopathy in Primary Healthcare in a Brazilian Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Teleophthalmology.

text: . No association was found between diabetic retinopathy and the variables investigated. Concordance test between self-reported and diagnosed diabetic retinopathy showed a Kappa coefficient of 0.30 (95% CI, 0.13-0.47), in which 16.5% of the participants reported having no diabetic retinopathy despite being diagnosed as having it
title: Diabetic Retinopathy in Primary Healthcare in a Brazilian Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Teleophthalmology.

text: . However, 9.9% of the participants self-reporting having diabetic retinopathy were not diagnosed with it. The prevalence of diabetic retinopathy is within the national range. The lack of knowledge on the diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy and aspects related to such a complication of diabetes was found to be worrying
title: Diabetic Retinopathy in Primary Healthcare in a Brazilian Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Teleophthalmology.

text: . Therefore, one highlights the importance of primary healthcare programmes in promoting integral care to people with diabetes, including ocular health.
title: Diabetic Retinopathy in Primary Healthcare in a Brazilian Municipality: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Teleophthalmology.

text: Beyond hyperglycaemia: diabetic retinopathy is a multifactorial complication of diabetes mellitus.. The remarkable researches have been made to clarify the pathogenesis of DR, but relatively little is known about it. The goal was to summarize the epidemiology and mechanism of DR, provide screening and biomarker information of DR and suggest the strategies for treatment and intervention of DR
title: Beyond hyperglycaemia: diabetic retinopathy is a multifactorial complication of diabetes mellitus.

text: . This article synthesizes recent findings on intricate interrelated patho-physiological mechanisms elicited by hyperglycaemia underlie the progression of DR. DR has long been considered a microvascular disorder, but accumulating evidences demonstrate that retinal neurodegeneration like activated microglial is involved as well
title: Beyond hyperglycaemia: diabetic retinopathy is a multifactorial complication of diabetes mellitus.

text: . The progression of DR is underpinned by complex, interconnected pathophysiological mechanisms triggered by hyperglycaemia, including vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), methylglyoxal (MGO), Wnt signalling pathways, retinal neurodegeneration and other factors
title: Beyond hyperglycaemia: diabetic retinopathy is a multifactorial complication of diabetes mellitus.

text: . Enhanced comprehension of the fundamental pathophysiological mechanisms, coupled with advancements in computer technology, fosters the development of innovative approaches to screening, diagnosis and early intervention for DR. DR, a multifactorial complication of diabetes mellitus, necessitates continued research into precise screening methodologies and targeted therapeutic strategies.
title: Beyond hyperglycaemia: diabetic retinopathy is a multifactorial complication of diabetes mellitus.

text: A bibliometric analysis of global trends in AI-driven digital health technologies for diabetes management.. Digital health technologies are increasingly applied in diabetes care, enabling continuous monitoring, personalized support and remote interventions. Meanwhile, artificial intelligence (AI) is enhancing the precision and effectiveness of these tools
title: A bibliometric analysis of global trends in AI-driven digital health technologies for diabetes management.

text: . This study aims to map global research trends and thematic developments in AI-driven digital health technologies for diabetes management and to explore their future directions
title: A bibliometric analysis of global trends in AI-driven digital health technologies for diabetes management.

text: . We collected data from the Web of Science Core Collection, including articles and reviews published up to July 12, 2025, using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Microsoft Excel to analyze countries/regions, institutions, journals, references, authors, and keywords. A total of 673 publications were included in the analysis
title: A bibliometric analysis of global trends in AI-driven digital health technologies for diabetes management.

text: . Global publications on AI-driven digital health technologies for diabetes increased steadily, with the USA leading in output. The University of London ranked as the most productive institution. Sensors and diabetes care were the most frequently published and cited journals in this field. Herrero P was among the most prolific authors
title: A bibliometric analysis of global trends in AI-driven digital health technologies for diabetes management.

text: . Herrero P was among the most prolific authors. The most cited article was "Development and Validation of a Deep Learning Algorithm for Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy in Retinal Fundus Photographs." "diabetes" was the most frequently occurring keyword
title: A bibliometric analysis of global trends in AI-driven digital health technologies for diabetes management.

text: . Keyword cluster analysis identified 3 primary research hotspots: AI-enabled monitoring, digital health interventions, and AI-based diabetic retinopathy screening. This study summarizes the evolution of AI-driven digital health technologies in diabetes care
title: A bibliometric analysis of global trends in AI-driven digital health technologies for diabetes management.

text: . Although challenges remain in data security, standardization and validation, these technologies hold increasing potential for accurate diagnosis, real-time monitoring and personalized care.
title: A bibliometric analysis of global trends in AI-driven digital health technologies for diabetes management.

text: Ultra-widefield color fundus images and artificial intelligence for diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.. Ultra-widefield (UWF) fundus cameras capture a larger retinal area without pupil dilation. We summarized evidence and diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diabetic retinopathy (DR) assessments using UWF images (UWFIs)
title: Ultra-widefield color fundus images and artificial intelligence for diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . We searched PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science to February 9, 2025, for studies evaluating DR using UWFIs and AI analyses. We followed the PRISMA guidelines and assessed study quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for diagnostic accuracy
title: Ultra-widefield color fundus images and artificial intelligence for diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Forest plots and summary receiver operating characteristic curves estimated sensitivity and specificity of AI-driven DR screening using UWFI. Of 527 records identified, 17 studies were included in the systematic review and four in the meta-analysis. All studies used Optos software
title: Ultra-widefield color fundus images and artificial intelligence for diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . All studies used Optos software. Among the included studies, two evaluated DR discrimination from multiple retinal disorders, six addressed DR stage classification based on guideline scales, six evaluated DR screening, and one each focused on referable retinal pathology detection, DR progression prediction, and detection of clinical DR features
title: Ultra-widefield color fundus images and artificial intelligence for diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . The summary sensitivity, specificity, and area under receiver operating characteristic curve for AI-driven DR screening using UWFI were 85.0%, 72.5%, and 0.870 (0.838-0.897), respectively. UWFI-based AI screening showed acceptable sensitivity but limited specificity
title: Ultra-widefield color fundus images and artificial intelligence for diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . AI-driven DR screening using UWFIs may achieve acceptable sensitivity but with limited specificity; however, these findings should be interpreted with caution, given the limited number of available studies. Further studies using larger, diverse datasets with rigorous external validation across UWF platforms are needed to improve generalizability and clarify the clinical role of UWFI-based AI.
title: Ultra-widefield color fundus images and artificial intelligence for diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: Changes in retinal venous diameter in proliferative diabetic retinopathy patients with diabetic macular edema following faricimab treatment: an observational study.. To evaluate the effect of intravitreal faricimab injections on retinal venous diameter in proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) patients with diabetic macular edema (DME)
title: Changes in retinal venous diameter in proliferative diabetic retinopathy patients with diabetic macular edema following faricimab treatment: an observational study.

text: . This single-center, retrospective cohort study included 46 PDR patients (46 eyes) with DME, treated between August 2024 and January 2025. All participants received intravitreal faricimab combined with panretinal photocoagulation (PRP)
title: Changes in retinal venous diameter in proliferative diabetic retinopathy patients with diabetic macular edema following faricimab treatment: an observational study.

text: . Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR), central foveal thickness (CFT, μm), microaneurysm (MA) count, hard exudates (HE), neovascularization (NV) area, and retinal venous diameter were assessed at baseline and at 1, 3, and 6 months post-treatment. Significant improvements in BCVA were observed at 1, 3, and 6 months (0.52 ± 0.16, 0.48 ± 0.18, 0.40 ± 0.15 vs
title: Changes in retinal venous diameter in proliferative diabetic retinopathy patients with diabetic macular edema following faricimab treatment: an observational study.

text: . baseline 0.66 ± 0.18; all P < 0.05). CFT showed a significant reduction at all time points (381.35 ± 40.75, 327.30 ± 43.40, 297.56 ± 35.81 μm vs. baseline 472.34 ± 47.23 μm; all P < 0.05). The MA count showed no significant reduction at 1 month (P > 0.05) but decreased significantly thereafter (72.71 ± 20.53 and 63.06 ± 17.08 at 3 and 6 months, respectively; both P < 0.05)
title: Changes in retinal venous diameter in proliferative diabetic retinopathy patients with diabetic macular edema following faricimab treatment: an observational study.

text: . Reductions in HE area were not significant at 1 or 3 months (in 2 and 6 patients, respectively; both P > 0.05). At 6 months, a significant reduction in HE area was observed in 14 patients (P < 0.05). The NV area was significantly reduced at 1, 3, and 6 months compared to baseline (0.17 ± 0.10 mm², 0.17 ± 0.09 mm², and 0.17 ± 0.08 mm² vs. 0.98 ± 0.17 mm²; all P<0.05)
title: Changes in retinal venous diameter in proliferative diabetic retinopathy patients with diabetic macular edema following faricimab treatment: an observational study.

text: . 0.98 ± 0.17 mm²; all P<0.05). Retinal venous diameter showed no significant change at 1 and 3 months compared with baseline (both P > 0.05) but was significantly reduced at 6 months (299.40 ± 19.56 μm; P < 0.05). Intravitreal faricimab was safe and effective for PDR patients with DME
title: Changes in retinal venous diameter in proliferative diabetic retinopathy patients with diabetic macular edema following faricimab treatment: an observational study.

text: . A trend toward morphological reversal of retinal venous diameter was demonstrated at 6 months, suggesting that faricimab may influence retinal microvascular remodeling through dual inhibition of the VEGF-A and Ang-2 pathways.
title: Changes in retinal venous diameter in proliferative diabetic retinopathy patients with diabetic macular edema following faricimab treatment: an observational study.

text: Associations between dietary nutrient intake and the risk of multiple age-related ocular diseases: evidence from longitudinal analysis.. This study aims to assess how dietary nutrient intake relates to the risk of developing four common age-related ocular diseases, including age-related macular degeneration, cataract, diabetic retinopathy, and glaucoma
title: Associations between dietary nutrient intake and the risk of multiple age-related ocular diseases: evidence from longitudinal analysis.
journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging

text: . This study utilized data from the UK Biobank, covering 36 nutrients. The analysis included 103192 participants after applying predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The outcomes were the incidences of four age-related ocular diseases, including age-related macular degeneration, cataract, diabetic retinopathy, and glaucoma, derived from UK Biobank hospital records
title: Associations between dietary nutrient intake and the risk of multiple age-related ocular diseases: evidence from longitudinal analysis.
journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging

text: . Associations between nutrient intake and the incidence risk of four diseases were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were also performed. During a median follow-up time of approximately 13 years, 1977 age-related macular degeneration cases, 11312 cataract cases, 618 diabetic retinopathy cases and 2213 glaucoma cases became incident
title: Associations between dietary nutrient intake and the risk of multiple age-related ocular diseases: evidence from longitudinal analysis.
journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging

text: . Pantothenic acid intake was positively associated with an elevated risk of AMD (HR: 1.05, 95%CI: 1.01-1.09, p = 0.013), which is more pronounced among older participants and men. Total iron (HR: 0.99, 95%CI: 0.98-1.00, p = 0.019), non-haem iron (HR: 0.99, 95% CI: 0.98-1.00, p = 0.014) and manganese (HR: 0.98, 95%CI: 0.96-1.00, p = 0.020) showed protective associations with cataract
title: Associations between dietary nutrient intake and the risk of multiple age-related ocular diseases: evidence from longitudinal analysis.
journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging

text: . The effects of total iron (HR: 1.05, 95%CI: 1.01-1.10, p = 0.022) and haem iron (HR: 1.34, 95%CI: 1.06-1.69, p = 0.014) on DR risk were also observed. Copper intake appeared to exert a protective effect against glaucoma (HR: 0.86, 95%CI: 0.75-0.99, p = 0.032). Several dietary nutrients were associated with the incidence of age-related eye diseases.
title: Associations between dietary nutrient intake and the risk of multiple age-related ocular diseases: evidence from longitudinal analysis.
journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging

text: A lightweight DeepME model based on improved YOLOv11 architecture for macular edema detection and treatment monitoring.. We developed and validated an improved YOLOv11-based deep learning algorithm for accurate macular edema detection in optical coherence tomography (OCT) images, and built DeepME-a lightweight system for diagnosis and treatment recommendations
title: A lightweight DeepME model based on improved YOLOv11 architecture for macular edema detection and treatment monitoring.

text: . We compiled a comprehensive dataset combining hospital clinical data and public OCT resources, covering macular edema and other retinal diseases. External validation used an anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) cohort of 336 eyes from 300 patients with diabetic retinopathy or retinal vein occlusion
title: A lightweight DeepME model based on improved YOLOv11 architecture for macular edema detection and treatment monitoring.

text: . The improved YOLOv11n integrated the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to enhance feature extraction. DeepME combined this detector with an optimized DeepSeek model, current clinical guidelines, and expert knowledge. DeepME achieved better performance over standard YOLOv11: accuracy 0.980, specificity 0.990, sensitivity 0.970, precision 0.990, F1-score 0.980, and AUC 0.9993
title: A lightweight DeepME model based on improved YOLOv11 architecture for macular edema detection and treatment monitoring.

text: . Grad-CAM visualizations confirmed precise localization of cystoid macular edema within anatomically correct retinal layers. In the anti-VEGF cohort, central foveal thickness decreased significantly at one-month follow-up (p < 0.001), and DeepME showed substantial agreement with manual grading (p < 0.001), enabling rapid, accurate diagnosis and treatment guidance
title: A lightweight DeepME model based on improved YOLOv11 architecture for macular edema detection and treatment monitoring.

text: . This study introduces DeepME, a novel clinical decision support system that integrates an improved YOLOv11 detection architecture for comprehensive macular edema management. DeepME delivers high accuracy in evaluating anti-VEGF treatment response and shows strong potential for real-world clinical decision support.
title: A lightweight DeepME model based on improved YOLOv11 architecture for macular edema detection and treatment monitoring.

text: Ultra-widefield OCTA in Clinical Practice: Expanding Insights into the Peripheral Retina. A Review.. Ultra-widefield optical coherence tomography angiography represents the latest technological advance that significantly expands the possibilities of non-invasive imaging, not only of retinal and choroidal microcirculation
title: Ultra-widefield OCTA in Clinical Practice: Expanding Insights into the Peripheral Retina. A Review.
journal: Ceska a slovenska oftalmologie : casopis Ceske oftalmologicke spolecnosti a Slovenske oftalmologicke spolecnosti

text: . Compared to conventional OCTA, it enables visualization of the peripheral retina, providing a  more comprehensive view of the distribution of vascular changes across a  wide spectrum of diseases
title: Ultra-widefield OCTA in Clinical Practice: Expanding Insights into the Peripheral Retina. A Review.
journal: Ceska a slovenska oftalmologie : casopis Ceske oftalmologicke spolecnosti a Slovenske oftalmologicke spolecnosti

text: . In clinical practice, this technology may reduce the need for invasive examinations, particularly fluorescein angiography, or contribute to more accurate identification of patients in whom such examination remains necessary. The aim of this paper is to highlight the clinical application of UWF-OCTA in everyday practice and to demonstrate its benefits based on original imaging material
title: Ultra-widefield OCTA in Clinical Practice: Expanding Insights into the Peripheral Retina. A Review.
journal: Ceska a slovenska oftalmologie : casopis Ceske oftalmologicke spolecnosti a Slovenske oftalmologicke spolecnosti

text: . The study presents typical findings in diabetic retinopathy, central serous chorioretinopathy, pediatric retinal vascular diseases, and vitreoretinal pathologies.
title: Ultra-widefield OCTA in Clinical Practice: Expanding Insights into the Peripheral Retina. A Review.

text: Teleophthalmology for Retinal Disease Screening and Referral in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Case Overview of India.. Innovations like teleophthalmology have made great strides in improving access to care for patients with retinal disease by enabling prompt screening and referral, especially in underprivileged areas
title: Teleophthalmology for Retinal Disease Screening and Referral in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Case Overview of India.

text: . This review highlights the growing role of teleophthalmology in addressing the burden of few retinal diseases like diabetic retinopathy (DR), age-related macular degeneration (ARMD), and retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), artificial intelligence (AI), electronic medical records (EMR) and portable imaging technologies have greatly increased the precision of detection and care coordination
title: Teleophthalmology for Retinal Disease Screening and Referral in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Case Overview of India.

text: . Its scalability is further supported by high patient satisfaction and cost-effectiveness. Barriers to implementation, however, include inadequate training, data security concerns, limited infrastructure and upfront investment costs
title: Teleophthalmology for Retinal Disease Screening and Referral in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Case Overview of India.

text: . We offer focused solutions to address existing gaps, drawing primarily on evidence and national teleophthalmology initiatives from India, which is presented as a representative LMIC case study. The findings may guide the development and scale-up of teleophthalmology services in other LMICs settings
title: Teleophthalmology for Retinal Disease Screening and Referral in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Case Overview of India.

text: . Teleophthalmology can become the backbone of equitable retinal disease care delivery with appropriate policy support and standardization of processes involved. These findings have broader implications for teleophthalmology implementation in LMICs that face similar healthcare delivery challenges.
title: Teleophthalmology for Retinal Disease Screening and Referral in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Case Overview of India.

text: GENERALIZABILITY OF DEEP LEARNING MODELS FOR REFERABLE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY DETECTION: A CROSS-POPULATION STUDY.. To evaluate cross-population performance of deep learning models for referable diabetic retinopathy (DR) detection and assess whether inclusion of local data improves robustness in a Turkish external validation setting
title: GENERALIZABILITY OF DEEP LEARNING MODELS FOR REFERABLE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY DETECTION: A CROSS-POPULATION STUDY.

text: . Global datasets (DDR, IDRiD, Messidor) and a Turkish real-world clinical dataset were used. Images were re-graded by three ophthalmologists and binarized as referable/non-referable DR. Five architectures were evaluated: EfficientNet-B0, EfficientNet-V2, ResNet50, ConvNeXt-V2-Tiny, and Swin V2 CR Small
title: GENERALIZABILITY OF DEEP LEARNING MODELS FOR REFERABLE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY DETECTION: A CROSS-POPULATION STUDY.

text: . Models were tested under three settings: Global Train-Global Test, Global Train-Local Test, and Mixed Train-Mixed Test. Performance metrics included accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, NPV, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC; Grad-CAM was used for explainability. The global training set included 9,881 images; two external test sets (2,042 images each) were used
title: GENERALIZABILITY OF DEEP LEARNING MODELS FOR REFERABLE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY DETECTION: A CROSS-POPULATION STUDY.

title: GENERALIZABILITY OF DEEP LEARNING MODELS FOR REFERABLE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY DETECTION: A CROSS-POPULATION STUDY.

title: ENHANCING THE PERFORMANCE OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY GRADING MODELS USING SYNTHETIC IMAGES.

title: ENHANCING THE PERFORMANCE OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY GRADING MODELS USING SYNTHETIC IMAGES.

title: ENHANCING THE PERFORMANCE OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY GRADING MODELS USING SYNTHETIC IMAGES.

title: ENHANCING THE PERFORMANCE OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY GRADING MODELS USING SYNTHETIC IMAGES.

title: An attention-based transformer algorithm integrated with yolo framework for lesion localization and detection in diabetic retinopathy.

title: An attention-based transformer algorithm integrated with yolo framework for lesion localization and detection in diabetic retinopathy.

title: An attention-based transformer algorithm integrated with yolo framework for lesion localization and detection in diabetic retinopathy.

text: VDAC1 O-GlcNAcylation Promotes mtDNA Release and Activates ZBP1-Dependent Neuroinflammation in Diabetic Retinopathy.. Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major cause of vision loss in working-age adults with diabetes
title: VDAC1 O-GlcNAcylation Promotes mtDNA Release and Activates ZBP1-Dependent Neuroinflammation in Diabetic Retinopathy.

title: VDAC1 O-GlcNAcylation Promotes mtDNA Release and Activates ZBP1-Dependent Neuroinflammation in Diabetic Retinopathy.

title: VDAC1 O-GlcNAcylation Promotes mtDNA Release and Activates ZBP1-Dependent Neuroinflammation in Diabetic Retinopathy.

title: VDAC1 O-GlcNAcylation Promotes mtDNA Release and Activates ZBP1-Dependent Neuroinflammation in Diabetic Retinopathy.

text: . title: VDAC1 O-GlcNAcylation Promotes mtDNA Release and Activates ZBP1-Dependent Neuroinflammation in Diabetic Retinopathy.

title: Type 2 diabetes and diabetic retinopathy in Finland during 2000-2017 based on nationwide survey and register data.
