text: The Changing Landscape of Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Aligning Access With the Clinical Obesity Framework.. Metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) is the most effective treatment for severe obesity, yet it remains profoundly underutilized
title: The Changing Landscape of Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Aligning Access With the Clinical Obesity Framework.
journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity

text: . Patients seeking MBS face pretreatment requirements, including mandatory psychological evaluation, documented failed diet attempts, and months of lifestyle interventions that are substantially more extensive than those required for most common gastrointestinal procedures
title: The Changing Landscape of Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Aligning Access With the Clinical Obesity Framework.
journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity

text: . These requirements were initially developed with patient safety in mind, but evidence has accumulated that many lack outcome-specific support and have become barriers to care, particularly as third-party payers have increasingly used them to restrict access
title: The Changing Landscape of Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Aligning Access With the Clinical Obesity Framework.
journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity

text: . Meanwhile, potent obesity management medications (OMMs) are prescribed with relatively limited oversight, often to individuals with preclinical disease, at costs that raise questions about economic sustainability
title: The Changing Landscape of Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Aligning Access With the Clinical Obesity Framework.
journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity

text: . The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology Commission's distinction between preclinical obesity (excess adiposity with preserved organ function) and clinical obesity (a systemic illness characterized by objective organ dysfunction or substantial limitations of daily activities) provides a framework for evaluating current treatment access patterns
title: The Changing Landscape of Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Aligning Access With the Clinical Obesity Framework.
journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity

text: . A critical implication of this framework, which warrants further exploration, is that it may narrow the population for whom medical treatment is considered necessary: for individuals with preclinical obesity, excess adiposity represents a risk state requiring monitoring and evidence-based counseling, not generally an ongoing illness requiring pharmacotherapy or surgery
title: The Changing Landscape of Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Aligning Access With the Clinical Obesity Framework.
journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity

text: . This paper examines whether the current pattern, relatively low barriers to expensive, chronic pharmacotherapy for preclinical or early-stage disease; relatively high barriers to durable, cost-effective surgery for established clinical obesity, represents a departure from severity-matched care that warrants systematic reconsideration.
title: The Changing Landscape of Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: Aligning Access With the Clinical Obesity Framework.
journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity

text: Personalized Nutrition for Hypertension: Current Evidence and Future Directions.. Hypertension is a leading risk factor for cardiovascular disease, with lifestyle interventions, particularly diet, playing a pivotal role in its management
title: Personalized Nutrition for Hypertension: Current Evidence and Future Directions.

text: . Recent advancements in personalized nutrition that tailor dietary recommendations based on an individual's unique biology (eg, genetics, microbiome) and lifestyle factors can potentially improve blood pressure control. Indeed, emerging evidence suggests that personalized nutrition can result in more effective and sustained blood pressure reductions than general dietary guidelines
title: Personalized Nutrition for Hypertension: Current Evidence and Future Directions.

text: . This review explores the current evidence supporting personalized nutrition as a novel strategy for managing hypertension, while leveraging established approaches for controlling glycemia. We evaluate studies integrating genetic markers and genomics, gut microbiome profiles, and metabolic phenotypes to design personalized dietary interventions to reduce blood pressure
title: Personalized Nutrition for Hypertension: Current Evidence and Future Directions.

text: . Specifically, we discuss how nutritional factors, including sodium and fiber intake and diets such as the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension, interact with an individual's genetic predisposition and gut microbiota composition to influence blood pressure outcomes
title: Personalized Nutrition for Hypertension: Current Evidence and Future Directions.

text: . However, challenges remain in translation to clinical practice, including the need for larger, long-term trials in real-world settings, accessibility of advanced dietary assessments, considerations of patient adherence, and equity
title: Personalized Nutrition for Hypertension: Current Evidence and Future Directions.

text: . We highlight the potential of personalized nutrition to refine hypertension treatment and call for further research to optimize its implementation at the public health and clinical practice levels. Particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where hypertension prevalence is higher, cost is an important consideration for successful implementation
title: Personalized Nutrition for Hypertension: Current Evidence and Future Directions.

text: . However, some personalized treatments focusing on diet are cost-effective and should be prioritized. Ultimately, a personalized nutrition approach may offer a powerful tool for mitigating the global burden of hypertension through targeted, individualized dietary strategies.
title: Personalized Nutrition for Hypertension: Current Evidence and Future Directions.

text: Effectiveness of a nurse-led phone intervention on body composition in adults with prediabetes and overweight/obesity: PREDIPHONE secondary analysis.. Prediabetes and obesity are strongly linked to metabolic risk, with visceral adipose tissue playing a central role
title: Effectiveness of a nurse-led phone intervention on body composition in adults with prediabetes and overweight/obesity: PREDIPHONE secondary analysis.

text: . Lifestyle interventions combining physical activity and healthy diet are effective for body composition improvement, but most are resource-intensive. Evidence on low-intensity, scalable approaches delivered by primary care professionals, such as nurse-led telephone interventions, remains limited
title: Effectiveness of a nurse-led phone intervention on body composition in adults with prediabetes and overweight/obesity: PREDIPHONE secondary analysis.

text: . This secondary analysis of the PREDIPHONE randomized controlled trial assessed the effectiveness of a low-intensity nurse-led telephone lifestyle intervention on body composition outcomes at 4 months (mid-intervention), 9 months (end of intervention), and 15 months (6 months post-intervention)
title: Effectiveness of a nurse-led phone intervention on body composition in adults with prediabetes and overweight/obesity: PREDIPHONE secondary analysis.

text: . The analysis included 174 participants with available body composition data originally enrolled in the PREDIPHONE trial. Original group allocation was retained. Body composition parameters (fat mass, muscle mass, and visceral adipose tissue) were measured using bioelectrical impedance analysis at each time point
title: Effectiveness of a nurse-led phone intervention on body composition in adults with prediabetes and overweight/obesity: PREDIPHONE secondary analysis.

text: . Physical activity and adherence to the Mediterranean diet were assessed using validated questionnaires. Group differences were evaluated using general linear models adjusted for baseline values, age, and sex. Participants had a mean age of 61.1 years, and 52.3% were women
title: Effectiveness of a nurse-led phone intervention on body composition in adults with prediabetes and overweight/obesity: PREDIPHONE secondary analysis.

text: . Compared with the active SMS-based control group, the intervention group achieved short-term reductions in visceral adipose tissue and fat mass at 4 months. These changes were not maintained at 9 or 15 months. No significant differences were observed in muscle mass or body mass index
title: Effectiveness of a nurse-led phone intervention on body composition in adults with prediabetes and overweight/obesity: PREDIPHONE secondary analysis.

text: . In this population, a low-intensity, nurse-led telephone intervention produced modest short-term improvements in body composition without sustained effects. More intensive or prolonged strategies may be required to produce clinically meaningful and sustainable changes in primary care settings. Clinicaltrials.gov, identifier NCT04735640.
title: Effectiveness of a nurse-led phone intervention on body composition in adults with prediabetes and overweight/obesity: PREDIPHONE secondary analysis.

text: Exploring Diabetes Management Behaviors with FreeStyle Libre 2: Insights from Adults with Type 2 Diabetes in Quebec.. To understand the long-term behavior changes associated with use of the FreeStyle Libre 2 sensor-based glucose monitor by people living with type 2 diabetes (T2D). This was a qualitative study of adults with T2D living in Quebec and using FreeStyle Libre 2
title: Exploring Diabetes Management Behaviors with FreeStyle Libre 2: Insights from Adults with Type 2 Diabetes in Quebec.

text: . Discussions were moderated by an experienced facilitator using a semi-directed discussion guide. Discussions were transcribed and analyzed thematically. 16 people living with T2D who had been using FreeStyle Libre 2 for > 6 months participated in two focus groups (non-insulin treatments, six women and three men; basal insulin, two women and five men)
title: Exploring Diabetes Management Behaviors with FreeStyle Libre 2: Insights from Adults with Type 2 Diabetes in Quebec.

text: . There were no material differences in responses or anecdotes between the two groups
title: Exploring Diabetes Management Behaviors with FreeStyle Libre 2: Insights from Adults with Type 2 Diabetes in Quebec.

text: . Use of FreeStyle Libre 2 was associated with four main themes: 1) Personalized knowledge, including participants' sense of autonomy and control and their ability to see the effect of their actions on glucose levels and to make informed choices, such as modifying their diet; 2) Improved communication with healthcare providers (HCPs), who can access patients' glucose data in real-time if shared
title: Exploring Diabetes Management Behaviors with FreeStyle Libre 2: Insights from Adults with Type 2 Diabetes in Quebec.

text: patients' glucose data in real-time if shared via the smartphone app; 3) Reductions in hypoglycemia, particularly due to warnings of low glucose levels; and 4) Long-term benefits, including reductions in stress and improved HRQoL
title: Exploring Diabetes Management Behaviors with FreeStyle Libre 2: Insights from Adults with Type 2 Diabetes in Quebec.

text: . Long-term users found that FreeStyle Libre 2 improved their diabetes self-management, communication with healthcare providers, HRQoL, and stress levels, and facilitated lifestyle changes. Individuals with T2D described the device empowering ongoing healthy behavior change. This research serves as a person-centered qualitative finding to consider in access decisions.
title: Exploring Diabetes Management Behaviors with FreeStyle Libre 2: Insights from Adults with Type 2 Diabetes in Quebec.

text: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Heart Failure, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.. Heart failure (HF) is a common condition with substantial geographical variation in its prevalence and underlying etiologies. Consistent and comparable data on the burden of HF within populations are needed to inform health system priorities
title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Heart Failure, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . To estimate the global burden of HF. This cross-sectional study estimates disease burden using Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) methodologies to integrate multiple information sources. Data come from 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023 representing the global population with prevalent HF. HF and underlying etiologies
title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Heart Failure, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . HF and underlying etiologies. Estimates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) for the prevalence and years lived with disability (YLDs) for HF by age, sex, location, year, and underlying etiology. text: Europe), and Chagas disease (southern, Andean, tropical, and central Latin America)
title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Heart Failure, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Heart failure is a significant global public health burden, and the impact is likely to increase as populations age. text: Assessing a multicomponent quality improvement strategy for chronic care of cardiovascular diseases in India: The C-QIP randomized feasibility trial.. Chronic cardiovascular diseases (CVD) care quality remains suboptimal, globally
title: Assessing a multicomponent quality improvement strategy for chronic care of cardiovascular diseases in India: The C-QIP randomized feasibility trial.

text: . We assessed the feasibility, acceptability, fidelity, and preliminary effect of a multicomponent, collaborative quality improvement (C-QIP) strategy among patients with CVD attending outpatient clinics in India
title: Assessing a multicomponent quality improvement strategy for chronic care of cardiovascular diseases in India: The C-QIP randomized feasibility trial.

text: . In this pragmatic feasibility randomized controlled trial, 410 adults with ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, or heart failure attending four public and private hospitals were randomized to C-QIP (electronic decision support for providers, non-physician care coordination, patient education, text-message reminders, and audit-feedback) or usual care
title: Assessing a multicomponent quality improvement strategy for chronic care of cardiovascular diseases in India: The C-QIP randomized feasibility trial.

text: . Primary outcomes were feasibility, fidelity, adoption, and acceptability; secondary outcomes included guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), self-reported adherence, care processes, and risk factors. At end of study (median follow-up 15 months), retention was 192/206 (93.2%) in C-QIP and 187/204 (91.7%) in usual care
title: Assessing a multicomponent quality improvement strategy for chronic care of cardiovascular diseases in India: The C-QIP randomized feasibility trial.

text: . Fidelity was high: 187/198 (94.4%) C-QIP participants received lifestyle counseling at end of study. C-QIP increased GDMT use for ischemic heart disease (58.3% versus 32.4%; relative risk [RR] 1.45, 95% CI [1.18, 1.78]) and ischemic stroke (76.7% versus 31.8%; RR 2.41, 95% CI [1.52, 3.81]), but not heart failure
title: Assessing a multicomponent quality improvement strategy for chronic care of cardiovascular diseases in India: The C-QIP randomized feasibility trial.

text: . Self-reported adherence was higher for medications (90.9% versus 82.3%; RR 1.08, 95% CI [1.04, 1.12]), diet (91.9% versus 82.3%; RR 1.07, 95% CI [1.02, 1.13]), and physical activity (91.4% versus 70.4%; RR 1.23, 95% CI [1.16, 1.30]). Limitations include feasibility design, individual randomization within shared clinics, and limited power for clinical outcomes and subgroup analysis
title: Assessing a multicomponent quality improvement strategy for chronic care of cardiovascular diseases in India: The C-QIP randomized feasibility trial.

text: . The C-QIP trial demonstrated that a multicomponent strategy is feasible, acceptable, and improved chronic CVD care processes in India. Future large, confirmatory hybrid trials are needed to establish whether such quality improvement strategies can reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. NCT05196659; CTRI/2022/04/041847.
title: Assessing a multicomponent quality improvement strategy for chronic care of cardiovascular diseases in India: The C-QIP randomized feasibility trial.

text: SMARTCLOTH-Odyssey for Nutrition Education in Type 1 Diabetes: Development and Acceptability Study of a Gamified Web-Based Platform for Diabetes Nurse Educators Using a Human-Centered Design Approach.. text: . Diabetes nurse educators identify a lack of adolescent-friendly educational resources, especially in nutrition education. Digital technology offers an opportunity to develop innovative tools to address these needs from a user-centered approach
title: SMARTCLOTH-Odyssey for Nutrition Education in Type 1 Diabetes: Development and Acceptability Study of a Gamified Web-Based Platform for Diabetes Nurse Educators Using a Human-Centered Design Approach.

title: SMARTCLOTH-Odyssey for Nutrition Education in Type 1 Diabetes: Development and Acceptability Study of a Gamified Web-Based Platform for Diabetes Nurse Educators Using a Human-Centered Design Approach.

text: through an ad hoc questionnaire applied to 40 professionals who tested the platform
title: SMARTCLOTH-Odyssey for Nutrition Education in Type 1 Diabetes: Development and Acceptability Study of a Gamified Web-Based Platform for Diabetes Nurse Educators Using a Human-Centered Design Approach.

text: Lifestyle and Psychosocial Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Across Adulthood: The Role of Burnout in a Large Occupational Cohort.. Lifestyle behaviors and psychosocial factors are key determinants of cardiometabolic health across the life course
title: Lifestyle and Psychosocial Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Across Adulthood: The Role of Burnout in a Large Occupational Cohort.

text: . Beyond traditional risk factors, emerging evidence suggests that chronic stress and burnout may influence metabolic risk through behavioral pathways such as physical inactivity and poor diet. However, their joint contribution to type 2 diabetes risk in working populations remains insufficiently understood
title: Lifestyle and Psychosocial Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Across Adulthood: The Role of Burnout in a Large Occupational Cohort.

text: . Our objectives were to examine the joint contribution of lifestyle habits, sociodemographic factors, and burnout to type 2 diabetes risk, and to explore potential behavioral pathways linking psychosocial stress to metabolic risk in a large adult population. A cross-sectional study was conducted in 92,480 Spanish workers undergoing routine occupational health assessments between 2021 and 2023
title: Lifestyle and Psychosocial Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Across Adulthood: The Role of Burnout in a Large Occupational Cohort.

text: . Type 2 diabetes risk was assessed using validated tools (FINDRISC, QDScore, CANRISK). Lifestyle indicators included adherence to the Mediterranean diet and physical activity levels; burnout was assessed using the Burnout Assessment Tool (BAT). Multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations between determinants and diabetes risk
title: Lifestyle and Psychosocial Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Across Adulthood: The Role of Burnout in a Large Occupational Cohort.

text: . Mediation analyses were performed to assess the contribution of lifestyle behaviors to the association between burnout and diabetes risk, and predictive performance analyses evaluated the incremental value of burnout. Burnout was independently associated with a higher probability of moderate-to-high diabetes risk across all screening tools
title: Lifestyle and Psychosocial Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Across Adulthood: The Role of Burnout in a Large Occupational Cohort.

text: . Exploratory cross-sectional mediation analyses indicated that lifestyle behaviors, particularly physical inactivity and low adherence to the Mediterranean diet, statistically accounted for approximately 45% of the observed association. Adding burnout to the models significantly improved discrimination and reclassification of moderate-to-high diabetes-risk classification
title: Lifestyle and Psychosocial Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Across Adulthood: The Role of Burnout in a Large Occupational Cohort.

text: . In addition, higher diabetes risk was consistently observed among individuals from lower socioeconomic groups and those with unhealthy lifestyle profiles. Lifestyle behaviors and psychosocial stress were associated with estimated diabetes risk across adulthood
title: Lifestyle and Psychosocial Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Across Adulthood: The Role of Burnout in a Large Occupational Cohort.

text: . Burnout was independently associated with a higher probability of moderate-to-high diabetes-risk classification, with exploratory analyses suggesting that lifestyle behaviors may statistically account for part of this association
title: Lifestyle and Psychosocial Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Across Adulthood: The Role of Burnout in a Large Occupational Cohort.

text: . These cross-sectional findings highlight the potential relevance of considering both behavioral and psychosocial factors when studying cardiometabolic risk in working populations, while prospective studies are needed to establish temporal and causal relationships.
title: Lifestyle and Psychosocial Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Risk Across Adulthood: The Role of Burnout in a Large Occupational Cohort.

text: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-a review of the cardiometabolic perspectives and treatments in children.
title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-a review of the cardiometabolic perspectives and treatments in children.

text: . The rising prevalence of childhood obesity is closely linked to the early onset of comorbid conditions, notably metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), a hepatic manifestation of metabolic syndrome characterized by hepatic steatosis in the absence of significant alcohol intake
title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-a review of the cardiometabolic perspectives and treatments in children.

text: . The pathophysiology of MASLD includes complex interactions among various factors such as hormonal, genetic, lifestyle and nutritional, and environmental dynamics. Emerging evidence indicates that MASLD is independently associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), irrespective of traditional CV-risk factors such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes mellitus
title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-a review of the cardiometabolic perspectives and treatments in children.

text: . A comprehensive, multipronged approach is central to the detection, monitoring, and management of MASLD and associated adverse cardiovascular outcomes in children. Currently, there are no approved medications or other specific therapies for pediatric MASLD
title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-a review of the cardiometabolic perspectives and treatments in children.

text: . While early stages of the disease are potentially reversible through lifestyle modifications, including diet/nutrition and physical activity, these strategies are often difficult to implement and sustain over time. Early detection of progression of MASLD to more severe conditions is hampered by the lack of reliable noninvasive methods of risk assessment tools
title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-a review of the cardiometabolic perspectives and treatments in children.

text: . The objective of this review is to (1) succinctly summarize the relationship between MASLD and CVD risk in children and (2) discuss advances in MASLD management and treatment in children. We believe that this article will stimulate new avenues for research into MASLD and its broader cardiometabolic implications in pediatric populations.
title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-a review of the cardiometabolic perspectives and treatments in children.

The main limitation of this review is the high between-study heterogeneity in pooled estimates across many of the outcomes
title: The effect of lifestyle interventions in women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Our review found that lifestyle interventions were associated with improved menstrual regularity and metabolic outcomes in women with PMOS, suggesting complementary benefits as no single intervention showed overall superiority. These findings support international recommendations, which endorse lifestyle interventions as first-line treatment, tailored to individual needs.

text: Ranking Antidiabetic Drugs Using a Multi-criteria Decision-making Approach Based on Domination Distance-based Topological Indices and QSPR Modeling.. Diabetes is a rapidly increasing metabolic disorder influenced by lifestyle and diet. Therefore, identifying effective therapeutic agents is of great importance
title: Ranking Antidiabetic Drugs Using a Multi-criteria Decision-making Approach Based on Domination Distance-based Topological Indices and QSPR Modeling.

text: . Chemical graph theory, through topological indices, helps relate molecular structures to physicochemical and thermodynamic properties. However, the application of domination distance-based topological indices (DDTIs) for quantitative structure-property relationship (QSPR) modeling and the ranking of antidiabetic drugs remains largely unexplored
title: Ranking Antidiabetic Drugs Using a Multi-criteria Decision-making Approach Based on Domination Distance-based Topological Indices and QSPR Modeling.

text: . This study investigates the relationships between DDTIs and the physicochemical properties of antidiabetic drugs using a QSPR model and ranks the drugs based on these indices integrated with multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods. A QSPR approach is employed using DDTIs. Cubic regression is applied to model the relationships between these indices and key physicochemical properties
title: Ranking Antidiabetic Drugs Using a Multi-criteria Decision-making Approach Based on Domination Distance-based Topological Indices and QSPR Modeling.

text: . To identify the most promising drug candidates, MCDM methods, namely, the technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS), weighted sum method (WSM), and weighted product method (WPM), are applied based on the calculated DDTIs
title: Ranking Antidiabetic Drugs Using a Multi-criteria Decision-making Approach Based on Domination Distance-based Topological Indices and QSPR Modeling.

text: . Strong correlations are observed between the DDTIs and the selected physicochemical properties, enabling the development of effective predictive models. Eighteen antidiabetic drugs are ranked using TOPSIS, WSM, and WPM, integrated with DDTIs, with high consistency among the rankings, demonstrating the robustness of the approach
title: Ranking Antidiabetic Drugs Using a Multi-criteria Decision-making Approach Based on Domination Distance-based Topological Indices and QSPR Modeling.

text: . The utility of domination distance-based indices in predicting drug properties and the effectiveness of MCDM methods in drug prioritization is highlighted. While the results align with previous QSPR studies, further validation with larger datasets is recommended. The findings demonstrate the predictive potential of DDTIs and the effectiveness of MCDM methods for drug prioritization
title: Ranking Antidiabetic Drugs Using a Multi-criteria Decision-making Approach Based on Domination Distance-based Topological Indices and QSPR Modeling.

text: . This framework enables the prediction and ranking of antidiabetic drugs, aiding the discovery of effective therapeutic candidates.
title: Ranking Antidiabetic Drugs Using a Multi-criteria Decision-making Approach Based on Domination Distance-based Topological Indices and QSPR Modeling.

text: Effectiveness of Structured Education Programmes on Diet and Exercise for Preventing Type 2 Diabetes in Adults With Prediabetes: A Systematic Review.. title: Effectiveness of Structured Education Programmes on Diet and Exercise for Preventing Type 2 Diabetes in Adults With Prediabetes: A Systematic Review.

text: . This systematic review assessed whether structured education programmes on diet and exercise are more effective than usual care, standard advice or less intensive lifestyle intervention in preventing or delaying type 2 diabetes among adults with prediabetes
title: Effectiveness of Structured Education Programmes on Diet and Exercise for Preventing Type 2 Diabetes in Adults With Prediabetes: A Systematic Review.

text: . The review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidance and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023484038). title: Effectiveness of Structured Education Programmes on Diet and Exercise for Preventing Type 2 Diabetes in Adults With Prediabetes: A Systematic Review.

text: . Randomised and cluster-randomised controlled trials involving adults with prediabetes, impaired glucose tolerance, or impaired fasting glucose were included if they compared structured education focused on diet, exercise or both with usual care, standard advice or a less intensive intervention. title: Effectiveness of Structured Education Programmes on Diet and Exercise for Preventing Type 2 Diabetes in Adults With Prediabetes: A Systematic Review.

text: . Data were synthesised narratively. Eighteen randomised or cluster-randomised controlled trials met the inclusion criteria. title: Effectiveness of Structured Education Programmes on Diet and Exercise for Preventing Type 2 Diabetes in Adults With Prediabetes: A Systematic Review.

text: . Structured education on diet and exercise appears more effective than usual care or less intensive lifestyle advice in preventing or delaying type 2 diabetes among adults with prediabetes.

title: Advancing Health Equity in Diabetes Prevention for Individuals With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities.

title: Advancing Health Equity in Diabetes Prevention for Individuals With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities.

title: Advancing Health Equity in Diabetes Prevention for Individuals With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities.

text: Nutrition transitions, obesity and T2DM in the Middle East and North Africa.. Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are global epidemics, but their burden is particularly pronounced in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region

text: . Metformin reduced placental weight in female fetuses and increased the fetal-to-placental weight ratio compared with the CO group. Metformin had no effect on neonatal survival but accelerated postnatal weight gain in both sexes and improved sensory-motor reflex maturation compared to OB neonates, most consistently for the geotactic reflex in both sexes and the cliff avoidance reflex in females
title: Maternal metformin treatment in obese pregnant dams normalizes neonatal sensory-motor reflexes.

text: . Metformin did not restore maternal metabolic parameters at mid-gestation, despite the numerically intermediate phenotype across several markers, but it significantly attenuated gestational weight gain
title: Maternal metformin treatment in obese pregnant dams normalizes neonatal sensory-motor reflexes.

text: . Although neonatal survival was not improved, gestational metformin was associated with accelerated postnatal weight gain and improved sensory-motor reflex maturation in offspring, though effects varied across reflex types. Accelerated postnatal weight gain warrants cautious interpretation and long-term follow-up, as it is a risk factor for childhood obesity and metabolic disorders in later life.
title: Maternal metformin treatment in obese pregnant dams normalizes neonatal sensory-motor reflexes.

text: Consumer insights into low-energy formula diet interventions for type 2 diabetes management - A scoping review.. Growing evidence indicates that early-stage type 2 diabetes is reversible. Remission may be achieved through substantial weight loss using low-energy and very-low-energy total diet replacement (LED and VLED TDR) interventions
title: Consumer insights into low-energy formula diet interventions for type 2 diabetes management - A scoping review.

text: . Despite proven effectiveness, there is limited understanding of consumers' experiences and acceptability of such interventions. This scoping review aimed to provide an overview of the insights and experiences of consumers undertaking LED and VLED TDR interventions for type 2 diabetes management
title: Consumer insights into low-energy formula diet interventions for type 2 diabetes management - A scoping review.

text: . A comprehensive literature search was conducted across five databases in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines (from inception to February 2026). Fifteen studies were included. Overall, LED and VLED interventions were acceptable and formula diet products well tolerated
title: Consumer insights into low-energy formula diet interventions for type 2 diabetes management - A scoping review.

text: . Key motivators for adherence during the intensive TDR phase included the potential for type 2 diabetes remission and weight loss. Broader benefits such as improvements in physical and psychological wellbeing were increasingly recognised as the interventions progressed
title: Consumer insights into low-energy formula diet interventions for type 2 diabetes management - A scoping review.

text: . Identified challenges included inconsistent education delivery, insufficient psychological support, and limited consideration of cultural needs. Understanding of dietary quality and behaviour change beyond program completion remains limited, and small, homogenous samples may restrict the generalisability of findings
title: Consumer insights into low-energy formula diet interventions for type 2 diabetes management - A scoping review.

text: . This highlights opportunities for tailored support in future programs to promote healthy lifestyle behaviours and optimise long-term remission outcomes.
title: Consumer insights into low-energy formula diet interventions for type 2 diabetes management - A scoping review.

text: Lifestyle mediates the association between normal-weight visceral obesity and MASLD in older adults with hypertension and diabetes.. Older adults with coexisting hypertension and type 2 diabetes are at high risk for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)
title: Lifestyle mediates the association between normal-weight visceral obesity and MASLD in older adults with hypertension and diabetes.

text: . Normal-weight visceral obesity (NWVO)-excess visceral fat despite normal body mass index and waist circumference-is an overlooked risk factor. Lifestyle is modifiable, but its role in explaining the NWVO-MASLD association is unknown. We quantified the proportion of this association statistically mediated by unhealthy lifestyle patterns
title: Lifestyle mediates the association between normal-weight visceral obesity and MASLD in older adults with hypertension and diabetes.

text: . This retrospective cohort study included 26,289 adults aged ≥50 years with hypertension and type 2 diabetes from the Shenzhen National Basic Public Health Services Program (2010-2023). NWVO was defined using the Chinese Visceral Adiposity Index alongside normal body size criteria. MASLD was diagnosed by ultrasound and cardiometabolic criteria
title: Lifestyle mediates the association between normal-weight visceral obesity and MASLD in older adults with hypertension and diabetes.

text: . A composite lifestyle score (physical activity, alcohol, smoking, dietary salt intake) was derived. We applied the generalized front-door formula for causal mediation analysis to estimate the path-specific effect of NWVO on MASLD incidence explained by lifestyle, robust to unmeasured confounding
title: Lifestyle mediates the association between normal-weight visceral obesity and MASLD in older adults with hypertension and diabetes.

text: . Over a mean 5.5-year follow-up, NWVO was associated with a significantly increased MASLD risk (adjusted  In this multimorbid older population, NWVO is a significant MASLD risk factor, and modifiable lifestyle patterns account for approximately one-fifth of this association
title: Lifestyle mediates the association between normal-weight visceral obesity and MASLD in older adults with hypertension and diabetes.

text: . Our findings support integrating visceral adiposity assessment into routine care and implementing multifaceted lifestyle interventions-targeting diet, physical activity, and substance use-to reduce the burden of MASLD in aging populations with metabolic comorbidities.
title: Lifestyle mediates the association between normal-weight visceral obesity and MASLD in older adults with hypertension and diabetes.

text: Epigenetic and genetic factors modifying the association between diet quality and incident type 2 diabetes: the EPIC-Potsdam cohort.. Benefits of healthy diets for type 2 diabetes (T2D) prevention are established. It remains unclear whether such recommendations should be tailored to specific subgroups according to their susceptibility to the disease
title: Epigenetic and genetic factors modifying the association between diet quality and incident type 2 diabetes: the EPIC-Potsdam cohort.

text: . This study aimed to assess whether the association of diet quality with T2D risk differs across subgroups with different genetic or epigenetic susceptibility
title: Epigenetic and genetic factors modifying the association between diet quality and incident type 2 diabetes: the EPIC-Potsdam cohort.

text: . We used data from a case-cohort within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC)-Potsdam cohort (random subsample with genetic data of 2204 participants, 750 verified incident T2D cases; random subsample with epigenetic data of 1065 participants, 676 verified incident T2D cases)
title: Epigenetic and genetic factors modifying the association between diet quality and incident type 2 diabetes: the EPIC-Potsdam cohort.

text: . The Alternative Healthy Eating Index (AHEI-2010), Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) and the Mediterranean Diet Pyramid score (MedPyr) were used to assess diet quality. A blood DNA methylation risk score (MRS) was used to reflect epigenetic risk
title: Epigenetic and genetic factors modifying the association between diet quality and incident type 2 diabetes: the EPIC-Potsdam cohort.

text: . Genetic risk was characterized using global polygenic risk scores (PRS) and pathway-specific polygenic risk scores (pPRS). Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the modification of the diet quality-diabetes risk association by the risk scores
title: Epigenetic and genetic factors modifying the association between diet quality and incident type 2 diabetes: the EPIC-Potsdam cohort.

text: . Higher adherence to the AHEI-2010 was associated with a lower risk of T2D, while higher MRS, PRS and pPRS predictably indicated higher risk in this population. We detected significant modification of the diet quality-T2D association by the MRS for AHEI-2010 (p = 0.008) and MedPyr (p < 0.0001) and DII (p = 0.010) but only the AHEI-2010 × MRS interaction was robust across all sensitivity analyses
title: Epigenetic and genetic factors modifying the association between diet quality and incident type 2 diabetes: the EPIC-Potsdam cohort.

text: . However, we did not find evidence of interaction between diet quality and genetic risk. The associations of healthy diets with T2D could depend on the diabetes risk captured by blood DNA methylation profiles, but they do not seem to depend on the genetic predisposition for T2D
title: Epigenetic and genetic factors modifying the association between diet quality and incident type 2 diabetes: the EPIC-Potsdam cohort.

text: . Confirmation of the effect modification by the MRS in independent populations is further required before considering clinical application.
title: Epigenetic and genetic factors modifying the association between diet quality and incident type 2 diabetes: the EPIC-Potsdam cohort.

text: Modern pharmacological therapies in nephrology: Progress, promises, and the forgotten role of diet.. The rapid expansion of pharmacological therapies for obesity, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease (CKD) has transformed clinical practice and broadened the therapeutic landscape for the management of metabolic diseases
title: Modern pharmacological therapies in nephrology: Progress, promises, and the forgotten role of diet.

text: . These agents provide well-established cardiometabolic and renal benefits; however, their use should be understood within the context of an integrated approach, alongside interventions targeting lifestyle-related determinants of disease. Lifestyle-related factors, including dietary patterns and physical activity, remain central to the pathophysiology of metabolic diseases and CKD
title: Modern pharmacological therapies in nephrology: Progress, promises, and the forgotten role of diet.

text: . At the same time, pharmacological modulation of metabolic pathways offers targeted therapeutic benefits, particularly in individuals at higher risk. Nutritional and pharmacological strategies act through complementary mechanisms and may provide synergistic effects when implemented concurrently and individualized according to clinical risk
title: Modern pharmacological therapies in nephrology: Progress, promises, and the forgotten role of diet.

text: . Dietary interventions, particularly those rich in minimally processed foods and bioactive compounds, exert pleiotropic effects on processes such as inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, premature aging, and gut dysbiosis, which are shared hallmarks of CKD
title: Modern pharmacological therapies in nephrology: Progress, promises, and the forgotten role of diet.

text: . The growing use of pharmacological therapies in metabolic diseases and CKD highlights the importance of understanding how to integrate them with lifestyle-based strategies. Individualized therapeutic approaches that incorporate nutritional and pharmacological interventions, when indicated, may help optimize cardiometabolic and renal outcomes
title: Modern pharmacological therapies in nephrology: Progress, promises, and the forgotten role of diet.

text: . Considering the chronic nature of these conditions, sustained strategies centered on diet and physical activity remain essential components for maintaining long-term metabolic and renal health.
title: Modern pharmacological therapies in nephrology: Progress, promises, and the forgotten role of diet.

text: Childhood misfortunes and metabolic syndrome in old age: European prospective cohort study.. The link between childhood misfortunes and the risk and trajectories of metabolic syndrome (MetS) in older age remains unclear
title: Childhood misfortunes and metabolic syndrome in old age: European prospective cohort study.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD

text: . The study examined (1) whether childhood misfortunes are associated with self-reported MetS and its trajectories in older age, and (2) whether life course socioeconomic conditions and unhealthy behaviours attenuate these associations
title: Childhood misfortunes and metabolic syndrome in old age: European prospective cohort study.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD

text: . Data from 39'251 respondents aged 50+ years, collected between 2004 and 2018 (Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe - SHARE) were analysed using logistic and multinomial regressions. MetS was defined as obesity plus hypertension, high cholesterol or diabetes. Childhood socioeconomic conditions, adverse experiences, and poor health were treated as distinct exposures
title: Childhood misfortunes and metabolic syndrome in old age: European prospective cohort study.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD

text: . Life course socioeconomic conditions included education, occupation and financial strain. Unhealthy behaviours included smoking, alcohol consumption, physical inactivity, and poor diet. Disadvantaged childhood socioeconomic conditions were associated with higher MetS risk, partially attenuated by life course socioeconomic conditions but not by unhealthy behaviours
title: Childhood misfortunes and metabolic syndrome in old age: European prospective cohort study.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD

text: . Four MetS trajectories were observed: "never MetS" (81%), "persistent MetS" (8%), "developed MetS" (6%) and "lost MetS" (4%). Disadvantaged childhood socioeconomic conditions, not childhood adverse experiences, increased the risk of each trajectory, partially reduced by adjustment for life course socioeconomic conditions but unaffected by behaviours
title: Childhood misfortunes and metabolic syndrome in old age: European prospective cohort study.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD

text: . Poor childhood health increased the risk of "persistent MetS", with no attenuation by life course conditions or behaviours. Childhood misfortune predicts elevated MetS risk and trajectory patterns in later life
title: Childhood misfortunes and metabolic syndrome in old age: European prospective cohort study.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD

text: . Early-life misfortune warrants clinical consideration in metabolic risk assessment, as its effects may not be visible through current lifestyle or socioeconomic indicators, pending further research.
title: Childhood misfortunes and metabolic syndrome in old age: European prospective cohort study.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD

text: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.. The aim of the study was to analyse whether children whose obesity occurred during the pandemic differed metabolically from children who were obese earlier and to assess the effect of one-year treatment following the end of pandemic restrictions
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . A prospective study of 55 children aged 10-18 years who were referred to the outpatient's clinic during the pandemic due to obesity was conducted
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . The following clinical data were analysed: time of obesity onset, body mass index (BMI) z-score, body mass composition, blood pressure, abdominal ultrasound, biochemical parameters of lipid and carbohydrate metabolism, aminotransferases and fetuin-A concentration. Participants received recommendations to improve their diet and increase physical activity (PA)
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . After 3, 6 and 12 months, we assessed: BMI z-score, compliance with recommendations, and biochemical parameters. No significant differences between pandemic obesity and non-pandemic obesity were observed at the beginning and after one year. Children who followed the dietary recommendations had a significantly lower BMI z-score after 3 months (median 2.08 vs. 1.89, p = 0.044)
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . 1.89, p = 0.044). Children who reported increased PA (47.3%) also showed lower BMI z-scores after 6 (median 2.12 vs. 1.86, p = 0.53) and 12 months (median 2.12 vs. 1.78, p = 0.008). The beneficial effect of PA was demonstrated in lower levels of fetuin-A in children with increased PA after 6 months (median 480 vs. 395 mg/ml, p = 0.07)
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . 395 mg/ml, p = 0.07). The "obesity pandemic" does not appear to be metabolically distinct from obesity that developed earlier and lasted longer. An increase in PA and compliance with dietary recommendations remain important elements of therapy, particularly in the context of metabolic complications
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . Fetuin-A may serve as a potential parameter for assessing compliance with PA recommendations and the rate of obesity progression. Celem badania była analiza, czy dzieci, u których otyłość rozwinęła się w czasie pandemii, różniły się metabolicznie od tych, które były otyłe wcześniej, oraz ocena wpływu rocznego leczenia po zniesieniu ograniczeń pandemicznych
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . Przeprowadzono prospektywne badanie obejmujące 55 dzieci w wieku 10–18 lat, które w trakcie pandemii zostały skierowane z powodu otyłości do poradni specjalistycznej
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . Analizowano dane kliniczne, w tym czas wystąpienia otyłości, wskaźnik masy ciała (BMI) wyrażony jako odchylenie standardowe (z-score), skład masy ciała, ciśnienie tętnicze, ultrasonografię jamy brzusznej, parametry biochemiczne metabolizmu lipidów i węglowodanów, aktywność aminotransferaz oraz stężenie fetuiny A
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . Uczestnicy otrzymali zalecenia dotyczące modyfikacji diety oraz zwiększenia aktywności fizycznej. Po 3, 6 i 12 miesiącach oceniano wskaźnik BMI z-score, stopień przestrzegania zaleceń oraz parametry biochemiczne
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . The aim of the study was to analyse whether children whose obesity occurred during the pandemic differed metabolically from children who were obese earlier and to assess the effect of one-year treatment following the end of pandemic restrictions. Nie stwierdzono istotnych różnic między otyłością pandemiczną a niepandemiczną
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . Dzieci przestrzegające zaleceń dietetycznych miały istotnie niższy wskaźnik BMI z-score po 3 miesiącach (mediana 2,08 vs 1,89; p = 0,044). Dzieci, które zadeklarowały zwiększenie aktywności fizycznej (47,3%), wykazywały niższe wartości BMI z-score po 6 (mediana 2,12 vs 1,86; p = 0,53) i 12 miesiącach (mediana 2,12 vs 1,78; p = 0,008)
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . Korzystny wpływ aktywności fizycznej obserwowano również w postaci niższych stężeń fetuiny A po 6 miesiącach (mediana 480 vs 395 mg/ml; p = 0,07). „Otyłość pandemiczna” nie wydaje się metabolicznie odmienna od otyłości rozwijającej się wcześniej i trwającej dłużej
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: . Zwiększenie aktywności fizycznej oraz przestrzeganie zaleceń żywieniowych pozostają istotnymi elementami terapii w kontekście powikłań metabolicznych. Fetuina A może stanowić potencjalny parametr oceny przestrzegania zaleceń dotyczących aktywności fizycznej oraz tempa postępu otyłości.
title: The epidemic of childhood obesity and the COVID-19 pandemic: metabolic characteristics and effects of therapy.

text: Primary Care-Linked Lifestyle Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Remission and Glucose-Lowering Medication Deintensification: A Systematic Review.. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a common chronic disease that affects millions of adults around the world. Primary care-linked lifestyle interventions offer a scalable pathway to remission
title: Primary Care-Linked Lifestyle Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Remission and Glucose-Lowering Medication Deintensification: A Systematic Review.

text: . However, evidence has not been synthesized with glucose-lowering medication deintensification as a co-primary outcome or with systematic separation of randomized, proof-of-concept, and real-world implementation evidence. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines
title: Primary Care-Linked Lifestyle Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Remission and Glucose-Lowering Medication Deintensification: A Systematic Review.

text: . Four databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL)) were searched in June 2026. Eligible studies included adults with T2DM enrolled in primary care-linked lifestyle interventions
title: Primary Care-Linked Lifestyle Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Remission and Glucose-Lowering Medication Deintensification: A Systematic Review.

text: . Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Quasi-Experimental Studies, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework
title: Primary Care-Linked Lifestyle Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Remission and Glucose-Lowering Medication Deintensification: A Systematic Review.

text: . Pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences were estimated using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models. Six studies met eligibility criteria, including two primary 12-month randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and four additional proof-of-concept or implementation evidence streams
title: Primary Care-Linked Lifestyle Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Remission and Glucose-Lowering Medication Deintensification: A Systematic Review.

text: . The two 12-month comparative RCTs (Diabetes Remission Clinical Trial (DiRECT) and Diabetes Intervention Acceleration through Mobilization I (DIADEM-I)) demonstrated a pooled remission RR of 7.42 (95% confidence interval (CI) 3.51-15.69; I² = 53%; moderate certainty) and medication-free status RR of 4.31 (95% CI 3.24-5.72; I² = 0%; moderate certainty)
title: Primary Care-Linked Lifestyle Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Remission and Glucose-Lowering Medication Deintensification: A Systematic Review.

text: . The pooled unadjusted mean difference in weight change was -8.75 kg (95% CI -10.01 to -7.48; I² = 0%), and the pooled mean difference in glycated hemoglobin change was -8.74 mmol/mol (95% CI -13.58 to -3.90; I² = 70%; low certainty)
title: Primary Care-Linked Lifestyle Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Remission and Glucose-Lowering Medication Deintensification: A Systematic Review.

text: . Single-arm and real-world implementation evidence showed a pooled remission proportion of 42.6% (95% CI 26.4-59.6%; I² = 95%; very low certainty), interpreted as implementation rates rather than causal treatment effects
title: Primary Care-Linked Lifestyle Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Remission and Glucose-Lowering Medication Deintensification: A Systematic Review.

text: . Primary care-linked lifestyle interventions, particularly total diet replacement-based pathways, substantially increase the likelihood of T2DM remission and medication-free status at 12 months. Sustained weight loss appears to be the primary mediating mechanism. Safe implementation requires structured medication withdrawal protocols and long-term primary care follow-up.
title: Primary Care-Linked Lifestyle Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Remission and Glucose-Lowering Medication Deintensification: A Systematic Review.

text: Prediabetes: Impact on cardiovascular risk and emerging therapeutic strategies.. Prediabetes is an umbrella term which refers to a collection of blood parameters related to glucose regulation exceeding their normal threshold, but not meeting the criteria for overt diabetes. Its prevalence is rising worldwide, largely driven by overweight/obesity, diet, lack of exercise and familiarity
title: Prediabetes: Impact on cardiovascular risk and emerging therapeutic strategies.

text: . To provide a state-of-the-art overview of epidemiology, pathophysiology, cardiovascular (CV) implications, and emerging therapeutic strategies in prediabetes. Narrative review with structured discussion of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and meta-analyses addressing progression to T2DM and cardiovascular outcomes
title: Prediabetes: Impact on cardiovascular risk and emerging therapeutic strategies.

text: . The risk of prediabetes progressing to T2DM is well established, with modest differences across phenotypes (impaired fasting glucose, impaired glucose tolerance, elevated HbA1c). In contrast, whether prediabetes independently increases CV risk remains debated
title: Prediabetes: Impact on cardiovascular risk and emerging therapeutic strategies.

text: . Observational studies and meta-analyses suggest a mild but statistically significant increase in CV events and mortality; however, randomized evidence demonstrating CV benefit from treating prediabetes is limited and methodologically heterogeneous. Current management of prediabetes primarily relies on lifestyle interventions, while metformin is recommended only in selected high-risk individuals
title: Prediabetes: Impact on cardiovascular risk and emerging therapeutic strategies.

text: . Glucagon-like peptide receptor-1 agonists and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors have shown disease-modifying effects in T2DM and related cardiometabolic conditions. Emerging data suggest potential benefits in individuals with prediabetes, although dedicated adequately powered CV outcome trials are lacking. Prediabetes is a clinically relevant cardiometabolic state
title: Prediabetes: Impact on cardiovascular risk and emerging therapeutic strategies.

text: . While progression to T2DM is well documented, its role as an independent CV therapeutic target remains uncertain. Future trials should address phenotype-specific risk stratification and evaluate contemporary cardiometabolic therapies in appropriately powered populations.
title: Prediabetes: Impact on cardiovascular risk and emerging therapeutic strategies.

text: LDL hypercholesterolemia in children: genetic influence and response to lifestyle advice - follow-up of the Fr1dolin-trial.. Although familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is common and associated with significant cardiovascular morbidity, screening programs are scarce
title: LDL hypercholesterolemia in children: genetic influence and response to lifestyle advice - follow-up of the Fr1dolin-trial.

text: . Furthermore, the effectiveness of nutritional advice for parents on children's LDL cholesterol (LDL-C) levels is unclear, especially in FH versus non-FH hypercholesterolemia. In the Fr1dolin study, 367 of 14,513 children in Lower Saxony and Hamburg were positively screened for LDL hypercholesterolemia with an LDL-C > 135 mg/dl (> 3.5 mmol/l)
title: LDL hypercholesterolemia in children: genetic influence and response to lifestyle advice - follow-up of the Fr1dolin-trial.

text: . The screening was considered positive if the first finding of hypercholesterolemia was confirmed in a second sample. These 367 children were invited to a follow-up examination including an extended lipid status, nutritional counseling and genetic analysis. 289 out of 367 screen-positive children (57.4% girls) were followed up for 12 months; 191 (66.1%) underwent genetic testing
title: LDL hypercholesterolemia in children: genetic influence and response to lifestyle advice - follow-up of the Fr1dolin-trial.

text: . Children with a FH-causing pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant (n = 40, 20.9%) had significantly higher LDL-C levels than children without a variant or with a variant of uncertain significance (p < 0.001)
title: LDL hypercholesterolemia in children: genetic influence and response to lifestyle advice - follow-up of the Fr1dolin-trial.

text: . After the nutritional counselling and after 6 and 12 months of follow-up, LDL-C levels did not improve significantly (median LDL-C at baseline 142 mg/dl, and 140 mg/dl at 6 and 12 months follow-up, respectively)
title: LDL hypercholesterolemia in children: genetic influence and response to lifestyle advice - follow-up of the Fr1dolin-trial.

text: . A population-based screening program detects LDL-hypercholesterolemia in up to 2.5% of children, with a significant proportion of them having FH genetic variants, supporting early detection
title: LDL hypercholesterolemia in children: genetic influence and response to lifestyle advice - follow-up of the Fr1dolin-trial.

text: . One-time nutritional advice had little effect on LDL-C in general, but particularly in FH, highlighting on the one hand need for structured lifestyle programs and on the other hand early genetic testing in population based FH screening.
title: LDL hypercholesterolemia in children: genetic influence and response to lifestyle advice - follow-up of the Fr1dolin-trial.

text: Ayurveda in Contemporary Clinical Practice: Integrating Traditional Principles With Preventive, Metabolic, and Mind-Body Medicine.. The increasing burden of chronic, metabolic, and stress-related disorders has created a need for clinical models that emphasize prevention, lifestyle modification, individualized care, and long-term risk reduction
title: Ayurveda in Contemporary Clinical Practice: Integrating Traditional Principles With Preventive, Metabolic, and Mind-Body Medicine.

text: . Ayurveda offers a structured framework for diet, behavior, metabolic regulation, constitutional assessment, and mind-body balance; however, its integration into contemporary clinical practice remains constrained by fragmented evidence, heterogeneous interventions, and variable methodological quality
title: Ayurveda in Contemporary Clinical Practice: Integrating Traditional Principles With Preventive, Metabolic, and Mind-Body Medicine.

text: . This review examines the relevance of Ayurveda in preventive, metabolic, and mind-body medicine and evaluates how traditional principles may be aligned with evidence-based clinical care. A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar to identify primarily English-language literature published between January 2015 and June 2026
title: Ayurveda in Contemporary Clinical Practice: Integrating Traditional Principles With Preventive, Metabolic, and Mind-Body Medicine.

text: . Original clinical studies, randomized trials, observational and translational studies, systematic reviews, methodological studies, and relevant policy documents were selected according to their relevance to preventive, metabolic, mind-body, personalized, safety, and regulatory aspects of Ayurveda
title: Ayurveda in Contemporary Clinical Practice: Integrating Traditional Principles With Preventive, Metabolic, and Mind-Body Medicine.

text: . The review was intended as an illustrative narrative synthesis rather than a comprehensive systematic review. The evidence suggests that Ayurveda is most appropriately positioned as an adjunctive framework for cardiometabolic risk reduction, diabetes and metabolic syndrome management, mood and sleep regulation, chronic pain care, and personalized prevention
title: Ayurveda in Contemporary Clinical Practice: Integrating Traditional Principles With Preventive, Metabolic, and Mind-Body Medicine.

text: . Emerging fields such as Ayurgenomics, Ayurinformatics, microbiome research, and systems biology may support the translation of traditional constructs such as
title: Ayurveda in Contemporary Clinical Practice: Integrating Traditional Principles With Preventive, Metabolic, and Mind-Body Medicine.

text: Impact of the Food4Moms produce prescription program on readiness for healthy eating, fruit and vegetable intake, and food security.. Produce prescription (PRx) programs targeting different populations and conditions have been found to be effective. However, few have focused on pregnant women
title: Impact of the Food4Moms produce prescription program on readiness for healthy eating, fruit and vegetable intake, and food security.

text: . However, few have focused on pregnant women. The objectives of this study were to assess the impact of the Food4Moms (F4M) PRx program on 1) healthy eating stages of change 2) intake of fruits and vegetables (i.e., produce), and 3) household food security among pregnant Latina women
title: Impact of the Food4Moms produce prescription program on readiness for healthy eating, fruit and vegetable intake, and food security.

text: . F4M recruited low-income Latinas living in Greater Hartford, Connecticut that received a "produce prescription" from a Registered Dietitian based at the community-based organization (CBO) where the program was implemented
title: Impact of the Food4Moms produce prescription program on readiness for healthy eating, fruit and vegetable intake, and food security.

text: . Participants were offered $100 per month for 10 months through Fresh Connect debit cards that only worked to purchase fresh produce from two food retailers or the equivalent value in fresh produce delivered at home. To be fully enrolled in F4M, participants had to complete a baseline survey and the first nutrition education interactive session
title: Impact of the Food4Moms produce prescription program on readiness for healthy eating, fruit and vegetable intake, and food security.

text: . Enrolled participants were offered additional nutrition education sessions at the CBO and received text messages with nutrition tips as well as reminders to spend their remaining benefit balances towards the end of each month. A single-group pre-post study design was used to assess the impact of F4M 10 months after the card activation
title: Impact of the Food4Moms produce prescription program on readiness for healthy eating, fruit and vegetable intake, and food security.

text: . No attrition bias was detected when comparing the characteristics of those completing (N = 113) vs. those not completing the endline survey (N = 41). Pre-post Wilcoxon signed-test or paired t-test analyses showed that F4M had a positive impact on healthy eating readiness (p < 0.001), the consumption of fruits (p < 0.001) and vegetables (p < 0.001), and household food security (p = 0.034)
title: Impact of the Food4Moms produce prescription program on readiness for healthy eating, fruit and vegetable intake, and food security.

text: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.. The Asia Pacific region is home to more than half of the world's 1·93 billion adolescents (aged 10-24 years)
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Addressing adolescent health in this region is of global importance, but to date a systematic analysis of key contributors to disease in adolescents has not been done, which is a barrier to responsive action
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . This systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 aims to provide a comprehensive assessment of adolescent health across the Asia Pacific region, at both the subregional and national levels, encompassing burden of disease, mortality, and prevalence of adolescent risk factors
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . As part of GBD 2023, we obtained estimates for cause-specific mortality, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and risk factor prevalence by sex for adolescents aged 10-24 years and 5-year age groups (10-14 years, 15-19 years, and 20-24 years) across 44 countries and territories (hereafter referred to collectively as Asia Pacific), grouped by seven UN subregions, from 2000 to 2023
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . We extracted GBD 2023 population counts and estimates of number and rate (per 100 000 population) for mortality and disease burden (DALYs). Risk prevalence estimates were obtained directly from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation, and binge drinking estimates were sourced from WHO. Estimates are reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) where possible
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . UIs were estimated by running 250 draws of the posterior distribution, ordering the draws, and selecting the 2·5th and 97·5th percentiles for each metric. In 2023, in adolescents across Asia Pacific, there were 637 496 deaths and a total disease burden of 115·8 million DALYs, representing 34·1% of global adolescent deaths and 40·6% of the global adolescent burden of disease
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Non-communicable diseases (NCDs; particularly mental disorders) were the leading causes of disease burden and mortality (64·8% of DALYs and 43·9% of deaths)
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Unintentional and transport injuries were also leading causes of death (14·7% of deaths due to transport injury and 13·3% of deaths due to unintentional injury) and leading causes of disease burden particularly among males in south-eastern Asia
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . In Melanesia, Micronesia, and some parts of south-eastern Asia (Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, the Philippines, and Timor-Leste), respiratory infections and tuberculosis remained important contributors
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Southern Asia had the largest reduction (1·5% per year) in all-cause DALYs over the study period, and Australia and New Zealand (0·2% per year) had the smallest, with females in Australia and New Zealand showing a slight increase contrary to regional trends. Eastern Asia had the largest reduction (2·8% per year) in all-cause mortality rate and Melanesia (0·8% per year) the smallest
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Risk factors generally had between-subregion and within-subregion variation; however, some regional trends stood out, with overweight and obesity increasing in all countries across the region, and binge drinking increasing in more countries than not
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . In 2023, prevalence of smoking in males exceeded that in females in every country, from 40% difference in Timor-Leste to less than 1% difference in Australia. Anaemia prevalence is decreasing in all countries, but female prevalence was higher and reducing at a slower rate than in males
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Bullying prevalence was slightly higher in Polynesia, Micronesia, and Melanesia combined, Australia and New Zealand, and eastern Asia compared with southern and south-eastern Asian subregions
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Several patterns were consistent across the region: the dominance of mental disorders and NCDs, the universal rise in overweight and obesity (particularly high in Oceanic countries but increasing rapidly in south and south-eastern Asia), and persistent sex-specific challenges across subregions: unintentional injuries and smoking in males, and anaemia in females
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Actions to tackle shared risk factors (while accounting for context-specific local health profiles, workforce deficits, cultural factors, and health system capacity) should not be forgone due to local variation. Future research could focus on subnational variation, intersecting inequalities, and multi-sectoral interventions targeting shared risk factors
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Priority actions should include regional investment in adolescent mental health services and obesity prevention, targeted injury reduction strategies for high-risk populations, and sex-specific approaches to smoking cessation and anaemia reduction, delivered through local health systems with the capacity and cultural responsiveness to meet local needs. Gates Foundation and Australian Government.
title: Adolescent health across Asia Pacific, 2000-23: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
