title: Metformin added to lifestyle intervention for physical function in older adults with obesity (DEMFOS trial): a randomised controlled trial.

text: Nutritional considerations for glucagon-like peptide-based therapies: An Asian Indian consensus recommendation.
title: Nutritional considerations for glucagon-like peptide-based therapies: An Asian Indian consensus recommendation.

text: . Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP-1 receptor agonists, collectively called GLP-based therapies (GBTs), cause gastrointestinal adverse effects and alter dietary intake, leading to nutritional deficiencies and loss of muscle mass and bone density
title: Nutritional considerations for glucagon-like peptide-based therapies: An Asian Indian consensus recommendation.

text: . Therefore, GBTs' use necessitates structured nutritional support, particularly among Asian Indians, given their diverse dietary patterns and high prevalence of sarcopenia. This consensus provides expert-driven, practical recommendations on key nutritional priorities to support the appropriate GBTs' use in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus and/or obesity
title: Nutritional considerations for glucagon-like peptide-based therapies: An Asian Indian consensus recommendation.

text: . This was a consensus-based study using a modified Delphi method with expert panel inputs informed by a literature review. The literature review was conducted before developing statements on challenges experienced by individuals on GBTs and strategies to mitigate micro- and macronutrient deficiencies to guide optimal GBTs' use
title: Nutritional considerations for glucagon-like peptide-based therapies: An Asian Indian consensus recommendation.

text: . A total of 13 domain experts (endocrinologists and diabetologists) across India were included in this process
title: Nutritional considerations for glucagon-like peptide-based therapies: An Asian Indian consensus recommendation.

text: . Among 44 statements (11 sub-statements), 43 received high or moderate consensus, emphasizing the importance of early nutritional assessment and monitoring metabolic outcomes, with a tailored, balanced diet comprising complex carbohydrates, optimal high-quality protein, good-quality fat, micronutrients, and adequate hydration
title: Nutritional considerations for glucagon-like peptide-based therapies: An Asian Indian consensus recommendation.

text: . The panel highlighted calorie-controlled meal replacement, including diabetes-specific nutritional (DSN) formulations, together with sustainable lifestyle practices and resistance exercise to support long-term metabolic health outcomes. After the discontinuation of GBTs, sustained nutritional support may help prevent metabolic rebound
title: Nutritional considerations for glucagon-like peptide-based therapies: An Asian Indian consensus recommendation.

text: . There is a need for structured nutritional support for individuals on GBTs, especially for Asian Indians, considering their dietary pattern and increased risk of sarcopenia. Implementing culturally driven nutritional recommendations, including DSN formula as an adjunct along with lifestyle modifications, can support optimizing long-term patient-centric outcomes
title: Nutritional considerations for glucagon-like peptide-based therapies: An Asian Indian consensus recommendation.

text: . The effectiveness and safety of GBTs, along with newly emerging nutrient-stimulating hormone (NuSH) based therapies, should be evaluated in long-term follow-up studies.
title: Nutritional considerations for glucagon-like peptide-based therapies: An Asian Indian consensus recommendation.

text: A narrative review of dietary patterns in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.. Driven by the global rise in obesity and lifestyle transitions, cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome has emerged as a pathophysiological continuum characterized by metabolic dysregulation and involving multi-organ interactions
title: A narrative review of dietary patterns in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.

text: . Within the comprehensive management of CKM syndrome, dietary patterns represent a cornerstone of intervention due to their high modifiability and cost-effectiveness
title: A narrative review of dietary patterns in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.

text: . Adopting the perspective of the CKM syndrome pathophysiological continuum, this narrative review provides a thematic overview of the current literature on the Mediterranean, DASH, plant-based, and ketogenic diets in relation to metabolic syndrome, type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease
title: A narrative review of dietary patterns in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.

text: . Evidence indicates that the Mediterranean and DASH diets, through established anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and endothelial protective mechanisms, are the most consistently supported dietary patterns for CKM risk mitigation
title: A narrative review of dietary patterns in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.

text: . The efficacy of plant-based diets is strictly quality-dependent: while healthful patterns rich in whole grains and vegetables are associated with improved cardiorenal outcomes, unhealthful patterns dominated by refined carbohydrates may exacerbate metabolic derangements
title: A narrative review of dietary patterns in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.

text: . Although the ketogenic diet may improve glucose metabolism in the short term, concerns regarding elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, potential hepatotoxicity, and limited long-term adherence suggest that its role may be more relevant in selected short-term settings than as a sustained long-term dietary pattern
title: A narrative review of dietary patterns in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.

text: . Furthermore, structured dietary quality indices may provide useful tools for characterizing dietary exposure in relation to CKM and for generating mechanistic hypotheses. By integrating clinical and mechanistic evidence, this review outlines a stage-oriented conceptual framework to discuss how different dietary patterns may relate to distinct phases of the CKM syndrome.
title: A narrative review of dietary patterns in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.

text: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.. Dietary counseling is an essential complement to the growing use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) to achieve sustainable weight loss
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: . Diverse patient needs, the demand for ongoing support, and limited resources underscore the potential of using digital support tools. This study aimed to evaluate the usability, treatment satisfaction, and weight effects of a personalized nutrition advisor (PNA), a prototype decision-support tool designed to facilitate personalized weight management counseling
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: . We assessed usability, treatment satisfaction, and weight effects of a web-based PNA prototype dashboard designed to help dietitians deliver personalized remote dietary counseling in overweight adults (BMI ≥28 kg/m² at pharmacotherapy initiation) who had achieved ≥5% weight loss with GLP-1 RA therapy over 12-weeks
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: . The PNA dashboard generated tailored nutritional recommendations to help participants achieve personalized weight loss goals based on an energy balance model that estimated daily caloric intake and nutritional quality using frequent body weight measurements, dietary logs, and physical activity data from a lifestyle-tracking app
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: . To evaluate the PNA's usability, we used a convergent parallel mixed-methods approach, combining a validated quantitative usability survey and qualitative focus-group interviews and feedback questionnaires with both dietitians and patients, alongside patient-reported satisfaction metrics for PNA-guided consultations (treatment satisfaction, general self-efficacy, and perceived health impact)
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: . Thematic analysis with a hybrid deductive-inductive methodology was applied to qualitative data, using 4 a priori themes derived from this study's conceptual framework regarding prior expectations, perceived utility and satisfaction, usability challenges, and suggestions for clinical integration. Percent weight loss during the intervention was assessed as an exploratory outcome
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: . Among 78 participants (58/78, 74% women), on GLP-1 RA (mean weight loss of -13.3%, SD 6.7%, after 10, SD 5, months of treatment), between 3 and 5 remote nutrition consultations were delivered with PNA support. After the 3-month intervention period, weight loss was sustained in all participants (-0.2%, SD 2.5%), with 21% (16/78) suspending the GLP-1 RA due to drug shortages
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: . Dietitians rated the PNA's usability as moderate (62%) on the Healthcare Systems Usability Scale. Patients evaluated the perceived health impact of the PNA-assisted consultations at 19.1 (SD 3.5) of 25 on the user version of the Mobile Application Rating Scale
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: . No significant differences were observed in patient-reported treatment satisfaction (P=.78) or self-efficacy (P=.57) before and after PNA-assisted care. Qualitative analysis identified convergence with quantitative findings across themes of usability, treatment satisfaction, and clinical integration, with divergence observed for self-efficacy and tracking motivation
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: . Both patients and dietitians found the PNA valuable for generating actionable nutritional insights
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: . While effective implementation of tools such as the PNA prototype demands dietitian training and workflow integration, they offer scalable, personalized nutrition or lifestyle guidance-as a therapeutic decision-support tool within weight loss interventions, with or without adjunct GLP-1 RA pharmacotherapy.
title: Clinical Decision Support for Digital Dietary Counseling Under GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Convergent Mixed Methods Usability and Treatment Satisfaction Pilot Study of the Personalized Nutrition Advisor.

text: Efficacy and Safety of the Dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 Inhibitor JP-2266 in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2 Study.. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of JP-2266, a novel dual sodium-glucose co-transporter 1 (SGLT1)/SGLT2 inhibitor, in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) inadequately controlled with diet and exercise
title: Efficacy and Safety of the Dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 Inhibitor JP-2266 in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2 Study.

text: . In this 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial, 156 patients with T2DM were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to receive once-daily JP-2266 5 mg (n=51), 10 mg (n=53), or placebo (n=52). The primary endpoint was the change in glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) from baseline to week 12 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06144788)
title: Efficacy and Safety of the Dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 Inhibitor JP-2266 in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2 Study.

text: . JP-2266 treatment led to significant, placebo-adjusted reductions in HbA1c of -0.94% (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.24 to -0.65; P<0.0001) for the 5 mg dose and -0.97% (95% CI, -1.26 to -0.68; P<0.0001) for the 10 mg dose
title: Efficacy and Safety of the Dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 Inhibitor JP-2266 in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2 Study.

text: . Significant reductions were also observed in fasting plasma glucose (-36.22 mg/dL [95% CI, -47.62 to -24.83] with 5 mg and -39.38 mg/dL [95% CI, -50.71 to -28.05] with 10 mg), and postprandial glucose (-62.30 mg/dL [95% CI, -84.97 to -39.64] with 5 mg and -66.89 mg/dL [95% CI, -89.71 to -44.07] with 10 mg) (all P<0.0001)
title: Efficacy and Safety of the Dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 Inhibitor JP-2266 in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2 Study.

text: . JP-2266 also reduced body weight of -2.0 to -2.1 kg and systolic blood pressure (-3.6 mm Hg with 10 mg). Improvements in insulin resistance and β-cell function were also observed, as assessed by homeostasis model assessment. Adverse event rates were similar to placebo
title: Efficacy and Safety of the Dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 Inhibitor JP-2266 in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2 Study.

text: . Adverse event rates were similar to placebo. In patients with T2DM inadequately controlled by lifestyle alone, JP-2266 significantly improved glycemic control, reduced body weight and blood pressure, and was well tolerated over 12 weeks. These findings support further investigation of JP-2266 as a potential therapeutic option for T2DM.
title: Efficacy and Safety of the Dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 Inhibitor JP-2266 in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2 Study.

text: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.. Takeaway food outlets ('takeaways') sell hot food for consumption off the premises. Takeaway management zones are areas around schools where new takeaways are not allowed to open. They are the most common planning intervention targeting takeaways across local authorities in England to date
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . We conducted an evaluation of these zones to: model their impact on adult health model their associated economic costs and benefits explore their acceptability and perceived effectiveness among young people investigate support and perceived effectiveness among adults explore barriers to and facilitators of their adoption and implementation among local authority staff
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . We used a forecast of takeaway growth and a statistical model to estimate the impact of zones on diet-related health outcomes, quality-adjusted life-years and healthcare costs to 2040. We did this for adults aged 25-64 years in six different local authorities
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . We conducted a linked economic analysis to understand the future costs and benefits of zones to local authorities, the National Health Service and national government. We estimated costs when denial of planning permission results in a 3-, 6- or 12-month vacancy before alternative retail uptake. We asked 46 young people about how acceptable they thought the policy was
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . By conducting 'go along' interviews, we gained insights into their everyday food habits within and outside the school gates. We used survey data to understand public acceptability and perceived effectiveness of zones. We also asked whether having fewer takeaways near schools could reduce how often young people consume takeaway food
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . To evaluate adoption and implementation, we interviewed 29 local authority public health and planning officers about what lessons they had learned. Compared to no intervention, future reductions in takeaway exposure ranged from 3 outlets/person in Fenland to 28 outlets/person in Manchester
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . Obesity prevalence was reduced in both sexes in all local authorities, for example, in Manchester, by 2.3 percentage points for males. We observed reductions in disease incidence, for example, in Manchester, by 964 type II diabetes cases/100,000 males. Zones produced a positive net economic impact of, for example, £8.49-12.78M in Manchester
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . Despite objections on economic grounds, zones are associated with economic benefits for local authorities, the National Health Service and national government. Young people found zones to be acceptable and perceived them to have some positive impacts. But, a wider policy, including other types of outlets selling convenience food, may better limit dietary risk
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . Out of 3323 adults, 51% supported zone adoption. Almost three-quarters believed that zones would help young people to eat better. Among those aged 16-17 years, 33% agreed that young people would consume takeaway food less often if there were fewer takeaways near schools. Effective working relationships between local authority colleagues were important for adoption and implementation
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . Some local authorities ensured this by developing cross-departmental roles and policy 'champions'. A formal implementation process ensured confidence and consistency in implementation. Takeaway management zones around schools were forecast to reduce obesity prevalence and disease incidence by 2040, with no net economic costs. The public see zones as acceptable and potentially effective
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . However, the reality of adopting and implementing zones is challenging, while other aspects of food retail also influence the behaviours of young people. This synopsis presents independent research funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Public Health Research programme as award number NIHR130597
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . There are many ways in which our neighbourhoods can make it hard to make healthy choices. Having more takeaway outlets means people tend to eat more of the unhealthy foods they sell. Designating zones around schools where new takeaways are not allowed to open is one way that local councils can encourage healthier lifestyles in children and adults
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . By 2019, 41 of 325 local councils in England had takeaway ‘management’ zones around schools. However, these councils have been working in the absence of evidence of their impact and acceptability. These evidence gaps have made it difficult for councils to demonstrate the value of management zones, curtailing further adoption and successful implementation
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . We used a computer model to estimate the impact of takeaway management zones on health to 2040. We also wanted to understand the costs and benefits of zones to local and national economies and the National Health Service over this period
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . We ran a survey to understand how acceptable and effective people thought zones would be and spoke to young people directly about what they thought of the policy overall. Finally, we asked public health and planning colleagues in local councils about their experiences of zones and what lessons they had learned
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . Although imperfect, takeaway management zones around schools were forecast to reduce obesity and related disease. For example, in Manchester, we forecast obesity prevalence for males to reduce by 2.3 percentage points. These health benefits were achieved with no overall economic harm. In fact, in Manchester, we forecast their adoption to save the council between £8M and £12M
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: . Local communities saw zones as acceptable and potentially effective. However, the reality of adopting and managing the ongoing implementation of zones was a challenge for councils, while other aspects of high street food retail also influence young people’s diets.
title: Evaluation of planning policy to regulate takeaway food outlets for improved health in England: Synopsis.

text: From Percutaneous Coronary Intervention to Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Case Report Highlighting the Impact of Ineffective Secondary Prevention.. Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with long-term outcomes heavily dependent on secondary prevention
title: From Percutaneous Coronary Intervention to Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Case Report Highlighting the Impact of Ineffective Secondary Prevention.

text: . Poor adherence to guideline-directed therapy and unhealthy dietary practices significantly increase the risk of recurrent ischemic events, restenosis, and heart failure. Long-term success after percutaneous coronary intervention depends heavily on continuous adherence to medical therapy and lifestyle modification
title: From Percutaneous Coronary Intervention to Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Case Report Highlighting the Impact of Ineffective Secondary Prevention.

text: . This study reports the case of a 63-year-old Indian male with diabetes and hypertension who previously underwent percutaneous coronary intervention in 2014 for myocardial infarction. In 2018, the patient stopped taking both dual antiplatelet therapy and statins and changed to a completely open dietary plan with a large amount of saturated fat in his diet
title: From Percutaneous Coronary Intervention to Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Case Report Highlighting the Impact of Ineffective Secondary Prevention.

text: . By 2025, he had unstable angina, which was ultimately diagnosed as a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. During coronary angiography, he was found to have significant triple-vessel disease, including in-stent restenosis and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25% to 35%
title: From Percutaneous Coronary Intervention to Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Case Report Highlighting the Impact of Ineffective Secondary Prevention.

text: . As a result, after revascularization, he was treated with a combination of dual antiplatelet therapy, a high-intensity statin, sacubitril/valsartan, and a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 Inhibitor
title: From Percutaneous Coronary Intervention to Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Case Report Highlighting the Impact of Ineffective Secondary Prevention.

text: . While initially all medications were successfully managed, the patient was ultimately found to have irreversible myocardial dysfunction due to prolonged nonadherence with proper management and lifestyle modifications. This case highlights the potential long-term consequences of discontinuing prescribed cardiac medications and neglecting dietary advice after revascularization
title: From Percutaneous Coronary Intervention to Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Case Report Highlighting the Impact of Ineffective Secondary Prevention.

text: . Although multiple factors such as progression of diabetes, metabolic disturbances, and recurrent ischemia may contribute to ventricular dysfunction, prolonged interruption of guideline-directed therapy and periodic assessment of therapeutic targets likely played an important role in the progression of coronary disease and development of heart failure.
title: From Percutaneous Coronary Intervention to Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Case Report Highlighting the Impact of Ineffective Secondary Prevention.

text: Dietary Intervention Is Associated with Lower CGM-Derived Glucose Rate-of-Change in Healthy Young Women: A Pilot Fixed Sequential-Intervention Study.. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) interpretation in people without diabetes is expanding beyond general glycemic control toward more dynamic metrics, such as Rate of Change (RoC)
title: Dietary Intervention Is Associated with Lower CGM-Derived Glucose Rate-of-Change in Healthy Young Women: A Pilot Fixed Sequential-Intervention Study.

text: . In this fixed-sequence pilot study conducted in 30 healthy adult females, we evaluated associations between two structured 14-day lifestyle interventions and free-living conditions using standard CGM-derived glycemic variability metrics and a novel framework based on the rate-of-change (RoC) metrics and data clarity using an unblinded Abbott FreeStyle Libre 2 monitoring
title: Dietary Intervention Is Associated with Lower CGM-Derived Glucose Rate-of-Change in Healthy Young Women: A Pilot Fixed Sequential-Intervention Study.

text: . The dietary intervention (calorie-tailored low-glycemic index regular meals) were associated with lower time spent in rising (+1 to +2 mg/dL/min) and falling (-2 to -1 mg/dL/min) RoC bins by 4.76 ± 1.87% (complete-case delta,
title: Dietary Intervention Is Associated with Lower CGM-Derived Glucose Rate-of-Change in Healthy Young Women: A Pilot Fixed Sequential-Intervention Study.

text: Targeting Reduced Glutathione (GSH) to Promote Metabolic Health: Insights on the Role of Bioactive-Rich Foods and Fasting Protocols.. The ever-increasing disparity between lifespan and healthspan represents a challenging global issue, with metabolic dysregulation playing a central role in the initiation and progression of chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs)
title: Targeting Reduced Glutathione (GSH) to Promote Metabolic Health: Insights on the Role of Bioactive-Rich Foods and Fasting Protocols.

text: . This review highlights the importance of maintaining optimal redox homeostasis, with particular emphasis on reduced glutathione (GSH), for preserving metabolic health during aging. GSH participates in several physiological processes, including antioxidant defense, xenobiotic detoxification, redox signaling, and metabolic regulation
title: Targeting Reduced Glutathione (GSH) to Promote Metabolic Health: Insights on the Role of Bioactive-Rich Foods and Fasting Protocols.

text: . Diminished GSH levels are consistently reported in obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes mellitus, non-alcoholic fatty liver, and cardiovascular diseases. Current evidence from human clinical studies indicates that foods rich in bioactive constituents can enhance GSH levels and stimulate GSH-dependent enzyme activity, with the Nrf2/Are signaling pathway being a central mechanistic link
title: Targeting Reduced Glutathione (GSH) to Promote Metabolic Health: Insights on the Role of Bioactive-Rich Foods and Fasting Protocols.

text: . Fasting may promote adaptive redox responses by inducing mild oxidative stress and activating the same molecular mechanism, although the effects on GSH-related antioxidant mechanisms remain heterogeneous across fasting protocols and study populations
title: Targeting Reduced Glutathione (GSH) to Promote Metabolic Health: Insights on the Role of Bioactive-Rich Foods and Fasting Protocols.

text: . Altogether, the available clinical evidence suggests that these nutritional and lifestyle interventions exhibit more consistent beneficial effects in individuals characterized by increased oxidative burden and underlying metabolic dysfunction
title: Targeting Reduced Glutathione (GSH) to Promote Metabolic Health: Insights on the Role of Bioactive-Rich Foods and Fasting Protocols.

text: . Interindividual differences in GSH responses further underscore the need for targeted, tailor-made approaches that account for genetic, epigenetic, and lifestyle factors
title: Targeting Reduced Glutathione (GSH) to Promote Metabolic Health: Insights on the Role of Bioactive-Rich Foods and Fasting Protocols.

text: . Collectively, targeting GSH homeostasis through nutritional and lifestyle interventions represents a promising strategy for improving metabolic health and may further contribute to healthy aging, positioning redox biology at the forefront of aging research and NCD prevention.
title: Targeting Reduced Glutathione (GSH) to Promote Metabolic Health: Insights on the Role of Bioactive-Rich Foods and Fasting Protocols.

text: Delivery of Dietary Advice for Type 2 Diabetes in Dental Settings and Its Relevance to Dental Practitioners: A Scoping Review.. Diabetes and periodontal disease are inflammatory conditions where lifestyle interventions such as dietary messages could improve outcomes of both chronic conditions
title: Delivery of Dietary Advice for Type 2 Diabetes in Dental Settings and Its Relevance to Dental Practitioners: A Scoping Review.

text: . Dental practitioners could support this behavioral intervention during periodontal treatment and maintenance in people with diabetes and periodontal diseases. However, studies that assess dietary interventions in type 2 diabetes patients within dental context setting are limited. This scoping review was completed based on the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for scoping reviews
title: Delivery of Dietary Advice for Type 2 Diabetes in Dental Settings and Its Relevance to Dental Practitioners: A Scoping Review.

text: . An initial comprehensive search on MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and Scopus databases was conducted in May 2024, and again in June 2025. Only English language texts were considered for this review
title: Delivery of Dietary Advice for Type 2 Diabetes in Dental Settings and Its Relevance to Dental Practitioners: A Scoping Review.

text: . The target question for the search on available literature was "What evidence is available on dietary counseling of type 2 diabetes patients in dental settings relevant to delivery by dental practitioners?" Initial search resulted in 394 studies with seven studies eligible for inclusion in this scoping review retrieved
title: Delivery of Dietary Advice for Type 2 Diabetes in Dental Settings and Its Relevance to Dental Practitioners: A Scoping Review.

text: . Two studies focused on dental treatment along with dietary advice, four studies developed and/or implemented diabetes-periodontitis educational programs, while one study explored the self-reported capabilities of a dental practitioner in delivering education, including dietary advice
title: Delivery of Dietary Advice for Type 2 Diabetes in Dental Settings and Its Relevance to Dental Practitioners: A Scoping Review.

text: . While all included studies acknowledged the opportunities for dietary advice in a dental setting, the lack of comparative studies and minimal evidence of delivery by dental practitioners limits the ability to draw strong conclusions. These findings underpin the need for designing a communication tool for dental practitioners in advising type 2 diabetes patients about dietary interventions.
title: Delivery of Dietary Advice for Type 2 Diabetes in Dental Settings and Its Relevance to Dental Practitioners: A Scoping Review.

text: The Association of Diabetes-Related Dietary Patterns with Pancreatic Cancer Risk in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition Study.. Pancreatic cancer is relatively rare but remains one of the most lethal tumors. Identifying modifiable risk factors is a crucial step to reduce disease burden. Evidence suggests a potential role of type 2 diabetes mellitus in its pathogenesis
title: The Association of Diabetes-Related Dietary Patterns with Pancreatic Cancer Risk in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition Study.

text: . The objective of this study is to examine the association between dietary patterns related to diabetes and pancreatic cancer risk in a European population. A total of 367,395 participants from the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition study were included. After a median follow-up of 14.9 y, 926 incident cases were identified
title: The Association of Diabetes-Related Dietary Patterns with Pancreatic Cancer Risk in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition Study.

text: . The Diabetes Risk Reduction Diet (DRRD), the Empirical Dietary Index for Hyperinsulinemia (EDIH), and the Empirical Dietary Index for Insulin Resistance (EDIR) were estimated from food frequency questionnaires at recruitment
title: The Association of Diabetes-Related Dietary Patterns with Pancreatic Cancer Risk in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition Study.

text: . Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between dietary patterns and pancreatic cancer were calculated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models, adjusted for relevant confounders
title: The Association of Diabetes-Related Dietary Patterns with Pancreatic Cancer Risk in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition Study.

text: . Adherence to DRRD showed no association with risk of pancreatic cancer (HR Higher adherence to a hyperinsulinemic dietary pattern may contribute to risk of developing pancreatic cancer in our population. Further research is warranted to elucidate the potential role of dietary factors in cancer risk prevention.
title: The Association of Diabetes-Related Dietary Patterns with Pancreatic Cancer Risk in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition Study.

text: Dynamic Changes in High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I Levels Associate With Variations in Cardiovascular Risk Scores in the General Population.. In the general population, elevated hs-cTnI (high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I) levels are linked to adverse cardiovascular outcomes
title: Dynamic Changes in High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I Levels Associate With Variations in Cardiovascular Risk Scores in the General Population.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Whether changes in hs-cTnI within the normal range are associated with variations in cardiovascular risk scores remains unclear. This observational substudy of the CV-PREVITAL (Strategies for Primary Cardiovascular Prevention in the Italian Population) project evaluated 810 subjects (522 women) in primary prevention. Hs-cTnI was measured at baseline and after 12 months in 473 participants
title: Dynamic Changes in High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I Levels Associate With Variations in Cardiovascular Risk Scores in the General Population.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Cardiovascular risk was assessed using validated scores along with diet adherence and sleep quality. Clinical and laboratory parameters were recorded. Participants received structured lifestyle counseling. At baseline, hs-cTnI was undetectable in 59% of participants
title: Dynamic Changes in High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I Levels Associate With Variations in Cardiovascular Risk Scores in the General Population.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Detectable hs-cTnI was associated with older age (58 versus 55 years), higher body mass index (26 versus 24 kg/m In this primary-prevention cohort, the presence of detectable hs-cTnI was associated with a less favorable risk profile. However, its usefulness in the longitudinal monitoring of cardiovascular risk changes requires validation against cardiovascular outcomes.
title: Dynamic Changes in High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I Levels Associate With Variations in Cardiovascular Risk Scores in the General Population.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.. The prevalence of pre-diabetes mellitus (pre-diabetes, pre-DM) is increasing globally, with 5%-10% of adults with pre-DM progressing to type 2 DM (T2DM) annually
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: . Despite the availability of national screening programmes and lifestyle interventions, uptake remains suboptimal and the lived experiences of individuals navigating pre-DM diagnosis and care in Singapore remain poorly understood
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: . Understanding these experiences is critical, as patient perspectives can reveal gaps in care delivery, particularly in a multiethnic population where cultural, social and systemic factors intersect in complex ways. The current study explores the barriers and facilitators in detecting and managing pre-DM in Singapore's multiethnic population
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: . This qualitative study employed purposive sampling and a phenomenological approach to capture the experiences of those living with pre-DM (n=13). Participants were recruited from National Healthcare Group polyclinics through clinician referrals and through self-referrals
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: . Eligible participants were aged 21 and above, Singapore citizens or permanent residents, diagnosed with pre-DM and conversant in at least one local language, while those with T2DM or type 1 DM were excluded. One-to-one in-depth interviews were conducted between August 2023 and February 2024, which were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed through reflexive thematic analysis
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: . Six overarching themes were identified: a) pathways to pre-DM diagnosis (detection during management of chronic conditions, self-initiated detection through health screening (HS)), b) dealing with diagnosis: navigating shock, acceptance and worry about the future, c) life before diagnosis: living in comfort and the absence of consequences (dietary habits and lifestyle choices before diagnosis,
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: habits and lifestyle choices before diagnosis, when not knowing felt safer: the reasons for not doing HS), d) life after diagnosis: reconfiguring daily life (lifestyle changes: renegotiating diet and exercise habits, alternative therapies: integrating traditional approaches), e) pre-DM care (challenges and enablers of pre-DM management) and f) reimagining care: suggestions for improving pre-DM
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: care: suggestions for improving pre-DM care
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

The main barriers were i) personal factors: the struggle to sustain behavioural changes (such as lack of awareness, difficulty with dietary and physical activity changes, lack of self-discipline), ii) navigating social and environmental barriers to lifestyle change, iii) the financial burden of lifestyle changes, iv) work-related factors: competing priorities and time constraints,v) feeling
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: priorities and time constraints,v) feeling unheard: the healthcare team-related barriers to care and vi) gaps in the systems: structural barriers to care (such as long waiting times, clinician rotation, short consultations)
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: . Enablers included i) fear to action: personal drivers of pre-DM self-management (such as personal factors including fear of developing T2DM), ii) family, peers and domestic help as daily support, iii) feeling heard and cared for: healthcare team-related factors, iv) seamless care through operational excellence and v) knowledge about pre-DM: sources and information seeking
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: . Our findings suggest the need for multilevel collaboration to promote effective strategies to manage pre-DM in the community. This requires interventions to promote early screening, healthcare reforms to reduce waiting times and clinician rotation, and sustaining lifestyle modifications
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

text: . Interventions should leverage the enablers identified in the study while addressing the barriers to ensure healthcare reforms. The insights derived from this study can directly inform locally contextualised interventions and policy reforms to strengthen pre-DM care delivery within a multiethnic healthcare setting.
title: From diagnosis to daily life: a qualitative investigation into patients' lived experiences of pre-diabetes diagnosis and care in a primary care setting in Singapore.

journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine

title: Efficacy of Ayurveda treatment protocol in the management of prediabetes- A randomized controlled clinical trial.

text: Cooking for control: assessing the relationship between culinary knowledge and home cooking habits in the type 1 diabetes population.. In this study we analyzed culinary knowledge, skills, and habits among Spanish adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus, exploring their relationship with sociodemographic variables and glycemic control
title: Cooking for control: assessing the relationship between culinary knowledge and home cooking habits in the type 1 diabetes population.

text: . A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted with 287 participants recruited via social media and diabetes associations. Data were collected using a culturally adapted questionnaire assessing culinary competencies, habits, and clinical variables. Participants demonstrated high self-perceived culinary competence, particularly in cooking vegetables and proteins
title: Cooking for control: assessing the relationship between culinary knowledge and home cooking habits in the type 1 diabetes population.

text: . While family remains the primary source of initial learning (79.8%), digital platforms have emerged as the leading resource for recipes (48.1%). Significant sex and age differences were observed: both women and adults over 30 reported higher home-cooking frequencies, women also reported more frequent use of healthy techniques, and younger adults relied more heavily on unhealthy techniques
title: Cooking for control: assessing the relationship between culinary knowledge and home cooking habits in the type 1 diabetes population.

text: . Notably, better glycemic control (HbA1c < 7%) was significantly associated with higher culinary knowledge scores and lower use of unhealthy cooking techniques and additives. Culinary self-efficacy is a key driver for healthier lifestyle choices in type 1 diabetes mellitus management
title: Cooking for control: assessing the relationship between culinary knowledge and home cooking habits in the type 1 diabetes population.

text: . These findings highlight the need to integrate practical culinary training and digital literacy into formal diabetes education to improve long-term metabolic outcomes.
title: Cooking for control: assessing the relationship between culinary knowledge and home cooking habits in the type 1 diabetes population.

text: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.. title: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.

text: . This study evaluated the comparative efficacy of a culturally adapted diabetes prevention program (DPP) intervention versus usual care in reducing T2D risk factors in Ecuadorian institutional settings. This quasi-experimental study included adults with high T2D risk (FINDRISC score ≥12)
title: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.

text: . Participants voluntarily enrolled to an experimental group (EG, N = 192) receiving a 16-week, 10 session culturally adapted DPP, or a control group (CG, N = 91), receiving usual care. Primary comparative efficacy was assessed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for key baseline imbalances
title: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.

text: . Intragroup analysis showed that EG achieved significant reductions in weight (average loss of 1.06%), BMI, and body fat mass (P < .05). However, the primary outcome reduction in FINDRISC score (P = .013) did not retain significance after Holm-Bonferroni correction
title: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.

text: . The comparative ANCOVA analysis revealed no significant difference between EG and CG for the primary outcomes of weight (P = .330) or FINDRISC score (P = .291)
title: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.

text: . The intervention showed a reduction in systolic blood pressure (SBP) that was statistically significant in the per-protocol analysis (adjusted Δ = -3.338 mmHg; F = 5.160, P = .024), although this effect was attenuated to a trend (P = .079) in a multiply imputed intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis
title: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.

text: . The short-term, culturally adapted DPP intervention failed to demonstrate superior comparative efficacy in achieving the primary goals of T2D risk reduction or weight loss compared to usual care
title: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.

text: . Nevertheless, the per-protocol analysis identified a promising reduction in SBP, whose robustness was supported by inverse probability of treatment weighting but attenuated under intention-to-treat multiple imputation
title: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.

text: . These findings suggest partial efficacy of the short-term adaptation on cardiovascular health and underscore the critical need for longer program duration and strategies to reduce attrition in similar institutional settings. The prevalence of type 2 diabetes is increasing rapidly around the world, particularly in Latin America
title: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.

text: . This study examines whether a program focusing on the DPP curriculum, with motivation and instruction to improve diet and encourage physical activity could reduce the risk of T2D and associated factors among high-risk Ecuadorian individuals
title: Effectiveness of a culturally adapted group-based lifestyle intervention in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in a high-risk Latin American population.

text: . The program, called “Transform your life with daily changes,” was implemented with one group of participants for 16 weeks, while the control group continued with their usual care. text: . Systolic blood pressure showed a promising reduction that requires confirmation with longer follow-up and reduced attrition, and may suggest that a simple, locally tailored intervention carried out in a group setting can help to improve metabolic parameters in at-risk individuals.

text: The role of nutrition literacy in dietary patterns, body composition, and glycemic control among adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus.. This study investigated the relationship between nutrition literacy (NL) among adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and their dietary habits, anthropometric measurements, and glycemic profiles
title: The role of nutrition literacy in dietary patterns, body composition, and glycemic control among adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

text: . A cross-sectional study was conducted with 103 adolescents diagnosed with T1DM. NL was assessed using the Adolescent Nutrition Literacy Scale (ANLS). Dietary intake was evaluated through single-day food records. Anthropometric measurements included body weight, height, waist circumference, and mid-upper arm circumference
title: The role of nutrition literacy in dietary patterns, body composition, and glycemic control among adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

text: . Glycemic control was assessed through glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and fasting blood glucose levels. Multivariable linear regression analyzed associations between NL and influencing factors. NL levels ranged from moderate to high
title: The role of nutrition literacy in dietary patterns, body composition, and glycemic control among adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

text: . NL levels ranged from moderate to high. Elevated ANLS and/or subscales were significantly associated with parental high school completion, paternal self-employment, target-range HbA1c, regular physical activity, structured meal patterns (3 meals, ≥3 snacks), and healthier dietary choices (lower fast-food and processed snacks, higher fruit/vegetable intake)
title: The role of nutrition literacy in dietary patterns, body composition, and glycemic control among adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

text: . Adolescents classified as having thinness based on mid-upper arm circumference demonstrated significantly lower functional NL compared to other groups. Positive correlations were observed between ANLS and/or subscale and dietary energy, protein, and micronutrients (riboflavin, pyridoxine, iron, zinc) intake, while negative associations occurred with carbohydrate and sodium consumption
title: The role of nutrition literacy in dietary patterns, body composition, and glycemic control among adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

text: . Multivariable linear regression analysis revealed positive relationships with age and dietary iron intake, alongside inverse relationships with HbA1c and energy intake. Higher NL is associated with healthier lifestyle behaviors, better dietary patterns, and enhanced glycemic stability in adolescents with T1DM
title: The role of nutrition literacy in dietary patterns, body composition, and glycemic control among adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

text: . Interventions aimed at enhancing NL may contribute to reducing both individual and societal burdens of T1DM by promoting improved disease management and long-term health outcomes.
title: The role of nutrition literacy in dietary patterns, body composition, and glycemic control among adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

text: Acute mild cold exposure with shivering reduces 24 h glucose levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes but not prediabetes.. Repeated cold exposure with shivering has been proposed as a potential strategy to enhance glucose metabolism by increasing energy expenditure and substrate utilisation
title: Acute mild cold exposure with shivering reduces 24 h glucose levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes but not prediabetes.

text: . However, acute effects/benefits of cold-induced shivering on glucose homeostasis in metabolically compromised individuals are unknown. Here, we aimed to determine whether cold exposure at two different intensities improves 24 h glucose homeostasis in individuals with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes
title: Acute mild cold exposure with shivering reduces 24 h glucose levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes but not prediabetes.

text: . In a randomised crossover trial conducted in the South Limburg/Maastricht region of the Netherlands, men and postmenopausal women with prediabetes (n=12) and stable type 2 diabetes (n=12), aged 40-75 years, body mass index ≥27 and ≤35 kg/m In both study groups and periods, RMR increased significantly vs baseline (p<0.001 for all)
title: Acute mild cold exposure with shivering reduces 24 h glucose levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes but not prediabetes.

text: . In prediabetes, the increase in the final 1 h of cold was 1.53 × RMR in mild and 1.94 × RMR in moderate cold. In type 2 diabetes, the increase was 1.57 × RMR and 2.09 × RMR in the final 1 h of mild and moderate cold, respectively. In prediabetes, neither mild nor moderate cold exposure altered mean 24 h glucose levels
title: Acute mild cold exposure with shivering reduces 24 h glucose levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes but not prediabetes.

text: . In contrast, after mild cold exposure the type 2 diabetes group exhibited a significant reduction in mean 24 h glucose levels (-0.6 ± 0.5 mmol/l, p=0.003) and fasting glucose (-0.6 ± 0.8 mmol/l, p=0.019), as well as an increase in time in normal range (+8.8 ± 10.3%, p=0.013) and reduced time in hyperglycaemia (-10.9 ± 12.9%, p=0.014)
title: Acute mild cold exposure with shivering reduces 24 h glucose levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes but not prediabetes.

text: . Moderate cold did not significantly affect any of the glucose outcomes in type 2 diabetes. title: Acute mild cold exposure with shivering reduces 24 h glucose levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes but not prediabetes.

title: Acute mild cold exposure with shivering reduces 24 h glucose levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes but not prediabetes.

text: SNP-derived CpG variation and DNA methylation linking genetic susceptibility to metabolic disease.. DNA methylation at CpG dinucleotides represents a key epigenetic mechanism linking genetic variation to gene regulation in complex human diseases
title: SNP-derived CpG variation and DNA methylation linking genetic susceptibility to metabolic disease.

text: . Single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that create or disrupt CpG sites can alter local DNA methylation and transcriptional activity, thereby influencing disease susceptibility. These CpG-modifying variants provide a functional interface between inherited genetic variation and epigenetic regulation in complex metabolic disorders
title: SNP-derived CpG variation and DNA methylation linking genetic susceptibility to metabolic disease.

text: . This review summarizes current evidence on SNP-derived CpG variation and its role in allele-specific DNA methylation and gene regulation in metabolically relevant tissues
title: SNP-derived CpG variation and DNA methylation linking genetic susceptibility to metabolic disease.

text: . By integrating findings from genome-wide association studies, epigenome-wide association studies, and multi-omics research, this review provides a mechanistic framework explaining how CpG-modifying polymorphisms influence adipogenesis, pancreatic β-cell function, inflammation, and glucose metabolism
title: SNP-derived CpG variation and DNA methylation linking genetic susceptibility to metabolic disease.

text: . Special emphasis is placed on South Asian populations, who exhibit early β-cell dysfunction and increased visceral adiposity. Many CpG-modifying variants act as methylation quantitative trait loci (meQTLs), influencing allele-specific methylation and gene expression
title: SNP-derived CpG variation and DNA methylation linking genetic susceptibility to metabolic disease.

text: . Understanding SNP-CpG-methylation interactions may improve functional interpretation of disease-associated genetic variants, enhance biomarker discovery, and support precision medicine strategies for metabolic disease. Obesity and type 2 diabetes are becoming increasingly common in South Asian populations, particularly in India
title: SNP-derived CpG variation and DNA methylation linking genetic susceptibility to metabolic disease.

text: . Many people develop diabetes at a younger age and at a lower body weight than people from Western countries. Scientists believe that changes in our genes alone cannot fully explain this increased risk. This review explains how small changes in DNA, called single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), can affect how genes are switched on or off through a natural process called DNA methylation
title: SNP-derived CpG variation and DNA methylation linking genetic susceptibility to metabolic disease.

text: . These changes may influence insulin production, body fat accumulation, inflammation, and blood sugar regulation.The review also describes how diet, lifestyle, and environmental factors work together with these genetic and epigenetic changes to increase the risk of obesity and type 2 diabetes
title: SNP-derived CpG variation and DNA methylation linking genetic susceptibility to metabolic disease.

text: . A better understanding of these interactions may help researchers develop improved methods for early disease detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, particularly for South Asian populations.
title: SNP-derived CpG variation and DNA methylation linking genetic susceptibility to metabolic disease.

text: Determinants of health-related quality of life in adults with type 1 diabetes: The predominant role of sleep among lifestyle parameters.. journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

text: Lifestyle modifications in individuals with blood pressure beyond treatment target despite pharmacological treatment: design and baseline characteristics of the MeDiPA randomised controlled trial.. title: Lifestyle modifications in individuals with blood pressure beyond treatment target despite pharmacological treatment: design and baseline characteristics of the MeDiPA randomised controlled trial.

title: Lifestyle modifications in individuals with blood pressure beyond treatment target despite pharmacological treatment: design and baseline characteristics of the MeDiPA randomised controlled trial.
