text: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.. Mitochondria are central regulators of cellular metabolism, redox homeostasis, and stress adaptation
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . Mitohormesis refers to an adaptive response in which mild or transient mitochondrial perturbation activates stress-response pathways that subsequently enhance mitochondrial or cellular resilience; however, persistent or excessive stress can overwhelm adaptive capacity and promote mitochondrial dysfunction and tissue injury
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . Metabolic diseases, including obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus, are major risk factors for cognitive decline and dementia, and clinical studies have demonstrated associations between metabolic dysfunction, structural brain abnormalities, accelerated brain aging, and impaired cognitive function
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . However, direct evidence linking mitochondrial dysfunction to neurodegeneration in humans remains limited, with most mechanistic insights derived from experimental animal models and cultured neuronal systems
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . Experimental evidence indicates that chronic metabolic stress can disrupt mitochondrial quality control and proteostasis, increase mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production, and promote neuroinflammation and neuronal dysfunction
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . Conversely, adaptive mitochondrial stress responses can preserve mitochondrial integrity and cellular resilience through coordinated regulation of the integrated stress response, mitochondrial quality-control mechanisms, lysosomal-mitochondrial crosstalk, extracellular vesicle-mediated communication, and inter-organ signaling
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . In Alzheimer's disease, mitochondrial dysfunction and amyloid-β/tau pathology may interact bidirectionally, potentially generating self-reinforcing cycles of neuronal injury
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . Lifestyle and pharmacological interventions-including exercise; caloric restriction; nutritional ketosis; and the use of metformin, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists-have been associated with adaptive mitochondrial and metabolic responses involving AMP-activated protein kinase, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2, mitochondrial
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: erythroid 2-related factor 2, mitochondrial biogenesis, mitophagy, and redox signaling
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . However, evidence that mitohormesis directly mediates their beneficial effects varies substantially across interventions and remains predominantly indirect or hypothesized in humans
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . Moreover, the discrepancy between encouraging preclinical findings and clinical outcomes highlights important translational barriers, including the lack of validated biomarkers, uncertainty regarding optimal stress intensity and timing, and tissue- and disease-specific differences in adaptive capacity
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . Collectively, current evidence supports mitohormesis as a conceptual framework for integrating mitochondrial stress adaptation, metabolic dysfunction, and neuronal resilience rather than as an established unifying mechanism underlying neurodegeneration
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: . Defining the conditions under which mitochondrial stress is adaptive, identifying reliable biomarkers of mitohormesis, and determining whether these responses can be safely and effectively modulated in humans will be essential for establishing its therapeutic relevance in metabolic and neurodegenerative diseases.
title: Mitohormesis linking metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration: implications for dementia and therapeutic strategies.

text: Genetic Insights Into Protective Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Stroke and Alzheimer Disease Across Ancestries.. Stroke and dementia are leading causes of death and disability worldwide, requiring enhanced preventive strategies
title: Genetic Insights Into Protective Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Stroke and Alzheimer Disease Across Ancestries.

text: . Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA), widely used for type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity, have demonstrated pleiotropic effects, including cardiovascular benefits, with mounting evidence also suggesting potential beneficial effects on brain health
title: Genetic Insights Into Protective Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Stroke and Alzheimer Disease Across Ancestries.

text: . The objective of this study was to investigate the genetically proxied effect of GLP-1RA on stroke, Alzheimer disease (AD), and related endophenotypes, in a cross-ancestry setting. We conducted a 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study using both a locus-based and a protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL)-based approach
title: Genetic Insights Into Protective Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Stroke and Alzheimer Disease Across Ancestries.

text: . The study leveraged summary statistics from large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS). These GWAS comprised participants of European, East-Asian, and African ancestry with and without T2D, stroke, and AD, and with measurements of fasting glucose, glycated hemoglobin, stroke, and AD endophenotypes. Sample size ranged from 3,026 to 1,812,017 individuals
title: Genetic Insights Into Protective Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Stroke and Alzheimer Disease Across Ancestries.

text: . Genetically proxied GLP-1RA exposure was instrumented using independent T2D-associated variants ( In Europeans, locus-based MR indicated significant protective associations of GLP-1RA with any stroke and ischemic stroke ( GLP-1RAs may confer protective effects against stroke (especially ischemic and cardioembolic) and AD risk, across ancestries
title: Genetic Insights Into Protective Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Stroke and Alzheimer Disease Across Ancestries.

text: . These findings warrant further investigation in experimental models and clinical trials to confirm benefits on brain health and understand underlying mechanisms.
title: Genetic Insights Into Protective Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Stroke and Alzheimer Disease Across Ancestries.

text: Impact of the Four Pillars on Electrolyte Derangements during State-of-the-Art Therapy for Diabetic Kidney Disease.. The pharmacological management of diabetic kidney disease (DKD) has shifted toward a "four-pillar" approach that offers robust cardiorenal protection
title: Impact of the Four Pillars on Electrolyte Derangements during State-of-the-Art Therapy for Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . While traditional renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitors carry well-documented electrolyte risks, the distinct electrolyte profiles of novel therapies-sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), and non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (nsMRAs)-warrant a comprehensive understanding
title: Impact of the Four Pillars on Electrolyte Derangements during State-of-the-Art Therapy for Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . This review examines these drug-induced electrolyte derangements. SGLT2 inhibitors demonstrate a highly favorable safety profile; despite inducing osmotic diuresis, they are notably associated with a reduced risk of hyperkalemia
title: Impact of the Four Pillars on Electrolyte Derangements during State-of-the-Art Therapy for Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . Similarly, GLP-1 RAs possess an exceptionally low risk of direct renal electrolyte wasting, with imbalances occurring primarily secondary to severe gastrointestinal intolerance
title: Impact of the Four Pillars on Electrolyte Derangements during State-of-the-Art Therapy for Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . Conversely, nsMRAs, such as finerenone, introduce a mild risk of hyperkalemia, though their unique receptor selectivity significantly diminishes this risk compared to traditional steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. Crucially, combining SGLT2 inhibitors and nsMRAs creates a physiological synergy that attenuates hyperkalemic adverse effects while maximizing antiproteinuric benefits
title: Impact of the Four Pillars on Electrolyte Derangements during State-of-the-Art Therapy for Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . By integrating these complementary mechanisms alongside routine electrolyte monitoring, clinicians can safely sustain these indispensable combination therapies and optimize clinical outcomes in DKD.
title: Impact of the Four Pillars on Electrolyte Derangements during State-of-the-Art Therapy for Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: GHRH and GLP-1 receptor agonism promote human β-cell survival and improve glucose homeostasis in diabetic mice.. Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by progressive loss of pancreatic β cell mass driven by inflammatory cytokine-induced apoptosis
title: GHRH and GLP-1 receptor agonism promote human β-cell survival and improve glucose homeostasis in diabetic mice.

text: . Although glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists improve β cell function and survival, their efficacy may be limited under hyperglycemic conditions. Growth hormone-releasing hormone receptor (GHRH-R) agonists have emerged as potential β cell-protective agents through activation of cAMP-dependent signaling pathways
title: GHRH and GLP-1 receptor agonism promote human β-cell survival and improve glucose homeostasis in diabetic mice.

text: . Here, we investigated the effects of the GHRH-R agonist MR-409, alone or in combination with the GLP-1R agonist exendin-4 (Ex-4), on β cell survival and glucose homeostasis. In human islets, combined MR-409 and Ex-4 treatment enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and increased CREB phosphorylation
title: GHRH and GLP-1 receptor agonism promote human β-cell survival and improve glucose homeostasis in diabetic mice.

text: . The combination also reduced cytokine-induced apoptosis, with decreased caspase 3/7 activity compared with MR-409 alone and reduced BAX protein levels compared with either individual treatment. MR-409 alone increased IRS2 protein levels, consistent with activation of pro-survival signaling pathways
title: GHRH and GLP-1 receptor agonism promote human β-cell survival and improve glucose homeostasis in diabetic mice.

text: . In a multiple low-dose streptozotocin (STZ) mouse model, MR-409, Ex-4, and their combination improved glucose homeostasis and increased β cell mass compared with vehicle-treated mice. However, the combination did not confer additional metabolic benefit over single treatments. Notably, MR-409 treatment was associated with greater improvements in glucose tolerance and insulin levels
title: GHRH and GLP-1 receptor agonism promote human β-cell survival and improve glucose homeostasis in diabetic mice.

text: . These findings support further investigation of GHRH receptor agonism as a strategy to preserve β-cell survival under diabetogenic stress.
title: GHRH and GLP-1 receptor agonism promote human β-cell survival and improve glucose homeostasis in diabetic mice.

text: Contemporary Initial Glucose-Lowering Strategies for Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.. To compare contemporary initial glucose-lowering strategies in adults with type 2 diabetes who were treatment-naïve or had completed adequate washout
title: Contemporary Initial Glucose-Lowering Strategies for Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.

text: . We searched MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library from inception to 20 September 2025 for randomized trials comparing sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) monotherapy, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) or dual incretin agonist monotherapy, SGLT2i plus metformin or placebo. Two reviewers independently selected studies and verified extracted data
title: Contemporary Initial Glucose-Lowering Strategies for Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.

text: . Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis was used. Twenty randomized trials with 8947 participants were included; all were at low risk of bias
title: Contemporary Initial Glucose-Lowering Strategies for Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.

text: . Compared with placebo, SGLT2i plus metformin produced the largest HbA1c reduction (mean difference [MD] -1.36%, 95% credible interval [CrI] -1.91 to -0.82), followed by GLP-1 RA or dual incretin agonist monotherapy (MD -1.25%, 95% CrI -1.68 to -0.83) and SGLT2i monotherapy (MD -0.76%, 95% CrI -1.10 to -0.41). Achievement of HbA1c < 7% and fasting plasma glucose reduction showed a similar pattern
title: Contemporary Initial Glucose-Lowering Strategies for Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.

text: . GLP-1 RA or dual incretin agonist monotherapy produced the greatest body weight percentage reduction (MD -4.74%, 95% CrI -6.71 to -2.90). Active-treatment comparisons were indirect, and baseline HbA1c was higher in the SGLT2i plus metformin node. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across key comparisons
title: Contemporary Initial Glucose-Lowering Strategies for Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.

text: . SGLT2i plus metformin and GLP-1 RA or dual incretin agonist therapy are both reasonable contemporary initial glucose-lowering strategies for type 2 diabetes. Selection between these strategies should take into consideration phenotype, treatment priorities, tolerability, cost, access and patient preference. PROSPERO: CRD420251178714.
title: Contemporary Initial Glucose-Lowering Strategies for Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.

text: Efficacy and Safety of Dual GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Agonism in Overweight and Obesity: A Class-Specific Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
title: Efficacy and Safety of Dual GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Agonism in Overweight and Obesity: A Class-Specific Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Dual glucagon-like peptide-1/glucagon receptor (GLP-1/GCGR) agonists represent a novel obesity treatment class, but existing meta-analyses often conflate them with GIP-containing agents (tirzepatide, retatrutide) or restrict analysis to one or two drugs, leaving class-specific efficacy and safety incompletely characterized
title: Efficacy and Safety of Dual GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Agonism in Overweight and Obesity: A Class-Specific Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus and ClinicalTrials.gov through 20 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials of mazdutide, survodutide, cotadutide, and efinopegdutide in adults with overweight/obesity (PROSPERO CRD420261456447)
title: Efficacy and Safety of Dual GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Agonism in Overweight and Obesity: A Class-Specific Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Random-effects meta-analysis pooled mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs; heterogeneity, subgroup, sensitivity, GRADE and publication bias analyses were performed. Nineteen RCTs were included
title: Efficacy and Safety of Dual GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Agonism in Overweight and Obesity: A Class-Specific Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Nineteen RCTs were included. Dual agonists significantly reduced absolute body weight (MD: -6.65 kg, moderate certainty), relative weight (MD: -7.15%), and increased likelihood of ≥ 5% weight loss (RR: 4.75, low certainty), with mazdutide and survodutide showing the largest effects. Significant improvements occurred in HbA1c, BMI, waist circumference, systolic blood pressure and triglycerides
title: Efficacy and Safety of Dual GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Agonism in Overweight and Obesity: A Class-Specific Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Any adverse events were more frequent with dual agonists (RR: 1.16), while serious adverse events did not differ from controls (RR: 0.90, high certainty). Dual GLP-1/GCGR agonists produce meaningful weight loss and metabolic improvements with acceptable short-term safety, though longer head-to-head trials are needed to confirm durability and cardiovascular safety.
title: Efficacy and Safety of Dual GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Agonism in Overweight and Obesity: A Class-Specific Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure in the periconceptional period and adverse obstetric outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.. This systematic review and meta-analysis assesses whether exposure to glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) during pregnancy or the periconceptional period is associated with adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes
title: GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure in the periconceptional period and adverse obstetric outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched for observational studies comparing pregnancies exposed and unexposed to GLP-1 RAs within 6 months before a positive pregnancy test
title: GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure in the periconceptional period and adverse obstetric outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Outcomes included miscarriage, intrauterine death, congenital anomalies, preterm birth (PTB), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), fetal growth restriction (FGR), small for gestational age (SGA), large for gestational age (LGA), and excess gestational weight gain. Random-effects meta-analyses and subgroup analyses by indication were performed
title: GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure in the periconceptional period and adverse obstetric outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Ten studies included 2,118,215 women, of whom 8,325 were exposed and 2,109,890 were unexposed. Pooled estimates did not show a clearly detectable increase in miscarriage or intrauterine death, congenital anomalies, preterm birth, HDP, gestational diabetes, abnormal fetal growth, or excess gestational weight gain
title: GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure in the periconceptional period and adverse obstetric outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . A lower pooled estimate for preeclampsia was observed (odds ratio [OR]: 0.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.78-0.98; p = 0.02), but this was based on two datasets and should be interpreted cautiously. Subgroup analyses showed no clearly detectable differences by indication
title: GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure in the periconceptional period and adverse obstetric outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . The exposure-window sensitivity analysis, covering 90 days before conception through the end of the first trimester, used the same four studies as the primary congenital-malformation analysis and therefore was not independent. Available observational evidence did not identify a clearly detectable increase in adverse maternal or perinatal outcomes following periconceptional exposure to GLP-1 RAs
title: GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure in the periconceptional period and adverse obstetric outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . However, these findings do not establish safety because of heterogeneity, residual confounding, and limited datasets. None.

text: Chilean Multidisciplinary Consensus on the Use of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Recommendations Based on the GRADE Methodology.. Type 2 diabetes (T2DM), obesity, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and heart failure (HF) pose a major public health burden in Chile and Latin America
title: Chilean Multidisciplinary Consensus on the Use of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Recommendations Based on the GRADE Methodology.

text: . Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) provide glycemic, cardiovascular, renal, and weight-loss benefits, extending their therapeutic role beyond glycemic control
title: Chilean Multidisciplinary Consensus on the Use of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Recommendations Based on the GRADE Methodology.

text: . To develop a national consensus, based on GRADE methodology, that synthesizes the best available evidence and adapts it to the Chilean healthcare context, providing practical recommendations for the rational use of GLP-1 RA (GLP-1 receptor agonists)
title: Chilean Multidisciplinary Consensus on the Use of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Recommendations Based on the GRADE Methodology.

text: . A multidisciplinary panel convened by six Chilean scientific societies developed this consensus, using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) framework. A systematic review of randomized trials and meta-analyses was conducted
title: Chilean Multidisciplinary Consensus on the Use of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Recommendations Based on the GRADE Methodology.

text: . Evidence tables were prepared and critically appraised to support transparent recommendations adapted to the Chilean healthcare context
title: Chilean Multidisciplinary Consensus on the Use of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Recommendations Based on the GRADE Methodology.

text: . The panel formulated seven key recommendations: (1) a strong recommendation for GLP-1 RAs in patients with T2DM and CKD; (2) a weak recommendation in CKD without diabetes; (3) a strong recommendation in T2DM with high cardiovascular risk; (4) a weak recommendation over sulfonylureas as add-on to metformin; (5) a strong recommendation in HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and BMI ≥27;
title: Chilean Multidisciplinary Consensus on the Use of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Recommendations Based on the GRADE Methodology.

text: preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and BMI ≥27; (6) a strong recommendation in obesity with T2DM; and (7) a weak recommendation in obesity without T2DM
title: Chilean Multidisciplinary Consensus on the Use of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Recommendations Based on the GRADE Methodology.

text: . This consensus synthesizes international evidence and contextualizes it to Chile, supporting rational, equitable, and transparent implementation of GLP-1 RAs. These agents are positioned as central tools in the management of the cardiorenal-metabolic syndrome, complementing current cost-effective therapies and lifestyle interventions.
title: Chilean Multidisciplinary Consensus on the Use of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Recommendations Based on the GRADE Methodology.

text: Hypothalamic obesity in pediatric vs. adult craniopharyngioma: mechanisms, management, and cardiometabolic outcomes.. Hypothalamic obesity (HO) is a treatment-related complication in craniopharyngioma (CP) survivors that markedly impairs long-term health and quality of life
title: Hypothalamic obesity in pediatric vs. adult craniopharyngioma: mechanisms, management, and cardiometabolic outcomes.

text: . Although overall survival exceeds 90% for both pediatric and adult CP, HO prevalence and clinical course differ substantially by age at onset. We aimed to compare HO manifestations, mechanisms, and treatment response between pediatric and adult CP cohorts
title: Hypothalamic obesity in pediatric vs. adult craniopharyngioma: mechanisms, management, and cardiometabolic outcomes.

text: . We conducted a scoping review of studies published between 2000 and 2025, comparing pediatric (childhood-onset) versus adult-onset CP cohorts, classified by age at diagnosis. Data on obesity prevalence, mechanistic pathways, therapeutic interventions, and cardiometabolic outcomes were extracted and synthesized
title: Hypothalamic obesity in pediatric vs. adult craniopharyngioma: mechanisms, management, and cardiometabolic outcomes.

text: . In pediatric CP survivors, obesity rates rise from 5.7% pre-treatment to 57% post-treatment; in adults, from 19.2% to 29.2%. HO severity correlates with the extent of hypothalamic damage by Puget and QST grading. Key mechanisms include disrupted melanocortin signaling, central leptin and insulin resistance, and neuroinflammation via resistin-TLR4 and NLRP3 pathways
title: Hypothalamic obesity in pediatric vs. adult craniopharyngioma: mechanisms, management, and cardiometabolic outcomes.

text: . GLP-1 receptor agonists (exenatide, semaglutide) have produced marked weight loss in small case series (up to 17% over 6 months with semaglutide), but randomized trials did not meet their primary weight outcomes and direct pediatric-versus-adult comparisons are lacking
title: Hypothalamic obesity in pediatric vs. adult craniopharyngioma: mechanisms, management, and cardiometabolic outcomes.

text: . Bariatric procedures yield moderate success; sleeve gastrectomy achieves 5-year weight loss comparable to that in non-CP controls (21.7% vs. 21.8%), whereas Roux-en-Y gastric bypass is less effective than in controls (22.7% vs. 32.0%)
title: Hypothalamic obesity in pediatric vs. adult craniopharyngioma: mechanisms, management, and cardiometabolic outcomes.

text: . 32.0%). Both cohorts face significant long-term risks: 2.2-fold higher all-cause mortality and 9.3-fold higher diabetes risk in adults, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in 47% of pediatric survivors, metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease in 67.4% of adults, and insulin resistance in approximately 30% of pediatric patients
title: Hypothalamic obesity in pediatric vs. adult craniopharyngioma: mechanisms, management, and cardiometabolic outcomes.

text: . HO following CP shows distinct age-dependent trajectories in prevalence, underlying mechanisms, and clinical course; suggested age-related differences in treatment response remain to be confirmed in direct comparative studies. Tailored management integrating mechanistic insights and age-specific therapies is critical to mitigating the cardiometabolic burden in these patients.
title: Hypothalamic obesity in pediatric vs. adult craniopharyngioma: mechanisms, management, and cardiometabolic outcomes.

text: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Men Seeking Fertility: A Structured Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Framework.
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Men Seeking Fertility: A Structured Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Framework.

text: . Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide are increasingly used to treat obesity and type 2 diabetes in men of reproductive age, but practical guidance for counseling men planning fatherhood remains limited
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Men Seeking Fertility: A Structured Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Framework.

text: . This structured narrative review distinguishes endocrine, semen, sexual-function, and clinical fertility outcomes
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Men Seeking Fertility: A Structured Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Framework.

text: . In metabolically impaired men, studies largely involving liraglutide or semaglutide report increases in total testosterone; free-testosterone findings are inconsistent, and the available small short-term studies did not show the marked gonadotropin suppression expected with exogenous testosterone
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Men Seeking Fertility: A Structured Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Framework.

text: . Some studies report favorable changes in semen parameters, but samples are small, populations heterogeneous, and medication effects cannot be separated reliably from weight loss. The present search identified no adequately powered GLP-1-specific prospective study that prespecified sperm DNA fragmentation, natural conception, assisted-reproduction outcomes, clinical pregnancy, or live birth
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Men Seeking Fertility: A Structured Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Framework.

text: . Sexual-function findings are mixed and do not establish causality. Evidence on paternal preconception exposure is insufficient, and pregnancy-related label precautions do not by themselves establish risk from paternal exposure. No eligible controlled tirzepatide-specific study assessing semen or clinical fertility outcomes was identified by this search
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Men Seeking Fertility: A Structured Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Framework.

text: . These therapies should be used for established metabolic indications, not as male infertility treatments. The proposed framework is author-developed, evidence-informed, non-validated, and intended for individualized counseling and prospective evaluation.
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Men Seeking Fertility: A Structured Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Framework.

text: Genetic Variants Associated with Response to GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Diabetes and Obesity.. text: GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pediatric Obesity: From Neuroendocrine Mechanisms to Clinical Application.. title: GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pediatric Obesity: From Neuroendocrine Mechanisms to Clinical Application.

text: . Incretin-based therapies translate this biology into mechanism-based treatment, yet their developmental implications remain incompletely defined. title: GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pediatric Obesity: From Neuroendocrine Mechanisms to Clinical Application.

text: . We describe how GLP-1 receptor agonists act across central and peripheral tissues to reduce appetite, delay gastric emptying, and enhance glucose-dependent insulin secretion and examine the rationale for dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonism
title: GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pediatric Obesity: From Neuroendocrine Mechanisms to Clinical Application.

title: GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pediatric Obesity: From Neuroendocrine Mechanisms to Clinical Application.

text: . Tirzepatide has shown greater weight-loss efficacy than selective GLP-1 receptor agonism in adults, but no randomized trial has evaluated it in pediatric obesity without diabetes. Incretin-based therapies should be integrated with nutritional, behavioral, psychological, and family-based care
title: GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pediatric Obesity: From Neuroendocrine Mechanisms to Clinical Application.

text: . Their future value will depend on durable efficacy, developmental safety, equitable access, and identification of patients most likely to benefit.
title: GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pediatric Obesity: From Neuroendocrine Mechanisms to Clinical Application.

text: Skeletal Muscle Effects of GLP 1 Receptor Agonists: Molecular Mechanisms and Comparative Insights on Semaglutide and Tirzepatide, a Narrative Review.. GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), dual GLP-1/GIP agonists, and the more recent triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonists have transformed the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, resulting in significant weight reduction
title: Skeletal Muscle Effects of GLP 1 Receptor Agonists: Molecular Mechanisms and Comparative Insights on Semaglutide and Tirzepatide, a Narrative Review.

text: . However, a substantial proportion (20-40%) of this weight loss is attributable to a decrease in lean mass, thereby raising concerns regarding potential sarcopenia-related risk
title: Skeletal Muscle Effects of GLP 1 Receptor Agonists: Molecular Mechanisms and Comparative Insights on Semaglutide and Tirzepatide, a Narrative Review.

text: . However, decreased lean mass is not sufficient to determine sarcopenia, which is now defined by the combined presence of decreased muscle mass, diminished strength, and impaired physical function, particularly in older or frail individuals. Thus, a further clarification of the potential mechanisms through which these molecules affect skeletal muscle is needed to optimize their use
title: Skeletal Muscle Effects of GLP 1 Receptor Agonists: Molecular Mechanisms and Comparative Insights on Semaglutide and Tirzepatide, a Narrative Review.

text: . The objective of this study is to synthesize preclinical, metabolomic, and clinical evidence on the effects of GLP-1RAs and dual/triple agonists on skeletal muscle, with a specific comparison between semaglutide and tirzepatide. This narrative review was based on a comprehensive literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar, encompassing articles published through June 2026
title: Skeletal Muscle Effects of GLP 1 Receptor Agonists: Molecular Mechanisms and Comparative Insights on Semaglutide and Tirzepatide, a Narrative Review.

text: . This search was supplemented by manual citation tracking, which identified additional studies including preclinical and metabolomic investigations, randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and meta-analyses. Preclinical data suggest that GLP-1R/GIPR activation can positively modulate anabolic pathways, mitochondrial biogenesis, and muscle inflammation
title: Skeletal Muscle Effects of GLP 1 Receptor Agonists: Molecular Mechanisms and Comparative Insights on Semaglutide and Tirzepatide, a Narrative Review.

text: . Metabolomic evidence reveals lipid and amino acid remodeling compatible with improved mitochondrial function. Clinically, lean mass loss proportional to weight reduction is consistently observed, generally without meaningful declines in strength or performance; data for tirzepatide are more limited. Lean mass, however, is not synonymous with skeletal muscle
title: Skeletal Muscle Effects of GLP 1 Receptor Agonists: Molecular Mechanisms and Comparative Insights on Semaglutide and Tirzepatide, a Narrative Review.

text: . A paradox emerges between the presence of protective molecular signals and the clinical evidence of lean-mass loss. This phenomenon may be explained by a systemic energy/protein deficit rather than a direct catabolic effect of the drugs, although current evidence does not fully distinguish these mechanisms
title: Skeletal Muscle Effects of GLP 1 Receptor Agonists: Molecular Mechanisms and Comparative Insights on Semaglutide and Tirzepatide, a Narrative Review.

text: . The effectiveness of weight reduction should be considered a pivotal metric in clinical practice, particularly in populations susceptible to sarcopenia.
title: Skeletal Muscle Effects of GLP 1 Receptor Agonists: Molecular Mechanisms and Comparative Insights on Semaglutide and Tirzepatide, a Narrative Review.

text: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . Although glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) reduce cardiovascular risk in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D), evidence in heart failure (HF) has expanded across diverse trial populations and HF phenotypes but remains fragmented
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . We therefore performed an integrated systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effects of GLP-1 RAs across the spectrum of HF using complementary trial-level and phenotype-based analyses. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched for studies published from inception to August 10, 2025
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . To provide an integrated assessment across heterogeneous HF populations, treatment effects were evaluated using dual analytical frameworks: trial-level analyses according to study design (dedicated HF with preserved ejection fraction [HFpEF] trials, HF with reduced ejection fraction [HFrEF] trials, and HF subgroups from cardiovascular outcome trials [CVOTs]) and phenotype-based analyses
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: trials [CVOTs]) and phenotype-based analyses according to left ventricular ejection fraction (HFpEF vs HFrEF using a pragmatic threshold of 40%)
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . A prespecified targeted analysis was conducted to specifically assess the efficacy of semaglutide. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and the secondary outcomes included hospitalization for HF (HHF), the composite of cardiovascular death or any worsening HF events, cardiovascular death alone, and all-cause mortality
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random‑effects models. This meta-analysis included 14 trials, with a pooled total of 15,882 patients with HF
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . In phenotype‑based analyses for HFpEF, GLP‑1 RAs significantly reduced MACE (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.66-0.94; p = 0.010), HHF (HR 0.48; 95% CI 0.27-0.85; p = 0.012), the composite of cardiovascular death or worsening HF (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.37-0.89; p = 0.013), and all‑cause mortality (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.62-0.89; p = 0.001)
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . In contrast, in HFrEF, no significant reductions were observed for HHF, the composite of cardiovascular death or worsening HF, all-cause mortality, or MACE, although a reduction in cardiovascular death was noted (HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.54-0.95; p = 0.019)
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . Trial-level analyses showed that cardiovascular benefits were primarily observed in HF subgroups from CVOTs, including reductions in MACE (HR 0.82; 95% CI 0.73-0.92; p = 0.001), cardiovascular death (HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.77-1.00; p = 0.05) and myocardial infarction (MI)/non-fatal MI (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.70-1.00; p = 0.046)
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . Semaglutide showed benefits in HHF and the composite of cardiovascular death or worsening HF events predominantly among overweight or obese patients with HFpEF. GLP-1 RAs also improved functional capacity and quality of life in HFpEF
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . GLP-1 RAs were associated with favorable cardiovascular and HF-related outcomes in HFpEF, predominantly among overweight or obese individuals, whereas evidence of benefit in HFrEF remains limited. In trial-level analyses, benefits were primarily observed for atherosclerotic endpoints in HF subgroups from CVOTs
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: . By integrating evidence, this study provides a unified overview of the effects of GLP-1 RAs across the spectrum of HF and supports further phenotype-specific randomized trials, particularly dedicated studies in HFrEF. Protocol registration PROSPERO (CRD420251079970).
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Phenotype-Specific Effects and Dual Analytical Frameworks.

text: The Role and Mechanism of Incretins in Gynaecologic Diseases.. Obesity is a major global public health concern closely linked to the development and progression of various gynaecological disorders, particularly polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and endometrial cancer
title: The Role and Mechanism of Incretins in Gynaecologic Diseases.

text: . Incretins, a group of gut-derived hormones primarily including glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), are widely recognised for their roles in glycemic control and insulin secretion
title: The Role and Mechanism of Incretins in Gynaecologic Diseases.

text: . Accumulating evidence reveals that GLP-1 and GIP also participate in modulating inflammation, autophagy, immune response and gut-brain communication through multiple signalling pathways, thereby playing important roles in female reproductive disorders. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the mechanisms and therapeutic potential of incretins in gynaecological conditions
title: The Role and Mechanism of Incretins in Gynaecologic Diseases.

text: . We performed a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Web of Science and Embase, covering studies published from January 1995 to July 2026. Search terms combined incretin-related keywords (GLP-1, GIP, GLP-1 receptor agonists) with gynaecological disease terms (polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, endometrial cancer, ovarian cancer, intrauterine adhesion)
title: The Role and Mechanism of Incretins in Gynaecologic Diseases.

text: . We primarily included original research studies and authoritative reviews, and excluded meeting abstracts, case reports and non-English literature. GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) exert multi-faceted benefits in PCOS, endometriosis, intrauterine adhesions and gynaecologic cancers through cAMP/PKA, PI3K and AMPK signalling pathways
title: The Role and Mechanism of Incretins in Gynaecologic Diseases.

text: . Special emphasis is placed on the multi-faceted benefits of GLP-1 RAs, while evidence supporting GIP-based therapies in gynaecology remains relatively limited and largely preclinical. The current status of clinical application, safety considerations and future directions are further discussed
title: The Role and Mechanism of Incretins in Gynaecologic Diseases.

text: . Incretin-based therapies offer novel approaches for metabolic and oncological gynaecological diseases, with significant translational value. Large-scale clinical studies and deeper mechanistic exploration are warranted to realise their full therapeutic potential.
title: The Role and Mechanism of Incretins in Gynaecologic Diseases.

text: Concurrent metformin-associated lactic acidosis and euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis from tirzepatide starvation ketosis.
title: Concurrent metformin-associated lactic acidosis and euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis from tirzepatide starvation ketosis.

text: The Interplay of Metabolic Dysfunction, Neuroinflammation, and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Balance Impairment: Insights from Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.. title: The Interplay of Metabolic Dysfunction, Neuroinflammation, and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Balance Impairment: Insights from Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.

text: . While traditional clinical models have largely separated these conditions, attributing balance loss in T2DM to peripheral neuropathy and in AD to central cortical atrophy, mounting evidence suggests a convergence of multi-system impairments driven by a shared central pathophysiology
title: The Interplay of Metabolic Dysfunction, Neuroinflammation, and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Balance Impairment: Insights from Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.

text: . This narrative review proposes an integrative framework centered on a vicious, self-reinforcing cycle involving metabolic dysfunction, chronic neuroinflammation, and mitochondrial failure as the core mechanistic link driving balance impairment
title: The Interplay of Metabolic Dysfunction, Neuroinflammation, and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Balance Impairment: Insights from Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.

text: . We detail how systemic and cerebral insulin resistance, coupled with glucotoxicity, trigger the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome and the subsequent release of pro-inflammatory cytokines
title: The Interplay of Metabolic Dysfunction, Neuroinflammation, and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Balance Impairment: Insights from Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.

text: . This inflammatory environment exacerbates mitochondrial bioenergetic failure and oxidative stress, selectively targeting high-energy motor circuits such as the striatum and basal ganglia while simultaneously contributing to musculoskeletal sarcopenia and peripheral nerve demyelination
title: The Interplay of Metabolic Dysfunction, Neuroinflammation, and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Balance Impairment: Insights from Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.

text: . By synthesizing the intricate interplay between these molecular pathways, this review moves beyond disease-specific silos to offer a novel perspective on the shared pathophysiology of postural instability
title: The Interplay of Metabolic Dysfunction, Neuroinflammation, and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Balance Impairment: Insights from Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.

text: . Furthermore, we explore the therapeutic potential of metabolic modulators, such as GLP-1 receptor agonists, and mitochondrial-targeted antioxidants, alongside multimodal rehabilitation strategies. Ultimately, this unified model provides a foundation for developing precision-based interventions to mitigate fall risk and preserve functional independence in vulnerable aging populations.
title: The Interplay of Metabolic Dysfunction, Neuroinflammation, and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Balance Impairment: Insights from Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.

text: Considerations and challenges in microdosing of GLP-1-based receptor agonists.. This commentary summarizes the pharmacologic rationale, emerging evidence, clinical considerations, and limitations of microdosing glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies
title: Considerations and challenges in microdosing of GLP-1-based receptor agonists.

title: Considerations and challenges in microdosing of GLP-1-based receptor agonists.

title: Considerations and challenges in microdosing of GLP-1-based receptor agonists.

text: . Techniques include 'click counting' with multidose pens or extended-interval dosing
title: Considerations and challenges in microdosing of GLP-1-based receptor agonists.

text: . Early reports suggest potential benefits, including reduced nausea, improved adherence, and modest weight loss; however, high-quality clinical evidence remains limited, and safety concerns persist regarding compounded products, nonstandard dose measurement, and dosing accuracy.
title: Considerations and challenges in microdosing of GLP-1-based receptor agonists.

text: Real-world Evidence for Improvements in Inflammation and Anemia Biomarkers After the Initiation of GLP-1RA in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.. title: Real-world Evidence for Improvements in Inflammation and Anemia Biomarkers After the Initiation of GLP-1RA in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.

text: . GLP-1RAs may influence inflammatory pathways relevant to anemia, although their effects in hemodialysis patients remain unclear. Retrospective matched cohort study. Data were derived from a large US dialysis provider (Fresenius Kidney Care)
title: Real-world Evidence for Improvements in Inflammation and Anemia Biomarkers After the Initiation of GLP-1RA in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.

text: . We identified 2,468 adult patients who initiated GLP-1RA therapy between January 1, 2023, and November 1, 2024, and matched 1:1 to nonusers using propensity scores based on demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and baseline laboratory values. Initiation of GLP-1RA therapy
title: Real-world Evidence for Improvements in Inflammation and Anemia Biomarkers After the Initiation of GLP-1RA in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.

text: . Initiation of GLP-1RA therapy. Longitudinal changes over 12 months in inflammatory markers (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, white blood cell count, and albumin level) and anemia parameters (hemoglobin level, ferritin level, transferrin saturation value, erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) dose, and erythropoietin resistance index)
title: Real-world Evidence for Improvements in Inflammation and Anemia Biomarkers After the Initiation of GLP-1RA in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.

title: Real-world Evidence for Improvements in Inflammation and Anemia Biomarkers After the Initiation of GLP-1RA in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.

title: Real-world Evidence for Improvements in Inflammation and Anemia Biomarkers After the Initiation of GLP-1RA in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.

text: . Additionally, iron stores (ferritin level and transferrin saturation value) were consistently higher in the GLP-1RA group. title: Real-world Evidence for Improvements in Inflammation and Anemia Biomarkers After the Initiation of GLP-1RA in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.

text: . These findings suggest GLP-1RAs may have potential benefits in managing inflammation and inflammation-mediated anemia in kidney failure. Patients receiving hemodialysis often experience inflammation and anemia, which can make treatment more difficult and affect outcomes
title: Real-world Evidence for Improvements in Inflammation and Anemia Biomarkers After the Initiation of GLP-1RA in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.

text: . Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), commonly used for diabetes and weight management, may also have anti-inflammatory effects. title: Real-world Evidence for Improvements in Inflammation and Anemia Biomarkers After the Initiation of GLP-1RA in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis.

text: Implicit Rationing of Incretin Therapy in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Call for Deliberate Allocation.. title: Implicit Rationing of Incretin Therapy in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Call for Deliberate Allocation.

text: . Yet the patients with the best claim to these drugs are often the ones least able to obtain them. Supply and price are driven less by nephrologic risk than by a consumer market organized around elective weight loss, direct-to-consumer telehealth, and, until recently, a large compounding economy; at list price, cost-effectiveness analyses place these agents well above accepted value thresholds
title: Implicit Rationing of Incretin Therapy in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Call for Deliberate Allocation.

text: . This editorial argues that the resulting pattern of access amounts to rationing by default rather than by policy, and that nephrology has an obligation to name it and to press for allocation guided by clinical need. Whether these agents work in CKD is settled. The open question is who receives them once ability to pay, rather than risk of kidney failure, sets the order of the line
title: Implicit Rationing of Incretin Therapy in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Call for Deliberate Allocation.

text: . When access is constrained, we argue, priority should follow indication and kidney risk rather than purchasing power.
title: Implicit Rationing of Incretin Therapy in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Call for Deliberate Allocation.

text: Potential protective associations of antidiabetic and lipid-lowering therapies with retinal vein occlusion risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) shares key pathophysiological pathways with metabolic and atherothrombotic disorders
title: Potential protective associations of antidiabetic and lipid-lowering therapies with retinal vein occlusion risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . title: Potential protective associations of antidiabetic and lipid-lowering therapies with retinal vein occlusion risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Potential protective associations of antidiabetic and lipid-lowering therapies with retinal vein occlusion risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Ten good-quality studies (six cohorts and four case-control) involving over 2 million adults met eligibility criteria. Meta-analysis results suggest that statin use consistently reduced RVO risk; pooled effect odds ratio (OR) = 0.65 (95% CI = 0.53-0.79; I² = 29%) with moderate certainty
title: Potential protective associations of antidiabetic and lipid-lowering therapies with retinal vein occlusion risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Potential protective associations of antidiabetic and lipid-lowering therapies with retinal vein occlusion risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Signals of benefit for metformin and GLP-1 receptor agonists arise from single large cohorts and require independent replication. text: Estimating the carbon footprint of oral semaglutide (Rybelsus): a comparative analysis of the medicine carbon footprint model and manufacturer life-cycle assessment in pharmaceutical production.. title: Estimating the carbon footprint of oral semaglutide (Rybelsus): a comparative analysis of the medicine carbon footprint model and manufacturer life-cycle assessment in pharmaceutical production.

text: . Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly being used for the management of type 2 diabetes and people living with obesity, but their carbon impact remains poorly characterised
title: Estimating the carbon footprint of oral semaglutide (Rybelsus): a comparative analysis of the medicine carbon footprint model and manufacturer life-cycle assessment in pharmaceutical production.

text: . We aimed to compare carbon footprint estimates for oral semaglutide (Rybelsus), a peptide-based medicine, generated using the medicine carbon footprint (MCF) framework and manufacturer-reported life cycle assessment (LCA) data. Comparative methodological analysis using cradle-to-gate boundaries to compare pharmaceutical carbon footprint estimates for oral semaglutide
title: Estimating the carbon footprint of oral semaglutide (Rybelsus): a comparative analysis of the medicine carbon footprint model and manufacturer life-cycle assessment in pharmaceutical production.

text: . Per-tablet MCF estimates for 3, 7 and 14 mg Rybelsus were annualised and compared with product-specific LCA results reported by Novo Nordisk. Differences between methods were assessed descriptively across the three dose strengths. Absolute differences and symmetric percentage differences were calculated
title: Estimating the carbon footprint of oral semaglutide (Rybelsus): a comparative analysis of the medicine carbon footprint model and manufacturer life-cycle assessment in pharmaceutical production.

text: . Annualised MCF estimates were 8.9, 20.0 and 39.3 kg CO₂e/year for 3, 7 and 14 mg tablets, respectively. Corresponding EU LCA estimates were 17.0, 25.2 and 39.9 kgCO₂e/year. title: Estimating the carbon footprint of oral semaglutide (Rybelsus): a comparative analysis of the medicine carbon footprint model and manufacturer life-cycle assessment in pharmaceutical production.

text: . For oral semaglutide, MCF generated lower carbon footprint estimates than manufacturer-reported LCA values, particularly at lower doses, where fixed device/excipient and packaging emissions are proportionally larger. title: Estimating the carbon footprint of oral semaglutide (Rybelsus): a comparative analysis of the medicine carbon footprint model and manufacturer life-cycle assessment in pharmaceutical production.

text: . Improved transparency and harmonised boundaries would strengthen comparability between pharmaceutical carbon footprint estimation approaches. These findings are specific to the Rybelsus formulation of oral semaglutide and may not be generalisable to other formulations or GLP-1 RAs.
title: Estimating the carbon footprint of oral semaglutide (Rybelsus): a comparative analysis of the medicine carbon footprint model and manufacturer life-cycle assessment in pharmaceutical production.

text: Clinical outcomes associated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapy in patients with peripheral artery disease and diabetes.. Peripheral artery disease (PAD) and diabetes are associated with high risks of limb complications and mortality
title: Clinical outcomes associated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapy in patients with peripheral artery disease and diabetes.

text: . Although glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP1-RAs) improve cardiovascular outcomes, their effect on limb outcomes in PAD remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Clalit Health Services database
title: Clinical outcomes associated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapy in patients with peripheral artery disease and diabetes.

text: . title: Clinical outcomes associated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapy in patients with peripheral artery disease and diabetes.

text: . In the original IPTW-weighted analysis, GLP1-RA exposure was associated with lower risks of MALE, revascularization, major amputation, and all-cause mortality. text: Hemoglobinopathies and diabetes mellitus: from pathophysiology to clinical practice.. Hemoglobinopathies, primarily β-thalassemia and sickle cell disease (SCD), represent a major global health burden. With extended lifespans, secondary diabetes mellitus (DM) has emerged as a frequent endocrine complication
title: Hemoglobinopathies and diabetes mellitus: from pathophysiology to clinical practice.

text: . This review examines the underlying pathophysiology, diagnostic pitfalls, and therapeutic strategies for this distinct population. A narrative review was performed using PubMed database, including English full-text articles published up to July 2026
title: Hemoglobinopathies and diabetes mellitus: from pathophysiology to clinical practice.

text: . The pathogenesis of DM in hemoglobinopathies involves a duality of iron-mediated β-cell apoptosis and hemolysis-driven hepatic and peripheral insulin resistance. HbA1c is often inaccurate due to method-specific analytical interference, as well as biological distortion driven by shortened erythrocyte survival and blood transfusions
title: Hemoglobinopathies and diabetes mellitus: from pathophysiology to clinical practice.

text: . Consequently, formal screening and diagnosis must rely on plasma glucose criteria, primarily fasting plasma glucose and the oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). Meanwhile, Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) metrics serve as valuable tools for glycemic monitoring and treatment optimization
title: Hemoglobinopathies and diabetes mellitus: from pathophysiology to clinical practice.

text: . Basal-bolus insulin remains the cornerstone for DM and emerging cardiorenal protective agents (SGLT-2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists) represent promising adjuncts, while intensive iron chelation therapy can reverse early-stage dysglycemia when initiated prior to irreversible β-cell damage
title: Hemoglobinopathies and diabetes mellitus: from pathophysiology to clinical practice.

text: . Implementing dedicated, multidisciplinary specialized care centers co-led by hemoglobinopathy specialists and diabetologists is essential to optimize long-term adult outcomes.
title: Hemoglobinopathies and diabetes mellitus: from pathophysiology to clinical practice.

text: Incretin-Based Therapies: A Testable Hypothesis Linking Incretin Signaling, Mitochondrial Redox, and OXPHOS Efficiency.. title: Incretin-Based Therapies: A Testable Hypothesis Linking Incretin Signaling, Mitochondrial Redox, and OXPHOS Efficiency.

text: . A recent case of acute generalized muscle weakness in a patient with mitochondrial myopathy after tirzepatide exposure raises concerns about IBTs' potential to uncouple oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). Given the widespread use of IBTs, this inquiry is crucial due to potential adverse effects
title: Incretin-Based Therapies: A Testable Hypothesis Linking Incretin Signaling, Mitochondrial Redox, and OXPHOS Efficiency.

text: . A narrative literature review of evidence linking incretins and IBTs to mitochondrial physiology, bioenergetics, and OXPHOS was conducted. Early research on incretin physiology focused on insulin secretion in pancreatic β-cells
title: Incretin-Based Therapies: A Testable Hypothesis Linking Incretin Signaling, Mitochondrial Redox, and OXPHOS Efficiency.

text: . However, GLP-1 counteracts insulin signaling during excessive nutrient delivery by activating anti-inflammatory pathways associated with fasting, suggesting it mitigates the adverse effects of overfeeding. Preclinical studies show that IBTs activate thermogenic genes and uncoupling proteins. We have identified indirect evidence suggesting that IBTs may induce OXPHOS uncoupling
title: Incretin-Based Therapies: A Testable Hypothesis Linking Incretin Signaling, Mitochondrial Redox, and OXPHOS Efficiency.

text: . We propose a testable hypothesis that establishes a close relationship between the distinct effects of IBTs on weight loss and their direct reduction of oxidative stress. Should this hypothesis be validated, it would enhance our comprehension of the physiology underlying IBTs and the potential adverse effects on muscle.

text: GLP-1 receptor agonists and podocyte senescence in diabetic kidney disease: structural pharmacology, mechanistic evidence, and multi-receptor agonism.. Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a major cause of chronic kidney disease and kidney failure worldwide
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and podocyte senescence in diabetic kidney disease: structural pharmacology, mechanistic evidence, and multi-receptor agonism.

text: . Podocyte senescence is increasingly recognized as a contributor to diabetic glomerular injury, but its importance in human DKD and its modulation by glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) remain incompletely defined. GLP-1RAs provide clinically meaningful kidney protection beyond glucose lowering, yet the responsible cellular mechanisms remain unresolved
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and podocyte senescence in diabetic kidney disease: structural pharmacology, mechanistic evidence, and multi-receptor agonism.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and podocyte senescence in diabetic kidney disease: structural pharmacology, mechanistic evidence, and multi-receptor agonism.

text: . title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and podocyte senescence in diabetic kidney disease: structural pharmacology, mechanistic evidence, and multi-receptor agonism.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and podocyte senescence in diabetic kidney disease: structural pharmacology, mechanistic evidence, and multi-receptor agonism.

text: [New Therapeutic Approaches for MASH: Mechanisms and Clinical Promise].. In recent years, therapeutic options have expanded significantly
title: [New Therapeutic Approaches for MASH: Mechanisms and Clinical Promise].

text: . The thyroid hormone receptor-β agonist resmetirom became the first drug approved in Germany in 2025 for non-cirrhotic MASH with moderate to advanced fibrosis. In a phase 3 study, semaglutide demonstrated significant improvements in hepatic inflammation and fibrosis
title: [New Therapeutic Approaches for MASH: Mechanisms and Clinical Promise].

text: . Beyond GLP-1 analogs, which act indirectly through metabolic pathways, several liver fibrosis-specific therapies are emerging, including FGF-21 analogs and dual incretin receptor agonists (e.g. survodutide) that directly affect hepatocytes via glucagon receptor signaling. Combination therapies are increasingly being explored to harness synergistic effects and enable individualized treatment
title: [New Therapeutic Approaches for MASH: Mechanisms and Clinical Promise].

text: . Ongoing phase 3 studies assess long-term efficacy and safety. In parallel, biomarkers are being refined for patient selection and treatment monitoring. The German SLD Registry will collect patient data and clinical outcomes following the implementation of new therapies. This review summarizes recent advances and future perspectives in the pharmacological treatment of MASH
title: [New Therapeutic Approaches for MASH: Mechanisms and Clinical Promise].

text: Diabetic kidney disease within the framework of cardio-kidney-metabolic health: a paradigm shift.. Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the most common cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and kidney failure in addition to determining an elevated risk of cardiovascular (CV) disease
title: Diabetic kidney disease within the framework of cardio-kidney-metabolic health: a paradigm shift.

text: . Traditional approaches to DKD management have focused primarily on slowing kidney disease progression through improved glycemic control
title: Diabetic kidney disease within the framework of cardio-kidney-metabolic health: a paradigm shift.

text: . However, growing recognition of the complex interplay among metabolic, kidney, and CV dysfunction has led to the emergence of the cardio-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome framework, emphasizing the interconnected pathophysiology and shared risk profiles of these conditions
title: Diabetic kidney disease within the framework of cardio-kidney-metabolic health: a paradigm shift.

text: . This evolving paradigm has transformed the understanding and management of DKD from an isolated kidney disorder to a multisystem disease requiring integrated therapeutic strategies. Recent advances have significantly altered the landscape of DKD management
title: Diabetic kidney disease within the framework of cardio-kidney-metabolic health: a paradigm shift.

text: . In addition to angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers, newer therapies including sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, and non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists have demonstrated substantial kidney and CV protective effects
title: Diabetic kidney disease within the framework of cardio-kidney-metabolic health: a paradigm shift.

text: . Emerging evidence suggests that combination therapy may potentially shift the treatment paradigm from slowing CKD progression toward preservation of kidney function. In this review, we discuss DKD within the broader framework of CKM syndrome, highlighting the epidemiologic, pathophysiologic, prognostic, and therapeutic intersections among diabetes, CKD, and CV disease
title: Diabetic kidney disease within the framework of cardio-kidney-metabolic health: a paradigm shift.

text: . We summarize major therapeutic advances, review evidence supporting multidrug combination strategies, and examine current gaps between clinical evidence and real-world implementation. We further propose a phenotype-driven framework for sequencing combination therapy based on each patient's dominant pathophysiologic driver as a hypothesis-generating alternative to uniform add-on strategies
title: Diabetic kidney disease within the framework of cardio-kidney-metabolic health: a paradigm shift.

text: . Finally, we discuss the future direction of DKD management and the need for integrated multidisciplinary approaches aimed at improving outcomes.
title: Diabetic kidney disease within the framework of cardio-kidney-metabolic health: a paradigm shift.

title: Comparative Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy Among Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists: An Integrated Safety and Mechanistic Analysis.

text: . Whether this risk differs across agents and the underlying mechanisms remains unclear. title: Comparative Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy Among Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists: An Integrated Safety and Mechanistic Analysis.

text: . Real-world pharmacovigilance data from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) were used for validation. title: Comparative Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy Among Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists: An Integrated Safety and Mechanistic Analysis.

text: . Compared with non-GLP-1RA treatments, semaglutide showed the highest risk (HR = 1.538, 95% CI: 1.305-1.816), followed by liraglutide (HR = 1.251, 95% CI: 1.080-1.450)
title: Comparative Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy Among Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists: An Integrated Safety and Mechanistic Analysis.

text: . The combined strategy of network meta-analysis, pharmacovigilance, network toxicology and molecular docking provides insights into possible risk differences and potential mechanisms, and may guide future research on the safety profile of GLP-1RAs.

text: Euglycaemic ketoacidosis associated with dual-acting GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist treatment following bariatric surgery.. Euglycaemic ketoacidosis is characterised by high anion gap metabolic acidosis with elevated serum ketone bodies in the absence of significant hyperglycaemia

text: Cargo-aware design of dissolving microneedles: an FEA-guided rational framework reveals distinct delivery mechanisms for small and large molecules.. Transdermal delivery of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) such as semaglutide (SEMA, 4113 Da) could replace weekly subcutaneous injections with patient-administered patches, thereby transforming diabetes and obesity management
title: Cargo-aware design of dissolving microneedles: an FEA-guided rational framework reveals distinct delivery mechanisms for small and large molecules.

text: . Oral SEMA offers a non-injectable alternative but achieves only 0.4-1% bioavailability due to gastric degradation and limited absorption efficiency in the stomach. Dissolving microneedles (DMNs) represent an ideal transdermal platform for GLP-1RAs, however, no DMN design reported to date has achieved subcutaneous-equivalent bioavailability for a 4  kDa peptide cargo
title: Cargo-aware design of dissolving microneedles: an FEA-guided rational framework reveals distinct delivery mechanisms for small and large molecules.

text: . Here, we screened a seven-mold MN library (varying needle shape, needle length and inter-needle spacing) using finite element analysis (FEA) of mechanical and skin-penetration performance. The optimal MN-T-1000-800, with the highest insertion force and most complex trapezoidal-stack needle, achieved 90.58% relative bioavailability of SEMA - the highest reported for DMN-mediated GLP-1RA delivery
title: Cargo-aware design of dissolving microneedles: an FEA-guided rational framework reveals distinct delivery mechanisms for small and large molecules.

text: . To validate the generality of FEA framework, a 10-fold smaller cargo, rizatriptan benzoate (RIZ, 391 Da), was selected as model drug. The results showed that, unlike the macromolecule, the optimal geometry for the small molecule was MN-C-800-800, which exhibited a relative bioavailability of 465.40% compared with the commercial oral formulation
title: Cargo-aware design of dissolving microneedles: an FEA-guided rational framework reveals distinct delivery mechanisms for small and large molecules.

text: . The two optimal geometries differed fundamentally in tip sharpness, base volume, and multi-stage profile, mechanistically rationalized by geometry-cargo matching and mechanics-dissolution coupling
title: Cargo-aware design of dissolving microneedles: an FEA-guided rational framework reveals distinct delivery mechanisms for small and large molecules.

text: . We propose a cargo-aware DMN design framework that couples FEA screening with cargo-specific bioavailability validation, providing both an immediate clinical candidate for the transdermal delivery of large and small molecules and a generalizable strategy for translational DMNs development.
title: Cargo-aware design of dissolving microneedles: an FEA-guided rational framework reveals distinct delivery mechanisms for small and large molecules.

text: Central nervous system effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists: A systematic review of human neuroimaging studies.. Interest in glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) has expanded beyond obesity and diabetes, with growing preclinical and clinical evidence supporting potential applications in psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders
title: Central nervous system effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists: A systematic review of human neuroimaging studies.

text: . However, the central nervous system (CNS) mechanisms engaged by GLP-1RAs remain poorly characterized, limiting the capacity to optimize their therapeutic potential. This systematic review synthesized the literature examining GLP-1RA-related CNS effects, focusing on treatment-related neural responsivity, temporal dynamics, and modulators of CNS response
title: Central nervous system effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists: A systematic review of human neuroimaging studies.

text: . PubMed and Embase were systematically searched from inception to January 2026 for human studies across structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), task-based and resting-state functional MRI, molecular imaging, and neurophysiological approaches. Thirty-seven studies met inclusion criteria. The reviewed evidence suggests that GLP-1RAs engage distributed cortical and subcortical brain systems
title: Central nervous system effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists: A systematic review of human neuroimaging studies.

text: . Attenuation of reward-related responsivity following acute GLP-1RA administration was among the more consistent findings. Notably, evidence suggests that GLP-1RAs differentially modulate reward-related processes rather than uniformly attenuate reward function, with neural effects further varying according to metabolic status and underlying phenotype
title: Central nervous system effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists: A systematic review of human neuroimaging studies.

text: . Several studies additionally indicated that CNS effects evolve over the course of treatment, with more pronounced neural modulation during short-term treatment and diminished or altered effects following prolonged exposure
title: Central nervous system effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists: A systematic review of human neuroimaging studies.

text: . However, the current neuroimaging literature is constrained by small sample sizes and methodological heterogeneity, limiting direct comparisons across studies and underscoring the need for greater standardization
title: Central nervous system effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists: A systematic review of human neuroimaging studies.

text: . This review provides insight into the neurobiological mechanisms engaged by GLP-1RAs, identifies emerging patterns of CNS response with potential implications for mechanistically informed treatment strategies, and highlights key mechanistic considerations and priorities for future neuroimaging research.
title: Central nervous system effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists: A systematic review of human neuroimaging studies.

text: HFpEF in Asia-Clinical Characterization and Therapeutic Strategies.. Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) prevalence is increasing in Asia, driven by aging populations and rising cardiometabolic risk

text: Epigenetic determinants of GLP-1 responsiveness: Integrating dietary modulation beyond genetics.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists have become major therapeutic agents for obesity and type 2 diabetes, yet clinical responses vary substantially among individuals
title: Epigenetic determinants of GLP-1 responsiveness: Integrating dietary modulation beyond genetics.

text: . Although genetic variation contributes to this heterogeneity, it does not fully explain differences in glycemic control, body weight reduction, or broader metabolic outcomes. title: Epigenetic determinants of GLP-1 responsiveness: Integrating dietary modulation beyond genetics.

text: . Endogenous GLP-1 biology and the pharmacological targeting of incretin signaling are first summarized, followed by genetic determinants of GLP-1 responsiveness and their limitations
title: Epigenetic determinants of GLP-1 responsiveness: Integrating dietary modulation beyond genetics.

text: . Major diet-sensitive regulatory mechanisms are then examined, including one-carbon metabolism and DNA methylation, histone modification and chromatin remodeling, microbiome-derived metabolites, and RNA-mediated or epitranscriptomic regulation
title: Epigenetic determinants of GLP-1 responsiveness: Integrating dietary modulation beyond genetics.

text: . These mechanisms may influence endogenous GLP-1 secretion and degradation, GLP-1R expression, β-cell functional capacity, and the broader metabolic or inflammatory context in which incretin signaling occurs. However, direct clinical evidence linking diet-induced epigenetic changes to GLP-1R agonist therapeutic response remains limited
title: Epigenetic determinants of GLP-1 responsiveness: Integrating dietary modulation beyond genetics.

text: . Therefore, diet-epigenome interactions should be interpreted as plausible modifiers of GLP-1-related metabolic biology rather than established determinants of pharmacological efficacy
title: Epigenetic determinants of GLP-1 responsiveness: Integrating dietary modulation beyond genetics.

text: . Future studies integrating dietary assessment, gut hormone profiling, microbiome analysis, epigenomic markers, and multidimensional therapeutic outcomes are needed to determine whether diet-sensitive molecular signatures can support precision nutrition strategies alongside GLP-1-based therapy.
