title: Real-World Adherence Trajectories of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Among Adults and Paediatric Patients With Obesity.

text: . Adherence was measured as monthly proportion of days covered (PDC) over 12 months. Group-based trajectory modelling was conducted separately in adult and paediatric cohorts. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with membership in the persistent-user trajectory. The study included 201 229 adults and 1139 paediatric patients
title: Real-World Adherence Trajectories of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Among Adults and Paediatric Patients With Obesity.

text: . Five adherence trajectories were identified in each cohort. Among adults, trajectories included immediate discontinuers (19.6%), early discontinuers (23.5%), late discontinuers (20.7%), intermittent adherents (5.5%) and persistent users (30.7%), with mean annual PDC ranging from 0.10 to 0.87
title: Real-World Adherence Trajectories of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Among Adults and Paediatric Patients With Obesity.

text: . Paediatric trajectory groups were more evenly distributed, with each group representing approximately 18%-22% of the cohort and persistent users comprising 20.3%. Geographic region was consistently associated with adherence, with higher odds of persistent use in the Northeast versus the South among adults (odds ratio [OR], 1.32) and paediatric patients (OR, 1.65)
title: Real-World Adherence Trajectories of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Among Adults and Paediatric Patients With Obesity.

text: . Most adults and paediatric patients with obesity had suboptimal adherence to GLP-1 RA use over 12 months. Distinct adherence trajectories and consistent regional differences highlight opportunities to better understand and address barriers to long-term obesity pharmacotherapy.
title: Real-World Adherence Trajectories of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Among Adults and Paediatric Patients With Obesity.

text: Impact of GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists before, during, and after pregnancy: a narrative review.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP) receptor agonists (GLP-1RA and GIP-RA) are a class of medications that mimic the endogenous effects of GLP-1 and have gained increasing attention due to their substantial clinical potential
title: Impact of GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists before, during, and after pregnancy: a narrative review.

text: . Originally developed for glycemic control in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), these agents have also been widely used for obesity management and weight control
title: Impact of GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists before, during, and after pregnancy: a narrative review.

text: . A narrative literature review was conducted to summarize the main findings available regarding the use of GLP-1RAs across three distinct phases of women's reproductive trajectory: the preconception period, pregnancy, and the postpartum
title: Impact of GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists before, during, and after pregnancy: a narrative review.

text: . Owing to their metabolic and hormonal optimization effects, GLP-1RAs have additionally emerged as a therapeutic ally in the management of infertility associated with hormonal imbalance secondary to metabolic syndrome. However, the safety of these medications during pregnancy remains insufficiently established, largely due to the limited number of published studies to date
title: Impact of GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists before, during, and after pregnancy: a narrative review.

text: . Similarly, their use during the postpartum period is controversial, given the same lack of robust evidence. Overall, current data are insufficient to support routine use of GLP-1RAs and GLP-1RA/GIP-RAs during pregnancy and postpartum.
title: Impact of GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists before, during, and after pregnancy: a narrative review.

text: Do Preoperative Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Influence Lumbar Fusion Outcomes? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, but lumbar fusion-specific associations with postoperative outcomes remain uncertain
title: Do Preoperative Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Influence Lumbar Fusion Outcomes? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . To evaluate the association between preoperative GLP-1RA exposure and surgical and postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing lumbar fusion. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through 14 May 2026. Comparative studies of adults undergoing lumbar fusion with and without preoperative GLP-1RA exposure were included
title: Do Preoperative Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Influence Lumbar Fusion Outcomes? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Random-effects meta-analyses generated odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261414637)
title: Do Preoperative Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Influence Lumbar Fusion Outcomes? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Seven retrospective cohorts involving 28,525 patients were included; 6 used propensity score matching or another matching strategy
title: Do Preoperative Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Influence Lumbar Fusion Outcomes? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . No statistically significant associations were observed between preoperative GLP-1RA exposure and reoperation or revision (OR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.44-1.24;  Across the evaluated outcomes, the available observational evidence did not identify a signal of increased postoperative risk associated with preoperative GLP-1RA exposure after lumbar fusion
title: Do Preoperative Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Influence Lumbar Fusion Outcomes? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Prospective studies with standardized exposure definitions and perioperative management protocols are warranted to confirm these findings and better define their clinical implications. Current observational evidence does not establish preoperative GLP-1RA exposure alone as an independent risk factor for adverse outcomes after lumbar fusion.
title: Do Preoperative Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Influence Lumbar Fusion Outcomes? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: Effects of semaglutide on subclinical cardiovascular health in people with HIV.. Lipohypertrophy, characterized by central adipose tissue accumulation, is common in people with HIV (PWH) and contributes to cardiometabolic risk
title: Effects of semaglutide on subclinical cardiovascular health in people with HIV.

text: . In a recent randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2b trial, semaglutide significantly improved weight, total fat, visceral adiposity, blood pressure, glucose metabolism, and lipids over 32 weeks in PWH with lipohypertrophy. This prespecified secondary analysis evaluated semaglutide's effects on subclinical cardiovascular health
title: Effects of semaglutide on subclinical cardiovascular health in people with HIV.

text: . Virologically suppressed adults with HIV without known diabetes, receiving stable antiretroviral therapy, with body mass index >25 kg/m2 and increased waist circumference/waist-to-hip ratio were enrolled. Participants were randomized 1 : 1 to semaglutide or placebo for 32 weeks
title: Effects of semaglutide on subclinical cardiovascular health in people with HIV.

text: . Pulse wave velocity (PWV) and endothelial peripheral arterial tonometry (endoPAT) assessed arterial stiffness and endothelial function, and coronary artery calcium (CAC) score assessed calcified coronary atherosclerosis. Indirect calorimetry measured resting energy expenditure (REE) and oxygen consumption (VO2). 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk scores were calculated
title: Effects of semaglutide on subclinical cardiovascular health in people with HIV.

text: . Analyses followed intention-to-treat principles using sex-adjusted multiplicative regression. One hundred eight participants (n = 54 semaglutide) were enrolled (median age 53 years; 60% male; 65% non-White; 35% smokers). Semaglutide had no significant effect on PWV, CAC score, reactive hyperemia index, augmentation index, or REE. VO2 showed a downward trend (β -43 ml/min; P = 0.087)
title: Effects of semaglutide on subclinical cardiovascular health in people with HIV.

text: . At week 32, significant reductions were observed in 10-year ASCVD risk (-32.6%; P = 0.026) and hsCRP (-23.4%; P = 0.02) in the semaglutide group relative to placebo. Semaglutide did not improve subclinical vascular markers over 32 weeks but significantly improved overall cardiometabolic health and cardiovascular disease risk
title: Effects of semaglutide on subclinical cardiovascular health in people with HIV.

text: . Longer and larger studies of GLP-1 RAs are indicated in HIV to further assess their effects on long-term cardiovascular disease outcomes. NCT04019197.
title: Effects of semaglutide on subclinical cardiovascular health in people with HIV.

text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists as adjunctive therapy in refractory hypertriglyceridemia following recurrent pancreatitis.
title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists as adjunctive therapy in refractory hypertriglyceridemia following recurrent pancreatitis.

text: . A 39-year-old Chinese man was first evaluated at a multidisciplinary metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease clinic following 6 episodes of hypertriglyceridemia-induced pancreatitis over 9 years despite maximal therapy with statins, fibrates, and omega-3 fatty acids
title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists as adjunctive therapy in refractory hypertriglyceridemia following recurrent pancreatitis.

text: . Peak triglycerides reached 2329 mg/dL (Système International [SI]: 26.3 mmol/L; reference range, <177 mg/dL [SI: <2 mmol/L]). Comorbidities included poorly controlled diabetes, recurrent hypoglycemia, and steatotic liver disease with moderate fibrosis
title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists as adjunctive therapy in refractory hypertriglyceridemia following recurrent pancreatitis.

text: . Despite historical safety concerns regarding glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in prior pancreatitis, semaglutide was cautiously initiated. This achieved sustained triglyceride normalization to 213 mg/dL (SI: 2.4 mmol/L), weight loss, glycemic improvement, hypoglycemia resolution, improved liver elastography parameters, and insulin cessation without pancreatitis recurrence
title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists as adjunctive therapy in refractory hypertriglyceridemia following recurrent pancreatitis.

text: . This case demonstrates that glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists warrant consideration in treatment-resistant hypertriglyceridemia with prior pancreatitis when conventional therapy fails, challenging traditional contraindications in carefully selected patients under multidisciplinary care.
title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists as adjunctive therapy in refractory hypertriglyceridemia following recurrent pancreatitis.

text: Efficacy and safety of orforglipron 12 mg versus orforglipron 36 mg maintenance dose among patients with obesity with or without diabetes: a systematic review and comprehensive meta-analysis.. Obesity is projected to affect about one billion adults by 2030 and is associated with cardiometabolic morbidity
title: Efficacy and safety of orforglipron 12 mg versus orforglipron 36 mg maintenance dose among patients with obesity with or without diabetes: a systematic review and comprehensive meta-analysis.

text: . Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist developed to provide weight and metabolic benefits. Prior meta-analyses have supported its efficacy and safety but were limited by shorter follow-up and a predominance of non-diabetic populations
title: Efficacy and safety of orforglipron 12 mg versus orforglipron 36 mg maintenance dose among patients with obesity with or without diabetes: a systematic review and comprehensive meta-analysis.

text: . This meta-analysis aims to provide the most comprehensive head-to-head comparison between the two most commonly studied maintenance doses (12 mg vs. 36 mg), assessing weight, glycemic, cardiometabolic, and safety outcomes. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane, and Scopus until March 1, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing orforglipron 12 mg and 36 mg in obese adults
title: Efficacy and safety of orforglipron 12 mg versus orforglipron 36 mg maintenance dose among patients with obesity with or without diabetes: a systematic review and comprehensive meta-analysis.

text: . Outcomes of interest included percentage and absolute body weight change, BMI, HbA1c, waist circumference, lipid parameters, blood pressure, and adverse events. Results were pooled using a fixed-effects model, and prespecified subgroup analyses examined differences by diabetes status and treatment duration. Six RCTs (3459 participants) were included
title: Efficacy and safety of orforglipron 12 mg versus orforglipron 36 mg maintenance dose among patients with obesity with or without diabetes: a systematic review and comprehensive meta-analysis.

text: . Six RCTs (3459 participants) were included. Compared with the 12 mg dose, the 36 mg dose was associated with greater reductions in percentage body weight change (p < 0.00001), absolute body weight change (p < 0.00001), body mass index (p < 0.00001), HbA1c (p < 0.00001), waist circumference (P < 0.00001), percent change in triglycerides (P = 0.002), and systolic blood pressure (P = 0.002)
title: Efficacy and safety of orforglipron 12 mg versus orforglipron 36 mg maintenance dose among patients with obesity with or without diabetes: a systematic review and comprehensive meta-analysis.

text: . Adverse events were comparable between doses. No significant differences were observed in gastrointestinal events or pancreatic functions. A small difference in pulse rate was noted but was not considered clinically significant. In obese adults, orforglipron 36 mg improved weight and metabolic outcomes compared with 12 mg
title: Efficacy and safety of orforglipron 12 mg versus orforglipron 36 mg maintenance dose among patients with obesity with or without diabetes: a systematic review and comprehensive meta-analysis.

text: . No statistically significant differences between doses were detected for the prespecified safety outcomes, although small increases in ALT and AST were observed with the 36 mg dose and the trials included were not powered to detect rare or long-term adverse events. These findings support consideration of the higher maintenance dose when clinically appropriate
title: Efficacy and safety of orforglipron 12 mg versus orforglipron 36 mg maintenance dose among patients with obesity with or without diabetes: a systematic review and comprehensive meta-analysis.

text: . Longer-term studies are needed to confirm the benefit and cardiovascular outcomes. Not applicable.
title: Efficacy and safety of orforglipron 12 mg versus orforglipron 36 mg maintenance dose among patients with obesity with or without diabetes: a systematic review and comprehensive meta-analysis.

text: Making Modern Diabetes Medications Affordable and Accessible: Lessons From India for Other Countries.. Diabetes affects 589 million adults globally, 80% of whom live in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs)
title: Making Modern Diabetes Medications Affordable and Accessible: Lessons From India for Other Countries.

text: . Although modern diabetes therapies such as sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) improve cardiovascular and renal outcomes and analog insulins help reduce risk of hypoglycemia, affordability remains a barrier to equitable access to these agents
title: Making Modern Diabetes Medications Affordable and Accessible: Lessons From India for Other Countries.

text: . This article analyzes how India has reduced the costs of modern diabetes therapies and improved affordability, pricing trends, regulatory frameworks, pharmaceutical manufacturing policies, and public distribution initiatives in India
title: Making Modern Diabetes Medications Affordable and Accessible: Lessons From India for Other Countries.

text: . India has achieved approximately 60%-90% price reductions for SGLT2i and GLP-1 RA following patent expiry, driven by strong generic competition, structured price regulation, and governmental support, leading to much greater access to these agents. Costs of insulin biosimilars of glargine are also much lower in India, making them more affordable
title: Making Modern Diabetes Medications Affordable and Accessible: Lessons From India for Other Countries.

text: . Cross-national price comparisons show 15- to 65-fold differences between Indian generic prices and U.S. list prices for selected agents. On the policy front, government initiatives like the Ayushman Bharat have considerably helped to increase accessibility for the poor and vulnerable sections of the society
title: Making Modern Diabetes Medications Affordable and Accessible: Lessons From India for Other Countries.

text: . Despite these advances, challenges remain, particularly in rural areas where modern therapies may still be unaffordable or unavailable. Moreover, due to multiple manufacturers providing generics, there could be differences in quality and pharmacokinetics, even between the branded generics
title: Making Modern Diabetes Medications Affordable and Accessible: Lessons From India for Other Countries.

text: . However, India's experience demonstrates that affordable access to modern diabetes medicines is achievable through coordinated pharmaceutical policy, regulatory efficiency, and enhanced manufacturing capacity, offering lessons for LMICs and high-income countries facing high drug costs.
title: Making Modern Diabetes Medications Affordable and Accessible: Lessons From India for Other Countries.

text: Efficacy and Safety of Semaglutide According to Frailty Status: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SELECT Randomized Clinical Trial.. Whether frailty influences the benefit-risk balance of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) is uncertain. To evaluate whether frailty modifies the efficacy and safety of the GLP-1 RA semaglutide in adults with cardiovascular disease and overweight/obesity
title: Efficacy and Safety of Semaglutide According to Frailty Status: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SELECT Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: . In this secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, participants were adults with a body mass index of 27 or higher and established cardiovascular disease without diabetes. A 31-item frailty index (FI) was constructed using the Rockwood cumulative deficit approach; participants were categorized as not frail (FI ≤0.210), more frail (FI 0.211-0.310), and most frail (FI ≥0.311)
title: Efficacy and Safety of Semaglutide According to Frailty Status: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SELECT Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: . Semaglutide, 2.4 mg, once weekly or placebo. The primary composite outcome was cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke. Key secondary clinical outcomes, health-related quality-of-life (assessed by EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level [EQ-5D-5L] score), and safety events were additionally examined
title: Efficacy and Safety of Semaglutide According to Frailty Status: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SELECT Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: . Of 17 604 participants, the mean (SD) age was 61.6 (8.9) years; 12 732 patients (72.3%) were male and 4872 were female (27.7%). A total of 5432 patients (31%) had an FI up to 0.210, 8349 (47%) had an FI of 0.211 to 0.310, and 3823 (22%) had an FI 0.311 or higher. The incidence of the primary outcome increased with higher baseline FI
title: Efficacy and Safety of Semaglutide According to Frailty Status: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SELECT Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: . Benefits of semaglutide vs placebo on the primary outcome appeared consistent across the FI categories (hazard ratio [HR], 0.84; 95% CI, 0.65-1.07, if the FI was ≤0.210; HR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82, if the FI was 0.211-0.310; HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.76-1.10, if the FI was ≥0.311; P = .09 for interaction). Similar findings were observed when the FI was examined continuously (P = .30 for interaction)
title: Efficacy and Safety of Semaglutide According to Frailty Status: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SELECT Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: . Semaglutide additionally reduced the composite heart failure outcome (P = .82 for interaction), all-cause hospitalization (P = .71 for interaction), and all-cause mortality (P = .28 for interaction) regardless of FI category. Benefits of semaglutide on EQ-5D-5L scores appeared larger with higher FI (P = .02 for interaction)
title: Efficacy and Safety of Semaglutide According to Frailty Status: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SELECT Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: . Between baseline and week 104, FI category was more likely to improve (odds ratio [OR], 2.46; 95% CI, 1.80-3.37), and less likely to worsen (OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.34-0.65) with semaglutide vs placebo. The HRs for adverse events leading to permanent discontinuation of semaglutide vs placebo appeared lower among participants with higher baseline FI (P < .001 for interaction)
title: Efficacy and Safety of Semaglutide According to Frailty Status: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SELECT Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: . This study found that semaglutide demonstrated beneficial effects on a broad range of clinical outcomes in SELECT, without detectable heterogeneity by baseline FI. Benefits of semaglutide on health-related quality of life appeared greater with higher FI. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03574597.
title: Efficacy and Safety of Semaglutide According to Frailty Status: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SELECT Randomized Clinical Trial.

text: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Rationale, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Knowledge Gaps.. Pulmonary hypertension (PH) frequently coexists with type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), particularly in World Symposium on Pulmonary Hypertension (WSPH) Group 2 disease
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Rationale, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Knowledge Gaps.

text: . Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists improve several cardiometabolic conditions and have anti-inflammatory and vascular effects. Whether these agents directly modify pulmonary haemodynamics or clinical outcomes in PH remains unknown
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Rationale, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Knowledge Gaps.

text: . A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar from database inception through March 2026, with additional studies identified by reference-list screening. Search terms encompassed GLP-1 receptor agonists, dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists, pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary vascular remodelling, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and HFpEF
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Rationale, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Knowledge Gaps.

text: . The structured search yielded 491 unique PubMed/MEDLINE records. Of these, 189 were assessed at full-text level alongside 40 additional articles identified through reference-list screening; 67 publications were included in the final synthesis. Evidence was organized by mechanism, experimental model, WSPH group, and whether PH evidence was direct or indirect
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Rationale, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Knowledge Gaps.

text: . GLP-1 receptor expression has been demonstrated in pulmonary arterial smooth muscle in human and non-human primate tissue and in selected alveolar cell populations in rodent studies; however, available studies do not establish greater expression in pulmonary than systemic vascular smooth muscle
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Rationale, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Knowledge Gaps.

text: . GLP-1 receptor signalling modulates inflammatory, endothelial nitric oxide, endothelin-1, and mitochondrial pathways relevant to PH
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Rationale, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Knowledge Gaps.

text: . In monocrotaline- and hypoxia-induced models that primarily resemble Group 1 pre-capillary pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), liraglutide reduced right ventricular pressures or hypertrophy and pulmonary vascular remodelling, while semaglutide improved right ventricular mitochondrial and functional measures in an experimental pressure-overload model
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Rationale, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Knowledge Gaps.

text: . By contrast, available human evidence is observational or derived indirectly from HFpEF studies, involves populations likely enriched for Group 2 or unclassified PH, and lacks prespecified, catheterization-confirmed PH endpoints. Consequently, these studies do not establish that GLP-1-based therapy prevents or treats PH
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Rationale, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Knowledge Gaps.

text: . Current evidence supports a mechanistic hypothesis and a preclinical signal, not clinical efficacy in PH. Future cardiometabolic and HFpEF trials should incorporate standardized PH and right ventricular measures, and dedicated prospective studies with haemodynamic classification are required before GLP-1-based therapies can be considered for PH.
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Pulmonary Hypertension: Mechanistic Rationale, Preclinical Evidence, and Clinical Knowledge Gaps.

text: Effectiveness of GLP-1 receptor agonists to prevent obstructive sleep apnea in patients with type 2 diabetes: active comparator, new user cohort study.. Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is highly prevalent in type 2 diabetes (T2D), sharing metabolic risk factors, notably obesity, and increased cardiovascular outcomes

title: Effectiveness of GLP-1 receptor agonists to prevent obstructive sleep apnea in patients with type 2 diabetes: active comparator, new user cohort study.

text: . We conducted a population-based cohort study using the UK CPRD (2007-2023) database with an active-comparator, new-user design. Adults with T2D and BMI ≥30 kg/m² initiating a GLP-1RA or DPP-4i were included, excluding individuals with prior sleep apnea. Propensity scores with fine-stratification weighting were used within BMI strata. The primary outcome was incident clinical diagnosis of OSA
title: Effectiveness of GLP-1 receptor agonists to prevent obstructive sleep apnea in patients with type 2 diabetes: active comparator, new user cohort study.
journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

text: . Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using an as-treated approach, with up to 3 years of follow-up. The cohort included 47,315 GLP-1RAs and 159,066 DPP-4i initiators with baseline characteristics well balanced after weighting
title: Effectiveness of GLP-1 receptor agonists to prevent obstructive sleep apnea in patients with type 2 diabetes: active comparator, new user cohort study.
journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

text: . During follow-up, 612 and 1,197 incident OSA cases occurred among GLP-1RAs and DPP-4i users, yielding incidence rates of 5.8 and 5.4 per 1000 person-years, respectively. journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

text: Computable longitudinal patient journeys from structured and unstructured EHR data.. Most electronic health record (EHR) data reside in unstructured text, recorded in encounters between healthcare providers and patients
title: Computable longitudinal patient journeys from structured and unstructured EHR data.

text: . These encounters capture symptom narratives, adverse effects, treatment rationales, adherence challenges, family history and other nuances that are not coded or only partially reflected in structured fields such as diagnosis and procedures codes. Yet the majority of real-world evidence studies rely on structured data fields
title: Computable longitudinal patient journeys from structured and unstructured EHR data.

text: . Here we present a new approach that uses large, pretrained language models to accurately extract computable clinical data from unstructured EHR text. Physician adjudication confirmed high accuracy against a blinded expert reference standard, with high expert physician inter-reviewer agreement. The framework is disease-agnostic and scales to large patient datasets across all clinical conditions
title: Computable longitudinal patient journeys from structured and unstructured EHR data.

text: . The extracted clinical entities are integrated with structured EHR data, embedded with medical ontologies, and organized into a knowledge graph, allowing all relationships between variables to be interrogated at the level of individual patients or at scale
title: Computable longitudinal patient journeys from structured and unstructured EHR data.

text: . An agentic-friendly programmatic interface navigates large-scale knowledge graph data, making analyses rapid, easy and cost-effective, both for exploration and hypothesis testing. This human-guided query environment enables acceleration of labor-intensive tasks, while study design, analytic decisions and interpretation remain under investigator control
title: Computable longitudinal patient journeys from structured and unstructured EHR data.

text: . To demonstrate clinical utility, we conducted a large-scale longitudinal analysis of treatment responses among individuals initiating glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) therapy
title: Computable longitudinal patient journeys from structured and unstructured EHR data.

text: . We identify large numbers of patients initiating GLP-1 RAs with high confidence, reconstruct patient-level trajectories, and model longitudinal changes in weight and hemoglobin A1c following GLP-1 RA initiation, revealing association between these parameters and response to therapy
title: Computable longitudinal patient journeys from structured and unstructured EHR data.

text: . Further, we characterize outcomes captured only in unstructured clinical notes and show time-to-event outcomes, moving beyond fixed-timepoint end points to provide a comprehensive understanding of real-world treatment responses.
title: Computable longitudinal patient journeys from structured and unstructured EHR data.

text: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Dual Agonist Therapeutics at the Intersection of Alcohol Use Disorder, Obesity, and Cardiometabolic Dysfunction.. The co-occurrence of metabolic dysfunction and heavy alcohol consumption contributes substantially to global morbidity, particularly through its impact on liver disease progression
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Dual Agonist Therapeutics at the Intersection of Alcohol Use Disorder, Obesity, and Cardiometabolic Dysfunction.

text: . Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) agonists and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR)/GLP1R dual agonists, currently approved for the treatment of diabetes and obesity and under investigation for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, are considered for repurposing to reduce alcohol consumption and stabilize metabolic health in heavy-drinking populations
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Dual Agonist Therapeutics at the Intersection of Alcohol Use Disorder, Obesity, and Cardiometabolic Dysfunction.

text: . This review summarizes existing evidence, highlights ongoing research, and outlines key unanswered questions regarding this therapeutic potential and the paradigm shift toward metabolic circuit-based interventions in addiction treatment. The dual-target GIPR/GLP1R approach could fill a critical gap for individuals struggling with both heavy alcohol consumption and metabolic dysfunction
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Dual Agonist Therapeutics at the Intersection of Alcohol Use Disorder, Obesity, and Cardiometabolic Dysfunction.

text: . GIPR/GLP1R agonists and related incretin-based therapies, originally developed for diabetes and obesity, may have therapeutic potential for treating alcohol use disorder and alcohol-related metabolic complications. In this review, we examine shared reward, inflammatory, and gut-brain-liver pathways linking harmful alcohol use and metabolic disease
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Dual Agonist Therapeutics at the Intersection of Alcohol Use Disorder, Obesity, and Cardiometabolic Dysfunction.

text: . Although early evidence is encouraging, dedicated trials are needed to determine their safety and efficacy in alcohol-related disease.
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Dual Agonist Therapeutics at the Intersection of Alcohol Use Disorder, Obesity, and Cardiometabolic Dysfunction.

text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide are associated with reduced mortality, cardiovascular, and psychiatric risks in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa and type 2 diabetes and/or obesity: a retrospective cohort study.. Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease strongly associated with obesity and diabetes mellitus type 2 (T2D)
title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide are associated with reduced mortality, cardiovascular, and psychiatric risks in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa and type 2 diabetes and/or obesity: a retrospective cohort study.

text: . GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and tirzepatide are increasingly used for metabolic control, but their systemic effects in HS remain poorly characterized. To compare all-cause mortality, cardiovascular, rheumatologic, metabolic, psychiatric, and non-communicable inflammatory outcomes in HS patients with T2D or obesity treated with GLP-1RAs/tirzepatide vs. alternative metabolic medications
title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide are associated with reduced mortality, cardiovascular, and psychiatric risks in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa and type 2 diabetes and/or obesity: a retrospective cohort study.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide are associated with reduced mortality, cardiovascular, and psychiatric risks in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa and type 2 diabetes and/or obesity: a retrospective cohort study.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide are associated with reduced mortality, cardiovascular, and psychiatric risks in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa and type 2 diabetes and/or obesity: a retrospective cohort study.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide are associated with reduced mortality, cardiovascular, and psychiatric risks in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa and type 2 diabetes and/or obesity: a retrospective cohort study.

text: Do glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists influence cervical fusion outcomes? A systematic review and meta-analysis.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, but their procedure-specific effects in cervical fusion remain unclear
title: Do glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists influence cervical fusion outcomes? A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . A systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA 2020 and MOOSE, prospectively registered in PROSPERO, searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through April 28, 2026. Comparative studies evaluating perioperative GLP-1RA use in adults undergoing cervical fusion were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias
title: Do glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists influence cervical fusion outcomes? A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Random-effects meta-analyses were performed in Review Manager Web (RevMan Web). Certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach for clinically important outcomes. Six propensity score-matched retrospective cohort studies involving 17,310 patients were included
title: Do glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists influence cervical fusion outcomes? A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . In the primary analyses, GLP-1RA use was not associated with significant differences in pseudarthrosis (odds ratio [OR] 0.98, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.33-2.89; p = .96), dysphagia (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.38-2.05; p = .68), hospital readmission (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.39-1.17; p = .12), or device failure (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.44-1.56; p = .41)
title: Do glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists influence cervical fusion outcomes? A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Secondary outcomes were also not significantly different between groups. Perioperative GLP-1RA use was not associated with a consistent pattern of worse postoperative outcomes after cervical fusion. Prospective, procedure-specific studies with standardized exposure and outcome definitions are needed.
title: Do glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists influence cervical fusion outcomes? A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: Beyond Weight Loss: Thromboinflammation as a Candidate Mechanism for the Cardiovascular Benefit of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have emerged as an important class of medications for managing type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular outcome trials demonstrating reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) for several agents
title: Beyond Weight Loss: Thromboinflammation as a Candidate Mechanism for the Cardiovascular Benefit of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . The SELECT trial, which enrolled 17,604 participants with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity but without diabetes, showed a 20% reduction in MACEs with semaglutide compared with placebo
title: Beyond Weight Loss: Thromboinflammation as a Candidate Mechanism for the Cardiovascular Benefit of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . Importantly, mediation analyses indicated that weight loss accounted for approximately one-third of this cardiovascular benefit, suggesting that additional mechanisms contribute substantially to the observed risk reduction
title: Beyond Weight Loss: Thromboinflammation as a Candidate Mechanism for the Cardiovascular Benefit of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . The temporal dissociation between weight loss and early MACEs reduction supports the hypothesis that GLP-1RAs exert direct vascular protective effects independent of their metabolic actions
title: Beyond Weight Loss: Thromboinflammation as a Candidate Mechanism for the Cardiovascular Benefit of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . This review synthesizes current evidence on the thromboinflammatory mechanisms through which GLP-1RAs may exert their cardiovascular benefits, with particular emphasis on the neutrophil-NET axis, platelet function, and plaque stabilization
title: Beyond Weight Loss: Thromboinflammation as a Candidate Mechanism for the Cardiovascular Benefit of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: . Overall, thromboinflammation represents a biologically reasonable candidate mechanism, but its contribution to the cardiovascular benefit of GLP-1RAs treatment is an open question. Still, residual treatment effects cannot be attributed specifically to thromboinflammation, because metabolic, renal, hemodynamic, and vascular pathways, among others, may also contribute.
title: Beyond Weight Loss: Thromboinflammation as a Candidate Mechanism for the Cardiovascular Benefit of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.

text: Computer-Aided Design of Novel Acrylamido Derivatives as Potential Oral Antidiabetic Agents.. Due to the significant problem of the pharmacokinetic properties of available oral antidiabetic drugs, it is necessary to focus on developing novel oral agents
title: Computer-Aided Design of Novel Acrylamido Derivatives as Potential Oral Antidiabetic Agents.

text: . This study utilized in silico methods to design novel GLP-1 receptor agonists as potential oral antidiabetic drugs based on the most promising studies in the literature
title: Computer-Aided Design of Novel Acrylamido Derivatives as Potential Oral Antidiabetic Agents.

text: . In the framework of available studies, novel methyl (S, E)-3-(4-substitutedphenyl)-2-(3-(3,4-dichlorophenyl) acrylamido)propanoate and (E)-3-(4-(2-(3-(3,4-dichlorophenyl)acrylamido) ethyl) phenyl) propanoic acid derivatives were designed as GLP-1 agonists. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADME analysis were applied to clarify the structure-activity relationship of compounds
title: Computer-Aided Design of Novel Acrylamido Derivatives as Potential Oral Antidiabetic Agents.

text: . Compounds were evaluated against specific protein targets, including the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor, the extracellular domain of the GLP-1 receptor, the extracellular domain of the human calcium-sensing receptor, the human maltase-glucoamylase enzyme, and the human dipeptidyl peptidase IV enzyme
title: Computer-Aided Design of Novel Acrylamido Derivatives as Potential Oral Antidiabetic Agents.

text: . Despite the various results obtained on the specific molecule and target, protein-ligand interactions of compounds were found to be strongly comparable to native ligands. Compound 3 and compound 8 showed very similar binding energies compared to the native ligands against the 6X19 and 3C5T protein targets, respectively, and exhibited similar stability in a biological environment
title: Computer-Aided Design of Novel Acrylamido Derivatives as Potential Oral Antidiabetic Agents.

text: . The computational results indicated that the molecules have significant binding properties. Therefore, it would be appropriate to test compounds 3 and 8 for antidiabetic efficacy due to their strong and stable binding properties. The computatıonal results revealed that compounds 3 and 8 are potential compounds for their anti-diabetic activities.
title: Computer-Aided Design of Novel Acrylamido Derivatives as Potential Oral Antidiabetic Agents.

text: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.. Obesity is associated with substantial cardiometabolic and psychosocial morbidity
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Although randomized controlled trials demonstrate the efficacy of anti-obesity therapies, outcomes in real-world practice may be attenuated due to limited access, tolerability, adherence and insufficient long-term support
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . This narrative review aimed to synthesize real-world evidence on adherence, tolerability, access and patient satisfaction across lifestyle programmes, pharmacotherapy, metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) and endoscopic procedures, with emphasis on incretin-based medications. PubMed/MEDLINE search was conducted through July 2026
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Studies reporting real-world treatment effectiveness, adherence, persistence, discontinuation, tolerability, access or patient satisfaction in adults or adolescents with overweight or obesity were included. Randomized trials and reviews were used to contextualize real-world findings
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Intensive lifestyle interventions generally achieve approximately 5% weight loss, but attrition and weight regain after programme completion are common
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Incretin-based therapies, including semaglutide and tirzepatide, produce substantial weight loss in trials but real-world effectiveness is relatively smaller because of non-initiation, incomplete dose escalation, gastrointestinal adverse effects, treatment interruptions, and financial or insurance barriers
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Older medications demonstrate poor persistence, largely related to neurologic, psychiatric or gastrointestinal intolerance, despite lower costs for some agents. MBS provides the greatest and most durable weight loss but remains substantially underused, with racial, socioeconomic and insurance disparities
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty offers moderate, durable weight loss with low serious adverse event rates, whereas intragastric balloons are more limited by intolerance, reintervention and weight regain after removal. Real-world effectiveness is determined not only by biological efficacy but also by treatment tolerability, adherence, access and sustained support
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Proactive adverse effect management, individualized behavioural support, streamlined referral pathways and policies that improve affordability and equitable access are essential to narrowing the trial-to-practice gap. Obesity is a major global health problem affecting almost half of all adults and many young people, and it is expected to rise further by 2050
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . It is driven by changes in how we live, eat and move. Obesity increases the risk of diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease and mental health challenges such as anxiety and depression, often worsened by stigma. Managing obesity requires more than weight loss alone
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Effective care combines healthier food choices, physical activity, sleep and stress management, mental health support and attention to social factors like affordability and access to care. Lifestyle programs can lead to modest, meaningful weight loss when they provide regular feedback and support, but many people regain weight after programs end
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Medicines for weight loss, especially GLP‐1 based treatments such as semaglutide and tirzepatide, can lead to substantial weight loss in clinical trials. However, in everyday practice, fewer patients start these medicines, many stop early due to side effects (often stomach‐related during dose increases) or cost, and weight loss is typically smaller
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Older medications are cheaper but have more side effects and lower long‐term use. Metabolic and bariatric surgery and newer endoscopic procedures can produce larger and more durable weight loss, but they are underused, with clear access and equity gaps
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: . Overall, improving real‐world results will require sustained behavioural support, careful side‐effect management, better referral pathways and policies that reduce costs and expand fair access to effective treatments.
title: Real-World Evidence for Existing Anti-Obesity Therapies-The Realities of Treatment Adherence, Tolerability, Access and Patient Satisfaction.

text: Real-World Cost and Utilisation Burden of Diagnosed Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes in the United States: A Retrospective Cohort Study.. This study quantified the real-world healthcare costs and utilisation associated with diagnosed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) among adults with Type 2 diabetes (T2D)
title: Real-World Cost and Utilisation Burden of Diagnosed Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes in the United States: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . We conducted a retrospective cohort study using IQVIA PharMetrics Plus Closed Health Plan data from January 2016 to June 2025. Eligible participants were adults aged 18-64 years with T2D. MASLD was identified during the baseline period, and patients with MASLD were matched 1:1 to T2D-only controls using propensity scores
title: Real-World Cost and Utilisation Burden of Diagnosed Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes in the United States: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . The primary outcome was all-cause total direct healthcare costs over 12 months of follow-up. Adjusted cost ratios (aCRs) and average marginal effects (AMEs) were estimated using generalised linear models. The final cohort included 155 172 adults with T2D. After PS matching, 17 412 matched pairs were retained
title: Real-World Cost and Utilisation Burden of Diagnosed Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes in the United States: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . Mean total healthcare costs were $29 734 among patients with MASLD and $18 320 among matched controls. MASLD was associated with 62% higher total healthcare costs (aCR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.58-1.67), corresponding to an AME of $11 411 (95% CI, $10 725-$12 097) per patient per year
title: Real-World Cost and Utilisation Burden of Diagnosed Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes in the United States: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . In medication-defined subgroups, excess costs remained substantial among patients receiving GLP-1 receptor agonists (AME, $10 653) and SGLT2 inhibitors (AME, $13 842). MASLD was also associated with greater healthcare utilisation across all service settings. Among adults with T2D, MASLD was associated with substantially higher healthcare costs and utilisation
title: Real-World Cost and Utilisation Burden of Diagnosed Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes in the United States: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: . These findings highlight the economic burden of MASLD in this high-risk population.
title: Real-World Cost and Utilisation Burden of Diagnosed Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes in the United States: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

text: Psychiatric Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Adolescents With Obesity.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists are increasingly used for adolescent obesity, but concerns persist regarding psychiatric adverse events, particularly suicidality
title: Psychiatric Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Adolescents With Obesity.

text: . This retrospective cohort study used deidentified electronic health records from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adolescents with overweight or obesity were included. New users of semaglutide, liraglutide, or tirzepatide were compared with those receiving lifestyle interventions. Cohorts were balanced using propensity score matching
title: Psychiatric Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Adolescents With Obesity.

text: . The primary outcome was suicide-related events (suicidal ideation or suicide attempt). Secondary outcomes included suicidal ideation, suicide attempt, anxiety, insomnia, depression, and eating disorders, assessed from 30 days to 1095 days after the index date. After propensity score matching, 9222 adolescents were included in each group
title: Psychiatric Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Adolescents With Obesity.

text: . Incretin-based therapy was associated with lower risks of suicide-related events (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.57-0.95), suicidal ideation (HR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.56-0.96), and anxiety (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.84-0.99) compared with lifestyle intervention. No significant differences were observed for suicide attempt, insomnia, depression, or eating disorders
title: Psychiatric Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Adolescents With Obesity.

text: . Risk reductions were significant among female adolescents (HR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.46-0.82) and those without Type 2 diabetes (HR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.47-0.85), but not among males or those with Type 2 diabetes. Sensitivity analyses supported the primary findings
title: Psychiatric Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Adolescents With Obesity.

text: . Among adolescents with obesity, incretin-based therapy was not associated with increased psychiatric risk and was associated with lower risks of suicide-related events, suicidal ideation, and anxiety compared with lifestyle intervention
title: Psychiatric Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Adolescents With Obesity.

text: . Although a lower risk was observed compared with lifestyle intervention, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given potential selection bias and the lack of a significant difference in the active-comparator analysis with metformin.
title: Psychiatric Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Adolescents With Obesity.

text: GLP-1 receptor agonists, epigenetic aging, and the prospect of pharmacological healthspan extension.. title: GLP-1 receptor agonists, epigenetic aging, and the prospect of pharmacological healthspan extension.

text: . The convergence of these findings with a maturing body of evidence linking metabolic dysfunction to accelerated epigenetic aging has prompted renewed interest in GLP-1 RAs as candidate gerotherapeutic agents. The present review synthesizes contemporary preclinical, mechanistic, and clinical evidence relevant to this question
title: GLP-1 receptor agonists, epigenetic aging, and the prospect of pharmacological healthspan extension.

The SELECT trial demonstrated a 19% reduction in all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 0.81) in patients with obesity without diabetes, the FLOW trial demonstrated a 24% reduction in the primary kidney composite endpoint (HR 0.76), and the first randomized evidence of GLP-1 RA modulation of validated DNA methylation clocks was reported in 2025, with significant deceleration of DunedinPACE,

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists, epigenetic aging, and the prospect of pharmacological healthspan extension.

text: Cardiovascular effects of chronic GIPR and GLP-1R agonism in lean and diet-induced obese mice: sex differences and dose-dependent remodeling.. title: Cardiovascular effects of chronic GIPR and GLP-1R agonism in lean and diet-induced obese mice: sex differences and dose-dependent remodeling.
journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology

text: . Although GLP-1 receptor agonists confer cardiovascular benefits, the cardiovascular effects of GIP receptor (GIPR) stimulation remain controversial. title: Cardiovascular effects of chronic GIPR and GLP-1R agonism in lean and diet-induced obese mice: sex differences and dose-dependent remodeling.

text: Low Preoperative Free Triiodothyronine, Particularly in Females, Is Associated With Reduced Weight Loss and Diabetes Remission After Bariatric Surgery in Euthyroid Adults.. title: Low Preoperative Free Triiodothyronine, Particularly in Females, Is Associated With Reduced Weight Loss and Diabetes Remission After Bariatric Surgery in Euthyroid Adults.

text: . We investigated cross-sectional relationships between thyroid hormones and obesity-related parameters, and evaluated the predictive value of baseline thyroid hormones for weight loss (WL) and diabetes remission (DR) after bariatric surgery
title: Low Preoperative Free Triiodothyronine, Particularly in Females, Is Associated With Reduced Weight Loss and Diabetes Remission After Bariatric Surgery in Euthyroid Adults.

text: . This study included a cross-sectional cohort of 1567 euthyroid patients with overweight or obesity, of whom 1034 with complete 1 year postoperative data were included in the longitudinal analysis. Body composition was assessed using validated predictive equations and abdominal MRI
title: Low Preoperative Free Triiodothyronine, Particularly in Females, Is Associated With Reduced Weight Loss and Diabetes Remission After Bariatric Surgery in Euthyroid Adults.

text: . The primary outcomes were successful WL (total WL ≥ 25%) and DR (fasting glucose < 5.6 mmol/L and HbA1c < 6.0% without antidiabetic medications) during the 3 year follow-up. Breakpoint analysis indicated that free triiodothyronine (FT3) plateaued beyond an age threshold while showing a linear correlation with fat-free mass index
title: Low Preoperative Free Triiodothyronine, Particularly in Females, Is Associated With Reduced Weight Loss and Diabetes Remission After Bariatric Surgery in Euthyroid Adults.

text: . Higher baseline FT3 tertiles were significantly linked to increased likelihood of achieving successful WL and DR at 1 year follow-up, with stronger associations in females. Optimal FT3 thresholds were identified as 4.75 (females) and 5.05 (males) for WL, and 4.57 (females) and 5.00 (males) for DR
title: Low Preoperative Free Triiodothyronine, Particularly in Females, Is Associated With Reduced Weight Loss and Diabetes Remission After Bariatric Surgery in Euthyroid Adults.

text: . Preoperative FT3 levels below these thresholds were significantly associated with reduced WL and DR over 3 years. title: Low Preoperative Free Triiodothyronine, Particularly in Females, Is Associated With Reduced Weight Loss and Diabetes Remission After Bariatric Surgery in Euthyroid Adults.

text: . Sex-specific FT3 thresholds may aid in preoperative risk stratification and inform personalised treatment decisions in the era of expanding obesity therapeutics.
title: Low Preoperative Free Triiodothyronine, Particularly in Females, Is Associated With Reduced Weight Loss and Diabetes Remission After Bariatric Surgery in Euthyroid Adults.

text: Integrating incretin-based therapies into comprehensive obesity care: an EASO position statement.. Incretin-based therapies have transformed obesity treatment, producing substantial weight loss and benefits across cardiometabolic outcomes
title: Integrating incretin-based therapies into comprehensive obesity care: an EASO position statement.

text: . However, translating therapeutic efficacy into sustainable population-level benefit remains challenging across European healthcare systems that vary in workforce capability, multidisciplinary care, reimbursement, access, and monitoring infrastructure
title: Integrating incretin-based therapies into comprehensive obesity care: an EASO position statement.

text: . We describe this mismatch as the EASO Integration Paradox: therapeutic innovation has advanced more rapidly than the health-system structures required for its optimal, equitable, and sustainable implementation. In this EASO Position Statement, we propose the EASO Integration Framework, a model for integrating incretin-based therapies into comprehensive obesity care
title: Integrating incretin-based therapies into comprehensive obesity care: an EASO position statement.

text: . The framework is organized around five interdependent pillars: Right Patient, Right Care, Right Workforce, Right Data, and Right Access. We also outline a European research and implementation agenda focused on real-world evidence, harmonised monitoring, workforce development, pharmacovigilance, and equitable access
title: Integrating incretin-based therapies into comprehensive obesity care: an EASO position statement.

text: . The challenge is no longer whether incretin-based therapies should be used, but how they should be implemented responsibly within comprehensive obesity care pathways.
title: Integrating incretin-based therapies into comprehensive obesity care: an EASO position statement.

text: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Musculoskeletal Outcomes: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, but their effects on musculoskeletal health remain completely misunderstood
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Musculoskeletal Outcomes: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . This systematic review/meta-analysis aims to synthesise clinical data on the effects of GLP-1 RAs on key relevant bone, muscle, and joint outcomes
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Musculoskeletal Outcomes: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . MEDLINE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) (both via Ovid From 1148 potentially relevant references, 60 articles (46 RCTs, 13 RWE studies and 1 pharmacovigilance study, comprising 1,250,717 individuals) met our inclusion criteria
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Musculoskeletal Outcomes: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Different GLP-1 RAs were represented across the panel of studies, i.e., semaglutide, liraglutide, exenatide, dulaglutide, tirzepatide (dual agonist gastric inhibitory polypeptide [GIP]/GLP-1) and others. No effect on bone outcomes (i.e., bone mineral density [all sites] and fractures [all sites]) were observed when the meta-analytical models included the most adjusted effect size
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Musculoskeletal Outcomes: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Regarding muscle outcomes, a significant decrease of lean body mass/fat-free mass was consistently observed with GLP-1 RAs in the global model (k = 28, standardised mean difference [SMD] 0.52, 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.8; -0.23, I This meta-analysis is the first to investigate the effects of GLP-1 RAs on a large panel of musculoskeletal health outcomes
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Musculoskeletal Outcomes: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . While no significant effects were observed on bone- or joint-related outcomes, GLP-1 RAs were associated with reductions in lean body mass/fat-free mass, although the certainty of evidence was low and these changes appeared largely related to weight loss. Whether these changes translate into clinically meaningful impairments in muscle function or physical performance remains uncertain
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Musculoskeletal Outcomes: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Further studies in this field, including those looking at muscle function, strength or performance and using multivariate models considering confounding are needed to better reinforce the models and final findings.
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Musculoskeletal Outcomes: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: SGK2 Promotes NEDD4L-Mediated ACSL4 Ubiquitination to Inhibit Ferroptosis and Alleviate Diabetic Kidney Disease.
title: SGK2 Promotes NEDD4L-Mediated ACSL4 Ubiquitination to Inhibit Ferroptosis and Alleviate Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . Despite major advances with sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, progressive tubulointerstitial injury remains a major determinant of renal function decline in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), and the molecular regulators of ferroptotic tubular injury remain incompletely defined
title: SGK2 Promotes NEDD4L-Mediated ACSL4 Ubiquitination to Inhibit Ferroptosis and Alleviate Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . Serum/glucocorticoid-regulated kinase 2 (SGK2), predominantly expressed in renal proximal tubular cells, reportedly regulates ferroptosis in prostate cancer; however, its precise role in DKD remains underexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the role of SGK2 in tubular ferroptosis in DKD
title: SGK2 Promotes NEDD4L-Mediated ACSL4 Ubiquitination to Inhibit Ferroptosis and Alleviate Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . We identified SGK2 as a ferroptosis-related gene through integrated transcriptomic analyses, which was significantly downregulated in renal tubular cells from patients with DKD and diabetic mice. Functional experiments demonstrated that SGK2 overexpression suppressed lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis, thereby alleviating tubular injury, inflammation, and fibrosis
title: SGK2 Promotes NEDD4L-Mediated ACSL4 Ubiquitination to Inhibit Ferroptosis and Alleviate Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . Mechanistically, SGK2 promoted the association of acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) with the E3 ubiquitin ligase neural precursor cell expressed developmentally downregulated 4-like (NEDD4L) and enhanced K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of ACSL4. This study identified SGK2 as a novel negative regulator of ferroptosis in patients with DKD
title: SGK2 Promotes NEDD4L-Mediated ACSL4 Ubiquitination to Inhibit Ferroptosis and Alleviate Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . We found that SGK2 suppresses ferroptosis by promoting NEDD4L-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of ACSL4, thereby limiting lipid peroxidation and protecting the renal tubules. The SGK2-ACSL4 axis offers new insights into the molecular regulation of tubular ferroptosis
title: SGK2 Promotes NEDD4L-Mediated ACSL4 Ubiquitination to Inhibit Ferroptosis and Alleviate Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: . SGK2 suppresses tubular ferroptosis in DKD through NEDD4L-dependent K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of ACSL4. These findings suggest that SGK2 is a potential regulatory target in DKD and provide a basis for further studies on its role in disease progression.
title: SGK2 Promotes NEDD4L-Mediated ACSL4 Ubiquitination to Inhibit Ferroptosis and Alleviate Diabetic Kidney Disease.

text: Clinical Significance of Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index in Stage A/B Heart Failure Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.. Heart failure (HF) is a medical condition with a poor prognosis; therefore, it is important to consider treatment strategies from the pre-onset stage, i.e., at stage A/B HF

title: Clinical Significance of Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index in Stage A/B Heart Failure Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

title: Clinical Significance of Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index in Stage A/B Heart Failure Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

title: Clinical Significance of Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index in Stage A/B Heart Failure Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

title: Clinical Significance of Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index in Stage A/B Heart Failure Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
