title: Routine Distributional Analysis of Health Inequality Impact by Socioeconomic Group: Technical Feasibility Study in Queensland, Australia.

text: . The calculator demonstrated that all 5 interventions would reduce health inequality. Population screening for diabetes had the greatest impact on reducing health inequality of 8562 QALYs. Among the 3 treatment interventions, intensive blood pressure control had the greatest impact, with a health inequality benefit of 514 QALYs
title: Routine Distributional Analysis of Health Inequality Impact by Socioeconomic Group: Technical Feasibility Study in Queensland, Australia.

text: . Routine aggregate distributional cost-effectiveness analysis of interventions in Queensland is feasible, once standard cost-effectiveness estimates are available. The calculator for Queensland enables fast, transparent, and replicable analysis of health inequality impacts using minimal data, with visual outputs to explore trade-offs between health outcomes, inequality, and cost-effectiveness.
title: Routine Distributional Analysis of Health Inequality Impact by Socioeconomic Group: Technical Feasibility Study in Queensland, Australia.

text: Impact of Health Promotion Programs on Incarcerated Individuals in Northern Mexico.. Individuals deprived of liberty exhibit high health vulnerability due to limited access to medical services and insufficient health promotion efforts. Implementing education and self-care programs constitutes an essential strategy to improve their wellbeing
title: Impact of Health Promotion Programs on Incarcerated Individuals in Northern Mexico.

text: . The objective of this study was to evaluate changes in clinical parameters following the implementation of health promotion programs among incarcerated individuals. A prospective pre-post intervention study was conducted between February 2023 and July 2024 at the Male Social Reintegration Center No. 1 in Aquiles Serdán, Chihuahua, Mexico
title: Impact of Health Promotion Programs on Incarcerated Individuals in Northern Mexico.

text: . 1 in Aquiles Serdán, Chihuahua, Mexico. Fifteen male inmates with type 2 diabetes mellitus and arterial hypertension participated in a structured health promotion program that included educational workshops on nutrition, physical activity, and chronic disease self-management. Anthropometric and biochemical data were collected before and after the intervention
title: Impact of Health Promotion Programs on Incarcerated Individuals in Northern Mexico.

text: . Statistical analysis included paired Student's  Significant reductions were observed in blood glucose (174.1 ± 123.2 vs. 111.1 ± 57.4 mg/dL;  Health promotion programs had a positive impact on the control of chronic diseases among the incarcerated population studied
title: Impact of Health Promotion Programs on Incarcerated Individuals in Northern Mexico.

text: . These findings highlight the need to strengthen sustainable interdisciplinary strategies that uphold the right to health in prison settings.
title: Impact of Health Promotion Programs on Incarcerated Individuals in Northern Mexico.

text: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.. Stroke is the second leading cause of death globally
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . We tested whether it was feasible to deliver a community-based intervention package for prevention of stroke and, whether such an intervention would reduce stroke mortality in a rural underserved community in central India
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . In this two-arm, parallel group, open label, cluster randomised controlled trial, 64 villages were randomly assigned with 1:1 allocation to the control and the intervention arm in a demographic surveillance site. The intervention was delivered for 3.5 years
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . The intervention was delivered for 3.5 years. It included community-based screening for hypertension, diabetes and stroke among individuals ≥ 50 years of age by trained community health workers followed by village-based treatment by an outreach physician, awareness generation and active follow up
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . In the control arm, households were provided information on the ill effects of tobacco and steps to quit it. Cause of death was ascertained on all deaths using verbal autopsies by physician coders who were blinded to the treatment allocation. There were 7671 individuals in the control arm and 8255 in the intervention arm who were ≥ 50 years of age
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . In the intervention arm, out of 8255 eligible individuals, 8026 were screened and 2793 were diagnosed with hypertension, 317 with diabetes and 182 with stroke and those with these three conditions received the intervention
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . The stroke mortality rate per 100,000 person-years in the last 2.5 years of the intervention, which was the primary outcome of the trial, was comparable in the intervention (416.7) and the control arm (484.9) (adjusted hazard ration [HR] 0.84, 95 % confidence interval [0.62,1.12]; p = 0.23). Important limitations include limited access to brain imaging and lipid profile measurements
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . In this under resourced rural community in central India, a community-based intervention for stroke risk reduction did not reduce stroke mortality over the final 2.5 years of the trial. However, the trial intervention was acceptable and led to improved medication compliance, blood pressure control and awareness about stroke
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . The trial was registered at the Clinical Trials Registry of India: CTRI/2015/12/006424. Stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide, and many people do not have their risk factors such as high blood pressure and diabetes under good control. We tested if a community-based program could be delivered in a rural setting in central India and whether it could reduce deaths from stroke
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . We conducted a trial in which one group of villages received a community-based preventive program for 3.5 years, while another group did not. We then compared stroke deaths between these two groups during the last 2.5 years of the program. In the intervention villages, trained community health workers screened adults aged 50 and above for high blood pressure, diabetes, and stroke symptoms
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . Those who screened positive were examined and treated by an outreach doctor. Health workers visited homes every month to check blood pressure, ensure people took their medicines, and give advice on reducing tobacco, alcohol, and salt. After 2.5 years, stroke deaths were lower in the intervention villages, but the difference was not statistically significant
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . The program did successfully reduce blood pressure and improve stroke awareness. It did not reduce blood sugar levels or the use of tobacco or alcohol. When we looked at the full 3.5-year trial period, stroke deaths were significantly lower in the intervention villages
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . Although the reduction in stroke deaths was not significant over the last 2.5 years, the improvement in awareness and blood pressure control suggests that community-based prevention of stroke with an active role for community health workers and making treatment available in villages could be included in India’s national program for prevention and control of non-communicable diseases (NP-NCD)
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: . The main limitations of the study were the lack of access to certain tests, such as brain scans, cholesterol testing, and measurements to assess long term blood sugar control.
title: Effect of a community-based intervention for cardiovascular risk factor control on stroke mortality in rural Gadchiroli, India: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.

text: Multidomain Arterial Afterload and Left Atrial-Left Ventricular Coupling in Hypertensive Phenotypes.. Brachial blood pressure may not fully reflect the multidimensional arterial load associated with left atrial-left ventricular (LA-LV) coupling
title: Multidomain Arterial Afterload and Left Atrial-Left Ventricular Coupling in Hypertensive Phenotypes.

text: . In this cross-sectional study, we examined local carotid pulse wave velocity (PWV), cuff-derived arterial pressure-volume index (API), and arterial velocity-pulse index (AVI), separately and as a composite afterload index (ACI), in 336 inpatients (71 controls, 183 with hypertension, and 82 with hypertension and type 2 diabetes)
title: Multidomain Arterial Afterload and Left Atrial-Left Ventricular Coupling in Hypertensive Phenotypes.

text: . Covariate-adjusted linear models related standardized exposures to the left atrial stiffness index (LASI) and LA-LV coupling index (LACI). Greater ACI was associated with higher LACI (β = 0.0142 per 1-SD, 95% CI 0.0011-0.0273; p = 0.033). The LASI estimate was directionally similar but less precise (β = 0.0232, 95% CI -0.0024-0.0488; p = 0.076), and all single-domain CIs included zero
title: Multidomain Arterial Afterload and Left Atrial-Left Ventricular Coupling in Hypertensive Phenotypes.

text: . These findings support further evaluation of accessible multidomain vascular assessment as a complement to brachial blood pressure. External calibration and longitudinal validation are needed to establish the clinical value of ACI.
title: Multidomain Arterial Afterload and Left Atrial-Left Ventricular Coupling in Hypertensive Phenotypes.

text: Blood Pressure Phenotypes in Patients Recently Diagnosed With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Matched Controls: A Study in Urban Mozambique.. Accurate characterization of blood pressure (BP) phenotypes is essential for cardiovascular risk assessment, particularly among type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients
title: Blood Pressure Phenotypes in Patients Recently Diagnosed With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Matched Controls: A Study in Urban Mozambique.

text: . We aimed to evaluate the prevalence of different BP phenotypes using multiple BP assessment methods, in Black Africans, with and without T2DM
title: Blood Pressure Phenotypes in Patients Recently Diagnosed With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Matched Controls: A Study in Urban Mozambique.

text: . Recently diagnosed T2DM patients (n = 151) and age- and sex- matched controls (1:1) without T2DM had their BP assessed using standard office BP measurement (OBPM), unattended automated office BP measurement (u-AOBP), 24 h ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM), and home BP monitoring (HBPM)
title: Blood Pressure Phenotypes in Patients Recently Diagnosed With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Matched Controls: A Study in Urban Mozambique.

text: . Four BP phenotypes were defined, combining OBPM with each of the remaining methods: normotension, white-coat, masked, and sustained hypertension. Using OBPM + ABPM, T2DM patients were less often classified as normotensive (32.5% vs. 48.3%) and more often as having masked hypertension (23.2% vs. 9.9%) than controls (p = 0.004)
title: Blood Pressure Phenotypes in Patients Recently Diagnosed With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Matched Controls: A Study in Urban Mozambique.

text: . 9.9%) than controls (p = 0.004). Both OBPM + HBPM and OBPM + u-AOBP underestimated masked hypertension and overestimated with-coat hypertension
title: Blood Pressure Phenotypes in Patients Recently Diagnosed With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Matched Controls: A Study in Urban Mozambique.

text: . When compared with OBPM + ABPM, concordance in the classification of participants into four phenotypes (κ, 95%CI) was higher for OBPM + HBPM (T2DM: 0.62, 0.52 - 0.71; controls: 0.70, 0.60-0.80) than for OBPM + u-AOBP (T2DM: 0.51, 0.40-0.61; controls: 0.61, 0.50-0.72) and lower among participants with T2DM
title: Blood Pressure Phenotypes in Patients Recently Diagnosed With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Matched Controls: A Study in Urban Mozambique.

text: . Recently diagnosed T2DM patients showed a higher prevalence of masked hypertension than participants without T2DM. When combined with OBPM, HBPM and u-AOBP failed to identify a large proportion of patients with masked hypertension and overestimated white-coat hypertensions, highlighting the need to incorporate ABPM into evaluation protocols.
title: Blood Pressure Phenotypes in Patients Recently Diagnosed With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Matched Controls: A Study in Urban Mozambique.

text: Impact of aquatic versus land exercise on glycated hemoglobin and blood pressure in older adults with multimorbidity: A randomized controlled trial protocol.. Multimorbidity is defined as the presence of two or more chronic conditions in the same individual, being a growing global health concern, particularly among older adults
title: Impact of aquatic versus land exercise on glycated hemoglobin and blood pressure in older adults with multimorbidity: A randomized controlled trial protocol.

text: . This condition is associated with decreased quality of life, increased healthcare utilization, and functional decline. Although physical exercise is widely recommended for managing chronic diseases, such as hypertension and type 2 diabetes, evidence remains limited regarding the most effective exercise modality for individuals with multimorbidity
title: Impact of aquatic versus land exercise on glycated hemoglobin and blood pressure in older adults with multimorbidity: A randomized controlled trial protocol.

text: . This study protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial designed to compare the effects of water-based and land-based exercise programs on glycated hemoglobin and blood pressure in older adults with multiple chronic conditions. This protocol describes a single center, randomized controlled trial with stratified allocation based on comorbidity burden
title: Impact of aquatic versus land exercise on glycated hemoglobin and blood pressure in older adults with multimorbidity: A randomized controlled trial protocol.

text: . A minimum of 42 participants aged 60 years or older, diagnosed with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus plus other chronic conditions (i.e. obesity, dyslipidemias, depression/anxiety or osteoarthritis) will be recruited. Participants will be randomly assigned to a water exercise, land exercise, or a control group
title: Impact of aquatic versus land exercise on glycated hemoglobin and blood pressure in older adults with multimorbidity: A randomized controlled trial protocol.

text: . The intervention groups will engage in supervised exercise sessions three times per week for 10 weeks, combining aerobic and resistance training
title: Impact of aquatic versus land exercise on glycated hemoglobin and blood pressure in older adults with multimorbidity: A randomized controlled trial protocol.

text: . Primary outcomes include glycated hemoglobin and systolic blood pressure, whereas secondary outcomes include heart rate variability, lipid profile, spirometry, physical function, anthropometry, and patient-reported outcomes on quality of life, physical activity, sleep quality, and psychological health
title: Impact of aquatic versus land exercise on glycated hemoglobin and blood pressure in older adults with multimorbidity: A randomized controlled trial protocol.

text: . Assessments will be conducted before and after the intervention following standardized procedures. This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06879639).
title: Impact of aquatic versus land exercise on glycated hemoglobin and blood pressure in older adults with multimorbidity: A randomized controlled trial protocol.

text: Primary hyperaldosteronism in patient with Bardet-Biedl syndrome: unmasking secondary hypertension.. Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS) is a rare autosomal recessive ciliopathy characterized by marked clinical and genetic heterogeneity, classically presenting with retinal dystrophy, obesity, polydactyly, renal dysfunction, and hypogonadism
title: Primary hyperaldosteronism in patient with Bardet-Biedl syndrome: unmasking secondary hypertension.

text: . Although arterial hypertension is frequently observed in affected individuals, it is not currently included in diagnostic criteria and remains insufficiently studied. We report the case of a 35-year-old man with clinically diagnosed BBS who developed severe, treatment-resistant hypertension and hypokalaemia
title: Primary hyperaldosteronism in patient with Bardet-Biedl syndrome: unmasking secondary hypertension.

text: . A comprehensive endocrine evaluation revealed primary hyperaldosteronism, confirmed by an elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio, saline suppression testing, and imaging evidence of a unilateral adrenal adenoma. Laparoscopic adrenalectomy resulted in normalization of potassium levels and a significant improvement in blood pressure control
title: Primary hyperaldosteronism in patient with Bardet-Biedl syndrome: unmasking secondary hypertension.

text: . This case illustrates the complex interplay between BBS-related renal, metabolic, and neuroendocrine dysfunction and secondary endocrine causes of hypertension. Existing evidence suggests that BBSome dysfunction may be associated with alterations in metabolic and cardiovascular regulation; however, its relationship with aldosterone-producing adenomas remains uncertain
title: Primary hyperaldosteronism in patient with Bardet-Biedl syndrome: unmasking secondary hypertension.

text: . The coexistence of BBS and primary aldosteronism may be coincidental; however, shared molecular pathways cannot be excluded. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of primary aldosteronism caused by an aldosterone-producing adrenal adenoma in a patient with BBS
title: Primary hyperaldosteronism in patient with Bardet-Biedl syndrome: unmasking secondary hypertension.

text: . This report highlights the importance of a thorough evaluation for secondary hypertension in BBS patients and underscores the need for further research into the pathophysiological links between ciliopathies and endocrine hypertension.
title: Primary hyperaldosteronism in patient with Bardet-Biedl syndrome: unmasking secondary hypertension.

text: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.. The drivers of mortality and their associated risk factors evolve throughout the course of life. Understanding these transitions is essential for effective, equitable, and age-appropriate health interventions
title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . As part of the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023, we examined life expectancy and the probability of death from birth to age 70 years (70q0) from 1990 to 2023 for each Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member state. In addition, we assessed causes of death and risk factor by age and sex across different life stages
title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Life expectancy was estimated from age-specific mortality rates with standard demographic techniques, and 70q0 from mortality and GBD life tables. Cause-specific mortality was estimated using the Cause of Death Ensemble model, and risk-attributable mortality using the comparative risk assessment framework
title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . In 2023, regional life expectancy was 70·1 years (95% uncertainty interval 69·6-70·7) for males and 76·2 years (75·7-76·7) for females, ranging from 87·5 years (87·3-87·8) for females in Singapore to 62·1 years (60·8-63·5) for males in Myanmar. Correspondingly, all-cause 70q0 was higher for males than for females
title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Neonatal disorders were the leading cause of mortality among infants younger than 1 year
title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Road injuries were the primary driver of mortality among males from adolescence through to early adulthood, accounting for 25·0% (17·0-31·0) of total mortality (8230 [5740-10 800] deaths) in males aged 15-19 years, with mortality rates varying from 3·0 per 100 000 population (2·3-3·7) to 49·0 per 100 000 population (25·0-67·1) between countries
title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Among females, maternal disorders were the leading cause of death in ages 25-34 years. In mid-adulthood, non-communicable diseases such as ischaemic heart disease and stroke emerged as major causes. Tobacco use was the dominant risk factor across most of adulthood in males, whereas high blood pressure was the prevailing risk factor among adult females
title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Although the leading causes of death have converged across countries, the outcomes of these causes remain divergent, reflecting persistent inequalities across the region. These patterns present a strategic opportunity for multilateral action to mobilise collective resources and achieve regional health equity. Gates Foundation.
title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: Integrating World Health Organization Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions at Primary Health Care - An Impact Evaluation Study from a Mountainous State of India.. Noncommunicable diseases are the leading cause of death globally. This single-arm interventional (pretest-posttest) study was conducted in one rural and one tribal district of Himachal Pradesh
title: Integrating World Health Organization Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions at Primary Health Care - An Impact Evaluation Study from a Mountainous State of India.

text: . Persons with NCDs (cardiovascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes mellitus) reporting to outpatient departments were enrolled. Components of the World Health Organization Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease (WHO-PEN) protocols 1 and 2 were used
title: Integrating World Health Organization Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions at Primary Health Care - An Impact Evaluation Study from a Mountainous State of India.

text: . Nonphysician health workers managed NCD patients, providing individualized counseling on behavioral risk factors of major NCDs. The counselling was conducted at baseline, three months, and six months from enrolment, using brief interventions based on the "5As" and "5Rs" models. Follow-up was done at baseline, three months, six months, and 12 months postenrollment to assess outcomes
title: Integrating World Health Organization Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions at Primary Health Care - An Impact Evaluation Study from a Mountainous State of India.

text: . Change of 10-year risk of developing cardiovascular disease (CVD) using the WHO/International Society of Hypertension risk-assessment charts for SEAR and changes in behavioral and biological risk factors were compared to the baseline after one year of behavioral change intervention
title: Integrating World Health Organization Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions at Primary Health Care - An Impact Evaluation Study from a Mountainous State of India.

text: . The 10-year CVD risk ≥20% decreased significantly from 17.9% at enrolment to 5.4% after one year of behavioral interventions. Significant improvements were seen in blood pressure, blood sugar control, and behavioral risk factors. Implementing the WHO-PEN protocols is feasible for managing NCDs at the primary healthcare level
title: Integrating World Health Organization Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions at Primary Health Care - An Impact Evaluation Study from a Mountainous State of India.

text: . Involving a health worker or counselor is essential for initiating and sustaining healthy behaviors and ensuring the individual's treatment compliance.
title: Integrating World Health Organization Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions at Primary Health Care - An Impact Evaluation Study from a Mountainous State of India.

text: Assessing 5-Year Outcomes of a Teamlet Care Model in Singapore Polyclinics: A Matched Difference-in-Difference Analysis.. A novel teamlet (small team) care model was introduced in 2014 within Singapore polyclinics to improve care continuity and comprehensiveness for patients with chronic disease
title: Assessing 5-Year Outcomes of a Teamlet Care Model in Singapore Polyclinics: A Matched Difference-in-Difference Analysis.

text: . Patients were enrolled in smaller teams comprising 2 family physicians, 1 nurse, and 1 care coordinator for coordinated team-based care. This study assessed 5-year outcomes focusing on clinical parameters, care adherence, health care utilization, and economic impact
title: Assessing 5-Year Outcomes of a Teamlet Care Model in Singapore Polyclinics: A Matched Difference-in-Difference Analysis.

text: . We conducted a retrospective matched cohort study of patients with diabetes, hypertension, or hyperlipidemia enrolled in the teamlet program from 2014 to 2016. Outcomes were compared with matched control patients receiving usual care. We analyzed data from Singapore's Ministry of Health databases using difference-in-differences analysis, controlling for individual and cohort-time fixed effects
title: Assessing 5-Year Outcomes of a Teamlet Care Model in Singapore Polyclinics: A Matched Difference-in-Difference Analysis.

text: . The teamlet model achieved modest clinical improvements; glycated hemoglobin decreased by 0.1% for subgroups with nonincreasing HbA Restructuring polyclinic workforces into smaller collaborative teams improved care processes and decreased high-cost health care utilization
title: Assessing 5-Year Outcomes of a Teamlet Care Model in Singapore Polyclinics: A Matched Difference-in-Difference Analysis.

text: . These findings suggest that scaling team-based care models in high-volume primary care settings might improve overall health care system efficiency and costs.Abstracts available in: يبرع (Arabic), (Chinese), Francais (French), Deutsch (German),हिन्दी (Hindi), Indonesian (Indonesian), (Japanese), Portugues (Portuguese), and Español (Spanish).

text: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.. The rapid rise in the burden of non-communicable disease (NCDs) in African communities has resulted in a considerable mortality, disability, and economic burden
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . A comprehensive evaluation of incidence, deaths, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and attributable risk factors related to NCDs by sex, and geographical location is essential for informing policy decisions aimed at controlling these diseases
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . This study used a comprehensive analysis based on the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 methodology to estimate the incidence, mortality, DALYs (estimated as the sum of years of life lost and years lived with disability [YLDs]), and attributable risk factors of NCDs in Africa
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Data were systematically searched for and extracted from various sources, including vital registration, verbal autopsy, surveillance systems, police reports, censuses, surveys, minimally invasive tissue sampling, and sibling history
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . The analysis employed the Cause of Death Ensemble model, DisMod-MR 2.1, and spatiotemporal Gaussian process regression to estimate both fatal and non-fatal health metrics associated with NCDs in Africa overall, and by region and country
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . In 2023, NCDs in Africa accounted for an estimated 2·33 billion (95% uncertainty interval 2·22-2·50) incident cases, 4·70 million (4·47-4·93) deaths, and 263 million (234-293) DALYs
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Although absolute numbers increased between 1990 and 2023, age-standardised rates (per 100 000 population) decreased modestly: incidence rate by 2·7% (0·2-5·0), mortality rate by 9·0% (2·5-15·5), and DALY rate by 6·4% (1·2-12·0)
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . The five leading Level 3 causes of death in Africa in 2023 were ischaemic heart disease (801 000 [653 000-965 000]), stroke (700 000 [544 000-863 000]), chronic kidney disease (293 000 [224 000-359 000], hypertensive heart disease (246 000 [170 000-337 000]), and diabetes (245 000 [190 000-314 000]) for all sexes and ages
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Leading Level 2 causes of YLDs were mental disorders (30·9 million [22·0-42·2]) and musculoskeletal disorders (17·1 million [12·5-22·7]). Overall, 35·1% (32·4-38·2) of DALYs and 57·4% (54·2-60·4) of deaths due to NCDs were attributable to the 88 GBD 2023 risk factors
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . High systolic blood pressure contributed the largest proportion at 26·2% (21·6-30·9) of all NCD deaths in Africa, followed by dietary risks (14·7% [5·1-21·6]) and air pollution (14·2% [11·6-16·9])
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . Our findings underscore the complex and evolving nature of the NCD burden in Africa, where modest declines in age-standardised mortality and DALY rates since 1990 have been substantially offset by rising absolute counts of deaths and DALYs-a paradox driven predominantly by rapid population growth and demographic changes
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: . That more than half of all NCD deaths and over a third of DALYs remain attributable to modifiable risk factors-principally high systolic blood pressure, dietary risks, and air pollution-suggests that a substantial and actionable proportion of this burden is preventable through available and effective interventions, carrying urgent implications for African governments, ministries of health, and
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: African governments, ministries of health, and global health partners, who must take decisive action to meet health commitments
title: Burden of non-communicable diseases and their attributable risk factors in Africa from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

text: Cascade of care for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension in rural Bangladesh: sub-regional mapping of gaps in care.. Bangladesh has a high burden of type two diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and hypertension. To better target non-communicable disease (NCD) programmes, populations with unmet care needs must be identified
title: Cascade of care for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension in rural Bangladesh: sub-regional mapping of gaps in care.

text: . We describe the unmet care needs for people living with T2DM and hypertension in rural Bangladesh at a subregional level. We conducted a secondary analysis of cross-sectional surveys conducted in 2021 and 2022 in Alfadanga Upazila, Faridpur District
title: Cascade of care for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension in rural Bangladesh: sub-regional mapping of gaps in care.

text: . Surveys were conducted among random samples of non-pregnant adults aged >30 years, including questions about demographics, NCD diagnoses, care-seeking and treatment. Study staff conducted blood pressure measurements to determine hypertension and 2-hour oral glucose tolerance tests to determine T2DM status
title: Cascade of care for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension in rural Bangladesh: sub-regional mapping of gaps in care.

text: . We calculated the prevalence of T2DM and hypertension and the unmet need for care, defined as the prevalence minus the proportion screened (T2DM only), diagnosed, treated and controlled, following the cascade of care (COC). We present the COC for 12 subregional geographical clusters and sex. 1982 participants (62.9% women) were analysed
title: Cascade of care for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension in rural Bangladesh: sub-regional mapping of gaps in care.

text: . 1982 participants (62.9% women) were analysed. The prevalence of T2DM was 19.0%, and the unmet need for care was 90.7%. The prevalence of hypertension was 37.9%, and the unmet need for care was 81.4%
title: Cascade of care for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension in rural Bangladesh: sub-regional mapping of gaps in care.

text: . For both T2DM and hypertension, women had a higher prevalence of disease, but there was a wider gap in the COC for hypertension, with 22.4% of women achieving good control compared with 10.9% of men. At the subregional level, the prevalence of T2DM ranged from 12.4% to 26.5%, and the unmet need for care from 85.0% to 95.6%
title: Cascade of care for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension in rural Bangladesh: sub-regional mapping of gaps in care.

text: . Variations in the prevalence and unmet need for care were also seen for hypertension but with different subregional distribution patterns. In this rural Bangladesh setting, the unmet care need was high for T2DM and hypertension, with subregional and sex differences. Understanding hyper-local factors driving NCD risks and access to care could support more effective programme delivery.
title: Cascade of care for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension in rural Bangladesh: sub-regional mapping of gaps in care.

text: Factors associated with poor cardiometabolic control in patients with type 2 diabetes: a Lasso-Firth penalized regression analysis.. title: Factors associated with poor cardiometabolic control in patients with type 2 diabetes: a Lasso-Firth penalized regression analysis.

title: Factors associated with poor cardiometabolic control in patients with type 2 diabetes: a Lasso-Firth penalized regression analysis.

title: Factors associated with poor cardiometabolic control in patients with type 2 diabetes: a Lasso-Firth penalized regression analysis.

title: Factors associated with poor cardiometabolic control in patients with type 2 diabetes: a Lasso-Firth penalized regression analysis.

title: Factors associated with poor cardiometabolic control in patients with type 2 diabetes: a Lasso-Firth penalized regression analysis.

text: . These exploratory findings require validation in independent cohorts. Cardiometabolic control among patients with T2DM in Shanxi Province remains suboptimal
title: Factors associated with poor cardiometabolic control in patients with type 2 diabetes: a Lasso-Firth penalized regression analysis.

text: . Exploratory analyses suggest that BMI, education level, and knowledge score are the variables most robustly associated with poor cardiometabolic control, whereas practice score, hypertension history, and T2DM duration represent additional, weaker candidate associations warranting further investigation
title: Factors associated with poor cardiometabolic control in patients with type 2 diabetes: a Lasso-Firth penalized regression analysis.

text: . These findings may inform future diabetes self-management education and intervention strategies aimed at improving glycemic, blood pressure, and lipid control. text: Calcium Channel Blockers are Safe and Beneficial in Patients with Heart Failure and Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.. Heart failure and advanced chronic kidney disease frequently coexist and are associated with high mortality and limited therapeutic options. Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) are commonly used for blood pressure control in this population
title: Calcium Channel Blockers are Safe and Beneficial in Patients with Heart Failure and Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.

text: . However, their effect on survival in patients with heart failure and advanced chronic kidney disease is uncertain. We evaluated the association between CCBs use and all-cause mortality in patients with heart failure and advanced chronic kidney disease
title: Calcium Channel Blockers are Safe and Beneficial in Patients with Heart Failure and Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.

text: . This retrospective cohort study included 1,835 consecutive patients with heart failure and advanced chronic kidney disease (GFR ≤30 mL/min/1.73 m²) treated between January 2014 and October 2025 at a national tertiary referral center. Patients were stratified by baseline CCBs use. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, obtained from a national registry
title: Calcium Channel Blockers are Safe and Beneficial in Patients with Heart Failure and Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.

text: . Multivariable Cox regression and inverse probability treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for confounders. Subgroup analyses were performed across heart failure phenotypes and key comorbidities. Of the cohort, 988 (53.8%) received CCBs therapy (45% dihydropyridine). Over a median follow-up of 1.68 years, 69.7% of patients died
title: Calcium Channel Blockers are Safe and Beneficial in Patients with Heart Failure and Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.

text: . CCBs use was associated with lower mortality in unadjusted (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.74-0.93; p=0.001) and IPTW-adjusted analyses (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-0.99; p=0.038). Findings were consistent across heart failure phenotypes, diabetes, and hypertension subgroups
title: Calcium Channel Blockers are Safe and Beneficial in Patients with Heart Failure and Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.

text: . In subclass analyses, non-dihydropyridine CCBs were associated with a significant reduction in mortality, whereas the association with dihydropyridine agents did not reach statistical significance
title: Calcium Channel Blockers are Safe and Beneficial in Patients with Heart Failure and Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.

text: . In patients with heart failure and advanced chronic kidney disease, CCBs use was associated with improved survival, supporting their potential role as a safe adjunctive therapy for blood pressure control in this high-risk population.
title: Calcium Channel Blockers are Safe and Beneficial in Patients with Heart Failure and Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.

text: Increased risk of steatotic liver disease, major adverse liver outcomes, cardiovascular events, and mortality in pheochromocytoma: a model of chronically elevated sympathetic tone.. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease globally, yet the contribution of autonomic dysfunction to its progression remains incompletely understood
title: Increased risk of steatotic liver disease, major adverse liver outcomes, cardiovascular events, and mortality in pheochromocytoma: a model of chronically elevated sympathetic tone.

text: . Pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL), characterized by excessive catecholamine production, provide a human model to investigate the impact of chronic sympathetic activation on MASLD and major adverse liver outcomes (MALO)
title: Increased risk of steatotic liver disease, major adverse liver outcomes, cardiovascular events, and mortality in pheochromocytoma: a model of chronically elevated sympathetic tone.

text: . We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from the TriNetX Network, including adults with PPGL (exposure) and essential hypertension (controls), defined using ICD-10 codes/anthropometry. Cohorts were propensity score matched (1:1) for demographic, metabolic, and blood pressure-related variables and followed for 5 years from index diagnosis
title: Increased risk of steatotic liver disease, major adverse liver outcomes, cardiovascular events, and mortality in pheochromocytoma: a model of chronically elevated sympathetic tone.

text: . The primary outcome was time to incident MASLD. Secondary outcomes included MALO, type 2 diabetes (T2D), major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and all-cause mortality. Survival analysis generated hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). After matching, 45 595 patients were included in each arm
title: Increased risk of steatotic liver disease, major adverse liver outcomes, cardiovascular events, and mortality in pheochromocytoma: a model of chronically elevated sympathetic tone.

text: . PPGL was associated with increased risk of incident MASLD (HR 1.48; 95% CI 1.38-1.58) and MALO (HR 1.59; 1.44-1.76), including hepatic decompensation (HR 1.73; 1.53-1.95) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HR 2.18; 1.70-2.80), compared with essential hypertension. A modest increase in MACE was observed (HR 1.13; 1.09-1.16), while incident T2D risk was not significantly different (HR 1.02; 0.98-1.06)
title: Increased risk of steatotic liver disease, major adverse liver outcomes, cardiovascular events, and mortality in pheochromocytoma: a model of chronically elevated sympathetic tone.

text: . Pheochromocytoma and PPGL treated with α-adrenergic blockade demonstrated greatest cardiometabolic risk. PPGL was associated with increased risk of MASLD, progressive liver complications, MACE, and mortality, supporting a link between chronic catecholamine excess and adverse hepatic outcomes
title: Increased risk of steatotic liver disease, major adverse liver outcomes, cardiovascular events, and mortality in pheochromocytoma: a model of chronically elevated sympathetic tone.

text: . These findings provide human evidence that sustained sympathetic overactivity may contribute to hepatic steatosis and progression.
title: Increased risk of steatotic liver disease, major adverse liver outcomes, cardiovascular events, and mortality in pheochromocytoma: a model of chronically elevated sympathetic tone.

text: Serum N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide and Phosphodiesterase 4D Levels in Adults With Overt Hypothyroidism: A Case-Control Study.. Thyroid hormone regulates cardiac and vascular function, and overt hypothyroidism predisposes to impaired ventricular relaxation, raised systemic vascular resistance, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
title: Serum N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide and Phosphodiesterase 4D Levels in Adults With Overt Hypothyroidism: A Case-Control Study.

text: . N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a sensitive marker of myocardial wall stress and is itself under thyroid-hormone control, while cyclic-nucleotide phosphodiesterases (PDEs) shape the intracellular signalling that underlies myocardial contractility. The two have rarely been measured together in adults with overt hypothyroidism and seldom in India
title: Serum N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide and Phosphodiesterase 4D Levels in Adults With Overt Hypothyroidism: A Case-Control Study.

text: . We compared serum NT-proBNP and phosphodiesterase 4D (PDE4D), a cAMP-specific isoform, between adults with overt hypothyroidism and euthyroid controls. This hospital-based case-control study at a tertiary-care teaching hospital in north India was conducted with institutional ethics committee approval and written informed consent
title: Serum N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide and Phosphodiesterase 4D Levels in Adults With Overt Hypothyroidism: A Case-Control Study.

text: . We enrolled 80 adults (older than 20 years) in equal, age- and sex-matched overt hypothyroid and euthyroid groups (40 each). Blinded personnel measured serum triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxine (T4), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and NT-proBNP by chemiluminescent immunoassay and serum PDE4D by a sandwich enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
title: Serum N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide and Phosphodiesterase 4D Levels in Adults With Overt Hypothyroidism: A Case-Control Study.

text: . Groups were compared with the independent-samples t-test or Mann-Whitney U test and the chi-square or Fisher's exact test, alongside univariable logistic regression and effect-size analysis (point-biserial r, Cramer's V); p < 0.05 was taken as significant. The groups matched closely for age (p = 0.617) and sex (72.5% female in each)
title: Serum N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide and Phosphodiesterase 4D Levels in Adults With Overt Hypothyroidism: A Case-Control Study.

text: . Serum NT-proBNP ran about fourfold higher in the hypothyroid group (927.10 ± 487.47 vs 233.32 ± 126.12 pg/mL; p < 0.001; r = 0.70), while serum PDE4D ran about twofold lower (19.0 ± 5.9 vs 38.7 ± 9.7 ng/mL; p < 0.001; r = 0.78); PDE4D gave the highest Nagelkerke R² of any variable studied (0.884). The two markers thus moved in opposite directions
title: Serum N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide and Phosphodiesterase 4D Levels in Adults With Overt Hypothyroidism: A Case-Control Study.

text: . The hypothyroid group also carried higher BMI and blood pressure and more hypertension (35% vs 10%) and peripheral oedema (45% vs 20%). In adults with long-standing overt hypothyroidism, serum NT-proBNP was markedly higher and serum PDE4D markedly lower than in euthyroid controls, a reciprocal pattern set against raised blood pressure, BMI, and hypertension
title: Serum N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide and Phosphodiesterase 4D Levels in Adults With Overt Hypothyroidism: A Case-Control Study.

text: . Cardiovascular surveillance in overt hypothyroidism may therefore be worthwhile, and serum PDE4D emerges as a promising, hypothesis-generating candidate marker that still needs prospective, multivariable-adjusted validation.
title: Serum N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide and Phosphodiesterase 4D Levels in Adults With Overt Hypothyroidism: A Case-Control Study.

text: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.. Clinical inertia, defined as the failure to initiate or intensify therapy when clinically indicated, represents a major and under-addressed barrier to achieving cardiovascular risk (CVR) factor control in primary care
title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

text: . Despite the availability of evidence-based guidelines and effective pharmacological treatments, many patients with uncontrolled hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidaemia do not receive appropriate treatment intensification
title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

text: . We aimed to evaluate the prevalence of clinical inertia, identify associated patient-level factors, and assess its impact on CVR factor outcomes in high-risk primary care patients
title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

text: . This was a pre-specified secondary analysis of the Objetivo Punto de Mira (OPM) study, a multicentre, prospective, quasi-experimental interventional study conducted in primary care settings across nine Spanish regions (2024-2025). We included 711 participants with at least one uncontrolled CVR factor at baseline (hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidaemia)
title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

text: . Clinical inertia was operationalised, among therapeutically adherent patients, as the absence of documented pharmacological treatment initiation, dose escalation, or appropriate combination therapy when a risk factor remained uncontrolled. We estimated prevalence with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with clinical inertia
title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

text: . Linear mixed-effects models assessed changes in CVR factors from baseline to 90-day follow-up, comparing patients with and without clinical inertia. Risk analysis quantified the association between clinical inertia and persistent uncontrolled status
title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

text: . At 90-day follow-up, patients with clinical inertia showed significantly smaller reductions in total cholesterol (between-group difference in change = 19.3 mg/dL; 95% CI = 12.4, 26.3, P < 0.001) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (15.5 mg/dL; 95% CI = 8.9, 22.0, P < 0.001) compared with patients who received treatment intensification
title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

text: . We also observed a small but statistically significant difference in body mass index reduction (0.25 kg/m Clinical inertia affects more than half of high-risk primary care patients with uncontrolled CVR factors
title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

text: . Patient demographic and clinical characteristics examined (age, sex, CVR category, excess weight) did not predict clinical inertia in this sample, consistent with, but not proof of, provider- and system-level influences described in prior literature.
title: Clinical inertia in cardiovascular risk management: prevalence, associated factors, and impact on outcomes of the OPM study.

text: Elevated lipoprotein(a) and prevalent cardiovascular disease burden in treated hypertension.. Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease across multiple clinical settings, but its relationship with prevalent cardiovascular disease burden among adults with treated hypertension (HTN) remains incompletely characterized
title: Elevated lipoprotein(a) and prevalent cardiovascular disease burden in treated hypertension.

text: . To evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and prevalent cardiovascular disease burden among adults with treated HTN after adjustment for contemporaneous office blood pressure (BP) control. We performed a predefined cross-sectional subanalysis of the multicenter Argentine Group for the Study of Lp(a) cohort, including adults with treated HTN and available Lp(a) measurements
title: Elevated lipoprotein(a) and prevalent cardiovascular disease burden in treated hypertension.

text: . BP control was defined as office BP ≤130/80 mmHg. Lp(a) was analyzed as a continuous variable using a high-risk threshold of ≥125 nmol/L
title: Elevated lipoprotein(a) and prevalent cardiovascular disease burden in treated hypertension.

text: . Multivariable generalized estimating equation models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, smoking status, low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol, statin therapy, and BP control were used to evaluate the association between Lp(a) and prevalent cardiovascular disease burden
title: Elevated lipoprotein(a) and prevalent cardiovascular disease burden in treated hypertension.

text: . Among 2313 patients with treated HTN, higher Lp(a) levels were independently associated with a greater prevalence of cardiovascular disease burden. Each 1-SD increase in log-transformed Lp(a) was associated with higher odds of prevalent cardiovascular disease burden (Odds ratio [OR] 1.24; 95% CI 1.09-1.41; P = .001)
title: Elevated lipoprotein(a) and prevalent cardiovascular disease burden in treated hypertension.

text: . Participants with Lp(a) ≥125 nmol/L had significantly higher odds of prevalent cardiovascular disease burden (OR 1.38; 95% CI 1.02-1.88; P = .037). Additional adjustment for body mass index and ethnicity yielded consistent results. No significant interaction was observed between Lp(a) levels and BP control status
title: Elevated lipoprotein(a) and prevalent cardiovascular disease burden in treated hypertension.

text: . In adults with treated HTN, elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with prevalent cardiovascular disease burden after adjustment for office BP control and conventional cardiovascular risk factors. These findings support the potential role of Lp(a) assessment in refining cardiovascular risk stratification in treated hypertensive populations.
title: Elevated lipoprotein(a) and prevalent cardiovascular disease burden in treated hypertension.

text: Thiazide Diuretics Are Associated with a Higher Triglyceride-Glucose Index Than Calcium Channel Blockers in Hypertensive Patients.. title: Thiazide Diuretics Are Associated with a Higher Triglyceride-Glucose Index Than Calcium Channel Blockers in Hypertensive Patients.

text: . This study aimed to compare TyG index values and related metabolic parameters between patients receiving RAAS blockers plus thiazide/thiazide-like diuretics and those receiving RAAS blockers plus calcium channel blockers (CCBs) as antihypertensive regimens
title: Thiazide Diuretics Are Associated with a Higher Triglyceride-Glucose Index Than Calcium Channel Blockers in Hypertensive Patients.

title: Integrative Monitoring of Hypertension Care Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data in Mexico's Emerging Federalised Public Health Care Provider.

text: . In October 2023, Mexico initiated the federalisation of public health services for the population without social security, creating an integrated national public health care provider and increasing the need for system-level monitoring tools capable of supporting longitudinal assessment across heterogeneous settings
title: Integrative Monitoring of Hypertension Care Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data in Mexico's Emerging Federalised Public Health Care Provider.

text: . To describe the development and early application of an integrative monitoring platform using routinely collected clinical data to support system-level oversight of hypertension care within Mexico's federalised public health care provider. Descriptive health services research study based on secondary analysis of routinely collected clinical data
title: Integrative Monitoring of Hypertension Care Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data in Mexico's Emerging Federalised Public Health Care Provider.

text: . An integrative monitoring platform was developed to organise data into a structured indicator framework covering four domains: care engagement and continuity; clinical care processes; intermediate clinical outcomes; and case-mix and clinical complexity. The platform enables longitudinal and subnational analyses across selected indicators presented as illustrative use cases
title: Integrative Monitoring of Hypertension Care Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data in Mexico's Emerging Federalised Public Health Care Provider.

text: . Institutional reach was assessed using an overall monitoring period from January 2024 to September 2025, while clinical process and intermediate outcome indicators, including blood pressure control, were calculated within a predefined active six-month monitoring cohort using the September 2025 reporting date
title: Integrative Monitoring of Hypertension Care Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data in Mexico's Emerging Federalised Public Health Care Provider.

text: . From January 2024 to September 2025, a total of 486,044 individuals received hypertension-related care within primary care services across participating states. The active six-month cohort included 322,661 individuals, with 67.2% (95% CI, 67.04-67.37) achieving blood pressure control (<140/90 mmHg), and 36.8% (95% CI, 36.62-36.96) achieving strict control (<130/80 mmHg)
title: Integrative Monitoring of Hypertension Care Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data in Mexico's Emerging Federalised Public Health Care Provider.

text: . For those with sub-optimal control, 63% had timely clinical follow-up and 48% underwent treatment intensification. A high proportion of individuals presented high risk features including obesity (36.4%; 95%CI, 36.2-36.5), diabetes (48.7%; 95%CI, 48.5-48.8) or high cardiovascular risk characteristics (81.7%, 95%IC, 81.5-81.8)
title: Integrative Monitoring of Hypertension Care Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data in Mexico's Emerging Federalised Public Health Care Provider.

text: . Transforming routinely collected clinical data into an integrative monitoring platform is feasible within a newly federalised public health care provider
title: Integrative Monitoring of Hypertension Care Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data in Mexico's Emerging Federalised Public Health Care Provider.

text: . Routine monitoring of relevant indicators across multiple dimensions of care provides a structured basis for system-level oversight, longitudinal assessment, data-informed decision-making, and continuous learning within large public service delivery systems.
title: Integrative Monitoring of Hypertension Care Using Routinely Collected Clinical Data in Mexico's Emerging Federalised Public Health Care Provider.

text: Hypertension in obesity: A focus on individualized pharmacotherapy and the role of body composition, on behalf of the European Society of Hypertension Working Group on Diabetes and Metabolic Risk Factors and Working Group on Lifestyle, Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy and Adherence.
title: Hypertension in obesity: A focus on individualized pharmacotherapy and the role of body composition, on behalf of the European Society of Hypertension Working Group on Diabetes and Metabolic Risk Factors and Working Group on Lifestyle, Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy and Adherence.

text: . Hypertension in obesity represents a major global health challenge, closely linked to the global epidemics of obesity, type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction
title: Hypertension in obesity: A focus on individualized pharmacotherapy and the role of body composition, on behalf of the European Society of Hypertension Working Group on Diabetes and Metabolic Risk Factors and Working Group on Lifestyle, Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy and Adherence.

text: . Excess adiposity contributes to elevated blood pressure through multiple, interrelated mechanisms, including activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, sympathetic nervous system overactivity, insulin resistance, inflammation and adipokine dysregulation
title: Hypertension in obesity: A focus on individualized pharmacotherapy and the role of body composition, on behalf of the European Society of Hypertension Working Group on Diabetes and Metabolic Risk Factors and Working Group on Lifestyle, Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy and Adherence.

text: . Importantly, emerging evidence indicates that body composition plays a critical role in modulating hypertension risk, treatment response and cardiovascular outcomes. This article highlights the need for a more individualized pharmacotherapeutic approach to hypertension in people with obesity
title: Hypertension in obesity: A focus on individualized pharmacotherapy and the role of body composition, on behalf of the European Society of Hypertension Working Group on Diabetes and Metabolic Risk Factors and Working Group on Lifestyle, Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy and Adherence.

text: . While lifestyle modification and weight reduction remain essential, pharmacological treatment should be tailored to underlying pathophysiological drivers, such as volume expansion, neurohormonal activation and metabolic abnormalities. The potential different antihypertensive drug classes in hypertension related with obesity are also discussed
title: Hypertension in obesity: A focus on individualized pharmacotherapy and the role of body composition, on behalf of the European Society of Hypertension Working Group on Diabetes and Metabolic Risk Factors and Working Group on Lifestyle, Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy and Adherence.

text: . A precision medicine approach that incorporates body composition and metabolic risk factors may improve blood pressure control and decrease residual cardiovascular risk in this high-risk population.
title: Hypertension in obesity: A focus on individualized pharmacotherapy and the role of body composition, on behalf of the European Society of Hypertension Working Group on Diabetes and Metabolic Risk Factors and Working Group on Lifestyle, Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy and Adherence.

text: Important Role of Renin-Angiotensin System and Vasopressin System in Cardiovascular, Metabolic and Psychogenic Disorders in Pregnancy and Early Postnatal Life: A Narrative Review.. The renin-angiotensin system (RAS) and vasopressin system (VAS) play an essential role in the regulation of multiple vital body functions
title: Important Role of Renin-Angiotensin System and Vasopressin System in Cardiovascular, Metabolic and Psychogenic Disorders in Pregnancy and Early Postnatal Life: A Narrative Review.

text: . A survey of the literature provides evidence that the central and systemic RAS and VAS are activated during pregnancy and cooperate in the regulation of blood circulation and in the exchange of substrates and metabolites between the mother and fetus
title: Important Role of Renin-Angiotensin System and Vasopressin System in Cardiovascular, Metabolic and Psychogenic Disorders in Pregnancy and Early Postnatal Life: A Narrative Review.

text: . The present review is focused on the engagement of the RAS and VAS in the regulation of blood circulation in healthy pregnant women and fetuses and in gestations complicated by cardiovascular, metabolic and psychogenic diseases
title: Important Role of Renin-Angiotensin System and Vasopressin System in Cardiovascular, Metabolic and Psychogenic Disorders in Pregnancy and Early Postnatal Life: A Narrative Review.

text: . The presence of several components of the RAS and VAS, such as renin, angiotensin-converting enzymes (ACE1, ACE2), angiotensins [Ang II, Ang-(1-7)], angiotensin receptors (AT1R, AT2R), and AVP receptors (V1aR), in the placenta and the myometrium allows us to assume that the RAS and VAS play a prominent role in function of the maternal-placental-fetal unit
title: Important Role of Renin-Angiotensin System and Vasopressin System in Cardiovascular, Metabolic and Psychogenic Disorders in Pregnancy and Early Postnatal Life: A Narrative Review.

text: . Gestation is also associated with the activation of components of the RAS and VAS in appropriate regions of the central nervous system that are involved in the regulation of blood pressure. Experimental studies suggest that the RAS and VAS participate in the autonomic control of blood circulation and in the regulation of emotional aspects of pregnancy and maternity
title: Important Role of Renin-Angiotensin System and Vasopressin System in Cardiovascular, Metabolic and Psychogenic Disorders in Pregnancy and Early Postnatal Life: A Narrative Review.

text: . Abnormal functioning of the RAS and/or VAS was found in eclampsia, metabolic diseases (diabetes mellitus) and psychogenic disorders (anxiety, stress, and depression). Some of these abnormalities may have an immunological or genetic background
title: Important Role of Renin-Angiotensin System and Vasopressin System in Cardiovascular, Metabolic and Psychogenic Disorders in Pregnancy and Early Postnatal Life: A Narrative Review.

text: . In eclampsia, the presence of specific agonistic angiotensin receptor autoantibodies (AT1-AA) and altered genotypes of AGT, ACE2, AT1R, and AT2R were reported. Polymorphism of the AVP promoter was also described. Inappropriate pharmacotherapy or toxic environmental pollution may disturb the regulation of the cardiovascular system of the mother and fetus by the RAS and VAS during gestation
title: Important Role of Renin-Angiotensin System and Vasopressin System in Cardiovascular, Metabolic and Psychogenic Disorders in Pregnancy and Early Postnatal Life: A Narrative Review.

text: . Further studies are necessary to better recognize the mechanisms of action of the RAS and VAS in healthy and pathological pregnancies.
title: Important Role of Renin-Angiotensin System and Vasopressin System in Cardiovascular, Metabolic and Psychogenic Disorders in Pregnancy and Early Postnatal Life: A Narrative Review.

text: Blood Pressure and Systemic Risk Factors in Patients Presenting With Post-Extraction and Periodontal Bleeding at a Dental Out-of-Hours Clinic.
title: Blood Pressure and Systemic Risk Factors in Patients Presenting With Post-Extraction and Periodontal Bleeding at a Dental Out-of-Hours Clinic.

text: . This study aimed to verify whether blood pressure was higher in patients presenting to the dental out-of-hours clinic with post-extraction bleeding (PEB) and periodontal disease-related gingival bleeding (PDB) compared to those presenting for other conditions (Control (C) group)
title: Blood Pressure and Systemic Risk Factors in Patients Presenting With Post-Extraction and Periodontal Bleeding at a Dental Out-of-Hours Clinic.

text: . Additionally, we examined differences in the prevalence of hypertension, antithrombotic use, and diabetes mellitus among the PEB, PDB, and C groups. Patients visiting the out-of-hours clinic were retrospectively categorized by sex and age (young (Y)-group: 20-39, middle (M)-group: 40-59, older (O)-group: ≥ 60)
title: Blood Pressure and Systemic Risk Factors in Patients Presenting With Post-Extraction and Periodontal Bleeding at a Dental Out-of-Hours Clinic.

text: . Data collected included systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) blood pressure, and the prevalence of treated hypertension, antithrombotic use, and diabetes mellitus. Mean BP values were compared using Welch's t-test. The prevalence of systemic factors was compared using Fisher's exact test. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed in the O-group
title: Blood Pressure and Systemic Risk Factors in Patients Presenting With Post-Extraction and Periodontal Bleeding at a Dental Out-of-Hours Clinic.

text: . A total of 416 bleeding patients were included, comprising 216 patients with PEB, 119 with PDB, and 81 with other bleeding. Because of the limited number of cases in the Y and M-groups, multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed only in the O-group (≥ 60 years). According to that, antithrombotic use was independently associated with both PDB and PEB in males and females
title: Blood Pressure and Systemic Risk Factors in Patients Presenting With Post-Extraction and Periodontal Bleeding at a Dental Out-of-Hours Clinic.

text: . Increased SBP was independently associated with PDB in both sexes and with PEB in males. Hypertension remained independently associated with PDB only in females, whereas diabetes mellitus was not independently associated with either bleeding condition
title: Blood Pressure and Systemic Risk Factors in Patients Presenting With Post-Extraction and Periodontal Bleeding at a Dental Out-of-Hours Clinic.

text: . Particularly among the O-group (≥ 60 years), antithrombotic use was independently associated with both PDB and PEB, whereas increased systolic blood pressure was independently associated with PDB and, to a lesser extent, PEB
title: Blood Pressure and Systemic Risk Factors in Patients Presenting With Post-Extraction and Periodontal Bleeding at a Dental Out-of-Hours Clinic.

text: . These findings highlight the importance of systemic assessment, particularly regarding blood pressure and antithrombotic therapy, in patients presenting with acute oral bleeding.
title: Blood Pressure and Systemic Risk Factors in Patients Presenting With Post-Extraction and Periodontal Bleeding at a Dental Out-of-Hours Clinic.

text: Body Weight in Relation to the Effectiveness of Intravenous Alteplase in Acute Ischemic Stroke: The ENCHANTED Trial.. The prognostic significance of body weight in patients receiving thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain
title: Body Weight in Relation to the Effectiveness of Intravenous Alteplase in Acute Ischemic Stroke: The ENCHANTED Trial.

title: Body Weight in Relation to the Effectiveness of Intravenous Alteplase in Acute Ischemic Stroke: The ENCHANTED Trial.

text: .
