text: Health Literacy and Blood Pressure Control: The Mediating Role of Self-Management Behaviors in Hypertensive Adults.. Health literacy is a modifiable determinant of chronic disease management; however, its direct association with objective blood pressure control remains inconsistent
title: Health Literacy and Blood Pressure Control: The Mediating Role of Self-Management Behaviors in Hypertensive Adults.

text: . Increasing evidence suggests that health literacy may influence cardiovascular outcomes through self-management behaviors. To examine the relationships among health literacy, hypertension management behaviors, antihypertensive treatment, and blood pressure control, and to determine whether behavioral pathways mediate the association between health literacy and blood pressure control
title: Health Literacy and Blood Pressure Control: The Mediating Role of Self-Management Behaviors in Hypertensive Adults.

text: . This cross-sectional secondary analysis used nationally representative data from 2932 Korean adults with hypertension. Survey-weighted logistic regression was conducted to identify factors associated with blood pressure control. Multiple mediation analyses were performed to assess indirect effects through hypertension management behaviors and antihypertensive treatment
title: Health Literacy and Blood Pressure Control: The Mediating Role of Self-Management Behaviors in Hypertensive Adults.

text: . The weighted blood pressure control rate was 45.0%. Antihypertensive treatment was strongly associated with blood pressure control (odds ratio: 3.20, 95% confidence interval: 2.19-4.67, P < .001). Hypertension management behaviors were also positively associated with control (odds ratio: 1.09 per 1-point increase, 95% confidence interval: 1.02-1.16, P = .011)
title: Health Literacy and Blood Pressure Control: The Mediating Role of Self-Management Behaviors in Hypertensive Adults.

text: . Health literacy was not independently associated with blood pressure control after adjustment. However, health literacy was significantly associated with management behaviors (β = 0.018, P = .001), which in turn were associated with blood pressure control (β = 0.102, P = .003)
title: Health Literacy and Blood Pressure Control: The Mediating Role of Self-Management Behaviors in Hypertensive Adults.

text: . The indirect effect through hypertension management behaviors was significant, whereas the pathway through antihypertensive treatment was not. Health literacy may contribute to blood pressure control primarily through behavioral self-management pathways rather than direct effects
title: Health Literacy and Blood Pressure Control: The Mediating Role of Self-Management Behaviors in Hypertensive Adults.

text: . Nursing interventions should prioritize behavior-focused strategies that translate health literacy into sustained self-management practices.
title: Health Literacy and Blood Pressure Control: The Mediating Role of Self-Management Behaviors in Hypertensive Adults.

text: Disease control and its correlates among hypertensive, diabetic, and asthmatic patients enrolled in secondary-level Integrated Chronic Care Clinics in Neno District, rural Malawi.. Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) account for nearly 74% of global deaths, with 86% of premature NCD mortality occurring in low- and middle-income countries
title: Disease control and its correlates among hypertensive, diabetic, and asthmatic patients enrolled in secondary-level Integrated Chronic Care Clinics in Neno District, rural Malawi.

text: . In Malawi, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and asthma contribute substantially to morbidity and mortality. Integrated service delivery models such as the Integrated Chronic Care Clinics (IC3) in Neno District aim to improve chronic disease management; however, evidence on disease control within these models remains limited
title: Disease control and its correlates among hypertensive, diabetic, and asthmatic patients enrolled in secondary-level Integrated Chronic Care Clinics in Neno District, rural Malawi.

text: . This study assessed disease control and associated correlates among patients receiving care in IC3 clinics in rural Malawi. We conducted a mixed-methods retrospective cross-sectional study at Neno District Hospital and Lisungwi Community Hospital. Quantitative data were extracted from OpenMRS electronic medical records for 1,790 patients diagnosed with hypertension, diabetes, or asthma
title: Disease control and its correlates among hypertensive, diabetic, and asthmatic patients enrolled in secondary-level Integrated Chronic Care Clinics in Neno District, rural Malawi.

text: . Disease control was defined as blood pressure <140/90 mmHg (<130/80 mmHg for hypertensive diabetics), HbA1c < 7% for diabetes, and symptom-based criteria for asthma. Associations between disease control and demographic or clinical variables were assessed using chi-square tests and logistic regression
title: Disease control and its correlates among hypertensive, diabetic, and asthmatic patients enrolled in secondary-level Integrated Chronic Care Clinics in Neno District, rural Malawi.

text: . Qualitative data were collected through 17 focus group discussions and 56 in-depth interviews with patients and healthcare providers. Hypertension control was achieved in 55% of patients, asthma control in 87%, and diabetes control in 32%. Males had lower odds of hypertension control than females (aOR 0.70, 95% CI 0.55-0.90)
title: Disease control and its correlates among hypertensive, diabetic, and asthmatic patients enrolled in secondary-level Integrated Chronic Care Clinics in Neno District, rural Malawi.

text: . Overweight patients and those receiving more than two antihypertensive medications also had lower odds of hypertension control. Asthma control was associated with inhaled corticosteroid use, while glycaemic control was associated with the number of prescribed medications
title: Disease control and its correlates among hypertensive, diabetic, and asthmatic patients enrolled in secondary-level Integrated Chronic Care Clinics in Neno District, rural Malawi.

text: . Qualitative findings identified health literacy, medication adherence, patient-provider communication, and access to care as key influences on disease management. Disease control varied across conditions within integrated chronic care clinics in rural Malawi and was influenced by demographic, treatment-related, and contextual factors.
title: Disease control and its correlates among hypertensive, diabetic, and asthmatic patients enrolled in secondary-level Integrated Chronic Care Clinics in Neno District, rural Malawi.

text: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.. Coronary heart disease (CHD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Early identification of high-risk hypertensive patients is crucial for preventing cardiovascular events
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: . While traditional risk scores rely on static clinical measurements, 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM)-derived time in target range (TTR) captures dynamic blood pressure control patterns that may improve risk stratification
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: . Machine learning methods, particularly deep neural networks, offer an enhanced capability to model complex non-linear relationships in high-dimensional clinical data, compared with conventional statistical approaches
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: . This single-center retrospective cohort study included 1,026 patients admitted between January 2023 and December 2024, with 718 patients allocated to model development and 308 to internal validation
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: . A deep neural network model with three hidden layers was developed and compared against eight conventional machine learning algorithms (logistic regression, naïve Bayes, k-nearest neighbors, random forest, support vector machine, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost)
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: . Thirty-two variables spanning demographics, clinical data, laboratory results, echocardiographic measures, and blood pressure indices were evaluated. Continuous variables were discretized into quartile-based categories to enhance clinical interpretability
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: . Feature selection employed a two-step process combining the Boruta algorithm and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, with variance inflation factor analysis confirming the absence of collinearity
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: . Model selection prioritized balanced performance across discrimination (AUC), calibration (Brier score), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis) in the independent validation cohort. Interpretability was evaluated using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: . The deep neural network model achieved optimal balanced performance with an AUC of 0.822 (95% CI: 0.793-0.850) in the training cohort and 0.796 (95% CI: 0.749-0.846) in the validation cohort, accompanied by the lowest Brier score (0.172), indicating superior calibration
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: . Nine predictors were retained: diabetes mellitus, mean systolic blood pressure, time in target range of systolic blood pressure, left atrial diameter, left ventricular end-systolic diameter, left ventricular ejection fraction, use of antihypertensive medications, calcium channel blockers, and  The developed deep neural network model enables early identification of high-risk CHD patients with
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: identification of high-risk CHD patients with hypertension through interpretable, routinely available clinical variables
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: . Prospective multicenter external validation is warranted to confirm its generalizability across diverse populations and clinical settings.
title: Development and validation of a deep neural network for predicting coronary heart disease in hypertensive patients using 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: a retrospective study.

text: Chrononutrition, Circadian Rhythms, and Genetic Susceptibility in Noncommunicable Diseases: Sex-Specific Perspective.. Obesity, diabetes, and hypertension are major global health burdens influenced not only by lifestyle factors but also by genetic predisposition, sleep quality, chrononutrition, and circadian rhythms
title: Chrononutrition, Circadian Rhythms, and Genetic Susceptibility in Noncommunicable Diseases: Sex-Specific Perspective.

text: . This review examined how these factors interact in metabolic and cardiovascular diseases, with emphasis on sex-specific differences. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases for studies published between 2006 and 2026
title: Chrononutrition, Circadian Rhythms, and Genetic Susceptibility in Noncommunicable Diseases: Sex-Specific Perspective.

text: . A total of 112 studies were synthesized, including randomized trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, Mendelian randomization, and mechanistic investigations. Evidence indicates that genetic susceptibility and circadian disruption contribute significantly to obesity, diabetes, and hypertension
title: Chrononutrition, Circadian Rhythms, and Genetic Susceptibility in Noncommunicable Diseases: Sex-Specific Perspective.

text: . Sleep deprivation, obstructive sleep apnea, and circadian misalignment were consistently associated with insulin resistance, appetite dysregulation, elevated blood pressure, and increased cardiometabolic risk, particularly among shift workers. Hormonal and metabolic pathways involving leptin, ghrelin, cortisol, and melatonin appear to mediate these effects
title: Chrononutrition, Circadian Rhythms, and Genetic Susceptibility in Noncommunicable Diseases: Sex-Specific Perspective.

text: . Important sex differences were observed, with women showing greater vulnerability to sleep-related appetite disturbances and men presenting a higher prevalence of visceral adiposity, sleep apnea, and hypertension
title: Chrononutrition, Circadian Rhythms, and Genetic Susceptibility in Noncommunicable Diseases: Sex-Specific Perspective.

text: . Chrononutrition strategies, including time-restricted eating and Mediterranean dietary patterns, showed beneficial effects on sleep quality, glycemic control, inflammation, and metabolic health. Emerging evidence also suggests bidirectional interactions between gut microbiota rhythmicity and circadian regulation
title: Chrononutrition, Circadian Rhythms, and Genetic Susceptibility in Noncommunicable Diseases: Sex-Specific Perspective.

text: . Genetic predisposition, sleep disturbances, and circadian disruption interact to influence metabolic and cardiovascular disease risk. Integrative approaches combining chrononutrition, sleep hygiene, circadian alignment, and personalized nutritional strategies may improve the prevention and management of cardiometabolic diseases.
title: Chrononutrition, Circadian Rhythms, and Genetic Susceptibility in Noncommunicable Diseases: Sex-Specific Perspective.

text: Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in coronary heart disease patients: results of the EUROASPIRE V survey conducted in 27 countries.. Hypertension is a highly common cardiovascular risk factor, and a large proportion of patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) have uncontrolled hypertension
title: Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in coronary heart disease patients: results of the EUROASPIRE V survey conducted in 27 countries.

text: . We report on the distribution and determinants of hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in CHD hypertensive patients. The EUROASPIRE V survey included 8261 CHD patients from 27 countries. Awareness was defined as patients reporting being told by a health professional to have raised blood pressure (BP), being aware of their BP target and latest measurement
title: Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in coronary heart disease patients: results of the EUROASPIRE V survey conducted in 27 countries.

text: . Patients using antihypertensive medication to lower BP were considered treated. Controlled hypertension was defined as BP <140/90mmHg (<140/85mmHg in patients with diabetes). Factors associated with hypertension awareness, treatment and control were identified with logistic regression
title: Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in coronary heart disease patients: results of the EUROASPIRE V survey conducted in 27 countries.

text: . A total of 6496 EUROASPIRE V patients were considered hypertensive, from which 60.4% were aware, 91.7% were on treatment, and 46.8% were controlled. Number of antihypertensive drugs and adherence were independently associated with awareness (OR 1.23, 95%CI 1.16-1.31, and 2.18, 1.74-2.74 respectively) and control (1.11, 1.05-1.17 and 1.93, 1.57-2.37 respectively)
title: Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in coronary heart disease patients: results of the EUROASPIRE V survey conducted in 27 countries.

text: . Secondary (1.32, 1.03-1.68) and tertiary (1.70, 1.32-2.17) education and undertaking lifestyle changes (1.60, 1.37-1.87) were associated with awareness. Controlled patients were more often aware (1.43, 1.23-1.65) and had a healthier risk factor profile (BMI >25kg/m2 0.73, 0.61-0.87, diabetes 0.67, 0.59-0.76, LDL ≥1.8mmol/L 0.75, 0.65-0.86) than uncontrolled patients
title: Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in coronary heart disease patients: results of the EUROASPIRE V survey conducted in 27 countries.

text: . Hypertension control remains poor in hypertensive CHD patients, despite high treatment and reasonable awareness levels. Communication with CHD hypertensive patients, especially those from vulnerable groups, needs to improve to facilitate change of health behaviours
title: Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in coronary heart disease patients: results of the EUROASPIRE V survey conducted in 27 countries.

text: . Controlling blood pressure levels is very important in patients with cardiovascular disease, therefore, we investigated the awareness, treatment and control of hypertension among coronary heart disease and hypertension.Less than half of the patients had their blood pressure controlled, despite most being on medication.Patients who were aware of their hypertension, took their medication
title: Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in coronary heart disease patients: results of the EUROASPIRE V survey conducted in 27 countries.

text: of their hypertension, took their medication regularly, had fewer risk factors, and adopted healthy lifestyle changes were more likely to have controlled hypertension.
title: Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in coronary heart disease patients: results of the EUROASPIRE V survey conducted in 27 countries.

text: Cardiovascular Disease Management Consensus in Kidney Transplantation Recipients.. Kidney transplantation is the definitive treatment for end-stage kidney disease; however, organ availability in Taiwan remains limited, with only 4.9% of patients on the waiting list receiving transplants in 2019
title: Cardiovascular Disease Management Consensus in Kidney Transplantation Recipients.

text: . More than 86,000 individuals require regular dialysis, highlighting the need for improved transplantation rates. Although the median survival time post-transplantation is 5.7 years, nearly half of Taiwanese transplant recipients died in 2019, emphasizing cardiovascular disease as a major concern
title: Cardiovascular Disease Management Consensus in Kidney Transplantation Recipients.

text: . Notably, patients who survive for more than a decade post-transplantation are increasingly prone to cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and hypertension
title: Cardiovascular Disease Management Consensus in Kidney Transplantation Recipients.

text: . The aim of this study was to develop a joint consensus with the Taiwan Society of Nephrology, Taiwan Society of Cardiology, and Transplantation Society of Taiwan, to outline the best practices for evaluating and managing cardiovascular disease in kidney transplant recipients
title: Cardiovascular Disease Management Consensus in Kidney Transplantation Recipients.

text: . A consensus committee of 24 Taiwanese nephrologists, cardiologists, and surgeons synthesized recommendations from the literature and international guidelines, finalizing them via a formal voting process (70%/90% agreement)
title: Cardiovascular Disease Management Consensus in Kidney Transplantation Recipients.

text: . Clinical recommendations emphasize pre-transplant cardiac assessment, including echocardiography and perfusion imaging; vigilant post-transplant surveillance of blood pressure, lipids, and glycemic control; and the judicious use of immunosuppressants to minimize metabolic complications
title: Cardiovascular Disease Management Consensus in Kidney Transplantation Recipients.

text: . Multidisciplinary collaboration between nephrologists, cardiologists, and transplant experts is crucial for delivering patient-centered care. By adopting these guidelines, clinicians can promote long-term graft survival, reduce cardiovascular complications, and improve patient outcomes in the evolving transplantation landscape in Taiwan.
title: Cardiovascular Disease Management Consensus in Kidney Transplantation Recipients.

text: Statin Use Patterns among hypertensive Patients in a population-based study.. Although previous studies have assessed the role of statins in managing cardiovascular risk and reducing blood pressure, few have examined their use patterns in relation to hypertension control at population level. This study addresses this gap among Iranian hypertensive patients
title: Statin Use Patterns among hypertensive Patients in a population-based study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders

text: . A cross-sectional analysis was conducted using data from the 2021 WHO STEPwise approach to Non-communicable Disease Risk Factor Surveillance (STEPS) in Iran, encompassing all 31 provinces. The study included 6,216 adults aged ≥ 25 years with hypertension, defined as systolic blood pressure (SBP) ≥ 140 mmHg, diastolic blood pressure (DBP) ≥ 90 mmHg, or current use of antihypertensive medication
title: Statin Use Patterns among hypertensive Patients in a population-based study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders

text: . Participants with missing data for key variables were excluded. Logistic and linear regression models were used to examine associations between statin use, demographic and clinical characteristics, and blood pressure control (SBP < 140 mmHg and DBP < 90 mmHg)
title: Statin Use Patterns among hypertensive Patients in a population-based study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders

text: . Among included 6,216 hypertensive patients, 1,815 (29.2%) were statin users, predominantly older (mean age: 61.79 years) and female (63.14%). Statin use was significantly associated with a 2.04 mmHg reduction in SBP (95% CI: -3.59, -0.48), whereas the association with DBP was non-significant (0.38 mmHg increase in (95% CI: -0.67 to 1.44)
title: Statin Use Patterns among hypertensive Patients in a population-based study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders

text: . In fully adjusted models, statin use was not associated with blood pressure control (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.79-1.21). Despite the high frequency of comorbidities in patients with hypertension, statin use remains low, which needs to great attention by clinicians
title: Statin Use Patterns among hypertensive Patients in a population-based study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders

text: . In addition, the observed association between statin use and blood pressure in current study is required to further clinical trials or cohort studies to confirm. The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s40200-026-02018-y.
title: Statin Use Patterns among hypertensive Patients in a population-based study.
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders

text: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.. While existing studies established an association between self-reported health status and healthcare service utilisation, its association with Blood Pressure (BP) medication use among persons living with hypertension remains under-explored
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: . This study examines the association between self-reported health status and BP medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya. We analysed data from the 2022 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey (KDHS). The primary outcome was BP medication use, while the main independent variable was self-reported health status
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: . Logistic regression models were fitted to assess the association between self-reported health status and BP medication use. We found that only 32.0% of women and 36.4% of men in this study reported consistent BP medication use
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: . Women who reported moderate or poor health were significantly more likely to use BP medication compared to those who perceived their health as good (aOR = 1.8, 95% CI: 1.4-2.4; aOR = 1.9, 95% CI: 1.2-3.0) respectively. However, no significant association between self-reported health status and BP medication use was found among men
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: . Women aged 20-24 years (aOR = 0.4, 95% CI: 0.2-0.9) and men aged 25-34 years (aOR = 0.2, 95% CI: 0.06-0.9) were less likely to use BP medication. Furthermore, women (aOR = 2.0, 95% CI: 1.1-3.8) and men (aOR = 2.0, 95% CI: 1.0-3.8) with diabetes were more likely to use BP medication
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: . These findings emphasise the need for gender specific health education and behaviour change interventions t to improve hypertension management. High blood pressure is a major public health problem and can lead to serious illness and death if not well controlled
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: . Taking blood pressure medication regularly is important for managing hypertension and preventing complications.This study examined whether people’s own view of their health, influences whether they take blood pressure medication or not
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: . We used data from the 2022 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey and analysed data for men and women separately.The study included 1,324 women and 479 men who reported that they had been diagnosed with hypertension. We compared blood pressure medication use across different levels of self-reported health status.Overall, blood pressure medication use was low
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: . Only 32.0% of women and 36.4% of men reported that they were taking medication to control their blood pressure.Among women, those who described their health as moderate or poor were more likely to take blood pressure medication than those who said their health was good
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: . This suggests that women who feel healthy may not see the need to use medication consistently.Among men, self-reported health status was not significantly associated with blood pressure medication use.Age and diabetes were also important
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: . Younger women aged 20 to 24 years and men aged 25 to 34 years were less likely to use medication, while respondents with diabetes were more likely to use it.These findings show the need for targeted health education and behaviour change strategies, especially for people who feel healthy but are living with hypertension.
title: Self-reported health status and blood pressure medication use among persons living with hypertension in Kenya.

text: Population-Level 10-Year Implications of the New 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Hypertension Guideline Recommendations for Primary Prevention in the United States: A NHANES-Based Cohort Study (2009-2018).. In August 2025, the American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology released updated hypertension guidelines
title: Population-Level 10-Year Implications of the New 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Hypertension Guideline Recommendations for Primary Prevention in the United States: A NHANES-Based Cohort Study (2009-2018).
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Under the new guidelines, therapy is advised at blood pressure ≥130/80 mm Hg in adults with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, or a Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-estimated 10-year cardiovascular disease risk ≥7.5%. The long-term population-level changes following these guidelines remains uncertain
title: Population-Level 10-Year Implications of the New 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Hypertension Guideline Recommendations for Primary Prevention in the United States: A NHANES-Based Cohort Study (2009-2018).
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . We analyzed NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) 2009 to 2018 data linked to mortality through 2019. Hypertensive adults without baseline cardiovascular disease were included. Treatment eligibility was defined using guideline criteria. Cox models estimated associations between antihypertensive therapy and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality
title: Population-Level 10-Year Implications of the New 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Hypertension Guideline Recommendations for Primary Prevention in the United States: A NHANES-Based Cohort Study (2009-2018).
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Simulation analyses projected lives saved under full and partial treatment uptake. The weighted cohort represented 81.0 million US adults with hypertension. Of these, 22.8 million (28%) were guideline eligible for therapy; 13.1 million (57%) were treated, and 9.7 million (43%) remained untreated
title: Population-Level 10-Year Implications of the New 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Hypertension Guideline Recommendations for Primary Prevention in the United States: A NHANES-Based Cohort Study (2009-2018).
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Antihypertensive therapy was associated with a 23% reduction in all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.77 [95% CI, 0.63-0.94]) and 50% reduction in cardiovascular mortality (HR, 0.50 [95% CI, 0.36-0.68]). At 10 years, universal treatment of eligible but untreated adults was projected to prevent ~200 900 all-cause and ~ 162 600 cardiovascular deaths
title: Population-Level 10-Year Implications of the New 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Hypertension Guideline Recommendations for Primary Prevention in the United States: A NHANES-Based Cohort Study (2009-2018).
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Benefits were greatest in adults with diabetes. In this nationally representative cohort, nearly 1 in 3 US adults with hypertension were newly eligible for therapy under the guideline, yet >2 in 5 remained untreated. Extending treatment to all eligible adults could prevent >200 000 all-cause and 160 000 cardiovascular deaths over the next decade.
title: Population-Level 10-Year Implications of the New 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Hypertension Guideline Recommendations for Primary Prevention in the United States: A NHANES-Based Cohort Study (2009-2018).
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: Evaluation of Antihypertensive Medication Adherence and Its Association With Blood Pressure Control Among Hypertensive Patients Attending Outpatient Clinics in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.
title: Evaluation of Antihypertensive Medication Adherence and Its Association With Blood Pressure Control Among Hypertensive Patients Attending Outpatient Clinics in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: .  Hypertension is a major noncommunicable disease in Pakistan, and suboptimal blood pressure (BP) control remains a significant public health challenge, largely influenced by poor adherence to antihypertensive medications
title: Evaluation of Antihypertensive Medication Adherence and Its Association With Blood Pressure Control Among Hypertensive Patients Attending Outpatient Clinics in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . This study aimed to assess the prevalence of antihypertensive medication adherence and its association with BP control among hypertensive patients attending outpatient clinics in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. This analytical cross-sectional study included 436 hypertensive patients selected through consecutive sampling from tertiary care hospitals
title: Evaluation of Antihypertensive Medication Adherence and Its Association With Blood Pressure Control Among Hypertensive Patients Attending Outpatient Clinics in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and the validated Brief Medication Questionnaire. BP was measured using standardized procedures with a Medico Aneroid Sphygmomanometer AND-85 and the Omron M3 Comfort device (Omron Healthcare, Kyoto, Japan). BP control was defined as <140/90 mmHg
title: Evaluation of Antihypertensive Medication Adherence and Its Association With Blood Pressure Control Among Hypertensive Patients Attending Outpatient Clinics in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . BP control was defined as <140/90 mmHg. Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version 25 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY). The chi-square test and multivariable binary logistic regression were used to assess associations and adjust for confounders. Of 436 participants, 196 (44.95%) were adherent and 240 (55.05%) were nonadherent
title: Evaluation of Antihypertensive Medication Adherence and Its Association With Blood Pressure Control Among Hypertensive Patients Attending Outpatient Clinics in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . BP was controlled in 178 (40.83%) patients and uncontrolled in 258 (59.17%). Controlled BP was significantly higher among adherent patients (67.35%) compared with nonadherent patients (19.17%) (P < 0.001). Nonadherence was independently associated with uncontrolled hypertension (adjusted odds ratio = 3.82; 95% confidence interval: 2.45-5.97; P < 0.001)
title: Evaluation of Antihypertensive Medication Adherence and Its Association With Blood Pressure Control Among Hypertensive Patients Attending Outpatient Clinics in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Other significant predictors included age ≥60 years, diabetes mellitus, and longer duration of hypertension. Medication nonadherence is a major independent and modifiable determinant of poor BP control among hypertensive patients in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Targeted adherence-enhancing interventions are urgently needed in outpatient clinical settings.
title: Evaluation of Antihypertensive Medication Adherence and Its Association With Blood Pressure Control Among Hypertensive Patients Attending Outpatient Clinics in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: Prevalence, Awareness, Treatment, Control, and Determinants of Hypertension: A Population-Based Cross-Sectional Study in Southwest Iran.. Hypertension is the primary modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Our study aimed to assess the prevalence, awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension in southwest Iran
title: Prevalence, Awareness, Treatment, Control, and Determinants of Hypertension: A Population-Based Cross-Sectional Study in Southwest Iran.
journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

text: . This population-based cross-sectional study was conducted in the enrollment phase of Hoveyzeh cohort study in 10,009 adults aged 35-70 in southwest Iran between 2016 and 2018. Information on demographic characteristics socioeconomic status, Hypertension, comorbidities, family history of Hypertension was collected
title: Prevalence, Awareness, Treatment, Control, and Determinants of Hypertension: A Population-Based Cross-Sectional Study in Southwest Iran.
journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

text: . Logistic regression was employed to identify the factors associated with hypertension, as well as awareness, treatment, and control. The overall prevalence of hypertension was 26.4% (95% confidence interval [CI]:25.5, 27.3)
title: Prevalence, Awareness, Treatment, Control, and Determinants of Hypertension: A Population-Based Cross-Sectional Study in Southwest Iran.
journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

text: . Among the population, 86.04% (95%CI: 84.7, 87.3) were aware of their condition, 81.18% (95%CI: 79.5, 82.8) were receiving treatment, and blood pressure was controlled in 70.15% (95%CI: 68, 72.2) of the treated hypertensive patients
title: Prevalence, Awareness, Treatment, Control, and Determinants of Hypertension: A Population-Based Cross-Sectional Study in Southwest Iran.
journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

text: . In the adjusted model, older participants, those with low physical activity, individuals with a family history of hypertension, and patients with a history of diabetes or comorbidities of diabetes and dyslipidemia exhibited higher odds of having hypertension, as well as increased awareness. Additionally, being overweight or obese, married, and illiterate were associated with hypertension
title: Prevalence, Awareness, Treatment, Control, and Determinants of Hypertension: A Population-Based Cross-Sectional Study in Southwest Iran.
journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

text: . Based on gender, women are more aware of their hypertension, receive more treatment, and have better control than men. The prevalence of hypertension is relatively high; therefore, health promotion strategies, including lifestyle modifications to reduce overweight and obesity and to increase physical activity, are recommended.
title: Prevalence, Awareness, Treatment, Control, and Determinants of Hypertension: A Population-Based Cross-Sectional Study in Southwest Iran.
journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

text: Determinants of ordered physiological myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake patterns on non-cardiac PET/computed tomography: an ordinal regression analysis.. On routine non-cardiac PET/computed tomography (CT), myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) uptake demonstrates substantial interindividual variability and may complicate image interpretation
title: Determinants of ordered physiological myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake patterns on non-cardiac PET/computed tomography: an ordinal regression analysis.

text: . However, the systemic metabolic and clinical determinants associated with different myocardial FDG uptake patterns remain incompletely understood. This retrospective single-center study included 292 patients who underwent whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT following a minimum 6-h fast, without dedicated cardiac preparation
title: Determinants of ordered physiological myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake patterns on non-cardiac PET/computed tomography: an ordinal regression analysis.

text: . Myocardial FDG uptake was visually categorized into three ordered patterns: no/low, focal, and diffuse uptake. Clinical, laboratory, hemodynamic, and treatment-related variables were analyzed using proportional odds ordinal logistic regression to identify factors associated with increasing uptake categories
title: Determinants of ordered physiological myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake patterns on non-cardiac PET/computed tomography: an ordinal regression analysis.

text: . Exploratory prediction models for higher myocardial uptake patterns and diffuse uptake were additionally constructed to support clinical interpretability. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves and calibration analysis. Among the 292 patients, 122 (41.8%) demonstrated no/low uptake, 60 (20.5%) focal uptake, and 110 (37.7%) diffuse uptake
title: Determinants of ordered physiological myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake patterns on non-cardiac PET/computed tomography: an ordinal regression analysis.

text: . In multivariable ordinal logistic regression, blood pressure control remained strongly associated with myocardial uptake patterns
title: Determinants of ordered physiological myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake patterns on non-cardiac PET/computed tomography: an ordinal regression analysis.

text: . Compared with poor blood pressure control, no hypertension [odds ratio (OR) 0.155, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.072-0.334, P < 0.001] and good blood pressure control (OR 0.054, 95% CI 0.019-0.151, P < 0.001) were associated with lower odds of higher uptake categories
title: Determinants of ordered physiological myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake patterns on non-cardiac PET/computed tomography: an ordinal regression analysis.

text: . Absence of hormone therapy was also independently associated with lower odds of higher uptake patterns (OR 0.216, 95% CI 0.098-0.476, P < 0.001). Fasting glucose, diabetes, blood-pool maximum standardized uptake value, and chemotherapy were not independently significant after adjustment
title: Determinants of ordered physiological myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake patterns on non-cardiac PET/computed tomography: an ordinal regression analysis.

text: . The higher uptake model achieved an area under the curve of 0.898, while the diffuse uptake model achieved an area under the curve of 0.839, with satisfactory calibration performance. Myocardial FDG uptake patterns observed on routine non-cardiac PET/CT were associated with a graded spectrum of systemic metabolic and hemodynamic characteristics
title: Determinants of ordered physiological myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake patterns on non-cardiac PET/computed tomography: an ordinal regression analysis.

text: . These findings may provide a framework for more structured interpretation of myocardial FDG uptake in routine PET/CT imaging. These findings should be interpreted as observational associations rather than evidence of causal relationships.
title: Determinants of ordered physiological myocardial 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose uptake patterns on non-cardiac PET/computed tomography: an ordinal regression analysis.

text: Hypercaloric Diet Induces Cardiovascular Dysfunction Through Altered Purinergic Signaling on Atrial and Vascular Contractility.. Hypercaloric diet and obesity are strongly associated with cardiovascular dysfunction, diabetes and hypertension development mediated by sympathetic nervous system hyperactivity
title: Hypercaloric Diet Induces Cardiovascular Dysfunction Through Altered Purinergic Signaling on Atrial and Vascular Contractility.

text: . In addition to the adrenergic system, purinergic signaling has emerged as a relevant modulator of cardiovascular physiopathology. However, its role in hypercaloric diet-induced cardiovascular dysfunction remains incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of a hypercaloric diet on metabolic parameters, atrial purinergic modulation and vascular reactivity
title: Hypercaloric Diet Induces Cardiovascular Dysfunction Through Altered Purinergic Signaling on Atrial and Vascular Contractility.

text: . Rats fed the hypercaloric diet consumed a diet with ~31% greater caloric density than control animals that received a standard (3.5 kcal/g) pellet diet for 8 weeks. Metabolic and cardiovascular parameters were measured, and isolated right atria (RA), left atria (LA) and thoracic aortic vessels were used to evaluate function, contractility and vascular responsiveness
title: Hypercaloric Diet Induces Cardiovascular Dysfunction Through Altered Purinergic Signaling on Atrial and Vascular Contractility.

text: . A hypercaloric diet significantly increased body weight and visceral adiposity, with elevated systolic blood pressure (SBP) and cardiac hypertrophy, associated with alterations in glucose levels and insulin sensitivity. In isolated atria, a hypercaloric diet increased basal contractile force in the LA
title: Hypercaloric Diet Induces Cardiovascular Dysfunction Through Altered Purinergic Signaling on Atrial and Vascular Contractility.

text: . Also, ATP induced a biphasic response characterized by an initial negative inotropic effect (NIE) followed by a positive inotropic effect (PIE). A hypercaloric diet reduced ATP-mediated NIE and enhanced PIE in both atria, suggesting an altered balance between inhibitory-P1 and excitatory-P2 purinergic signaling
title: Hypercaloric Diet Induces Cardiovascular Dysfunction Through Altered Purinergic Signaling on Atrial and Vascular Contractility.

text: . At the vascular level, a hypercaloric diet impaired adenosine-mediated relaxation and increased contraction, indicating vascular hyperreactivity
title: Hypercaloric Diet Induces Cardiovascular Dysfunction Through Altered Purinergic Signaling on Atrial and Vascular Contractility.

text: . Collectively, these findings suggest that a hypercaloric diet induces cardiometabolic dysfunction associated with alterations in cardiovascular function linked to impaired P1/P2 purinergic regulation, contributing to obesity-associated cardiovascular remodeling and hypertension.
title: Hypercaloric Diet Induces Cardiovascular Dysfunction Through Altered Purinergic Signaling on Atrial and Vascular Contractility.

text: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.. Improvements in cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality have plateaued in the US and have increased among adults with fewer years of education, a pattern not seen in peer countries. Differences in health system performance managing CVD risk factors may be important in this disparity
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.

text: . To compare cardiovascular disease risk factor prevalence and management in the US, England, and South Korea over time and by education strata. This secondary analysis of a serial cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from adults 50 years or older from 3 countries during years ranging from 1998 to 2020. Data were analyzed from May 2025 to April 2026
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.

text: . Data were analyzed from May 2025 to April 2026. For each risk factor (cholesterol, blood pressure, and diabetes), the share at risk, the care cascade, and the share with uncontrolled risk were measured. This study assessed data from 120 678 adults (mean [SD] age, 63.5 [9.9] years; No. [weighted %], 54 167 [46%] male and 66 511 [54%] female)
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.

text: . For each risk factor, the US (n = 27 327) had higher shares at risk than England (n = 41 986) or South Korea (n = 51 365). For example, England had a smaller proportion at risk: 52% in period 4 (mean [SE], 11.1 [1.6] percentage points [pp] lower than in the US)
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.

text: . Cholesterol risk in South Korea increased from 46% in 2005 to 2008 to 51% in 2015 to 2020 (P for trend < .001), with levels ultimately similar to England but 12.1 (1.1) pp below the US. US patients at risk were more likely to be aware, treated, and have controlled risk using medications, resulting in more similar uncontrolled risk across countries
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.

text: . Because of higher control of condition risks in the US, the rates of uncontrolled cholesterol risk in the US and England were both 29% (mean [SE] difference, <0.1 [1.5] pp), and the rate uncontrolled in South Korea was 2.2 (1.0) pp higher than the US despite higher at-risk rates
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.

text: . South Korea achieved rapid gains in treatment and control, especially hypertension (6% controlled in 1998-2001 to 42% in 2005-2008, P for trend < .001) and cholesterol (6% controlled in 2005-2008 to 31% in 2015-2020, P for trend < .001). Across countries, risk was higher among adults without a college degree, but control rates among those at risk were similar by education strata
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.

text: . Diabetes risk increased substantially over time (15% to 22% in the US, 9% to 10% in England, and 13% to 19% in South Korea, P for trend < .001), whereas cholesterol and hypertension risk remained stable or decreased
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.

text: . In this repeated cross-sectional study of adults aged 50 years and older in the US, England, and South Korea, despite higher baseline risk, the US health system achieved comparable or better performance than England and South Korea in managing CVD risk factors
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.

text: . Differences in risk factor treatment did not explain disparities by country or education strata, suggesting that upstream risk accumulation, rather than care delivery, may be associated with increasing disparities in CVD risk.
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence and Control by Education Strata in Older Adults in 3 Countries.

text: Risk factors and management of adverse events in tooth extraction among medically compromised patients.. Tooth extraction in medically compromised adults presents significant clinical challenges due to an increased risk of bleeding, infection, delayed healing, and systemic complications
title: Risk factors and management of adverse events in tooth extraction among medically compromised patients.

text: . The review indicated that Diabetes mellitus affects 8-12% of dental patients and is associated with a 10-15% risk of intraoperative hypoglycemia, while anticoagulated patients experience postoperative bleeding in 8-12% of cases compared with 2-3% in controls
title: Risk factors and management of adverse events in tooth extraction among medically compromised patients.

text: . Hypertension affects up to 30% of adults, leading to perioperative blood pressure elevations in 20-25%, and asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease COPD occurs in 7-10% of patients with a 3-6% risk of bronchospasm. Immunosuppressed and transplant patients show postoperative infection rates as high as 20%
title: Risk factors and management of adverse events in tooth extraction among medically compromised patients.

text: . Five structured tables summarize medical classifications, safe clinical thresholds, emergency management, referral criteria, and a stepwise safety ladder for pre-, intra-, and postoperative care. The review emphasizes the importance of strict risk stratification and adherence to validated clinical cut-offs, including HbA1c <9%, INR ≤3.5, and blood pressure <180/110 mmHg
title: Risk factors and management of adverse events in tooth extraction among medically compromised patients.

text: . Implementation of standardized safety ladders and evidence-based thresholds can enhance patient safety, improve decision-making, and promote global consistency in managing medically compromised dental patients.
title: Risk factors and management of adverse events in tooth extraction among medically compromised patients.

text: Low-renin hypertension: a distinct phenotype enabling mechanism-based treatment.. Low-renin hypertension is increasingly recognized as a common and clinically important form of hypertension
title: Low-renin hypertension: a distinct phenotype enabling mechanism-based treatment.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

text: . Expanded screening for primary aldosteronism has revealed many individuals with suppressed renin who do not meet the diagnostic criteria for aldosterone excess, yet exhibit features consistent with sodium retention or increased mineralocorticoid activity
title: Low-renin hypertension: a distinct phenotype enabling mechanism-based treatment.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

text: . This review synthesizes evidence from targeted literature searches on the epidemiology, mechanisms, diagnostic challenges, and treatment of low-renin hypertension. Early studies proposed renin, in the presence of hypertension, as a marker of excess sodium retention and volume expansion, suggesting that renin could guide individualized therapy
title: Low-renin hypertension: a distinct phenotype enabling mechanism-based treatment.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

text: . Adoption of a renin-guided treatment approach was historically limited by assay variability and concerns regarding adverse effects from high-dose mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists
title: Low-renin hypertension: a distinct phenotype enabling mechanism-based treatment.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

text: . However, improvements in renin assay performance, increased accessibility and use of renin testing, and the availability of lower-dose and better-tolerated mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists have renewed interest in this strategy. Low-renin hypertension encompasses primary aldosteronism, conditions that mimic mineralocorticoid excess, and disorders of renal tubular sodium transport
title: Low-renin hypertension: a distinct phenotype enabling mechanism-based treatment.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

text: . Across this spectrum, patients respond more favorably to therapies targeting sodium retention: mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, epithelial sodium channel inhibitors, or thiazide diuretics, than to agents directed primarily at vasoconstriction
title: Low-renin hypertension: a distinct phenotype enabling mechanism-based treatment.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

text: . Recognition of low-renin hypertension as a distinct phenotype enables mechanism-based therapy and may improve blood pressure control, reduce medication burden, and mitigate long-term cardiovascular risk.
title: Low-renin hypertension: a distinct phenotype enabling mechanism-based treatment.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

text: Pre-diabetes and Diabetes in Heart Transplant Recipients: Epidemiological Insights from a Decade-Long Study.. Post-transplant diabetes mellitus (PTDM) is a serious complication after heart transplantation, with reported incidence rates ranging from 2% to 53% among solid organ transplant recipients
title: Pre-diabetes and Diabetes in Heart Transplant Recipients: Epidemiological Insights from a Decade-Long Study.
journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . Comprehensive epidemiological data on prediabetes (Pre-DM) and diabetes mellitus (DM) in heart transplant populations remain limited, particularly in Middle Eastern populations. This decade-long study investigated the prevalence of DM and Pre-DM among heart transplant recipients and evaluated selected intraoperative risk factors
title: Pre-diabetes and Diabetes in Heart Transplant Recipients: Epidemiological Insights from a Decade-Long Study.
journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . This retrospective cohort study included 250 heart transplant recipients who received post-transplant care at Dr. Masih Daneshvari Hospital, Tehran, Iran, between 2010 and 2020. Overall, 244 patients were included in the final analysis. Data included anthropometric measurements, cardiovascular parameters, and metabolic profiles
title: Pre-diabetes and Diabetes in Heart Transplant Recipients: Epidemiological Insights from a Decade-Long Study.
journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . Pre-DM and DM were diagnosed according to the American Diabetes Association criteria. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 26. The study population comprised 192 males (78.7%) and 52 females (21.3%), with a mean age of 38.46 ± 12.69 years. At transplantation, 36.5% of recipients had established DM, 29.1% had Pre-DM, and 34.4% had normal glucose metabolism
title: Pre-diabetes and Diabetes in Heart Transplant Recipients: Epidemiological Insights from a Decade-Long Study.
journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . Among patients with DM, 58.4% (52 of 89) were unaware of their diagnosis before transplantation. New-onset PTDM occurred in 6.8% of previously normoglycemic patients by 6 months
title: Pre-diabetes and Diabetes in Heart Transplant Recipients: Epidemiological Insights from a Decade-Long Study.
journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . The prevalence of hypertension differed markedly by glucose status (P < 0.001): 100% of the normal group had normal blood pressure, 97.2% of patients with Pre-DM had stage 1 hypertension, and 87.6% of patients with DM had stage 2 hypertension. Dyslipidemia, particularly low high-density lipoprotein (HDL), was present in all groups
title: Pre-diabetes and Diabetes in Heart Transplant Recipients: Epidemiological Insights from a Decade-Long Study.
journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . Pre-transplant hyperglycemia was associated with a numerically higher, but nonsignificant, mortality risk (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.371; 95% CI, 0.891 - 2.132; P = 0.162), which reversed after age adjustment (HR = 0.676; P = 0.083), consistent with negative confounding. Pre-transplant metabolic dysfunction was highly prevalent, and 58.4% of diabetic recipients were unaware of their diagnosis
title: Pre-diabetes and Diabetes in Heart Transplant Recipients: Epidemiological Insights from a Decade-Long Study.
journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: . Although the association with mortality was nonsignificant and reversed after adjustment for age, these findings underscore the need for systematic pre-transplant metabolic screening, post-transplant glucose monitoring, and multidisciplinary care in heart transplant recipients.
title: Pre-diabetes and Diabetes in Heart Transplant Recipients: Epidemiological Insights from a Decade-Long Study.
journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism

text: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting hypertension risk in patients with psoriasis.. Hypertension is a common yet frequently underdiagnosed comorbidity in psoriasis patients. Early identification and blood pressure control are critical to improving outcomes
title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting hypertension risk in patients with psoriasis.

text: . Although machine learning (ML) is widely used in disease prediction, a model for hypertension risk within the psoriasis population remains unavailable. This study aims to develop and validate such a model in patients with psoriasis
title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting hypertension risk in patients with psoriasis.

text: . In this retrospective study, 2,957 psoriasis patients from a single tertiary center were used for model development and internal validation, and 567 psoriasis participants from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) served as the external validation cohort
title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting hypertension risk in patients with psoriasis.

text: . After missForest imputation and consensus feature selection, the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied to the training set only. Nine machine learning algorithms were trained and evaluated for discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation. Nine nonredundant predictors were retained
title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting hypertension risk in patients with psoriasis.

text: . Nine nonredundant predictors were retained. The SMOTE-enhanced logistic regression model showed the most balanced and generalizable performance, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.850, 0.816, and 0.789 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively, together with acceptable calibration and favorable net clinical benefit
title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting hypertension risk in patients with psoriasis.

text: . SHAP identified age, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus as the leading contributors. The final model was deployed as a publicly accessible web application
title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting hypertension risk in patients with psoriasis.

text: . This interpretable and externally validated machine learning model provides a practical tool for hypertension risk stratification in psoriasis patients and may support earlier identification and individualized preventive management in clinical practice.
title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting hypertension risk in patients with psoriasis.

text: Renal denervation triage tool: a practical approach to the management of resistant hypertension.. Despite the availability of medications and advocacy for lifestyle interventions, over half of individuals with hypertension do not achieve recommended treatment goals owing to limitations with medications, such as high cost, side effects, and poor adherence
title: Renal denervation triage tool: a practical approach to the management of resistant hypertension.

text: . Renal denervation (RDN), a minimally invasive endovascular procedure targeting sympathetic nerves near the renal arteries, is gaining recognition as a safe and effective adjunctive therapy for blood pressure control in resistant hypertension, supported by several clinical trials and meta-analyses
title: Renal denervation triage tool: a practical approach to the management of resistant hypertension.

text: . Recognising the clinical complexity of resistant hypertension, a group of hypertension experts from India convened to develop an "RDN triage tool" to guide clinicians in selecting appropriate candidates for RDN therapy based on demographics, blood pressure, renal function, and cardiac status
title: Renal denervation triage tool: a practical approach to the management of resistant hypertension.

text: . This approach is supported by clinical evidence and expert recommendations and aims to optimise patient selection for RDN therapy, aid clinical decision-making, minimise risks, and enhance patient outcomes.
title: Renal denervation triage tool: a practical approach to the management of resistant hypertension.

text: Perioperative nursing care for a patient undergoing image-guided planned autologous islet transplantation after total pancreatectomy: A case report.. Total pancreatectomy (TP) often leads to insulin-deficient diabetes, including unstable "brittle diabetes." Autologous islet transplantation during or after TP can prevent or treat diabetes by reinfusing functional islets into the portal vein
title: Perioperative nursing care for a patient undergoing image-guided planned autologous islet transplantation after total pancreatectomy: A case report.

text: . This case report details the perioperative nursing strategies for a patient undergoing image-guided planned autologous islet transplantation following TP. A 64-year-old male with pancreatic cancer, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension underwent TP and initial autologous islet transplantation but required a second transplantation due to poor graft function
title: Perioperative nursing care for a patient undergoing image-guided planned autologous islet transplantation after total pancreatectomy: A case report.

text: . Preoperatively, he exhibited fluctuating blood glucose (8.9-14.5 mmol/L) and anxiety about surgical outcomes. The patient was diagnosed with recurrent pancreatic cancer post-TP and chemotherapy, compounded by insulin-dependent diabetes and suboptimal islet function necessitating secondary transplantation
title: Perioperative nursing care for a patient undergoing image-guided planned autologous islet transplantation after total pancreatectomy: A case report.

text: . A multidisciplinary approach included meticulous preoperative islet quality control, intraoperative portal vein catheterization under ultrasound guidance, and dynamic monitoring of portal pressure. Postoperative care featured anticoagulation (heparin/low-molecular-weight heparin), glycemic management via insulin micropump, and thromboprophylaxis using intermittent pneumatic compression
title: Perioperative nursing care for a patient undergoing image-guided planned autologous islet transplantation after total pancreatectomy: A case report.

text: . Psychological support and preoperative education alleviated patient anxiety. Posttransplantation, blood glucose stabilized (3.9-7.7 mmol/L), enabling discontinuation of exogenous insulin. The patient was discharged on day 18 without complications such as thrombosis or hemorrhage
title: Perioperative nursing care for a patient undergoing image-guided planned autologous islet transplantation after total pancreatectomy: A case report.

text: . Multidisciplinary collaboration, tailored nursing interventions, and rigorous complication prevention ensured successful outcomes. This case highlights the critical role of structured perioperative care in achieving insulin independence after complex islet transplantation.
title: Perioperative nursing care for a patient undergoing image-guided planned autologous islet transplantation after total pancreatectomy: A case report.

text: Intensive blood-pressure control for the prevention of major cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes: Rationale, design and baseline characteristics of the OPTIMAL-DIABETES randomized trial.. Evidence on the beneficial effects of intensive blood pressure (BP) control is still uncertain in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), particularly in an ethnically diverse population
title: Intensive blood-pressure control for the prevention of major cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes: Rationale, design and baseline characteristics of the OPTIMAL-DIABETES randomized trial.

text: . To assess whether a target of systolic BP (SBP) < 120 mm Hg reduces major cardiovascular (CV) events compared with a target of SBP < 140 mm Hg in patients with T2D and high CV risk
title: Intensive blood-pressure control for the prevention of major cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes: Rationale, design and baseline characteristics of the OPTIMAL-DIABETES randomized trial.

text: . This is a multicentre, 2-arm, open-label, randomized clinical trial, in which individuals aged ≥50 years, with a SBP between 130 and 180 mm Hg, T2D and high CV risk are randomly assigned to a target SBP of <120 or <140 mm Hg
title: Intensive blood-pressure control for the prevention of major cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes: Rationale, design and baseline characteristics of the OPTIMAL-DIABETES randomized trial.

text: . The primary endpoint is a composite of CV mortality, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina, or hospitalization for heart failure. Maximum follow-up duration is 48 months. Main analysis will follow the intention-to-treat principle. From August 2019 through October 2021, 9,476 participants from 33 sites in Brazil were enrolled
title: Intensive blood-pressure control for the prevention of major cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes: Rationale, design and baseline characteristics of the OPTIMAL-DIABETES randomized trial.

text: . The overall mean age was 64.74 years (standard deviation [SD], 8.16), and 5,871 (62.0%) were women. Race distribution was diverse with 4,025/9,467 (42.5%) self-described as mixed-race, 3,971/9,467 (41.9%) as White, and 1,374/9,467 (14.5%) as Black. Overall, 2,697/9,475 (28.5%) and 371 (3.9%) had established and subclinical CV disease, respectively
title: Intensive blood-pressure control for the prevention of major cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes: Rationale, design and baseline characteristics of the OPTIMAL-DIABETES randomized trial.

text: . Antihypertensive medication was prescribed to 9,104/9,473 (96.1%) of the participants. Mean SBP is 145.89 mm Hg (SD, 12.13) and mean diastolic BP is 79.48 mm Hg (SD, 10.61)
title: Intensive blood-pressure control for the prevention of major cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes: Rationale, design and baseline characteristics of the OPTIMAL-DIABETES randomized trial.

text: . The OPTIMAL-DIABETES trial results will provide valuable evidence regarding the benefits and risks of antihypertensive treatment to an SBP < 120 vs <140 mm Hg in a diverse population of patients with T2D, elevated BP, and high CV risk. The trial is registered at the ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04040634).
title: Intensive blood-pressure control for the prevention of major cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes: Rationale, design and baseline characteristics of the OPTIMAL-DIABETES randomized trial.

text: Hyperandrogenism Synergizes With Obesity to Increase the Risk of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy After Frozen Embryo Transfer.. Hyperandrogenism has been linked to increased preeclampsia risk, but its independent role remains unclear due to confounding by polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
title: Hyperandrogenism Synergizes With Obesity to Increase the Risk of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy After Frozen Embryo Transfer.

text: . This retrospective cohort study investigated whether non-PCOS hyperandrogenism is associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) and adverse pregnancy outcomes in women undergoing frozen embryo transfer (FET), and whether hyperandrogenism synergizes with overweight/obesity to further increase these risks
title: Hyperandrogenism Synergizes With Obesity to Increase the Risk of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy After Frozen Embryo Transfer.

text: . We analyzed data from 1556 infertile women who underwent FET at Ruijin Hospital and delivered between January 2015 and December 2022. Participants were classified into four groups based on the presence of hyperandrogenism and overweight/obesity: controls (n = 1201), hyperandrogenism only (n = 116), overweight/obesity only (n = 209), and both hyperandrogenism and overweight/obesity (n = 30)
title: Hyperandrogenism Synergizes With Obesity to Increase the Risk of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy After Frozen Embryo Transfer.

text: . Multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations with HDP and related adverse outcomes
title: Hyperandrogenism Synergizes With Obesity to Increase the Risk of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy After Frozen Embryo Transfer.

text: . In multivariable analyses, overweight/obesity was independently associated with an increased risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.62) and gestational hypertension (aOR 3.45), whereas the coexistence of overweight/obesity and hyperandrogenism was strongly associated with higher risks of preeclampsia (13.3%, aOR 7.53), preterm birth (23.3%, aOR 3.67), and
title: Hyperandrogenism Synergizes With Obesity to Increase the Risk of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy After Frozen Embryo Transfer.

text: aOR 7.53), preterm birth (23.3%, aOR 3.67), and cervical length shortening (CLS) (6.7%) compared to the controls
title: Hyperandrogenism Synergizes With Obesity to Increase the Risk of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy After Frozen Embryo Transfer.

text: . These results suggest that in women without PCOS undergoing FET, the coexistence of hyperandrogenism and overweight/obesity identifies a high-risk hypertensive phenotype characterized by a substantially elevated risk of preeclampsia
title: Hyperandrogenism Synergizes With Obesity to Increase the Risk of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy After Frozen Embryo Transfer.

text: . Moreover, our findings may indicate synergistic effects of endocrine and metabolic disturbances on pregnancy-related blood pressure dysregulation and could facilitate early risk stratification for HDP.
title: Hyperandrogenism Synergizes With Obesity to Increase the Risk of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy After Frozen Embryo Transfer.

text: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Its Determinants Among Older Adults in India: Evidence From a Nationally Representative Survey.. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality, posing a major challenge to its rapidly aging demographic. Early identification of individuals at high risk for future cardiovascular events is paramount for implementing timely preventative strategies
title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Its Determinants Among Older Adults in India: Evidence From a Nationally Representative Survey.

text: . However, comprehensive population-level estimates using validated assessment tools remain limited in this setting. This study was to ascertain the prevalence and determinants of persons at high risk of experiencing any cardiovascular event within the next 10 years among older adults in India
title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Its Determinants Among Older Adults in India: Evidence From a Nationally Representative Survey.

text: . We analyzed data from the Longitudinal Aging Study in India Wave-1 (2017-2018), including 64,266 participants aged 40-74 years. We used the World Health Organization CVD Risk Chart 2019 version, a nonlaboratory-based risk assessment model, to stratify cardiovascular risk based on age, sex, smoking status, systolic blood pressure, and body mass index
title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Its Determinants Among Older Adults in India: Evidence From a Nationally Representative Survey.

text: . Weighted prevalence of high CVD risk ( ≥ 20%) was 2.67% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.44, 2.91), while intermediate risk (10% to < 20%) was 28.41% (95% CI: 27.60, 29.25). Overall, 31.08% had ≥ 10% risk. In the diabetes and hypertension (HTN) subgroups, high risk ( ≥ 20%) was 3.53% and 4.36%, respectively
title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Its Determinants Among Older Adults in India: Evidence From a Nationally Representative Survey.

text: . Adjusted analysis showed significantly higher odds of high risk among alcohol users, individuals with prior HTN, and widowed/separated participants. Conversely, college education and current employment were associated with significantly lower odds
title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Its Determinants Among Older Adults in India: Evidence From a Nationally Representative Survey.

text: . Over 3 in 100 Indian adults aged ≥ 40 years with diabetes or HTN face a ≥ 20% 10-year CVD risk, highlighting an urgent need for targeted primary care interventions. Prioritizing alcohol cessation, aggressive blood pressure management, and glycemic control through universal standard care coverage is essential to mitigate this burden.
title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Its Determinants Among Older Adults in India: Evidence From a Nationally Representative Survey.
