text: Protocol for Monitoring Postpartum Hypertension Outcomes via a Smartphone App (MOMitor): Ecological Momentary Assessment.. Postpartum hypertension defined as elevated blood pressure after childbirth, affects approximately 20% of women after delivery
title: Protocol for Monitoring Postpartum Hypertension Outcomes via a Smartphone App (MOMitor): Ecological Momentary Assessment.

text: . Digital health interventions that include remote monitoring therefore, present an important opportunity to facilitate regular blood pressure assessment in this high-risk population. The primary objective is to assess within- and between-person changes in hypertension status over the first 6 weeks postpartum using a smartphone-based ecological momentary assessment protocol
title: Protocol for Monitoring Postpartum Hypertension Outcomes via a Smartphone App (MOMitor): Ecological Momentary Assessment.

text: . The secondary objective is to characterize the trajectory of hypertension indicators across the 6-week period and to compare hypertension screening results from week one and week six within participants. This study uses a time-series design using data from prospectively enrolled patients within a large health system
title: Protocol for Monitoring Postpartum Hypertension Outcomes via a Smartphone App (MOMitor): Ecological Momentary Assessment.

text: . Patients eligible for recruitment were women aged 18 years or older who spoke English, owned a smartphone, had a liveborn neonate, and were willing to download an app and respond to survey questions within the app
title: Protocol for Monitoring Postpartum Hypertension Outcomes via a Smartphone App (MOMitor): Ecological Momentary Assessment.

text: . Throughout the study period, all participants received hypertension screening items that asked whether their blood pressure was greater than 140/90 mm Hg and whether they felt dizzy or lightheaded, short of breath, or had a severe headache. A subset of participants were additionally asked to report their blood pressure readings
title: Protocol for Monitoring Postpartum Hypertension Outcomes via a Smartphone App (MOMitor): Ecological Momentary Assessment.

text: . We estimate within- and between-participant effects using a generalized linear mixed model for a positive hypertension screen during weeks one through six. The model includes both fixed and random effects, controlling for age, race, marital status, education, insurance status, mode of delivery, total number of pregnancies, and history of diabetes mellitus
title: Protocol for Monitoring Postpartum Hypertension Outcomes via a Smartphone App (MOMitor): Ecological Momentary Assessment.

text: . The study was funded July 2021 and data collection was initiated in November 2021. Data collection for this study, per protocol, was completed in June 2025, though other participants continue to be enrolled in the ongoing parent study. Data analysis is expected to be completed by Spring 2026 with publication planned for Summer 2026
title: Protocol for Monitoring Postpartum Hypertension Outcomes via a Smartphone App (MOMitor): Ecological Momentary Assessment.

text: . The study findings will provide insight into trajectories of hypertension outcomes in postpartum women and the utility for smartphone app-based remote blood pressure monitoring among postpartum women whose blood pressure was regularly tracked
title: Protocol for Monitoring Postpartum Hypertension Outcomes via a Smartphone App (MOMitor): Ecological Momentary Assessment.

text: . Findings will provide evidence to support whether widespread implementation of this digital health surveillance approach to improve outcomes in maternal health, especially in the postpartum period, is clinically warranted.
title: Protocol for Monitoring Postpartum Hypertension Outcomes via a Smartphone App (MOMitor): Ecological Momentary Assessment.

text: Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity and strain echocardiography in neonates: impact of maternal diabetes and hypertension.. The arterial wall tends to stiffen owing to prolonged exposure to cardiovascular disease risk factors such as high blood pressure, hyperglycemia, and chronic inflammation
title: Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity and strain echocardiography in neonates: impact of maternal diabetes and hypertension.

text: . Epidemiological research has demonstrated that maternal factors, demographic characteristics, and clinical data influence arterial stiffness and echocardiographic findings
title: Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity and strain echocardiography in neonates: impact of maternal diabetes and hypertension.

text: . This study aimed to evaluate the association between arterial stiffness and echocardiographic findings with maternal factors and demographic and clinical characteristics in infants of mothers with gestational diabetes or hypertension during the neonatal period
title: Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity and strain echocardiography in neonates: impact of maternal diabetes and hypertension.

text: . A total of 67 newborns between 12-29 days of age, including 15 neonates of hypertensive mothers, 26 neonates of diabetic mothers, and 26 neonates in the control group, were included. Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV) was used as a marker of arterial stiffness and measurements were performed using echocardiography
title: Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity and strain echocardiography in neonates: impact of maternal diabetes and hypertension.

text: . Basic echocardiographic evaluations and atrial and ventricular strain assessments were performed. The mean cfPWV value of infants of diabetic mothers (6.34 m/s) was significantly higher than that of infants of hypertensive mothers (4.65 m/s) and the control group (4.56 m/s) (p<0.001)
title: Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity and strain echocardiography in neonates: impact of maternal diabetes and hypertension.

text: . Multivariate linear regression analysis revealed that increasing maternal age and the presence of diabetes in the mother were predictors of carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity values. The right ventricular free wall longitudinal strain z-scores were higher in hypertensive infants, while no significant difference was found in other strain measurements
title: Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity and strain echocardiography in neonates: impact of maternal diabetes and hypertension.

text: . The analysis of arterial stiffness in infants of diabetic mothers, infants of hypertensive mothers, and controls showed that advanced maternal age and maternal diabetes were particularly associated with increased cfPWV. This study highlights the potential influence of maternal metabolic status on neonatal cardiac morphology and vascular function
title: Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity and strain echocardiography in neonates: impact of maternal diabetes and hypertension.

text: . Based on the data presented, further research is warranted to investigate whether the observed effects on arterial stiffness in infants of diabetic mothers persist into older ages and have long-term implications for the health of these patients.
title: Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity and strain echocardiography in neonates: impact of maternal diabetes and hypertension.

text: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . The inaugural 2025 Cardiometabolic Summit in Saclay, France, aimed to (i) disseminate the latest research on cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs) from the Maghreb and/or Middle East and North Africa region; (ii) discuss CMD management and provide clinical practice suggestions for improving adherence and reducing clinical inertia; and (iii) suggest policy and clinical practice initiatives to improve
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: and clinical practice initiatives to improve outcomes in patients with CMDs
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide, with 80% of CVD fatalities occurring in low- and middle-income countries. This trend is mirrored in Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia, three countries in the Maghreb region. In these countries, CMDs, such as type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and hypertension, have high prevalence and are undertreated
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . At the Cardiometabolic Summit, attended by 110 clinicians from Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia, regional CMD epidemiology and management data were presented, along with evidence on regional research initiatives to reduce the burden of CMDs and CVD and how Ramadan fasting affects adults with T2DM
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . Context-specific holistic strategies to improve the management of patients with multimorbidities were reviewed, including targeting modifiable risk factors to prevent T2DM and hypertension. Two barriers to optimal CMD management were addressed: (i) poor patient treatment adherence and (ii) clinician-related therapeutic inertia, noting the latter may be a greater contributor to poor outcomes
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . Prescription of single-pill combinations was recommended for initial blood pressure control, and a cost-effective sulfonylurea plus a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor or glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist (whenever feasible) was recommended for glycaemic control plus cardiorenal protection. Polypills may be appropriate where intervention for additional CMDs is required
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . Strategies for enhancing patient adherence and opportunities for reducing therapeutic inertia were presented. Finally, policy actions and clinical practice priorities were suggested. These steps provide a realistic path towards reducing CMD and CVD burden in the Maghreb
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . Cardiovascular disease is a collection of disorders that affect the heart and blood vessels, and the leading cause of death worldwide. Cardiometabolic disorders refer to a group of interconnected conditions (type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension and dyslipidaemia) that are known to increase the risk of cardiovascular complications
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . Cardiometabolic disorders often remain underdiagnosed and undertreated, particularly in the Maghreb region, where there is a pressing need for enhanced patient care and outcomes. To address this critical issue, 110 clinicians from Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia convened at the inaugural Cardiometabolic Summit in Saclay, France, in April 2025
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . The Summit showcased the latest research findings on cardiometabolic disorders from the Maghreb and the broader Middle East and North Africa region. It also provided clinical practice recommendations for Maghreb-based healthcare professionals, with an emphasis on strategies to improve treatment adherence (i.e
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . how well the patient follows their prescribed treatment) and reduce clinical inertia (i.e. clinician-based delays in start or intensifying treatment)
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . Key initiatives proposed to enhance cardiometabolic disorder outcomes included the strengthening of public healthcare policies, the adaptation of global guidelines to local contexts, increased investment in professional training and patient engagement, and the expansion of both regional and global collaborations
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: . This strategic call-to-action aims to catalyse a significant transformation of cardiometabolic care, ultimately leading to improved outcomes for patients with cardiometabolic disorders in the Maghreb region, and remains the main objective of this manuscript.
title: A Summary of Cardiometabolic Disorders in the Maghreb: Insights from the 2025 Saclay Cardiometabolic Summit.

text: Sex-specific differences in clinical characteristics and organ damage in Hypertensive Urgencies.. Acute blood pressure disorders are a common yet heterogeneous clinical challenge in the Emergency Department (ED), often requiring rapid assessment and risk stratification
title: Sex-specific differences in clinical characteristics and organ damage in Hypertensive Urgencies.

text: . Among these, Hypertensive Urgency (HU) is a frequent presentation, characterized by severely elevated blood pressure (BP) without acute hypertension-mediated organ damage (HMOD). Despite its clinical relevance, sex-related differences in HU remain poorly understood.
title: Sex-specific differences in clinical characteristics and organ damage in Hypertensive Urgencies.

text: . . This study aimed to investigate sex differences in clinical presentation, BP control and HMOD prevalence in subjects presenting with HU. Methods. A multicentric prospective study was conducted, enrolling symptomatic patients with HU, admitted to six Italian EDs. They were assessed within 72 h after ED discharge to evaluate BP control and to detect subclinical HMOD.
title: Sex-specific differences in clinical characteristics and organ damage in Hypertensive Urgencies.

text: . A total of 257 patients were enrolled, including 134 females (52%). The mean age was 59.7 ± 14 years, with women being significantly older than men (62.4 ± 15 vs. 56.8 ± 13, p value = 0.002). Men were more frequently active smokers and had a higher rate of diabetes and obesity. They also had higher diastolic BP, at both ED admission and discharge, and higher systo-diastolic BP at the 72-h visit
title: Sex-specific differences in clinical characteristics and organ damage in Hypertensive Urgencies.

text: . Male sex was independently associated with increased rate of HMOD-regardless of the specific organ involved-and with poor BP control at 72 h from ED discharge. . Compared to women, men with HU exhibited higher BP levels and poorer BP control at 72 h. They also showed a higher prevalence and greater severity of HMOD. Male sex emerged as independently associated with HMOD.
title: Sex-specific differences in clinical characteristics and organ damage in Hypertensive Urgencies.

text: Region-specific vulnerability to vascular risk factors and modifiable protective influences on white matter hyperintensities.. Region-specific vulnerabilities to single and combined vascular risk factors and the role of modifiable behaviors in white matter hyperintensity (WMH) progression remain unclear
title: Region-specific vulnerability to vascular risk factors and modifiable protective influences on white matter hyperintensities.

text: . We aimed to characterize neuroanatomical patterns of WMH vulnerability and to identify subgroup-specific factors associated with lower burden and slower progression
title: Region-specific vulnerability to vascular risk factors and modifiable protective influences on white matter hyperintensities.

text: . We included 1146 participants (60.9% female; age 45-86 years) from the Beijing Aging Brain Rejuvenation Initiative (2008-2023), all of whom underwent standardized magnetic resonance imaging together with clinical and behavioral assessments. We used age- and sex-specific centile curves of WMH burden to examine associations with vascular risk factors, their combinations, and behavioral profiles
title: Region-specific vulnerability to vascular risk factors and modifiable protective influences on white matter hyperintensities.

text: . Here we show that vascular risk factors have region-specific associations with WMH burden: hypertension is linked mainly to periventricular frontal regions, whereas smoking is linked to deep subcortical regions. Combined risk factors show broader involvement, especially in periventricular frontal regions and the corpus callosum
title: Region-specific vulnerability to vascular risk factors and modifiable protective influences on white matter hyperintensities.

text: . Better control of some vascular risk factors is associated with lower burden (e.g., diabetes: approximately 2.0 mL lower; hyperlipidemia: approximately 2.3 mL lower) and slower progression (e.g., controlled total cholesterol: 0.176 vs. 0.939 mL/year, p = 0.007), and behavioral associations differ across risk profiles
title: Region-specific vulnerability to vascular risk factors and modifiable protective influences on white matter hyperintensities.

text: . More frequent leisure activity is associated with lower burden mainly in obesity, whereas lower depressive symptoms are associated with lower burden or slower progression in some vascular-risk subgroups. Vascular risk factors and behavioral factors show subgroup- and region-specific associations with WMH burden and progression
title: Region-specific vulnerability to vascular risk factors and modifiable protective influences on white matter hyperintensities.

text: . These findings may help refine risk stratification, improve understanding of vulnerability patterns, and inform future intervention studies. White matter hyperintensities are small white areas that are seen on a type of brain scan called MRI. They are indicative of changes in the brain and are often seen in scans from older adults
title: Region-specific vulnerability to vascular risk factors and modifiable protective influences on white matter hyperintensities.

text: . They are linked to higher risks of developing stroke and dementia. However, it is unclear whether different risk factors that influence the blood vascular system, such as high blood pressure or smoking, affect different brain regions in different ways. We evaluated brain MRI plus health and lifestyle information from 1,146 adults
title: Region-specific vulnerability to vascular risk factors and modifiable protective influences on white matter hyperintensities.

text: . We found that different risk factors were linked to different patterns of brain change, and that multiple risk factors were linked to more widespread damage. Better control of some risk factors, together with favorable lifestyle and emotional factors, was linked to less presence of disease or slower progression. These findings may support more personalized disease prevention and care.
title: Region-specific vulnerability to vascular risk factors and modifiable protective influences on white matter hyperintensities.

text: The Effects of Combined Antihypertensive and Antidiabetic Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.. Hypertension and diabetes frequently coexist, yet the net clinical impact of intentionally combining antihypertensive (AHTN) and antidiabetic (ADA) therapies on cardiovascular (CV) outcomes is uncertain
title: The Effects of Combined Antihypertensive and Antidiabetic Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Here we quantified the effects of AHTN and ADA co-therapy on CV and blood pressure (BP)/heart rate (HR) outcomes. The MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus databases were searched from database inception through November 2025. Eligible studies were randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing combined AHTN+ADA versus AHTN or ADA alone and reporting CV events and/or (BP)/(HR) outcomes
title: The Effects of Combined Antihypertensive and Antidiabetic Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% CIs were pooled using random-effects models. A prespecified exploratory analysis synthesised CV outcome trials of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) versus placebo. Nine RCTs (n = 13 955 subjects) met inclusion criteria
title: The Effects of Combined Antihypertensive and Antidiabetic Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Compared with AHTN alone, AHTN+ADA reduced composite CV events as defined in each trial, CV death, and HF hospitalisation. Combination therapy achieved modest but significant BP reductions (systolic -2.57 mmHg; diastolic -1.03 mmHg) without excess risk of hypotension, and HR effects were combination specific
title: The Effects of Combined Antihypertensive and Antidiabetic Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Exploratory analysis of seven GLP-1 RA trials (n = ~56 000) showed reductions in composite CV events and CV death versus placebo, but no effect on HF hospitalisation. AHTN+ADA co-therapy was associated with improved CV outcomes and modest BP reduction compared with monotherapy, with effects predominantly driven by SGLT2 inhibitor-based combinations
title: The Effects of Combined Antihypertensive and Antidiabetic Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: . Exploratory evidence indicates that GLP-1 RAs provide complementary reductions in CV outcomes and mortality but not HF events. Together, these findings support phenotype-guided integration of ADA with guideline-directed AHTN in cardiometabolic disease.
title: The Effects of Combined Antihypertensive and Antidiabetic Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

text: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].. Hypertension is one of the most important comorbidities of diabetes, significantly contributing to increased mortality and leading to macrovascular and microvascular complications
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . When assessing the medical priorities for patients with diabetes, treating hypertension should be a primary consideration. In the present review practical approaches to hypertension in diabetes, including individualized targets for preventing specific complications are discussed according to the current evidence and guidelines
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . Blood pressure values of 120-129/70-79 mm Hg are associated with the best outcome; most importantly, at least blood pressure values < 140/90 mm Hg should be achieved in most patients
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . Most patients with diabetes require combination therapy to achieve blood pressure goals; agents with clear evidence of cardiovascular risk reduction should be used (including, besides angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers, dihydropyridine calcium channel antagonists and thiazide diuretics), preferable in single pill combinations
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . Once the target is achieved, antihypertensive drugs should be continued. The use of SGLT‑2 inhibitors and GLP‑1 receptor agonists contribute to blood pressure lowering in diabetes. This also holds true für the newly available combined GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist tirzepatide
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . Since the last release of these guidelines evidence from clinical trials has become available that supports more stringent blood pressure control in diabetes, which is reflected in international guidelines and has also been adopted in these recommendations. The individualization of blood pressure management, however, remains a core recommendation of the Austrian Diabetes Association
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . Hypertonie ist eine sehr häufige Komorbidität bei Diabetes mellitus, die – wenn unzureichend behandelt – signifikant zur erhöhten Mortalität und zum Auftreten von mikrovaskulären und makrovaskulären Komplikationen beiträgt
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . Blutdruckzielwerte um 120–129/70–79 mm Hg waren in den Studien mit der besten Prognose assoziiert, wobei die Blutdruckzielwerte je nach Alter und Komorbiditäten individualisiert werden sollten; besonders wichtig ist, dass ein Blutdruck < 140/90 mm Hg erreicht wird
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . Für die meisten Menschen mit Diabetes ist eine Kombinationstherapie notwendig, wobei Medikamente mit gut evidenzbasierter Reduktion des kardiovaskulären Risikos (neben ACE-Hemmern und Angiotensinrezeptorblockern Dihydropyridin-Calciumantagonisten und Thiaziddiuretika) eingesetzt werden sollten, präferenziell als Kombinationspräparate
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . Nach Erreichung der Zielwerte muss die antihypertensive Therapie fortgeführt werden, wobei regelmäßige Selbstmessungen des Blutdrucks für die Optimierung der Blutdruckeinstellung sehr hilfreich sind. SGLT-2-Inhibitoren oder GLP-1-Rezeptoragonisten tragen ebenfalls zur Blutdrucksenkung bei Diabetes bei
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . Dies gilt auch für den seit der letzten Auflage der Leitlinien neu verfügbaren kombinierten GLP-1/GIP-Rezeptoragonisten Tirzepatid
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: . Seit der letzten Auflage der Leitlinien zeigten Interventionsstudien Vorteile einer intensiveren Blutdrucksenkung bei Typ-2-Diabetes, was sich in den aktuellen Leitlinien internationaler Gesellschaften widerspiegelt und auch in die vorliegenden Empfehlungen übernommen wird; die Individualisierung der Blutdrucktherapie bleibt aber eine Kernempfehlung der Österreichischen Diabetes-Gesellschaft.
title: [Individualizing antihypertensive therapy in diabetes mellitus. Guidelines of the Austrian Diabetes Association (Update 2026)].

text: Diastolic dysfunction is equally common in pre-diabetes and diabetes and associated with concomitant cardiometabolic risk factors.. To investigate the prevalence of diastolic dysfunction and associated risk factors in pre-diabetes and diabetes in the general population
title: Diastolic dysfunction is equally common in pre-diabetes and diabetes and associated with concomitant cardiometabolic risk factors.

text: . Diastolic function was assessed by transthoracic echocardiography in a cross-sectional sample of 3840 men and women aged 50-64 years from the Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study. Anthropometry, medical history, blood pressure, biochemistry and coronary atherosclerosis assessed by CT were recorded. Population-specific reference ranges were applied
title: Diastolic dysfunction is equally common in pre-diabetes and diabetes and associated with concomitant cardiometabolic risk factors.

text: . Diastolic function was compared across glycaemic groups and analysed in relation to risk factors. Normoglycaemia was present in 82%, pre-diabetes in 12% and diabetes in 6%. Diastolic function was impaired (p<0.001) in pre-diabetes and diabetes, with higher prevalence of abnormal diastolic variables in pre-diabetes (30%) and diabetes (33%) than in normoglycaemia (21%)
title: Diastolic dysfunction is equally common in pre-diabetes and diabetes and associated with concomitant cardiometabolic risk factors.

text: . Among participants with pre-diabetes/diabetes, diastolic dysfunction was associated with hypertension and more severe coronary atherosclerosis (p<0.001)
title: Diastolic dysfunction is equally common in pre-diabetes and diabetes and associated with concomitant cardiometabolic risk factors.

text: . In multivariable analyses, waist circumference (OR 1.034, 95% CI 1.013 to 1.054) and high Coronary Artery Calcium Score (OR 2.897, 95% CI 1.373 to 6.113) were independently associated with diastolic dysfunction, also after exclusion of subjects with ischaemic heart disease
title: Diastolic dysfunction is equally common in pre-diabetes and diabetes and associated with concomitant cardiometabolic risk factors.

text: . In those without coronary atherosclerosis and hypertension, systolic blood pressure was the only independent risk factor (OR 1.027, 95% CI 1.002 to 1.053). Diastolic dysfunction was as common in pre-diabetes as in diabetes and was mainly associated with central adiposity, hypertension and coronary atherosclerosis
title: Diastolic dysfunction is equally common in pre-diabetes and diabetes and associated with concomitant cardiometabolic risk factors.

text: . In individuals without coronary atherosclerosis or hypertension, systolic blood pressure was still the only independent predictor. These findings challenge the concept of a clinically relevant isolated diabetic cardiomyopathy and highlight the importance of early and comprehensive cardiometabolic risk factor control to prevent heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
title: Diastolic dysfunction is equally common in pre-diabetes and diabetes and associated with concomitant cardiometabolic risk factors.

text: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and Early Vascular Aging in young and middle-aged adults.. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide. Early vascular aging (EVA) is an independent predictor of cardiovascular risk in young and middle-aged adults. The plausible association between EVA and vitamin D warrants further investigation
title: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and Early Vascular Aging in young and middle-aged adults.

text: . This study examined the relationship between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] levels and EVA in young and middle-aged healthy adults.This cross-sectional study included 2047 eligible participants who underwent physical examinations at the Health Management Center of the Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University between May 2023 and May 2025
title: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and Early Vascular Aging in young and middle-aged adults.

text: . Participants were categorized into EVA group (n = 687) and control group (n = 1360) based on brachial ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV). Logistic regression and restricted cubic splines assessed the association between 25(OH)D and EVA, with an inflection point identified using two-piecewise linear regression
title: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and Early Vascular Aging in young and middle-aged adults.

text: . Subgroup analyses and interaction tests were conducted by age, sex, blood collection month, smoking status, alcohol drinking status, hypertension, diabetes, and body mass index (BMI). The prevalence of EVA was 33.56%
title: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and Early Vascular Aging in young and middle-aged adults.

text: . The prevalence of EVA was 33.56%. Each 10 ng/mL increase in 25(OH)D was associated with a 19% decrease in the likelihood of EVA (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.70-0.94, P = 0.008).Compared with Q1, Q4 had a significantly lower risk (OR = 0.55, 95% CI: 0.40-0.76, P < 0.001), while Q2 and Q3 did not differ (both P > 0.05)
title: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and Early Vascular Aging in young and middle-aged adults.

text: . Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a nonlinear L-shaped association (P for non linearity = 0.015) with a threshold at 17.90 ng/mL: below this level, higher 25(OH)D was linked to a lower EVA risk (OR=0.90，95%CI: 0.85-0.96), whereas no significant association was observed above it
title: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and Early Vascular Aging in young and middle-aged adults.

text: . Subgroup analyses indicated a particularly significant inverse association between 25(OH)D levels and EVA in men and overweight/obese individuals. Significant interactions were observed for sex, BMI, and age (all P < 0.05), while interactions with other factors, such as blood collection month, hypertension, diabetes, smoking status, drinking status were not statistically significant
title: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and Early Vascular Aging in young and middle-aged adults.

text: . This study suggests an inverse association between 25(OH)D levels and EVA, with a more pronounced association possibly observed in men and individuals with overweight/obesity, and further indicates a threshold at 17.9 ng/mL below which this inverse association is significantly enhanced.
title: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and Early Vascular Aging in young and middle-aged adults.

text: Intraprocedural re-rupture during endovascular treatment of ruptured intracranial aneurysms: A single-center experience.. Intraprocedural re-rupture (IPR-RR) of ruptured intracranial aneurysms is rare but often catastrophic. We aimed to quantify the incidence of IPR-RR at our institution and describe its clinical characteristics, procedural context, and outcomes
title: Intraprocedural re-rupture during endovascular treatment of ruptured intracranial aneurysms: A single-center experience.

text: . Endovascular treatments for ruptured aneurysms at a tertiary center were reviewed. Intraprocedural re-rupture (IPR-RR) was defined as angiographic contrast extravasation or extrusion of a device tip beyond the aneurysm wall. The primary objective was to characterize the incidence of IPR-RR and identify associated clinical and procedural factors
title: Intraprocedural re-rupture during endovascular treatment of ruptured intracranial aneurysms: A single-center experience.

text: . Secondary endpoints included in-hospital mortality and discharge functional status as measured by the modified Rankin Scale (mRS 0-2 vs. > 2). IPR-RR occurred in 17/702 cases (2.4%). Patients with IPR-RR were more frequently aged 18-40 years (35.3% vs. 12.2%, p = 0.011) and had aneurysms > 10 mm (18% vs. 4%)
title: Intraprocedural re-rupture during endovascular treatment of ruptured intracranial aneurysms: A single-center experience.

text: . 4%). Vascular risk factors, including hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and smoking history, were similarly distributed between groups. Balloon-assisted coiling was used in 82.4% vs. 58.0% (p = 0.114). Favorable discharge outcome occurred in 29.4% vs. 51.5% (p = 0.072), while in-hospital mortality was 17.6% vs. 10.2% (p = 0.580)
title: Intraprocedural re-rupture during endovascular treatment of ruptured intracranial aneurysms: A single-center experience.

text: . 10.2% (p = 0.580). Intraprocedural re-rupture occurred in 2.4% of ruptured aneurysm treatments and was associated with worse early outcomes. Effective management relied on immediate coil packing, balloon inflation, and anticoagulation reversal
title: Intraprocedural re-rupture during endovascular treatment of ruptured intracranial aneurysms: A single-center experience.

text: . Procedural preparedness, including strict blood pressure control and readiness for cerebrospinal fluid diversion, is essential to limit secondary neurological injury in this rare but serious complication.
title: Intraprocedural re-rupture during endovascular treatment of ruptured intracranial aneurysms: A single-center experience.

text: The comparative effectiveness of different exercise training modes on ambulatory blood pressure: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
title: The comparative effectiveness of different exercise training modes on ambulatory blood pressure: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

text: . Exercise training is an effective non-pharmacological strategy for reducing blood pressure; however, current guideline recommendations are largely derived from studies reporting resting clinic blood pressure rather than ambulatory blood pressure (ABP), which provides greater prognostic value. Comparative evidence on the effects of different exercise modalities on ABP remains limited
title: The comparative effectiveness of different exercise training modes on ambulatory blood pressure: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

text: . To compare the effects of major exercise modalities on 24-h systolic ABP using a Bayesian network meta-analysis, and to outline practical implications for antihypertensive exercise prescription
title: The comparative effectiveness of different exercise training modes on ambulatory blood pressure: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

text: . PubMed (MEDLINE) and the Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials published before January 2025 reporting changes in 24-h systolic ABP following an exercise intervention of at least 2 weeks' duration
title: The comparative effectiveness of different exercise training modes on ambulatory blood pressure: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

text: . Eligible studies included adults and compared aerobic exercise training (AET), resistance training (RT), high-intensity interval training (HIIT), combined training (CT), or isometric exercise training (IET), with a non-exercise control or another exercise modality
title: The comparative effectiveness of different exercise training modes on ambulatory blood pressure: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

text: . Bayesian network meta-analyses were conducted, with interventions ranked using surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values. Twenty-five studies (1096 participants) met inclusion criteria; 16 were included in the network meta-analysis. AET and HIIT reduced 24-h systolic ABP (-4.77 mmHg and -6.86 mmHg), with a smaller reduction following RT (-2.25 mmHg)
title: The comparative effectiveness of different exercise training modes on ambulatory blood pressure: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

text: . Data were insufficient to analyse comparative effects for CT or IET. In the Bayesian network, rank order of effectiveness based on SUCRA values was HIIT (91.4%), AET (68.2%), and RT (35.4%). No statistically significant comparative differences were observed between exercise modalities
title: The comparative effectiveness of different exercise training modes on ambulatory blood pressure: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

text: . This Bayesian NMA demonstrates HIIT and AET as effective for reducing 24-h systolic ABP, supporting their role in hypertension management. However, the limited scale and connectivity of available trials restrict definitive comparisons between wider exercise modes
title: The comparative effectiveness of different exercise training modes on ambulatory blood pressure: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

text: . Larger, well-designed head-to-head trials incorporating ABP outcomes are needed to clarify the relative effectiveness of different exercise strategies and to better inform evidence-based exercise prescription for blood pressure management. Registration:PROSPERO: CRD420251177743.
title: The comparative effectiveness of different exercise training modes on ambulatory blood pressure: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

text: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Hypertension Among Type 2 Diabetic Patients in Private Health Facilities, Kampala, Uganda.. Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) such as Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) and hypertension (HTN) are the leading causes of mortality worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs)
title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Hypertension Among Type 2 Diabetic Patients in Private Health Facilities, Kampala, Uganda.

text: . In Uganda, while private health facilities in urban areas are preferred for managing these conditions, there is limited information on the prevalence of HTN and associated risk factors among T2D patients in these settings. This study assessed the prevalence of HTN and associated factors among T2D patients in private health facilities, Kampala, Uganda
title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Hypertension Among Type 2 Diabetic Patients in Private Health Facilities, Kampala, Uganda.

text: . A health facility-based cross-sectional study using quantitative methods was employed, which included obtaining information from the patient records and a structured questionnaire. The study recruited 295 participants at the diabetes clinics in selected private health facilities. The collected data were analysed using STATA 15.0 statistical software
title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Hypertension Among Type 2 Diabetic Patients in Private Health Facilities, Kampala, Uganda.

text: . Bivariate and multivariable analyses were conducted using a generalised linear model of modified Poisson regression. Almost a third, 28.9% (85/295) of the participants had lived with T2D for more than 10 years. The prevalence of HTN among participants was 63.7%
title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Hypertension Among Type 2 Diabetic Patients in Private Health Facilities, Kampala, Uganda.

text: . Knowledge of HTN was low, with only 44.1% of the participants knowing about blood pressure, and 56.3% had a low level of knowledge overall. Participants who smoked (APR = 2.15, 95% Cl: 1.34-3.46), consumed an alcoholic drink in the past 30 days (APR = 1.56, 95% Cl: 1.10-2.20) and had a high level of knowledge on HTN (APR = 2.16, 95% Cl: 1.56-2.99) were more likely to have HTN
title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Hypertension Among Type 2 Diabetic Patients in Private Health Facilities, Kampala, Uganda.

text: . Our study found a worrying high burden of uncontrolled HTN among T2D patients, which could be due to risky behaviours including smoking and alcohol use. The generated evidence will inform feasible HTN risk reduction measures among T2D patients, which will improve awareness and existing controls set up by the different stakeholders
title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Hypertension Among Type 2 Diabetic Patients in Private Health Facilities, Kampala, Uganda.

text: . Therefore, there is a need for consolidated efforts aimed at addressing the identified gaps through community health education and lifestyle adjustments at facilities they attend to, especially for high-risk behaviours such as smoking and alcohol use, to effectively reduce HTN prevalence in similar populations.
title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Hypertension Among Type 2 Diabetic Patients in Private Health Facilities, Kampala, Uganda.

text: Design considerations for hypertension chronotherapy trials: insights from experience and modelling.. Chronotherapy aims to maximise treatment efficacy while minimising side effects by scheduling treatment according to personal biological rhythms
title: Design considerations for hypertension chronotherapy trials: insights from experience and modelling.

text: . In recent years, randomised clinical trials (RCTs) have been conducted to evaluate whether scheduled blood pressure interventions can improve patient outcomes. However, reports of time-of-day effects have attracted rebuttals and engendered methodological debate
title: Design considerations for hypertension chronotherapy trials: insights from experience and modelling.

text: . A perfectly controlled chronotherapy trial (i.e., a trial that assesses the effect of assigning time of intervention) will never be feasible in the real world; yet some factors may be more critical to consider and control for than others
title: Design considerations for hypertension chronotherapy trials: insights from experience and modelling.

text: . To advance the conversation about how best to evaluate the effects of antihypertensive chronotherapeutic interventions in RCTs, we discuss critical considerations for clinical trials of chronotherapy for hypertension and apply mathematical modelling to provide quantitative insights into the extent to which such factors may influence the detected effect size.
title: Design considerations for hypertension chronotherapy trials: insights from experience and modelling.

text: Reduced antihypertensive treatment with maintained ambulatory blood pressure control following weight loss in type 2 diabetes.. In individuals with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, weight loss may reduce antihypertensive treatment needs, but effects on blood pressure variability and nocturnal dipping are unclear
title: Reduced antihypertensive treatment with maintained ambulatory blood pressure control following weight loss in type 2 diabetes.

text: . We investigated changes in antihypertensive treatment and ambulatory blood pressure following a weight-loss intervention in adults with overweight and type 2 diabetes. This single-arm intervention trial included 32 participants with type 2 diabetes undergoing a dietary weight-loss intervention
title: Reduced antihypertensive treatment with maintained ambulatory blood pressure control following weight loss in type 2 diabetes.

text: . Antihypertensive medications were discontinued at intervention start and reintroduced if blood pressure increased. Changes in antihypertensive treatment, ambulatory blood pressure, and office blood pressure were assessed from baseline to 12 months. Mean (SD) age was 61 ± 6 years and baseline weight 102 ± 16 kg. text: Probable case of anaphylaxis due to hydrocortisone in a septic shock patient.. title: Probable case of anaphylaxis due to hydrocortisone in a septic shock patient.

title: Probable case of anaphylaxis due to hydrocortisone in a septic shock patient.

text: . In this narrative review, we evaluated evidence from case reports, small case series, retrospective cohort, and case-control studies to outline the incidence, risk factors, and proposed pathophysiological mechanisms of post-RRD optic neuropathy
title: Risk factors and pathophysiological insights into optic neuropathy after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair: A literature review.

text: . We also highlight areas of controversy, including the relative contribution of pars plana vitrectomy versus scleral buckle and the potential neurotoxicity of silicone oil, and we discuss the strength of evidence supporting each risk factor
title: Risk factors and pathophysiological insights into optic neuropathy after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair: A literature review.

text: . Defining high-risk patients, optimising perioperative IOP control, and evaluating neuroprotective and monitoring strategies represent key priorities for future research. Surgery to repair a detached retina is generally successful at restoring retinal structure, but some patients still experience postoperative vision loss
title: Risk factors and pathophysiological insights into optic neuropathy after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair: A literature review.

text: . One possible cause of this is damage to the optic nerve, a condition known as optic neuropathy. The optic nerve is like a cable that sends signals from the eye to the brain, and damage to it can cause permanent vision loss. In this paper, we reviewed the existing literature to understand why optic nerve damage can occur after retinal detachment surgery
title: Risk factors and pathophysiological insights into optic neuropathy after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair: A literature review.

text: . Although this complication is rare, when it occurs, it often results in severe vision impairment. We found that many different factors may increase the risk of this problem. These include high intraocular pressure after surgery, reduced blood flow to the nerve, long or complex operations, and certain surgical materials, such as silicone oil or gas
title: Risk factors and pathophysiological insights into optic neuropathy after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair: A literature review.

text: . People with health conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure may also be more vulnerable. There is currently no official guideline to help doctors detect or prevent this complication. However, special eye scans and vision tests can sometimes find early signs of optic nerve injury
title: Risk factors and pathophysiological insights into optic neuropathy after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair: A literature review.

text: . Referring patients to nerve specialists may be helpful when vision loss can't be explained solely by retinal problems. By synthesising the existing evidence, this review helps identify which patients may be at higher risk and what physicians should monitor
title: Risk factors and pathophysiological insights into optic neuropathy after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair: A literature review.

text: . More studies are needed to develop better tools, techniques, and treatments to protect the optic nerve and improve long-term vision after surgery.
title: Risk factors and pathophysiological insights into optic neuropathy after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair: A literature review.

text: Drug-induced hyperglycemia in obstetrics: key offending drugs, mechanisms, and practical management.. Drug-induced hyperglycemia is an important metabolic complication that may arise when medications disrupt insulin secretion, insulin sensitivity, or glucose homeostasis
title: Drug-induced hyperglycemia in obstetrics: key offending drugs, mechanisms, and practical management.

title: Drug-induced hyperglycemia in obstetrics: key offending drugs, mechanisms, and practical management.

title: Drug-induced hyperglycemia in obstetrics: key offending drugs, mechanisms, and practical management.

title: Drug-induced hyperglycemia in obstetrics: key offending drugs, mechanisms, and practical management.

title: Drug-induced hyperglycemia in obstetrics: key offending drugs, mechanisms, and practical management.

title: Drug-induced hyperglycemia in obstetrics: key offending drugs, mechanisms, and practical management.

title: Investigation of the relationship between expression patterns of plasma microRNAs and pregnancy complications.

text: . Fold change (2-ΔΔCt) analysis was used to examine the microRNA expression patterns. MIR375-3p expression levels demonstrated a statistically significant difference between two groups. It was significantly lower in women with pregnancy complications than healthy pregnant women
title: Investigation of the relationship between expression patterns of plasma microRNAs and pregnancy complications.

text: . We found that MIR375-3p might be a useful indicator for non-invasive diagnosis and play a crucial part in predicting pregnancy complications. Given the limited patient cohort, more research using bigger samples is required to validate our findings.
title: Investigation of the relationship between expression patterns of plasma microRNAs and pregnancy complications.

text: Postpartum Linkage to Primary Care Among Patients With Diabetes and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy Following Medicaid ACO Implementation.. Timely postpartum linkage to primary care is important for managing diabetes and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), yet linkage remains suboptimal
title: Postpartum Linkage to Primary Care Among Patients With Diabetes and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy Following Medicaid ACO Implementation.

text: . Medicaid accountable care organizations (ACOs) aim to strengthen care coordination and improve postpartum linkage, although effects may vary by ACO design. Evaluate whether Massachusetts Medicaid ACO implementation was associated with changes in postpartum primary care linkage among enrollees with diabetes or HDP and whether effects differed by ACO model
title: Postpartum Linkage to Primary Care Among Patients With Diabetes and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy Following Medicaid ACO Implementation.

text: . Retrospective cohort study using the 2016-2023 Massachusetts All-Payer Claims Database (APCD). Using a difference-in-differences approach, we compared outcomes before (2016-2017) versus after (2018-2023) implementation among health system/managed care partnership ACOs, primary care-led ACOs, and non-ACO enrollees
title: Postpartum Linkage to Primary Care Among Patients With Diabetes and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy Following Medicaid ACO Implementation.

text: . In total, 38,340 Medicaid-covered deliveries among enrollees ages 18-44 with diabetes or HDP, continuously enrolled for at least 60 days before and after delivery. A primary care visit within 3, 6, and 12 months postpartum. Overall, 53.6%, 76.8%, and 90.3% were linked to primary care by 3, 6, and 12 months, respectively
title: Postpartum Linkage to Primary Care Among Patients With Diabetes and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy Following Medicaid ACO Implementation.

text: . Although positive, ACO implementation was not associated with statistically significant changes at any interval for either model. At 3 months, model 1 was associated with a 2.44 percentage point [PP] increase (95% CI: -1.7 to 6.6) and model 2 with a 3.73 PP increase (95% CI: -0.5 to 8.0) versus non-ACO enrollees
title: Postpartum Linkage to Primary Care Among Patients With Diabetes and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy Following Medicaid ACO Implementation.

text: . Massachusetts Medicaid ACO implementation was not associated with significant changes in postpartum primary care linkage. Explicit postpartum performance measures and stronger coordination between maternity and primary care clinicians may be needed to improve transitions to ongoing care.
title: Postpartum Linkage to Primary Care Among Patients With Diabetes and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy Following Medicaid ACO Implementation.

text: Maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index, hemoglobin concentration, and gestational diabetes as predictors of neonatal macrosomia: A retrospective study in Kenitra, Morocco.. Neonatal macrosomia is a major perinatal complication associated with maternal metabolic disorders
title: Maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index, hemoglobin concentration, and gestational diabetes as predictors of neonatal macrosomia: A retrospective study in Kenitra, Morocco.

text: . This study aimed to assess whether hemoglobin concentration and gestational diabetes mediate the association between pre-pregnancy body mass index and neonatal macrosomia. A retrospective analysis was conducted among 700 singleton full-term pregnancies at El Idrissi Provincial Hospital, Kenitra, Morocco. Macrosomia was defined as birth weight ≥4000 g, and elevated hemoglobin as ≥12.5 g/dL
title: Maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index, hemoglobin concentration, and gestational diabetes as predictors of neonatal macrosomia: A retrospective study in Kenitra, Morocco.

text: . Gestational diabetes was diagnosed using fasting glucose or a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test. Mediation analysis using the Karlson-Holm-Breen method was adjusted for maternal age, parity, gestational hypertension, and infant sex. The prevalence of gestational diabetes was 11.9%, and macrosomia occurred in 14.7% of cases
title: Maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index, hemoglobin concentration, and gestational diabetes as predictors of neonatal macrosomia: A retrospective study in Kenitra, Morocco.

text: . Overweight and obesity were significantly associated with macrosomia, and 71.86% (overweight) and 67.52% (obesity) of these associations were jointly explained by hemoglobin concentration and gestational diabetes, mainly through gestational diabetes. Early metabolic screening during pregnancy may reduce the risk of adverse birth outcomes
title: Maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index, hemoglobin concentration, and gestational diabetes as predictors of neonatal macrosomia: A retrospective study in Kenitra, Morocco.

text: . La macrosomie néonatale est une complication périnatale majeure associée aux troubles métaboliques maternels. Cette étude visait à évaluer si la concentration d’hémoglobine et le diabète gestationnel médient l’association entre l’indice de masse corporelle préconceptionnel et la macrosomie néonatale
title: Maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index, hemoglobin concentration, and gestational diabetes as predictors of neonatal macrosomia: A retrospective study in Kenitra, Morocco.

title: Maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index, hemoglobin concentration, and gestational diabetes as predictors of neonatal macrosomia: A retrospective study in Kenitra, Morocco.

text: Maternal and umbilical cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in pregnancies affected by COVID-19: A case-control study.. This study aimed to compare maternal and umbilical cord blood pro-BNP levels in pregnant women with a history of COVID-19 infection and to evaluate possible cardiac effects during pregnancy
title: Maternal and umbilical cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in pregnancies affected by COVID-19: A case-control study.

text: . In this prospective case-control study conducted between January and October 2023, 88 pregnant women were included: 44 with a history of COVID-19 infection after the second trimester and 44 healthy controls. Women with diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, or severe pregnancy complications were excluded
title: Maternal and umbilical cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in pregnancies affected by COVID-19: A case-control study.

text: . Maternal venous and umbilical cord arterial blood samples were collected immediately after delivery, and pro-BNP levels were measured using standard laboratory procedures. Maternal pro-BNP levels were significantly higher in the COVID-19 group, whereas cord blood pro-BNP levels did not differ significantly between groups. Obstetric and neonatal outcomes were similar
title: Maternal and umbilical cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in pregnancies affected by COVID-19: A case-control study.

text: . Obstetric and neonatal outcomes were similar. These findings suggest that prior COVID-19 infection may cause subclinical maternal cardiac stress, while placental mechanisms may protect the fetus from cardiac involvement
title: Maternal and umbilical cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in pregnancies affected by COVID-19: A case-control study.

text: . Cette étude visait à comparer les taux de pro-BNP dans le sang maternel et le sang du cordon ombilical chez des femmes enceintes ayant des antécédents d'infection par la COVID-19, ainsi qu'à évaluer les effets cardiaques potentiels durant la grossesse
title: Maternal and umbilical cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in pregnancies affected by COVID-19: A case-control study.

text: . Dans le cadre de cette étude cas-témoins prospective menée entre janvier et octobre 2023, 88 femmes enceintes ont été incluses : 44 ayant contracté la COVID-19 après le deuxième trimestre et 44 témoins en bonne santé. Les femmes atteintes de diabète, d'hypertension, de cardiopathie ou de complications graves de la grossesse ont été exclues
title: Maternal and umbilical cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in pregnancies affected by COVID-19: A case-control study.

text: . Des prélèvements de sang veineux maternel et de sang artériel du cordon ombilical ont été effectués immédiatement après l'accouchement, et les taux de pro-BNP ont été mesurés selon les procédures de laboratoire standard
title: Maternal and umbilical cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in pregnancies affected by COVID-19: A case-control study.

text: . Les taux de pro-BNP maternels étaient significativement plus élevés dans le groupe COVID-19, alors qu'aucune différence significative n'a été observée entre les groupes concernant les taux de pro-BNP dans le sang du cordon. Les issues obstétricales et néonatales étaient similaires
title: Maternal and umbilical cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in pregnancies affected by COVID-19: A case-control study.

text: . Ces résultats suggèrent qu'une infection antérieure par la COVID-19 pourrait induire un stress cardiaque maternel infraclinique, tandis que des mécanismes placentaires pourraient protéger le fœtus d'une atteinte cardiaque.
title: Maternal and umbilical cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in pregnancies affected by COVID-19: A case-control study.

text: Exploring the associations of overweight and obesity with pregnancy outcomes in type 1 and type 2 diabetes: An Australian retrospective cohort study.. To explore the associations of maternal overweight/obesity and pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) on glycemia and pregnancy outcomes in women with pregestational type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) or type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
title: Exploring the associations of overweight and obesity with pregnancy outcomes in type 1 and type 2 diabetes: An Australian retrospective cohort study.

text: . We examined prospectively collected data (2010-2019) involving 264 singleton pregnancies affected by pregestational T1DM or T2DM. On separate analyses within each diabetes subtype, pregnancy outcomes were compared across maternal BMI categories and using BMI as a continuous variable. Co-primary outcomes included preterm delivery, large-for-gestational age (LGA) infants, and pre-eclampsia
title: Exploring the associations of overweight and obesity with pregnancy outcomes in type 1 and type 2 diabetes: An Australian retrospective cohort study.

text: . In those with T1DM (N = 124, 46% overweight or obese), we did not find an association between increasing BMI category and greater risks of pre-eclampsia, preterm delivery, or LGA infants
title: Exploring the associations of overweight and obesity with pregnancy outcomes in type 1 and type 2 diabetes: An Australian retrospective cohort study.

text: . However, amongst the women with T1DM, overweight and obesity were associated with higher odds of exceeding the first trimester HbA1c target (6.5%), and each 1 kg/m On separate analyses within each diabetes subtype, maternal overweight/obesity was potentially associated with increased odds of pre-eclampsia and preterm delivery in the T2DM cohort
title: Exploring the associations of overweight and obesity with pregnancy outcomes in type 1 and type 2 diabetes: An Australian retrospective cohort study.

text: . Amongst those with T1DM, maternal overweight/obesity was associated with non-attainment of first trimester HbA1c targets. Regression analyses were performed in an exploratory and hypothesis-generating manner, and larger-scale studies are required to directly compare the effects of maternal overweight/obesity on pregnancy outcomes in T1DM vs T2DM.
title: Exploring the associations of overweight and obesity with pregnancy outcomes in type 1 and type 2 diabetes: An Australian retrospective cohort study.

text: Uncovering Placental Endocrine Dysregulation in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Using Bioinformatics and Machine Learning.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common metabolic disorder, posing serious health risks to both mother and fetus. This study aims to explore the placental endocrine mechanisms involved in GDM
title: Uncovering Placental Endocrine Dysregulation in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Using Bioinformatics and Machine Learning.
journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)

text: . The training dataset GSE203346 and endocrine-related gene sets from the Molecular Signatures Database were used to identify endocrine-related differentially expressed genes (ER-DEGs). Support vector machine recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE) and Boruta algorithms were employed to identify hub genes. Diagnostic performance was analyzed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves
title: Uncovering Placental Endocrine Dysregulation in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Using Bioinformatics and Machine Learning.
journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)

text: . Immune cell infiltration was evaluated using the CIBERSORT algorithm, followed by single-gene gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). A total of 57 ER-DEGs were identified in the GDM placental samples
title: Uncovering Placental Endocrine Dysregulation in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Using Bioinformatics and Machine Learning.
journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)

text: . Machine learning identified nine important genes, of which CACNA1C, CCDC102B, and KIF21A exhibited high diagnostic performance (AUC > 0.80) in two external validation datasets (GSE154414 and GSE255075). Immune infiltration analysis revealed potential differences in several immune cell proportions between high- and low-expression groups of the hub genes
title: Uncovering Placental Endocrine Dysregulation in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Using Bioinformatics and Machine Learning.
journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)

text: . High expression of CACNA1C, CCDC102B, and KIF21A was associated with the Notch pathway, mTOR pathway, and autophagy. CACNA1C, CCDC102B, and KIF21A may be the potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for GDM.
title: Uncovering Placental Endocrine Dysregulation in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Using Bioinformatics and Machine Learning.
