text: Reduced serum acetyl-L-carnitine is associated with hypertensive disorders in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-omics study.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are common metabolic complications during pregnancy
title: Reduced serum acetyl-L-carnitine is associated with hypertensive disorders in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-omics study.

text: . GDM is an independent risk factor for HDP, while HDP is a major contributor to maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. Reliable early tools for identifying women with GDM who are at risk of subsequently developing HDP remain limited
title: Reduced serum acetyl-L-carnitine is associated with hypertensive disorders in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-omics study.

text: . This study aimed to integrate metabolomic, lipidomic, and clinical data to identify reproducible candidate biomarkers associated with subsequently diagnosed HDP in women with GDM and to characterize the accompanying metabolic and lipidomic alterations. In this prospective exploratory biomarker study, a discovery cohort (n = 128) and a validation cohort (n = 55) were recruited
title: Reduced serum acetyl-L-carnitine is associated with hypertensive disorders in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-omics study.

text: . Serum samples collected at 24-28 weeks of gestation were analyzed using untargeted and targeted metabolomics. Lipidomics was performed to complement the metabolomic analysis and characterize lipid-related alterations. A combined predictive model was constructed using logistic regression, and its predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis
title: Reduced serum acetyl-L-carnitine is associated with hypertensive disorders in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-omics study.

text: . Untargeted metabolomics identified lower serum acetyl-L-carnitine (ALC) in the GDMHDP group than in the GDM group, and this difference was confirmed by targeted LC-MS/MS in the validation cohort. The combined ALC-diastolic blood pressure (DBP) model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.907 in the discovery cohort and 0.886 in the validation cohort
title: Reduced serum acetyl-L-carnitine is associated with hypertensive disorders in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-omics study.

text: . Adding ALC to DBP improved discrimination and reclassification in both cohorts. Multi-omics analysis showed complementary and partly distinct lipid associations with ALC and DBP
title: Reduced serum acetyl-L-carnitine is associated with hypertensive disorders in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-omics study.

text: . Lower ALC was associated with selected ceramide and monolysocardiolipin species, as well as with lipid patterns consistent with altered fatty-acid handling, whereas DBP showed a partly distinct pattern of lipid correlations. Reduced serum ALC at 24-28 weeks of gestation was reproducibly associated with GDM complicated by HDP
title: Reduced serum acetyl-L-carnitine is associated with hypertensive disorders in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-omics study.

text: . Combining ALC with DBP improved discrimination between GDMHDP and uncomplicated GDM, suggesting complementary metabolic and hemodynamic information
title: Reduced serum acetyl-L-carnitine is associated with hypertensive disorders in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-omics study.

text: . Given the modest number of GDMHDP cases and the single-center design, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating; they support further evaluation of ALC as a candidate metabolic marker but require confirmation in larger independent cohorts.
title: Reduced serum acetyl-L-carnitine is associated with hypertensive disorders in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-omics study.

text: First and second trimester concentrations of environmental phenols in association with gestational weight gain in the ECHO Cohort.. Inconsistent evidence links pregnancy concentrations of environmental phenols to altered gestational weight gain
title: First and second trimester concentrations of environmental phenols in association with gestational weight gain in the ECHO Cohort.

text: . We analyzed maternal urinary concentrations of 10 phenols in first trimester and 12 phenols in second trimester in the Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) cohort study sites (n=3,960)
title: First and second trimester concentrations of environmental phenols in association with gestational weight gain in the ECHO Cohort.

text: . Phenols ≥85% above the limit of detection (LOD) were modeled continuously; phenols with 55% - 85% of samples > LOD were modeled as three categories; and phenols with <55% of samples > LOD were modeled as detected/non-detected
title: First and second trimester concentrations of environmental phenols in association with gestational weight gain in the ECHO Cohort.

text: . We used generalized estimating equations models to evaluate associations between each phenol and gestational weight gain (difference between pre-pregnancy and delivery weight). Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression assessed associations of the second trimester phenol mixture with gestational weight gain. We also evaluated effect modification by pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI)
title: First and second trimester concentrations of environmental phenols in association with gestational weight gain in the ECHO Cohort.

text: . First trimester concentrations of many phenols, including bisphenol A (BPA), bisphenol S (BPS), benzophenone-3 (BP3), ∑bisphenols (∑BPA, BPS, bisphenol F), and ∑parabens (ethyl, methyl, propyl, butyl paraben) were associated with greater total gestational weight gain
title: First and second trimester concentrations of environmental phenols in association with gestational weight gain in the ECHO Cohort.

text: . For example, each doubling in ∑bisphenols and ∑parabens were associated with 0.28 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.18, 0.39) kg and 0.45 (95%CI: 0.07, 0.83) kg greater gestational weight gain, respectively. In contrast, associations between second trimester concentrations of phenols and total gestational weight gain were generally null both for individual phenols and the phenol mixture
title: First and second trimester concentrations of environmental phenols in association with gestational weight gain in the ECHO Cohort.

text: . Associations were not consistently modified by pre-pregnancy BMI. Early pregnancy exposure to environmental phenols is associated with greater gestational weight gain. Further investigation into potential windows for endocrine disruption is warranted.
title: First and second trimester concentrations of environmental phenols in association with gestational weight gain in the ECHO Cohort.

text: Metals and metalloids signatures in early pregnancy suggest cadmium and arsenic as major mixture components associated with gestational diabetes mellitus risk.. Pregnancy is a vulnerable window for environmental pollutant exposure, yet the contribution of metals and metalloids (metal(loid)s) to gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) remains insufficiently characterized
title: Metals and metalloids signatures in early pregnancy suggest cadmium and arsenic as major mixture components associated with gestational diabetes mellitus risk.

text: . This prospective cohort study evaluated whether early-pregnancy urinary metal(loid)s were associated with subsequent GDM and explored their predictive and mechanistic value. Among 1201 pregnant women included in Guilin, China, nine urinary metal(loid)s were measured by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. GDM was diagnosed by a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24-28 gestational weeks
title: Metals and metalloids signatures in early pregnancy suggest cadmium and arsenic as major mixture components associated with gestational diabetes mellitus risk.

text: . Restricted cubic spline and weighted quantile sum regression assessed dose-response and mixture effects. Machine learning models evaluated early prediction, and network toxicology explored molecular pathways. GDM occurred in 312 participants. Cadmium, arsenic, manganese, thallium, and lead showed nonlinear associations with GDM risk. Cadmium and arsenic dominated the overall mixture effect
title: Metals and metalloids signatures in early pregnancy suggest cadmium and arsenic as major mixture components associated with gestational diabetes mellitus risk.

text: . Adding urinary metal(loid)s to conventional biochemical indicators modestly improved discrimination, with the XGBoost performing best. Network toxicology identified shared cadmium/arsenic targets enriched in oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, endothelial dysfunction, and insulin-resistance pathways, including AGE-RAGE, HIF-1, TNF, and IL-17 signaling
title: Metals and metalloids signatures in early pregnancy suggest cadmium and arsenic as major mixture components associated with gestational diabetes mellitus risk.

text: . These findings suggest that early-pregnancy metal(loid)s mixture exposure, particularly cadmium and arsenic, is associated with GDM risk, with arsenic the most consistent contributor across mixture methods and non-linear signals for lead and manganese warranting further investigation. Urinary metal(loid)s may serve as complementary biomarkers for early GDM risk stratification.
title: Metals and metalloids signatures in early pregnancy suggest cadmium and arsenic as major mixture components associated with gestational diabetes mellitus risk.

text: Prevalence, socio-demographic, and socio-economic factors associated with gestational diabetes in Australia: A population study.. To examine the prevalence of gestational diabetes mellitus and associated socio-demographic and socio-economic factors in Victoria, Australia. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the Victorian Perinatal Data Collection, a population-based dataset
title: Prevalence, socio-demographic, and socio-economic factors associated with gestational diabetes in Australia: A population study.

text: . The analysis included all women who gave birth in Victoria in 2020, excluding those with pre-existing diabetes. Associations between socio-demographic, obstetric, and area-level factors and gestational diabetes mellitus were assessed using mixed-effects Poisson regression to estimate relative risks with 95% confidence intervals
title: Prevalence, socio-demographic, and socio-economic factors associated with gestational diabetes in Australia: A population study.

text: . Overall, 18% of women who gave birth in Victoria in 2020 reported being diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus. Higher prevalence was reported in the most disadvantaged areas compared with the most advantaged areas. About of 19% of gestational diabetes mellitus cases were diagnosed before 20 weeks of gestation
title: Prevalence, socio-demographic, and socio-economic factors associated with gestational diabetes in Australia: A population study.

text: . Women in the least disadvantaged areas had a significantly lower risk compared to those in the most disadvantaged areas (adjusted prevalence ratio (aPR) 0.62, 95% CI 0.57-0.67). Compared with women >35 years, younger women had lower gestational diabetes mellitus prevalence ratio: ≤20 (aPR 0.32, 95% CI 0.26-0.4), 21-25 (0.48, 0.45-0.52), 26-30 (0.61, 0.58-0.64), and 31-35 (0.77, 0.74-0.8)
title: Prevalence, socio-demographic, and socio-economic factors associated with gestational diabetes in Australia: A population study.

text: . Grand multigravida women had a higher prevalence ratio than primigravida women (aPR 1.14, 95% CI 1.07-1.22). Spatial analysis identified gestational diabetes mellitus hotspots in south-eastern Melbourne and western Victoria. Gestational diabetes mellitus prevalence in Victoria shows geographic and area level disparities, highlighting the need for targeted public health interventions.
title: Prevalence, socio-demographic, and socio-economic factors associated with gestational diabetes in Australia: A population study.

text: Metabolic syndrome during pregnancy and adverse pregnancy outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.. Metabolic syndrome (MetS), a cluster of cardiometabolic risk factors, is increasingly prevalent among women of reproductive age. Pregnancy involves substantial metabolic and cardiovascular adaptations, and the presence of MetS may increase susceptibility to adverse pregnancy outcomes
title: Metabolic syndrome during pregnancy and adverse pregnancy outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate whether MetS during pregnancy is associated with higher odds of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preeclampsia, small for gestational age, preterm birth, and gestational diabetes mellitus. We searched PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Scopus databases. We registered the review protocol with PROSPERO (CRD42024568396)
title: Metabolic syndrome during pregnancy and adverse pregnancy outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . We conducted study selection, data extraction, and analyses in accordance with the MOOSE (Meta-analysis of Observational Studies in Epidemiology) guidelines. We estimated pooled odds ratios (ORs) for adverse pregnancy outcomes using a DerSimonian and Laird random-effects model in JBI SUMARI software. We assessed study quality using the JBI critical appraisal checklist for cohort studies
title: Metabolic syndrome during pregnancy and adverse pregnancy outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . We defined MetS according to IDF (International Diabetes Federation), NCEP ATP III (National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III), WHO (World Health Organization), or the Harmonizing the Metabolic Syndrome criteria. Seven studies met the inclusion criteria and included data on 3,677 pregnant women with MetS and 44,166 pregnant women without MetS
title: Metabolic syndrome during pregnancy and adverse pregnancy outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Women with MetS during pregnancy had higher odds of adverse pregnancy outcomes than women without MetS (OR 2.72, 95 percent CI 1.77-4.17, I
title: Metabolic syndrome during pregnancy and adverse pregnancy outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: Diagnostic significance of histopathological assessment of villous extracellular matrix in normal and pathological placentas.. The extracellular matrix of chorionic villi is an important factor ensuring the structural and functional viability of the placenta
title: Diagnostic significance of histopathological assessment of villous extracellular matrix in normal and pathological placentas.

text: . The aim of the study was to compare the collagen-elastic frame of different types of chorionic villi in normal and pathological pregnancy in the I-III trimesters
title: Diagnostic significance of histopathological assessment of villous extracellular matrix in normal and pathological placentas.

text: . We compared placentas of the I, II and III trimesters in pathological pregnancies associated with (1) fetal and placental malformations/genetic aberrations/dysgenesis, as well as (2) chronic fetoplacental hypoxia/asphyxia with the group of placentas from uncomplicated pregnancies of the appropriate gestational period
title: Diagnostic significance of histopathological assessment of villous extracellular matrix in normal and pathological placentas.

text: . The study was performed by light microscopy on sections stained by Weigert (elastic fibers), Masson's trichrome (type I collagen) and Gomori's silver staining (type III collagen). Physiological pregnancies showed stage-specific remodeling of the collagen-elastic frame. The dominance of the reticular organization of the stroma decreased as the villi matured
title: Diagnostic significance of histopathological assessment of villous extracellular matrix in normal and pathological placentas.

text: . At the same time, the proportion of collagen fibrillar structures increased and was accompanied by the relative decrease in the number of subtrophoblastic elastic fibers in the distal, mainly terminal villi
title: Diagnostic significance of histopathological assessment of villous extracellular matrix in normal and pathological placentas.

text: . The persistence of diffuse fibrillar and elastic stromal patterns in the terminal villi of full-term placentas was observed with delayed maturation of the villi and diabetes-associated changes in the placenta. Peripheral granular pattern of elastic fiber distribution in aberrant hydropic and dysmorphic villi was detected in fetal and placental malformations, genetic abnormalities, and dysgenesis
title: Diagnostic significance of histopathological assessment of villous extracellular matrix in normal and pathological placentas.

text: . A diffuse homogeneous type I collagen pattern was associated with impaired fetoplacental unit formation and hypoxic damage
title: Diagnostic significance of histopathological assessment of villous extracellular matrix in normal and pathological placentas.

text: . Placentas of the I-III trimester with disorders of the formation of the fetoplacental unit, dysmetabolic conditions and hypoxic damage demonstrate patterns of remodeling of the collagen-elastic framework of chorionic villi, which differ from normal placentas of the corresponding gestational age.
title: Diagnostic significance of histopathological assessment of villous extracellular matrix in normal and pathological placentas.

text: Educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications in the postpartum period: A scoping review.. Previous research provides evidence that the postpartum period is a crucial time for individuals who have just given birth to understand and engage in their health to mitigate current and future risks
title: Educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications in the postpartum period: A scoping review.

text: . The present study is a scoping review of research on educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications for postpartum patients. We aimed to determine the extent to which these tools exist and how they have been studied among postpartum people
title: Educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications in the postpartum period: A scoping review.

text: . PubMed, CINAHL (Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature), and Embase were searched from inception to June 2025 to identify publications on patient-facing educational tools for the postpartum period that focus on pregnancy-related complications
title: Educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications in the postpartum period: A scoping review.

text: . Educational tools were evaluated for application to the Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation (COM-B) framework for health behavior change. Of 3216 records, 32 studies met the inclusion criteria, and 11 patient educational tools were accessible for analysis. Two reviewers independently screened and assessed the titles, abstracts, and full texts of identified articles for inclusion
title: Educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications in the postpartum period: A scoping review.

text: . These tools were delivered through a variety of media, including mobile applications and traditional written pamphlets. Topics of the tools included postpartum mental health, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, gestational diabetes, breastfeeding after a complicated pregnancy, and warning signs for postpartum morbidity and mortality
title: Educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications in the postpartum period: A scoping review.

text: . Enhancers to postpartum care were addressed more often in the educational tools than barriers to postpartum care. The educational tools most often covered the following facilitators of behavior change identified by the COM-B framework: psychological capability, social opportunity, and reflective motivation
title: Educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications in the postpartum period: A scoping review.

text: . This scoping review highlights the limited availability of educational tools for postpartum care and recovery that address pregnancy-related complications. Findings of this scoping review suggest that educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications for postpartum patients were limited in topics covered, language availability, and diversity of postpartum populations tested
title: Educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications in the postpartum period: A scoping review.

text: . Further research is needed to expand the network of accessible postpartum educational tools and to assess the efficacy and acceptability of these educational tools in historically marginalized populations
title: Educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications in the postpartum period: A scoping review.

text: . Structuring these tools within a framework for behavior change such as COM-B may be a useful method for better understanding and improving postpartum care engagement and access to educational resources.
title: Educational tools that address pregnancy-related complications in the postpartum period: A scoping review.

text: Postpartum visit attendance after spontaneous and medically indicated preterm birth.. Individuals with preterm birth (PTB) are less likely to attend postpartum visits compared to those with term birth but are more likely to have conditions such as hypertensive disorders
title: Postpartum visit attendance after spontaneous and medically indicated preterm birth.

text: . PTB can be classified as spontaneous PTB (sPTB) (premature rupture of membranes or preterm labor) and medically indicated PTB (mPTB) (clinician-initiated due to maternal or fetal conditions). We compared postpartum visit attendance after sPTB and mPTB to term birth
title: Postpartum visit attendance after spontaneous and medically indicated preterm birth.

text: . We hypothesized that sPTB and mPTB would be associated with increased risk of not attending postpartum visits compared to term, but risk would be higher after sPTB as mPTB is more often preceded by chronic conditions requiring more healthcare engagement
title: Postpartum visit attendance after spontaneous and medically indicated preterm birth.

text: . We performed a retrospective cohort study of births from 2008 to 2019 in  Of the 69,110 included births, 3464 (5.0%) were sPTB and 2755 (4.0%) were mPTB. There were 693 (1.0%) excluded as unclassifiable PTBs
title: Postpartum visit attendance after spontaneous and medically indicated preterm birth.

text: . Overall, 37.2% of births had no postpartum visit within 12 weeks, with higher proportions after sPTB (46.5%) and mPTB (42.8%) than term birth (36.4%) ( Individuals with both sPTB and mPTB are at higher risk of not attending postpartum visits compared to term births
title: Postpartum visit attendance after spontaneous and medically indicated preterm birth.

text: . Innovative, collaborative, multidisciplinary efforts are essential to meet the needs of this vulnerable population to ensure postpartum healthcare.
title: Postpartum visit attendance after spontaneous and medically indicated preterm birth.

text: Neonatal humeral fracture and scalp laceration following difficult cesarean delivery for transverse lie: a case report.. Transverse lie in advanced labor presents significant obstetric challenges and may complicate fetal extraction during cesarean delivery
title: Neonatal humeral fracture and scalp laceration following difficult cesarean delivery for transverse lie: a case report.

text: . Although cesarean delivery is generally considered protective against birth trauma, neonatal injuries may still occur during technically difficult extractions. A 41-year-old gravida 6 para 5 woman with gestational diabetes mellitus, polyhydramnios, and an unstable transverse lie underwent external cephalic version at 37+3 weeks' gestation
title: Neonatal humeral fracture and scalp laceration following difficult cesarean delivery for transverse lie: a case report.

text: . Although cephalic presentation was initially achieved, the fetus reverted to a transverse lie within 3 h. With cervical dilatation of 8 cm and no presenting part, emergency cesarean delivery was performed under general anaesthesia
title: Neonatal humeral fracture and scalp laceration following difficult cesarean delivery for transverse lie: a case report.

text: . A poorly formed lower uterine segment intraoperatively necessitated the use of an inverted T uterine incision, and the neonate sustained a 2 cm scalp laceration and a minimally displaced right humeral shaft fracture. The scalp laceration was repaired immediately, while the humeral fracture was diagnosed on postnatal day 3 following the development of upper limb weakness and an absent Moro reflex
title: Neonatal humeral fracture and scalp laceration following difficult cesarean delivery for transverse lie: a case report.

text: . Both injuries were managed successfully with favourable outcomes. This case highlights the challenges of cesarean delivery for transverse lie in advanced labor and demonstrates that neonatal trauma may occur despite operative delivery. Careful surgical planning, experienced obstetric involvement, and thorough neonatal assessment following difficult extraction are essential.
title: Neonatal humeral fracture and scalp laceration following difficult cesarean delivery for transverse lie: a case report.

text: Association of CDKAL1 rs7754840 with gestational diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a widespread condition during pregnancy with substantial fetal and maternal morbidity
title: Association of CDKAL1 rs7754840 with gestational diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . However, the correlation between GDM risk and the CDKAL1 rs7754840 polymorphism is inconsistent.This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate this association through an updated systematic review and meta-analysis. This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines
title: Association of CDKAL1 rs7754840 with gestational diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . A comprehensive literature search of case-control studies was conducted in CNKI, Embase, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception to December 17, 2025. Five genetic models were selected, along with their odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals. Subsequently, stratified analyses were performed by ethnicity and according to diagnostic criteria for GDM
title: Association of CDKAL1 rs7754840 with gestational diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Heterogeneity, publication bias, and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were assessed. The meta-analysis included 18 studies comprising 8,025 women with GDM and 8,605 controls. Pooled analyses showed an association between the CDKAL1 rs7754840 polymorphism and increased GDM risk, with moderate to substantial between-study heterogeneity across genetic models
title: Association of CDKAL1 rs7754840 with gestational diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Stratified analyses showed consistent associations in Asian populations (15 studies; 7,012 cases/7,921 controls), whereas evidence in Caucasian populations (3 studies; 1,013 cases/684 controls) was inconclusive. Heterogeneity varied across GDM diagnostic criteria, with lower heterogeneity observed among studies using the IADPSG (2010) criteria
title: Association of CDKAL1 rs7754840 with gestational diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . TSA showed that the cumulative Z-curve crossed the monitoring boundary but did not reach the required information size, indicating supportive but inconclusive evidence. This meta-analysis supports the association between GDM risk and CDKAL1 rs7754840 in Asian populations. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251270398, identifier CRD420251270398.
title: Association of CDKAL1 rs7754840 with gestational diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: Maternal and offspring genome-wide association study of C-reactive protein reveals limited polygenic association with gestational diabetes mellitus.. C-reactive protein (CRP) is a well-established biomarker of systemic inflammation. In pregnancy, several studies show association of elevated CRP with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)
title: Maternal and offspring genome-wide association study of C-reactive protein reveals limited polygenic association with gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . However, the genetic contributions of CRP levels during early pregnancy and their potential association with GDM remain largely understudied
title: Maternal and offspring genome-wide association study of C-reactive protein reveals limited polygenic association with gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . The Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-to-Be (nuMoM2b) provides a unique opportunity to investigate these questions due to its rich design, including early pregnancy biospecimens, genome-wide genotype data, and detailed clinical outcomes across multiple ancestry groups
title: Maternal and offspring genome-wide association study of C-reactive protein reveals limited polygenic association with gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . We performed genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of first-trimester CRP levels using maternal (n = 4,326) and offspring (n = 2,140) genotypes from the nuMoM2b cohort
title: Maternal and offspring genome-wide association study of C-reactive protein reveals limited polygenic association with gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . In the European-ancestry maternal sub-cohort of nuMoM2b, three genome-wide significant loci (CRP, LEPR, and HNF1A) were associated with early pregnancy CRP levels, consistent with findings from previous GWAS in non-pregnant populations. Analysis of the full multi-ancestry maternal cohort identified two additional loci (ENSG00000257703 and APOC1) associated with CRP levels
title: Maternal and offspring genome-wide association study of C-reactive protein reveals limited polygenic association with gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . No genome-wide significant associations were detected in the offspring GWAS of CRP levels. Linkage disequilibrium score regression did not detect a significant genetic correlation between CRP and GDM using the nuMoM2b CRP GWAS
title: Maternal and offspring genome-wide association study of C-reactive protein reveals limited polygenic association with gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . In contrast, a significant correlation was observed when using an external large population-based CRP GWAS, suggesting that genetic overlap between CRP and GDM may vary across study contexts. However, Polygenic risk scores for CRP derived from either GWAS source were not significantly associated with GDM risk in the nuMoM2b cohort
title: Maternal and offspring genome-wide association study of C-reactive protein reveals limited polygenic association with gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . These findings provide insights into the genetic architecture of CRP levels during early pregnancy and illustrate the potential value of pregnancy-specific genomic studies for improving understanding of inflammatory processes relevant to maternal-fetal health
title: Maternal and offspring genome-wide association study of C-reactive protein reveals limited polygenic association with gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . They also highlight the need for larger pregnancy cohorts to better understand the relationship between inflammation and metabolic complications during pregnancy.
title: Maternal and offspring genome-wide association study of C-reactive protein reveals limited polygenic association with gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: Pregnancy-associated MINOCA: Diagnostic challenges and emergency management in young women.. Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is identified in approximately 5 to 10% of patients with myocardial infarction referred for coronary angiography, and it remains a working diagnosis rather than a final mechanistic one
title: Pregnancy-associated MINOCA: Diagnostic challenges and emergency management in young women.
journal: The American journal of emergency medicine

text: . The diagnostic challenge is greatest in young women during pregnancy and the early postpartum period. Pregnancy-related and pregnancy-amplified conditions are increasingly recognized contributors, yet direct MINOCA evidence is uneven
title: Pregnancy-associated MINOCA: Diagnostic challenges and emergency management in young women.
journal: The American journal of emergency medicine

text: . This review examines how hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and inherited thrombophilia, and spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) map onto distinct patterns of coronary and microvascular injury
title: Pregnancy-associated MINOCA: Diagnostic challenges and emergency management in young women.
journal: The American journal of emergency medicine

text: . The links between HDP or GDM and MINOCA are supported mainly by mechanistic and microvascular studies outside dedicated MINOCA cohorts. APS, by contrast, is supported by direct although limited MINOCA-specific data, and pregnancy-associated SCAD is better characterized as a cause of myocardial infarction, although only cases with less than 50% angiographic stenosis meet MINOCA criteria
title: Pregnancy-associated MINOCA: Diagnostic challenges and emergency management in young women.
journal: The American journal of emergency medicine

text: . Serial high-sensitivity cardiac troponin and standard acute coronary syndrome assessment remain the diagnostic foundation. Cardiac magnetic resonance, selective intracoronary imaging, and targeted antiphospholipid testing can refine mechanism assignment after stabilization
title: Pregnancy-associated MINOCA: Diagnostic challenges and emergency management in young women.
journal: The American journal of emergency medicine

text: . The ratio of soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 to placental growth factor is established for the evaluation of suspected preeclampsia, but its relevance to coronary microvascular injury in MINOCA remains uncertain. Inherited thrombophilia testing should be individualized rather than applied routinely
title: Pregnancy-associated MINOCA: Diagnostic challenges and emergency management in young women.
journal: The American journal of emergency medicine

text: . The assigned mechanism should then guide antithrombotic treatment, revascularization decisions, and follow-up. Prospective phenotype-defined studies are needed before routine biomarker-driven strategies can be recommended.
title: Pregnancy-associated MINOCA: Diagnostic challenges and emergency management in young women.
journal: The American journal of emergency medicine

text: Vascular Physiology and Pregnancy Complications.. Maternal vascular adaptations to pregnancy optimize uterine and fetoplacental perfusion. When vascular remodeling and/or function are impaired, the maternal circulation may fail to meet the physiological demands of pregnancy, thereby increasing the risk of complications
title: Vascular Physiology and Pregnancy Complications.

text: . The most common complications of pregnancy affecting maternal vascular health include hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, particularly preeclampsia; infectious or autoimmune diseases that often induce a preeclampsia-like phenotype; metabolic disorders such as gestational diabetes mellitus and excessive hypercholesterolemia; and advanced maternal age
title: Vascular Physiology and Pregnancy Complications.

text: . Moreover, women with a history of a complicated pregnancy have an increased risk of developing later-life cardiovascular disease, representing a sex-specific risk factor
title: Vascular Physiology and Pregnancy Complications.

text: . This review summarizes the mechanisms underlying vascular adaptations to pregnancy and examines how abnormal vascular changes within and beyond the uteroplacental circulation contribute to the development of pregnancy complications, as well as how these complications, in turn, affect maternal vascular health during pregnancy and later in life, focusing on underlying mechanisms.
title: Vascular Physiology and Pregnancy Complications.

text: The Intertwined Threat: How Diabetes Impacts Neurological Disorders - A Review Article.. The chronic illness known as diabetes mellitus (DM) is typified by persistently high blood glucose levels or hyperglycemia
title: The Intertwined Threat: How Diabetes Impacts Neurological Disorders - A Review Article.

text: . Both type 1 and type 2 diabetes, the latter of which is frequently referred to as "adult-onset diabetes" or "insulin-dependent diabetes," are progressing conditions with complex and poorly understood etiologies. Often, patients show positive pancreatic beta-cell antibodies, signifying an autoimmune factor
title: The Intertwined Threat: How Diabetes Impacts Neurological Disorders - A Review Article.

text: . The long-term complications of uncontrolled diabetes are numerous, not just physically based and encompassing everything from kidney failure to foot ulcers and damage to the cardiovascular system, but also with serious neurological disorders, including stroke, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease (AD), and epilepsy
title: The Intertwined Threat: How Diabetes Impacts Neurological Disorders - A Review Article.

text: . The interplay between neurological disorders and diabetes is complex, and the association of these pathological states in their general description proposes common events, namely oxidative stress, mitochondrial damage, amyloid protein aggregation, glucagon-like peptide-1 secretion skewing, and inflammation
title: The Intertwined Threat: How Diabetes Impacts Neurological Disorders - A Review Article.

text: . Learning about these interconnections will help us to develop effective strategies for managing both diabetes and its neurological complications.
title: The Intertwined Threat: How Diabetes Impacts Neurological Disorders - A Review Article.

text: Sleep regularity and efficiency are associated with nocturnal glycemic control in pregnant women with gestational diabetes.. Nocturnal glycemic control is a critical component of blood glucose management for pregnant women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). This study aims to investigate the associations of sleep quality with nocturnal glycemic control among GDM participants
title: Sleep regularity and efficiency are associated with nocturnal glycemic control in pregnant women with gestational diabetes.

text: . This study included 1,186 GDM participants with available data from the WeBirth cohort in Hangzhou, China. Sleep quality and blood glucose levels were assessed simultaneously over 14 days using accelerometers and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices
title: Sleep regularity and efficiency are associated with nocturnal glycemic control in pregnant women with gestational diabetes.

text: . Multivariate linear mixed-effects models were applied to examine the associations of the sleep regularity index (SRI) and sleep efficiency (SE) with CGM-derived nocturnal metrics, adjusting for potential confounders (e.g., maternal age, pre-pregnancy BMI and gestational weeks)
title: Sleep regularity and efficiency are associated with nocturnal glycemic control in pregnant women with gestational diabetes.

text: . Per 1-SD increment in SRI was associated with lower nocturnal glycemic metrics, including coefficient of variation (β = -0.11 SD; 95% CI, -0.13 to -0.08) and time-above-range (β = -0.08 SD; 95% CI, -0.10 to -0.05). SE demonstrated comparable associations with these metrics (coefficient of variation: β = -0.13 SD; 95% CI, -0.16 to -0.11; time-above-range: β = -0.10 SD; 95% CI, -0.12 to -0.08)
title: Sleep regularity and efficiency are associated with nocturnal glycemic control in pregnant women with gestational diabetes.

text: . Further joint analyses indicated that SE exerts an independent, additive effect beyond sleep regularity. Specifically, individuals characterized by both irregular and inefficient sleep exhibited substantially higher mean blood glucose levels compared to those with regular and efficient sleep (β = 0.34 SD; 95% CI, 0.21 to 0.47)
title: Sleep regularity and efficiency are associated with nocturnal glycemic control in pregnant women with gestational diabetes.

text: . This study highlights that regular and efficient sleep patterns are independently and jointly associated with more favourable nocturnal glycemic outcomes in pregnant women with GDM.
title: Sleep regularity and efficiency are associated with nocturnal glycemic control in pregnant women with gestational diabetes.

text: South Asian Women's Perspectives and Recommendations on Gestational Diabetes Care and Postpartum Type 2 Diabetes Prevention in Aotearoa New Zealand: A Qualitative Study.. South Asian (SA) women in New Zealand face a disproportionately high risk of developing gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and subsequent Type 2 diabetes (T2D)
title: South Asian Women's Perspectives and Recommendations on Gestational Diabetes Care and Postpartum Type 2 Diabetes Prevention in Aotearoa New Zealand: A Qualitative Study.

text: . Despite this elevated risk, significant gaps exist in culturally appropriate care for GDM and long-term postpartum follow-up. This qualitative study explored the experiences of SA women to identify the gaps and barriers encountered during and after GDM in transitioning from antenatal GDM care to postpartum primary healthcare and seek suggestions for improvement
title: South Asian Women's Perspectives and Recommendations on Gestational Diabetes Care and Postpartum Type 2 Diabetes Prevention in Aotearoa New Zealand: A Qualitative Study.

text: . To inform culturally responsive care strategies that can reduce the risk of progression to T2D after GDM, 30 semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted with SA women diagnosed with GDM within the past 5 years. Participants were recruited through purposive sampling across New Zealand. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed using an inductive thematic approach
title: South Asian Women's Perspectives and Recommendations on Gestational Diabetes Care and Postpartum Type 2 Diabetes Prevention in Aotearoa New Zealand: A Qualitative Study.

text: . Six key themes with sub-themes were developed: (1) awareness and education; (2) culturally tailored resources; (3) community support; (4) moving backwards to an unhealthy lifestyle; (5) preventing T2D; and (6) improving GDM and postpartum care
title: South Asian Women's Perspectives and Recommendations on Gestational Diabetes Care and Postpartum Type 2 Diabetes Prevention in Aotearoa New Zealand: A Qualitative Study.

text: . Participants advocated for prepregnancy or early counselling, community-based education to reduce stigma, culturally relevant dietary guidance, subsidised follow-up healthcare providers and structured long-term postpartum follow-up. The emotional burden of GDM and inconsistent healthcare communication were also prominent concerns
title: South Asian Women's Perspectives and Recommendations on Gestational Diabetes Care and Postpartum Type 2 Diabetes Prevention in Aotearoa New Zealand: A Qualitative Study.

text: . The findings highlight the need for integrated, culturally congruent and continuous care models for SA and ethnicities at high risk during and after GDM. Incorporating women's suggestions based on their lived experiences into service design may improve postpartum health outcomes and reduce future risk of GDM and T2D.
title: South Asian Women's Perspectives and Recommendations on Gestational Diabetes Care and Postpartum Type 2 Diabetes Prevention in Aotearoa New Zealand: A Qualitative Study.

text: Placental Pathophysiology and Developmental Programming of Adult Cardiometabolic Risk: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Exposures.. Non-communicable diseases remain the dominant cause of adult morbidity and mortality, yet cardiometabolic, vascular and renal risk may originate before birth
title: Placental Pathophysiology and Developmental Programming of Adult Cardiometabolic Risk: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Exposures.
journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

text: . This structured narrative review critically evaluates human evidence linking pregnancy-related exposures, placental pathophysiology and later offspring health within a maternal-placental-fetal-life-course framework. Evidence published from 2020 to 2026 was emphasised, while seminal earlier cohorts were retained when they provided uniquely long follow-up or direct placental measurements
title: Placental Pathophysiology and Developmental Programming of Adult Cardiometabolic Risk: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Exposures.
journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

text: . The most consistent associations concern maternal obesity, gestational diabetes, excessive gestational weight gain and hypertensive disorders, which are linked with higher offspring blood pressure, greater adiposity and adverse glucose-insulin profiles
title: Placental Pathophysiology and Developmental Programming of Adult Cardiometabolic Risk: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Exposures.
journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

text: . Human placental studies implicate vascular malperfusion, altered nutrient transport, inflammatory and oxidative signalling, endocrine function and epigenetic regulation
title: Placental Pathophysiology and Developmental Programming of Adult Cardiometabolic Risk: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Exposures.
journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

text: . Few studies, however, have measured the prenatal exposure, a specific placental phenotype and a long-term offspring outcome within the same longitudinal design; most proposed placental pathways are supported by convergent evidence or biological plausibility rather than demonstrated mediation
title: Placental Pathophysiology and Developmental Programming of Adult Cardiometabolic Risk: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Exposures.
journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

text: . Preterm birth and fetal growth restriction are clinically observable, etiologically heterogeneous sentinel phenotypes, not obligatory mediators. Placental and offspring epigenetic signatures, telomere biology and mitochondrial function represent distinct domains of biological embedding; their causal and prognostic significance remains uncertain
title: Placental Pathophysiology and Developmental Programming of Adult Cardiometabolic Risk: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Exposures.
journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

text: . Longitudinal studies integrating maternal exposures, placental histopathology and molecular phenotypes, fetal organ development, childhood cardiometabolic trajectories and adult clinical outcomes are needed to determine whether, and under what circumstances, the placenta plays an intermediary role rather than merely serving as a marker of an adverse pregnancy environment.
title: Placental Pathophysiology and Developmental Programming of Adult Cardiometabolic Risk: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Exposures.
journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

text: Folate: An Emerging Target in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Its Complications.. Folate, which is also known as folic acid, vitamin B9, is a key coenzyme in one-carbon metabolism (OCM) and participates in nucleic acid synthesis, methylation, and redox regulation
title: Folate: An Emerging Target in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Its Complications.

text: . In recent years, numerous studies have demonstrated its close association with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and diabetic complications. Serum folate levels are decreased in patients with T2DM, which is associated with increased urinary excretion and metformin-mediated inhibition of folate absorption
title: Folate: An Emerging Target in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Its Complications.

text: . The onset of GDM is characterized by a folate dose-dependent imbalance characteristic, high folate combined with vitamin B12 deficiency significantly increases the risk of GDM. Maternal folate status can also modulate offspring insulin sensitivity through epigenetic modifications
title: Folate: An Emerging Target in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Its Complications.

text: . The mechanisms by which folate regulates diabetes mainly include lowering homocysteine (Hcy) concentrations, suppressing oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, modulating OCM, and mediating DNA methylation modifications
title: Folate: An Emerging Target in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Its Complications.

text: . Cumulative evidence-based data indicate that appropriate folic acid supplementation can improve insulin resistance, restore vascular endothelial function, reduce the risk of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), diabetic peripheral neuropathy, retinopathy, cognitive impairment, and other complications, and alleviate damage induced by high glucose
title: Folate: An Emerging Target in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Its Complications.

text: . This review systematically summarizes the roles and molecular mechanisms of folate in diabetes and its complications, highlighting folate as a potential intervention target for diabetes.
title: Folate: An Emerging Target in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Its Complications.

text: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Incident Dementia.. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs) are established markers of later-life cardiovascular disease, but their association with dementia remains uncertain. To investigate whether HDPs are associated with incident dementia in a nationwide population-based cohort with more than 2 decades of follow-up
title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Incident Dementia.

text: . This retrospective cohort study used the Korean National Health Insurance Service database to identify females aged 16 years or older who delivered between January 1, 2002, and December 31, 2005, and followed up through December 31, 2024. Statistical analyses were conducted between October 2025 and May 2026
title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Incident Dementia.

text: . HDPs were defined as gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, HELLP (hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelet count) syndrome, or eclampsia. The primary outcome was incident dementia, including Alzheimer disease and vascular dementia. Cox proportional hazards regression models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs
title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Incident Dementia.

text: . Among 1 370 485 females (mean [SD] age, 29.2 [3.9] years), 28 747 (2.1%) experienced HDPs. The cumulative incidence of dementia was higher among females with HDPs than among those without HDPs (7.2 vs 2.8 per 10 000 females; P < .001), as was the incidence density of dementia (3.00 vs 1.05 per 100 000 person-years; P < .001)
title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Incident Dementia.

text: . In model 1, HDPs were associated with an increased risk of incident dementia after adjustment for baseline maternal, socioeconomic, and obstetric factors (adjusted HR, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.19-3.23)
title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Incident Dementia.

text: . In model 2, after additional adjustment for postdelivery hypertension, diabetes, myocardial infarction, and stroke, the association was attenuated and was no longer statistically significant (adjusted HR, 1.15; 95% CI, 0.70-1.91). In this cohort study, HDPs were associated with an increased risk of incident dementia after adjustment for baseline maternal, socioeconomic, and obstetric factors
title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Incident Dementia.

text: . However, this association was no longer statistically significant after additional adjustment for postdelivery vascular and metabolic conditions. Given the small number of dementia events among females with HDPs, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. These findings suggest that HDPs may serve as an early-life marker of long-term neurovascular vulnerability.
title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Incident Dementia.

text: Lipodystrophies and female reproduction: pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, and management across the reproductive lifespan.. Lipodystrophies represent a heterogeneous group of rare disorders characterized by partial or generalized loss of adipose tissue, leading to severe metabolic derangements and endocrine dysfunction
title: Lipodystrophies and female reproduction: pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, and management across the reproductive lifespan.

text: . In women, these disorders are frequently accompanied by reproductive abnormalities ranging from hypogonadotropic amenorrhea to hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovary syndrome-like phenotypes
title: Lipodystrophies and female reproduction: pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, and management across the reproductive lifespan.

text: . To summarize current knowledge linking adipose-tissue dysfunction and female reproductive health, focusing on mechanistic pathways, clinical manifestations, fertility outcomes, contraception, pregnancy complications, and therapeutic perspectives including leptin replacement
title: Lipodystrophies and female reproduction: pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, and management across the reproductive lifespan.

text: . A comprehensive review of PubMed and guideline literature (1996-2025) was performed, prioritizing official recommendations, registry data, and recent mechanistic and clinical studies
title: Lipodystrophies and female reproduction: pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, and management across the reproductive lifespan.

text: . Profound leptin deficiency in generalized lipodystrophy leads to hypothalamic suppression of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) and amenorrhea, whereas hyperinsulinemia and androgen excess dominate partial forms, producing anovulation and infertility
title: Lipodystrophies and female reproduction: pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, and management across the reproductive lifespan.

text: . Metreleptin therapy restores ovulatory cycles in leptin-deficient women and improves metabolic control, while pregnancy carries heightened risks of gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, and pancreatitis. Oral estrogens exacerbate hypertriglyceridemia; thus, progestin-only or non-hormonal contraception is preferred, and transdermal estrogen may be considered for hormone replacement
title: Lipodystrophies and female reproduction: pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, and management across the reproductive lifespan.

text: . Female reproductive dysfunction in lipodystrophy results from complex interactions between leptin, insulin, and gonadal steroid pathways. A multidisciplinary approach is required to optimize metabolic and reproductive outcomes, while prospective data on fertility and pregnancy under metreleptin remain crucial for future practice.
title: Lipodystrophies and female reproduction: pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, and management across the reproductive lifespan.

text: Automated Insulin Delivery for Pregnancy With Type 1 Diabetes: A Call to Action.. Type 1 diabetes (T1D) requires intensive glycemic management in pregnancy with insulin to achieve pregnancy-specific glycemic targets and avoid serious maternal and perinatal morbidity
title: Automated Insulin Delivery for Pregnancy With Type 1 Diabetes: A Call to Action.

text: . Glycemic targets for pregnancy, which are lower than those outside pregnancy, are extremely challenging to achieve, resulting in considerable burden and psychosocial distress for pregnant women living with T1D. While automated insulin delivery (AID) is now the recommended mode of insulin delivery for T1D, pregnant women with T1D have been left behind. AID systems approved by the U.S
title: Automated Insulin Delivery for Pregnancy With Type 1 Diabetes: A Call to Action.

text: . AID systems approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for use in the U.S. are not designed to meet pregnancy glycemic targets, and most are not labeled for pregnancy. Broad exclusion of pregnant participants from clinical trials, including those of AID systems, has resulted in extremely limited data to guide the use of these devices in pregnancy
title: Automated Insulin Delivery for Pregnancy With Type 1 Diabetes: A Call to Action.

text: . Furthermore, for most devices insulin delivery is reduced when continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) sensor values are in the optimal range for fetal well-being. We call on stakeholders to deliver AID systems that meet the needs of pregnant women with T1D so that they can use AID at a time in life when they stand to benefit the most
title: Automated Insulin Delivery for Pregnancy With Type 1 Diabetes: A Call to Action.

text: . Specifically, we should include pregnant women in clinical trials of new AID technologies, design AID systems that can meet the unique glycemic management challenges of pregnancy, and support real-world studies of currently approved AID systems while we await pregnancy-specific innovations.
title: Automated Insulin Delivery for Pregnancy With Type 1 Diabetes: A Call to Action.

text: Metabolite Signatures in Postpartum Prediabetes and Diabetes Among Indian Women With Prior Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Insights From CHIP-F Study.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) increases the risk of postpartum dysglycaemia
title: Metabolite Signatures in Postpartum Prediabetes and Diabetes Among Indian Women With Prior Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Insights From CHIP-F Study.

text: . This study investigates candidate metabolites and perturbed metabolic pathways associated with postpartum prediabetes/diabetes among high-risk Indian/South-Asian women with prior GDM, a largely unexplored population
title: Metabolite Signatures in Postpartum Prediabetes and Diabetes Among Indian Women With Prior Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Insights From CHIP-F Study.

text: . In this nested case-control study within the Cohort of Indian Women with Hyperglycaemia in Pregnancy and their Families (CHIP-F), untargeted metabolomics (UPLC-MS/MS) was performed on plasma samples from 216 women with prior GDM, which included 22 participants with postpartum diabetes, 88 with prediabetes and 106 with normoglycaemia
title: Metabolite Signatures in Postpartum Prediabetes and Diabetes Among Indian Women With Prior Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Insights From CHIP-F Study.

text: . Untargeted metabolomics combined with machine learning approach revealed distinct metabolic alterations associated with postpartum dysglycaemia (prediabetes/diabetes) among women with prior GDM
title: Metabolite Signatures in Postpartum Prediabetes and Diabetes Among Indian Women With Prior Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Insights From CHIP-F Study.

text: . After adjustment for age, body mass index, family history of diabetes, and postpartum duration, each 1-standard deviation increase in the log-transformed concentrations of Tyrosine (aOR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.01-2.91) and L-Kynurenine (aOR = 1.69, 1.02-2.80) was associated with higher odds of diabetes
title: Metabolite Signatures in Postpartum Prediabetes and Diabetes Among Indian Women With Prior Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Insights From CHIP-F Study.

text: . Similarly, higher concentrations of 2-Aminoisobutyric acid (aOR = 1.50, 1.09-2.06), Butyrylcarnitine (aOR = 1.99, 1.44-2.75), L-Norleucine (aOR = 1.96, 1.41-2.72), and Propionylcarnitine (aOR = 1.94, 1.41-2.67) were associated with higher odds of prediabetes. Pathway analysis revealed potential dysregulation of aromatic amino acids (AAAs) metabolism in prediabetes
title: Metabolite Signatures in Postpartum Prediabetes and Diabetes Among Indian Women With Prior Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Insights From CHIP-F Study.

text: . In diabetes, in addition to dysregulation of AAAs, potential lipid metabolic disturbances were also present. This study identified distinct candidate metabolic signatures associated with postpartum prediabetes and diabetes in Indian/South-Asian women with a history of prior GDM, highlighting early disruptions in AAAs and lipid metabolism.
title: Metabolite Signatures in Postpartum Prediabetes and Diabetes Among Indian Women With Prior Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Insights From CHIP-F Study.

text: Phospholipid transfer protein: The link between lipid metabolism and inflammation in healthy pregnancy and pregnancy with cardiometabolic complications.. Phospholipid transfer protein (PLTP) regulates high-density lipoprotein (HDL) remodelling by transferring cholesterol and phospholipids and affecting particle size and function
title: Phospholipid transfer protein: The link between lipid metabolism and inflammation in healthy pregnancy and pregnancy with cardiometabolic complications.

text: . Pregnancy alters lipid metabolism, but the adaptation of PLTP to pregnancy remains poorly understood. This study investigated longitudinal changes in PLTP gene expression and concentration during healthy pregnancy and pregnancy with cardiometabolic complications, and their associations with maternal lipid metabolism and inflammatory status
title: Phospholipid transfer protein: The link between lipid metabolism and inflammation in healthy pregnancy and pregnancy with cardiometabolic complications.

text: . We followed 84 healthy and 20 pregnant women who developed gestational diabetes mellitus and hypertensive disorders during pregnancy. PLTP gene expression, PLTP concentration, advanced lipid profile parameters, and inflammatory status were analysed throughout the trimesters
title: Phospholipid transfer protein: The link between lipid metabolism and inflammation in healthy pregnancy and pregnancy with cardiometabolic complications.

text: . Fosfolipidni transfer protein (PLTP) reguliše remodelovanje lipoproteina visoke gustine (HDL) prenosom holesterola i fosfolipida, menjajući njihovu veličinu i funkcionalnost. Trudnoća je praćena promenom u metabolizmu lipida, međutim, uloga PLTP-a tokom trudnoće još uvek nije u potpunosti razjašnjena
title: Phospholipid transfer protein: The link between lipid metabolism and inflammation in healthy pregnancy and pregnancy with cardiometabolic complications.

text: . Ova studija je ispitivala longitudinalne promene ekspresije PLTP gena i koncentracije tokom zdrave trudnoće i trudnoće sa kardiometabolickim komplikacijama, kao i njihovu povezanost sa metabolizmom lipida i inflamatornim statusom majke. Praćeno je 84 zdravih trudnica i 20 trudnica kod kojih su se tokom trudnoće razvili gestacijski dijabetes mellitus ili hipertenzivni poremećaji
title: Phospholipid transfer protein: The link between lipid metabolism and inflammation in healthy pregnancy and pregnancy with cardiometabolic complications.

text: . Ekspresija gena za PLTP, koncentracija PLTP-a, parametri proširenog lipidnog profila i inflamatorni status analizirani su tokom trimestra. Sličan tok promena ekspresije gena za PLTP i koncentracija PLTP-a uočen je u obe grupe, ali je ekspresija gena za PLTP u prvom trimestru bila značajno niža u grupi sa komplikacijama (p<0,05)
title: Phospholipid transfer protein: The link between lipid metabolism and inflammation in healthy pregnancy and pregnancy with cardiometabolic complications.

text: . Analiza serumskih neholesterolskih sterola u HDL subfrakcijama (NCSHDL) i plazmatskih ceramida [ceramid C16:0 (Cer C16:0), ceramid C24:0 (Cer C24:0)] pokazala je značajno niže koncentracije dezmosterolaHDL (p<0,05), kao i značajno više koncentracije C24:0 (p<0,001) u grupi sa komplikacijama u prvom trimestru
title: Phospholipid transfer protein: The link between lipid metabolism and inflammation in healthy pregnancy and pregnancy with cardiometabolic complications.

text: . Rezultati studije ukazuju na izmenjenu ekspresiju gena za PLTP, prošireni lipidni profil i inflamatorni status u prvom trimestru trudnoće sa kardiometaboličkim komplikacijama. Dobijeni rezultati naglašavaju značaj detaljnog ispitivanja metabolizma lipida i inflamatornih puteva u ranoj trudnoći u cilju unapređenja ishoda trudnoće.
title: Phospholipid transfer protein: The link between lipid metabolism and inflammation in healthy pregnancy and pregnancy with cardiometabolic complications.

text: Disparities in low-dose aspirin prescription among patients at risk for preeclampsia.. Low-dose aspirin (LDA) reduces preeclampsia risk, yet prescribing rates among eligible pregnant patients remain low
title: Disparities in low-dose aspirin prescription among patients at risk for preeclampsia.

text: . This study aims to determine whether there are disparities in LDA prescription to eligible patients based on race/ethnicity, primary language, or insurance after implementation of a standardized electronic health record (EHR) preeclampsia risk screening tool
title: Disparities in low-dose aspirin prescription among patients at risk for preeclampsia.

text: . The primary outcome was rate of LDA recommendation/prescription, determined by recommendation documentation in the risk screening tool or prescription in the EHR medication log
title: Disparities in low-dose aspirin prescription among patients at risk for preeclampsia.

text: . Data were extracted from Epic Clinical Data Warehouse. Chi-square or  Of 5737 LDA-eligible patients, 3995 (69.6%) were recommended/prescribed LDA and 1742 (30.4%) were not
title: Disparities in low-dose aspirin prescription among patients at risk for preeclampsia.

text: . Patients recommended/prescribed LDA were more likely to be older, multiparous, English speaking, and privately insured and/or have pregestational diabetes or chronic hypertension, as well as high-risk factors for preeclampsia ( After implementation of a standardized preeclmapsia risk screening tool, LDA was more often prescribed to eligible Black patients than White, likely reflecting ACOG's

text: patients than White, likely reflecting ACOG's inclusion of Black race as a proxy for racism as a preeclmapsia risk factor

text: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.. Insulin resistance is a central biochemical abnormality in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and is closely linked to chronic low-grade inflammation
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Pro-inflammatory cytokines and adipokines, including tumor necrosis factor-a (TNF-a), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and adiponectin (APN), play key roles in metabolic dysregulation during pregnancy. This study investigated the effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-related inflammatory biomarkers and their gene polymorphisms in pregnant women with GDM
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . In this retrospective comparative cohort study, 400 pregnant women diagnosed with GDM at Hainan Women and Children's Medical Center between October 2023 and December 2024 were enrolled and assigned to a conventional treatment group (CT, n = 200) or a nutritional intervention group (NC, n = 200)
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Both groups received standard glycemic management, while the NC group additionally underwent individualized nutritional intervention. Serum levels of TNF-a, IL-6, and APN were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and polymorphisms of the corresponding genes were analyzed using fluorescence quantitative PCR. Glycemic and lipid parameters were evaluated concurrently
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Clinical efficacy and pregnancy outcomes were assessed as secondary endpoints. Insulinska rezistencija je centralna biohemjska abnormalnost kod gestacijskog dijabetes melitusa (GDM) i usko j'e povezana sa hroničnom upalom niskog stepena
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Proinflamatorni citokini i adipokini, uklj'učuj'ući faktor tumorske nekroze-a (TNF-a), interleukin-6 (IL-6) i adiponektin (APN), igraj'u klj'učnu ulogu u metaboličkoj' disregulaciji tokom trudnoće. Ova studija je istraživala efekte nutritivne intervencij'e na inflamatorne biomarkere povezane sa insulinskom rezistencij'om i nj'ihove genske polimorfizme kod trudnica sa GDM
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . U ovoj' retrospektivnoj' komparativnoj' kohortnoj' studiji, 400 trudnica sa dijagnozom gestacijskog dijabetesa (GD) u Medicinskom centru za žene i decu Haj'nan između oktobra 2023. i decembra 2024. godine uklj'učene su i raspoređene u konvencionalnu grupu za lečenje (KT, n = 200) ili grupu za nutritivnu intervencju (NK, n = 200)
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Obe grupe su primale standardno upravljanje glikemijom, dok je NK grupa dodatno podvrgnuta individualizovanoj nutritivnoj' intervencij'i. Serumski nivoi TNF-a, IL-6 i APN mereni su imunosorbentnim testom povezanim sa enzimima, a polimorfizmi odgovaraj'ućih gena analizirani su korišćenj'em fluorescentne kvantitativne PCR. Glikemij'ski i lipidni parametri su procenj'eni istovremeno
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Klinička efikasnost i ishodi trudnoće procenjeni su kao sekundarni krajnji ciljevi. Distribucija genotipova TNF-a, IL-6 i APN nije pokazala značajne razlike između dve grupe (P > 0,05). Početni inflamatorni, glikemijski i lipidni indeksi bili su uporedivi između grupa
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Nakon intervencije, obe grupe su pokazale značajna poboljšanja inflamatornih markera, glukoze u krvi i lipidnih profila u poređenju sa početnim vrednostima (P < 0,05). Primetno je da su nivoi TNF-a i IL-6 nakon tretmana bili značajno niži, dok su nivoi APN bili povoljnije regulisani u NC grupi u poređenju sa CT grupom (P < 0,05)
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . NC grupa je takođe pokazala superiornu metaboličku kontrolu i manju učestalost neželjenih ishoda trudnoće. Nutritivna intervencija značajno poboljšava inflamatorne i metaboličke profile povezane sa insulinskom rezistencijom kod trudnica sa gestacijskim dijabetesom (GDM), nezavisno od polimorfizama gena TNF-a, IL-6 i APN
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Ovi nalazi ističu biohemijske koristi nutritivne modulacije u smanjenju upale i poboljšanju metaboličke homeostaze kod GDM.
title: Effects of nutritional intervention on insulin resistance-associated inflammatory biomarkers and gene polymorphisms in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: First-trimester SPISE mediates the association between early-pregnancy body fat percentage change and gestational diabetes mellitus: an exploratory secondary analysis of a prospective cohort.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is closely related to maternal adiposity and insulin resistance
title: First-trimester SPISE mediates the association between early-pregnancy body fat percentage change and gestational diabetes mellitus: an exploratory secondary analysis of a prospective cohort.

text: . The rate of body fat percentage (BFP) change in early pregnancy may describe estimated BFP gain before routine glucose screening. The Single-Point Insulin Sensitivity Estimator (SPISE) offers a fasting estimate of insulin sensitivity without insulin testing. title: Cohort profile: the Shenzhen Birth Cohort (SZBC) study.

title: Investigating the association between COVID-19 exposure and fetal and maternal health before public health vaccinations: A retrospective cohort study.

text: Metformin Inhibits Trophoblast Ferroptosis by Suppressing ATF2 and Activating the PI3K/Akt/Nrf2 Pathway to Improve Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.. text: Pregnancy-unmasked latent autoimmune arginine vasopressin deficiency with anti-rabphilin-3a antibody positivity.. title: Pregnancy-unmasked latent autoimmune arginine vasopressin deficiency with anti-rabphilin-3a antibody positivity.

title: Pregnancy-unmasked latent autoimmune arginine vasopressin deficiency with anti-rabphilin-3a antibody positivity.

title: Beyond histocompatibility: human leukocyte antigen as a cross-disciplinary platform for immune recognition and clinical decision-making.

title: Beyond histocompatibility: human leukocyte antigen as a cross-disciplinary platform for immune recognition and clinical decision-making.

title: Beyond histocompatibility: human leukocyte antigen as a cross-disciplinary platform for immune recognition and clinical decision-making.

title: Beyond histocompatibility: human leukocyte antigen as a cross-disciplinary platform for immune recognition and clinical decision-making.

text: . In transfusion medicine, recipient alloimmunisation can cause platelet refractoriness and complicate future transplantation, whereas donor antibodies contribute to transfusion-related acute lung injury. Transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease is a different cellular complication
title: Beyond histocompatibility: human leukocyte antigen as a cross-disciplinary platform for immune recognition and clinical decision-making.

title: Beyond histocompatibility: human leukocyte antigen as a cross-disciplinary platform for immune recognition and clinical decision-making.

title: Beyond histocompatibility: human leukocyte antigen as a cross-disciplinary platform for immune recognition and clinical decision-making.

title: Beyond histocompatibility: human leukocyte antigen as a cross-disciplinary platform for immune recognition and clinical decision-making.
