text: Thyroid disease in pregnancy and the risk of venous thromboembolism: a Danish nationwide cohort study.. Thyroid hormones have widespread regulatory effects, including an effect on haemostasis. It has been hypothesised that abnormal levels of thyroid hormones can influence the risk of developing thrombosis, and the association is yet to be investigated during pregnancy and the postpartum period
title: Thyroid disease in pregnancy and the risk of venous thromboembolism: a Danish nationwide cohort study.

text: . A retrospective cohort study utilising nationwide health registers on diagnoses and medications was performed examining pregnancies in Denmark from 1999 to 2015 exposed to maternal hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism. Cases of venous thromboembolism (VTE) during pregnancy and up to one year after the pregnancy had ended were identified
title: Thyroid disease in pregnancy and the risk of venous thromboembolism: a Danish nationwide cohort study.

text: . Multivariate logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between maternal thyroid disease and venous thromboses, reported as adjusted odds ratio (aOR) with a 95% confidence interval (CI). Among 1,149,871 pregnancies studied, 12,633 (1.1%) were exposed to maternal hyperthyroidism and 17,940 (1.6%) to maternal hypothyroidism
title: Thyroid disease in pregnancy and the risk of venous thromboembolism: a Danish nationwide cohort study.

text: . Overall, VTE was diagnosed more often among women with hyperthyroidism (0.41%; aOR: 1.39, 95% CI: 1.06-1.83) and hypothyroidism (0.44%; aOR: 1.43, 95% CI: 1.14-1.79) than among non-exposed women (0.28%)
title: Thyroid disease in pregnancy and the risk of venous thromboembolism: a Danish nationwide cohort study.

text: . However, when adjusting for maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index, a higher risk of thrombosis was found among women with hyperthyroidism (aOR: 1.47, 95% CI: 1.08-2.01), whereas the association with hypothyroidism levelled out (aOR: 1.25, 95% CI: 0.96-1.62). In a large, nationwide cohort, an association between maternal thyroid disease and VTE diagnosed in relation to pregnancy was found
title: Thyroid disease in pregnancy and the risk of venous thromboembolism: a Danish nationwide cohort study.

text: . Results point towards maternal hyperthyroidism as the predominant risk factor for thrombosis and draw attention to confounding factors in the association with hypothyroidism.
title: Thyroid disease in pregnancy and the risk of venous thromboembolism: a Danish nationwide cohort study.

text: Type C esophageal atresia masked by multiple overlapping causes of polyhydramnios in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy: A case report.. Polyhydramnios is a condition defined as an increase of amniotic fluid volume. Common causes include maternal diabetes, multiple pregnancies, and congenital anomalies
title: Type C esophageal atresia masked by multiple overlapping causes of polyhydramnios in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy: A case report.

text: . Congenital type C esophageal atresia is one of the causes and often presents with a visible stomach, making prenatal diagnosis difficult. A 37-year-old woman with monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy was hospitalized for threatened preterm labor at 26 weeks of gestation
title: Type C esophageal atresia masked by multiple overlapping causes of polyhydramnios in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy: A case report.

text: . She was also diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus and her glucose levels were consistently high during pregnancy despite the initiation of insulin therapy. After admission to hospital, the amniotic fluid volume of the leading twin remained at the lower limit of the normal range, while polyhydramnios appeared in the following twin
title: Type C esophageal atresia masked by multiple overlapping causes of polyhydramnios in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy: A case report.

text: . Persistent amniotic fluid discordance raised concern for a possible evolving intertwin transfusion process, although the diagnostic criteria for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome were not met. An emergency cesarean section was performed at 28 weeks due to onset of labor. After birth, twin B showed mild cardiomegaly and polycythemia, findings compatible with recipient-like pathophysiology
title: Type C esophageal atresia masked by multiple overlapping causes of polyhydramnios in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy: A case report.

text: . Furthermore, the same twin showed a coiled nasogastric tube on chest X-ray and was diagnosed with type C esophageal atresia postnatally. This case illustrates polyhydramnios in the setting of overlapping etiologies, gestational diabetes mellitus, esophageal atresia, and twin amniotic fluid discordance suggestive of an evolving intertwin transfusion process
title: Type C esophageal atresia masked by multiple overlapping causes of polyhydramnios in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy: A case report.

text: . Clinicians should consider multifactorial causes when managing unexplained polyhydramnios and perform comprehensive fetal evaluations.
title: Type C esophageal atresia masked by multiple overlapping causes of polyhydramnios in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy: A case report.

text: [Prognostic research in endocrinology: design and common errors].. This article provides a conceptual overview of the methodology and design of prognostic research. It presents cohort studies as the most suitable design for prognostic investigations and discusses in detail the distinctions between traditional etio logical cohort studies and those primarily aimed at predicting outcomes
title: [Prognostic research in endocrinology: design and common errors].

text: . The article reviews examples of prognostic studies that focus on predicting gestational diabetes mellitus, renal failure in type 2 diabetes mellitus, osteoporotic fractures in postmenopausal women, outcomes of infertility treatment in women with elevated follicle-stimulating hormone levels, and survival in patients with adrenocortical carcinoma
title: [Prognostic research in endocrinology: design and common errors].

text: . The importance of adhering to the methodological standards outlined in the STROBE and TRIPOD guidelines is emphasized. It also highlights the need to avoid common design and analytical pitfalls, such as measuring predictors after the outcome has occurred or using ROC analysis without developing a multivari able prediction model
title: [Prognostic research in endocrinology: design and common errors].

text: . Particular attention is given to employing appropriate statistical methods, as a lack of understanding of these methods may lead to biased inferences and diminish the scientific value of the published research. Incorporating well-designed prognostic cohort studies and rigorous analytical approaches will enhance clinical practice and strengthen the evidence base in modern endocrinology
title: [Prognostic research in endocrinology: design and common errors].

text: . Данная статья представляет собой аналитический обзор методологии и дизайна прогностических исследований. Оптимальным дизайном для прогностических исследований являются когортные исследования. В обзоре подробно рассматриваются различия между традиционными этиологическими когортными исследованиями и исследованиями, ориентированными на прогнозирование исходов
title: [Prognostic research in endocrinology: design and common errors].

text: . Приводятся примеры прогностических исследований, посвященных оценке риска гестационного сахарного диабета (ГСД), почечной недостаточности при сахарном диабете 2 типа (СД2), остеопоротических переломов у женщин в постменопаузе, результатов лечения бесплодия у женщин с повышенным уровнем фолликулостимулирующего гормона и выживаемости у пациентов с адренокортикальным раком
title: [Prognostic research in endocrinology: design and common errors].

text: . Подчеркивается важность соблюдения методологических стандартов, изложенных в руководствах STROBE и TRIPOD, а также необходимость предотвращения типичных методологических ошибок, таких как измерение предикторов после наступления исхода или использование ROC-анализа без предварительного построения прогностической модели
title: [Prognostic research in endocrinology: design and common errors].

text: . Особое внимание уделяется применению корректных статистических методов, поскольку их недостаточное понимание может привести к искаженным выводам и снижению научной достоверности результатов. Развитие прогностических когортных исследований и внедрение строгих аналитических подходов способствует повышению качества клинической практики и укреплению доказательной базы современной эндокринологии.
title: [Prognostic research in endocrinology: design and common errors].

text: Adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with atopic dermatitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.. The impact of atopic dermatitis (AD) on pregnancy outcomes has been largely uncertain, and clarifying this association is essential for improving maternal counselling, risk stratification and clinical management. To assess the association between AD in pregnant women and adverse pregnancy outcomes
title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with atopic dermatitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV

text: . MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 7th September 2025. We included cohort studies that assessed the association between AD and pregnancy outcomes. Maternal outcomes included mode of delivery, obstetric complications and maternal mortality
title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with atopic dermatitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV

text: . Neonatal outcomes included preterm birth, perinatal mortality, impaired foetal growth, congenital anomalies, neonatal infections and other adverse neonatal outcomes. We used the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) to assess the risk of bias of included studies. A random-effects model meta-analysis was undertaken
title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with atopic dermatitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV

text: . We included eight cohort studies involving 278,671 women with AD and over 2,738,216 controls. The meta-analysis found associations of maternal AD with premature rupture of membranes [pooled odds ratio (OR) 1.16, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.09-1.24] and low birth weight (<2500 g, pooled OR 1.11, 95% CI 1.02-1.20)
title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with atopic dermatitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV

text: . Maternal AD was also associated with increased risk of gestational hypertension (pooled OR 1.15, 95% CI 1.02-1.29) and pre-eclampsia/eclampsia (pooled OR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.19). One study indicated increased neonatal septicaemia caused by Staphylococcal species (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.33-4.49)
title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with atopic dermatitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV

text: . Maternal AD is associated with a modestly increased risk of premature rupture of membranes, gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia/eclampsia and notably neonatal Staphylococcal septicaemia. Obstetricians and dermatologists should be aware of these risks, monitor pregnancy complications closely and provide appropriate management when necessary.
title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with atopic dermatitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV

text: Why the Gap Persists: A Systematic Review of Sociocultural, Clinical, and Systemic Factors Driving Maternal Health Disparities Between Black and White Women in the United Kingdom.. Despite overall low maternal mortality rates in the United Kingdom, Black women are approximately four times more likely to die during pregnancy, childbirth, or the postnatal period than White women
title: Why the Gap Persists: A Systematic Review of Sociocultural, Clinical, and Systemic Factors Driving Maternal Health Disparities Between Black and White Women in the United Kingdom.

text: . This disparity has persisted for over a decade despite national initiatives. This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence from 2010-2025 on sociocultural, clinical, and systemic factors contributing to maternal health disparities between Black and White women in the United Kingdom (UK)
title: Why the Gap Persists: A Systematic Review of Sociocultural, Clinical, and Systemic Factors Driving Maternal Health Disparities Between Black and White Women in the United Kingdom.

text: . Databases such as MEDLINE, Embase, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), PsycINFO, and Web of Science (January 2010-December 2025) were searched along with grey literature sources including EthOS, OpenGrey, Mothers and Babies: Reducing Risk through Audits and Confidential Enquiries across the UK (MBRRACE-UK), Birthrights, and NHS Race and Health Observatory
title: Why the Gap Persists: A Systematic Review of Sociocultural, Clinical, and Systemic Factors Driving Maternal Health Disparities Between Black and White Women in the United Kingdom.

text: . We included primary research studies (quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-methods) published in English that examined maternal health outcomes, experiences, or carer processes for Black and White women in the UK and analyzed at least one sociocultural, clinical, or systemic factor associated with disparities
title: Why the Gap Persists: A Systematic Review of Sociocultural, Clinical, and Systemic Factors Driving Maternal Health Disparities Between Black and White Women in the United Kingdom.

text: . Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts in Rayyan, extracted data using a piloted form, and assessed quality using Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklists, Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP), and Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Narrative synthesis was conducted. Thirty-six studies were included, with 66.7% published post-2020
title: Why the Gap Persists: A Systematic Review of Sociocultural, Clinical, and Systemic Factors Driving Maternal Health Disparities Between Black and White Women in the United Kingdom.

text: . Sociocultural factors centered on experiences of discrimination and "not being listened to," which eroded trust and delayed care-seeking. Clinical factors confirmed higher prevalence of hypertensive disorders, pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, and postpartum hemorrhage in Black women; however, disparities in escalation and response persisted after adjusting for comorbidities
title: Why the Gap Persists: A Systematic Review of Sociocultural, Clinical, and Systemic Factors Driving Maternal Health Disparities Between Black and White Women in the United Kingdom.

text: . Systemic issues included inconsistent continuity of care implementation, workforce underrepresentation, and a "postcode lottery" in service provision. The evidence demonstrates that disparities arise from the interaction of all three domains rather than any single factor. Multi-level interventions addressing sociocultural, clinical, and systemic factors simultaneously are essential
title: Why the Gap Persists: A Systematic Review of Sociocultural, Clinical, and Systemic Factors Driving Maternal Health Disparities Between Black and White Women in the United Kingdom.

text: . Future priorities include continuity of carer models, discrimination-focused longitudinal studies, and implementation science research. The persistence of these disparities requires sustained commitment from clinicians, policymakers, and researchers to translate evidence into meaningful action.
title: Why the Gap Persists: A Systematic Review of Sociocultural, Clinical, and Systemic Factors Driving Maternal Health Disparities Between Black and White Women in the United Kingdom.

text: Brain and behavioural responses to food viewing in women during pregnancy and their relationship with metabolic health: study protocol for the FOODY Play Study - a prospective observational study.. Food cravings are common in pregnancy and contribute to excessive gestational weight gain (GWG)
title: Brain and behavioural responses to food viewing in women during pregnancy and their relationship with metabolic health: study protocol for the FOODY Play Study - a prospective observational study.

text: . Excessive GWG is present across all body mass index (BMI) categories and is associated with adverse outcomes. Outside of pregnancy, highly palatable food cues activate brain regions involved in reward and attention, which may influence eating behaviour and behavioural responses
title: Brain and behavioural responses to food viewing in women during pregnancy and their relationship with metabolic health: study protocol for the FOODY Play Study - a prospective observational study.

text: . However, brain and behavioural responses to food cues across pregnancy, and their association with psychological and metabolic factors, remain poorly understood. This study aims to investigate spatiotemporal brain responses to visual food cues across individuals with different BMI categories and their associations with behavioural, psychological and metabolic outcomes during pregnancy
title: Brain and behavioural responses to food viewing in women during pregnancy and their relationship with metabolic health: study protocol for the FOODY Play Study - a prospective observational study.

title: Brain and behavioural responses to food viewing in women during pregnancy and their relationship with metabolic health: study protocol for the FOODY Play Study - a prospective observational study.

title: Brain and behavioural responses to food viewing in women during pregnancy and their relationship with metabolic health: study protocol for the FOODY Play Study - a prospective observational study.

text: . Secondary validated outcomes include heart rate variability (Actiheart), body composition (InBody S10), glycated haemoglobin (Afinion), cardiorespiratory fitness (The Chester step test), snack intake, eating behaviour (Intuitive Eating Scale-2, Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire-Revised), food cravings (Food Craving Questionnaire-state), mood and depressive symptoms (Edinburgh Postnatal
title: Brain and behavioural responses to food viewing in women during pregnancy and their relationship with metabolic health: study protocol for the FOODY Play Study - a prospective observational study.

title: Brain and behavioural responses to food viewing in women during pregnancy and their relationship with metabolic health: study protocol for the FOODY Play Study - a prospective observational study.

text: Baseline differences and comparative change in pregnancy and birth outcomes for the Asian Indian American population: Findings from the 2014-2022 National Vital Statistics System natality data.. title: Baseline differences and comparative change in pregnancy and birth outcomes for the Asian Indian American population: Findings from the 2014-2022 National Vital Statistics System natality data.

text: . title: Baseline differences and comparative change in pregnancy and birth outcomes for the Asian Indian American population: Findings from the 2014-2022 National Vital Statistics System natality data.

text: . In 2024 the AIA population was older and more educated with a higher prevalence of pre-pregnancy hypertension, diabetes, and obesity. title: Baseline differences and comparative change in pregnancy and birth outcomes for the Asian Indian American population: Findings from the 2014-2022 National Vital Statistics System natality data.

text: . The AIA birthing population is affected by increasing pre-pregnancy risk factors and adverse metabolic and hypertensive conditions. By 2024, over 20% of AIA birthing individuals experienced at least one adverse pregnancy or birth outcome
title: Baseline differences and comparative change in pregnancy and birth outcomes for the Asian Indian American population: Findings from the 2014-2022 National Vital Statistics System natality data.

text: . These findings pose a major life course challenge to the health of pregnant individuals and their offspring that require both public health and clinical interventions.
title: Baseline differences and comparative change in pregnancy and birth outcomes for the Asian Indian American population: Findings from the 2014-2022 National Vital Statistics System natality data.

text: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.. BackgroundSocial determinants of health (SDOH) and related social needs (e.g., food insecurity, financial strain) are major drivers of maternal health disparities
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . Pregnant women of color and those with low socioeconomic status (SES) experience a disproportionate burden of social needs, which are associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and increased risk of chronic disease for both mothers and children
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . Home visiting programs represent a promising, community-based platform for identifying and addressing social needs; however, little is known about how these processes occur in practice or how they can be strengthened.ObjectivesExplore how social needs are identified and referred for intervention within the Parents as Teachers (PAT) home visiting model.DesignQualitative.MethodsWe conducted
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: model.DesignQualitative.MethodsWe conducted semi-structured interviews with supervisors, parent educators (home visitors), and pregnant women of color and low SES participating in PAT across seven U.S
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . states. Interview guides and analysis were informed by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) and the Healthy People 2030 SDOH framework.ResultsParticipants (25 PAT providers; 15 pregnant women) described social needs as pervasive and central to maternal well-being, with limited and variable community resources. Determinants spanned multiple CFIR domains
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . Determinants spanned multiple CFIR domains. In the outer setting, availability of community resources and interorganizational partnerships shaped referral success. In the inner setting, time constraints, inconsistent resource tracking systems, and variable infrastructure posed barriers
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . At the implementer level, educators reported role strain and uncertainty regarding scope of practice, while noting that trusting relationships facilitated disclosure of sensitive needs.ConclusionHome visiting programs are uniquely positioned to identify and address social needs through longitudinal, relationship-based engagement
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . Findings highlight the need for brief assessment processes; enhanced training and role clarity for home visitors; and systems to support resource management and partnerships. These insights can inform scalable social needs interventions within home visiting to advance maternal health equity
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . Social and economic factors such as food insecurity, financial stress, housing instability, and lack of transportation play a major role in maternal health. Pregnant women of color and those with lower incomes are more likely to experience these social needs, which can negatively affect pregnancy outcomes and increase long-term health risks for both mothers and children
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . Home visiting programs, which provide regular, relationship-based support to families during pregnancy and early childhood, may be well positioned to help identify and address these needs
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . However, little is known about how social needs are identified and addressed within these programs in real-world settings.This study explored how social needs are identified and referred for support within the Parents as Teachers (PAT) home visiting program. We conducted interviews with 25 PAT supervisors and home visitors and 15 pregnant women of color or with low incomes across seven U.S
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . states. Interviews focused on experiences with discussing social needs, connecting families to resources, and barriers to providing support.Participants described social needs as widespread and closely linked to maternal well-being. Home visitors and families emphasized that limited availability of community resources often made it difficult to meet families’ needs
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . Challenges included limited time during visits, inconsistent systems for tracking resources, and uncertainty among home visitors about their role and responsibilities
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . At the same time, strong, trusting relationships between home visitors and families helped women feel comfortable sharing sensitive information about their needs.Overall, findings suggest that home visiting programs can play an important role in identifying and addressing social needs during pregnancy
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

text: . Improving training, clarifying roles, simplifying assessment processes, and strengthening partnerships with community organizations may help home visiting programs better support families and promote maternal health equity.
title: A qualitative assessment for planning the implementation of a social needs intervention in community-based home visiting.

title: Systemic Inflammation and Subclinical Hepatic Synthetic Dysfunction Following Doxorubicin-Cyclophosphamide Chemotherapy in Ethiopian Women With Breast Cancer: A Prospective Cohort Study.

title: Systemic Inflammation and Subclinical Hepatic Synthetic Dysfunction Following Doxorubicin-Cyclophosphamide Chemotherapy in Ethiopian Women With Breast Cancer: A Prospective Cohort Study.

This prospective cohort study enrolled consecutive women (≥ 18 years) with breast cancer scheduled for four cycles of adjuvant/neoadjuvant AC (doxorubicin 60 mg/m Among 43 enrolled patients, 39 (90.7%) completed paired assessments (mean age 43.5 ± 12.3 years; 43.6% premenopausal; 53.5% stage I-II)
title: Systemic Inflammation and Subclinical Hepatic Synthetic Dysfunction Following Doxorubicin-Cyclophosphamide Chemotherapy in Ethiopian Women With Breast Cancer: A Prospective Cohort Study.

text: Transient neonatal hypothyroidism due to maternal seaweed soup ingestion: a report of 3 cases.. Seaweed soup (miyeok-guk) is traditionally consumed daily by Korean women during pregnancy and postpartum, often resulting in maternal iodine intake exceeding 2000 µg/day, which can induce neonatal hypothyroidism (NH) in breastfed infants
title: Transient neonatal hypothyroidism due to maternal seaweed soup ingestion: a report of 3 cases.

text: . Neonatal hypothyroidism refers to transient thyroid dysfunction from extrinsic iodine exposure, distinct from congenital hypothyroidism (CH) due to intrinsic thyroid defects. We present 3 infants of Korean descent with NH associated with maternal seaweed soup consumption
title: Transient neonatal hypothyroidism due to maternal seaweed soup ingestion: a report of 3 cases.

text: . Case 1 is a preterm infant with severe hypothyroidism resolving rapidly after maternal discontinuation of seaweed soup, with levothyroxine discontinued at 6 months. Case 2 presented with subclinical hypothyroidism on day of life 11 and an atypical course requiring dose adjustments before proving transient at age 3.5 years
title: Transient neonatal hypothyroidism due to maternal seaweed soup ingestion: a report of 3 cases.

text: . Case 3 had severe hypothyroidism at birth and was treated for 6 years as presumed CH; however, levothyroxine dose remained unchanged despite significant growth, and therapy was discontinued after maternal dietary history was obtained, confirming transient disease
title: Transient neonatal hypothyroidism due to maternal seaweed soup ingestion: a report of 3 cases.

text: . These cases demonstrate that initial thyroid-stimulating hormone severity poorly predicts permanence and that levothyroxine dose trajectory is more reliable. Culturally sensitive history-taking and systematic reevaluation at age 3 can prevent unnecessary lifelong therapy.
title: Transient neonatal hypothyroidism due to maternal seaweed soup ingestion: a report of 3 cases.

text: Melatonin in Pregnancy-Related Disorders: A Review of Protective Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.. Melatonin (N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine), classically known as a pineal neurohormone regulating circadian rhythms, has emerged as a critical pleiotropic molecule in reproductive physiology
title: Melatonin in Pregnancy-Related Disorders: A Review of Protective Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.

text: . Beyond its role in establishing circadian entrainment, it acts as a potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory agent, and mitochondrial function modulator
title: Melatonin in Pregnancy-Related Disorders: A Review of Protective Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.

text: . This review synthesizes current knowledge on the multifaceted roles of melatonin in normal pregnancy and its pathophysiological implications in major gestational disorders, including preeclampsia (PE), fetal growth restriction (FGR), gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and preterm birth (PTB)
title: Melatonin in Pregnancy-Related Disorders: A Review of Protective Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.

text: . Distinct from prior reviews, this work provides a structured, disorder-specific analysis of translational evidence with a critical evaluation of pharmacological optimization strategies, biomarker-driven trial design, and long-term developmental safety considerations. We highlight the dual source of melatonin maternal and placental and its receptor-mediated and receptor-independent actions
title: Melatonin in Pregnancy-Related Disorders: A Review of Protective Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.

text: . Compelling preclinical data and emerging clinical studies suggest that melatonin supplementation may represent a novel, safe, and effective therapeutic strategy for mitigating oxidative stress and inflammation at the maternal-fetal interface
title: Melatonin in Pregnancy-Related Disorders: A Review of Protective Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.

text: . This article reviews the mechanistic underpinnings, summarizes existing evidence in a structured format, and identifies critical gaps for future translational research.
title: Melatonin in Pregnancy-Related Disorders: A Review of Protective Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.

text: Maternal and Fetal HLA Heterozygosity in Preeclampsia: Insights From a Large Multi-Ancestry Pregnancy Cohort.. Preeclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal and neonatal morbidity, with immune dysregulation at the maternal-fetal interface central to its pathogenesis
title: Maternal and Fetal HLA Heterozygosity in Preeclampsia: Insights From a Large Multi-Ancestry Pregnancy Cohort.

text: . The highly polymorphic HLA region mediates maternal immune tolerance of the semi-allogeneic fetus, yet the contribution of HLA diversity to PE risk remains poorly defined. Whether the HLA heterozygote advantage observed in other immune disorders is relevant to PE has not been systematically evaluated
title: Maternal and Fetal HLA Heterozygosity in Preeclampsia: Insights From a Large Multi-Ancestry Pregnancy Cohort.

text: . Using data from the multi-ancestry TOPMed Boston-Colombia Collaborative for Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes (n = 12,790; 4770 PE, 8020 controls; 10,808 maternal, 1982 fetal, including 1848 pairs), we evaluated associations between heterozygosity across eight classical HLA loci and PE and four sub-phenotypes, adjusting for genetic ancestry. HLA heterozygosity was common across most loci (> 80%)
title: Maternal and Fetal HLA Heterozygosity in Preeclampsia: Insights From a Large Multi-Ancestry Pregnancy Cohort.

text: . No individual maternal HLA locus was associated with overall PE; however, heterozygosity across Class I loci showed a protective effect in preterm PE (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.68-0.97), with a similar pattern for HLA-A heterozygosity (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.64-0.97)
title: Maternal and Fetal HLA Heterozygosity in Preeclampsia: Insights From a Large Multi-Ancestry Pregnancy Cohort.

text: . In contrast, fetal heterozygosity at HLA-DQB1 was nominally associated with increased risk of PE (OR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.03-1.80) and preterm PE (OR = 1.73, 95% CI: 1.13-2.74). No individual maternal or fetal HLA alleles were associated with PE
title: Maternal and Fetal HLA Heterozygosity in Preeclampsia: Insights From a Large Multi-Ancestry Pregnancy Cohort.

text: . Maternal-fetal mismatch analysis demonstrated locus-specific associations with preterm PE, including increased risk with HLA-DQA1 mismatch and reduced risk with HLA-C mismatch. These findings highlight distinct maternal and fetal immunogenetic contributions to PE risk and underscore the importance of considering HLA diversity-rather than individual alleles alone-in studies of PE aetiology.
title: Maternal and Fetal HLA Heterozygosity in Preeclampsia: Insights From a Large Multi-Ancestry Pregnancy Cohort.

text: Clinical applicability of breath measurements for detecting disturbances in systemic glucose metabolism: a systematised review.. Breath analysis is a candidate non-invasive approach for detecting disturbances in glucose metabolism, but its clinical applicability has not been systematically assessed across analytical platforms and clinical targets
title: Clinical applicability of breath measurements for detecting disturbances in systemic glucose metabolism: a systematised review.

text: . This systematised review evaluates breath-based biomarkers and analytical technologies for the detection of diabetes, prediabetes, insulin resistance, gestational diabetes, and hypoglycaemia, and for blood glucose estimation. A structured PubMed search identified human studies published between 2010 and 2025; 30 studies met the inclusion criteria
title: Clinical applicability of breath measurements for detecting disturbances in systemic glucose metabolism: a systematised review.

text: . Most analysed volatile organic compounds using laboratory platforms such as gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (MS) or proton transfer reaction MS, a growing number used portable sensor-based systems including electronic noses and single-gas sensors, and a smaller group used isotope-based breath tests measuring labelled carbon dioxide after substrate ingestion
title: Clinical applicability of breath measurements for detecting disturbances in systemic glucose metabolism: a systematised review.

text: . Reported diagnostic performance was highest and most consistent for hypoglycaemia detection in type 1 diabetes mellitus (sensitivity and specificity approximately 90%-95%) and for isotope-based discrimination of prediabetes and diabetes subtypes (approximately 90%-100%), whereas qualitative diabetes detection and quantitative blood glucose prediction were more variable
title: Clinical applicability of breath measurements for detecting disturbances in systemic glucose metabolism: a systematised review.

text: . Both findings are based on a small number of studies, and the isotope-based results originate from a single research group and require independent replication. Performance depended strongly on signal complexity, with multivariable and spectral approaches outperforming single-compound methods
title: Clinical applicability of breath measurements for detecting disturbances in systemic glucose metabolism: a systematised review.

text: . However, most studies used small cohorts and internal validation only, and sampling procedures and reporting were poorly standardised. Standardised protocols, larger externally validated cohorts, and platform selection matched to the intended clinical role are required before implementation.
title: Clinical applicability of breath measurements for detecting disturbances in systemic glucose metabolism: a systematised review.

text: Low-grade intrapartum fever and operative vaginal delivery: A retrospective cohort study.. To evaluate the association between low-grade intrapartum fever (37.5-37.9°C) and obstetric and neonatal outcomes, and to compare its clinical significance with that of overt intrapartum fever (≥38.0°C)
title: Low-grade intrapartum fever and operative vaginal delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . This retrospective cohort study included nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies who delivered over a 7-year period at a single tertiary academic medical center. Participants were categorized according to maximal intrapartum maternal temperature into three groups: low-grade intrapartum fever (37.5-37.9°C), overt intrapartum fever (≥38.0°C), and afebrile controls
title: Low-grade intrapartum fever and operative vaginal delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . The primary analysis focused on outcomes associated with low-grade fever compared with afebrile women, while the intrapartum fever group was included as a reference to contextualize the magnitude of risk. The primary outcomes were operative vaginal delivery (OVD) and intrapartum cesarean delivery (CD), analyzed separately
title: Low-grade intrapartum fever and operative vaginal delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . Secondary outcomes included selected neonatal outcomes, including a 5-minute Apgar score < 7. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to adjust for potential confounders. A total of 15,093 women met inclusion criteria, including 1,294 (8.6%) with low-grade intrapartum fever, 934 (6.2%) with overt intrapartum fever (≥38.0°C), and 12,865 (85.2%) afebrile controls
title: Low-grade intrapartum fever and operative vaginal delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . Compared with afebrile controls, women with low-grade fever had higher rates of OVD (27.0% vs. 17.0%, p < 0.001), although rates remained lower than those observed in the overt fever group (31.0%, p < 0.001). Cesarean delivery rates were increased only among women with overt intrapartum fever and were comparable between the low-grade fever and afebrile groups
title: Low-grade intrapartum fever and operative vaginal delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . Low-grade fever was also associated with a higher rate of 5-minute Apgar score < 7 compared with controls (0.9% vs. 0.4%, p = 0.034)
title: Low-grade intrapartum fever and operative vaginal delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . 0.4%, p = 0.034). After adjustment for maternal age, diabetes mellitus, hypertensive disorders, gestational age at delivery, labor induction, epidural analgesia, and neonatal birthweight, low-grade intrapartum fever remained independently associated with increased risk of OVD (adjusted OR 1.54, 95% CI 1.35-1.76) and 5-minute Apgar score < 7 (adjusted OR 2.50, 95% CI 1.28-4.89)
title: Low-grade intrapartum fever and operative vaginal delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . Low-grade intrapartum temperature elevation was independently associated with increased operative vaginal delivery and low 5-minute Apgar score
title: Low-grade intrapartum fever and operative vaginal delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . These findings suggest that subfebrile temperature elevations may identify a more complicated intrapartum course, although the temporal relationship between temperature elevation and labor progression or delivery mode, and therefore causality, cannot be established.

text: Impact of post-recurrent pregnancy loss depression and anxiety on subsequent live birth rates: A nationwide population-based cohort study.. Depression and anxiety are common disorders in women with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL). but their combined impact with other comorbidities on live births remains understudied
title: Impact of post-recurrent pregnancy loss depression and anxiety on subsequent live birth rates: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . To compare live birth rates between RPL women with and without anxiety, depression, and other comorbidities. This retrospective cohort study used Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) from 2003 to 2020
title: Impact of post-recurrent pregnancy loss depression and anxiety on subsequent live birth rates: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . From 507,001 eligible women aged 18-49, we established subcohorts with anxiety (n = 57,164), depression (n = 10,925), and both (n = 2799), alongside 1:1 propensity score-matched controls. Live birth rates and adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) were assessed using Cox regression. Approximately 30 % of women with RPL developed mental disorders and increased with age
title: Impact of post-recurrent pregnancy loss depression and anxiety on subsequent live birth rates: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . The live birth rate was lower in the pooled mental disorders cohort than in all controls (3.73 versus 8.19 per 1000 person-years) with an adjusted HR of 0.52 (95 % confidence interval (CI) = 0.49-0.54). The live birth rate in all women with RPL decreased with increasing age, approximately 44-fold higher in 18-29-year-olds than in 40-49-year-olds (aHR = 36.4)
title: Impact of post-recurrent pregnancy loss depression and anxiety on subsequent live birth rates: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . Sociodemographic disadvantages further compromised outcomes: low income (≤ NTD 20,000) or blue-collar roles predicted lower birth rates, whereas income > NTD 40,000 (aHR = 1.73) and white-collar jobs (aHR = 1.10) improved likelihoods. Live birth rates were significantly reduced by baseline hypertension (aHR = 0.54), dyslipidemia (aHR = 0.71), diabetes (aHR = 0.76), and asthma (aHR = 0.87)
title: Impact of post-recurrent pregnancy loss depression and anxiety on subsequent live birth rates: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . Psychiatric disorders post-RPL, sociodemographic disadvantages, advanced age, and specific cardiometabolic/respiratory comorbidities significantly reduce live birth success.

text: A composite tool for predicting gestational diabetes or hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: development and temporal validation.. Cardiometabolic pregnancy complications, including gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), share similar risk factors and increase cardiometabolic risk in women
title: A composite tool for predicting gestational diabetes or hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: development and temporal validation.

text: . Medical/lifestyle management reduces their risk but requires early identification of high risk individuals. This study aimed to develop a risk prediction model identifying women at high risk of developing GDM and/or HDP
title: A composite tool for predicting gestational diabetes or hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: development and temporal validation.

text: . A composite prognostic risk prediction model for developing GDM and/or HDP comprising first trimester sociodemographic and clinical variables was developed using routinely collected health data from women delivering singleton pregnancies in Australia from 2016 to 2022
title: A composite tool for predicting gestational diabetes or hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: development and temporal validation.

text: . Variables comprised age; ethnicity; height; body mass index; parity; family history of diabetes; history of GDM, pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, chronic hypertension, polycystic ovary syndrome, chronic kidney disease and fetal macrosomia
title: A composite tool for predicting gestational diabetes or hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: development and temporal validation.

text: . Model development used logistic regression with performance evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrapped internal and temporal validations, recalibration of intercept and slopes and decision curve analyses. GDM/HDP prevalence was 25.4% (n = 48,502). On temporal validation (n = 12,868), the model had a C-statistic of 0.739 (95% CI: 0.727, 0.738)
title: A composite tool for predicting gestational diabetes or hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: development and temporal validation.

text: . Following recalibration, the calibration-in-the-large was -0.001 (95%CI: -0.04, 0.04) and the calibration slope was 1.00 (95% CI: 0.95, 1.05)]. On decision curve analysis, the model outperformed both treat-all and treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities from 8 to 72%. The model demonstrated fair-good discrimination and excellent calibration
title: A composite tool for predicting gestational diabetes or hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: development and temporal validation.

text: . Decision curve analysis indicated potential clinical utility across a range of threshold probabilities for identifying women at high risk. External validation is required.
title: A composite tool for predicting gestational diabetes or hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: development and temporal validation.

text: Culturally grounded health communication to support self-care among pregnant women with diabetes: Development and content validation of an educational cordel in Brazil.. Diabetes in pregnancy requires sustained self-care and clear guidance across hospital, home, and primary care settings
title: Culturally grounded health communication to support self-care among pregnant women with diabetes: Development and content validation of an educational cordel in Brazil.

text: . Conventional educational materials may be less accessible to women facing social vulnerability or limited health literacy. Culturally grounded communication may improve the understandability and relevance of discharge guidance
title: Culturally grounded health communication to support self-care among pregnant women with diabetes: Development and content validation of an educational cordel in Brazil.

text: . We conducted a methodological study in two public tertiary maternity hospitals in Fortaleza, Brazil, to develop and content-validate an educational cordel, a traditional Brazilian form of rhymed popular literature. The material was developed through a structured evidence search, collaboration with health researchers and cordelistas, and pilot testing
title: Culturally grounded health communication to support self-care among pregnant women with diabetes: Development and content validation of an educational cordel in Brazil.

text: . It was evaluated by 22 hospitalized pregnant women with gestational diabetes mellitus or pre-existing type 2 diabetes and by 40 expert judges. Item-level Content Validity Indices (I-CVIs), scale-level CVI by averaging item values (S-CVI/Ave), Cronbach's alpha, and Kendall's coefficient of concordance were calculated
title: Culturally grounded health communication to support self-care among pregnant women with diabetes: Development and content validation of an educational cordel in Brazil.

text: . All target-population items achieved an I-CVI of 1.00, and the S-CVI/Ave was 1.00. The evaluation responses showed modest internal consistency (raw alpha = 0.67; standardized alpha = 0.66). Among expert judges, I-CVIs ranged from 0.95 to 1.00 and the S-CVI/Ave was 0.99
title: Culturally grounded health communication to support self-care among pregnant women with diabetes: Development and content validation of an educational cordel in Brazil.

text: . Internal consistency of expert responses was high (raw alpha = 0.96; standardized alpha = 0.97), whereas Kendall's W was 0.039, indicating weak concordance in the relative ranking of items despite high absolute favorable agreement. title: Culturally grounded health communication to support self-care among pregnant women with diabetes: Development and content validation of an educational cordel in Brazil.

text: . The findings support further testing in larger and more diverse samples, using standardized measures of understandability and actionability and designs that evaluate effects on knowledge, self-care, continuity of care, and clinical outcomes.
title: Culturally grounded health communication to support self-care among pregnant women with diabetes: Development and content validation of an educational cordel in Brazil.

text: METTL14 alleviates pyroptosis of placental trophoblasts in gestational diabetes mellitus through the lncRNA MEG8/WNT7A axis via m6A modification.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a pregnancy complication associated with abnormal placental trophoblast function. Pyroptosis has been implicated in GDM pathogenesis, yet the role of m6A modification in this process remains unclear
title: METTL14 alleviates pyroptosis of placental trophoblasts in gestational diabetes mellitus through the lncRNA MEG8/WNT7A axis via m6A modification.

text: . We hypothesized that METTL14 regulates trophoblast pyroptosis through m6A-dependent modulation of the lncRNA MEG8/WNT7A axis. This study investigated the mechanism of METTL14 in pyroptosis of placental trophoblasts in GDM. HG-treated HTR8/SVneo cells were used as a cell model. METTL14, WNT7A, and lncRNA MEG8 expression was detected by RT-qPCR and western blot
title: METTL14 alleviates pyroptosis of placental trophoblasts in gestational diabetes mellitus through the lncRNA MEG8/WNT7A axis via m6A modification.

text: . Placental damage, cell injury, and pyroptosis markers were assessed. YTHDF2-mediated m6A enrichment on lncRNA MEG8, the interaction between lncRNA MEG8 and EZH2, and H3K27me3 enrichment on the WNT7A promoter were analyzed. Results showed that lncRNA MEG8 was upregulated, while METTL14 and WNT7A were downregulated. METTL14 overexpression reduced placental damage and trophoblast pyroptosis
title: METTL14 alleviates pyroptosis of placental trophoblasts in gestational diabetes mellitus through the lncRNA MEG8/WNT7A axis via m6A modification.

text: . Mechanistically, METTL14 suppressed lncRNA MEG8 expression through YTHDF2-mediated m6A methylation. Reduced lncRNA MEG8 decreased EZH2 recruitment to the WNT7A promoter, lowered H3K27me3 levels, and consequently promoted WNT7A expression. Rescue experiments confirmed that lncRNA MEG8 overexpression or WNT7A knockdown attenuated the suppressive effect of METTL14 on pyroptosis
title: METTL14 alleviates pyroptosis of placental trophoblasts in gestational diabetes mellitus through the lncRNA MEG8/WNT7A axis via m6A modification.

text: . In conclusion, METTL14 acts as an upstream regulator that inhibits trophoblast pyroptosis and ameliorates GDM-induced damage through the lncRNA MEG8/WNT7A axis via YTHDF2-mediated m6A modification, highlighting METTL14 as a potential therapeutic target.
title: METTL14 alleviates pyroptosis of placental trophoblasts in gestational diabetes mellitus through the lncRNA MEG8/WNT7A axis via m6A modification.

text: Interventions to reduce diabetes-related distress among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.. Diabetes distress refers to the emotional and psychological burden specifically associated with living with and managing diabetes
title: Interventions to reduce diabetes-related distress among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

text: . We aimed to systematically identify, summarise and critically appraise the available evidence from RCTs assessing the efficacy of interventions for reducing diabetes distress among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. We searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, APA PsycInfo and CINAHL from inception until 23 September 2024
title: Interventions to reduce diabetes-related distress among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

text: . Studies were eligible if they were RCTs conducted in adults (aged ≥18 years) with type 1 or type 2 diabetes in which the effect of an active intervention on diabetes distress was recorded as a primary or a secondary outcome. Studies with combined populations (e.g. children plus adults) where no separate results were reported for adults were excluded
title: Interventions to reduce diabetes-related distress among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

text: . When possible, we performed a random-effects meta-analysis of the standardised mean difference (SMD) of the endpoint, diabetes distress, measured with a validated questionnaire. We conducted subgroup analyses based on baseline diabetes distress level, intervention delivery method, risk of bias assessment (using the Cochrane RoB2 tool) and trial duration
title: Interventions to reduce diabetes-related distress among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

text: . We used GRADE methodology to assess the certainty of evidence. We included 248 trials, with 59 trials reporting on psychological interventions, 68 on psychoeducational interventions and 121 on miscellaneous interventions (non-psychological or non-psychoeducational, i.e
title: Interventions to reduce diabetes-related distress among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

title: Interventions to reduce diabetes-related distress among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

text: . The total sample size was 55,497 participants (range 12-4034). The analysed trials were judged to have either some concerns for risk of bias (94 trials) or a high risk of bias (71 trials)
title: Interventions to reduce diabetes-related distress among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

title: Interventions to reduce diabetes-related distress among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

text: Soluble P2X7 receptor (sP2X7R) as a marker of inflammation in pregnancy.. The purinergic P2X7 receptor (P2X7R) is a key regulator of inflammation and pro-inflammatory cytokine release. Recently, a soluble form of P2X7R (sP2X7R) has been identified in the circulation of healthy individuals and significantly increased in patients with inflammatory disorders
title: Soluble P2X7 receptor (sP2X7R) as a marker of inflammation in pregnancy.

text: . As pregnancy is characterized by finely regulated inflammatory adaptations and considered a state of low-grade inflammation, we hypothesized that P2X7R may contribute to the physiological inflammatory status of pregnancy and to pregnancy-related inflammatory disorders
title: Soluble P2X7 receptor (sP2X7R) as a marker of inflammation in pregnancy.

text: . A cohort of 90 pregnant women was evaluated at the first, second, and third trimester of pregnancy, and 30 age-matched non-pregnant women were used as controls. We measured sP2X7R blood concentrations, and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) was used as a reference inflammatory marker. Associations with maternal characteristics, pregnancy complications and foetal sex were investigated
title: Soluble P2X7 receptor (sP2X7R) as a marker of inflammation in pregnancy.

text: . Serum sP2X7R concentrations were significantly higher in pregnant than in control women and increased progressively throughout pregnancy. Although sP2X7R and NLR showed similar trends, sP2X7R provided complementary information. First-trimester sP2X7R concentrations were significantly higher in multigravida women, in those with gestational hypothyroidism, and in those carrying a male foetus
title: Soluble P2X7 receptor (sP2X7R) as a marker of inflammation in pregnancy.

text: . No significant differences were observed according to Body Mass Index (BMI), gestational diabetes, or gestational hypertension. Furthermore, sP2X7R was detectable in umbilical cord blood and positively correlated with maternal circulating concentrations
title: Soluble P2X7 receptor (sP2X7R) as a marker of inflammation in pregnancy.

text: . To our knowledge, this is the first study to show that circulating sP2X7R increases during normal pregnancy and reflects the physiological inflammatory adaptations of gestation. The results indicate that circulating sP2X7R is a potential biomarker of inflammatory responses and maternal-fetal immune interactions during pregnancy.
title: Soluble P2X7 receptor (sP2X7R) as a marker of inflammation in pregnancy.

text: Phenotypic discordance in semilobar holoprosencephaly: a case report of total arhinia and median clefting linked to gestational diabetes.. Holoprosencephaly (HPE) is a complex spectrum of cephalic malformations resulting from incomplete prosencephalic division. title: Phenotypic discordance in semilobar holoprosencephaly: a case report of total arhinia and median clefting linked to gestational diabetes.

text: . We present a preterm female infant born to a mother with unmanaged gestational diabetes. At birth, she exhibited microcephaly, total arhinia, and a median cleft lip and palate. MRI confirmed semilobar HPE. Clinical progression included hypotonia, seizures, and recurrent hyperpyrexia associated with hypothalamic dysfunction
title: Phenotypic discordance in semilobar holoprosencephaly: a case report of total arhinia and median clefting linked to gestational diabetes.

text: . Despite the absence of a nasal airway, the infant transitioned to reflexive mouth breathing and required long-term orogastric tube feeding. Notably, she has maintained systemic stability throughout an 8-month follow-up, facilitated by a proactive, multidisciplinary home-based care model
title: Phenotypic discordance in semilobar holoprosencephaly: a case report of total arhinia and median clefting linked to gestational diabetes.

text: . This case illustrates a phenotypic discordance in which severe arhinia occurs alongside intermediate cerebral cleavage, suggesting a potential vulnerability in which nasal placode development may be highly sensitive to maternal hyperglycemia, which is hypothesized to perturb cholesterol-dependent Sonic Hedgehog signaling
title: Phenotypic discordance in semilobar holoprosencephaly: a case report of total arhinia and median clefting linked to gestational diabetes.

text: . Our clinical experience demonstrates that by prioritizing rigorous caloric titration and proactive monitoring of autonomic and infectious triggers, it is possible to successfully navigate the patient's precarious equilibrium and prevent the secondary morbidity typically associated with hypothalamic instability
title: Phenotypic discordance in semilobar holoprosencephaly: a case report of total arhinia and median clefting linked to gestational diabetes.

text: . This report demonstrates that even in the presence of profound structural and autonomic vulnerabilities, proactive multidisciplinary management can effectively mitigate secondary systemic morbidity and support survival beyond the neonatal period
title: Phenotypic discordance in semilobar holoprosencephaly: a case report of total arhinia and median clefting linked to gestational diabetes.

text: . This approach provides a viable model for stabilizing patients with severe holoprosencephaly through consistent, home-based surveillance and functional support.
title: Phenotypic discordance in semilobar holoprosencephaly: a case report of total arhinia and median clefting linked to gestational diabetes.

text: Association of atherogenic index of plasma and its modified indices with gestational diabetes mellitus: a prospective cohort study based on the Korean population.. title: Association of atherogenic index of plasma and its modified indices with gestational diabetes mellitus: a prospective cohort study based on the Korean population.

text: . The atherogenic index of plasma (AIP, log₁₀[TG/HDL-C]) has shown promise for early GDM risk stratification, but it does not incorporate obesity-related parameters. title: Association of atherogenic index of plasma and its modified indices with gestational diabetes mellitus: a prospective cohort study based on the Korean population.

text: Pregnancy Outcomes Following Maternal Fenofibrate Exposure.. Fenofibrate is a fibric acid derivative used in the management of severe hypertriglyceridemia, a condition that may lead to serious maternal and fetal complications during pregnancy
title: Pregnancy Outcomes Following Maternal Fenofibrate Exposure.

text: . However, evidence regarding the safety of fenofibrate exposure in pregnancy remains extremely limited, and the available human data are largely restricted to isolated case reports. The aim of this study was to evaluate pregnancy outcomes of women who consulted a university teratology information service (TIS) due to fenofibrate exposure during pregnancy
title: Pregnancy Outcomes Following Maternal Fenofibrate Exposure.

text: . The data for this retrospective case series include consultation records and follow-up interviews of pregnant women who consulted the TIS at Marmara University Hospital due to fenofibrate exposure between 2012 and 2025. Eleven pregnancies with fenofibrate exposure were identified, and pregnancy outcomes were available for 10 pregnancies
title: Pregnancy Outcomes Following Maternal Fenofibrate Exposure.

text: . Six pregnancies resulted in live births and four resulted in stillbirth. Due to one twin pregnancy, a total of 11 infants were recorded, including seven live-born and four stillborn infants. No major congenital malformations were identified among live-born infants. One child was reported to have been diagnosed with autism during follow-up
title: Pregnancy Outcomes Following Maternal Fenofibrate Exposure.

text: . Although the proportion of stillbirths in this series appears higher than expected, most affected pregnancies were complicated by significant maternal comorbidities, including severe hypertriglyceridemia, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and acute pancreatitis, which are known risk factors for adverse pregnancy outcomes
title: Pregnancy Outcomes Following Maternal Fenofibrate Exposure.

text: . Therefore, the observed stillbirths may be related to underlying maternal disease rather than fenofibrate exposure. Overall, the findings of this case series do not suggest a clear teratogenic signal associated with maternal fenofibrate exposure during pregnancy.
title: Pregnancy Outcomes Following Maternal Fenofibrate Exposure.

text: Predictors of Shoulder Dystocia: A Retrospective Case-Control Study.. Shoulder dystocia (SD) is rare, but it has serious consequences. Antepartum risk stratification for SD has demonstrated variability across populations, reflecting differences in assessment methodologies. We conducted a retrospective analysis using a prospectively audited electronic database from a single center
title: Predictors of Shoulder Dystocia: A Retrospective Case-Control Study.

text: . All singleton vertex deliveries between January 2012 and December 2017 were reviewed. SD cases were identified by the recorded use of ancillary maneuvers during shoulder delivery. Case-control matching was informed by previously published odds ratios for key variables and evaluated using conditional logistic regression
title: Predictors of Shoulder Dystocia: A Retrospective Case-Control Study.

text: . A total of 80,349 eligible delivery records were reviewed, of which 23,392 (29.11%) were Cesarean deliveries. Among the remaining 56,957 vaginal births, 58 cases of SD were identified, representing an incidence of 0.10%. title: Predictors of Shoulder Dystocia: A Retrospective Case-Control Study.

text: . Maternal and neonatal birth injuries were documented in 5 SD cases (8.6%) and 6 control cases (0.7%), respectively (p < 0.001). title: Predictors of Shoulder Dystocia: A Retrospective Case-Control Study.

text: . Maternal overweight and diabetes mellitus were contributory and modifiable risk factors. Parity did not independently predict SD events, likely due to a Type I statistical error.

text: Pesticide exposure during pregnancy and the risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes: a systematic review.. title: Pesticide exposure during pregnancy and the risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes: a systematic review.

text: . However, epidemiological evidence remains inconsistent and often focuses on specific pesticide classes or isolated reproductive outcomes. To systematically review and synthesize observational evidence on associations between maternal exposure to currently used pesticide classes and maternal and fetal outcomes
title: Pesticide exposure during pregnancy and the risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes: a systematic review.

text: . A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect from inception to November 14, 2025. During screening, studies assessing pesticide exposure prior to 2000 were excluded due to regulatory restrictions over recent decades. Eligible studies measured prenatal pesticide exposure using biological samples and reported maternal or fetal outcomes
title: Pesticide exposure during pregnancy and the risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes: a systematic review.

text: . Three reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using the NHLBI quality assessment tools. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251172677). Of 6776 records identified, 39 studies including 24,532 participants from 17 countries and territories met the inclusion criteria
title: Pesticide exposure during pregnancy and the risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes: a systematic review.

text: . Exposure to organophosphate pesticides (OPs) was associated with impaired fetal growth in several studies, with evidence pointing to trimester- and sex-specific effects. title: Pesticide exposure during pregnancy and the risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes: a systematic review.

text: . Evidence for neonicotinoid exposure and gestational diabetes mellitus was suggestive, but derived exclusively from Chinese cohorts, limiting generalizability. Maternal exposure to currently used pesticides during pregnancy may be associated with fetal growth outcomes and maternal health
title: Pesticide exposure during pregnancy and the risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes: a systematic review.

text: . Future research should prioritize repeated biomarker measurements and mixture modelling to improve the characterization of potential reproductive health effects associated with these pesticides.

text: Periodontal diseases and pregnancy.. Pregnancy induces significant hormonal, immunological, and physiological changes that affect the periodontium. These modifications increase vascular permeability, alter subgingival microbiota, and modulate immune defenses, making women more susceptible to gingivitis, epulis, and the progression of pre-existing periodontitis
title: Periodontal diseases and pregnancy.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . Gingivitis affects up to 75% of pregnant women, while epulis gravidarum, although less frequent, also reflects the impact of hormonal and inflammatory responses. Periodontitis, a chronic destructive disease, has been studied as a possible risk factor for adverse pregnancy outcomes such as preterm birth, low birth weight, preeclampsia, and gestational diabetes
title: Periodontal diseases and pregnancy.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . Proposed mechanisms include systemic dissemination of periodontal pathogens and inflammatory mediators affecting the feto-placental environment. Despite numerous epidemiological studies, results remain heterogeneous and inconclusive, and the benefits of periodontal treatment during pregnancy on obstetric outcomes are uncertain
title: Periodontal diseases and pregnancy.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . Prevention and early management, ideally before conception, appear to be the most effective strategies for preserving maternal oral health and potentially reducing risks. During pregnancy, treatment should focus on inflammation control, comfort, and reduction of local irritants, with safe use of mechanical debridement and selected antiseptics or antibiotics when needed
title: Periodontal diseases and pregnancy.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

text: . Clinically, these findings underline the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration between dentists and other healthcare providers. Promoting oral health in women of reproductive age is essential to optimize both maternal well-being and pregnancy outcomes.

text: Mobile Health Interventions in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Scoping Review.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), one of the rising epidemics in pregnancies worldwide, is defined as glucose intolerance that is first recognised during pregnancy. GDM is associated with adverse maternal and fetal outcomes, including pre-eclampsia, caesarean delivery, and macrosomia
title: Mobile Health Interventions in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Scoping Review.

text: . Mobile health (mHealth) interventions have emerged as promising tools for managing GDM, enabling remote monitoring, education, and communication. Hence, the present study was undertaken to map the nature of the use of mHealth interventions in GDM and report pregnancy outcomes based on the available literature
title: Mobile Health Interventions in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Scoping Review.

text: . The scoping review was conducted following a systematic search for studies in PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar databases in the last five years (2019-2024) that investigated an mHealth app intervention for mothers with GDM and reported maternal or fetal outcomes. Both randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies were included
title: Mobile Health Interventions in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Scoping Review.

text: . A total of seven studies were included in this review, of which four were randomised trials and three were observational studies. The types of mHealth interventions varied widely, including mobile applications, SMS-based platforms, wearable devices, and teleconsultation systems
title: Mobile Health Interventions in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Scoping Review.

text: . An RCT (China, 2019) reported that a nurse-guided smartphone app significantly improved glucose control and reduced weight gain in patients with GDM compared with usual care. Further, a study (Sweden, 2021) reported improved glycaemic control and compliance
title: Mobile Health Interventions in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Scoping Review.

text: . Another trial (Slovenia, 2023) showed that a comprehensive telemedicine programme led to better postprandial glucose control and fewer caesarean deliveries. A Swiss trial (MySweetheart trial, 2024) combining app-based and telehealth coaching reduced gestational weight gain
title: Mobile Health Interventions in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Scoping Review.

title: Mobile Health Interventions in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Scoping Review.
