text: Antenatal Corticosteroids in Gestational Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Glycemic Response and Management Strategies.. Antenatal corticosteroids (ACS) promote foetal lung maturation in pregnancies at risk of preterm birth; however, in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), they can exacerbate maternal glycemia and contribute to adverse neonatal outcomes
title: Antenatal Corticosteroids in Gestational Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Glycemic Response and Management Strategies.

text: . Clinical guidelines offer limited direction on optimal treatment adjustment. To synthesize the evidence on glycaemic responses and management strategies following ACS exposure in individuals with GDM. A systematic review of Embase, MEDLINE and CENTRAL in October 2025 in accordance with PRISMA guidelines
title: Antenatal Corticosteroids in Gestational Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Glycemic Response and Management Strategies.

text: . Studies reporting on glycaemic outcomes and/or management strategies following ACS exposure in individuals with GDM were included. Twenty studies were included. Maternal glycemia rose predictably after ACS, with hyperglycaemia typically emerging within 9-16 h, peaking over the subsequent 24-72 h and often persisting up to 5 days
title: Antenatal Corticosteroids in Gestational Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Glycemic Response and Management Strategies.

text: . Among individuals managed with medical nutrition therapy or oral hypoglycaemic agents at baseline, insulin initiation ranged from 13% to 91%. Among those already using insulin, 67%-88% required dose escalation, with mean increases typically ranging from 47% to 91%
title: Antenatal Corticosteroids in Gestational Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Glycemic Response and Management Strategies.

text: . Pregnancy-adapted intravenous insulin (IVI) pathways reported higher time-in-range and fewer hyperglycaemic/hypoglycaemic events than adult IVI protocols. However, emerging evidence suggests that structured, pregnancy-specific subcutaneous insulin protocols may achieve comparable or improved glycaemic control
title: Antenatal Corticosteroids in Gestational Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Glycemic Response and Management Strategies.

text: . ACS exposure in GDM is associated with a predictable but variable, transient deterioration in maternal glycaemia. GDM-specific evidence suggests that structured pregnancy-adapted monitoring and insulin-adjustment pathways may help attenuate post-ACS hyperglycaemia. However, the evidence remains heterogeneous and largely observational
title: Antenatal Corticosteroids in Gestational Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Glycemic Response and Management Strategies.

text: . Prospective studies are needed to validate GDM-specific algorithms, clarify thresholds for insulin initiation or escalation and define indications for subcutaneous versus IVI.
title: Antenatal Corticosteroids in Gestational Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Glycemic Response and Management Strategies.

text: Prescription Medication Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Sweden 2007 to 2022.. Medication use during pregnancy has increased worldwide. The aim was to investigate patterns of prescription medication use during pregnancy and postpartum in Sweden 2007-2022. We conducted a population-based drug utilization study with linked data from the Swedish Medical Birth and Prescribed Drug Registers
title: Prescription Medication Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Sweden 2007 to 2022.

text: . From 90 days before pregnancy to 90 days after delivery, all dispensed prescriptions for each full-level ATC code were identified. The proportion of women, by year and age, with ≥ 1 dispensed medication was calculated, as well as the number of different medications and dispensed prescriptions of structural teratogens and specific medication groups
title: Prescription Medication Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Sweden 2007 to 2022.

text: . Overall, 1 065 593 (60.5%) women were dispensed ≥ 1 medication during pregnancy and 900 536 (51.1%) within 3 months postpartum. The proportion of women with ≥ 1 dispensed prescription in the postpartum period was stable but increased during pregnancy from 57.1% in 2007 to 67.5% in 2022, with the largest increase in women ≥ 40 years
title: Prescription Medication Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Sweden 2007 to 2022.

text: . The proportion using ≥ 5 different medications increased, while the proportion with a recognized or suspected structural teratogen in the first trimester remained low (< 1%). There was a notable decrease in the use of antibiotics and prescribed analgesics, and an increase in antiemetics, psychotropics, acetylsalicylic acid, anticoagulants, antihypertensives, and antidiabetics
title: Prescription Medication Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Sweden 2007 to 2022.

text: . Medication use during pregnancy in Sweden increased from 2007 to 2022, particularly among women ≥ 40 years, while postpartum use remained stable. Shifts in the use of specific medication groups highlight evolving maternal characteristics and clinical practice, as well as the importance of continuous surveillance and investigation of medication safety
title: Prescription Medication Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Sweden 2007 to 2022.

text: . Over the past 15 years, the use of medications during pregnancy has increased in Sweden. In this study, we included all pregnancies from 2007 to 2022 and examined which medications women had dispensed during pregnancy and in the first 3 months after giving birth when breastfeeding decisions are made
title: Prescription Medication Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Sweden 2007 to 2022.

text: . We found that most pregnant women were dispensed at least one prescription; the proportion increased from 57% in 2007 to 68% in 2022, with the largest increases in the youngest and oldest women. The number of women taking multiple medications also rose
title: Prescription Medication Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Sweden 2007 to 2022.

text: . The most used medications during pregnancy were: antibiotics, medicines for nausea, and painkillers, and after birth: antibiotics, pain relievers, and blood‐thinners. The use of some medicines, such as those for nausea, mental health conditions, diabetes, blood‐thinning, high blood pressure, and diabetes, increased over time, whereas the use of antibiotics and painkillers after birth declined
title: Prescription Medication Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Sweden 2007 to 2022.

text: . Importantly, the proportion of women using medications with recognized or suspected risk of fetal malformations was very low. The trends in medication use reflect changes in maternal characteristics and evolving clinical needs for pregnant women. Findings highlight the importance of medication use surveillance and safety investigations for mothers and their infants.
title: Prescription Medication Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Sweden 2007 to 2022.

text: The redox architecture of gestational diabetes mellitus: from cellular stress engine to epigenetic and mitochondrial rewiring.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common pregnancy complication with a rising global prevalence, posing serious short-term and long-term health threats to both mothers and offspring
title: The redox architecture of gestational diabetes mellitus: from cellular stress engine to epigenetic and mitochondrial rewiring.

text: . This review repositions GDM as a systemic disorder in which oxidative stress acts as a proposed mechanistic hub, linking upstream risk factors to downstream pathophysiology. We first examine how "upstream" factors-including genetic susceptibility, pre-conception status, and environmental exposures-converge to promote a state of pathological redox imbalance
title: The redox architecture of gestational diabetes mellitus: from cellular stress engine to epigenetic and mitochondrial rewiring.

text: . We then examine key mechanistic pathways through which oxidative stress is thought to contribute to systemic insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell failure, highlighting novel pathways involving intercellular communication via tunneling nanotubes and exosomes
title: The redox architecture of gestational diabetes mellitus: from cellular stress engine to epigenetic and mitochondrial rewiring.

text: . Furthermore, we explore the downstream cascade, where oxidative stress may program maternal accelerated biological aging and multi-organ offspring disease trajectories through nuclear epigenetic programming and mitochondrial dysfunction programming, leaving what has been termed a persistent "metabolic memory"
title: The redox architecture of gestational diabetes mellitus: from cellular stress engine to epigenetic and mitochondrial rewiring.

text: . Consequently, this review evaluates emerging strategies that target oxidative stress for early prediction and precision intervention. Early prediction models based on direct redox biomarkers and multi-omics signatures hold potential to shift diagnosis from late-gestation oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) to first-trimester risk stratification
title: The redox architecture of gestational diabetes mellitus: from cellular stress engine to epigenetic and mitochondrial rewiring.

text: . Current supporting evidence draws from human epidemiological associations, ex vivo placental analyses, and experimental models. However, direct causal and interventional validation in pregnant women remains limited
title: The redox architecture of gestational diabetes mellitus: from cellular stress engine to epigenetic and mitochondrial rewiring.

text: . Integrating targeted redox risk stratification and precision interventions into a life-course clinical framework may help interrupt the intergenerational transmission of metabolic disease initiated by GDM.
title: The redox architecture of gestational diabetes mellitus: from cellular stress engine to epigenetic and mitochondrial rewiring.

text: Influence of maternal obesity, gestational weight gain and gestational diabetes on child metabolic profile: A prospective study from the intrauterine period until early childhood.. Impacts of maternal exposures on infant metabolic profiles, particularly tracked up to school age, are poorly known
title: Influence of maternal obesity, gestational weight gain and gestational diabetes on child metabolic profile: A prospective study from the intrauterine period until early childhood.

text: . The aim was to investigate associations of maternal obesity, gestational weight gain (GWG) and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) with children's serum metabolites. Serum metabolites were analyzed using nuclear magnetic resonance metabolomics at 6 months (n = 257) and 1 (n = 256), 2 (n = 238), and 5-6 years of age (n = 139)
title: Influence of maternal obesity, gestational weight gain and gestational diabetes on child metabolic profile: A prospective study from the intrauterine period until early childhood.

text: . Associations between maternal exposures and offspring metabolites were examined using multivariable regression models adjusted for confounders and correction for multiple comparisons
title: Influence of maternal obesity, gestational weight gain and gestational diabetes on child metabolic profile: A prospective study from the intrauterine period until early childhood.

text: . Maternal pre-pregnancy body mass index (pBMI) associated positively with the ratio of n-6 fatty acids to n-3 fatty acids and the particle sizes of very low-density lipoprotein (VLDL), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), and high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and inversely with n-3 fatty acids, docosahexaenoic acid and ratio of phospholipids to total lipids in large LDL-particles at 6 months (false
title: Influence of maternal obesity, gestational weight gain and gestational diabetes on child metabolic profile: A prospective study from the intrauterine period until early childhood.

text: lipids in large LDL-particles at 6 months (false discovery rate <0.05)
title: Influence of maternal obesity, gestational weight gain and gestational diabetes on child metabolic profile: A prospective study from the intrauterine period until early childhood.

text: . Accordingly, maternal obesity showed positive associations with ratio of n-6 fatty acids to n-3 fatty acids and inverse associations with n-3 fatty acids. GDM was negatively associated with the phospholipid-to-total lipids ratio in small VLDL-particles in 2-year-old children (false discovery rate <0.05)
title: Influence of maternal obesity, gestational weight gain and gestational diabetes on child metabolic profile: A prospective study from the intrauterine period until early childhood.

text: . No associations of child metabolites were seen with pBMI, obesity at 1-year, 2-years, and 5-6 years of age, or at any age with GWG after correcting for multiple comparisons. These findings suggest that maternal obesity and GDM, shape the offspring's metabolic profile; these may be of significance for later health.

text: Porphyromonas gingivalis as a keystone pathogen in systemic diseases.. Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis) is a Gram-negative anaerobic bacterium recognized as a keystone pathogen in periodontitis. Beyond its established role in periodontal tissue destruction, accumulating evidence links P
title: Porphyromonas gingivalis as a keystone pathogen in systemic diseases.

text: . gingivalis to several systemic conditions, including cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's disease, rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes mellitus, and adverse pregnancy outcomes. This review synthesizes current evidence on how P
title: Porphyromonas gingivalis as a keystone pathogen in systemic diseases.

text: . gingivalis may contribute to systemic disease beyond the oral cavity, with particular emphasis on its virulence factors, including gingipains and lipopolysaccharide, and the pathways linking periodontal infection to pathological processes in distant organs. We discuss how hematogenous dissemination, immune-evasion mechanisms, and chronic inflammatory responses may mediate these systemic effects
title: Porphyromonas gingivalis as a keystone pathogen in systemic diseases.

text: . A clearer understanding of these associations may inform integrated approaches to periodontal care and systemic disease management.
title: Porphyromonas gingivalis as a keystone pathogen in systemic diseases.

text: Gestational weight loss relative to prepregnancy weight in women with gestational diabetes: impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes.
title: Gestational weight loss relative to prepregnancy weight in women with gestational diabetes: impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes.

text: . Gestational weight loss (GWL) of overweight or obese women with gestational diabetes (GDM) during the third trimester has been associated with lower risk of macrosomia, caesarean delivery (CS) or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission but with higher risk of preterm delivery (PTD) and small-for-gestational-age (SGA)
title: Gestational weight loss relative to prepregnancy weight in women with gestational diabetes: impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes.

text: . We studied the association between GWL during the whole pregnancy and perinatal outcomes. We conducted a retrospective study of the Portuguese national GDM database including all women with singleton pregnancies diagnosed by 24-28 week OGTT (oral glucose tolerance test) who delivered a liveborn infant and had recorded perinatal outcomes and gestational weight change
title: Gestational weight loss relative to prepregnancy weight in women with gestational diabetes: impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes.

text: . GWL was defined as weight loss between the maternal weight at delivery and pregestational weight. Among 7768 women, 180 (2.3%) had GWL; they had higher BMI, more frequent family history of type 2 diabetes, previous GDM, chronic hypertension, multiparity, higher fasting OGTT glucose and more frequent metformin treatment than women without GWL
title: Gestational weight loss relative to prepregnancy weight in women with gestational diabetes: impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes.

text: . GWL was associated with higher odds of PTD (OR 2.35, 95%CI 1.40-3.97, p- value = 0.001) and SGA (2.71, 1.70-4.33, p-value < 0.001) and lower odds of CS (0.62, 0.44-0.88, p-value = 0.006) and LGA (0.40, 0.22-0.70, p-value = 0.002), with non significant associations for HDP, NH, RDS and NICU admission
title: Gestational weight loss relative to prepregnancy weight in women with gestational diabetes: impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes.

text: . GWL was uncommon among women with GDM and was associated with over 2.3-fold higher risk of PTD, 2.7-fold higher risk of SGA newborns, and a 48% lower risk of CS and 60% lower risk of LGA infants.
title: Gestational weight loss relative to prepregnancy weight in women with gestational diabetes: impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes.

text: Prepregnancy Body Mass Index, Pregnancy Physical Activity Trajectories, and Postpartum Blood Pressure.. How prepregnancy body mass index (BMI) and pregnancy physical activity (PA) jointly shape postpartum cardiovascular risk remains unclear
title: Prepregnancy Body Mass Index, Pregnancy Physical Activity Trajectories, and Postpartum Blood Pressure.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . This study evaluated whether joint trajectories of PA and sedentary behavior during pregnancy mediate the association between prepregnancy BMI and postpartum blood pressure (BP). Pregnancy 24/7 is a multisite observational cohort enrolling individuals <13 weeks' gestation, aged 18 to 45 years, without chronic hypertension, diabetes, sleep disorders, or severe mobility limitation (n=500)
title: Prepregnancy Body Mass Index, Pregnancy Physical Activity Trajectories, and Postpartum Blood Pressure.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Participants with valid PA/sedentary behavior data for ≥1 trimester and a clinic BP reading 4 to 8 weeks postpartum were analyzed. Prepregnancy BMI was chart-abstracted; PA/sedentary behavior were measured each trimester via the activPAL3 micro. Hypertensive postpartum BP was defined as systolic BP ≥130 mm Hg or diastolic BP ≥80 mm Hg
title: Prepregnancy Body Mass Index, Pregnancy Physical Activity Trajectories, and Postpartum Blood Pressure.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Parallel-process latent growth modeling and K-means clustering identified PA trajectory groups; mediation analysis tested whether these groups explained the BMI-BP association. Among 388 participants (aged 30.9±4.5 years), 109 (28.4%) had hypertensive postpartum BP
title: Prepregnancy Body Mass Index, Pregnancy Physical Activity Trajectories, and Postpartum Blood Pressure.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Each 1-unit increase in prepregnancy BMI was associated with 6.0% greater risk of hypertensive postpartum BP (risk ratio, 1.06 [95% CI, 1.04-1.09]), adjusting for demographic and pregnancy characteristics. Three trajectory groups emerged: active-declining (n=142), active-improving (n=103), and consistently sedentary (n=143)
title: Prepregnancy Body Mass Index, Pregnancy Physical Activity Trajectories, and Postpartum Blood Pressure.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . The active-declining group had 37% lower risk than the consistently sedentary group, but this attenuated after BMI adjustment. Physical activity trajectories did not mediate the BMI-BP relationship, which was largely explained by prepregnancy BMI alone
title: Prepregnancy Body Mass Index, Pregnancy Physical Activity Trajectories, and Postpartum Blood Pressure.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

text: . Prepregnancy BMI predicted hypertensive postpartum BP independent of activity patterns, underscoring the clinical value of prepregnancy weight optimization and vigilant postpartum monitoring for those entering pregnancy with elevated BMI. text: High Serum Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids for the Increased Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Through LPC Pathways: A Prospective Nested Case-Control Study in China.
title: High Serum Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids for the Increased Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Through LPC Pathways: A Prospective Nested Case-Control Study in China.

text: . The study aimed to investigate the following: (1) whether early-pregnancy serum polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) species are associated with the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM); and (2) whether lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC)18:0 may statistically explain these associations in Chinese pregnant women
title: High Serum Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids for the Increased Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Through LPC Pathways: A Prospective Nested Case-Control Study in China.

text: . We conducted a 1:1 age-matched case-control study of 486 pregnant women nested within a prospective cohort in Tianjin, China. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) logistic regression analysis was used to identify the PUFA species independently associated with GDM. Conditional logistic regression was conducted to obtain odds ratios (ORs) and their 95% confidence intervals (CIs)
title: High Serum Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids for the Increased Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Through LPC Pathways: A Prospective Nested Case-Control Study in China.

text: . Sobel mediation analysis was used to assess the potential statistical role of LPC18:0. Among five PUFA species that differed significantly between cases and controls, arachidonic acid (AA, 20:4) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA, 22:6) were selected and further analyzed
title: High Serum Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids for the Increased Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Through LPC Pathways: A Prospective Nested Case-Control Study in China.

text: . High AA (≥ 3.63 nmol/mL) and DHA (≥ 0.59 nmol/mL) were associated with increased GDM risk, with multivariable-adjusted ORs of 2.89 (95% CI: 1.84-4.54) and 2.90 (95% CI: 1.82-4.63), respectively. These associations were stronger among women with pre-pregnancy overweight/obesity (AA, OR: 5.32, 95% CI: 2.48-11.42; DHA, OR: 3.39, 95% CI: 1.65-6.99)
title: High Serum Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids for the Increased Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Through LPC Pathways: A Prospective Nested Case-Control Study in China.

text: . Further adjustment for high LPC18:0 substantially attenuated the associations of AA (OR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.45-1.80) and DHA (OR: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.51-1.85) with GDM risk, with Sobel test p values < 0.0001. Higher serum AA and DHA levels in early pregnancy were associated with increased GDM risk. LPC18:0 may statistically explain part of these observed associations.
title: High Serum Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids for the Increased Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Through LPC Pathways: A Prospective Nested Case-Control Study in China.

text: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.
title: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.

text: . Is fetal exposure to paracetamol associated with markers of ovarian function in infancy? Mild to moderate doses of prenatal paracetamol exposure, assessed by detailed maternal reports and urinary measurements, are associated with ovarian morphology and activity as well as reduced size of estrogen-responsive tissues in infant girls. Maternal use of paracetamol is widespread
title: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.

text: . Maternal use of paracetamol is widespread. Across multiple independent animal studies, fetal exposure consistently impairs the formation of primordial ovarian follicles, causing subfertility and premature estropause in female offspring
title: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.

text: . The Copenhagen Analgesic study (COPANA) is a single-center, prospective, observational cohort study conducted at a university hospital (March 2020 to November 2022). From 3425 eligible participants, 685 healthy singleton pregnant women of Caucasian origin, were enrolled in the first trimester of pregnancy, and 302 infant daughters were examined at follow-up
title: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.

text: . Exclusion criteria included maternal diabetes or thyroid disease, pre- or post-term delivery, or severe infant illness. Pregnant women reported paracetamol use biweekly and provided first-trimester urinary samples which were analyzed for paracetamol levels (LC-MS/MS) and adjusted for urinary osmolarity (n = 299)
title: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.

text: . Girls were classified by timing of initial exposure: early fetal life (<17 weeks, n = 92), mid-late fetal life (≥17 weeks, n = 67), or unexposed controls (n = 143). Of the 92 girls initially exposed in early fetal life, a subgroup was exposed exclusively in early fetal life (n = 22).In an independent confirmatory cohort, 1210 girls were followed from infancy to adolescence
title: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.

text: . Their exposure was maternal self-reported (any) use of paracetamol during pregnancy and reported early in the third trimester (yes/no)
title: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.

text: . Early fetal exposure was associated with reduced ovarian volume (-0.11 cm The observational design of the study allows evaluation of exposure outcome associations, while the causality interpretation is supported by consistency with experimental models demonstrating comparable effects
title: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.

text: . Residual confounding by indication for paracetamol use cannot be completely excluded, although the results were robust after accounting for fever and other maternal factors. title: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.

In this prospective cohort study of infant girls, prenatal exposure to paracetamol was associated with differences in several markers of ovarian development, including ovarian volume, follicle number, and circulating AMH, as well as uterine volume and breast tissue diameter. title: Fetal exposure to paracetamol is associated with altered markers of ovarian development and reduced uterine volume in girls: the COPANA study.

text: Developing a prediction model of neonatal pneumonia in patients with gestational diabetes mellitus in primary medical institutions.. The incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) continues to rise in China, and the risk of neonatal pneumonia is significantly increased, but the primary medical institutions lack simple and effective early risk assessment methods
title: Developing a prediction model of neonatal pneumonia in patients with gestational diabetes mellitus in primary medical institutions.

text: . To construct a prediction model for neonatal pneumonia suitable for primary medical institutions, based on readily available clinical characteristics of pregnant women with GDM, we aimed to identify key risk factors and provide a basis for developing clinical intervention strategies
title: Developing a prediction model of neonatal pneumonia in patients with gestational diabetes mellitus in primary medical institutions.

text: . Data on pregnant women and their newborns at Anyue Maternal and Child Health Hospital from 2023 to 2025 were retrospectively collected. Eight machine learning methods were used to construct the prediction model by bootstrap method and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to enhance the model's interpretability
title: Developing a prediction model of neonatal pneumonia in patients with gestational diabetes mellitus in primary medical institutions.

text: . A total of 328 pairs of mothers and newborns were included, and the incidence of neonatal pneumonia was 8.8%. Among the eight prediction models, Random Forest model performed the best and Decision tree model was the worst; SHAP results indicated education level, BMI, hyperemesis gravidarum, primipara, hyperlipidemia during pregnancy, premature birth and job were most influencing factors
title: Developing a prediction model of neonatal pneumonia in patients with gestational diabetes mellitus in primary medical institutions.

text: . Binary logistic regression analysis showed that premature birth (OR = 4.763, 95% CI = 1.522-14.901,  Despite the limited number of neonatal pneumonia events, our findings provide preliminary evidence that it may be feasible to develop a simplified risk-stratification tool for neonatal pneumonia in pregnancies complicated by GDM using routinely available clinical variables
title: Developing a prediction model of neonatal pneumonia in patients with gestational diabetes mellitus in primary medical institutions.

text: Exploratory association of OGTT area under the curve with early-night glycemic patterns and pharmacotherapy use in gestational diabetes mellitus.
title: Exploratory association of OGTT area under the curve with early-night glycemic patterns and pharmacotherapy use in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . In gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), the relationship between baseline 75-g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) area under the curve (AUC), subsequent continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived glycemic patterns, and pharmacotherapy use remains incompletely understood
title: Exploratory association of OGTT area under the curve with early-night glycemic patterns and pharmacotherapy use in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . This study aimed to examine the association of OGTT AUC with 14-day CGM profiles, with particular attention to nocturnal glycemic patterns, and pharmacotherapy use under routine clinical management. This single-center retrospective study included 64 singleton women with GDM identified from an institutional CGM registration cohort
title: Exploratory association of OGTT area under the curve with early-night glycemic patterns and pharmacotherapy use in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Participants were stratified into quartiles according to baseline OGTT AUC. CGM-derived metrics were evaluated overall and across prespecified time windows. Hierarchical regression models were used to examine the associations of OGTT AUC with overall TAR and pharmacotherapy use. ROC analysis was performed as an exploratory assessment of discriminatory ability
title: Exploratory association of OGTT area under the curve with early-night glycemic patterns and pharmacotherapy use in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Women in the highest OGTT AUC quartile showed less favorable CGM-derived glycemic profiles, with higher hyperglycemic exposure and greater glycemic variability, particularly during waking hours (06:00-22:00) and the early-night (22:00-02:00) period
title: Exploratory association of OGTT area under the curve with early-night glycemic patterns and pharmacotherapy use in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . Higher OGTT AUC was associated with greater overall TAR in linear regression models and with higher odds of pharmacotherapy use in logistic regression models. The association persisted in sensitivity models additionally adjusted for CGM-derived mean glucose, although these models were interpreted cautiously because mean glucose may lie downstream of OGTT AUC
title: Exploratory association of OGTT area under the curve with early-night glycemic patterns and pharmacotherapy use in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.770, with a potential cut-off of 17.34. In this exploratory CGM cohort of women with GDM, higher baseline OGTT AUC was associated with less favorable CGM-derived glycemic profiles, more apparent early-night glycemic abnormalities, and greater pharmacotherapy use under routine clinical management
title: Exploratory association of OGTT area under the curve with early-night glycemic patterns and pharmacotherapy use in gestational diabetes mellitus.

text: . OGTT AUC may help characterize subsequent glycemic burden and identify women who warrant closer glucose monitoring, but its clinical utility and candidate treatment-related thresholds require validation in larger prospective cohorts with standardized treatment-initiation criteria.

text: Evaluation of machine learning models for early prediction of gestational diabetes using retrospective electronic health records from current and previous pregnancies.
title: Evaluation of machine learning models for early prediction of gestational diabetes using retrospective electronic health records from current and previous pregnancies.

text: . To assess the performance of machine learning (ML) models in predicting gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) using electronic health record (EHR) data from the first antenatal visit, and determine whether incorporating previous pregnancies data improves performance. In this retrospective cohort study, ML models were developed to predict GDM using EHR data (n=27 561, GDM 11.6%)
title: Evaluation of machine learning models for early prediction of gestational diabetes using retrospective electronic health records from current and previous pregnancies.

text: . Four ML algorithms: Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB) and Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) were trained with seven to nine top clinical predictors from the EHRs. Models were trained and evaluated in separate first-trimester (n=27 561), nulliparous (n=11 623) and multiparous and past-pregnancy (n=4005) cohorts
title: Evaluation of machine learning models for early prediction of gestational diabetes using retrospective electronic health records from current and previous pregnancies.

text: . Discrimination was measured by the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC, 95 % CI), and calibration was assessed by slope and intercept. Decision-curve analysis was performed for models
title: Evaluation of machine learning models for early prediction of gestational diabetes using retrospective electronic health records from current and previous pregnancies.

text: . Decision-curve analysis was performed for models. First-trimester models achieved AUC 0.819 (95% CI 0.811-0.827, slope=1.010, intercept=0.013) with LR, similar to more complex models such as XGB (AUC 0.818, slope=1.004, intercept=0.007), EBM (AUC 0.817, slope=0.988, intercept=-0.017) and RF (AUC 0.817, slope=1.062, intercept=0.103)
title: Evaluation of machine learning models for early prediction of gestational diabetes using retrospective electronic health records from current and previous pregnancies.

text: . Among nulliparous women, there was little difference between LR (AUC 0.813) and XGB, EBM or RF (0.805-0.814). When past pregnancy features were added to first-trimester data in multiparous women, discrimination improved: EBM AUC 0.885 (95% CI 0.867 to 0.900; slope 0.994), RF 0.878, LR 0.874 and XGB 0.876
title: Evaluation of machine learning models for early prediction of gestational diabetes using retrospective electronic health records from current and previous pregnancies.

text: . Models using data from past pregnancies only achieved good discrimination (AUC 0.860, 95% CI 0.839 to 0.879; slope=1.028). A small panel of clinically selected variables provides robust early-pregnancy GDM prediction (AUC ∼0.81) and even stronger performance (AUC ∼0.86-0.89) when past pregnancy information is incorporated in multiparous women
title: Evaluation of machine learning models for early prediction of gestational diabetes using retrospective electronic health records from current and previous pregnancies.

text: . Past pregnancy data alone gives useful preconception risk estimates. These findings highlight the promise of early GDM risk identification in both nulliparous and multiparous populations; however, additional research, including external validation and clinical trials, is needed to determine the models' practical utility and effect on maternal and neonatal outcomes.
title: Evaluation of machine learning models for early prediction of gestational diabetes using retrospective electronic health records from current and previous pregnancies.

text: Late Onset Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Clinical Implications of Delayed Diagnosis and a Pragmatic Approach to Screening: A Narrative Review.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) increases maternal and neonatal risks and its reported prevalence has risen with evolving diagnostic criteria and screening strategies
title: Late Onset Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Clinical Implications of Delayed Diagnosis and a Pragmatic Approach to Screening: A Narrative Review.

text: . Although screening at 24-28 weeks is widely recommended, optimal testing methods and the value of screening outside that window remain contested. The aim of this narrative review is to critically examine the clinical significance, epidemiology, and pragmatic screening strategies for GDM first identified or retested in late pregnancy (the third trimester) after normal midpregnancy screening
title: Late Onset Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Clinical Implications of Delayed Diagnosis and a Pragmatic Approach to Screening: A Narrative Review.

text: . This narrative synthesis integrates findings from observational studies, retrospective cohorts, guideline statements, and relevant systematic reviews (including a 2024 meta-analysis) to summarize current knowledge and highlight gaps. Reports show that repeat testing can detect new GDM cases
title: Late Onset Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Clinical Implications of Delayed Diagnosis and a Pragmatic Approach to Screening: A Narrative Review.

text: . For example, one published retrospective cohort reported an 18.3% incidence among high-risk women retested in the third trimester
title: Late Onset Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Clinical Implications of Delayed Diagnosis and a Pragmatic Approach to Screening: A Narrative Review.

text: . Observational evidence and published reviews indicate associations between late-diagnosed GDM and higher rates of shoulder dystocia, cesarean delivery, and low 5-min Apgar scores, though findings for macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycemia, and NICU admission are inconsistent
title: Late Onset Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Clinical Implications of Delayed Diagnosis and a Pragmatic Approach to Screening: A Narrative Review.

text: . The short interval between late diagnosis and delivery limits the potential impact of interventions, and diagnosis itself may increase medicalization. Standard IADPSG OGTT thresholds were derived from 24-32-week cohorts and their applicability in later gestation is uncertain
title: Late Onset Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Clinical Implications of Delayed Diagnosis and a Pragmatic Approach to Screening: A Narrative Review.

text: . Pragmatic, selective strategies-targeted retesting based on ultrasound or clinical risk, or screening with random glucose/HbA1c to detect overt hyperglycemia-may reduce unnecessary OGTTs while identifying clinically meaningful cases
title: Late Onset Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Clinical Implications of Delayed Diagnosis and a Pragmatic Approach to Screening: A Narrative Review.

text: . As a narrative review, this article synthesizes current evidence to conclude that late-onset GDM is clinically relevant but understudied; universal third-trimester OGTT is not yet supported by robust outcome data. Prospective studies are needed to define optimal screening populations, diagnostic criteria, and management in late pregnancy.
title: Late Onset Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Clinical Implications of Delayed Diagnosis and a Pragmatic Approach to Screening: A Narrative Review.

text: Conflicting evidence for continuous glucose monitoring in gestational diabetes: current challenges and the imperative for individual participant data meta-analysis.. The incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is rising along with rates of obesity and type 2 diabetes
title: Conflicting evidence for continuous glucose monitoring in gestational diabetes: current challenges and the imperative for individual participant data meta-analysis.

text: . GDM is associated with an increased risk of various short- and long-term complications for both mother and child, including type 2 diabetes. Managing GDM requires a multidisciplinary approach that includes dietary guidance, promoting regular physical activity, and performing self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG)
title: Conflicting evidence for continuous glucose monitoring in gestational diabetes: current challenges and the imperative for individual participant data meta-analysis.

text: . Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has transformed pregnancy care in women with type 1 diabetes and is increasingly being proposed as a strategy to improve glycaemic management in GDM
title: Conflicting evidence for continuous glucose monitoring in gestational diabetes: current challenges and the imperative for individual participant data meta-analysis.

text: . By capturing postprandial glucose excursions, glycaemic variability, and time in range, CGM provides a more detailed picture of glycaemia and has raised expectations of improved metabolic control and pregnancy outcomes. Despite these theoretical advantages, evidence for CGM in GDM remains conflicting
title: Conflicting evidence for continuous glucose monitoring in gestational diabetes: current challenges and the imperative for individual participant data meta-analysis.

text: . More recently, several large randomized controlled trials (RCT's) show conflicting data: some studies show modest improvements in glycaemic measures, whereas others report no clear benefit for key maternal or neonatal outcomes, leaving the clinical value and cost-effectiveness of CGM unclear
title: Conflicting evidence for continuous glucose monitoring in gestational diabetes: current challenges and the imperative for individual participant data meta-analysis.

text: . A major limitation is the absence of validated CGM-based glycaemic targets specific to GDM, and current guidelines offer little direction beyond conventional SMBG guidelines
title: Conflicting evidence for continuous glucose monitoring in gestational diabetes: current challenges and the imperative for individual participant data meta-analysis.

text: . Future research should prioritize adequately powered large RCT's representing a broad population, and, importantly, individual participant data meta-analyses to reconcile inconsistent findings, identify subgroups most likely to benefit, establish pregnancy-specific CGM thresholds, and evaluate the impact on both obstetric outcomes and long-term postpartum metabolic risk
title: Conflicting evidence for continuous glucose monitoring in gestational diabetes: current challenges and the imperative for individual participant data meta-analysis.

text: . This ongoing debate underscores the need to critically appraise the role of CGM in GDM, summarize results from completed RCT's and meta-analyses, recognize key methodological and clinical evidence gaps, and outline the steps required for CGM to become fully integrated into standard GDM care.
title: Conflicting evidence for continuous glucose monitoring in gestational diabetes: current challenges and the imperative for individual participant data meta-analysis.

text: Investigating the associations between prepregnancy lipoprotein(a) and birth outcomes: The Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos.. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an atherosclerotic risk factor that may influence adverse pregnancy complications, although mechanisms remain poorly understood
title: Investigating the associations between prepregnancy lipoprotein(a) and birth outcomes: The Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos.

text: . Evidence linking Lp(a) with pregnancy outcomes relies on small cross-sectional studies, nonuniform Lp(a) measurement across pregnancy, and isoform-sensitive assays. We identified 508 women with singleton live birth >43 weeks after baseline (2008-2011)
title: Investigating the associations between prepregnancy lipoprotein(a) and birth outcomes: The Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos.

text: . Self-reported outcomes at second visit include: gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM, n = 80 [16%]), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP, n = 55 [11%]), preterm birth (PTB, n = 55 [11%]), small for gestational age (SGA, n = 37 [8%]), and birth weight Z-score (BWZ, n = 483). Adverse pregnancy outcome (APO, n = 179 [37%]) was defined as the presence of GDM, HDP, PTB, or SGA
title: Investigating the associations between prepregnancy lipoprotein(a) and birth outcomes: The Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos.

text: . Confounder-adjusted (age, kidney function, Hispanic/Latino background) logistic regression examined linear, curvilinear, quartile-categorized, and binary risk-threshold (≥75 nmol/L) patterns. Baseline mean age was 26.4 (SD = 5.8), almost half were of Mexican background, and the Lp(a) median = 16.9 nmol/L (range: 2.8-415.1; IQR: 6.7-52.8 nmol/L; n = 93 [18%] with Lp(a) >75 nmol/L)
title: Investigating the associations between prepregnancy lipoprotein(a) and birth outcomes: The Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos.

text: . Lp(a) >75 nmol/L had an odds ratio of 0.77 for HDP (95%CI: 0.31-1.92) and 0.86 for PTB (95%CI: 0.32-2.32), both imprecise and did not reach statistical significance. The curvilinear model, though imprecise, suggested an inverted U-shaped dose-response pattern for odds of GDM and HDP, while PTB and BWZ showed downward and upward trends, respectively, across increasing Lp(a)
title: Investigating the associations between prepregnancy lipoprotein(a) and birth outcomes: The Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos.

text: . Other associations showed no clear pattern. Prepregnancy Lp(a) may exhibit a U-shaped dose-response with HDP and GDM, and a downward trend in PTB; however, there were no definite associations. Future work with larger samples is needed to understand the physiological implications of Lp(a) for pregnancy.
title: Investigating the associations between prepregnancy lipoprotein(a) and birth outcomes: The Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos.

text: Risk factors for hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Identifying risk factors associated with hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza is crucial for guiding clinical management and public health strategies
title: Risk factors for hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . To support an update of WHO influenza clinical guidelines, this systematic review and meta-analysis assessed risk factors for hospital admission and all-cause mortality in patients with seasonal influenza
title: Risk factors for hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . We systematically searched Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, and Global Health for observational studies published from Jan 1, 2000, until Oct 30, 2025, that enrolled patients of any age with laboratory-confirmed seasonal influenza and reported an adjusted effect estimate for the association between at least
title: Risk factors for hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: estimate for the association between at least one risk factor and hospital admission or all-cause mortality, or both
title: Risk factors for hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . We conducted inverse-variance random-effects model meta-analyses to summarise the evidence and assessed the certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach. We registered the protocol with PROSPERO, CRD42024535669. We identified 35 808 records, of which 63 studies enrolling 2 150 518 participants (mean age 3·6-87·9 years) were eligible
title: Risk factors for hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . title: Risk factors for hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Risk factors for hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

title: Risk factors for hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Age 65 years or older, immunocompromised status, cardiovascular disease, neurological disease, and chronic respiratory disease are major risk factors for hospital admission in patients with non-severe seasonal influenza
title: Risk factors for hospital admission and mortality in patients with influenza virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

text: . Secondary bacterial infection, malnutrition, sepsis, acute kidney injury, age 65 years or older, chronic cardiovascular disease, malignancy, and chronic neurological disease are major risk factors for all-cause mortality in patients with severe seasonal influenza. Our findings support risk stratification and targeted prevention and treatment strategies for seasonal influenza. WHO.

text: Device measured physical activity among women with and without adverse pregnancy outcomes: Data from the HUNT study.
title: Device measured physical activity among women with and without adverse pregnancy outcomes: Data from the HUNT study.

text: . Women with a history of adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs), including gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), small for gestational age (SGA) offspring, preterm birth and placental abruption, are at increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and diabetes mellitus (DM) later in life. Physical inactivity is a risk factor for developing CVD and DM
title: Device measured physical activity among women with and without adverse pregnancy outcomes: Data from the HUNT study.

text: . Thus, for women with a history of APOs, it is particularly important to achieve recommended levels of physical activity (PA). The aim of this study was to investigate differences in PA levels among women with and without a history of APOs, using accelerometers to objectively measure PA levels. This is a population-based cohort study
title: Device measured physical activity among women with and without adverse pregnancy outcomes: Data from the HUNT study.

text: . This is a population-based cohort study. Women who participated in the fourth survey of Trøndelag health study (HUNT4) and were registered with one or more births in the Medical Birth Registry of Norway (MBRN) before participation, were included in the study. PA levels were objectively measured with two accelerometers worn by the participants for 3-7 consecutive days
title: Device measured physical activity among women with and without adverse pregnancy outcomes: Data from the HUNT study.

text: . Three different paces of walking, running and cycling were measured by the accelerometers and used to calculate our two outcomes: moderate-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in metabolic equivalent of task (MET)-minutes/week and total PA in min/day. MVPA included moderate and fast walking, running and cycling, and total PA included additionally slow walking
title: Device measured physical activity among women with and without adverse pregnancy outcomes: Data from the HUNT study.

text: . We used linear and logistic regression to examine the associations between history of APOs and PA levels. Among 3771 women, 868 (23.0%) had a history of one or more APOs. We found that women with a history of APOs had lower levels of PA. These differences diminished after accounting for postpartum general health and modifiable lifestyle factors
title: Device measured physical activity among women with and without adverse pregnancy outcomes: Data from the HUNT study.

text: . Among women with and without a history of APOs, respectively 17.7% and 15.9% did not achieve recommended levels of PA. There were no significant associations between history of APOs and PA levels in the fully adjusted regression analyses
title: Device measured physical activity among women with and without adverse pregnancy outcomes: Data from the HUNT study.

text: . Nevertheless, almost every fifth woman (15.9-17.7%) did not achieve recommended levels of PA, and postpartum follow up of women with APOs aimed at increasing their PA is important to prevent CVD and DM later in life.
title: Device measured physical activity among women with and without adverse pregnancy outcomes: Data from the HUNT study.

text: Postpartum Glycaemic Phenotype and Continuous Glucose Monitoring at 4-6 Years After Gestational Diabetes Defined by Different Diagnostic Criteria.
title: Postpartum Glycaemic Phenotype and Continuous Glucose Monitoring at 4-6 Years After Gestational Diabetes Defined by Different Diagnostic Criteria.

text: . To characterise glycaemic outcomes 4-6 years postpartum according to gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) diagnostic thresholds and evaluate whether continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) identifies differences not captured by conventional clinical measures. Women recruited before and after introduction of WHO GDM criteria were followed at 4 and 6 years postpartum
title: Postpartum Glycaemic Phenotype and Continuous Glucose Monitoring at 4-6 Years After Gestational Diabetes Defined by Different Diagnostic Criteria.

text: . At each follow-up, participants underwent oral glucose tolerance testing (OGTT), HbA1c measurement, body composition assessment and 14-day CGM. Based on pregnancy OGTT results and the diagnostic criteria in use at the time of testing, women were classified as meeting EASD 1991 criteria (GDM Women classified as GDM Long-term glycaemic risk aligns with diagnostic thresholds used during pregnancy
title: Postpartum Glycaemic Phenotype and Continuous Glucose Monitoring at 4-6 Years After Gestational Diabetes Defined by Different Diagnostic Criteria.

text: . Women diagnosed by older, higher thresholds exhibit a persistently less favourable glycaemic profile. Women meeting the lower WHO 2013 glucose thresholds represent a large group with a high prevalence of prediabetes, regardless of diagnosis during pregnancy. CGM detects modest differences in free-living glycaemic patterns not apparent from conventional clinical measures.
title: Postpartum Glycaemic Phenotype and Continuous Glucose Monitoring at 4-6 Years After Gestational Diabetes Defined by Different Diagnostic Criteria.

text: Global Oral Health Birth Cohort Studies: A Living Scoping Review.. In 2020, a scoping review mapped the existing Oral Health Birth Cohort Studies (OHBCS). Given the rapid growth and disparate nature of this field, this living scoping review aimed to identify new OHBCS and report their findings. A three-step search strategy was adopted
title: Global Oral Health Birth Cohort Studies: A Living Scoping Review.

text: . A three-step search strategy was adopted. Studies were searched using the databases PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus, along with the grey literature with no language restrictions. Two independent reviewers screened the studies
title: Global Oral Health Birth Cohort Studies: A Living Scoping Review.

text: . Two independent reviewers screened the studies. OHBCS included those with baseline data collection during pregnancy or within the first year of the child's life or linked future oral health data to exposures during either of these two life stages. Of the 5374 records, 32 new OHBCS from 16 countries (Northern Ireland and Scotland as part of the UK), comprising 184 studies, were identified
title: Global Oral Health Birth Cohort Studies: A Living Scoping Review.

text: . These were categorized as OHBCS with a single oral health publication (n = 17), OHBCS with two or more oral health publications (n = 10), cohorts nested within interventional studies (n = 2) and data linkage cohorts (n = 3). Most of the OHBCS (66%) were established in very high Human Development Index (HDI) countries
title: Global Oral Health Birth Cohort Studies: A Living Scoping Review.

text: . OHBCS, with a single publication, included participants from birth to 15, with participation rates ranging from 14.6% to 100.0%. Similarly, those with two or more publications, nested interventions, or data linkage had participation rates ranging from 13.3% to 99.4% by age 6
title: Global Oral Health Birth Cohort Studies: A Living Scoping Review.

text: . The most commonly reported primary outcomes were dental caries (n = 18), enamel defect/hypomineralization (n = 9), and oral microbiome (n = 5). The review highlights the rapid growth of new OHBCs, particularly in very high-human development countries and identifies emerging approaches in genetics and microbiome research
title: Global Oral Health Birth Cohort Studies: A Living Scoping Review.

text: . Efforts should encourage new OHBCS in low- and middle-income countries and support engagement in pooled analyses. Initiatives by GLOBICS (Global Consortium of Oral Health Birth Cohort Studies) may help define critical actions to leverage new and well-established OHBCS.
title: Global Oral Health Birth Cohort Studies: A Living Scoping Review.
