text: Revolutionising healthcare access: student-led clinics as catalysts for change in an underserved urban community in Karachi, Pakistan.. Karachi, Pakistan's largest metropolitan city, faces profound healthcare disparities, with an estimated 45-49% of the population residing in underserved informal settlements
title: Revolutionising healthcare access: student-led clinics as catalysts for change in an underserved urban community in Karachi, Pakistan.

text: . Within these communities, the primary healthcare system is not merely under-resourced but structurally fractured, leaving patients to navigate prohibitively expensive private providers or overcrowded public hospitals
title: Revolutionising healthcare access: student-led clinics as catalysts for change in an underserved urban community in Karachi, Pakistan.

text: . To address these systemic gaps, the Humanity Initiative, a student-led non-governmental organisation, implemented student-led clinics (SLCs) as a community-embedded, cost-effective model to bridge critical care deficits. We conducted a descriptive study examining the implementation and early outcomes of two SLCs conducted in Agra Taj Colony, Lyari Town, Karachi
title: Revolutionising healthcare access: student-led clinics as catalysts for change in an underserved urban community in Karachi, Pakistan.

text: . Operating every three weeks under licensed physician supervision, each SLC provided free primary consultations, dispensed essential medications, and delivered structured health education. We analysed patient demographics, disease burden, operational costs, and process-level indicators across both clinic cycles
title: Revolutionising healthcare access: student-led clinics as catalysts for change in an underserved urban community in Karachi, Pakistan.

text: . A total of 371 patients were seen across SLC1 (n = 194) and SLC3 (n = 177), with a higher proportion of female patients (n = 224, 60.4%)
title: Revolutionising healthcare access: student-led clinics as catalysts for change in an underserved urban community in Karachi, Pakistan.

text: . The disease burden was dominated by non-communicable diseases, including hypertension (14.3%) and diabetes (8.6%), alongside a notable number of acute infections and multi-system complaints reflecting the dual epidemiological burden characteristic of urban low- and middle-income country (LMIC) settings
title: Revolutionising healthcare access: student-led clinics as catalysts for change in an underserved urban community in Karachi, Pakistan.

text: . Operational costs were maintained at PKR 128-136 (USD 0.45-0.48) per patient, demonstrating exceptional cost-efficiency. We found significant gaps in health literacy, particularly regarding chronic disease self-management, and gendered barriers to healthcare access
title: Revolutionising healthcare access: student-led clinics as catalysts for change in an underserved urban community in Karachi, Pakistan.

text: . The SLC model demonstrates proof-of-concept as a viable, scalable strategy for bridging structural gaps in fractured primary healthcare systems in LMICs. By embedding care within the community, SLCs advance Universal Health Coverage, rebuild community trust in allopathic medicine, and provide supervised experiential learning opportunities for future healthcare professionals
title: Revolutionising healthcare access: student-led clinics as catalysts for change in an underserved urban community in Karachi, Pakistan.

text: . Replication of this model across similar underserved communities holds significant potential for reducing healthcare inequity in resource-constrained urban settings.
title: Revolutionising healthcare access: student-led clinics as catalysts for change in an underserved urban community in Karachi, Pakistan.

text: Stakeholder perspectives on managing insulin pump-related skin complications in children with type 1 diabetes: a mixed methods study in China.. Insulin pump-related skin complications are common in children with type 1 diabetes, yet stakeholder perspectives and management practices remain poorly characterized
title: Stakeholder perspectives on managing insulin pump-related skin complications in children with type 1 diabetes: a mixed methods study in China.

text: . We aimed to investigate knowledge, attitudes, practices, and educational needs related to these complications among caregivers, healthcare professionals, and manufacturer technical support staff in China. This sequential explanatory mixed methods study included a cross-sectional, questionnaire-based survey (n=951) and semi-structured interviews (n=40)
title: Stakeholder perspectives on managing insulin pump-related skin complications in children with type 1 diabetes: a mixed methods study in China.

text: . Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, and qualitative data were analyzed using framework analysis. The quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated through triangulation. Among 510 children represented by caregivers, 42.0% were reported to have experienced skin complications
title: Stakeholder perspectives on managing insulin pump-related skin complications in children with type 1 diabetes: a mixed methods study in China.

text: . Despite widespread concern, knowledge gaps persisted, particularly regarding infection management, and a knowledge-practice gap was evident. Qualitative findings identified role ambiguity as a structural barrier, with no stakeholder group assuming clear ownership of skin management. Participants described management as largely empirical and lacking standardized protocols
title: Stakeholder perspectives on managing insulin pump-related skin complications in children with type 1 diabetes: a mixed methods study in China.

text: . More than 96% of healthcare professionals and manufacturer technical support staff agreed that children and caregivers should receive comprehensive skin management training before pump initiation. Based on self-reported data, this descriptive study suggests that insulin pump-related skin complications were common among Chinese children with type 1 diabetes
title: Stakeholder perspectives on managing insulin pump-related skin complications in children with type 1 diabetes: a mixed methods study in China.

text: . Four hypothesis-generating challenges for skin management were identified, including knowledge-practice gaps, role ambiguity, empirical management, and insufficient training. They point to directions for future research such as developing evidence-based guidelines, clarifying interdisciplinary roles, and developing/implementing longitudinal education programs.
title: Stakeholder perspectives on managing insulin pump-related skin complications in children with type 1 diabetes: a mixed methods study in China.

text: Prevalence of polycystic ovary syndrome among college students in kashmir (J&K) india: a cross-sectional study.. Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder and a major cause of infertility among reproductive-age women
title: Prevalence of polycystic ovary syndrome among college students in kashmir (J&K) india: a cross-sectional study.

text: . Despite its high prevalence, awareness and early diagnosis remain inadequate, particularly among young women, and epidemiological data on college-aged women in the Indian subcontinent, including Kashmir, are limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of self-reported and symptom-screened PCOS and evaluate awareness among female university students in the Kashmir division
title: Prevalence of polycystic ovary syndrome among college students in kashmir (J&K) india: a cross-sectional study.

text: . By identifying symptom patterns and knowledge gaps, it provides evidence to support early detection and targeted educational interventions. A cross-sectional study was conducted between July and December 2024 among female students from randomly selected colleges in the Kashmir region. A total of 1,217 participants were enrolled using convenience sampling
title: Prevalence of polycystic ovary syndrome among college students in kashmir (J&K) india: a cross-sectional study.

text: . Data were collected using a structured, pre-validated questionnaire assessing demographics, PCOS awareness, and symptoms. Participants with a self-reported previous diagnosis of PCOS were excluded from symptom screening
title: Prevalence of polycystic ovary syndrome among college students in kashmir (J&K) india: a cross-sectional study.

text: . The psychometric properties of the 20-item PCOS knowledge questionnaire were evaluated using the Kuder-Richardson Formula 20 (KR-20) and a two-parameter Logistic Item Response Theory (IRT) model. The mean age of participants was 21.86 ± 2.24 years
title: Prevalence of polycystic ovary syndrome among college students in kashmir (J&K) india: a cross-sectional study.

text: . Among participants without a previous diagnosis of PCOS, 33.64% were identified as being at risk of PCOS and 1.28% had symptom profiles highly suggestive of PCOS. Additionally, 29.90% of participants reported a previous diagnosis of PCOS. Awareness of the broader health implications of PCOS remained inadequate
title: Prevalence of polycystic ovary syndrome among college students in kashmir (J&K) india: a cross-sectional study.

text: . Although gynecological symptoms were generally well recognized, knowledge of metabolic consequences and long-term complications was limited. Less than half of the participants were aware of the association between PCOS and insulin resistance (44.53%), type 2 diabetes (45.02%), and cardiovascular disease (33.00%)
title: Prevalence of polycystic ovary syndrome among college students in kashmir (J&K) india: a cross-sectional study.

text: . The findings suggest a substantial burden of previously undiagnosed, symptom-screened PCOS and inadequate awareness of its long-term health implications. Targeted health education, early screening, and appropriate clinical evaluation are needed to improve PCOS awareness and management.
title: Prevalence of polycystic ovary syndrome among college students in kashmir (J&K) india: a cross-sectional study.

text: The Neighborhood Health Hub Model: Extending Primary Care into Medically Underserved Neighborhoods to Improve Health Equity.. Limited research documents feasibility of deploying health coaches to extend primary care into medically underserved neighborhoods
title: The Neighborhood Health Hub Model: Extending Primary Care into Medically Underserved Neighborhoods to Improve Health Equity.

text: . To assess early experience implementing the Neighborhood Health Hub Model, an innovative, person-centered, place-based, neighborhood-level approach for providing convenient access to essential preventive services. Memphis/Shelby County, Tennessee PARTICIPANTS: Adults seeking care from January 2022-June 2024 at Neighborhood Health Hub facilities
title: The Neighborhood Health Hub Model: Extending Primary Care into Medically Underserved Neighborhoods to Improve Health Equity.

text: . Hubs are staffed by lay health coaches recruited from the community, trained in motivational interviewing, and supervised by a telehealth-connected health professional. Services include: 1) screening for obesity, hypertension, diabetes, and social determinants; 2) individual/group health coaching for chronic disease management; 3) referrals for medical, behavioral, and social needs
title: The Neighborhood Health Hub Model: Extending Primary Care into Medically Underserved Neighborhoods to Improve Health Equity.

text: . A total of 1,252 clients were served, 1,151 received health coaching, and 383 (31%) participated in ≥ 2 coaching sessions, for a total of 3367 coaching sessions and 2,951 group visits. Average weight change with obesity was - 3.32 pounds (95% confidence interval [CI] - 5.72, - 0.92) and systolic blood pressure change with hypertension was - 15.17 mmHg (CI - 19.64, - 10.69)
title: The Neighborhood Health Hub Model: Extending Primary Care into Medically Underserved Neighborhoods to Improve Health Equity.

text: . Higher number of health coaching sessions was significantly associated with greater weight loss. Dissemination of the Neighborhood Health Hub Model could improve health equity nationwide.
title: The Neighborhood Health Hub Model: Extending Primary Care into Medically Underserved Neighborhoods to Improve Health Equity.

text: Harnessing Cloud-Based Technology to Train School Nurses: A Type 1 Diabetes Exemplar.. In the United States, more than 40% of children and adolescents live with a chronic health condition, behavioral health need, or a specific learning disability that impacts their daily experience in the school setting
title: Harnessing Cloud-Based Technology to Train School Nurses: A Type 1 Diabetes Exemplar.

text: . Among these conditions, type 1 diabetes (T1D) is one of the most prevalent chronic health conditions among youth. School nurses are essential in promoting student health and academic success by ensuring students have the support and resources needed to remain healthy and ready to learn
title: Harnessing Cloud-Based Technology to Train School Nurses: A Type 1 Diabetes Exemplar.

text: . This exemplar describes an online back-to-school training for school nurses utilizing the school district's Google Workspace platform, providing school nurses with five evidence-based practice (EBP) resources and a recorded training on T1D management in a self-paced, online format
title: Harnessing Cloud-Based Technology to Train School Nurses: A Type 1 Diabetes Exemplar.

text: . With the evolving landscape of technology, school districts should ascertain how to harness available technology in their district to create accessible and sustainable EBP resources and training materials for school nurses.
title: Harnessing Cloud-Based Technology to Train School Nurses: A Type 1 Diabetes Exemplar.

text: The Use of Social Media in Health Interventions for People Living with Cancer: A Systematic Review.. Social media offers scalable opportunities for social connection and health communication; however, its role in cancer interventions remains unclear. This systematic review examines the use of social media in cancer-related health interventions and their targeted outcomes
title: The Use of Social Media in Health Interventions for People Living with Cancer: A Systematic Review.

text: . The review was registered with PROSPERO and conducted according to the PRISMA guidelines. Seven databases were searched for English-language randomized controlled trials (RCTs) (2000-2024) evaluating cancer interventions with a social media component
title: The Use of Social Media in Health Interventions for People Living with Cancer: A Systematic Review.

text: . Eligible studies involved adults (≥18 years) with a cancer diagnosis and reported outcomes related to physical, psychological, or social well-being. Intervention characteristics were categorized by social media role, intended effects, and platform affordances. Seventeen RCTs were included
title: The Use of Social Media in Health Interventions for People Living with Cancer: A Systematic Review.

text: . Seventeen RCTs were included. Quality of life was the most assessed outcome, with frequent improvements in psychosocial measures (e.g., anxiety, depression, and social support) and some physical benefits (e.g., fatigue, pulmonary function, and daily step count). WeChat was the dominant social media platform, followed by Facebook
title: The Use of Social Media in Health Interventions for People Living with Cancer: A Systematic Review.

text: . Most interventions delivered education, social support, and disease management, although few studies measured actual platform usage. The reported effects were shaped by common platform affordances, flexibility, structure, adaptation, narration, and identity, which enabled private communication, real-time clinician support, narrative sharing, and tailored guidance
title: The Use of Social Media in Health Interventions for People Living with Cancer: A Systematic Review.

text: . Findings suggest that social media platforms can enhance well-being, self-management, and social support for people living with cancer when these features are intentionally aligned with communication and behavior-change mechanisms. This review underscores the importance of theory-informed, context-specific design, rather than assuming benefit from social media use alone.
title: The Use of Social Media in Health Interventions for People Living with Cancer: A Systematic Review.

text: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.. The rapid growth of digital health technologies is changing how chronic illness patients access & view their health information
title: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.

text: . During the COVID-19 pandemic there was an increase in mobile health (mHealth) service usage and an increasing number of people exposing themselves to false information via social media. To develop safe and effective health communication strategies, it is important to understand how diabetic patients navigate this new digital world
title: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.

text: . to examine the health information seeking behaviour of diabetic patients in Saudi Arabia, including the use of digital health tools; interactions with the MOH; the use of social media; and how individuals verify information they find online. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among 419 adults with diabetes
title: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.

text: . Participants were recruited through stratified random sampling to ensure variation in age, education, and digital health familiarity. Data were collected using a structured online questionnaire comprising demographic items, Likert-scale measures of digital health engagement, and perceptions of MOH-provided AI services (e.g., chatbots and self-assessment tools)
title: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.

text: . Analyses were performed using SPSS and R. Structural equation modelling (SEM) examined relationships between latent constructs, while UpSet plots visualised behavioural intersections. Reliability was assessed using Cronbach's alpha
title: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.

text: . Reliability was assessed using Cronbach's alpha. Participants demonstrated multidimensional information-seeking patterns, frequently combining physician consultation (n = 245), peer-reviewed sources (n = 213), and government-affiliated platforms (n = 187). MOH digital services, particularly the 937 consultation hotline and Sehhaty virtual clinics, were widely utilised
title: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.

text: . Trust in AI-based tools remained moderate, with most respondents viewing them as supportive rather than decision-making substitutes. SEM revealed a strong positive association between eHealth engagement and trust in AI tools (β = 0.69, p < 0.001). UpSet plots indicated common co-occurrence of cautious behaviours, including cross-source verification
title: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.

text: . Cronbach's alpha values ranged from 0.73 to 0.91, confirming acceptable to high internal consistency. Diabetes patients in Saudi Arabia appear digitally engaged yet critically evaluative, favouring authoritative sources and cautiously adopting AI-enabled services
title: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.

text: . These findings emphasise the need to strengthen digital health literacy, integrate trusted information within widely used platforms, and enhance transparency and credibility in AI-driven health systems.
title: Health information seeking and digital tool engagement among diabetes patients: post-COVID-19 perspectives on trust, misinformation, and AI-Based MOH services.

text: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: . Frameworks that classify the financial burdens of managing pediatric type 1 diabetes (T1D) primarily focus on measurable material hardship, affordability, and cost-related distress and therefore do not sufficiently detail the household-level resources that care requires from families
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: . This study is a conceptual narrative review that aims to integrate the missing elements into a new three-level burden model, thereby linking the costs visible in clinical care, the household implementation burden borne by families, and the lived everyday experience of the child-parent-family triad
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: . The proposed contribution of the model is to interpret the sustainability of modern T1D care not exclusively in terms of technology access, reimbursement, or clinical effectiveness, but also as a function of families' temporal, digital, organizational, and decision-making capacity in relation to everyday self-management, educational-setting coordination, caregiver time investment, digital health
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: caregiver time investment, digital health literacy, and the digital divide
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: . The literature documents direct healthcare costs, out-of-pocket expenses, informal care, dietary adaptation, technology-related costs, parental distress, and time burden well when considered separately. However, these elements often do not appear as an integrated, cumulative household implementation burden
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: . In pediatric T1D, the actual usability and sustainability of technology depend not only on device availability and reimbursement but also on the family's organizational, digital, temporal, and decision-making capacity
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: . The T1D-ELB-P framework interprets the burdens placed on families as an organizing principle: it does not merely list domains but shows how financial, digital, temporal, decision-making, and institutional requirements can accumulate as household implementation burdens
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: . The proposed Type 1 Diabetes Everyday-Life Burden-Pediatric framework (T1D-ELB-P) conceptualizes the everyday-life economic burden of pediatric type 1 diabetes as a complementary dimension interpretable at the household and caregiver levels
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: . It highlights five interrelated domains: lifestyle and dietary adaptation; non-reimbursed or partially reimbursed consumables and accessories; digital infrastructure and digital health literacy; time, attention, and decision burden; and educational, extracurricular, and workplace coordination
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: . In this model, technology is not a separate focus but a cross-cutting factor that makes the implementation work borne by families visible across several domains. The clinical and health-policy significance of the framework lies in its highlighting of how the real-world use of modern T1D care is embedded in the everyday functioning of the child-parent-family triad
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: . Future cost-of-illness, health technology assessment, and patient-centered studies would benefit from explicitly measuring family implementation costs and capacities.
title: The Hidden Everyday-Life Burden of Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes: A Household Implementation Framework for Modern Diabetes Technology and Family Care.

text: Experiential knowledge and peer support in type 1 diabetes: insights from endurance running communities.. Managing type 1 diabetes (T1D) during endurance running requires highly individualized strategies, yet conventional healthcare offers limited sport-specific guidance. Peer communities have emerged as key sources of experiential knowledge, emotional support, and practical tools
title: Experiential knowledge and peer support in type 1 diabetes: insights from endurance running communities.

text: . To explore how endurance runners with T1D build self-management strategies, use peer networks and digital platforms, and integrate these exchanges into identity and daily life. Thirteen French-speaking adults with T1D who had completed at least one marathon or ultra-endurance event participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using constructivist grounded theory
title: Experiential knowledge and peer support in type 1 diabetes: insights from endurance running communities.

text: . Two patient contributors living with T1D supported interpretation and writing. COREQ guidelines were followed. Peer communities operated as informal educational systems that transformed individual trial-and-error into shared, actionable knowledge. Digital platforms provided rapid troubleshooting, reflective tools, and distributed mentorship
title: Experiential knowledge and peer support in type 1 diabetes: insights from endurance running communities.

text: . Role models facilitated confidence, self-efficacy, and identity reconstruction. Despite strong collective dynamics, management remained highly individualized through context-aware "micro-protocols" developed via safe experimentation and peer comparison. Peer communities play a central role in translating clinical recommendations into real-world endurance strategies
title: Experiential knowledge and peer support in type 1 diabetes: insights from endurance running communities.

text: . Integrating peer mentoring, digital literacy, and structured reflective practice into patient education may enhance personalization and confidence for people living with T1D
title: Experiential knowledge and peer support in type 1 diabetes: insights from endurance running communities.

text: . This study demonstrates how communities of practice and digital infrastructures can support experiential learning in high-variability contexts and illustrates the contribution of patient partners to qualitative analysis and manuscript co-construction. Two individuals living with T1D contributed to interpretation and writing, ensuring relevance and accessibility for the patient community.
title: Experiential knowledge and peer support in type 1 diabetes: insights from endurance running communities.

text: Digital Structured Education With Behavioral Nudge Tools for Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.. Digital interventions offer scalable alternatives to traditional face-to-face diabetes education, but often face challenges related to inconsistent clinical effectiveness, and declining user engagement
title: Digital Structured Education With Behavioral Nudge Tools for Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . However, whether a digital structured education program integrated with behavioral nudge tools can improve metabolic, behavioral, and psychological outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes remains unclear
title: Digital Structured Education With Behavioral Nudge Tools for Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a digital structured education program integrated with behavioral nudge tools in improving metabolic, behavioral, and psychological outcomes among adults with type 2 diabetes. This multicenter randomized controlled trial was conducted in the endocrinology departments of 4 hospitals in China
title: Digital Structured Education With Behavioral Nudge Tools for Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . Adults with type 2 diabetes were randomly assigned to an intervention group receiving a digital structured education program integrated with behavioral nudge tools (n=146) or a control group receiving standard digital diabetes education (n=147). Assessments were conducted at baseline and 12-week follow-up
title: Digital Structured Education With Behavioral Nudge Tools for Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . The primary outcome was hemoglobin A Among 293 participants (mean age 49.19, SD 10.02 y), 287 (97.9%) completed follow-up
title: Digital Structured Education With Behavioral Nudge Tools for Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . At 12 weeks, the intervention group demonstrated significantly greater improvements than the control group in HbA Digital structured education integrated with behavioral nudge tools improved metabolic outcomes and strengthened psychological and behavioral determinants of self-management among adults with type 2 diabetes over a 12-week period

text: Supporting continuous glucose monitoring for people with serious mental illness and type 2 diabetes: a co-design study for a structured intervention.. title: Supporting continuous glucose monitoring for people with serious mental illness and type 2 diabetes: a co-design study for a structured intervention.

text: . Diabetes self-management in this population is challenging, and existing interventions are poorly suited to their needs. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) offers potential benefits but remains underused
title: Supporting continuous glucose monitoring for people with serious mental illness and type 2 diabetes: a co-design study for a structured intervention.

text: . This study aimed to co-design a logic model and programme theory for a structured CGM intervention tailored to adults with SMI and type 2 diabetes, as a resource to support the planned future co-production of the content and the implementation of the full intervention
title: Supporting continuous glucose monitoring for people with serious mental illness and type 2 diabetes: a co-design study for a structured intervention.

text: . Using experience-based co-design, this study engaged service users, carers, and healthcare professionals (HCPs) in workshops and discussions to identify challenges and facilitators for CGM use. Participants co-developed an outline of candidate intervention components, which were summarised in a logic model and programme theory
title: Supporting continuous glucose monitoring for people with serious mental illness and type 2 diabetes: a co-design study for a structured intervention.

text: . The process included synthesising existing evidence, exploring personas, and mapping CGM user journeys. The draft intervention outline was iteratively refined across multiple sessions. Ten participants (four HCPs, four service users, and two carers) contributed to the co-design process
title: Supporting continuous glucose monitoring for people with serious mental illness and type 2 diabetes: a co-design study for a structured intervention.

text: . Barriers identified included limited technical support, accessibility challenges, and a lack of integrated physical and mental healthcare. Key components for a structured CGM intervention include personalised CGM training, flexible delivery methods, ongoing support, and peer networks. The proposed intervention was conceptualised in three phases: set-up, early days, and living with CGM
title: Supporting continuous glucose monitoring for people with serious mental illness and type 2 diabetes: a co-design study for a structured intervention.

text: . Participants prioritised flexibility and tailored intervention adjustments, emphasising the importance of addressing both physical and mental health needs concurrently
title: Supporting continuous glucose monitoring for people with serious mental illness and type 2 diabetes: a co-design study for a structured intervention.

text: . This study demonstrates the feasibility of co-designing interventions with individuals often considered "hard to reach." Our study highlights that people with SMI can take an interest in their physical health and see the potential for CGM to improve diabetes management, provided they receive appropriate and flexible support
title: Supporting continuous glucose monitoring for people with serious mental illness and type 2 diabetes: a co-design study for a structured intervention.

text: . Future work will develop and refine the intervention and evaluate its clinical and cost-effectiveness in diverse populations, aiming to address significant unmet needs in diabetes care for this vulnerable group. https://osf.io/4ae3g/ (2 February 2024).

text: Predictors of quality of life in adolescents with type 1 diabetes: The role of diabetes technology satisfaction and self-efficacy.. This study aimed to examine the associations among diabetes technology satisfaction, self-efficacy, and quality of life in adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D)
title: Predictors of quality of life in adolescents with type 1 diabetes: The role of diabetes technology satisfaction and self-efficacy.

text: . This descriptive, cross-sectional study included 235 adolescents with T1D registered at Family Health Centers in a provincial center in Turkey's Western Black Sea Region. title: Predictors of quality of life in adolescents with type 1 diabetes: The role of diabetes technology satisfaction and self-efficacy.

text: "Coach in your pocket": Men's digital self-management of type 2 diabetes.. To explore how adult men use digital technologies to support type 2 diabetes self-management and examine the perceived benefits, challenges, and meanings associated with technology use in everyday life
title: "Coach in your pocket": Men's digital self-management of type 2 diabetes.

text: . A qualitative study was conducted with 41 adult men with type 2 diabetes recruited between September 2025 and May 2026 through Prolific, community-based outreach, social media, and participant referrals. Semi-structured interviews were conducted virtually via Zoom, lasted approximately 25-75 minutes, and were professionally transcribed
title: "Coach in your pocket": Men's digital self-management of type 2 diabetes.

text: . Both authors analyzed transcripts using an inductive thematic approach in MAXQDA. Data saturation was observed at approximately interviews 36-38, with the remaining scheduled interviews supporting the adequacy of the dataset
title: "Coach in your pocket": Men's digital self-management of type 2 diabetes.

text: . Six interrelated themes characterized participants' experiences: real-time monitoring and awareness; technology as a reminder and organizational tool; learning and self-education; communication with healthcare providers; motivation and accountability; and barriers and frustrations with technology use
title: "Coach in your pocket": Men's digital self-management of type 2 diabetes.

text: . Across themes, participants described digital tools as helping them act independently on health information, maintain routines, make diabetes visible and actionable, and approach clinical encounters with organized personal data. Cost, usability, and trust in device accuracy remained important constraints
title: "Coach in your pocket": Men's digital self-management of type 2 diabetes.

text: . Digital technologies were embedded in participants' everyday diabetes self-management and often supported autonomy, practical problem-solving, accountability, and communication. Digital interventions for men with type 2 diabetes may be most useful when they provide actionable feedback, support self-directed management, integrate with clinical care, and minimize cost and usability burdens.
title: "Coach in your pocket": Men's digital self-management of type 2 diabetes.

text: Understanding Diabetes Self-Management in Low-Income Patients: Insights From a Qualitative Study.. title: Understanding Diabetes Self-Management in Low-Income Patients: Insights From a Qualitative Study.
journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care

text: . Data were collected through face-to-face interviews between February and August 2022, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's 6-phase framework. The results revealed that participants developed diabetes due to factors including busy and stressful lifestyles, alcohol dependence, and treatments for other illnesses
title: Understanding Diabetes Self-Management in Low-Income Patients: Insights From a Qualitative Study.
journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care

text: . Unemployment, smoking and drinking, and financial difficulties hindered self-management, resulting in the participants losing motivation. Financial instability made diabetes management more difficult. Their medical and living expenses were covered by government support, which led them to prioritize maintaining their eligibility for this assistance over having a job and income
title: Understanding Diabetes Self-Management in Low-Income Patients: Insights From a Qualitative Study.
journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care

text: . However, this ultimately had a devastating effect on the management of their disease. The hardships of life, financial burden of diabetes self-management, and lack of motivation and education on diabetes self-management hinder effective self-management
title: Understanding Diabetes Self-Management in Low-Income Patients: Insights From a Qualitative Study.
journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care

text: . It is recommended that a program be developed that can help low-income patients with diabetes cope with the disease, provide continuous motivation, and increase their self-efficacy. text: Medicaid Claims-Based Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support Utilization in Adults With Diabetes: Sociodemographic and Geographic Assessments.. text: . This pooled cross-sectional study analyzed Transformed Medicaid Statistical Information System Analytic Files from 2016 to 2023 for adults ages 19 to 64 years with diabetes (N = 3 735 182). text: . Overall, 5.6% (n = 210 078) of study beneficiaries with diabetes received ≥1 DSMES encounter. Utilization was higher among females (6.2%) and younger adults ages 19 to 34 years (7.5%)
title: Medicaid Claims-Based Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support Utilization in Adults With Diabetes: Sociodemographic and Geographic Assessments.
journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care

text: . DSMES was received by 8.9% of non-Hispanic (NH) multiracial beneficiaries, 7.5% of Hawaiians/Pacific Islanders, 7.4% of NH Asians, 6.7% of NH Whites, 5.6% of NH Blacks, 4.6% of NH American Indians/Alaska Natives, and 4.4% of Hispanics
title: Medicaid Claims-Based Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support Utilization in Adults With Diabetes: Sociodemographic and Geographic Assessments.
journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care

text: . Utilization was higher in counties with a lower Social Vulnerability Index (8.7% in the lowest quartile) and slightly higher for those living in rural areas (6.2%) than those in urban areas (5.8%). title: Medicaid Claims-Based Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support Utilization in Adults With Diabetes: Sociodemographic and Geographic Assessments.
journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care

title: Medicaid Claims-Based Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support Utilization in Adults With Diabetes: Sociodemographic and Geographic Assessments.
journal: The science of diabetes self-management and care

text: The Influence of Hospitalization and Nursing Interventions on Inpatients' Sleep Quality: A Multicenter Observational Study.. Sleep quality is a critical component of health and recovery, yet it remains a significant challenge during hospitalization. Poor sleep among inpatients is common and worsens throughout hospital stays, adversely affecting health outcomes and patient wellbeing
title: The Influence of Hospitalization and Nursing Interventions on Inpatients' Sleep Quality: A Multicenter Observational Study.

text: . Despite its importance, sleep often receives limited attention within hospital policies and nursing practices. To evaluate the impact of hospitalization and night-time nursing interventions on the sleep quality of noncritical patients in Spanish public hospitals. An observational, multicenter study was conducted across 12 public hospitals
title: The Influence of Hospitalization and Nursing Interventions on Inpatients' Sleep Quality: A Multicenter Observational Study.

text: . Data were collected from patients admitted to surgical and medical units between January 2020 and February 2022. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index at hospital admission and discharge
title: The Influence of Hospitalization and Nursing Interventions on Inpatients' Sleep Quality: A Multicenter Observational Study.

text: . Night-time nursing interventions (including medication administration, vital signs monitoring, blood sample collection, and anxiety management interventions), sociodemographic, anthropometric, clinical variables, and self-reported disturbances were also recorded. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics and linear regression models adjusted for potential confounding factors
title: The Influence of Hospitalization and Nursing Interventions on Inpatients' Sleep Quality: A Multicenter Observational Study.

text: . The study included 383 patients. Most patients (71%) presented poor sleep quality upon admission, which worsened during hospitalization (85.9%). A significant association was found between the number of intervention days and poorer sleep quality
title: The Influence of Hospitalization and Nursing Interventions on Inpatients' Sleep Quality: A Multicenter Observational Study.

text: . Collection of blood samples was significantly associated with worsened sleep quality in female patients, while anxiety management was associated with lower sleep quality in males. Discomfort with roommates and night-time nursing interventions were also related to worse sleep quality. Hospitalization exacerbates poor sleep quality in noncritical patients
title: The Influence of Hospitalization and Nursing Interventions on Inpatients' Sleep Quality: A Multicenter Observational Study.

text: . Night-time nursing interventions, discomfort with the hospital environment, and anxiety management are key factors. Interventions addressing these modifiable factors could improve patients' sleep quality and recovery. Hospital policies should incorporate sleep as a key quality indicator, promoting strategies to reduce unnecessary night-time interventions and environmental disturbances
title: The Influence of Hospitalization and Nursing Interventions on Inpatients' Sleep Quality: A Multicenter Observational Study.

text: . Nursing education must emphasize sleep-friendly care practices and appropriate planning of night-time activities.
title: The Influence of Hospitalization and Nursing Interventions on Inpatients' Sleep Quality: A Multicenter Observational Study.

text: Associations of Illness Perception, Resignation Coping, and Social Support With Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.. title: Associations of Illness Perception, Resignation Coping, and Social Support With Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . The study specifically explores whether resignation coping and social support exhibit indirect associations with SRF in the context of illness perception. A cross-sectional study. From November 2024 to October 2025, a convenience sample of 302 adult patients with T2DM was recruited from a tertiary general hospital in China
title: Associations of Illness Perception, Resignation Coping, and Social Support With Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Participants completed validated instruments with established psychometric properties, namely the Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire, the Medical Coping Modes Questionnaire, the Perceived Social Support Scale, and the Self-Regulatory Fatigue Scale
title: Associations of Illness Perception, Resignation Coping, and Social Support With Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Statistical analyses included Spearman correlation and serial mediation analysis using the PROCESS Macro (Model 6) with bias-corrected bootstrapping. SRF was positively correlated with negative illness perception (r = 0.579, p < 0.01) and resignation coping (r = 0.612, p < 0.01), and negatively correlated with social support (r = -0.598, p < 0.01)
title: Associations of Illness Perception, Resignation Coping, and Social Support With Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Serial mediation analysis revealed that illness perception was associated with SRF through indirect pathways involving resignation coping and social support. Resignation coping and social support mediated the association between illness perception and self-regulatory fatigue, both individually and sequentially. Negative illness perception correlates with higher SRF
title: Associations of Illness Perception, Resignation Coping, and Social Support With Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . This observed correlation is additionally linked to indirect pathways involving resignation coping and lower social support. Collectively, these findings highlight a pattern of interrelated cognitive (illness perception), behavioural (resignation coping), and resource (social support) factors that are associated with self-regulatory fatigue in this cross-sectional study
title: Associations of Illness Perception, Resignation Coping, and Social Support With Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . The findings offer a clear, evidence-based framework for nursing practice. They highlight the potential value of integrated assessment and intervention that simultaneously addresses patients' illness beliefs, maladaptive coping strategies, and social support systems, which are associated with lower SRF and better diabetes self-management
title: Associations of Illness Perception, Resignation Coping, and Social Support With Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . This study adheres to the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines for cross-sectional studies. title: Associations of Illness Perception, Resignation Coping, and Social Support With Self-Regulatory Fatigue in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: Pilot randomized controlled trial of a peer coach-led behavioral and educational intervention to enhance quality of life in patients living with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: Protocol for the RISE-HP study.. title: Pilot randomized controlled trial of a peer coach-led behavioral and educational intervention to enhance quality of life in patients living with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: Protocol for the RISE-HP study.

text: . Patients living with HP experience significant stress, uncertainty, and hypervigilance about the management of their disease and prognosis. The goal of this behavioral and educational intervention, RISE-HP, is to improve HRQOL in people who have HP
title: Pilot randomized controlled trial of a peer coach-led behavioral and educational intervention to enhance quality of life in patients living with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: Protocol for the RISE-HP study.

text: . The objective of this pilot study is to assess feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effectiveness of the RISE-HP intervention. This pilot randomized controlled trial will be conducted in patients over the age of 18 with a diagnosis of HP
title: Pilot randomized controlled trial of a peer coach-led behavioral and educational intervention to enhance quality of life in patients living with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: Protocol for the RISE-HP study.

text: . Forty participants will be randomly assigned to receive either the RISE-HP intervention (meetings with a peer coach focused on living well with their HP using cognitive behavioral techniques and motivational interviewing) or an attention control (general health education sessions with a research assistant) for 10 weeks
title: Pilot randomized controlled trial of a peer coach-led behavioral and educational intervention to enhance quality of life in patients living with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: Protocol for the RISE-HP study.

text: . Participants will complete four additional study visits (enrollment, 5 weeks, 10 weeks, and 14 weeks after intervention start) for patient reported outcome measure completion. Primary implementation outcomes will be feasibility and acceptability
title: Pilot randomized controlled trial of a peer coach-led behavioral and educational intervention to enhance quality of life in patients living with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: Protocol for the RISE-HP study.

text: . Secondary patient-centered effectiveness clinical outcomes will be improvement in HRQOL as measured by the Kings Brief Interstitial Lung Disease (KBILD) questionnaire. Additional secondary patient-reported clinical outcomes include fatigue, anxiety, depression, and self-efficacy
title: Pilot randomized controlled trial of a peer coach-led behavioral and educational intervention to enhance quality of life in patients living with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: Protocol for the RISE-HP study.

text: . Overall, this study addresses an important gap in HP care by targeting HRQOL and offers a novel non-pharmacologic patient-centered approach to therapy in patients with HP.
title: Pilot randomized controlled trial of a peer coach-led behavioral and educational intervention to enhance quality of life in patients living with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: Protocol for the RISE-HP study.

title: Protocol for the DECIDE+ trial: a quasi-experimental hybrid effectiveness-implementation study of social support and CVD self-management through community health workers in Philadelphia.

text: . This study aims to (1) determine the effectiveness of the Decision-making Education for Choices in Diabetes Everyday (DECIDE)+ intervention in improving CVD self-management skills among Philadelphia residents with CVD risk factors and unmet social needs compared with standard community health worker (CHW) engagement and (2) assess the reach, adoption, fidelity and maintenance of DECIDE+
title: Protocol for the DECIDE+ trial: a quasi-experimental hybrid effectiveness-implementation study of social support and CVD self-management through community health workers in Philadelphia.

text: . Using a type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation design, this quasi-experimental study will compare outcomes between participants who enrol in the DECIDE+ group (n=250) or receive standard CHW services (n=250). DECIDE+ combines a structured nine-session problem-solving programme for chronic disease management with ongoing CHW support addressing social needs
title: Protocol for the DECIDE+ trial: a quasi-experimental hybrid effectiveness-implementation study of social support and CVD self-management through community health workers in Philadelphia.

text: . Both groups will be randomly assigned to either monthly or biweekly CHW follow-up to examine the impact of contact frequency on health behaviour outcomes. Primary outcomes include CVD self-management skills measured by the Self-care of Chronic Illness Inventory
title: Protocol for the DECIDE+ trial: a quasi-experimental hybrid effectiveness-implementation study of social support and CVD self-management through community health workers in Philadelphia.

text: . Implementation outcomes will be assessed through a mixed-methods approach including structured interviews with CHWs and analysis of programme-level data. This study was approved by the University of Pennsylvania Institutional Review Board (Protocol #856216). Written informed consent is obtained from all participants prior to enrolment
title: Protocol for the DECIDE+ trial: a quasi-experimental hybrid effectiveness-implementation study of social support and CVD self-management through community health workers in Philadelphia.

text: . This pragmatic trial addresses cardiovascular health disparities by simultaneously enhancing problem-solving skills for chronic disease management and addressing social and environmental barriers to effective self-management
title: Protocol for the DECIDE+ trial: a quasi-experimental hybrid effectiveness-implementation study of social support and CVD self-management through community health workers in Philadelphia.

text: . The study will provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of multilevel CHW-delivered interventions and optimal implementation strategies in real-world community settings. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific conference presentations. NCT06732102.
title: Protocol for the DECIDE+ trial: a quasi-experimental hybrid effectiveness-implementation study of social support and CVD self-management through community health workers in Philadelphia.

text: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.. Effective diabetes management requires continuous interpretation of glycemic trends, personalized dietary guidance, and sustained patient education
title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.

text: . Although large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for health-related applications, existing general-purpose and biomedical models often struggle with diabetes-specific reasoning and instruction-following, limiting their reliability for domain-focused tasks such as clinical question answering and dietary recommendation tasks
title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.

text: . This study aimed to develop and evaluate a diabetes-specialized LLM optimized for diabetes-specific reasoning, instruction-following, and dietary recommendation tasks. This was a model development and benchmark evaluation study
title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.

text: . We developed a model-centric instruction refinement framework using instruction-following difficulty and reversed instruction-following difficulty to identify and replace suboptimal instruction-response pairs during instruction tuning. Curriculum-based instruction tuning was applied by sequencing instructions from lower to higher difficulty
title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.

text: . The resulting diabetes-specialized model was evaluated across diabetes-related question answering, natural language inference, information extraction, summarization, clinical answer generation, and dietary recommendation tasks. Performance was compared with biomedical LLMs and general-purpose baselines using diabetes-specific benchmark subsets and simulation-based glycemic evaluation
title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.

text: . Across diabetes-related benchmark tasks, the proposed model demonstrated improved performance in question answering, information extraction, and generative tasks. Ablation experiments showed that the full reflection- and curriculum-based instruction tuning strategy improved overall performance by 59.03% relative to the zero-shot LLaMA3.1 8B baseline
title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.

text: . For dietary recommendation tasks, the proposed model achieved a 0.66% improvement in the Diet Quality Index-International score compared with ChatGPT (GPT-4)
title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.

text: . Simulation-based evaluation using the SimGlucose simulator further showed that meal plans generated by the proposed model resulted in a reduced postprandial glycemic burden, as measured by a lower incremental area under the curve, compared with GPT-4-generated meal plans
title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.

text: . This study demonstrates that domain-specific instruction tuning can effectively adapt general-purpose LLMs for diabetes management. By combining reflection-based instruction replacement with curriculum-based instruction tuning, the proposed approach enhances instruction-following, reasoning capability, and dietary guidance for diabetes
title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.

text: . The results highlight the potential of specialized LLMs to provide more reliable and clinically aligned support for diabetes-related decision-making and self-management, offering a promising direction for safe and effective AI deployment in chronic disease care.
title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.

text: Psychological resilience and psychosocial adaptation in type 2 diabetes mellitus: Associations with executive functioning and clinical indicators.. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has been associated with executive-function vulnerability, yet the role of psychological resilience in neuropsychological and psychosocial functioning remains unclear
title: Psychological resilience and psychosocial adaptation in type 2 diabetes mellitus: Associations with executive functioning and clinical indicators.

text: . This study examined whether resilience was associated with executive-function performance, clinical indicators, and psychosocial adaptation in adults with T2DM and healthy controls. This cross-sectional study included 206 adults (102 with T2DM and 104 healthy controls) after excluding individuals with low global cognitive screening scores
title: Psychological resilience and psychosocial adaptation in type 2 diabetes mellitus: Associations with executive functioning and clinical indicators.

text: . Resilience was assessed using the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale and classified as low or moderate-to-high. Participants completed executive-function tests and questionnaires assessing diabetes self-management, depressive symptoms, quality of life, and perceived family support
title: Psychological resilience and psychosocial adaptation in type 2 diabetes mellitus: Associations with executive functioning and clinical indicators.

text: . General linear models controlled for age and education, with Holm-Bonferroni correction applied within related outcome sets; sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for depressive symptoms and body mass index
title: Psychological resilience and psychosocial adaptation in type 2 diabetes mellitus: Associations with executive functioning and clinical indicators.

text: . Participants with T2DM showed poorer Digit Span and WCST performance after correction, indicating vulnerabilities in attention span, working memory, cognitive flexibility, and concept formation
title: Psychological resilience and psychosocial adaptation in type 2 diabetes mellitus: Associations with executive functioning and clinical indicators.

text: . A significant disease status × resilience interaction was found for Tower of London (planning) performance; simple main-effects analysis indicated a significant resilience effect within the T2DM group but not among controls, and this interaction remained significant after adjustment for depressive symptoms and body mass index
title: Psychological resilience and psychosocial adaptation in type 2 diabetes mellitus: Associations with executive functioning and clinical indicators.

text: . Resilience was broadly associated with better psychosocial outcomes, and lower resilience in T2DM was also associated with higher mean HbA1c and systolic blood pressure. T2DM was associated with executive-function vulnerability, whereas resilience was selectively related to planning performance and more broadly associated with psychosocial adaptation.
title: Psychological resilience and psychosocial adaptation in type 2 diabetes mellitus: Associations with executive functioning and clinical indicators.

text: Research progress on the intervention of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine nursing for diabetic foot.. Diabetic foot (DF) is a serious disabling, recurrent chronic complication of diabetes. While integrated Chinese-Western nursing for DF is widely studied, few systematic reviews frame relevant research based on the nursing process
title: Research progress on the intervention of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine nursing for diabetic foot.

text: . This narrative review systematically retrieved literature from major Chinese and English databases up to December 2025, sorting included studies into nursing assessment, intervention and health education to assess evidence quality, analyze synergistic mechanisms of dual nursing modes, and verify their benefits in lowering amputation risk, accelerating wound repair and improving patients' quality
title: Research progress on the intervention of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine nursing for diabetic foot.

text: wound repair and improving patients' quality of life
title: Research progress on the intervention of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine nursing for diabetic foot.

text: . In assessment, Western nursing relies mainly on Wagner/Texas grading and ankle-brachial index detection
title: Research progress on the intervention of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine nursing for diabetic foot.

text: . Western interventions center on debridement, dressing change and blood glucose management, matched with syndrome-differentiated TCM measures including herbal fumigation, acupoint massage and dietary conditioning; combined nursing outperforms single-mode care, yet timing and connection strategies remain unclear
title: Research progress on the intervention of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine nursing for diabetic foot.

text: . Integrated foot self-management and dietary education are commonly used, though long-term efficacy and standardized pathways are debated. Existing research is evolving from efficacy observation to standardized protocol construction with an emerging "precise Western intervention+holistic TCM regulation" consensus
title: Research progress on the intervention of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine nursing for diabetic foot.

text: . Major barriers include non-standardized TCM nursing operations, flawed study designs, and insufficient integrated clinical pathways instead of separate parallel implementation. This review constructs a nursing-process-based synthesis framework, pinpointing integration gaps across assessment, intervention and education to support subsequent evidence-based research
title: Research progress on the intervention of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine nursing for diabetic foot.

text: . Future work should standardize TCM nursing operations, build nursing-sensitive indicators and launch multi-center cooperation, transforming empirical nursing into evidence-based practice. The summarized regimens can guide personalized nursing plan formulation and provide references for industry standardization and quality improvement.
title: Research progress on the intervention of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine nursing for diabetic foot.

text: Quality and reliability of information about blood glucose monitoring on TikTok and Bilibili: A cross-sectional analysis.. Monitoring blood glucose is essential for diabetes management, and many patients use short-video platforms to learn capillary blood glucose testing
title: Quality and reliability of information about blood glucose monitoring on TikTok and Bilibili: A cross-sectional analysis.

text: . We evaluated whether previously reported concerns about online health information also apply to this narrower procedural task and compared high-ranking videos on TikTok/Douyin and Bilibili. We included 192 videos (TikTok, n = 100; Bilibili, n = 92) and extracted duration, engagement metrics, uploader type, and video category
title: Quality and reliability of information about blood glucose monitoring on TikTok and Bilibili: A cross-sectional analysis.

text: . Two trained nursing reviewers assessed general educational quality and reliability-related characteristics using the Global Quality Score (GQS) and modified DISCERN (mDISCERN). Between-platform comparisons used Mann-Whitney U tests or Pearson's chi-square tests, with standardized Mann-Whitney effect sizes; Spearman correlations examined associations with quality scores
title: Quality and reliability of information about blood glucose monitoring on TikTok and Bilibili: A cross-sectional analysis.

text: . TikTok videos received more likes, platform-specific saving actions, comments, and shares and were shorter than Bilibili videos (all P < 0.001; r = 0.315-0.403). TikTok also had higher proportions of accounts classified as professional uploaders (63.0% vs 35.9%, P < 0.001) and popular-science videos (53.0% vs 32.6%, P = 0.004)
title: Quality and reliability of information about blood glucose monitoring on TikTok and Bilibili: A cross-sectional analysis.

text: . However, GQS and mDISCERN scores did not differ significantly between platforms (GQS, P = 0.246; mDISCERN, P = 0.072). Coverage of four prespecified procedural elements was incomplete on both platforms, with guidance on first-drop discard, alcohol drying, and post-puncture pressing time appearing in only a minority of videos
title: Quality and reliability of information about blood glucose monitoring on TikTok and Bilibili: A cross-sectional analysis.

text: . TikTok achieved substantially greater engagement, but popularity did not indicate significantly better educational quality or reliability-related characteristics. Standardized, professionally developed procedural videos may improve online diabetes self-management guidance.
title: Quality and reliability of information about blood glucose monitoring on TikTok and Bilibili: A cross-sectional analysis.

text: Profiles of Self-Management Behaviors and Psychological Characteristics in Patients with Diabetic Retinopathy: A Cross-Sectional Study.
title: Profiles of Self-Management Behaviors and Psychological Characteristics in Patients with Diabetic Retinopathy: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . This study aimed to identify the heterogeneity in self-management behaviors and psychological characteristics among patients with diabetic retinopathy (DR), and to construct patient user profiles by integrating demographic and clinical characteristics, thereby providing a basis for developing personalized nursing strategies
title: Profiles of Self-Management Behaviors and Psychological Characteristics in Patients with Diabetic Retinopathy: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . A total of 273 patients with DR were recruited from a tertiary hospital in Wenzhou between March and August 2025. Data were collected using a general information questionnaire, the Summary of Diabetes Self-Care Activities Scale, the Self-Efficacy to Manage Chronic Disease Scale, the Medical Coping Modes Questionnaire, and the NEI VFQ-25 scale
title: Profiles of Self-Management Behaviors and Psychological Characteristics in Patients with Diabetic Retinopathy: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . K-means clustering was employed to identify potential subgroups, and statistical comparisons were made to examine demographic differences across clusters. Three clusters were identified, forming three distinct user profiles: distressed dependent type, proactive pioneering type, and balanced transitional type
title: Profiles of Self-Management Behaviors and Psychological Characteristics in Patients with Diabetic Retinopathy: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Significant differences were observed among the three profiles in education level, occupational status, place of residence, per capita monthly household income, diabetes treatment methods, diabetes duration, HbA1c, fasting blood glucose, left eye intraocular pressure, and quality of life related to visual function. This study developed three patient profiles
title: Profiles of Self-Management Behaviors and Psychological Characteristics in Patients with Diabetic Retinopathy: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . This study developed three patient profiles. In future clinical practice, healthcare professionals can rapidly identify patients with different risk characteristics based on these profiles and implement targeted, stratified interventions, thereby improving self-management ability, prognosis, and quality of life in patients with DR.
title: Profiles of Self-Management Behaviors and Psychological Characteristics in Patients with Diabetic Retinopathy: A Cross-Sectional Study.

text: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.. To map the diabetes camp literature across five epistemic layers and to construct an operationalised evidence gap matrix identifying structural knowledge gaps relevant to nursing practice, education and policy. Scoping review reported in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guideline
title: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

text: . Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, OVID/MEDLINE and PubMed, searched on 19 June 2026 without date restriction (results spanned 1931-2026)
title: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

text: . A title-field search ('diabet*' AND 'camp') across four databases yielded 1591 records that, after homonym screening, cross-database deduplication, publication-type and English-language filtering, and a supplementary PubMed search, produced a deduplicated evidence map of 279 records
title: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

text: . Two reviewers independently double-coded the analytic set; inter-rater reliability was almost perfect (Cohen's kappa 0.955 for outcome direction and 0.960 for study design)
title: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

text: . The 199 records carrying an extractable abstract formed the analytic set and were coded across four dimensions (outcome direction, study design, follow-up duration and thematic area); proportions are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals
title: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

text: . Of the 199 analytic records, 104 (52.3%) reported a measured directional outcome; of these, 90.4% documented benefit in at least one dimension, but 32.7% contained mixed or non-significant sub-outcomes and only 57.7% were entirely positive
title: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

text: . Only 12 records (6.0%) reported follow-up of 6 months or longer, and post-camp glycaemic deterioration was documented consistently across the longitudinal evidence. The evidence base was predominantly descriptive (51.8%), with only 6.5% employing a controlled experimental design; just 9 records (4.5%) combined an analytic-or-stronger design, follow-up of at least 6 months and a measured outcome
title: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

text: . No study provided cost-effectiveness analysis, per-camp unit cost data or comparative evidence on physical versus virtual delivery models. The diabetes camp literature is structurally incomplete: benefit is selective, temporally fragile, socially inequitable and entirely uncosted
title: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

text: . Resolving this paradox requires temporal expansion (12-month follow-up), dimensional expansion (multidimensional outcome packages) and structural expansion (cost-effectiveness analysis and delivery-model comparison)
title: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

text: . This review identifies actionable evidence gaps for paediatric, public health and school nurses involved in camp-based diabetes self-management education, informing nurse-led longitudinal follow-up, equitable access strategies and economic accountability in nursing-delivered camp interventions
title: The Diabetes Camp Paradox: An Evidence Gap Map of 279 Publications and the Anatomy of Known Unknowns.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

text: . The first author is fathering a child with autism, and he is focusing on rationalistic design of health services during his career. The co-author is the head of a nonprofit association established in 2010, the mission of which is advocating, supporting, educating and motivating children with diabetes and their families

Its board is made of three mothers of children with diabetes, one young adult with diabetes, one social worker who has been part of the paediatric diabetes team for 20 years and one diabetes specialist nurse. This association conducts numerous diabetes camps every year and is pioneering camp activities in the country by far
