text: Association between educational attainment and diabetes self-management, glycemic control, and health outcomes among older Nigerian adults with type 2 diabetes.. This study investigated how educational disparities affect self-management practices, glycemic control, and diabetes-related health outcomes among older adults living with type 2 diabetes in Nigeria
title: Association between educational attainment and diabetes self-management, glycemic control, and health outcomes among older Nigerian adults with type 2 diabetes.

text: . Findings were interpreted to identify implications for geriatric nursing practice, education, research, and policy in low-resource settings. A multicenter, cross-sectional study was conducted from April 2023 to May 2025 across 30 communities in Nigeria's six geopolitical zones
title: Association between educational attainment and diabetes self-management, glycemic control, and health outcomes among older Nigerian adults with type 2 diabetes.

text: . A stratified cluster sampling technique was employed, enrolling 896 participants aged ≥60 years with confirmed type 2 diabetes. Data were collected using the validated Type 2 Diabetes Assessment Questionnaire (T2DAQ) through domiciliary and clinic-based interviews. Statistical analyses included descriptive summaries, chi-square tests, and logistic regression, with significance set at p ≤ 0.05
title: Association between educational attainment and diabetes self-management, glycemic control, and health outcomes among older Nigerian adults with type 2 diabetes.

text: . Of the 896 participants, 65.3% had lower education. Higher education was significantly associated with better diabetes knowledge, medication adherence (42.6%vs. 22.8%; p = 0.034), dietary compliance (38.1%vs. 33.3%; p = 0.011), and glycemic control (p = 0.024)
title: Association between educational attainment and diabetes self-management, glycemic control, and health outcomes among older Nigerian adults with type 2 diabetes.

text: . Urban residency (OR = 2.0), absence of comorbidities (OR = 0.63), and alcohol use (OR = 1.72) predicted higher education, while tobacco use and rural residence were negatively associated. Educational attainment significantly influences diabetes self-management and outcomes among older Nigerian adults
title: Association between educational attainment and diabetes self-management, glycemic control, and health outcomes among older Nigerian adults with type 2 diabetes.

text: . Geriatric nursing should incorporate health literacy screening and simplified, culturally tailored education. Nurse training curricula must emphasize adaptive strategies for low-literacy patients. Policy reforms should embed structured Diabetes Self-Management Education (DSME) into primary care
title: Association between educational attainment and diabetes self-management, glycemic control, and health outcomes among older Nigerian adults with type 2 diabetes.

text: . Future research should evaluate longitudinal impacts of education-sensitive interventions to promote equitable chronic disease care in aging populations.
title: Association between educational attainment and diabetes self-management, glycemic control, and health outcomes among older Nigerian adults with type 2 diabetes.

text: [Construction of obesity self-management education and support framework].. Obesity is a chronic metabolic disease requiring long-term intervention and sustained behavioral management
title: [Construction of obesity self-management education and support framework].

text: . Given the current paucity of systematic education and support standards in obesity care, this paper proposes the obesity self-management education and support (OSMES) framework, modeled on the mature theoretical and practical foundations of diabetes self-management education and support framework
title: [Construction of obesity self-management education and support framework].

text: . Grounded in the L.I.F.E.care four-dimensional model: load management (L), integration fitness (I), form optimization (F), and equilibrium mindset (E)
title: [Construction of obesity self-management education and support framework].

text: . The framework establishes 6 core standards: support system development, target population assessment, multidisciplinary team collaboration, service design and delivery, person-centered longitudinal care, and outcome evaluation with continuous quality improvement
title: [Construction of obesity self-management education and support framework].

text: . Unlike traditional approaches focusing solely on weight reduction, OSMES elevates body form, functional capacity, and psychological well-being to equal importance alongside metabolic indicators
title: [Construction of obesity self-management education and support framework].

text: . Considering China's healthcare context, the framework explores collaborative models between medical institutions and third-party organizations, diversified payment pathways, and digital remote support to provide an implementable reference for long-term obesity management
title: [Construction of obesity self-management education and support framework].

text: . 肥胖症是一种需要长期干预与持续行为管理的慢性代谢性疾病。针对当前肥胖症管理缺乏系统化教育与支持标准的问题，该文借鉴糖尿病自我管理教育与支持的成熟经验，提出“肥胖症自我管理教育与支持标准框架”。该框架以L.I.F.E.care四维模型为理论基础，涵盖体重负荷管理（L）、体形塑造（I）、姿态改善（F）及心态调整（E），构建六项核心标准：支持体系构建、目标人群评估、多学科团队协作、服务设计与实施、以人为本的全程照护以及结果评价与质量改进。与传统以体重下降为单一目标的管理模式不同，该框架强调将体态、功能与心理健康提升至与代谢指标同等重要的地位，并结合我国医疗服务环境，探索医院与第三方专业机构协同的服务模式、多元化支付路径及数字化远程支持，为肥胖症长期管理提供可实施的结构化参考。.
title: [Construction of obesity self-management education and support framework].

text: Latent profiles analysis and associated factors of digital health literacy among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes.. Digital health technologies are increasingly used in chronic disease management, but their effective use requires adequate digital health literacy (DHL)
title: Latent profiles analysis and associated factors of digital health literacy among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes.

text: . Because an overall DHL score may mask heterogeneity across its multiple dimensions, this study aimed to identify latent profiles of DHL among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes and to examine factors associated with profile membership, thereby informing individualized health education and stratified health promotion strategies for diabetes management
title: Latent profiles analysis and associated factors of digital health literacy among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes.

text: . Guided by the health ecology model, a cross-sectional study was conducted among 504 hospitalized patients with diabetes aged 18-59 years from two tertiary hospitals in Anhui Province, China, between June 2025 and March 2026
title: Latent profiles analysis and associated factors of digital health literacy among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes.

text: . Data were collected using a general information questionnaire, the Digital Health Literacy Instrument, the Diabetes Self-Management Questionnaire, the Technophobia Scale, and the Social Support Rating Scale. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was used to identify DHL profiles
title: Latent profiles analysis and associated factors of digital health literacy among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes.

text: . LASSO regression was applied to screen candidate variables, and multinomial logistic regression was used to examine factors associated with profile membership. The mean DHLI score was 2.02 ± 0.61. LPA identified four profiles: limited DHL profile, basic application-low navigation profile, operational strength-limited critical appraisal profile, and high-level comprehensive DHL profile
title: Latent profiles analysis and associated factors of digital health literacy among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes.

text: . Multinomial logistic regression showed that age, educational level, residence, complications, mobile health tool use, daily internet use, online health information seeking, diversity of information sources, technophobia, and social support were significantly associated with DHL profile membership ( DHL among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes showed distinct profile characteristics in
title: Latent profiles analysis and associated factors of digital health literacy among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes.

text: showed distinct profile characteristics in information access, appraisal, interaction, and privacy protection
title: Latent profiles analysis and associated factors of digital health literacy among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes.

text: . These findings provide a basis for individualized health education and stratified health promotion strategies based on patients' DHL profiles in diabetes management.
title: Latent profiles analysis and associated factors of digital health literacy among young and middle-aged adults with diabetes.

text: Digital health solutions for chronic disease physical activity management: wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and public health implementation.. Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior are major modifiable risk factors in chronic disease management, yet conventional clinic-based follow-up is poorly suited to capture real-world behavioral dynamics or deliver timely personalized support
title: Digital health solutions for chronic disease physical activity management: wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and public health implementation.

text: . Wearable devices provide longitudinal data on steps, activity intensity, sedentary time, sleep, heart rate, and selected physiological signals, while artificial intelligence (AI) may support feedback personalization, risk prediction, dynamic goal setting, and remote coordination
title: Digital health solutions for chronic disease physical activity management: wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and public health implementation.

text: . This review synthesizes evidence on wearable- and AI-supported physical activity management across diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular disease, chronic respiratory disease, cancer survivorship, and older-adult multimorbidity
title: Digital health solutions for chronic disease physical activity management: wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and public health implementation.

text: . Current evidence most consistently supports improvements in behavioral outcomes, including steps, physical activity levels, self-monitoring, and in some cases sedentary behavior. Evidence for functional and intermediate clinical outcomes is promising but heterogeneous, while evidence for long-term clinical endpoints, cost-effectiveness, and health-system integration remains less definitive
title: Digital health solutions for chronic disease physical activity management: wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and public health implementation.

text: . AI-specific evidence remains comparatively early, heterogeneous, and often feasibility-oriented, so claims about AI-enabled benefit require cautious interpretation
title: Digital health solutions for chronic disease physical activity management: wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and public health implementation.

text: . The review argues that wearable devices and AI should not replace clinical care, but should be understood as components of digital public health closed loops that connect continuous sensing, personalized behavioral support, clinical actionability, governance, and equity
title: Digital health solutions for chronic disease physical activity management: wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and public health implementation.

text: . Future research should move beyond isolated devices or apps toward validating explainable, actionable, equitable, and sustainable digital intervention pathways in real chronic disease populations and health systems.
title: Digital health solutions for chronic disease physical activity management: wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and public health implementation.

text: Culturally adapting an evidence-based diabetes self-management education program for black adults: a pilot mixed methods implementation study.. Black adults in the United States disproportionately experience type 2 diabetes and related complications, yet participation in diabetes self-management education (DSME) is low. Culturally adapted approaches are needed to improve engagement and outcomes
title: Culturally adapting an evidence-based diabetes self-management education program for black adults: a pilot mixed methods implementation study.

text: . This pilot study evaluated the implementation of a co-designed culturally adapted DSME program for Black adults using the RE-AIM framework and Proctor's implementation outcomes. This pilot mixed-methods implementation study evaluated a culturally adapted 6-week group based DSME program delivered in community settings. Thirty-two Black adults with diabetes or prediabetes were enrolled
title: Culturally adapting an evidence-based diabetes self-management education program for black adults: a pilot mixed methods implementation study.

text: . Implementation outcomes included attendance, retention, and satisfaction. Participant-reported outcomes were assessed at baseline and 6 months, and qualitative interviews explored participant experiences. Retention was 100%, with high attendance (86%) and strong satisfaction, indicating high feasibility and acceptability
title: Culturally adapting an evidence-based diabetes self-management education program for black adults: a pilot mixed methods implementation study.

text: . Participants reported improvements in engagement, empowerment, and self-care behaviors. Qualitative findings highlighted the role of culturally affirming facilitation, trust and group support in promoting participation in DSME. Participants' mean age was 57; 81% were female, and 75% had type 2 diabetes
title: Culturally adapting an evidence-based diabetes self-management education program for black adults: a pilot mixed methods implementation study.

text: . text: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.. Cardiovascular diseases and metabolic disorders, including obesity and type 2 diabetes, remain leading global health challenges
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . Despite major advances in pharmacotherapy, the implementation of effective cardiometabolic prevention strategies remains suboptimal
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . Incretin-based therapies, particularly glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), have substantially transformed the management of metabolic diseases by providing benefits beyond glycaemic control, including sustained weight loss, improvements in metabolic parameters, and cardiovascular risk reduction
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . To evaluate Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk management, with particular emphasis on perceived effectiveness, safety, selected psychological and behavioural effects, and reimbursement. Cross-sectional online survey conducted among healthcare professionals in Poland between May and August 2025
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . A structured, anonymous online questionnaire was disseminated through professional, institutional, and academic communication channels in Poland. The questionnaire assessed self-reported perceptions, beliefs, perceived clinical value, perceived safety, and implementation-related views regarding GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk management
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . The final analytical sample included 1,100 healthcare professionals representing physicians, nurses, pharmacists, dietitians, and physiotherapists. Categorical responses were compared between professional groups using the chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between respondent characteristics and selected perceptions; adjusted odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and p-values were reported
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . The final analytical sample included 1,100 healthcare professionals: physicians (n = 164), pharmacists (n = 133), nurses (n = 160), physiotherapists (n = 361), and dietitians (n = 282). GLP-1 receptor agonists were most frequently rated as "very effective" for weight loss by physiotherapists (87.3%) and dietitians (84.8%), followed by nurses (59.4%) and physicians (52.4%)
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . Perceived safety was high across all groups, with GLP-1 receptor agonists considered safe by 94.0% of dietitians, 93.9% of physiotherapists, 87.2% of physicians, 85.0% of pharmacists, and 69.4% of nurses. Support for reimbursement was also high, ranging from 75.0% among nurses to 97.2% among dietitians
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . In multivariable analyses among physicians, employment in a diabetology or endocrinology setting was strongly associated with perceiving GLP-1 receptor agonists as very effective for weight reduction (adjusted OR 11.80, 95% CI 3.88-35.84; p < 0.001), as well as with perceived stress reduction (adjusted OR 2.71, 95% CI 1.05-7.02; p = 0.039), anxiety reduction (adjusted OR 7.00, 95% CI 2.01-24.42;
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: reduction (adjusted OR 7.00, 95% CI 2.01-24.42; p = 0.002), and improvement in depressive symptoms (adjusted OR 5.81, 95% CI 1.68-20.07; p = 0.005)
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . Among participating healthcare professionals in Poland, GLP-1 receptor agonists were generally perceived as effective and safe options for cardiometabolic risk management. Perceptions differed across professional groups, particularly regarding weight reduction, safety, psychological and behavioural effects, and reimbursement
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: . Because educational gaps, implementation barriers, real-world adoption, and interdisciplinary care models were not directly assessed as primary outcomes, these areas should be addressed in future studies using dedicated instruments.
title: Polish healthcare professionals' perceptions of GLP-1 receptor agonists in cardiometabolic risk reduction: a cross-sectional online survey in Poland.

text: Assessing Challenges and Barriers to Effective Wound Care in Rural Indigenous Communities.. To explore the lived experiences of patients with chronic wounds from a remote Indigenous community in Northern Manitoba, Canada, focusing on challenges in wound management, the impact on quality of life, barriers to wound care access, and the role of traditional healing practices
title: Assessing Challenges and Barriers to Effective Wound Care in Rural Indigenous Communities.

text: . A qualitative descriptive study was co-created with members of the Nisichawayasihk Cree Nation (NCN) and conducted in alignment with OCAP (Ownership, Control, Access, and Possession) principles. Fifteen participants with current or past chronic wounds participated in semi-structured, in-person interviews at the NCN Family and Community Wellness Centre in June 2024
title: Assessing Challenges and Barriers to Effective Wound Care in Rural Indigenous Communities.

text: . Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed inductively using NVivo to identify key thematic domains
title: Assessing Challenges and Barriers to Effective Wound Care in Rural Indigenous Communities.

text: . Five thematic domains emerged: (1) access to health care-limited local services, long wait times, and substantial travel and financial burden to obtain specialty care; (2) inadequate wound care-inconsistent follow-up and reliance on self-management at home; (3) patient education-focused largely on diabetes control with little wound-specific guidance; (4) living with pain-persistent pain limiting
title: Assessing Challenges and Barriers to Effective Wound Care in Rural Indigenous Communities.

text: (4) living with pain-persistent pain limiting mobility, sleep, and emotional well-being; and (5) traditional Indigenous medicine-frequent use of culturally rooted treatments, though often not acknowledged or integrated by Western providers
title: Assessing Challenges and Barriers to Effective Wound Care in Rural Indigenous Communities.

text: . Indigenous patients experience major barriers to timely, effective wound care, driven by geographic isolation, fragmented services, and gaps in patient education. Integrating traditional healing with Western practice, strengthening community-based care pathways, and improving specialist access may support limb preservation, reduce preventable amputation, and enhance quality of life.
title: Assessing Challenges and Barriers to Effective Wound Care in Rural Indigenous Communities.

text: Experience of diabetes self-care and well-being among adults with type 2 diabetes in South Ethiopia: a qualitative descriptive study.. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) poses an escalating challenge in resource-limited settings where daily self-care practices are often compromised. The everyday realities of individuals with T2DM in Sub-Saharan Africa remain insufficiently understood
title: Experience of diabetes self-care and well-being among adults with type 2 diabetes in South Ethiopia: a qualitative descriptive study.
journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being

text: . This study explored self-care experiences among adults with T2DM in South Ethiopia, focusing on factors shaping their daily lives and well-being. A qualitative descriptive design with reflexive thematic analysis was employed. In-depth interviews were conducted with 21 purposefully selected participants (12 patients, 9 providers) from three hospitals in South Ethiopia
title: Experience of diabetes self-care and well-being among adults with type 2 diabetes in South Ethiopia: a qualitative descriptive study.
journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being

text: . Provider interviews provided complementary contextual information about health system barriers. Well-being, from participants' perspectives, was defined by the ability to maintain daily activities, fulfill family roles, and sustain hope
title: Experience of diabetes self-care and well-being among adults with type 2 diabetes in South Ethiopia: a qualitative descriptive study.
journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being

text: . Analysis of patient interviews yielded four major themes capturing the experience of self-care: 1) Navigating daily self-care routines (medication intake, diet management, self-monitoring, and foot care); 2) Multilevel barriers eroding well-being (medication stock-outs, economic constraints, cultural beliefs, lack of support, knowledge gaps, provider training deficits); 3) Education and
title: Experience of diabetes self-care and well-being among adults with type 2 diabetes in South Ethiopia: a qualitative descriptive study.
journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being

text: provider training deficits); 3) Education and counselling as sources of empowerment (building knowledge, instilling hope); and 4) Envisioning supportive environments (continued counselling, medication availability, peer support)
title: Experience of diabetes self-care and well-being among adults with type 2 diabetes in South Ethiopia: a qualitative descriptive study.
journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being

text: . Healthcare provider interviews provided complementary contextual information about health system barriers. For individuals with T2DM in South Ethiopia, self-care involves daily negotiation shaped by economic hardship, cultural factors, and health system limitations
title: Experience of diabetes self-care and well-being among adults with type 2 diabetes in South Ethiopia: a qualitative descriptive study.
journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being

text: . Empowering patients through tailored support, continued counselling, peer support network, and reliable healthcare systems is essential for enhancing their health and well-being.
title: Experience of diabetes self-care and well-being among adults with type 2 diabetes in South Ethiopia: a qualitative descriptive study.

text: Effects of Peer-Based Experiential Education on Psychosocial Adaptation in Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.. Adolescents with Type 1 diabetes face significant challenges in achieving effective self-management and maintaining psychosocial well-being
title: Effects of Peer-Based Experiential Education on Psychosocial Adaptation in Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . Peer-based and participatory health education approaches, grounded in Social Learning Theory, may strengthen adolescents' motivation, confidence, and experiential learning in diabetes care
title: Effects of Peer-Based Experiential Education on Psychosocial Adaptation in Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a peer-based participatory health education program on psychosocial adaptation outcomes - self-efficacy, illness attitudes, and diabetes knowledge - and to explore its short-term effects on glycemic control among adolescents with Type 1 diabetes
title: Effects of Peer-Based Experiential Education on Psychosocial Adaptation in Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

title: Effects of Peer-Based Experiential Education on Psychosocial Adaptation in Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . Participants were randomly allocated to an intervention group ( Adolescents in the intervention group showed significantly higher posttest scores for self-efficacy, illness attitudes, and diabetes knowledge compared with the control group ( Peer-based participatory health education improved psychosocial outcomes among adolescents with Type 1 diabetes
title: Effects of Peer-Based Experiential Education on Psychosocial Adaptation in Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . Incorporating peer interaction and experiential learning into diabetes education programs may strengthen psychosocial adaptation and support the foundations of effective self-management.
title: Effects of Peer-Based Experiential Education on Psychosocial Adaptation in Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: Knowledge and practices related to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease among university students in Bangladesh.. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a growing public health concern associated with obesity, diabetes, and metabolic syndromes. However, awareness and preventive behaviors remain understudied among young adults in low- and middle-income countries
title: Knowledge and practices related to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease among university students in Bangladesh.

text: . This cross-sectional study assesses knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to NAFLD. This study is carried out among 343 university students (predominantly undergraduate students, mean age 24.6 years) at the Islamic University of Technology(IUT), Bangladesh. Even with 76.1% awareness, knowledge was very poor (39.1%) or moderate (40.2%)
title: Knowledge and practices related to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease among university students in Bangladesh.

text: . This shows significant gaps in understanding risk factors, treatment, prevention, and a strong dependence on informal information sources. Knowledge was particularly associated with age, region, and educational level. Preventive measures were extremely low, with only 11.1% followed by dieting restrictions and 31.2% making lifestyle changes
title: Knowledge and practices related to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease among university students in Bangladesh.

title: Knowledge and practices related to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease among university students in Bangladesh.

text: Nurse-Led Interventions on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management for Minority Ethnic Groups in World Health Organisation European Region: A Scoping Review.. To map the available evidence on nurse-led interventions on type 2 diabetes management for minority ethnic groups in the World Health Organisation (WHO) European region
title: Nurse-Led Interventions on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management for Minority Ethnic Groups in World Health Organisation European Region: A Scoping Review.

text: . Although research on nurse-led interventions for type 2 diabetes mellitus is well-established, the extent of nurse-led interventions for minority ethnic groups in the World Health Organisation (WHO) European region is not well explored. Scoping review design according to Joanna Briggs institute (JBI)
title: Nurse-Led Interventions on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management for Minority Ethnic Groups in World Health Organisation European Region: A Scoping Review.

text: . A systematic search of published English articles was carried out in 6 electronic databases (PubMed, CINAHL, MEDLINE, Sabinet, Scopus, EBSCO host) and 2 search engines (Google, Google Scholar)
title: Nurse-Led Interventions on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management for Minority Ethnic Groups in World Health Organisation European Region: A Scoping Review.

text: . Population (minority ethnic groups with type 2 diabetes mellitus), Concept (nurse-led interventions), and Context (World Health Organisation European region) were used to define the inclusion and exclusion criteria. The three-step search strategy was used to find 322 eligible articles. The identified articles were imported into the Systematic Review Web app, Rayyan, in preparation for selection
title: Nurse-Led Interventions on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management for Minority Ethnic Groups in World Health Organisation European Region: A Scoping Review.

text: . The selection process involved the title and abstract initially followed by full text screening of potentially relevant papers. Fourteen (14) articles were included. Results showed minimal relevant publications per year between 2006 and 2018; an increase between 2019 and 2021 (n = 5), with a greater number from the UK (n = 7)
title: Nurse-Led Interventions on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management for Minority Ethnic Groups in World Health Organisation European Region: A Scoping Review.

text: . Four studies were reviews, followed by quantitative (n = 4), qualitative (n = 4),and mixed methods (n = 2)
title: Nurse-Led Interventions on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management for Minority Ethnic Groups in World Health Organisation European Region: A Scoping Review.

text: . The implemented nurse-led interventions included culturally sensitive (n = 5), Self-management (n = 3), community based enhanced care package (n = 2), psychological (n = 1), web and mHealth technologies (n = 1), Group-based diabetes education model (n = 1), Type 2 diabetes lifestyle (n = 1)
title: Nurse-Led Interventions on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management for Minority Ethnic Groups in World Health Organisation European Region: A Scoping Review.

text: . Findings suggest that nurse-led interventions on type 2 diabetes management improve self-care knowledge, skills, and behaviour change. In addition, patients are empowered, and this improves non-pharmacological lifestyle change. Furthermore, it improves the knowledge and skills of nurses in type 2 diabetes management
title: Nurse-Led Interventions on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management for Minority Ethnic Groups in World Health Organisation European Region: A Scoping Review.

text: . This review will promote the development of culturally specific interventions for type 2 diabetes mellitus for ethnic minority groups in the United Kingdom. This will enhance proper care and improve the quality of life among the population affected. No patient or public contribution. Open Science Framework; https://doi.org/10.17605/osf.10/4D6Q9.
title: Nurse-Led Interventions on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management for Minority Ethnic Groups in World Health Organisation European Region: A Scoping Review.

text: Digital Health Technology Use by Vietnamese Americans: Cross-Sectional Study.. Digital health technologies (DHTs), including mobile health (mHealth) apps and online medical records, are increasingly being used to support self-management and communication with health care professionals among the general population across the United States
title: Digital Health Technology Use by Vietnamese Americans: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . However, few studies have explored whether cultural, privacy, and sociodemographic factors may influence DHT adoption among Vietnamese Americans specifically. This cross-sectional study aimed to explore DHT use, barriers to adoption, and their associations with social determinants, such as age, sex, social support, and mental health concerns, among Vietnamese Americans
title: Digital Health Technology Use by Vietnamese Americans: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Data were collected from a sample of Vietnamese American adults (n=304) through surveys assessing DHT engagement, confidence in medical record security, and social and psychological factors. Descriptive statistics and inferential analyses, including 2-tailed t tests and chi-square tests, were used to examine differences across demographic groups
title: Digital Health Technology Use by Vietnamese Americans: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Many participants had engaged with mHealth tools (253/304, 83.2%), including using mobile devices for health tracking (185/302, 60.9%), and health care professional discussions (194/301, 64.5%). Online medical records were reported to be widely available (230/304, 75.7%), with a large proportion of the participants (182/227, 80.2%) accessing them at least once in the past year
title: Digital Health Technology Use by Vietnamese Americans: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Privacy concerns were a key barrier to using online medical records, with 40.5% (17/42) of nonusers citing security fears, and 26.6% (81/304) reporting withholding health information from health care professionals
title: Digital Health Technology Use by Vietnamese Americans: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . The main reasons participants did not access online medical records (45/304, 14.8%) were that they preferred to speak to health care professionals directly (31/44, 70.5%) or did not perceive a need to access their online medical records (30/43, 69.8%). There were no statistically significant differences in sociodemographic characteristics between DHT users and nonusers
title: Digital Health Technology Use by Vietnamese Americans: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . There were statistically significant differences in the levels of social support of participants who had varying levels of confidence in the security of their medical records (F2,301=10.19; P<.001; η²=0.063)
title: Digital Health Technology Use by Vietnamese Americans: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . A greater proportion of male participants reported distrust (ie, being "not confident" in the security of their medical records) than female participants (χ22=20.8; P<.001), indicating a significant association between sex and confidence level. While DHT adoption is high among Vietnamese Americans, privacy concerns remain a major barrier to full use of online medical records
title: Digital Health Technology Use by Vietnamese Americans: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: . Health care professionals and public health initiatives should focus on improving trust in medical record security, incorporating culturally tailored education on the benefits of digital health, and leveraging social media and mHealth tools to optimize patient engagement. Developing stronger family and community support may facilitate the adoption of DHTs.
title: Digital Health Technology Use by Vietnamese Americans: Cross-Sectional Study.

text: Empowering patients to take charge of their kidney health: a healthcare staff perspective in the UK.. Self-management is an essential component in the effective management of people living with chronic kidney disease (CKD)
title: Empowering patients to take charge of their kidney health: a healthcare staff perspective in the UK.

text: . While self-management is part of practice guidelines, there is limited understanding of healthcare professionals' views on self-management and how patient self-management is supported and integrated in everyday clinical practice
title: Empowering patients to take charge of their kidney health: a healthcare staff perspective in the UK.

text: . This qualitative study explored healthcare professionals' perspectives on self-management in CKD, including current clinical practices and the requirements for providing effective self-management support. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with a range of healthcare professionals working in the National Health Service (NHS) in the UK
title: Empowering patients to take charge of their kidney health: a healthcare staff perspective in the UK.

text: . Topics explored perspectives and experiences of self-management support, lifestyle and education in practice. Interviews were audio recorded, transcribed and analysed using thematic analysis to analyse the data and report themes. Forty-two healthcare professionals were interviewed, and four overarching themes were identified
title: Empowering patients to take charge of their kidney health: a healthcare staff perspective in the UK.

text: . The themes reflected healthcare professionals' perceptions on CKD self-management, which were: (1) "the problem with the healthcare landscape in CKD self-management", (2) need for a personalised approach to CKD management, (3) how to improve self--management support resources, and (4) considerations to improve health equity
title: Empowering patients to take charge of their kidney health: a healthcare staff perspective in the UK.

text: . The healthcare professionals perceived that the healthcare structure within the NHS does not adequately support self-management, with a notable lack of accessible self-management resources, suggesting a need for evidence-based self-management interventions in CKD that are tailored responsively to individual needs
title: Empowering patients to take charge of their kidney health: a healthcare staff perspective in the UK.

text: . While these findings arise from the UK context, the issues identified are likely to be relevant and applicable to healthcare systems in other countries.
title: Empowering patients to take charge of their kidney health: a healthcare staff perspective in the UK.

text: Barriers and facilitators to insulin management in pregnant people with gestational diabetes mellitus: A qualitative study.. To explore barriers and facilitators to gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) self-management and insulin use, aiming to inform future interventions, in a diverse population of pregnant people
title: Barriers and facilitators to insulin management in pregnant people with gestational diabetes mellitus: A qualitative study.

text: . In this ancillary study of an ongoing randomized controlled trial testing thresholds for insulin initiation for GDM, participants in the parent trial were recruited from February 2023 to January 2024. Purposive sampling was used to recruit diverse participants with respect to age, race, ethnicity, insurance status, parity, and insulin use
title: Barriers and facilitators to insulin management in pregnant people with gestational diabetes mellitus: A qualitative study.

text: . In-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted after 34 weeks' gestation. Interview guides addressed topics related to pregnancy with GDM; this analysis focused on experiences with insulin and adherence to their treatment plan. Transcripts were analyzed using a reflexive thematic analysis approach to develop themes
title: Barriers and facilitators to insulin management in pregnant people with gestational diabetes mellitus: A qualitative study.

text: . Of 20 participants, 80% had GDM for the first time and 50% required insulin treatment. Analysis identified key barriers and facilitators to treatment plan adherence
title: Barriers and facilitators to insulin management in pregnant people with gestational diabetes mellitus: A qualitative study.

text: . Barriers included: (1) fear of insulin ("When I was first told about it, I threw a tantrum… I do not like needles, and that's all I could think about."), (2) the time and cognitive effort to learn self-management, (3) managing emotions related to GDM diagnosis and self-management with insulin, and both (4) jobs and (5) family/friends unawareness made it difficult to manage GDM as recommended
title: Barriers and facilitators to insulin management in pregnant people with gestational diabetes mellitus: A qualitative study.

text: . Facilitators included (1) training from the medical team ("once I saw my insulin pen, it wasn't that bad."), (2) support from family/friends, and (3) concern for the well-being of the fetus. Self-management of GDM requires substantial social and institutional support, learning, and adjusting to a new lifestyle in a short period of time
title: Barriers and facilitators to insulin management in pregnant people with gestational diabetes mellitus: A qualitative study.

text: . For some, the recommendation to use insulin caused a strong negative reaction, but hands-on education provided by the medical team helped to alleviate fear and other barriers.
title: Barriers and facilitators to insulin management in pregnant people with gestational diabetes mellitus: A qualitative study.

text: Understanding patient perspectives on glycemic control: A mixed methods study of diverse patients with gestational diabetes.. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) increases risk for adverse health outcomes and disproportionately affects racial and ethnic minority populations
title: Understanding patient perspectives on glycemic control: A mixed methods study of diverse patients with gestational diabetes.

text: . Achieving optimal glycemic control during pregnancy mitigates risks but requires consistent blood glucose monitoring, diet, physical activity, and, when needed, medication adherence
title: Understanding patient perspectives on glycemic control: A mixed methods study of diverse patients with gestational diabetes.

text: . To identify barriers and facilitators of GDM treatment adherence among racially and ethnically diverse patients with suboptimal glycemic control (<80% of glucose values/week within goal) or monitoring (<14 measurements/week) in their most recent GDM-affected pregnancy
title: Understanding patient perspectives on glycemic control: A mixed methods study of diverse patients with gestational diabetes.

text: . Using a convergent parallel mixed methods design guided by the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) framework, we collected quantitative data using validated online survey tools and conducted racially concordant virtual focus groups. Forty participants (25% Asian, 18% Black, 20% Hispanic, 23% White, 15% multiracial) completed surveys; 28 joined focus groups
title: Understanding patient perspectives on glycemic control: A mixed methods study of diverse patients with gestational diabetes.

text: . Self-reported adherence was 55% for glucose monitoring, 70% for diet, and 45% for physical activity. Among those prescribed medication (n=26), 85% reported taking it as prescribed, with higher adherence for insulin (90%) than oral agents (67%)
title: Understanding patient perspectives on glycemic control: A mixed methods study of diverse patients with gestational diabetes.

text: . Barriers included unsupportive workplaces, discomfort with fingersticks, limited time for activity, and frustration when goals were unmet despite perceived adherence. While 85% reported food security, participants wanted greater nutritional support from family and community. Preferences for holistic and less invasive management, including continuous glucose monitors, were expressed
title: Understanding patient perspectives on glycemic control: A mixed methods study of diverse patients with gestational diabetes.

text: . Patients with suboptimal glycemic control or monitoring reported barriers such as workplace constraints, limited nutritional resources, and invasive treatments. Patient-centered education, community support, and expanded treatment options may improve adherence and outcomes in diverse populations with GDM.
title: Understanding patient perspectives on glycemic control: A mixed methods study of diverse patients with gestational diabetes.

text: Healthcare-community partnership to improve nutrition insecurity for optimal glycaemic control and pregnancy outcomes in women with pregestational diabetes: clinical trial protocol for the NOURISH study.. Pregestational diabetes is one of the most frequent medical conditions in pregnancy
title: Healthcare-community partnership to improve nutrition insecurity for optimal glycaemic control and pregnancy outcomes in women with pregestational diabetes: clinical trial protocol for the NOURISH study.

text: . Nutrition insecurity is a non-medical, health-related social need and affects glycaemic management and pregnancy outcomes for women with both type 1 and type 2 pregestational diabetes
title: Healthcare-community partnership to improve nutrition insecurity for optimal glycaemic control and pregnancy outcomes in women with pregestational diabetes: clinical trial protocol for the NOURISH study.

text: . Collaborative healthcare-community partnerships to enhance food access, facilitate culinary medicine, diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) and address unmet social needs for pregnant women with pregestational diabetes remain to be evaluated
title: Healthcare-community partnership to improve nutrition insecurity for optimal glycaemic control and pregnancy outcomes in women with pregestational diabetes: clinical trial protocol for the NOURISH study.

text: . In a two-arm randomised controlled trial, we will examine the combined effects of a tripartite NOURISH intervention ((1) produce home delivery, (2) culinary medicine with DSMES and (3) community health worker-led social needs assessment and support) versus the current standard of diabetes and prenatal care
title: Healthcare-community partnership to improve nutrition insecurity for optimal glycaemic control and pregnancy outcomes in women with pregestational diabetes: clinical trial protocol for the NOURISH study.

text: . We will recruit and enrol 174 pregnant women (87 NOURISH, 87 standard care) ≤22+6 weeks of gestation with pregestational diabetes, inadequate glycaemic management (haemoglobin A1c≥6.5%) and self-reported risk of food insecurity from a diabetes and prenatal care programme at a tertiary care academic health system located in the USA
title: Healthcare-community partnership to improve nutrition insecurity for optimal glycaemic control and pregnancy outcomes in women with pregestational diabetes: clinical trial protocol for the NOURISH study.

text: . We will measure the primary outcome of glycaemic management by delivery (haemoglobin A1c<6.5%), and secondarily, adverse pregnancy outcomes (gestational weight gain and composite neonatal morbidity) and patient-reported outcomes (nutrition security)
title: Healthcare-community partnership to improve nutrition insecurity for optimal glycaemic control and pregnancy outcomes in women with pregestational diabetes: clinical trial protocol for the NOURISH study.

text: . We will also use cost-effectiveness analysis to assess the intervention's value relative to standard care and use process evaluation to characterise intervention and contextual factors influencing uptake, effectiveness and sustainability. The Institutional Review Board at The Ohio State University approved this study (IRB: STUDY20260307; date: 23 April 2026)
title: Healthcare-community partnership to improve nutrition insecurity for optimal glycaemic control and pregnancy outcomes in women with pregestational diabetes: clinical trial protocol for the NOURISH study.

text: . We plan to submit results of the trial for publication in peer-reviewed journals and presentations at international scientific meetings. NCT07560813.
title: Healthcare-community partnership to improve nutrition insecurity for optimal glycaemic control and pregnancy outcomes in women with pregestational diabetes: clinical trial protocol for the NOURISH study.

text: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.. BackgroundGestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) presents significant psychological and behavioural challenges, with diagnosis often triggering stress, anxiety, and fear
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: . Despite these burdens, structured psychosocial support remains limited within existing GDM care
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: . Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) show promise for reducing distress in perinatal contexts, but few are tailored to the unique needs of individuals with GDM, and digital delivery remains rare.ObjectivesThis study aimed to develop a digitally delivered mindfulness programme tailored to the psychological needs of individuals with GDM using a user-centred, multi-phase design approach.DesignA
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: user-centred, multi-phase design approach.DesignA qualitative, multi-phase participatory design study involving needs assessment and co-design workshops, guided by the Obesity-Related Behavioural Intervention Trials (ORBIT) model for behavioural intervention development and Loucks et al.'s evidence-based adaptation framework for Mindfulness-Based Programmes (MBPs).MethodsA qualitative needs
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: Programmes (MBPs).MethodsA qualitative needs assessment was conducted through focus groups with individuals with GDM (n=11) and healthcare professionals (n=4) to identify psychological experiences, mental health support, and the feasibility of a digital mindfulness intervention
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: . Findings informed the initial mindfulness programme framework, which was further refined through participatory co-design workshops (n=10) and iterative tailoring of scripts and multimedia content.ResultsParticipants reported high levels of emotional distress following GDM diagnosis, citing a strong desire for brief, flexible, and supportive psychosocial interventions
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: . Co-design feedback highlighted preferences for short audio-guided sessions, soft and calming voice characteristics, and seamless integration into daily routines
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: . The final one-month programme comprised 20 mindfulness exercises, delivered via audio and video for integration within a holistic GDM self-management app.ConclusionA systematically developed, contextually relevant digital mindfulness programme may address critical gaps in GDM care, supporting psychological well-being and self-management
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: . Gestational diabetes (GDM) can be stressful and overwhelming, as people are asked to manage blood sugar levels, diet, and medical appointments during pregnancy. Emotional support is not always included as part of routine GDM care, even though stress and anxiety are common and can affect daily self-management
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: . This study describes how a digital mindfulness programme was developed specifically for people with GDM. Mindfulness involves simple practices, such as guided breathing and awareness exercises, that can help people manage stress and feel calmer. Using a user-centred approach, individuals with GDM and healthcare professionals were involved at every stage of development
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: . Their feedback helped shape the content, length, and delivery of the programme to ensure it was practical, supportive, and easy to use during pregnancy. The final programme includes short, flexible audio and video mindfulness sessions designed to fit into daily routines without adding extra pressure
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: . This work shows that tailored digital mindfulness programmes are feasible and may help address an important gap in emotional support for people living with gestational diabetes.
title: Integrating psychological support into gestational diabetes self-management: Development of a user-centred digital mindfulness programme.

text: The influence of emotions and healthcare provider interactions on self-management behavior and HbA1c in Korean patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional descriptive study.
title: The influence of emotions and healthcare provider interactions on self-management behavior and HbA1c in Korean patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional descriptive study.
journal: Journal of Korean biological nursing science

text: . This study examined the effects of emotional experiences and interactions with healthcare providers on self-management behaviors and glycemic control, as measured by hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. This cross-sectional study included 120 patients recruited from six local clinics between April 12 and July 15, 2021
title: The influence of emotions and healthcare provider interactions on self-management behavior and HbA1c in Korean patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional descriptive study.
journal: Journal of Korean biological nursing science

text: . Data were collected using the Scale of Positive and Negative Experience, the Client Satisfaction Tool, the Summary of Diabetes Self-Care Activities Questionnaire, and HbA1c measurements. title: The influence of emotions and healthcare provider interactions on self-management behavior and HbA1c in Korean patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional descriptive study.
journal: Journal of Korean biological nursing science

text: Mediating effect of health literacy on the relationship between diabetes status and aerobic physical activity adherence among middle-aged Korean adults: a theory-based secondary analysis of the second year of the ninth Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
title: Mediating effect of health literacy on the relationship between diabetes status and aerobic physical activity adherence among middle-aged Korean adults: a theory-based secondary analysis of the second year of the ninth Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
journal: Journal of Korean biological nursing science

text: . This study applied Orem's self-care theory to examine differences in adherence to aerobic physical activity according to diabetes status among middle-aged adults and to evaluate the mediating effect of health literacy. By distinguishing between diabetes and prediabetes, the study aimed to reflect the stepwise nature of self-care demand while conceptualizing health literacy as a self-care agent
title: Mediating effect of health literacy on the relationship between diabetes status and aerobic physical activity adherence among middle-aged Korean adults: a theory-based secondary analysis of the second year of the ninth Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
journal: Journal of Korean biological nursing science

text: . A secondary analysis was conducted using data from the second year of the ninth Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. The study included 2,781 adults aged 40-64 years. Variables were constructed based on Orem's self-care theory. Complex sample hierarchical logistic regression and mediation analyses were conducted using SPSS version 28.0 and R version 4.4.2
title: Mediating effect of health literacy on the relationship between diabetes status and aerobic physical activity adherence among middle-aged Korean adults: a theory-based secondary analysis of the second year of the ninth Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
journal: Journal of Korean biological nursing science

text: . Among the participants, 14.3% had diabetes and 34.1% had prediabetes. Higher educational attainment and personal income were significantly associated with adherence to aerobic physical activity. Diabetes status was significantly associated with decreased adherence, whereas prediabetes status showed no significant association. Health literacy was positively associated with adherence
title: Mediating effect of health literacy on the relationship between diabetes status and aerobic physical activity adherence among middle-aged Korean adults: a theory-based secondary analysis of the second year of the ninth Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
journal: Journal of Korean biological nursing science

text: . Mediation analysis indicated that health literacy partially mediated the negative effects of diabetes and prediabetes on adherence to aerobic physical activity. By empirically applying Orem's self-care theory, this study identified differences in adherence to aerobic physical activity according to diabetes status and demonstrated the critical role of health literacy as a self-care agent
title: Mediating effect of health literacy on the relationship between diabetes status and aerobic physical activity adherence among middle-aged Korean adults: a theory-based secondary analysis of the second year of the ninth Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
journal: Journal of Korean biological nursing science

text: . These findings suggest that nursing interventions for diabetes prevention and management should adopt stratified approaches based on health status, with an emphasis on enhancing health literacy and strengthening self-care behaviors.
title: Mediating effect of health literacy on the relationship between diabetes status and aerobic physical activity adherence among middle-aged Korean adults: a theory-based secondary analysis of the second year of the ninth Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
