text: Financial incentives and health coaching to improve glycemic outcomes among young adults with type 1 diabetes: A factorial randomized trial (SweetGoals).. This study aimed to improve glycemic control among young adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D), an at-risk and understudied population
title: Financial incentives and health coaching to improve glycemic outcomes among young adults with type 1 diabetes: A factorial randomized trial (SweetGoals).

text: . N = 300 young adults with T1D recruited nationally were randomized to the factorial combination of (1) financial incentives targeting glucose checking and mealtime behaviors and (2) web health coaching focused on increasing motivation and goal setting for self-management behaviors. All received a smartphone app that accessed device data and provided weekly goal feedback
title: Financial incentives and health coaching to improve glycemic outcomes among young adults with type 1 diabetes: A factorial randomized trial (SweetGoals).

text: . The intervention lasted 6 months. HbA1c (A1c) was assessed at baseline, +6 months, and +12 months. The mean number of glucose checking and mealtime goals met per week during the intervention were tested as mediators of intervention effects on A1c at 12 months. A1c was significantly reduced from baseline to +12 months across all participants
title: Financial incentives and health coaching to improve glycemic outcomes among young adults with type 1 diabetes: A factorial randomized trial (SweetGoals).

text: . Indirect effects of both incentives and coaching on A1c reductions were significant and partially mediated by mealtime but not glucose checking goal achievement. There was no synergistic (interaction) effect of incentives and coaching. Incentives and coaching both improved critical mealtime behavior but through different strategies
title: Financial incentives and health coaching to improve glycemic outcomes among young adults with type 1 diabetes: A factorial randomized trial (SweetGoals).

text: . These results suggest that either intervention would be suitable for future testing and dissemination, and that lower cost of incentives may favor their prioritization.
title: Financial incentives and health coaching to improve glycemic outcomes among young adults with type 1 diabetes: A factorial randomized trial (SweetGoals).

text: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.. Sustaining self-management is critical for optimizing clinical outcomes in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . Although digital health interventions (DHIs) have shown benefits for glycemic control and self-care, much of this evidence has focused on efficacy, and the behavioral mechanisms through which DHIs produce sustained effects remain insufficiently understood. Clarifying these mechanisms could inform the development of theory-driven interventions
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . This study examined the longitudinal behavioral pathways through which Artificial Intelligence-based Health Education Accurately Linking System, a WeChat (Tencent)-based digital health program, influences T2DM self-management, using the Extended Multi-Theory Model (MTM) of health behavior change
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . An explanatory sequential mixed methods prospective longitudinal cohort study was conducted among adults with T2DM (aged ≥18 y and proficient in WeChat use), recruited from 45 primary health care institutions in Beijing, China, between July 2023 and July 2024
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . Self-management behavior was assessed as the primary outcome using the Summary of Diabetes Self-Care Activities, and psychosocial determinants using the Extended MTM Scale and the Diabetes-related Skills Scale. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses assessed the construct validity of the Extended MTM Scale
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . Structural equation modeling examined longitudinal pathways among Artificial Intelligence-based Health Education Accurately Linking System users across baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . For the qualitative phase, a purposive subsample was selected through maximum variation sampling based on baseline glycated hemoglobin; interviews were analyzed thematically until thematic saturation, and integrated with quantitative findings using a joint display. Of the 406 enrolled participants, 391 completed baseline assessments
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . The Extended MTM Scale demonstrated a 6-factor, 22-item structure with excellent internal consistency (Cronbach α=0.928) and satisfactory construct validity. The structural equation modeling showed satisfactory fit (CFI=0.984, RMSEA=0.036)
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . Changes in the social environment (β=0.23, 95% CI 0.07-0.38; P=.003) and physical environment (β=0.25, 95% CI 0.10-0.40; P=.001) at baseline, and diabetes-related skills at month 6 (β=0.16, 95% CI 0.03-0.29; P=.01), were directly associated with self-management behavior at month 12, whereas behavioral confidence and emotional transformation showed no significant direct effects
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . Social environment changes were indirectly associated with behavioral confidence through participatory dialogue at month 3 (β=0.20, 95% CI 0.04-0.36; P=.01; β=0.66, 95% CI 0.57-0.74; P<.001). Thematic analysis of 17 interviews identified 3 domains: environmental context, cognitive processes, and attitudes and skills
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . Environmental factors converged across both data strands, while qualitative data expanded on the cognitive and attitudinal processes underlying sustained self-management. This study is among the first to apply the Extended MTM framework to DHI-supported T2DM self-management, with environmental factors emerging as key drivers alongside selected cognitive, attitudinal, and skills-related processes
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: . Complementing efficacy-focused research, it illuminates the psychosocial pathways underlying sustained self-management and refines the Extended MTM in digital health contexts. These insights can inform the design of theory-driven DHIs in primary care.
title: Behavioral Mechanisms of a Digital Health Intervention for Self-Management in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.

text: Perceived Competence and GLP-1RA Weight Management Engagement: Mixed-Methods Insights From Six Patient Groups.. This study aimed to explore patients' perspectives on GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for weight loss across the continuum of contemplating use to discontinuation, with and without achieving weight loss goals
title: Perceived Competence and GLP-1RA Weight Management Engagement: Mixed-Methods Insights From Six Patient Groups.

text: . From June to October 2025, participants completed a 30-item survey and ~30-question semi-structured interview regarding their perceptions of GLP-1RAs for weight loss
title: Perceived Competence and GLP-1RA Weight Management Engagement: Mixed-Methods Insights From Six Patient Groups.

text: . Interviews were tailored to six GLP-1RA groups: (1) considering use; (2) < 3 months on therapy; (3) ≥ 3 months on therapy without achieving weight loss goal; (4) ≥ 3 months on therapy with achieving weight loss goal; (5) discontinued without achieving goal; and (6) discontinued after achieving goal
title: Perceived Competence and GLP-1RA Weight Management Engagement: Mixed-Methods Insights From Six Patient Groups.

text: . Qualitative coding and thematic analysis were conducted in Dedoose (9.0.107); quantitative analyses used SAS 9.4. A total of 185 participants consented, and 141 completed data collection (76%). Descriptive profiles suggested heterogeneity across psychosocial and behavioral domains. Groups 3 and 4 showed stronger profiles (higher perceived competence, intrinsic motivation, and self-monitoring)
title: Perceived Competence and GLP-1RA Weight Management Engagement: Mixed-Methods Insights From Six Patient Groups.

text: . After false discovery rate adjustment across 78 comparisons, perceived competence was the only statistically significant differentiator: Group 1 was lower (z = -3.15; q = 0.0347) and Group 4 higher (z = 4.44; q < 0.001). Findings underscore the importance of tailoring behavioral support to individuals' stage of engagement in GLP-1RA-supported weight loss journeys.
title: Perceived Competence and GLP-1RA Weight Management Engagement: Mixed-Methods Insights From Six Patient Groups.

text: Perceived Barriers and Needs Related to Chronic Disease Self-Management among Rural Appalachian Kentucky Residents.. In rural Appalachian Kentucky, managing chronic conditions presents a challenge due to limited healthcare access, inadequate health education, and poor dietary resources
title: Perceived Barriers and Needs Related to Chronic Disease Self-Management among Rural Appalachian Kentucky Residents.

text: . This study explores factors contributing to healthcare barriers and examines how social support may help individuals better manage chronic illness. We interviewed residents of rural Appalachian Kentucky and asked them to describe resources that helped or hindered their access to adequate health care and identify qualities essential for an effective healthcare leader
title: Perceived Barriers and Needs Related to Chronic Disease Self-Management among Rural Appalachian Kentucky Residents.

text: . Thematic analysis was used to identify recurring patterns related to healthcare barriers, resources needed for self-management, and social support and its role in managing chronic illness. Among the 79 interviewees, most were long-term residents of the region, and approximately half were currently employed
title: Perceived Barriers and Needs Related to Chronic Disease Self-Management among Rural Appalachian Kentucky Residents.

text: . Barriers to chronic disease management included distrust of medical professionals, limited health education, restricted access to care, and challenges with affordability and transportation. Participants cited a need for both general health education and diabetes mellitus-specific education. This study highlighted significant barriers to the management of chronic illness in Appalachian Kentucky
title: Perceived Barriers and Needs Related to Chronic Disease Self-Management among Rural Appalachian Kentucky Residents.

text: . Strong existing community bonds present an opportunity to improve outcomes. Such programs could leverage local support networks to enhance self-management for chronic diseases, including type 2 diabetes mellitus.
title: Perceived Barriers and Needs Related to Chronic Disease Self-Management among Rural Appalachian Kentucky Residents.

text: A Serious Digital Game (SugarVita) to Support Diabetes Self-Management: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.. Serious digital games have been proposed as a novel approach to support diabetes education and self-management, but evidence regarding their effectiveness remains limited
title: A Serious Digital Game (SugarVita) to Support Diabetes Self-Management: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . This study aimed to evaluate the effects of SugarVita, a serious game for people with type 2 diabetes, on diabetes-related knowledge, self-confidence, and self-management. Secondary outcomes included hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), engagement, and user evaluation
title: A Serious Digital Game (SugarVita) to Support Diabetes Self-Management: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . In this pilot randomized controlled trial, 30 adults with type 2 diabetes were randomized to SugarVita plus standard care or standard care alone for 8 weeks. Outcomes were assessed before and after the intervention using validated questionnaires and laboratory HbA1c values
title: A Serious Digital Game (SugarVita) to Support Diabetes Self-Management: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . Within-group changes were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and between-group differences using Mann-Whitney U tests. Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple primary outcomes. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed for diabetes-related knowledge, self-confidence, or self-management after correction for multiple testing
title: A Serious Digital Game (SugarVita) to Support Diabetes Self-Management: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . Both groups showed numerical improvements over time. HbA1c decreased significantly within the intervention group (median 73.0, IQR 70.8-81.5 to median 64.5, IQR 60.8-72.0 mmol/mol; P=.007), whereas no significant change was observed in the control group. Greater total playtime was moderately associated with HbA1c reduction. User evaluations indicated high perceived educational value
title: A Serious Digital Game (SugarVita) to Support Diabetes Self-Management: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: . Participants reported positive experiences with SugarVita and perceived the game as educational and user-friendly. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed for the primary outcomes. These findings support the feasibility and acceptability of SugarVita as a digital educational intervention and warrant further evaluation in larger studies.
title: A Serious Digital Game (SugarVita) to Support Diabetes Self-Management: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.

text: Bridging the Digital Divide in Diabetes Care With an AI-Powered Health Coaching Intervention: Qualitative Formative Study.. Despite advancements in digital health coaching (DHC) for type 2 diabetes self-management, a persistent digital divide limits access among underserved populations, necessitating low-tech, telephone-based alternatives
title: Bridging the Digital Divide in Diabetes Care With an AI-Powered Health Coaching Intervention: Qualitative Formative Study.

text: . This formative qualitative study explored the lived experiences of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) self-management challenges among adults in Alabama and elicited preferences for telephone-based DHC to inform intervention optimization
title: Bridging the Digital Divide in Diabetes Care With an AI-Powered Health Coaching Intervention: Qualitative Formative Study.

text: . This study was part of a larger National Institutes of Health clinical trial (5R01DK129378) that examined the feasibility and needs of a telephone-based DHC intervention for self-management of T2DM. The study employed a qualitative, phenomenological approach to assess patients' needs surrounding digital coaching. Twelve patients diagnosed with T2DM were recruited between August and December 2022
title: Bridging the Digital Divide in Diabetes Care With an AI-Powered Health Coaching Intervention: Qualitative Formative Study.

text: . Data collection involved in-depth, semistructured interviews conducted via telephone calls or secure Zoom sessions. All interviews were audio-recorded, professionally transcribed, and verified for accuracy. Two independent coders analyzed the data using NVivo software version 14 Plus
title: Bridging the Digital Divide in Diabetes Care With an AI-Powered Health Coaching Intervention: Qualitative Formative Study.

text: . Two themes emerged: (1) multifaceted barriers to diabetes self-management spanning behavioral (dietary adherence and nutritional gaps), physical/environmental (mobility limitations and weather constraints), and structural domains (medication shortages, insurance coverage limiting continuous glucose monitoring); (2) expectations for telephone-based DHC, including targeted education (meal
title: Bridging the Digital Divide in Diabetes Care With an AI-Powered Health Coaching Intervention: Qualitative Formative Study.

text: DHC, including targeted education (meal planning, exercise adaptations, and medication effects), health coaches as accountability partners, daily reminders and check-ins via texts/calls, and incentives as extrinsic motivators to adherence
title: Bridging the Digital Divide in Diabetes Care With an AI-Powered Health Coaching Intervention: Qualitative Formative Study.

text: . Insights from the study directly shaped the intervention components of a pilot feasibility trial (NCT05344859). Key challenges in day-to-day T2DM management included diet, physical activity, medication unavailability, and lack of insurance coverage for continuous glucose monitors
title: Bridging the Digital Divide in Diabetes Care With an AI-Powered Health Coaching Intervention: Qualitative Formative Study.

text: . Expectations for a potential telephone-based DHC intervention included targeted education on diet, exercise, and medication effects; perceptions of health coaches as accountability partners; reminders via texts/calls as beneficial; and monetary incentives as extrinsic motivators for adherence to the intervention.
title: Bridging the Digital Divide in Diabetes Care With an AI-Powered Health Coaching Intervention: Qualitative Formative Study.

text: Ecological momentary assessment in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: A scoping review.. To conduct a scoping review of the application of ecological momentary assessment (EMA) in adolescents with type 1 diabetes (T1DM), providing references for future research and practice in this field
title: Ecological momentary assessment in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: A scoping review.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

text: . This review followed the JBI scoping review methodology framework and systematically searched 10 databases, including CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, CBM, PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, EMbase, PsycINFO and CINAHL, from the establishment of the databases to 29 September 2025. The included literature was summarised and analysed. Sixteen studies were included
title: Ecological momentary assessment in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: A scoping review.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

text: . Sixteen studies were included. EMA was used to investigate self-management, glycaemic control, psychosocial factors and cognitive function in adolescents with T1DM. Key findings revealed dynamic, real-time associations: self-management behaviours showed time- and context-dependent effects on glycaemic control (e.g
title: Ecological momentary assessment in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: A scoping review.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

text: . higher risk of omissions in mornings or social situations); affect and glucose levels exhibited bidirectional interactions, with negative affect impairing and positive affect improving glycaemic stability; social environment (peer and family support) and cognitive function (e.g. executive function) significantly moderated management outcomes
title: Ecological momentary assessment in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: A scoping review.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

text: . Most identified associations were within-person and contemporaneous; few studies examined between-person differences or time-lagged predictive effects. EMA demonstrated acceptable feasibility across diverse protocols. However, considerable methodological heterogeneity existed across studies, and most evidence was limited to Western populations
title: Ecological momentary assessment in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: A scoping review.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

text: . EMA is a feasible method for managing type 1 diabetes in adolescents and is capable of capturing real-time, dynamic associations among behaviour, affect, social context and glycaemic control
title: Ecological momentary assessment in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: A scoping review.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

text: . Future research should prioritise methodological standardisation, develop culturally adapted assessment tools and explore real-time intervention strategies to enable precise and personalised diabetes management. From a clinical perspective, EMA can guide individualised care by identifying high-risk time windows (e.g. mornings), social contexts (e.g. peer dining) and emotional triggers (e.g
title: Ecological momentary assessment in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: A scoping review.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

text: . peer dining) and emotional triggers (e.g. negative affect), supporting targeted patient education, just-in-time behavioural reminders and collaborative mental health interventions.
title: Ecological momentary assessment in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: A scoping review.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

text: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.. Chronic non-communicable disease (NCD) care in Nigeria remains largely financed out of pocket, exposing households to affordability barriers and harmful coping strategies
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . This study examined the prevalence and patterning of affordability barriers, financial coping strategies, and predictors of foregone care and distress financing among chronic NCD patients attending public health facilities in Lagos, Nigeria
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . A facility-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among 480 adults receiving outpatient care for chronic NCDs, such as hypertension, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, cancer, chronic respiratory conditions, and sickle cell disease across primary, secondary, and tertiary public facilities
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Participants were recruited using a multistage sampling approach, with eligible patients selected systematically from clinic registers
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Data were collected using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire capturing sociodemographic and household characteristics, employment status, chronic NCD diagnosis and treatment duration, out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure, affordability barriers, and financial coping strategies
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Affordability outcomes included being offered unaffordable treatment, cost-driven treatment decisions, irregular clinic attendance, and inability to access care because of inability to pay. Financial coping strategies were grouped as self-directed financing, social-network support, and distress financing, defined as borrowing or the sale of assets
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Prevalence estimates were reported with exact 95% CIs
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Facility-tier differences and subgroup associations were assessed using chi-square, Fisher's exact, and ANOVA tests. Binary logistic regression models identified predictors of foregone care and distress financing, with average marginal effects and adjusted predicted probabilities estimated to aid interpretation. Statistical significance was set at a two-sided p<0.05
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Affordability barriers were common: 42.9% of patients had been offered unaffordable treatment, 41.9% reported that cost shaped treatment decisions, and 45.0% had forgone care because they could not pay
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Among affordability challenges, medication unaffordability was especially prominent and was comparable across facility tiers, suggesting system-wide pharmaceutical cost pressures rather than isolated access gaps
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Coping followed a clear financial hierarchy: patients first relied on savings or household income (82.9%), many then mobilized social-network support (69.6%), and a substantial minority resorted to distress financing through borrowing or asset sale (28.5%)
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Financial-exposure intensity and treatment duration independently predicted distress financing; financial-exposure intensity also predicted foregone care. Pension income reduced the probability of distress financing by 15.2 pp, while insurance showed no detectable protection
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Chronic NCD care in Lagos public facilities becomes a financial crisis through pervasive affordability barriers, prominent medication unaffordability, reliance on informal household coping, financial-exposure intensity, and treatment chronicity, which drive care rationing and distress financing
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: . Nigeria's universal health coverage agenda should include scaling insurance enrolment for chronic NCD patients, benefit-package redesign, pharmaceutical-pricing reform, and income-protection mechanisms that absorb the recurrent costs of chronic illness care.
title: When Paying for Care Becomes a Crisis: Affordability Barriers, Coping Strategies, and Financial Consequences of Chronic Illness in Lagos, Nigeria.

text: Culturally and linguistically adapted digital diabetes health applications improve self-management and clinical outcomes in racialized immigrants: a systematic scoping review.. title: Culturally and linguistically adapted digital diabetes health applications improve self-management and clinical outcomes in racialized immigrants: a systematic scoping review.

text: . Immigrants and refugees face access, education and management inequities as the prevalence and cost of chronic disease management escalates in host countries. Digital health applications may offer effective and equitable solutions to support self-management and empower immigrants
title: Culturally and linguistically adapted digital diabetes health applications improve self-management and clinical outcomes in racialized immigrants: a systematic scoping review.

text: . This study systematically scoped published evidence on digital health applications tailored for type 2 diabetes management among racialized immigrants, addressing an important intersection of digital innovation and health equity
title: Culturally and linguistically adapted digital diabetes health applications improve self-management and clinical outcomes in racialized immigrants: a systematic scoping review.

text: . Searching multiple databases (2010-March 2025), 14 primary studies and 15 reviews were identified, featuring culturally adapted, multimodal interventions with human (peer or provider) support across patient-matched languages and cultures such as Arabic, Chinese, Spanish, and Vietnamese
title: Culturally and linguistically adapted digital diabetes health applications improve self-management and clinical outcomes in racialized immigrants: a systematic scoping review.

text: . The 15 reviews on mainstream digital education allowed us to contextualize digital features, outcomes, and practice mediators and challenges. Primary studies found that tailored digital health interventions significantly enhanced engagement, self-efficacy, health literacy and motivation for self-management, and most clinically significantly lowered HbA1c levels (moderate-high risk of bias)
title: Culturally and linguistically adapted digital diabetes health applications improve self-management and clinical outcomes in racialized immigrants: a systematic scoping review.

text: . Tailoring included cultural food advice, education framed around family and faith, and apps in patients' native language. In comparing digital application features and type 2 diabetes outcomes with our review of reviews results, we were able to show successful replication in racialized immigrant populations, demonstrating health equity opportunities
title: Culturally and linguistically adapted digital diabetes health applications improve self-management and clinical outcomes in racialized immigrants: a systematic scoping review.

text: . These results demonstrate the importance of adapting, personalizing, creating a trusted environment, and integrating human supports to ensure long-term engagement and equitable health outcomes.

text: Cultural Adaptation, Translation, and Psychometric Validation of the Chinese Diabetes Education Questionnaire (DATE-Q-Chinese).. title: Cultural Adaptation, Translation, and Psychometric Validation of the Chinese Diabetes Education Questionnaire (DATE-Q-Chinese).

title: Cultural Adaptation, Translation, and Psychometric Validation of the Chinese Diabetes Education Questionnaire (DATE-Q-Chinese).

text: . title: Cultural Adaptation, Translation, and Psychometric Validation of the Chinese Diabetes Education Questionnaire (DATE-Q-Chinese).

text: . title: Cultural Adaptation, Translation, and Psychometric Validation of the Chinese Diabetes Education Questionnaire (DATE-Q-Chinese).

text: . Mean content validity and face validity scores were 4.7 (standard deviation 0.6) and 4.7 (0.5) out of 5. Validation study participants were 35.9% female (mean age 63.5 (12.6) years). Five factors matching the original DATE-Q domains (self-management, long-term complications, being active, healthy eating, psychosocial wellbeing) explained 64.2% of the total variance
title: Cultural Adaptation, Translation, and Psychometric Validation of the Chinese Diabetes Education Questionnaire (DATE-Q-Chinese).

text: . Cronbach's α was 0.84 (range: 0.70-0.85 across domains). The total DATE-Q-Chinese score (mean 13.4 (3.8) out of 20) was positively correlated with health literacy (r=0.269, p=0.006) and increased with education level (p=0.01)
title: Cultural Adaptation, Translation, and Psychometric Validation of the Chinese Diabetes Education Questionnaire (DATE-Q-Chinese).

text: . title: Cultural Adaptation, Translation, and Psychometric Validation of the Chinese Diabetes Education Questionnaire (DATE-Q-Chinese).
